### - [ ] T-5.3.6 — Pod Overhead values are asserted only as Helm renders, never as scheduler behavior [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Each `RuntimeClass` should define `Pod Overhead` so scheduling accounts for the isolation cost. ... `sandboxed` (gVisor) ~200m CPU / ~200Mi memory; `microvm` (Kata) ~500m CPU / ~500Mi memory." (spec/05_runtime-registry-and-pool-model.md:676-682)
- **Existing tests:** `charts/lenny/tests/runtimeclasses_test.yaml:18-59` asserts the rendered `gvisor` and `kata` RuntimeClass manifests carry the reference `overhead.podFixed` CPU and memory values (Helm-unit, tier0/1). No component, integration, or e2e test confirms the kube-scheduler actually adds the declared Pod Overhead to a sandboxed/microvm pod's effective resource request when placing it, which is the behavior the field exists to produce.
- **Gap:** The scheduling effect of Pod Overhead is unverified. This is a tier5 e2e gap (it needs a real kube-scheduler). It is a real operator-capacity journey (a `sandboxed` pod's effective request includes the ~200m/~200Mi overhead so a node's allocatable accounting is correct). Severity is Medium because the spec uses "should" and the rendered values are confirmed; the residual risk is that the overhead never reaches the scheduler.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today on Kind with the gVisor RuntimeClass installed; the `tests/testinfra/kind` harness registers runc and gVisor RuntimeClasses when host gVisor is available (TESTING.md line 724).

### - [x] T-5.3.7 — Kata cross-tenant scrub step 7 (guest VM restart) is validated for admission only, never for execution [Medium] — RESOLVED 468ac6de (reconciled against proposal 0034)
- **Resolution:** Proposal 0034 reworded §5.2 step 7 of the Kata/microvm scrub variant from an in-guest "guest VM restart" via "the Kata runtime's VM lifecycle API" to a "fresh-guest reprovision": the finding's premise (an in-guest adapter drives a guest reboot and re-runs scrub verification in place) is unimplementable, because the adapter holds zero RBAC with default-deny egress and host-sharing forbidden ([Section 13.1](spec/13_security-model.md)), and a full guest restart would kill the process issuing and reporting it. The reconciled mechanism retires the pod at the occupancy-zero recycle boundary after the whole-pod scrub reports, and the gateway's WarmPoolController provisions a fresh replacement pod (a fresh guest VM), landed in `pkg/sandbox/podscrub` as the `if in.VMRestart` retire branch (commit `19bc1821`, "0034 S3: add the vm-restart retire disposition in podscrub Decide (C3 core)"). `tests/tier9_security/pool_admission_isolation_test.go::TestVMRestartCrossTenantRecycleRetires_spec_5_2_step_7` (updated to the new disposition in commit `07b79299`) now drives `podscrub.Decide` across preConnect/non-preConnect and clean/warn-failed combinations and asserts the vm-restart pod is retired (`Retire=true`, `NextPhase=Draining`, reason `ReasonVMRestartReprovision`) rather than reused, closing the execution-path gap the finding named. A companion control test, `TestNonVMRestartRecycleReusesControl_spec_5_2`, confirms a non-vm-restart microvm pool still reuses the pod, ruling out a blanket-retire false positive.

### - [x] T-5.3.8 — Cross-tenant reuse is permitted only on microvm; the rejection on gVisor/runc pools has no component-tier coverage [Medium] — RESOLVED 4d424028 (reconciled against proposal 0002)
- **Resolution:** Proposal 0002's session/service execution-model reconciliation renamed the field to `sessionPolicy.recycle.allowCrossTenantReuse` and relocated its validation from the CRD-level `pool_config_validator` webhook to the gateway's Postgres-backed `poolstore.ValidatePool` path (`pkg/gateway/runtime/poolstore/poolstore.go:573`, `"poolstore: recycle.allowCrossTenantReuse is permitted only when isolationProfile is microvm (§5.2)"`), with a unit-tier case in `pkg/gateway/runtime/poolstore/poolstore_test.go:493` ("sequential cross-tenant reuse without microvm is rejected", `IsolationProfile: isolation.ProfileSandboxed`). The live-admission gap the finding named is now closed: `tests/tier9_security/pool_admission_isolation_test.go::TestPoolAdmissionDerivedPropertyGates_spec_5_2` (case `microvm-cross-tenant-gate`, added in commit `4d424028`, "0002 S5b: tier-9 + component tests for session/service derived-property gates") drives a `sandboxed`-profile pool with `allowCrossTenantReuse: true` through the live `POST /v1/admin/pools` admin API on a Kind cluster backed by real Postgres, asserts a 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` mentioning "isolationProfile is microvm", and asserts a corrected `microvm`-profile control pool is admitted. This is the persisted-store-plus-live-admission coverage the finding found missing; the `tests/tier2_component/stores/poolstore_test.go` direct-pgstore variant remains unextended with this specific case, but the live tier-9 path already exercises the same rejection against a real Postgres-backed registry at a stronger tier than the originally suggested test.

Severity is Low because Confidential Containers is an AKS-specific advanced option rather than a normative §5.3 profile (the §5.3 table defines only standard/sandboxed/microvm).

- **Suggested test:** Add a `confidential_containers` capability row to `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml` (validated on AKS, skip with reason on GKE/EKS) and a `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/confidential_containers_test.go` that boots a CoCo-backed pod and asserts it accepts a claim and tears down.

### - [ ] T-5.3.11 — RuntimeProvider / KubeVirt extension point is a forward-looking abstraction with no test [Info] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "A `RuntimeProvider` abstraction keeps the door open for future backends (e.g., KubeVirt)." (spec/05_runtime-registry-and-pool-model.md:686)
- **Existing tests:** A repository-wide search for `RuntimeProvider` and `KubeVirt` in `pkg/`, `tests/`, and `charts/` returns no implementation or test.
- **Gap:** No test exists, and none is warranted yet because the abstraction is explicitly forward-looking and not part of the v1 isolation surface. This is recorded as an observation so a future reviewer does not re-flag it as a missing test. No action is required until a concrete `RuntimeProvider` backend (such as KubeVirt) ships.
- **Dependencies:** none — no test is required for v1.
- **Suggested test:** No test for v1. When a `RuntimeProvider` backend ships, add a tier2 contract test under `tests/tier2_component/` pinning the provider interface and a tier6 e2e test for the concrete backend.

## §6.1 What a Pre-Warmed Pod Looks Like <a id="t-6.1"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/06_warm-pod-model.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
Proposal 0002 (landed 2026-06-12) rewrote §6.1's execution-mode vocabulary: the old `executionMode: task` / `executionMode: concurrent` split is gone, replaced by a single `sessionPolicy` block (`maxConcurrentSessions`, `recycle.enabled`) that unifies the one-session-per-pod default, the recycle-opt-in (former task-mode) pod-reuse path, and the concurrent-slot (former concurrent-mode) path under one model. Since the 2026-06-03 audit, substantial SDK-warm coverage has landed: a real `preConnect`-capable reference runtime (`cmd/runtimes/preconnect-echo`) now exists and is wired into the Kind e2e fixture and a §6.3 Kind load benchmark (`TestStartupLatencySDKWarm`) that drives real sessions against it; the gateway-to-adapter demotion handoff (`pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/sdkwarm_bind_test.go`) is now verified against a real adapter over gRPC and a real envtest-backed `Sandbox`, closing both the demotion-on-blocking-path happy path and the `SDK_DEMOTION_NOT_SUPPORTED` failure path; the recycle re-warm edge's `sdkConnectTimeoutSeconds` watchdog and clock-anchoring (`pkg/controller/sandbox/sdkwarm_recycle_test.go`) is now covered against envtest; and the `SDKWarmDemotionRateHigh` advisory event plus its `acknowledgeHighDemotionRate` suppression (`pkg/controller/poolscaling/circuitbreaker_override_test.go`) is now covered at the reconciler level. Four findings resolve this pass on that evidence (T-6.1.1, T-6.1.2, T-6.1.12, T-6.1.13). What remains open: the circuit-breaker's leader-failover persistence and `pool.sdk_warm_circuit_breaker_open` audit emission are still untested against a live PSC (T-6.1.3); the one-session-per-pod termination invariant and the per-slot/per-session credential lease lifecycle still lack tier4/tier5 coverage against real warm pods, though per-slot file-mode and rotation-isolation now have real unit/tier9 tests (T-6.1.4, T-6.1.5); the recycling-pool per-session demotion contribution to the shared breaker threshold is untested (T-6.1.6); the two preConnect-rejection messages have no wire-level contract test (T-6.1.7); the blocking-path glob-matching table has no dedicated component-tier test (T-6.1.8); the chaos-tier SIGTERM-during-connect-on-a-real-pod scenario is still missing even though the adapter-internal logic is now unit-tested (T-6.1.9); the warm-pod anatomy invariants are still asserted only on the rendered podspec, never on a running pod (T-6.1.10); the gradual-drain-after-breaker-trip behavior is untested (T-6.1.11); and the spec-map.json §6.1 entry still misattributes the tier6 isolation tests (T-6.1.14).
Counts: 6 High (2 resolved, 4 open), 5 Medium (all open), 2 Low (both resolved), 1 Info (open).

### Findings

### - [x] T-6.1.1 — SDK-warm mode is never exercised against a live runtime at tier2 or above [High] — RESOLVED a109d62e
- **Resolution:** Commit `a109d62e` ("F-6.1.1 + F-6.2.4 + F-6.1.5: §6.1 SDK-warm adapter entry point, gateway consumption, reference runtime") added the `preconnect-echo` reference runtime (`cmd/runtimes/preconnect-echo`, fixture `RuntimePreConnectEcho`) that declares `capabilities.preConnect: true`, closing the "no test runtime declares preConnect" dependency this finding was blocked on. The same commit added `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/sdkwarm_bind_test.go`, which drives the SDK-warm claim path against a real adapter over gRPC (bufconn) and a real envtest-backed `Sandbox` object. Commit `b3692225` ("0002 S24: sdk_connecting reserved terminus and recycle re-warm clock re-anchor") added `pkg/controller/sandbox/sdkwarm_recycle_test.go`, which drives the Sandbox-to-Pod reconciler through the `warming → sdk_connecting → idle` and `claimed → sdk_connecting → reserved` edges against envtest. Commit `766f1f5f` ("test: implement §6.3 per-runtime-class startup benchmark (F-6.3.5)") added `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go::TestStartupLatencySDKWarm`, which installs the `preconnect-echo-runtime` pool on a real Kind cluster (`tests/testinfra/kind/agent-workload.yaml`) via the real `PoolScalingController`/`WarmPoolController` and drives real `POST /v1/sessions/start` calls against it, asserting claim-to-ready latency at or under the pod-warm budget — direct live-cluster evidence that pods warm through `sdk_connecting` to `idle` and that a claim attaches without paying SDK cold-start. Together these close the primary end-to-end gap this finding named: the full SDK-warm path is now exercised against a live runtime at both component (envtest) and Kind e2e tiers, even though no single test lives at the exact `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/sdk_warm_lifecycle_test.go` path originally suggested.

### - [x] T-6.1.2 — Demotion-on-demand happy path (blocking-path upload triggers DemoteSDK) has no tier2-or-higher test [High] — RESOLVED a109d62e
- **Resolution:** Commit `a109d62e` added `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/sdkwarm_bind_test.go::TestBindSDKWarmDemotesOnBlockingPath_spec_6_1`, which drives `podsession.Binder.Bind` with a workspace plan containing `CLAUDE.md` against a real adapter (`adapter.Server` over a real gRPC connection via `bufconn`) and a real envtest-backed `Sandbox`, and asserts: `DemoteSDK` is called exactly once, `ConfigureWorkspace` (the SDK-warm path) is not called, the pod-warm `StartSession` path runs instead, and the `SDKDemotion` metric callback fires with the pool name and a non-negative teardown duration. The sibling `TestBindSDKWarmConfiguresWhenNoBlockingPath_spec_6_1` in the same file covers the no-demotion arm (claim attaches via `ConfigureWorkspace`, no `StartSession`, no demotion). This closes the gateway-to-adapter demotion handoff this finding described as unverified above the unit boundary.

### - [ ] T-6.1.3 — Circuit-breaker trip, audit emission, and leader-failover hold are never driven through a live PoolScalingController [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "If the rolling 5-minute demotion rate exceeds 90% ... the PoolScalingController automatically disables SDK-warm for the pool by setting `spec.sdkWarmDisabled: true` ... The gateway emits an audit event (`pool.sdk_warm_circuit_breaker_open`) when this occurs." and "the breaker's open/closed state is persisted on the `SandboxWarmPool.status.sdkWarmCircuitBreaker` subresource so that it survives PSC leader crashes (up to 25s failover)." (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:50, spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:52)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/controller/poolscaling/circuitbreaker_sync_test.go` covers the SSA write of `spec.sdkWarmDisabled` and the three status fields, the low-rate no-trip case, the persisted-`minOpenUntil` hold across a fresh leader, and grace-window close, all against a fake client at unit tier. `pkg/controller/poolscaling/circuitbreaker_override_test.go` (new since the 2026-06-03 audit) adds the operator-override SSA paths (`TestSyncDisabledOverrideForcesSDKWarmOff_spec_6_1`, `TestSyncEnabledOverrideClearsTrippedBreakerAheadOfGraceWindow_spec_6_1`, `TestSyncEnabledOverrideReTripsWhenRateStillHigh_spec_6_1`), still against a fake client. `tests/tier8_chaos/leader_election_test.go` exercises generic WarmPoolController lease failover but never references the breaker, `sdkWarmDisabled`, or demotion (verified by grep). The audit event `pool.sdk_warm_circuit_breaker_open` is still not asserted by any test (grep returns no match outside the metrics catalog); the admin-API audit test that does exist, `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/pools_circuit_breaker_test.go::TestCircuitBreakerOverrideEnabled_spec_15_1`, asserts the distinct `pool.sdk_warm_circuit_breaker_override` event fired by the operator-override endpoint, not the PSC's own trip-open event.
- **Gap:** The breaker has no integration or chaos coverage with a real PSC reconciling a real CRD: no test drives a high demotion rate to a live trip, asserts the `pool.sdk_warm_circuit_breaker_open` audit event is emitted, kills the PSC leader, and asserts the new leader honors the persisted `minOpenUntil`. The leader-failover persistence is a resilience-under-failure scenario that belongs in tier8 chaos. The audit emission on trip is a security-observability surface with no conformance check. Target tiers are tier4 (PSC plus envtest), tier8 (chaos, leader kill mid-open), and tier9 (audit-event assertion).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the preConnect test runtime (now available: `cmd/runtimes/preconnect-echo`, closing the prior blocker) to generate demotions, `tests/testinfra/envtest` or `tests/testinfra/kind` for a live PSC, and `tests/testinfra/audit` to assert the audit event. The chaos kill-leader harness exists in `tests/tier8_chaos/chaos_helpers_test.go`.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier8_chaos/sdk_warm_breaker_failover_test.go` that drives the demotion rate above 90% against the `preconnect-echo` pool, asserts `spec.sdkWarmDisabled: true` and the `pool.sdk_warm_circuit_breaker_open` audit event, kills the PSC leader inside the grace window, and asserts the new leader keeps the breaker open until `minOpenUntil`, using `tests/testinfra/chaos` and `tests/testinfra/audit`.

### - [ ] T-6.1.4 — Session-mode one-session-only termination invariant is unverified end to end [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "**One-session-per-pod default and the recycle opt-in.** With the default `sessionPolicy` (`maxConcurrentSessions: 1`, `recycle.enabled: false`), a pod serves exactly one session: after the session completes or fails, the pod is terminated and replaced. This prevents cross-session data leakage through residual workspace files, session transcripts, cached DNS, or runtime memory." (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:24)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/pod_lifecycle_test.go::TestPodLifecycle` asserts a warmed pod is `idle` and matches its deployment-model container topology, but it never runs a session to completion and then asserts the pod is terminated rather than reassigned. No tier4, tier5, tier8, or tier9 test asserts that a second session for the same pool receives a different pod and that the first pod is gone.
- **Gap:** The single-session termination invariant is a stated security control (cross-session data-leakage prevention) and has no end-to-end verification, nor an adversarial test confirming a freshly claimed pod carries no residual workspace files or transcripts from a prior session on the same node. This is both a user-journey assertion (two sequential session-mode sessions land on distinct pods) and a security control (no residual state). Target tiers are tier5 (Kind, pod identity across sessions) and tier9 (residual-state probe).
- **Dependencies:** Requires `tests/testinfra/kind` and `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver` to run two sequential session-mode sessions and a pod-identity diff. The security probe (reading `/workspace/current` and `/sessions` on the replacement pod) can reuse `tests/testinfra/security`. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/session_pod_no_recycle_test.go` that completes one session-mode session, records its pod name, starts a second session for the same pool, and asserts the second pod is distinct and the first pod object is deleted; add a tier9 case that inspects the replacement pod's `/workspace/current` and `/sessions` for residual files.

### - [ ] T-6.1.5 — Task-mode and concurrent-mode credential lease lifecycle has no tier2-or-higher test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "**Per-session credential lease lifecycle on recycling pods.** Credentials are leased per session rather than per pod. A fresh credential assignment (`AssignCredentials` RPC) is performed at each session dispatch ... `/run/lenny/credentials.json` is rewritten with the new lease before the runtime binary is spawned for each session. The previous lease is revoked when the session completes or the runtime exits." and "**Per-slot credential lease lifecycle (`maxConcurrentSessions > 1`).** ... The adapter writes per-slot credential files at `/run/lenny/slots/{slotId}/credentials.json` (mode `0440`, tmpfs-backed ...)" (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:26, spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:28)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier4_integration/concurrent_workspace_test.go` (rewritten since the audit for the `sessionPolicy.maxConcurrentSessions > 1` model) now drives a real `adapter.Server` and a real `cmd/runtimes/echo-concurrent` process end to end at tier4, asserting per-slot workspace isolation and per-slot `slotId` response tagging, but it asserts no credential-file behavior. The per-slot credential surface itself is now covered at unit tier by `pkg/adapter/slot_test.go::TestAssignCredentialsSlotWritesPerSlotFile_spec_6_1` (per-slot file creation, no global file written) and `::TestRotateCredentialsSlotIsIndependent_spec_6_1` (a rotation on one slot leaves a sibling slot's credential file untouched), and the file-mode/ownership control is now covered by `tests/tier9_security/concurrent_slot_isolation_test.go::TestPerSlotCredentialFileReadScope_spec_6_60`, which asserts mode `0o440`, no world access, and that each slot's file contains only its own lease. None of these three run against a real warm pod (Kind); they exercise the adapter server and `credfile` package directly. Per-session (former per-task) re-leasing on a recycling pod — a fresh `AssignCredentials` at each session dispatch with the prior lease revoked — still has no test above the unit boundary.
- **Gap:** The file-mode `0440` and independent-rotation guarantees that were previously entirely untested now have real unit/tier9 coverage, closing that specific security-relevant sub-gap. What remains: per-session re-leasing on a recycling pod (a fresh `AssignCredentials` at each session dispatch, the previous lease revoked on completion) has no test above the unit boundary, and none of the per-slot credential tests run against a real warm pod, so the tier4/tier5 "real adapter writing the slot files on a live pod" wiring this finding named is still missing. Target tiers are tier4 (compose) and tier5 (Kind, real adapter writing the slot files on a live pod).
- **Dependencies:** Requires real warm pods (`tests/testinfra/kind`), a concurrent-workspace pool fixture with `maxConcurrentSessions >= 2` (the fixture and a real per-slot runtime, `cmd/runtimes/echo-concurrent`, now exist per `tests/tier4_integration/concurrent_workspace_test.go`), and the credential-leasing service from `tests/testinfra/tokenservice`. A recycling-pool (`recycle.enabled: true`) fixture is needed for the per-session re-lease case. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/concurrent_slot_credentials_test.go` that assigns two slots on one pod, asserts each has its own `/run/lenny/slots/{slotId}/credentials.json` at mode `0440` on the live pod, rotates one slot's lease, and asserts the sibling slot's in-flight LLM call is unaffected; add a tier4 case on a `recycle.enabled: true` pool asserting `/run/lenny/credentials.json` is rewritten and the prior lease revoked between two sequential sessions on the same pod.

### - [ ] T-6.1.6 — preConnect demotion rate contributes to the circuit breaker per task and per slot, but the cross-mode aggregation is untested above unit [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The `sdkWarmBlockingPaths` check is evaluated per session at dispatch time (each session may upload different files); if a file in the new session's workspace plan matches a blocking pattern, the gateway sets `requiresDemotion: true` on the session's `ClaimOpts` and the adapter calls `DemoteSDK` before materializing that session's workspace ... The per-session demotion rate contributes to the same circuit-breaker threshold." (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:76)
- **Existing tests:** The compatibility-matrix validator (`pkg/gateway/runtime/poolstore/sdkwarm_test.go::TestValidatePreConnectExecutionMode_spec_5_2_6_1`) asserts that `sessionPolicy.maxConcurrentSessions > 1` and `executionMode: service` are both rejected for `preConnect: true`, and that the one-session-per-pod default (with or without `recycle.enabled`) is admitted, all at unit tier. There is no test that drives per-session demotions on a recycling preConnect pool and asserts they feed the same breaker counter that non-recycling session demotions feed.
- **Gap:** The per-session demotion and re-warm cycle on a recycling preConnect pool (session A uploads a blocking file → demotion → pod-warm path for session A → SDK re-warmed at the next recycle boundary → session B) is unverified end to end, and its contribution to the shared circuit-breaker rate is untested. This is a deployment-combination gap (recycling session mode crossed with SDK-warm) on top of the gaps in T-6.1.1 and T-6.1.2. Target tiers are tier4 and tier5.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the preConnect test runtime (`cmd/runtimes/preconnect-echo`, now available) configured on a `recycle.enabled: true` pool with `onScrubFailure` set, plus the per-session dispatch harness. Reuse `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver` and `tests/testinfra/kind`. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/sdk_warm_recycle_demotion_test.go` that runs a sequence of sessions on a recycling preConnect pool, alternating blocking and non-blocking workspace plans, and asserts per-session demotion is applied only when the plan matches, the SDK is re-warmed through `sdk_connecting` between sessions at the recycle boundary, and the breaker counter reflects the aggregate rate.

### - [ ] T-6.1.7 — preConnect-plus-concurrent-sessions rejection error messages have no wire-level contract test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The pool controller rejects pool definitions that combine `sessionPolicy.maxConcurrentSessions > 1` with `capabilities.preConnect: true` at validation time with error: \"preConnect: true requires sessionPolicy.maxConcurrentSessions: 1; concurrent sessions require independent per-slot agent initialization\"" and "The pool controller rejects pool definitions that combine `executionMode: service` with `capabilities.preConnect: true` at validation time with error: \"preConnect: true is not supported with executionMode: service; service mode has no Lenny-managed agent lifecycle\"." (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:77, spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:78)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/runtime/poolstore/sdkwarm_test.go::TestValidatePreConnectExecutionMode_spec_5_2_6_1` (moved from `pkg/gateway/poolstore/sdkwarm_test.go` in the `pkg/gateway/runtime` package regrouping) calls the validator function directly and asserts each rejection contains the substrings `"maxConcurrentSessions > 1"` / `"executionMode: service"` plus `"preConnect: true"`, but not the full verbatim message text, and it is a unit call rather than a request through the admin API or admission webhook. Note the implementation's actual string (`pkg/gateway/runtime/poolstore/poolstore.go`: `"preConnect: true is not supported with sessionPolicy.maxConcurrentSessions > 1; ..."`) does not match the spec's quoted verbatim text (`"preConnect: true requires sessionPolicy.maxConcurrentSessions: 1; ..."`) — a code/spec text drift the wire-level contract test below would also catch. No tier3 contract test pins the exact rejection string returned over the wire on a `POST`/`PUT` to the pool admin endpoint.
- **Gap:** The two verbatim rejection messages are a documented API contract that an operator (and tooling) reads. They are asserted only as a substring at unit level, so a regression that changes the message text or moves the rejection from the admin API to a different surface would ship undetected; the current code/spec text mismatch noted above is exactly the kind of drift this gap allows to persist silently. Target tier is tier3 (admin-API wire conformance).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the admin-API harness in `tests/testinfra/gateway` and a pool-creation request fixture. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier3 case in `tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/` that `POST`s a `sessionPolicy.maxConcurrentSessions > 1` pool and a `service`-mode pool, each with `capabilities.preConnect: true`, and asserts the response status and the exact rejection message for both, plus the admission-webhook path via `tests/testinfra/fakekube`; reconcile the code/spec text mismatch this test would surface.

### - [ ] T-6.1.8 — `sdkWarmBlockingPaths` glob-matching contract (** dialect, case-sensitivity, symlink-not-resolved, workspaceDefaults inclusion) is untested above unit [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The glob dialect is Go's `path.Match` extended with `**` support ... `*` matches within a single path segment only (no `/`) ... Matching is case-sensitive on all platforms ... Symlinks are not resolved ... Files injected via `workspaceDefaults` ... are included in the matching check alongside client-uploaded files." (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:36)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/runtime/runtimestore/sdkwarm_setuppolicy_test.go` (moved from `pkg/gateway/runtimestore/sdkwarm_setuppolicy_test.go` in the `pkg/gateway/runtime` package regrouping) covers the default seeding (`["CLAUDE.md", ".claude/*"]`) and merge inheritance of the pattern list, but it does not exercise the match decision against sample relative paths. `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/sdkwarm_bind_test.go::TestRequiresDemotionDecision_spec_6_1` now exercises `RequiresDemotion` against a small case table (no-preConnect, matching path, non-matching path, empty list, nil plan), but it does not cover the `**`-versus-`*` segment semantics, case sensitivity, the literal-symlink-path rule, or `workspaceDefaults` inclusion. No test asserts that `**/CLAUDE.md` matches `subdir/CLAUDE.md` while `CLAUDE.md` does not, that matching is case-sensitive, that a symlink's literal path is checked rather than its target, or that a `workspaceDefaults` file triggers demotion when the client uploads nothing.
- **Gap:** The match-decision contract that determines whether `requiresDemotion` is set is the precise boundary between an SDK-warm and a pod-warm session, and its `**`-versus-`*` semantics, case sensitivity, symlink handling, and `workspaceDefaults` inclusion are each a documented rule with no behavioral test at component tier. The most security-relevant of these is the symlink-not-resolved rule (a crafted symlink must not be used to evade demotion). This combines a standards-style matching contract with an adversarial evasion path. Target tiers are tier2 (the matcher with its real backing runtime store) and tier4 (the decision observed on a claim).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the preConnect test runtime for the tier4 leg (now available: `cmd/runtimes/preconnect-echo`) and a table of relative paths for the tier2 leg. The tier2 matcher table is buildable today against `pkg/gateway/runtime/runtimestore`.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier2_component/gateway_subsystems/sdk_warm_blocking_match_test.go` with a path-matching table covering `**` segment matching, single-segment `*`, case sensitivity, the literal-symlink-path rule, and a `workspaceDefaults`-only match, asserting `requiresDemotion` for each, then a tier4 case confirming a `workspaceDefaults`-triggered demotion fires with zero client uploads.

### - [ ] T-6.1.9 — SIGTERM during `sdk_connecting` and the `sdkConnectTimeoutSeconds` watchdog have no resilience test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The adapter must handle SIGTERM during `sdk_connecting` as follows: (1) call `DemoteSDK` internally with a bounded timeout ... (2) if `DemoteSDK` does not complete within the timeout, force-terminate the SDK process; (3) exit the adapter process. The pod then transitions to `terminated` (not `failed`)" and "If the SDK does not complete its connection and transition out of `sdk_connecting` to `idle` or `reserved` within this timeout, the WarmPoolController transitions the pod to `failed` and increments `lenny_warmpool_sdk_connect_timeout_total`." (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:67, spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:69)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/adapter/shutdown_demote_test.go` (new since the audit) now covers the SIGTERM-during-`sdk_connecting` handling directly at unit tier: `TestShutdownDemoteSDKDemotesPreConnected_spec_6_1_67` and `TestShutdownDemoteSDKForceTerminatesOnTimeout_spec_6_1_67` assert `DemoteSDK` is attempted with the bounded timeout and the SDK process is force-terminated on timeout, `TestDemoteTimeoutFromEnv_spec_6_1_67` covers the `LENNY_DEMOTE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` override, and `TestSDKWarmInProcessForceTerminate_spec_6_1_67` exercises the force-terminate path directly. The `sdkConnectTimeoutSeconds` watchdog is now covered at component (envtest) tier by `pkg/controller/sandbox/sdkwarm_recycle_test.go::TestReconcileRecycleRewarmWatchdogRetiresOverBudget` (an over-budget re-warm retires the pod to `failed`) and `::TestReconcileRecycleRewarmAnchorsClockAtRewarmStamp` (the watchdog clock is anchored at the re-warm-start stamp rather than pod start, so a long-lived pod's prior occupancy episode does not count against the re-warm budget). None of these send an actual SIGTERM to a running adapter process in a real pod, and none evict a real Kind pod mid-`sdk_connecting`.
- **Gap:** The adapter-internal SIGTERM-handling logic and the watchdog's clock-anchoring rule are now both unit/component-tested, closing the logic-level gap this finding originally named. What remains untested is the resilience scenario itself: a real SIGTERM (or a real node eviction) delivered to a live adapter process mid-`sdk_connecting` in a real pod, confirming the pod reaches `terminated` (not `failed`) end to end and the SDK process is actually gone from the node. This is a credential-leak-prevention control under failure and is a chaos-tier scenario, not a unit-tier one. Target tier is tier8 (chaos, SIGTERM/eviction during connect on a real Kind pod).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the preConnect test runtime (now available: `cmd/runtimes/preconnect-echo`) plus the ability to hold the runtime in `sdk_connecting` (a runtime stub that stalls connect) and a real pod-eviction/SIGTERM injector. Reuse `tests/testinfra/chaos`; the stalling-connect stub does not exist yet and building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier8_chaos/sdk_connecting_sigterm_test.go` that evicts a real Kind pod mid-`sdk_connecting` (using `preconnect-echo` or a stalling-connect variant) and asserts the pod reaches `terminated` (not `failed`) and the SDK process is gone from the node, using `tests/testinfra/chaos` and `tests/testinfra/kind`.

### - [ ] T-6.1.10 — Warm-pod anatomy invariants are asserted only on the rendered podspec, never on a running idle pod [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`/workspace/current` exists but is empty; `/workspace/staging` exists for upload staging; `/sessions` directory present for session files ... No LLM provider credentials assigned (the credential lease is assigned at finalize, after the pod is claimed and before the session reaches `ready`); No user session bound; No client files present; Marked \"idle and claimable\" via readiness gate." (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:11)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/controller/sandbox/podspec/sa_token_test.go` asserts the projected SA token volume (audience-bound, 900s TTL) at unit tier, and `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/pod_lifecycle_test.go` asserts a warm pod is `idle` with the expected container set and `RuntimeClass runc`. No test inspects a running idle pod to confirm `/workspace/current` is present and empty, `/workspace/staging` and `/sessions` exist, no credential file is present at `/run/lenny/credentials.json` before finalize, and no client files are present.
- **Gap:** The filesystem-layout and no-credentials-at-warm-time invariants are verified only against the rendered pod spec, not against the live pod. The "no LLM credential assigned at warm time" invariant is a security control (the lease now arrives at finalize, after claim and before `ready`, rather than at claim time itself) with no on-pod assertion. This is a deployment-state verification gap. Target tiers are tier5 (Kind, exec into the idle pod) and tier9 (assert the absence of a credential file on a warm pod).
- **Dependencies:** Requires `tests/testinfra/kind` and a `kubectl exec` helper to read the warm pod's filesystem. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/warm_pod_anatomy_test.go` that execs into an idle warm pod and asserts `/workspace/current` exists and is empty, `/workspace/staging` and `/sessions` exist, and `/run/lenny/credentials.json` is absent before finalize, using `tests/testinfra/kind`.

## §6.2 Pod State Machine <a id="t-6.2"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/06_warm-pod-model.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
Proposal 0002 (session/service execution model, per-pod occupancy claims; commit `fe3956e8`) retired task mode and the `attached`/`task_cleanup` state names entirely, replacing them with a two-layer model: a coarse `Sandbox.status.phase` occupancy enum (`warming`, `idle`, `reserved`, `claimed`, `sdk_connecting`, `draining`, `failed`, `terminated`) that the WarmPoolController projects from the per-pod `SandboxClaim`, plus the fine Postgres session-lifecycle states (`running`, `input_required`, `suspended`, `resume_pending`, `resuming`, `awaiting_client_action`, and the terminals). Proposals 0007 (eager claim), 0018, 0024, 0034 (vm-restart scrub profile), and 0035 (concurrent-session slot lifecycle end-to-end; commits `468ac6de`, `ca0d70b8`, and the closing build-out through `c3014435`) layered the `reserved` hold, the `recycle` disposition, the `claimed → sdk_connecting` re-warm edge, and the renamed concurrent-occupancy model (`slot_active` re-keyed to the coarse `claimed`) on top. Two findings (T-6.2.2 task-mode cleanup, T-6.2.12 the bespoke 5-second label-stabilization delay) target mechanisms this rewrite removed outright and are resolved as moot. The spec-map under-reporting finding (T-6.2.14) is resolved: `tests/spec-map.json` §6.2 now lists the slothealth, slotclaimer, slotretry, recycle-scrub, and tier-11 doc-reconciliation suites the 0035 close-out registered. The remaining eleven findings stay open: most gained substantial new unit- and component-tier coverage from the 0035/0034/0007 build-outs (SDK-warm SIGTERM/watchdog decision logic, the claim-time `RequiresDemotion` bind path, the eager-claim pool-exhaustion `SESSION_CREATION_FAILED` case, the `resuming → cancelled` coordination-generation bump), but the live cluster/real-store journeys they originally asked for — a tier5 e2e SDK-warm or concurrent-modes test, a tier2 envtest against a real Postgres `sessionstore` for the resume watchdog, and a tier3 contract test pinning the timeout reason codes on the wire — still do not exist. Counts: 5 High, 5 Medium, 1 Low, 0 Info (open); 6 High, 5 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info (all findings, open and resolved).

### Findings

### - [ ] T-6.2.1 — SDK-warm fork (warming → sdk_connecting → idle), DemoteSDK, and the demotion circuit breaker have no component-or-higher test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Warm fill (SDK-warm path, preConnect: true): warming ──→ sdk_connecting ... sdk_connecting ──→ idle (SDK pre-connect completes ...) ... sdk_connecting ──→ terminated (SIGTERM received: DemoteSDK called with timeout, then process exits)" and "the adapter calls the `DemoteSDK` RPC ... transitions the pod back to `idle` (pod-warm)" (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:89-93, 34). The `session, maxConcurrentSessions: 1, recycle.enabled: true` compatibility row additionally defines a second SDK-warm terminus, the `claimed → sdk_connecting` recycle re-warm edge before the claim enters `reserved` (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:76).
- **Existing tests:** Coverage grew substantially since the last review, all still at or below the fake-client/in-process tier. `pkg/adapter/sdkwarm_test.go` and `pkg/adapter/shutdown_demote_test.go` unit-test `DemoteSDK`/`ConfigureWorkspace`/`ShutdownDemoteSDK` against a `fakeSDKWarmRuntime`. `pkg/controller/sandbox/sdkwarm_internal_test.go` and `pkg/controller/sandbox/sdkwarm_recycle_test.go` now drive the actual `Reconcile` decision function (`TestReconcileWarmFillReadyPodReachesIdle`, `TestReconcileRecycleRewarmWatchdogRetiresOverBudget`) against a controller-runtime fake client — no build tag, so this is unit tier rather than envtest. `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/sdkwarm_bind_test.go` unit-tests the claim-time `RequiresDemotion`/`BindSDKWarm` decision (`TestBindSDKWarmDemotesOnBlockingPath_spec_6_1`). `tests/tier2_component/stores/crdpodregistry_claim_test.go` is a real envtest but exercises the per-pod claim CRD schema, not the SDK-warm phase transitions. No test found under `tests/tier2_component/controllers` or any higher tier that drives a live WarmPoolController through `warming → sdk_connecting → idle` against a real kube-apiserver. The e2e workload (`tests/testinfra/kind/agent-workload.yaml`) now registers a `preconnect-echo-runtime` with `preConnect: true` (this did not exist at the last review), but the only consumer of it is `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go` (a load scaffold); no `tests/tier5_e2e_kind` test claims or demotes against it.
- **Gap:** The decision logic for every SDK-warm edge is now well unit-tested, but nothing exercises the same transitions against a real kube-apiserver (tier2 envtest) or a live Kind cluster (tier5). The e2e preConnect runtime exists and is unused by any e2e test — the dependency this finding originally flagged (no preConnect runtime in the workload) is resolved, but the e2e test that would consume it is still missing. This remains both a core-capability gap (SDK-warm has never run in a live cluster test) and a deployment-combination gap.
- **Dependencies:** The `preconnect-echo-runtime` and its `SandboxWarmPool` already exist in `tests/testinfra/kind/agent-workload.yaml`. A `DemoteSDK`-capable claim path against it (uploading a file matching `sdkWarmBlockingPaths`) still needs a tier5 test; none — buildable today against the existing workload.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier2_component/controllers/sdkwarm_test.go` (envtest) asserting the WarmPoolController transitions a `preConnect` pool `warming → sdk_connecting → idle`, plus `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/sdkwarm_demotion_test.go` driving a session against `preconnect-echo-runtime` whose workspace plan includes `CLAUDE.md` and asserting demotion via `lenny_warmpool_sdk_demotions_total`, using `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver` and `tests/testinfra/kind`.

### - [x] T-6.2.2 — Task-mode cleanup edges (task_cleanup, scrub, maxTasksPerPod, host-node schedulability draining) have no integration, e2e, or chaos test [High] — RESOLVED fe3956e8 (reconciled against proposal 0002)
- **Resolution:** Proposal 0002 ("Session/service execution model: task mode removed, one parameterized session mode, per-pod occupancy claims") retired `executionMode: task` and the entire `task_cleanup` sub-state machine this finding targeted; `spec/06_warm-pod-model.md` no longer defines `task_cleanup`, `maxTasksPerPod`, `maxScrubFailures` as a task-mode field, or the between-task scrub-and-rewarm transitions. `pkg/sandbox/state/state_test.go` and `pkg/admission/pool_config_validator/validator_test.go` now assert `task_cleanup` is an *invalid* transition target/config, confirming the removal. The successor behavior (whole-pod scrub at the occupancy-zero recycle boundary, `recycle.maxSessionsPerPod`, host-node schedulability gating the `claimed → sdk_connecting` re-warm edge) is a materially different mechanism covered by its own current suite: `pkg/sandbox/podscrub/podscrub_test.go`, `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/recycle_scrub_fold_component_test.go`, `tests/tier4_integration/recycle_scrub_path_test.go`, and `tests/tier11_docs/concurrent_slot_lifecycle_doc_reconciliation_test.go`. No further action is needed against the retired task-mode surface; any residual gap in the recycle/scrub successor path is out of this finding's scope.

### - [ ] T-6.2.3 — Concurrent-session slot state machine (claimed occupancy, leaked, unhealthy-threshold draining) has no live tier5 test; TESTING.md previously named a file that did not exist [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "idle ──→ claimed (first session assigned — per-pod claim CREATE wins and the atomic Redis counter increment succeeds, slotId allocated)", "claimed ──→ draining (ceil(maxConcurrentSessions/2) slots fail (5-min window) or leak (persistent) — pod marked unhealthy)", and the per-slot sub-states `slot_assigned → receiving_uploads → running → slot_cleanup → released/leaked` (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:129-146, 148-154). `slot_active` as a distinct pod-level phase is gone; concurrent occupancy is now the coarse `claimed` phase whenever the Redis-counter occupancy is nonzero (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:129-130, 174).
- **Existing tests:** Considerably more coverage exists than at the last review, still short of a live cluster test. `pkg/gateway/runtime/slothealth/slothealth_test.go` (moved from the retired `pkg/gateway/slothealth`) unit-tests the `ceil(maxConcurrentSessions/2)` fail-or-leak threshold with a fake clock. `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podclaim/slotclaimer_test.go`, `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/slotretry_load_test.go` (`TestSlotRetryConcurrentLeaksReachThreshold_spec_6_2`), and `tests/tier4_integration/recycle_scrub_path_test.go` exercise slot release/leak/retry logic against miniredis and an envtest kube-apiserver with a real adapter over in-memory gRPC — a stronger integration than the previous miniredis-only load test, but still not a real pod. `tests/tier11_docs/concurrent_slot_lifecycle_doc_reconciliation_test.go` pins the leaked-slot-lifetime and per-release drain doc/code agreement (F-5.2.31). No `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/concurrent_modes_test.go` exists; a filesystem search still finds only `tests/tier4_integration/concurrent_workspace_test.go` and the tier12 load variants. `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/scaffolds_test.go::TestConcurrentExecutionModes` still states the concurrent execution modes are not exercisable there because the e2e workload registers only `executionMode: session` runtimes without `maxConcurrentSessions > 1`.
- **Gap:** The two-level slot state machine is now verified by threshold unit tests, a miniredis/envtest/in-memory-gRPC integration test for the recycle-scrub fold, and a doc-reconciliation test, but no test drives multiple concurrent slots onto a real pod through a live gateway and adapter, the `claimed → idle`-via-recycle last-slot-drains edge, or the `slot_active → draining` (now `claimed → draining`) unhealthy-threshold transition end to end. This is a core-capability gap for the concurrent execution mode.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a concurrent-session (`maxConcurrentSessions > 1`) reference runtime and pool in the e2e workload; the workload currently registers only single-session runtimes. Building the runtime and workload entry is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Create `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/concurrent_modes_test.go` that assigns N slots to one `maxConcurrentSessions > 1` pod, asserts the per-slot `/workspace/slots/{slotId}` trees, and asserts the pod returns to `idle` (via the recycle path or direct drain) after the last slot drains, using `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver` and `tests/testinfra/kind`.

### - [ ] T-6.2.4 — Pod failure during an active session and pod failure while suspended have no chaos or integration recovery test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Pod crash during an active session ... The crashed pod is always retired through the drain path regardless of `recycle` settings ... If `retryCount < maxSessionRetries` ... the gateway transitions the session to `resume_pending`, claims a fresh pod ... and re-dispatches the session" and "Pod failure while `suspended` (pod still held) ... the session transitions to `resume_pending` and follows the standard retry-and-resume path ... On successful recovery ... the session transitions to `running` — not back to `suspended`" (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:165-172, 226). Task-mode-specific retry language (`maxTaskRetries`, "retry-on-new-pod path") is gone; the crash-recovery path is now uniformly the session-mode path with checkpoint-based resume.
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier8_chaos/live_session_test.go::TestPodKillDuringActiveSession` kills the bound pod and asserts only that the warm pool replenishes to `minWarm`; it still skips (`t.Skipf`) when the e2e gateway runs without `--agent-namespace`, which remains the case, so it never asserts the session reaches `resume_pending` or re-attaches. `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/scaffolds_test.go::TestNodeDrainDuringActiveSession` is unchanged and still notes the checkpoint half is deferred. No test injects a pod failure against a `suspended` session.
- **Gap:** Unchanged: the recovery transitions on involuntary pod loss are unverified end to end. Missing are a chaos test that drives a session to `running`, kills the pod, and asserts `attached-equivalent → resume_pending → resuming → running` recovery, and a `suspended`-while-pod-held variant asserting `suspended → resume_pending → running` (not back to `suspended`).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the gateway running with `--agent-namespace` so sessions bind to real pods (still absent from the e2e install per the skip messages), and the checkpointer wired against MinIO. Wiring both is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier8_chaos/session_recovery_test.go` using `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver` to reach `running`, kill the bound pod, and assert full recovery to `running`; add a `suspended`-state variant in the same file, using `tests/testinfra/chaos` for the injection.

- **Existing tests:** `pkg/sandbox/state/state_test.go` validates the Go-level transition table (now including `reserved`). `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/crd_test.go` still asserts only that the Sandbox/SandboxWarmPool CRDs reach `Established`, never reading `.status.phase`. `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/pod_lifecycle_test.go` reads `.status.phase` opportunistically to assert warm pods are `idle`, but does not validate the phase against the full enum or a schema. `charts/lenny/crds/lenny.dev_sandboxes.yaml` defines the OpenAPI schema; no helm-unit or contract test asserts its enum against the Go constants.
- **Gap:** Unchanged: there is no conformance test that the deployed CRD's `.status.phase` accepts exactly the current (now eight-value, including `reserved`) enumeration and that the controller writes canonical strings. A drift between `pkg/sandbox/state` and the CRD OpenAPI schema would not be caught above the unit tier.

Backoff: Exponential — 500ms, 1s" (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:282-289). The invisible-retry half (fail the first one or two pod claims or setup attempts on an already-eager-claimed pod, then assert the client sees only the eventual `running` outcome with no visible `resume_pending`) is still untested at integration tier or above.

No further action needed against the retired 5-second-delay mechanism.

## §6.3 Startup Latency Analysis <a id="t-6.3"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/06_warm-pod-model.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§6.3 defines the pod-warm startup-latency SLO (P95 claim-to-ready < 2s runc, < 5s gVisor), an SDK-warm hot-path variant, a per-phase latency budget across runtime classes, a Tier 1 to Tier 2 promotion gate that blocks on validated P50/P95/P99 measurements, and a per-phase instrumentation requirement that the benchmark harness measure pod-warm versus SDK-warm latency per runtime class. The spec text for this unit is unchanged since the 2026-06-03 audit, but the surrounding implementation and test surface moved substantially: the `startup_latency` benchmark harness was rebuilt from a host-process echo heartbeat into a cluster-resident k6 scenario that drives real `POST /v1/sessions/start` on Kind (pod-warm and SDK-warm, runc) and on a provisioned cloud cluster (SDK-warm across runc, gVisor, and Kata), and the production start path now emits the full `lenny_session_startup_duration_seconds` / `lenny_session_startup_phase_duration_seconds` / `lenny_session_time_to_first_token_seconds` chain end to end (proposal `0006_build_startup-benchmark-per-runtime-class.md`; commits `766f1f5f`, `0ce97870`, `2a4c8e7a`, `9bb9648a`, `a109d62e`). This closes the two highest-severity findings this unit carried on the harness itself and on SDK-warm observability. What remains open is narrower than before: the landed cluster-resident tests measure and log the real P95 but treat a budget breach as a soft warning rather than a hard failure, no test asserts the per-phase budget rows against real measurements, the `session_throughput` scenario still does not exercise the create-and-start path, the Tier 1 to Tier 2 promotion gate still has no executable representation in `pkg/tierpromotion`, and the tier-6 cloud cross-reference still points at a tier-5 scaffold that only `t.Skip`s. `tests/spec-map.json`'s §6.3 notes still describe the retired heartbeat harness.
Counts: 3 High, 4 Medium, 1 Low, 3 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-6.3.1 — The pod-warm startup SLO (P95 < 2s runc / < 5s gVisor) is asserted end to end on real clusters, but a budget breach is only logged, never failed [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Startup latency SLO target: P95 pod-warm session start (pod claim through agent session ready) < 2s for runc, < 5s for gVisor, excluding client file upload and workspace materialization time." (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:336)
- **Existing tests:** Unit coverage unchanged: `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/startupmetrics_internal_test.go` and `pkg/gateway/gatewaymetrics/gatewaymetrics_test.go:1397,1424`. New since 2026-06-03: `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go::TestStartupLatencyPodWarm` (commit `766f1f5f`, part of proposal 0006) drives `POST /v1/sessions/start` against a real Kind gateway and pod-warm pool on the runc RuntimeClass, scrapes `/metrics`, and calls `recordClaimToReadyP95`, which `t.Fatalf`s if `lenny_session_startup_duration_seconds{runtime_class="runc"}` recorded no new observation — a real, hard assertion that the claim-to-ready path populates the SLO metric. But when a new observation exists, `recordClaimToReadyP95` (`tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go:333-345`) only `t.Logf`s a WARNING if the measured P95 exceeds the 2.0s budget and returns without failing, "so the noisy Kind port-forward smoke run does not gate on a latency regression." `tests/tier12_load_cloud/session_startup_latency_test.go` measures SDK-warm across runc, gVisor, and Kata but has no pod-warm arm at all, and its own `recordCloudSDKWarmP95` likewise only logs the P95 (lines 98-107) rather than asserting it against a target.
- **Gap:** The claim-to-ready path is now exercised on a real cluster and the histogram-population half of the SLO contract is hard-asserted, closing the "never asserted end to end" half of the original finding. The threshold half remains open: no test anywhere fails when the measured P95 exceeds 2s (runc) or 5s (gVisor); both landed tests are deliberately soft-fail pending the Tier 2 promotion gate (T-6.3.20). There is also no pod-warm gVisor arm on any tier — pod-warm is measured only on runc (tier7b); gVisor is only exercised through the SDK-warm cloud arms. A regression that pushed real P95 well past the SLO would produce a log line, not a test failure. Target tier is tier7b (harden the existing arm) plus a gVisor pod-warm arm at tier7b or tier12.
- **Dependencies:** none for hardening the runc arm to a hard assertion — buildable today, gated on the Tier 2 promotion decision (T-6.3.20) since §6.3 line 358 says the budget "MUST NOT be used as an SLO" until the gate clears. The gVisor pod-warm arm needs a gVisor-capable node pool (`scripts/cloud/<provider>/up-runtimeclass-pools.sh`), already used by the SDK-warm gVisor arm.
- **Suggested test:** Once T-6.3.20's promotion gate is satisfied, change `recordClaimToReadyP95`'s over-budget branch from `t.Logf` to `t.Fatalf` for `TestStartupLatencyPodWarm`, and add a `TestCloudStartupLatencyPodWarmGvisor` alongside the existing `TestCloudStartupLatencySDKWarmGvisor` in `tests/tier12_load_cloud/session_startup_latency_test.go` asserting the gVisor pod-warm P95 against the 5s target.

### - [x] T-6.3.5 — The startup benchmark harness measures a local echo heartbeat, not the §6.3 per-phase pod-warm vs SDK-warm latency per runtime class [High] — RESOLVED 766f1f5f (reconciled by proposal 0006)
- **Resolution:** Proposal `0006_build_startup-benchmark-per-runtime-class.md` (build-gap/test-infrastructure, no spec edits) replaced the host-process echo-heartbeat harness with a cluster-resident benchmark. Commit `766f1f5f` added `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/startup_latency/main.js` and `TestStartupLatencyPodWarm`/`TestStartupLatencySDKWarm` in `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go`, which drive real `POST /v1/sessions/start` against Kind pod-warm and SDK-warm pools (`echo` vs `preconnect-echo` runtimes) on the runc RuntimeClass every PR, and `tests/tier12_load_cloud/session_startup_latency_test.go`, which extends the SDK-warm comparison to gVisor and Kata on an operator-provisioned cloud cluster (each arm gated on `LENNY_BENCH_RUNTIME_CLASSES`, skipping with a `NEEDS-OPERATOR` message when the node pool is absent). BUILD-GAPS.md records F-6.3.5 and its duplicate F-6.3.10 CLOSED 2026-06-18 on this basis. The harness now measures real session-start latency, is runtime-class-labeled, and drives both warming models, closing the finding's title defect. The residual — a pod-warm gVisor cloud arm and the Phase 2 exit-gate ADR the promotion gate also requires — is carried forward under T-6.3.1 and T-6.3.20 rather than reopening this finding.

### - [ ] T-6.3.20 — The §6.3 Tier 1 to Tier 2 promotion gate is not encoded as an executable check [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Promotion from Tier 1 to Tier 2 is blocked until the Phase 2 startup benchmark harness has produced validated P50/P95/P99 measurements for all hot-path phases across all supported runtime classes (runc, gVisor, Kata). The gate is satisfied when: (a) actual P95 pod-warm session start latency has been measured and is ≤ the targets above for runc and gVisor, and (b) the per-phase histogram metrics ... are fully instrumented and producing data in the benchmark environment, and (c) the benchmark results are recorded as an annotated benchmark run." (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:358)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/tierpromotion/` still implements only the §17.8.3/§17.8.2 replica-floor, storage, secret-encryption, audit-retention, and Phase 13.5 benchmark-attestation gates; a grep of `pkg/tierpromotion` for `6.3`, `startup`, `pod-warm`, or `Phase 2 exit gate` returns nothing. This is unchanged since 2026-06-03. What changed is the data the gate would consume: condition (b) (per-phase histograms instrumented and producing data) is now genuinely satisfied in production (`lenny_session_startup_phase_duration_seconds{phase,runtime_class}`, commit `0ce97870`), and condition (a)'s runc measurement now has a real source (T-6.3.5's tier7b arm, commit `766f1f5f`). `docs/adr/` still has no Phase 2 exit-gate entry (condition (c)), and no code path reads any of this into a gate decision. BUILD-GAPS.md tracks the underlying promotion-gate status as F-6.3.20, DEFERRED at `[Info]` severity pending gVisor- and Kata-enabled host RuntimeClasses (`NEEDS-OPERATOR`) to produce the full runc/gVisor/Kata attestation.
- **Gap:** The §6.3 promotion gate is a normative blocker on tier promotion and still has no executable representation, so nothing prevents promoting Tier 1 to Tier 2 without the validated measurements and the Phase 2 exit-gate ADR, even though two of its three preconditions (instrumentation, and a real runc measurement) are now satisfiable from data that exists. This is a spec-versus-implementation inconsistency that would let an unvalidated SLO ship as a customer-facing commitment. Target tier is tier 0 / tier 11 (the `lenny-tier-promote` gate plus its documentation conformance check).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the §6.3 benchmark-run attestation inputs (benchmark run ID, cluster configuration, date, measured P95 per runtime class) to be added to `pkg/tierpromotion.Inputs` and a corresponding check function. The full attestation (runc, gVisor, Kata) needs gVisor- and Kata-enabled host RuntimeClasses per the BUILD-GAPS `NEEDS-OPERATOR` note; the check function itself and a runc-only interim attestation are buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add a `CheckStartupBenchmarkGate` to `pkg/tierpromotion/checks.go` with a `pkg/tierpromotion/tierpromotion_test.go` case that fails promotion to Tier 2 when the runc/gVisor/Kata startup-benchmark attestation is absent or the measured P95 exceeds the §6.3 target, mirroring the existing Phase 13.5 attestation checks.

### - [ ] T-6.3.4 — The per-phase latency budget is never asserted against real per-phase measurements [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Per-phase latency budget ... Pod claim and routing ≤ 100ms; Credential assignment ≤ 100ms; Workspace materialization ≤ 1s (small) / ≤ 3s (large); Agent session start ≤ 1.5s (runc) / ≤ 4.5s (gVisor); ... Total (platform-controlled, no setup cmds) ≤ 6s (runc) / ≤ 9s (gVisor)." (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:346)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/startupmetrics_internal_test.go` (`TestRecordStartupMetrics_spec_6_3`) asserts each phase is observed from a synthetic `BindTimings`. No test reads this phase-level series: a grep of `tests/tier7b_load_kind` and `tests/tier12_load_cloud` for `credential_assignment`, `workspace_materialization`, or `agent_session_start` returns nothing outside comments and baseline JSON. `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/pod_claim_latency/main.js` remains the sole phase-specific load scenario, and it asserts against its own stored baseline (P95 ≈ 113ms, already over budget) rather than the §6.3 100ms number (T-6.3.17).
- **Gap:** The per-phase budget table is now measurable from telemetry (each phase has a production histogram), but no test reads and asserts against any phase besides `pod_claim`, and even that one asserts against a regression baseline rather than the §6.3 budget. - **Spec/Doc:** "See [Section 16.1] for the `lenny_session_startup_duration_seconds` metric boundary." and "Each hot-path phase ... must be independently instrumented with histogram metrics (`lenny_session_startup_phase_duration_seconds{phase, runtime_class}`)." (spec/06_warm-pod-model.md:336, 360)
