(spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:1046)
- **Existing tests:** No test found. `grep` for the recovery-path policy behavior across tests returns nothing. tests/tier2_component/stores/delegationpolicystore_test.go and tests/tier4_integration/delegation_test.go cover delegation-time policy evaluation, not the recovery-time non-re-evaluation invariant. Searched tests/tier2_component, tests/tier4_integration, tests/tier9_security, and pkg/**/*_test.go.
- **Gap:** A normative MUST that is also a security boundary (a recovering child must resume under its persisted lease even after the referenced policy is narrowed) is unverified. The adversarial scenario is that alice narrows a `DelegationPolicy` or `maxDelegationPolicy` after a tree is running, a node fails, and recovery must resume the node under the original lease rather than fail it or re-admit it under the live policy. A regression that re-evaluates live policy during recovery would either break legitimate recovery or open a re-admission path, and no test would catch it. Target tiers: tier2 component and tier9 security.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a real Postgres-backed `SessionStore` carrying a persisted lease with effective `maxDelegationPolicy` and (for the snapshot branch) `snapshotted_pool_ids` (tests/testinfra/envtest), plus the admin policy-mutation surface to narrow the policy mid-tree. The recovery worker wiring from T-8.10.1 is now shipped (commit `4cc6f317`).
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier9_security/delegation_recovery_policy_test.go that persists a node lease, narrows the referenced `DelegationPolicy` so the node's runtime would no longer be admitted, drives recovery, and asserts the node resumes under the original lease; add a companion tier2 test in tests/tier2_component covering the `snapshotPolicyAtLease: true` snapshotted-pool branch via tests/testinfra/envtest.

### - [x] T-8.10.13 — `delegate_task` duplicate-spawn-across-recovery residual (proposal 0027) is fully covered by a dedicated integration test [Medium] — RESOLVED 5bf4af35 (reconciled against proposal 0027)
- **Resolution:** Proposal 0027 (applied 2026-07-03) added a new normative paragraph to §8.10, "Duplicate spawn across parent recovery" (spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:1068), documenting that a restored parent re-deriving its next actions from a possibly-stale checkpoint can re-issue a `lenny/delegate_task` call whose result already exists (in flight at the crash, or completed but recorded after the last durable checkpoint), producing a duplicate child subtree alongside the reattached original; the §11.5 idempotency key does not suppress this because it runs only on the client-facing `/mcp` edge, not the intra-pod platform-tool dispatch path a restored parent uses. This was a genuinely new testable requirement not present at the 2026-06-03 audit. Commit `5bf4af35` ("0027 S3: tier-4 integration test for the delegate_task recovery duplicate-spawn residual") landed tests/tier4_integration/delegate_task_recovery_residual_test.go, which drives two `delegate_task` calls through the intra-pod `mcp.Server.DispatchTool` entry point (with and without a §11.5 `idempotencyKey`) and asserts each produces a distinct child subtree — the unmitigated residual — and, as a contrast case, drives the same call through the client-facing `/mcp` HTTP surface with an `Idempotency-Key` header and asserts a same-body retry collapses while a changed body returns `422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`, confirming the mitigation is client-facing only. The test carries `// spec: 8.10 (duplicate spawn across parent recovery), 11.5 (idempotency)` annotations. The companion handler-comment change in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/mcptools_register.go` (the `IdempotencyKey` field comment pointing at the §8.10 residual) has also landed.

## §9.1 Where MCP Is Used <a id="t-9.1"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/09_mcp-integration.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§9.1 defines the MCP boundary table, the platform MCP server tool inventory, and the Runtime Discovery contract exposed over four external interfaces (MCP `list_runtimes`, REST `GET /v1/runtimes`, OpenAI Completions `GET /v1/models`, and Open Responses `GET /v1/models`). Unit-and-component coverage of the discovery handlers exists in `pkg/gateway/mcptools/discover_agents_filtering_test.go` and `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/runtimes_test.go`, and one tier4 test (`tests/tier4_integration/environment_test.go`) drives `/v1/runtimes` against the live gateway for §10.6 filtering only. No contract test pins the cross-surface consistency the spec requires (the same runtime appearing across all four discovery surfaces with an `adapterCapabilities` block in each), the normative MUST that consumers inspect `adapterCapabilities.supportsElicitation` has no conformance check against the four adapters, the anti-enumeration "identical not-found and not-authorized responses" rule is unverified at the discovery layer, and the `Gateway ↔ type:mcp runtimes` boundary (`/mcp/runtimes/{name}`, "Implicit session for audit/billing") is mounted with a nil dispatcher, has no implicit-session/audit/billing implementation, and is exercised only by handler unit tests. The spec-map entry for §9.1 also lists two glob paths (`pkg/gateway/mcp/...`, `pkg/adapter/mcp/...`) that contain no §9.1 discovery assertions.
Counts: 4 High, 4 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-9.1.1 — Runtime discovery cross-surface consistency is unverified by any contract test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Every external interface exposes runtime discovery via `HandleDiscovery`. All results are identity-filtered and policy-scoped. ... MCP: `list_runtimes` tool ... REST: `GET /v1/runtimes` ... OpenAI Completions: `GET /v1/models` ... Open Responses: `GET /v1/models`" (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:35-40)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcptools/discover_agents_filtering_test.go` exercises `lenny/list_runtimes` against memory stores in-process. `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/runtimes_test.go` exercises `GET /v1/runtimes` and `GET /v1/models` against the in-process handler. `tests/tier3_contract/rest_sessions/unexercised_endpoints_test.go::TestListRuntimesReturnsList` and `TestListModelsReturnsList` pin only that each REST surface returns the right envelope key in isolation. No test registers one runtime catalog and asserts that the same runtime set surfaces consistently across all four discovery surfaces driven through the live gateway. spec-map §9.1 lists `pkg/gateway/mcp/...` and `pkg/adapter/mcp/...`, neither of which contains a `list_runtimes`, `adapterCapabilities`, or `HandleDiscovery` assertion (verified by grep).
- **Gap:** The four discovery surfaces share the §10.6 filtering path but are coded in three packages (`mcptools`, `sessionserver`, `translator`). No contract test confirms that a runtime visible to a caller over REST is also visible over MCP `list_runtimes` and surfaces as a model over `/v1/models`, nor that a runtime hidden by filtering is hidden on every surface. This is a tier3 cross-surface contract gap and a real user journey: alice discovers a runtime over MCP and expects the identical target over the OpenAI surface.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. Use the live gateway subprocess harness in `tests/testinfra/gateway` and the token helper in `tests/testinfra/tokenservice`.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/rest_mcp_consistency/discovery_parity_test.go` that registers a runtime set, then calls `GET /v1/runtimes`, `lenny/list_runtimes`, `GET /v1/models?adapter=openai-completions`, and `GET /v1/models?adapter=open-responses` as the same principal and asserts the runtime names match across all four surfaces.

### - [ ] T-9.1.2 — `adapterCapabilities.supportsElicitation` consumer-gating MUST has no conformance check across the four adapters [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Every discovery response includes an `adapterCapabilities` block ... reflecting the capabilities of the adapter serving the request — consumers must inspect `adapterCapabilities.supportsElicitation` before initiating elicitation-dependent workflows." (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:35)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcptools/discover_agents_filtering_test.go::TestListRuntimesToolEmbedsAdapterCapabilities` asserts the MCP block reports `supportsElicitation=true`. `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/runtimes_test.go` and `pkg/gateway/adapter/capabilities_test.go` cover the REST and translator capability structs in isolation. The OpenAI Chat and Open Responses adapters set `SupportsElicitation: false` (pkg/gateway/translator/openai_chat.go:41, open_responses.go:32), but no test confirms that an elicitation-dependent workflow over those surfaces is actually unavailable, so the capability flag and the behavior it advertises are never cross-checked.
- **Gap:** The normative MUST binds a discovery-advertised flag to runtime behavior. No conformance or contract test verifies that each of the four adapters reports a `supportsElicitation` value that matches whether that surface can in fact carry a `lenny/request_elicitation` to the client. The OpenAI surfaces advertising `false` while the MCP and REST surfaces advertise `true` is exactly the contract a consumer relies on; it is unverified end to end. This is a tier3 contract and tier10 conformance gap.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The OpenAI fidelity matrix harness lives in `cmd/lenny-compliance` and `tests/testinfra/sdkhelper`.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/rest_mcp_consistency/adapter_capabilities_elicitation_test.go` asserting each surface's discovery `adapterCapabilities.supportsElicitation` equals the surface's actual elicitation capability, plus a negative case that an elicitation attempt over an OpenAI surface (which reports `false`) returns the documented unsupported-operation error.

### - [ ] T-9.1.3 — Anti-enumeration "identical not-found and not-authorized responses" is unverified at the discovery layer [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Not-found and not-authorized produce identical responses — no enumeration." (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:35)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcptools/discover_agents_filtering_test.go` and `tests/tier4_integration/environment_test.go` assert that an out-of-scope runtime is absent from a caller's discovery list. `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/runtimes.go` `handleRuntimeMeta` returns an identical 404 for a missing, soft-deleted, missing-key, or non-public entry, and `runtimes_test.go` covers some of these, but no test compares the not-found response and the not-authorized response byte-for-byte (status, code, body) to prove they are indistinguishable to an unauthorized caller.
- **Gap:** The anti-enumeration property is a security control on the discovery and metadata surfaces. The absence of an assertion that an unauthorized caller and a caller asking for a non-existent runtime receive byte-identical responses means a future change that adds a distinguishing field (for example a different error code or a timing-visible branch) would ship undetected. This is a tier9 security gap and an adversarial scenario: a hostile caller bob enumerating which runtimes exist by diffing responses.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. Use `tests/testinfra/security` assertion helpers and the live gateway harness in `tests/testinfra/gateway`.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier9_security/discovery_enumeration_test.go` that, for `GET /v1/runtimes/{name}/meta/{key}`, the per-runtime MCP endpoint, and discovery filtering, asserts the response for a non-existent runtime is byte-identical to the response for a runtime the caller is not authorized to see.

### - [ ] T-9.1.4 — `Gateway ↔ type:mcp runtimes` boundary advertises "Implicit session for audit/billing" that is neither implemented nor tested [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Gateway ↔ `type:mcp` runtimes | MCP (dedicated endpoints at `/mcp/runtimes/{name}`) | Direct MCP server access. Implicit session for audit/billing." (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:11)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpruntimes/mcpruntimes_test.go` covers the four error patterns (404 unknown runtime, 400 INVALID_RUNTIME_TYPE for type:agent, 503 RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE with no dispatcher, OK for a dispatched type:mcp runtime) and `capability_filter_test.go` covers the §10.6 tool-capability filter. `tests/tier4_integration/scaffolds_test.go::TestMCPRuntimeEndpoints` is a `t.Logf`-only scaffold that declares the surface "covered by its unit tests." The handler in `pkg/gateway/mcpruntimes/mcpruntimes.go` contains no session-creation, audit-emission, or billing code (grep finds no `audit`, `billing`, or implicit-session symbols), and `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:4425` mounts it with a `nil` dispatcher.
- **Gap:** The spec promises that a direct call to `/mcp/runtimes/{name}` creates an implicit session so the call is audited and billed. No implementation emits a session, an audit event, or a billing record for these calls, and no component, integration, or e2e test asserts any of the three. It targets tier4 integration and tier2 component.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a live MCP-runtime dispatcher wired into the gateway and a Postgres-backed audit/billing store. The dispatcher is `nil` in production wiring today; building the implicit-session path and a dispatcher stub in `tests/testinfra/stubs` is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/mcp_runtime_endpoint_test.go` that drives a `tools/call` against `/mcp/runtimes/{name}` for a wired type:mcp runtime and asserts an implicit session row, an audit event, and a billing record are produced; reference `tests/testinfra/audit` for the hash-chain assertions.

## §9.2 Elicitation Chain <a id="t-9.2"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/09_mcp-integration.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The §9.2 primitives in `pkg/elicitation` and the gateway dispatcher in `pkg/gateway/mcptools` carry dense unit coverage, and the Postgres-backed pending-interaction registry has a real tier2 component contract test (`tests/tier2_component/stores/interactionstore_test.go`) that exercises the authorization triple and the budget query against a real container. The component-and-above coverage thins sharply for the security-critical content-integrity path. The production tamper detector is structurally inert (BUILD-GAPS F-9.2.1, DEFERRED): the per-hop `elicitation/create` re-emission wire mechanism is unbuilt, so `forwardedContentFor` is nil in `cmd/lenny-gateway`, the `enforce` and `detect-only` modes have no observable effect on a live chain, and no test detects this divergence between the spec and the binary. The tier4 chain test (`tests/tier4_integration/elicitation_test.go`) exercises the happy-path forward and the URL-mode provenance drop but never injects a tampered payload; the tier9 suite (`tests/tier9_security/elicitation_tamper_test.go`) only pins the admin-API enforcement-mode wire contract and skips when a cluster is absent; the tier3 consistency test (`TestRESTMCPElicitation`) is a no-op `t.Logf` stub; the named chaos test (`TestElicitationDeadlockDetection`) is a scaffold mapped to four P0/P1 runbook scenarios; and the Helm tests assert neither the floor ConfigMap key nor the floor flag. There is no tier5 Kind end-to-end chain test, no tier10 conformance pin of the native MCP `elicitation/create` frame, and the floor-change audit events are catalogued but unemitted and untested.
Counts: 5 High, 7 Medium, 3 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-9.2.1 — Production tamper detector is structurally inert and no test catches the spec-versus-binary divergence [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "an intermediate pod re-emits the upstream `elicitation/create` frame carrying the original `{message, schema}` payload. The gateway canonicalizes the forwarded frame's `{message, schema}` pair ... and compares its SHA-256 digest against the digest recorded at origination. The behavior on divergence is governed by the tenant's elicitation content integrity enforcement mode" (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:56).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcptools/elicitation_tamper_internal_test.go` drives all three modes, but only by injecting a synthetic `forwardedContentFor` provider; `TestDispatchNoProviderNeverDetects_spec_9_2` (line 201) explicitly documents that production leaves the provider nil and the chain "advances the chain unverified even under enforce." `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` never wires the provider (confirmed: `forwardedContentFor` has no production caller). BUILD-GAPS.md:10920 records F-9.2.1 as DEFERRED. `tests/tier4_integration/elicitation_test.go` and `tests/tier9_security/elicitation_tamper_test.go` never trigger a real tamper. No test asserts that an unbuilt wire path leaves the entire content-integrity feature non-functional.
- **Gap:** The §9.2 gateway-origin binding, the core security capability of this subsection, has no end-to-end test that drives a second `{message, schema}` submission through a real intermediate hop and asserts the gateway either rejects (`enforce`) or records and forwards (`detect-only`). Every passing tamper test is a unit test against an injected stub. This is a spec-versus-implementation inconsistency that lets the regression "content integrity does nothing in production" ship undetected. The work covers both the missing wire mechanism (the deferred infrastructure) and a real user journey (an agent answering an elicitation forwarded through a tampering intermediary) plus the adversarial path.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the deferred per-hop `elicitation/create` re-emission subsystem (intermediate pods re-emitting the frame over virtual MCP so the gateway receives a second payload). The subsystem does not exist; building it is part of this finding. Requires the tier4 compose stack (`tests/testinfra/gateway`) and the `delegation-echo` test runtime extended to re-emit a frame, plus a malicious-intermediary variant in `tests/testinfra/stubs`.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier4 test `tests/tier4_integration/elicitation_tamper_chain_test.go` that builds a root → child → leaf tree, has the child re-emit a mutated `elicitation/create` frame, and asserts under `enforce` the leaf's `lenny/request_elicitation` fails with `ELICITATION_CONTENT_TAMPERED` while the unmodified path resolves, using `tests/testinfra/gateway` and the `delegation-echo` runtime.

### - [ ] T-9.2.2 — No tier5 Kind end-to-end elicitation-chain test exists despite the declared Tier 5 coverage [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "External Tool → (elicitation) → Gateway connector / Gateway connector → ... → Child pod ... → Parent pod ... → Gateway edge → Client / Human. Response flows back down the same chain. The gateway mediates every hop but does not erase the hop structure." (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:47-54). TESTING.md:1889 declares §14.5 coverage "spans Tier 2 (integrity), Tier 4 (chain flow), Tier 5 (provenance display, depth suppression), Tier 9 (tamper detection)."
- **Existing tests:** No test found. Searched `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/` (grep for elicitation returned nothing); the directory holds `lifecycle_test.go`, `pod_lifecycle_test.go`, `mtls_test.go`, `audit_test.go`, and others, none touching elicitation. The only chain exercise is `tests/tier4_integration/elicitation_test.go` on the compose stack. TESTING.md:1712-1713 records `mcp_elicitation_chain_test.go` and `mcp_provenance_test.go` as deferred to "the K8s-integration phase that ships the gateway's virtual MCP server."
- **Gap:** The hop-by-hop chain is never exercised on Kind under real NetworkPolicy, pod-to-gateway mTLS, and the full chart. The Tier 5 coverage TESTING.md §14.5 claims for provenance display and depth suppression is absent. This is a real user journey (alice answers a prompt raised by a depth-2 delegated agent) that runs only against in-process compose, so the cluster-mediated forward path is unverified end to end.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`) and the gateway virtual MCP server forwarding path. Buildable against the existing Kind install once the chart is up; the session-driving helper in `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver` and the MCP client pattern from `tests/tier4_integration/elicitation_test.go` are reusable.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/elicitation_chain_test.go` driving a delegation tree on Kind via `tests/testinfra/kind` and `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`, raising an elicitation from the deepest child and resolving it at the human-facing root through the in-cluster gateway.

### - [ ] T-9.2.3 — Tier3 REST/MCP consistency test for elicitation is a no-op stub with no MCP `elicitation/create` conformance pin [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The forward-hop wire mechanism is the native MCP `elicitation/create` frame defined in the per-kind wire projection ([Section 15.2.1] ...)" (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:56).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier3_contract/rest_mcp_consistency/scaffolds_test.go:388` defines `TestRESTMCPElicitation`, whose entire body is `t.Logf("§15.2.1: elicitation respond/dismiss is REST-only by design; no MCP parity surface required")` with no assertion. No conformance test pins an `elicitation/create` frame against the MCP JSON-RPC schema. The MCP respond/dismiss tools are covered only by `pkg/gateway/mcptools/elicitation_test.go` unit tests.
- **Gap:** The native MCP `elicitation/create` frame, an external-standard protocol surface, has no contract or conformance test pinning its wire format against the MCP schema. The stub asserts the surface is "by design absent," which conflates the deferred-wire-mechanism gap (F-9.2.1) with a deliberate design choice and locks in zero coverage. A conformance check against the external MCP schema is required for any protocol surface, so its absence is a finding.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the deferred `elicitation/create` forward path (shared with T-9.2.1) and an MCP-schema fixture in `tests/testinfra/sdkhelper` or `tests/testinfra/stubs`. The forward path does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Replace the `TestRESTMCPElicitation` stub with a tier3 conformance case in `tests/tier3_contract/rest_mcp_consistency/` that captures the gateway-emitted `elicitation/create` JSON-RPC frame and validates it against the MCP elicitation schema, plus a parity assertion that REST respond and MCP `lenny/respond_to_elicitation` return identical `(category, retryable)` envelopes.

### - [ ] T-9.2.4 — Tier9 tamper suite verifies only the admin wire contract and never injects a tampered payload [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Any divergence is rejected with `ELICITATION_CONTENT_TAMPERED` (`PERMANENT`/409 ...); ... the gateway emits the `elicitation.content_tamper_detected` audit event ... with `enforcement_mode: \"enforce\"`, and `lenny_elicitation_content_tamper_detected_total{origin_pod, tampering_pod, enforcement_mode=\"enforce\"}` ... is incremented, firing the `ElicitationContentTamperDetected` critical alert" (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:60).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier9_security/elicitation_tamper_test.go` drives `PUT`/`GET /v1/admin/tenants/{id}/elicitation-content-integrity` and asserts the `storedMode`/`effectiveMode` round-trip (lines 176-299). Every test `t.Skipf`s when the cluster or admin path is unreachable. None inject a tampered elicitation, none assert the `ELICITATION_CONTENT_TAMPERED` rejection, the audit event, or the metric increment on a live cluster. The audit event and metric are unit-asserted only in `pkg/gateway/mcptools/elicitation_tamper_internal_test.go`.
- **Gap:** The security-relevant rejection path, the audit emission, and the critical-alert metric are never verified end to end against a real cluster. The tier9 suite is a configuration-API conformance check mislabeled as a tamper-detection suite. The adversarial scenario (a hostile intermediary pod mutating the rendered text) is unexercised at the security tier. This is the controls-verified-end-to-end requirement for a security control, and it is unmet.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the deferred re-emission wire path (shared with T-9.2.1), the tier5/tier9 Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`), and a metric/audit assertion helper (`tests/testinfra/audit`, `tests/testinfra/security`). The wire path does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `tests/tier9_security/elicitation_tamper_test.go` with a live-cluster case that delegates a tree, has an intermediary re-emit a mutated frame under `enforce`, and asserts the `409 ELICITATION_CONTENT_TAMPERED` response plus the `elicitation.content_tamper_detected` audit row and the `lenny_elicitation_content_tamper_detected_total{enforcement_mode="enforce"}` increment via `tests/testinfra/audit`.

### - [ ] T-9.2.5 — detect-only client-delivery semantics and the permissive-tamper warning alert are never exercised above unit level [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`detect-only`. The divergent payload is forwarded to the client as received (the gateway-recorded original is NOT substituted back in), but the gateway still emits the `elicitation.content_tamper_detected` audit event with `enforcement_mode: \"detect-only\"` ... firing the separate `ElicitationContentIntegrityPermissiveTamper` warning alert" (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:61).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcptools/elicitation_tamper_internal_test.go::TestDispatchDetectOnlyForwardsTamper_spec_9_2_61` asserts the dispatcher forwards-as-received and records the metric/audit with an injected provider. `tests/tier9_security/elicitation_tamper_test.go::TestElicitationTamperDetectOnlyMode` asserts only the admin `storedMode` read-back, not delivery of the divergent payload to a client. No integration, e2e, or chaos test verifies that the client actually receives the divergent text and that the `ElicitationContentIntegrityPermissiveTamper` alert fires.
- **Gap:** The detect-only path (a deliberately reduced-integrity posture an operator runs as a pre-enforcement canary) is verified only by a unit test against a stub. The client-visible behavior (divergent text delivered, original not substituted) and the distinct warning alert have no component-or-higher coverage. This combines a real user journey under a weakened tenant with a standards-adjacent alerting contract.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the deferred re-emission wire path (shared with T-9.2.1) and an alert-firing assertion against the rules in `pkg/alerting/rules`. The wire path does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier4 case in `tests/tier4_integration/elicitation_tamper_chain_test.go` that sets a tenant to `detect-only`, drives a mutated re-emission, asserts the client receives the divergent payload and the gateway records the `enforcement_mode="detect-only"` audit event, then a tier7/alerting unit asserting `ElicitationContentIntegrityPermissiveTamper` fires on the `detect-only` metric stream.

### - [ ] T-9.2.6 — Chaos test for elicitation deadlock and tamper is a scaffold mapped to four P0/P1 runbook scenarios [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Elicitation chains and `input_required` chains are independent blocking mechanisms, but both participate in the gateway's subtree deadlock detection ... A task blocked on an elicitation waiting for a human response is not considered deadlocked" (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:110).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier8_chaos/scaffolds_test.go:356` defines `TestElicitationDeadlockDetection` whose body is a single `t.Logf` placeholder. `tests/tier8_chaos/runbook-map.yaml` maps four distinct runbook scenarios to this one scaffold: `elicitation-deadlock` (P1), `elicitation-backlog` (P1), `elicitation-content-integrity-weakened` (P1), and `elicitation-content-tamper-detected` (P0). None has a real fault-injection implementation.
- **Gap:** Four declared chaos runbook scenarios, including a P0 content-tamper scenario, are backed by an empty scaffold. The resilience behavior (a human-blocked elicitation is not treated as deadlocked, the backlog gauge fires, the integrity-weakened standing alert holds) is unverified under failure injection. A declared suite standing in as a scaffold is a finding.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier8 chaos harness (`tests/testinfra/chaos`), the deadlock detector (BUILD-GAPS F-9.2.20 / F-8.8.6, DEFERRED, the detector itself is unbuilt), and the clock-stepping helper (`tests/testinfra/clockstep`) for backlog and timeout. The detector does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Split `TestElicitationDeadlockDetection` into real chaos cases in `tests/tier8_chaos/elicitation_test.go`: one holding a human-blocked elicitation while a sibling `request_input` chain deadlocks (asserting the elicitation is excluded from the circular-wait set), and one driving the backlog gauge past the alert threshold via `tests/testinfra/chaos` and `tests/testinfra/clockstep`.

### - [ ] T-9.2.7 — Helm tests do not assert the platform-floor ConfigMap key or the gateway floor flag [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The platform operator configures a minimum-enforcement floor via the Helm value `.Values.security.elicitationContentIntegrity.floor` (default `off` ...), rendered into the `lenny-deployment-phase-stamp` ConfigMap at install/upgrade time." (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:64).
- **Existing tests:** `charts/lenny/templates/phase-stamp-configmap.yaml:82` renders `security.elicitationContentIntegrity.floor` and `charts/lenny/templates/gateway-deployment.yaml:442` renders `--elicitation-content-integrity-floor`, but `charts/lenny/tests/phase-stamp-configmap_test.yaml` (grep for floor/integrity returned nothing) and `charts/lenny/tests/gateway-deployment_test.yaml` (floor matches are unrelated to elicitation) assert neither value.
- **Gap:** The platform-floor rendering path, the install-time mechanism that clamps every tenant's effective enforcement, has no Helm unit test. A chart change that drops the floor key from the ConfigMap or the flag from the deployment would not be caught, so the `max(platform_floor, tenant_stored_mode)` clamp could silently degrade to no floor. This is a deployment-combination gap on the platform-operator path.
- **Dependencies:** None — buildable today with the existing helm-unittest harness in `charts/lenny/tests`.

## §9.3 Connector Definition and OAuth/OIDC <a id="t-9.3"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/09_mcp-integration.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
Component-level coverage of the connector registry and the OAuth authorization-code flow is strong: `tests/tier2_component/stores/connectorstore_test.go` exercises CRUD, SSRF rejection, and tenant isolation against a real Postgres, `tests/tier4_integration/connector_oauth_test.go` drives the authorize and callback flow through the live gateway binary against a fake provider, and `tests/tier9_security/ssrf_test.go` enforces the HTTPS-scheme boundary on Kind. The per-delegation-level connector authorizer (`pkg/gateway/connectorauthz`) and the outbound invoke path (`pkg/gateway/connectorinvoke`) are unit-tested only, with no multi-component or e2e exercise. The two highest-value invariants in the subsection have no end-to-end test: "tokens never transit through pods" and "a child cannot use connectors not permitted by its policy even if tokens exist at the root level." The OAuth 2.1 authorization-URL and PKCE S256 wire output has no contract test pinning it against the external standard, the connector OAuth flow has no Kind or cloud e2e, no chaos test exercises the Redis-backed `state` store under outage, and the TESTING.md `oauth_connector_flow` suite claims assertions (encrypted storage, token-never-in-pod) that the actual integration test does not make.
Counts: 3 High, 5 Medium, 1 Low, 2 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-9.3.1 — The "tokens never transit through pods" invariant has no end-to-end or integration verification [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Tokens never transit through pods. The gateway owns all downstream credential state." and "Gateway connector receives and stores resulting tokens (encrypted, never in pods)" (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:163, spec/09_mcp-integration.md:152)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier4_integration/connector_oauth_test.go` drives authorize and callback but stops after the gateway exchanges the code and reports `connector_authorized`; it never asserts that the resulting token is absent from any pod-bound surface (env, `/proc/<pid>/environ`, adapter manifest, mounted secret). `tests/tier2_component/stores/connectorcredstore_test.go` proves the token is envelope-encrypted at rest under §13.3, but that is a store-layer check, not a pod-isolation check. `pkg/gateway/connectorinvoke/invoker_test.go::TestInvokerCallToolUsesStoredCredential_spec_9_3_142` proves the gateway injects the bearer on the outbound call, which is the opposite assertion (the gateway holds it). The §14.3 negative assertion "Credential never on the agent pod's disk in proxy mode; never in environment variables; not present in `/proc/<pid>/environ`" (TESTING.md:1870) is stated for end-user credentials and is not exercised for connector OAuth tokens. No test found in tiers 4, 5, 6, or 9 that asserts a connector OAuth token never reaches a pod.
- **Gap:** This is the load-bearing security invariant of the OAuth flow and the reason every connector must be gateway-registered. It needs an adversarial, pod-side negative test: complete an OAuth flow for a connector, then from inside a pod that invokes that connector inspect the environment, the adapter manifest, the mounted secrets, and `/proc/self/environ`, and assert the access and refresh tokens never appear. Target tier5 (Kind) for the real pod boundary, with a tier4 compose-level precursor that asserts the adapter manifest the gateway hands a pod carries no token material for an OAuth connector.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`) and a pod that calls a connector tool, plus a fake external MCP tool endpoint that issues an auth challenge (no external MCP tool stub exists in `tests/testinfra/stubs/`; building it is part of this finding). The tier4 manifest check is buildable today against the live gateway via `tests/testinfra/gateway`.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/connector_token_isolation_test.go` that authorizes a connector, runs a pod through `connectorinvoke`, and asserts the OAuth token is absent from the pod's env, manifest, and `/proc/self/environ`; back it with a tier4 manifest-inspection assertion using `tests/testinfra/gateway` and a new `tests/testinfra/stubs/mcptool` external-tool stub.

### - [ ] T-9.3.2 — Per-delegation-level connector scoping (child cannot use a root-level connector) has no multi-component or e2e proof [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Connector access is scoped per delegation level. ... The gateway validates the `connector_id` in every external tool call against the calling pod's effective delegation policy before proxying. A child cannot use connectors not permitted by its policy, even if tokens exist for them at the root level." (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:164)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/connectorauthz/connectorauthz_test.go` covers the authorizer with a `fakeResolver` (runtime-policy deny, environment-default intersection, no-policy fall-through). `pkg/gateway/connectorinvoke/invoker_test.go::TestInvokerCallToolDeniedByPolicy_spec_9_3_164` and `TestInvokerCallToolPermittedByPolicy_spec_9_3_164` wire a `fakeAuthz` that replays a fixed verdict. Both are unit tests with fakes on both sides of the boundary. No test found in tiers 4, 5, or 6 that creates a root session holding a connector credential, delegates to a child whose effective `DelegationPolicy` excludes that connector, and asserts the child's tool call is rejected while the root's succeeds against a live gateway and real stores.
- **Gap:** The unit tests prove the authorizer's verdict logic and that the invoker calls the authorizer, but nothing proves the assembled gateway enforces the boundary with a real `delegation.Service`, a real `connectorcredstore` holding a root-level token, and an actual parent-child task tree. This is both a real user journey (alice's root agent authorizes GitHub, the delegated child must not reach GitHub) and an adversarial scenario (a compromised child attempts to ride the parent's credential). Target tier4 against the compose stack for the assembled-gateway boundary, and tier5 for the real multi-pod delegation path.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the compose gateway (`tests/testinfra/gateway`), a delegation policy fixture, and the external MCP tool stub from T-9.3.1. The tier5 variant needs the Kind harness and `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver` to drive parent-then-child delegation. None of these wires the authorizer to a real policy resolver in a test today; building that wiring is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/connector_delegation_scope_test.go` that seeds a root credential, delegates to a child with a connector-excluding `DelegationPolicy`, and asserts `ErrConnectorNotPermitted` (the documented denial) for the child and success for the root; escalate to `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/connector_delegation_scope_test.go` using `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`.

### - [ ] T-9.3.3 — No contract test pins the OAuth 2.1 authorization-URL and PKCE S256 output against the external standard [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "the gateway MUST generate a `code_verifier` (≥43 random characters, unreserved alphabet) and send the corresponding `code_challenge` (SHA-256 hash, base64url-encoded, `code_challenge_method=S256`) in the authorization request" and "For every authorization request the gateway generates a cryptographically random `state` value (≥128 bits, base64url-encoded)" (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:158, spec/09_mcp-integration.md:157)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier4_integration/connector_oauth_test.go` asserts `response_type=code`, that `state` matches, and that `code_challenge` is present with `code_challenge_method=S256`, but it does not verify the verifier-to-challenge relation (BASE64URL(SHA256(verifier)) == challenge), the ≥43-character verifier alphabet, or the ≥128-bit state entropy. `pkg/connectoroauth/pkce_test.go` is a unit test of the PKCE helper. The tier3 contract directory holds `oauth_token/` which pins the RFC 8693 token-exchange envelope, a different concern (internal STS, not the connector authorization-code grant). No tier3 contract test pins the connector authorization request against RFC 6749 / OAuth 2.1 / RFC 7636.
- **Gap:** The authorization request is a wire-format surface consumed by every external OAuth provider, and the spec cites the external standard (S256, base64url, the unreserved alphabet, the OAuth 2.1 removal of the implicit grant). A standards-conformance test is required and is absent. The test must reconstruct the challenge from the captured verifier, validate the state entropy and encoding, and confirm `response_type` is never `token`. Target tier3 contract.
- **Dependencies:** None — buildable today. The flow runs against an in-process gateway and a fake provider, and the verifier is recoverable from the gateway's state store (`pkg/connectoroauth` exposes `MemoryStateStore`).
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/connector_oauth/authorization_request_test.go` that mints an authorization request, recomputes `base64url(sha256(code_verifier))` and asserts equality with `code_challenge`, asserts `code_challenge_method=S256`, asserts the state decodes to ≥16 bytes, and asserts `response_type=code` with no `token` value.

### - [ ] T-9.3.4 — The connector OAuth flow has no Kind or cloud end-to-end coverage [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "When a nested agent calls an external MCP tool requiring user auth: 1. Pod calls the connector's local MCP server ... 3. Gateway emits URL-mode elicitation through the chain ... 5. Gateway connector receives and stores resulting tokens ... 6. Future calls from pods authorized for that connector use gateway-held connector state" (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:146-153)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier4_integration/connector_oauth_test.go` drives authorize and callback directly against the gateway HTTP API; it invokes the callback endpoint itself rather than completing the full pod-to-connector-to-elicitation-to-callback path. `grep` of `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/` and `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/` for connector, oauth, or invoke returns no matches. The TESTING.md tier5 suite table (TESTING.md:1065-1087) lists no connector or OAuth suite, and `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml` lists no connector or OAuth capability.
- **Gap:** The end-to-end flow joins the pod's local connector MCP server, the URL-mode elicitation chain, the user completing OAuth, and the gateway storing and later replaying the credential. The tier4 test exercises only the gateway-internal authorize and callback handlers in isolation. The composed flow on a real cluster (pod calls connector, elicitation surfaces to the client, credential is stored, a subsequent pod call succeeds) is a real user journey and is unverified. Target tier5 (Kind) and tier6 (cloud) so workload-identity-issued credentials and the provider-equivalent sandbox are exercised at least once.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`), the external MCP tool stub from T-9.3.1 issuing an auth challenge, a fake OAuth provider (`tests/testinfra/stubs/oidc` or `tests/testinfra/mocks/oauth-connector/` named in TESTING.md:759), and `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`. The OAuth-connector mock directory is named in TESTING.md but not present on disk; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/connector_oauth_flow_test.go` that drives a pod to call a connector requiring auth, completes the elicitation-mediated OAuth against a fake provider, and asserts a subsequent connector call succeeds with gateway-held state; register the capability in `parity-matrix.yaml` and add a tier6 variant.

### - [ ] T-9.3.5 — The TESTING.md `oauth_connector_flow` suite claims encrypted-storage and token-never-in-pod assertions the implemented test does not make [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "oauth_connector_flow | State parameter, PKCE S256, code exchange, token storage encrypted, token never transits pod" (TESTING.md:1042)
- **Existing tests:** The implemented integration test `tests/tier4_integration/connector_oauth_test.go` asserts the state parameter, PKCE S256, the code exchange, and the single-use state replay rejection. It makes no assertion about encrypted token storage or about the token never transiting a pod. Encrypted storage is asserted separately in `tests/tier2_component/stores/connectorcredstore_test.go` under §13.3, and the token-never-in-pod assertion has no test (see T-9.3.1).
- **Gap:** The suite description in TESTING.md overstates what the suite verifies, which would let a regression in either the encryption-at-rest wiring or the pod-isolation boundary ship while the named suite still passes. Either the two missing assertions are added to the integration suite (storage-encryption cross-check and the pod-isolation negative), or the suite description is corrected to point at the §13.3 store test and the T-9.3.1 isolation test. This is a spec-versus-test inconsistency. Target tier4.
- **Dependencies:** The encrypted-storage cross-check is buildable today by reading the connector credential row after the callback and asserting the blob is not the plaintext token, using the live gateway's Postgres. The token-never-in-pod half depends on T-9.3.1.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `tests/tier4_integration/connector_oauth_test.go` to read the stored credential row and assert the access-token column is ciphertext, and link the token-never-in-pod assertion to the T-9.3.1 tier5 test; alternatively amend TESTING.md:1042 to reference the §13.3 and tier5 tests for the two claims.

### - [ ] T-9.3.6 — No chaos test exercises the Redis-backed OAuth `state` store under outage or failover [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "stores it bound to the initiating session ID and connector ID (Redis, TTL = 10 min), and validates the returned `state` exactly on the redirect callback before exchanging the code for tokens. Mismatched or missing `state` values cause the flow to be aborted and the pending record deleted." (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:157)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/connectoroauth/redis_state_store_test.go` exercises put, consume, replay, and TTL expiry against `miniredis` (an in-process fake), covering the happy path and single-use consumption at the unit level. `tests/tier8_chaos/store_failure_test.go` covers Postgres, Redis-cluster-degraded, and MinIO outages for the session and quota paths (`TestRedisClusterDegraded`, `TestDualStoreUnavailable`), but none of these drives an in-flight OAuth authorization whose `state` lives in Redis. No test found in tier8 that fails Redis between authorize and callback.
- **Gap:** The OAuth `state` entry is the anti-CSRF binding and the PKCE-verifier custody point, and it lives in Redis with a 10-minute TTL. A Redis outage or failover between authorize and callback decides whether the flow fails closed (the pending record is gone, the callback is rejected) or fails open (a stale or duplicate exchange proceeds). The spec mandates the flow is aborted on a missing state. This failure path is unverified end to end. Target tier8 chaos against the compose Redis.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier8 chaos harness (`tests/testinfra/chaos`, `tests/tier8_chaos/chaos_helpers_test.go`), a real Redis container (the chaos suite already uses one), and the gateway authorize/callback endpoints. Buildable today on the existing chaos infrastructure.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier8_chaos/connector_oauth_state_outage_test.go` that initiates an authorization, kills or partitions Redis, drives the callback, and asserts the flow is rejected with a `CONNECTOR_OAUTH_STATE_*` error rather than completing a token exchange, then restores Redis and confirms a fresh flow succeeds.

- **Spec/Doc:** "Future calls from pods authorized for that connector use gateway-held connector state" and the refresh-token grant the gateway runs to keep that state current (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:153; the refresh path is `pkg/connectoroauth.RefreshAccessToken` and `pkg/gateway/connectorinvoke/refresh.go`)

The comment names §9.3, but the scenario validates its own mock rather than the production refresh path. `pkg/gateway/connectorinvoke/refresh_test.go` unit-tests the refresh helper in isolation.
- **Gap:** The named scenario is a placeholder that proves a `sync.Once` works, not that the gateway performs exactly one refresh when N concurrent pod calls observe an expired connector token and that siblings re-read the refreshed credential from `connectorcredstore`. The concurrent-refresh contract against the real store and refresh path is unexercised under load. Target a tier7b or tier4 concurrency test that drives concurrent invokes through the assembled refresh path against a real Postgres-backed `connectorcredstore` and a fake provider token endpoint.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a Postgres-backed `connectorcredstore` (`tests/testinfra` Postgres container), a fake provider token endpoint counting refresh calls, and the `connectorinvoke` refresh wiring. The fake provider exists inline in `connector_oauth_test.go` and can be reused; the concurrency harness in `tests/testinfra/loadgen` is available.
- **Suggested test:** Replace the mock in `tests/tier7a_load_local/scenarios/connector_oauth_refresh_race/scenario.go` (or add `tests/tier4_integration/connector_refresh_concurrency_test.go`) with N concurrent `Invoker.CallTool` calls against an expired credential, asserting the provider token endpoint sees exactly one refresh per epoch and every caller reads the rotated token.

- **Spec/Doc:** "All connectors must be registered before they can be used — unregistered external endpoints cannot be called from inside a pod (security: gateway must know about every external endpoint for OAuth flow, audit logging, and protocol mediation)." (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:140)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/connectorinvoke/invoker_test.go::TestInvokerRejectsUnregisteredConnector_spec_9_3_140` and `TestInvokerRejectsSoftDeletedConnector_spec_9_3_140` cover the rejection at the invoker unit level with an in-memory connector store. No test found in tiers 4, 5, or 9 that drives a pod attempting to reach an unregistered external endpoint through the assembled gateway and asserts the call is blocked, nor that the attempt is audited.

The unit test proves the invoker rejects an unknown connector ID, but nothing proves the assembled pod-to-gateway path blocks an attempt to call an endpoint that was never registered, and the spec ties registration to audit logging, so the audit emission on a blocked attempt is also unverified. This is an adversarial scenario (a compromised agent attempts to exfiltrate to an arbitrary host). Target tier9 security against the compose or Kind gateway, with an audit-event assertion.
