## §10.3 mTLS PKI <a id="t-10.3"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/10_gateway-internals.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§10.3 specifies the internal mTLS PKI: a cert-manager-issued certificate lifecycle, three symmetric SPIFFE/DNS peer-validation rules (Pod↔Gateway NET-060, Gateway↔Interceptor NET-063, Token Service↔Gateway), a projected SA token with deployment-specific audience, admission-time zero-RBAC enforcement, an in-memory certificate deny list propagated over Redis pub/sub, Redis and PgBouncer TLS enforcement with a gateway startup probe, gateway startup configuration validation, warm-pool certificate awareness, and a CA-rotation procedure. The spec text itself is unchanged since the 2026-06-03 audit (`git diff` against `d9074016` touches only §10.1 and §10.2 in this file). Reconciling against the tree shows five of the fourteen original findings are now resolved by work that landed independent of any spec change: the gateway↔interceptor NET-063 hop gained a `spiffe.InterceptorPeerVerifier`, an `interceptordial` package with a real net.Pipe TLS handshake test, and a chart `Certificate` (T-10.3.2); the preflight NET-064 uniqueness checks are now exercised end to end through `preflight.Run` with fabricated colliding gateway Deployments (T-10.3.6); the warm-pool controller's 60s issuance-failure replacement and 30-minute proactive-drain are covered against envtest (T-10.3.7); the mTLS certificate deny list's Redis pub/sub cross-replica propagation is exercised against a real Redis container (T-10.3.11); and the cert-manager minimum-version preflight check now has a full pass/fail matrix (T-10.3.12). The remaining nine findings hold: no live TLS handshake test exists for the Pod↔Gateway (T-10.3.1) or Token Service↔Gateway (T-10.3.3) links, Redis/PgBouncer TLS enforcement is still proved only against loopback fixtures rather than the CI-deployed stores the spec names (T-10.3.4), the gateway config-validation gate is still proved only by calling the validation function rather than observing a real process refuse readiness and crash (T-10.3.5), certificate auto-renewal and no-drop reload lack a chart `renewBefore` assertion and a connection-survival test (T-10.3.8), the CA-rotation procedure's dual-CA overlap is still unverified against a live handshake despite a new durable `carotationstore`/admin-API orchestration layer (T-10.3.9), live Kyverno admission enforcement is untested (T-10.3.10), and the chart required-value guard (T-10.3.13) and the spec-map JWKS/JWT misattribution (T-10.3.14) are both unchanged.
Counts (all 14 findings, open and resolved): 6 High, 6 Medium, 1 Low, 1 Info. Of the 6 High findings, 2 are now resolved (T-10.3.2, T-10.3.6) and 4 remain open (T-10.3.1, T-10.3.3, T-10.3.4, T-10.3.5). Of the 6 Medium findings, 3 are now resolved (T-10.3.7, T-10.3.11, T-10.3.12) and 3 remain open (T-10.3.8, T-10.3.9, T-10.3.10). The Low (T-10.3.13) and Info (T-10.3.14) findings remain open. Net: 5 resolved this pass, 9 still open.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-10.3.1 — Pod↔Gateway mTLS SAN validation (NET-060) is never exercised over a live TLS handshake [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Both sides reject on SAN mismatch at TLS handshake time — before any gRPC frame is sent — so an attacker holding a valid cluster-CA-signed cert for an unrelated workload cannot impersonate either endpoint." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:324); "A certificate whose SPIFFE URI parses correctly but belongs to a different pool or pod — or whose trust domain does not equal `global.spiffeTrustDomain` — is rejected at handshake with no gRPC response, and the attempt is logged as `pod_identity_mismatch`." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:321)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/mtls/spiffe/verify_test.go` calls `AgentPeerVerifier.VerifyPeerCertificate` directly with fabricated certificates (foreign trust domain, interceptor kind, pool/pod mismatch, deny-listed serial); these are tier1 unit tests against the verifier function. `pkg/mtls/spiffe/spiffe_test.go` unit-tests `ValidateAgent`. The tier5 `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/mtls_test.go` and tier9 `tests/tier9_security/tls_test.go` only assert cert-manager `Certificate`/`Issuer` readiness. spec-map.json §10.3 lists exactly these. A search for `NET-060`, `RequireAndVerifyClientCert`, and `adapter.*ServerName.*lenny-gateway` under `tests/` returns no integration or e2e test. Unlike the NET-063 gateway↔interceptor hop (see the T-10.3.2 resolution below), no `AgentPeerVerifier`-equivalent live-handshake package (analogous to `pkg/mtls/interceptordial`) exists for the pod↔gateway link.
- **Gap:** No tier4/tier5 test stands up a gateway gRPC listener with `RequireAndVerifyClientCert` and the `AgentPeerVerifier` wired in, then drives a real adapter handshake presenting (a) a matching agent cert that is accepted, (b) a cluster-CA cert for a different pool/pod that is rejected at handshake with no gRPC frame, and (c) a Token Service or interceptor cert that is rejected. This is both a real user journey (an adapter connecting on the §4.7 startup sequence) and an adversarial scenario (a workload presenting a valid-but-wrong cluster cert). The `pod_identity_mismatch` log emission is also unverified end to end.
- **Dependencies:** Requires an in-process gRPC server-with-verifier harness plus a cert-minting fixture; `tests/testinfra/gateway` and the ECDSA cert builder pattern already in `pkg/mtls/spiffe/verify_test.go` (and now also `pkg/mtls/interceptordial/handshake_test.go`, which demonstrates the net.Pipe pattern for the sibling NET-063 hop) are reusable. None — buildable today at tier4 with in-process listeners; the live-cluster variant additionally needs `tests/testinfra/kind` and cert-manager-issued pod certs.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/mtls_pod_gateway_handshake_test.go` that boots the gateway gRPC server with the agent verifier, then asserts a matching cert connects, a wrong-pool cluster cert is refused at TLS handshake (no gRPC response), and the `pod_identity_mismatch` event is emitted; reuse the cert builder from `pkg/mtls/spiffe/verify_test.go`, or add a `pkg/mtls/agentdial` package mirroring `pkg/mtls/interceptordial`'s net.Pipe handshake test.

### - [x] T-10.3.2 — Gateway↔Interceptor mTLS peer validation (NET-063) has no test or chart Certificate at any tier [High] — RESOLVED 5eee9d30
- **Resolution:** Commit `5eee9d30` ("F-10.3.3/F-10.3.19: enforce §10.3 NET-063 gateway→interceptor mTLS") closes the core of this finding. `pkg/mtls/spiffe/InterceptorPeerVerifier` (`interceptor_verify_test.go`) mirrors `AgentPeerVerifier`, validating the peer's SPIFFE URI against the trust domain and `gateway.interceptorNamespaces` allowlist plus the deny list. New package `pkg/mtls/interceptordial` builds the dial credentials, pinning `tls.Config.ServerName` to the registered endpoint (DNS-SAN validation) and timing every handshake into the §16.1 histogram; its `handshake_test.go` performs a **real net.Pipe TLS handshake** (not a direct verifier call) and asserts a matching in-namespace interceptor cert succeeds, a wrong-namespace cert is rejected with `san_mismatch`, and a DNS-SAN mismatch is rejected by `ServerName` pinning — closing the "no test at any tier" half of the finding. The chart's `lenny.interceptorCertificate` helper (`charts/lenny/templates/mtls-pki.yaml:104-112`) now renders one cert-manager `Certificate` per declared `gateway.interceptorNamespaces` entry with both SANs, gated on `mtls.interceptorCertificates.enabled`, and `charts/lenny/tests/mtls-pki_test.yaml` (`renders one interceptor certificate per declared namespace`, `stamps the SPIFFE and DNS SANs...`, `omits interceptor certificates when the toggle is off`) closes the "no chart Certificate" half. `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` wires `dialInterceptor` to log `interceptor_identity_mismatch` on a mismatch (per `pkg/gateway/gatewaymetrics`'s `ObserveInterceptorMTLSHandshake`). The residual gap the finding also named — the interceptor-side validation of the inbound gateway DNS SAN, which the spec assigns to "the reference interceptor library shipped with Lenny" — has no such reference interceptor server implementation in this repo to test; this is out of Lenny's own testable surface until a reference interceptor binary exists (not tracked as a separate finding here since there is no code to test). Plaintext/`h2c`/`InsecureSkipVerify` refusal is structural (grpc `credentials.NewTLS` offers no such option) rather than separately tested, consistent with how the sibling Redis/PgBouncer findings treat structural impossibility.

### - [ ] T-10.3.3 — Token Service↔Gateway mutual SAN validation handshake is unverified [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The gateway validates the Token Service's DNS SAN (`lenny-token-service.lenny-system.svc`) on every mTLS connection — it must not accept any certificate from the cluster CA. The Token Service validates that incoming connections present a gateway replica certificate (matching the gateway's DNS SAN `lenny-gateway.lenny-system.svc`), rejecting connections from any other component." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:318)
- **Existing tests:** `charts/lenny/tests/gateway-deployment_test.yaml` asserts the gateway is wired with `--token-service-tls-cert/-key/-ca` flags and dials `lenny-token-service.NAMESPACE.svc:50052`. The tier5/tier9 suites assert the `lenny-token-service-tls` `Certificate` is Ready. `tests/testinfra/tokenservice/tokenservice.go` (the harness `tests/tier4_integration/tokenservice_cutover_test.go` drives) carries no TLS configuration. A search of `tests/` and `pkg/` for `TokenServicePeer`, `token.service.*mtls`, and a `lenny-token-service.lenny-system.svc` SAN check still returns no handshake-level test.
- **Gap:** No component/integration test drives a Token Service↔Gateway mTLS handshake and asserts that (a) the gateway rejects a cluster-CA cert that is not the Token Service DNS SAN, and (b) the Token Service rejects any non-gateway cert. The spec states "compromise of an unrelated component's certificate cannot be used to impersonate either the gateway or the Token Service," and that mutual rejection is the security property; it is verified only by chart-flag rendering. This is an adversarial path.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the `tests/testinfra/tokenservice` harness with TLS configured and a cert-minting fixture for gateway and non-gateway SANs. None — buildable today at tier4 with in-process listeners.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/mtls_tokenservice_gateway_test.go` using `tests/testinfra/tokenservice` and `tests/testinfra/gateway` to assert mutual SAN rejection: a controller-SAN cert is refused on the gateway client leg and on the Token Service server leg.

### - [ ] T-10.3.4 — Redis and PgBouncer TLS enforcement and the gateway startup TLS probe are not exercised against real stores [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Each gateway replica **must** run a startup probe that verifies TLS connectivity to Redis and PgBouncer before the replica is marked ready. The probe attempts a TLS handshake to both endpoints and fails startup if either handshake fails or if a plaintext connection is accepted." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:359); "**Integration test requirement:** The test suite **must** include tests (`TestRedisTLSEnforcement`, `TestPgBouncerTLSEnforcement`) that assert plaintext connection attempts to Redis and PgBouncer are rejected with a connection error. These tests run in the CI environment where Redis and PgBouncer are deployed with the production TLS configuration." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:373)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/pki/tlsprobe/tlsprobe_test.go` (moved from `pkg/gateway/tlsprobe` since the audit; no behavior change) defines `TestRedisTLSEnforcement_spec_10_3_373` and `TestPgBouncerTLSEnforcement_spec_10_3_373`, but they still run against in-process loopback `tls.Listen`/`net.Listen` fixtures, so they remain tier1 unit tests of the probe logic, not the CI-deployed-stores integration test the spec mandates. `compose/mtls.yml` exists but no tier4 test consumes it for plaintext rejection.
- **Gap:** The spec explicitly requires `TestRedisTLSEnforcement` and `TestPgBouncerTLSEnforcement` to run against Redis and PgBouncer "deployed with the production TLS configuration." The current tests prove only the probe's branching logic. The integration behavior (a real TLS-only Redis with `port 0` rejecting plaintext, the startup probe flipping readiness to false on a misconfigured port) is unexercised. This is a security control and a deployment-combination gap (Redis single/HA, PgBouncer require/verify-full).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the `mtls` compose profile wired into a tier4 harness, or the tier5 Kind stores with production TLS config. `tests/testinfra/stubs` and `compose/mtls.yml` provide the substrate. None — buildable today at tier4 against the compose `mtls` profile.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/store_tls_enforcement_test.go` that brings up the `mtls` compose profile and asserts a plaintext dial to Redis (`6380` TLS-only, `port 0`) and PgBouncer (`client_tls_sslmode=require`) is rejected, and that the gateway startup probe fails readiness when pointed at a plaintext port.

### - [ ] T-10.3.5 — Gateway startup configuration validation (`LENNY_CONFIG_MISSING` readiness gate) is not verified against a live gateway [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "each gateway replica **MUST** validate that required platform-level configuration keys are present before marking itself ready. Missing any required key is a hard startup failure — the gateway MUST refuse to become ready (readiness probe returns `false` ...) and MUST emit a `LENNY_CONFIG_MISSING` structured log entry at `FATAL` level identifying the missing key(s)." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:361); "The test suite **must** also include a `TestGatewayConfigValidation` test that asserts each required key ... causes a startup failure when absent, that the corresponding `LENNY_CONFIG_MISSING` log entry is emitted with the correct `config_key` value, and that the OIDC keys ... are exempt from the startup gate when `LENNY_DEV_MODE=true`." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:373)
- **Existing tests:** `cmd/lenny-gateway/main_test.go` has `TestGatewayConfigValidation_spec_11_1` and `TestGatewayConfigValidationRequiredKeys_spec_10_3` that call the in-process `validatePlatformConfig` function and assert the missing-key error and dev-mode OIDC exemption; `TestBuildStartupProbeTLSConfig_spec_10_3` unit-tests the startup-gate composition helper (`startupgates.go`). These are tier1 unit tests of the validation function, not the assembled process. No test spawns `cmd/lenny-gateway` as a process or drives it through envtest/Kind to observe readiness and exit behavior.
- **Gap:** No component/e2e test asserts that the assembled gateway process actually refuses readiness (`/healthz` or readiness probe returns false) and exits non-zero into `CrashLoopBackOff` when a required key is absent, nor that the `LENNY_CONFIG_MISSING` log reaches the operator with the structured `config_key`/`scope`/`remediation` fields. The behavioral contract is the readiness gate and crash, which the unit test does not reach. This is a deployment-failure path that the spec frames as catching config errors before traffic.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the `tests/testinfra/gateway` boot harness or a tier5 Kind install that omits a required Helm value. None — buildable today at tier4 with the gateway boot harness for the crash-and-no-ready assertion; the Kind variant needs `tests/testinfra/kind`.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/gateway_config_gate_test.go` that boots `cmd/lenny-gateway` with `defaultMaxSessionDuration` unset and asserts the process exits non-zero, never reports ready, and emits `LENNY_CONFIG_MISSING` with `config_key=defaultMaxSessionDuration`; add a dev-mode case proving OIDC keys are exempt.

### - [x] T-10.3.6 — Cross-deployment SPIFFE/audience uniqueness preflight abort is not exercised end to end against a second deployment [High] — RESOLVED 6b4ab327
- **Resolution:** Commit `6b4ab327` ("preflight: §13.2 NetworkPolicy selector-consistency and parity audits (§18.33)") added `pkg/preflight/run_networkpolicy_test.go`, which drives the full `preflight.Run` (not the pure `CheckSPIFFETrustDomainUniqueness`/`CheckSATokenAudienceUniqueness` functions in isolation) against a fabricated controller-runtime client. `TestRunFailsOnNET064TrustDomainCollision` seeds a `lenny-gateway` Deployment in a second namespace carrying the `lenny.dev/spiffe-trust-domain`/`lenny.dev/sa-token-audience` annotations, configures the install under test with the same trust domain, and asserts the `spiffe-trust-domain-uniqueness` check fails and the overall report fails — exercising the live `gatherGatewayIdentities` enumeration path the original finding said was untested. `TestRunPassesNET064WhenNoExistingGateway` covers the fresh-install pass case, and `TestRunReportsGatewayIdentityListFailureFailClosed` pins the fail-closed posture when the Deployment `List` call itself errors. This closes the finding's core gap: the cluster-enumeration query and the abort-decision wiring are now exercised together, not just the pure decision functions. Two narrower gaps remain outside this resolution's scope: no test exercises an `sa-token-audience` collision specifically (only the trust-domain collision path is asserted end to end; the audience path is asserted in isolation via the pre-existing unit tests), and no test asserts the `cmd/lenny-preflight` binary itself exits with code 1 on this failure (only the `Decision`-level failure is asserted). These are narrow enough residuals of an otherwise-resolved finding rather than a distinct new finding.

### - [x] T-10.3.7 — Warm-pool certificate awareness (issuance-failure replacement and proactive expiry drain) is untested above unit [Medium] — RESOLVED 1f2bb711,f3dc340c
- **Resolution:** Commits `1f2bb711` ("F-4.6.7: §4.6.1 per-pod reconciler (host-schedulable label + cert-expiry replacement)") and `f3dc340c` ("F-10.3.17: warm-pool cert-issuance grace + lenny_cert_expiry_seconds gauge") add a WarmPoolController per-pod reconciler with envtest-backed component tests in `pkg/controller/warmpool/pod_reconciler_test.go`: `TestPodReconcileCertExpiryDrainsIdlePod_spec_4_6` and `TestPodReconcileCertExpiryKeepsFreshPod_spec_4_6` exercise the 30-minute proactive-drain threshold (`defaultCertExpiryThreshold`) against an idle pod's certificate expiry annotation; `TestPodReconcileCertIssuanceFailureDrainsPreIdlePod_spec_10_3`, `TestPodReconcileCertIssuanceInsideGraceKeepsPreIdlePod_spec_10_3`, and `TestPodReconcileCertIssuanceDisabledKeepsPreIdlePod_spec_10_3` exercise the 60-second issuance-failure replacement (`defaultCertIssuanceGrace`) for a pod whose certificate never becomes Ready. `TestPodReconcileCertExpiryGaugeEmitted_spec_10_3` and `...GaugeClearedOnMissingPod_spec_10_3` cover the `lenny_cert_expiry_seconds` gauge lifecycle. `newClient` in `pkg/controller/warmpool/controller_test.go` backs these with a real envtest API server, satisfying the component-tier bar the finding asked for. Both core behaviors the finding named — issuance-failure replacement and proactive expiry drain — now have envtest-backed coverage.

### - [ ] T-10.3.8 — Certificate auto-renewal at 2/3 lifetime and filesystem-watching reload (no gRPC drop) are untested above unit [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Both the gateway and the runtime adapter **must** use filesystem-watching TLS configuration (`tls.Config` with `GetCertificate`/`GetClientCertificate` callbacks that re-read from the cert-manager-managed projected volume) so that renewed certificates are picked up transparently without restarting the pod or dropping the gRPC connection. This decouples session duration from certificate lifetime ..." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:338); auto-renewal "at 2/3 lifetime" (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:310, 314).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/mtls/certreload/certreload_test.go` unit-tests the reloader picking up a rewritten keypair from disk (`TestReloaderPicksUpRenewedCert_spec_10_3_338`, plus cache-when-unchanged and keep-last-good-on-error cases). The chart renders `renewBefore` in `_helpers.tpl` and `mtls-pki.yaml:69`, but no chart test asserts the `renewBefore` value matches the 2/3-lifetime rule. A search of `charts/lenny/tests/*.yaml` for `renewBefore` returns no assertion.
- **Gap:** No integration/e2e test proves that an in-flight gRPC connection survives a certificate rotation (the decoupling of `maxSessionAge` from cert TTL), and no chart test pins `renewBefore` to 2/3 of the leaf duration. This is a long-running-session user journey (a session outliving the 4h pod cert TTL).
- **Dependencies:** Requires a tier4 harness that swaps the projected cert file mid-connection, or a tier5 Kind cert-manager rotation under traffic. `pkg/mtls/certreload` plus `tests/testinfra/gateway` are reusable. None for the connection-survival tier4 case; the live-rotation case needs `tests/testinfra/kind`.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/cert_rotation_no_drop_test.go` that opens a gRPC stream over mTLS, rewrites the cert file on disk, and asserts the stream continues; add a helm unit assertion that `renewBefore` equals one third of the leaf duration.

### - [ ] T-10.3.9 — CA rotation procedure (dual-CA overlap, end-to-end) is untested above the in-process state machine [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "**CA rotation procedure:** When rotating the cluster-internal CA ... Deploy a new CA certificate alongside the old one (both trusted during overlap period) ... Gateway, controller, and Token Service trust bundles must include both CAs during the overlap window" (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:345-350).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/mtls/rotation_test.go` and `pkg/mtls/rotation_restore_test.go` unit-test the in-process `CARotation` state machine (begin adds new CA to trust bundle, promote flips issuer keeps trust, retire guards overlap window, restore-after-restart invariants). Since the audit, a durable orchestration layer has landed on top of this state machine: `pkg/gateway/pki/carotation.Manager` persists the rotation stage via `pkg/gateway/pki/carotationstore` (with a `pgstore` Postgres-backed implementation whose `pgstore_test.go` unit-tests only the row-scan mapping via a fake `Scan`, not a real Postgres) and emits a `platform.ca_rotated` audit row; `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/ca_rotation_test.go`'s `TestCARotation_fullLifecycle_spec_10_3` drives the admin API (`GET/POST /v1/admin/ca-rotation`) through status→begin→promote→retire against an in-memory store and a movable clock. All of this remains in-process: no test brings up a second cert-manager `ClusterIssuer`, drives real TLS handshakes against leaves from both CAs during the overlap window, or confirms an old-CA leaf is rejected after retire. `tests/tier8_chaos/runbook-map.yaml` still references only a `cert-manager-outage` runbook, not CA rotation.
- **Gap:** No integration/e2e test executes the documented dual-CA overlap: deploy a second CA, confirm both CAs validate inbound handshakes during the overlap, rotate leaves to the new CA, then remove the old CA from the trust bundle and confirm old-CA certs are then rejected. The trust-bundle-includes-both-CAs invariant during overlap, and now also the durable-store persistence layer, are verified only by in-memory/mocked substrates, not against a real handshake or a real Postgres. This is an operational user journey (annual or on-compromise CA rotation).
- **Dependencies:** Requires a tier5 Kind harness with two cert-manager CA issuers and a way to drive the overlap window, plus `tests/testinfra/kind`. The dual-CA Kind fixture does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding. A tier2 envtest/real-Postgres variant of `pgstore_test.go` would additionally close the persistence-layer gap without needing Kind.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/ca_rotation_test.go` that introduces a second CA, asserts both old- and new-CA leaves handshake during overlap, then removes the old CA and asserts old-CA leaves are rejected; reference `tests/testinfra/kind`. Add a `pgstore` component test against a real Postgres alongside the existing chaos/component Postgres fixtures.

## §10.4 Gateway Reliability <a id="t-10.4"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/10_gateway-internals.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§10.4 has component-level coverage for the in-process synthesis logic. The handler-level tests in `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/events_test.go` and `resumed_event_test.go` exercise the coordinator-handoff reattach synthesis (`session.resumed`, `status_change`, `children_reattached`) and the gap-marker emission against an in-memory store and bus, and `tests/tier3_contract/sdks/go_client_test.go` drives a same-coordinator reconnect-with-cursor through the SDK against an in-process gateway. The design principle that a coordinating-replica death produces a reconnect rather than session loss is never exercised end to end: tier8 `TestGatewayReplicaFailure` asserts only Deployment reschedule and Service endpoint continuity, and no tier4/tier5/tier8 test kills the coordinating replica and then reattaches a client to verify the event stream, the synthesized reattach frames, or `SeqNum` durability survive a real handoff. The named tier4 suite `streaming_reconnect` and its file `tests/tier4_integration/streaming_reconnect_test.go` do not exist on disk; the standing scaffold is a `t.Logf` stub. The session-event replay buffer default disagrees between the spec (512) and the Go library default (256), and no test pins either value. The `gap_detected`, `session.resumed`, and `children_reattached` SSE frames have no contract or conformance test that pins them against a fixed wire schema. The §10.4 spec text itself has not changed since the 2026-06-03 audit; the packages it names have moved (`pkg/gateway/sessionevents` → `pkg/gateway/session/sessionevents`, `pkg/gateway/events` → `pkg/gateway/eventbuffer`, `pkg/gateway/pdbwatcher` → `pkg/gateway/coordination/pdbwatcher`, `pkg/gateway/health` → `pkg/gateway/operability/health`) and none of the ten findings' suggested tests have landed. Counts: 3 High, 4 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-10.4.1 — Coordinating-replica death with client reattach has no end-to-end test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Gateway pod failure causes a broken stream and reconnect, never session loss." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:376)
- **Existing tests:** tier8 `tests/tier8_chaos/pod_disruption_test.go::TestGatewayReplicaFailure` deletes one gateway pod and asserts the Deployment returns to fully Ready and the `lenny-gateway` Service keeps a non-empty endpoint set; it is tagged §17.2 and never opens a client stream, never reconnects, and never inspects session state. `tests/tier4_integration/gateway_redis_e2e_test.go::TestGatewayRedisCoordinationE2E` verifies a Redis coordination lease is acquired with a TTL but does not kill the coordinator or reattach. The synthesis logic is covered only in-process in `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/events_test.go::TestEventsStreamSynthesizesHandoffReattach_spec_10_4` against `memstore.New()` and `sessionevents.NewBus(0)`. No test in tiers 4, 5, or 8 (searched `tests/tier4_integration`, `tests/tier5_e2e_kind`, `tests/tier8_chaos`) drives a live client onto a session, kills the coordinating replica, and asserts the client reconnects and the session is preserved.
- **Gap:** The core §10.4 design principle is unverified end to end. The missing test is both a real user journey (alice holds a live session on replica A, replica A dies, alice's client reconnects and the session continues) and an adversarial/failure scenario (coordinator death mid-stream). Target tier5 on Kind for a true coordinating-replica kill, with a tier8 chaos variant under load. This is the highest-risk gap because a regression that loses sessions on replica death would ship undetected.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a Kind harness with a multi-replica gateway and the ability to identify and delete the replica coordinating a specific session (the lease key `t:{tenant}:lease:session:{id}` in Redis maps session to coordinator). Building the "kill the coordinator of session X, not an arbitrary replica" helper is part of this finding; it can extend `tests/testinfra/kind` and `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/coordinator_handoff_reattach_test.go` using tests/testinfra/kind and tests/testinfra/sessiondriver: open an SSE stream against a session, resolve and delete its coordinating replica via the Redis lease holder, then assert the client reconnects and continues receiving events with no session loss.

### - [ ] T-10.4.2 — SeqNum durability across coordinator handoff is untested against real Postgres [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The `SessionEvent.SeqNum` counter ... is per-session and MUST survive coordinator handoff without rewinds or duplicates. The counter is durably tracked in Postgres as the `sessions.last_seq` column ... Synthesized state-frame events consume fresh `SeqNum` values from this counter exactly like any other persisted event." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:398)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/events_test.go::TestEventsStreamSynthesizesHandoffReattach_spec_10_4` seeds `LastSeq: 5` in a `memstore` and checks synthesized frames carry no `id:` line. `pkg/gateway/session/sessionevents` (moved from `pkg/gateway/sessionevents`) and `tests/tier2_component/stores/eventstore_test.go` touch `last_seq` at the store level. No test advances `last_seq` on a real Postgres-backed coordinator, performs a handoff to a second coordinator process, and asserts the second coordinator's first emitted `SeqNum` is strictly greater than the last persisted value with no rewind and no duplicate.
- **Gap:** This is a normative MUST with a monotonicity and no-duplicate guarantee that only manifests across an actual handoff between two coordinators sharing real Postgres state. The in-memory test cannot observe a rewind because there is a single process and a single counter. The missing test is a failure-path correctness check at tier4 (two gateway processes over one Postgres) or tier5 (handoff on Kind). Its absence would let a counter-priming regression (handoff step 0 cache vs authoritative `sessions.last_seq` read) ship.
- **Dependencies:** Requires two gateway instances sharing one Postgres (extend `tests/tier4_integration/gateway_postgres_e2e_test.go` style with a second `gateway.StartWith`) or the tier5 handoff harness from T-10.4.1. The shared-Postgres two-coordinator fixture is buildable today with tests/testinfra/gateway and a real Postgres container.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/seqnum_handoff_durability_test.go` driving two gateway subprocesses over one Postgres: persist events on coordinator A up to a known `last_seq`, force coordinator B to take over and emit synthesized frames, then assert B's emitted `SeqNum` values are strictly increasing past A's high-water mark with no repeats.

### - [ ] T-10.4.3 — TESTING.md-declared tier4 `streaming_reconnect` suite is absent; standing scaffold is a no-op stub [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "streaming_reconnect | Client disconnects mid-stream, reconnects with `Last-Event-ID`, replay from cursor, no duplicate or missing events" (TESTING.md:1025) and "`tests/tier4_integration/streaming_reconnect_test.go` covers reconnect with cursor under controlled disconnects." (TESTING.md:1657)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier4_integration/streaming_reconnect_test.go` does not exist (directory listing of `tests/tier4_integration` confirms its absence). The only artifact is `tests/tier4_integration/scaffolds_test.go::TestStreamingReconnect`, which calls `t.Logf` and asserts nothing; it punts coverage to `pkg/gateway/eventbuffer` (renamed from `pkg/gateway/events`), `sessionserver/events_test.go`, the tier7 baseline, and `streaming-echo`. The renamed package's own doc comment (`pkg/gateway/eventbuffer/buffer.go`) now states explicitly that it implements the §25.3 operational-event ring buffer and "is distinct from `pkg/gateway/session/sessionevents`, which is the session event bus backing the §15.1 session SSE stream" — confirming the scaffold's citation still names the wrong buffer for the §10.4 session-event replay guarantee it claims to cover.
- **Gap:** A suite the project declares in its own §14 domain table and in the §13.16 phase plan has no implementation through the compose stack, and the placeholder asserts nothing, while also misattributing coverage to a package the renamed package's own documentation now disowns for this purpose. This is a spec-versus-test inconsistency that hides the §10.4 replay-through-the-gateway-proxy gap at every run. Target tier4: a real reconnect-with-cursor through the gateway subprocess against a real backing bus, asserting zero duplicate and zero missing events.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the live gateway subprocess harness (tests/testinfra/gateway) plus a backing event source that the test can drive across a forced disconnect. None of the infrastructure is missing; the building blocks already back `TestGatewayRedisCoordinationE2E`.
- **Suggested test:** Create `tests/tier4_integration/streaming_reconnect_test.go` using tests/testinfra/gateway: create a session, stream a known event sequence, drop the connection mid-stream, reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`, and assert the union of received `SeqNum` values is the contiguous full set with no gaps and no repeats. Remove the `t.Logf` stub once landed.

### - [ ] T-10.4.4 — Replay-buffer eviction `gap_detected` frame has no contract or conformance test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "When a requested `resumeFromSeq` points to an event that has been evicted, the adapter emits a single protocol-level `gap_detected` frame (`{\"lastSeenSeq\": N, \"nextSeq\": M}`) before resuming at the oldest retained event ... The `gap_detected` frame is a stream-control signal ... carries no `SeqNum`, and is not part of the `SessionEventKind` closed enum." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:388)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/events_test.go::TestEventsStreamEmitsGapAndCheckpointMarkers_spec_7_2` and `TestEventsStreamOmitsGapMarkersWhenCursorWithinBuffer_spec_7_2` exercise the gap-marker handler against an in-memory bus and are tagged §7.2. `tests/tier3_contract/sdks/go_client_test.go::TestGoClientStreamingReconnect` reconnects with a cursor but never forces an out-of-buffer cursor, so the `gap_detected` frame is never produced in any contract test. No tier3 contract test and no tier10 conformance test pins the exact `{"lastSeenSeq": N, "nextSeq": M}` JSON, the single-frame guarantee, or the "no `SeqNum`, not in the closed enum" property against a fixed schema.
- **Gap:** The `gap_detected` frame is a wire-protocol surface on the SSE stream that clients parse, and §10.4 fixes its exact JSON. The contract for the eviction case (cursor below the retained window) is unverified at tier3 and unpinned at tier10. The missing test is a standards/wire-format conformance check: force eviction, then assert exactly one `gap_detected` frame with the documented field names and no `id:` line. Target tier3 contract.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The in-process sessionserver plus a small replay buffer (depth below the published event count) reproduces eviction; tests/testinfra/sdkhelper and the existing `disconnector` pattern apply.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/rest_sessions/events_gap_detected_test.go` that fills the per-session buffer past its depth, reconnects with a `Last-Event-ID` below the oldest retained `SeqNum`, and asserts exactly one `event: gap_detected` frame whose data is `{"lastSeenSeq":N,"nextSeq":M}` with no `id:` line, followed by replay from the oldest retained event.

### - [ ] T-10.4.5 — Coordinator-handoff reattach synthesis exercised only in-process, never across a real handoff or full surface [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "before the new coordinator permits the reattach path to emit any `gap_detected` frame, it MUST re-synthesize the set of reconstructible `SessionEvent`s from durable Postgres state ... One `session.resumed` with `resumeMode: \"coordinator_handoff\"` ... Zero-or-one `status_change(state)` ... One `children_reattached(children)` ..." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:390-396)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/events_test.go::TestEventsStreamSynthesizesHandoffReattach_spec_10_4`, `TestEventsStreamHandoffSynthesisStreamsChildren_spec_10_4`, `TestEventsStreamNoHandoffSynthesisWithLocalHistory_spec_10_4`, and `TestEventsStreamNoHandoffSynthesisOnFreshConnect_spec_10_4` cover the four synthesis branches, plus `resumed_event_test.go::TestResumeEmitsResumedBeforeChildrenReattached`. All run against `memstore.New()`, `sessionevents.NewBus(0)`, and `treearchive.NewMemory()` in one process; the "handoff" is simulated by a session row with `LastSeq > Last-Event-ID` and an empty local bus rather than by an actual change of coordinator over real Postgres.
- **Gap:** The synthesis must read durable Postgres state on a coordinator that did not author the original events; the in-memory tests cannot show that the synthesis set is correctly reconstructed from a foreign coordinator's persisted rows, that the volatile ring contents are genuinely discarded on handoff, or that the ordering holds when the archive and `sessions` rows are served by real backing stores. This is a partial-coverage finding: the happy-path logic is covered, but the deployment combination (real handoff, real Postgres, real tree archive) is unexercised. Target tier4 (two coordinators over one Postgres) or tier5.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the two-coordinator-over-one-Postgres fixture from T-10.4.2 plus a real `session_tree_archive`. Buildable today with tests/testinfra/gateway and a Postgres container.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/handoff_reattach_synthesis_test.go`: persist a parent session with archived children on coordinator A, force a handoff to coordinator B, reattach a client with `resumeFromSeq` below `lastSeqBeforeHandoff`, and assert B emits exactly one `session.resumed` with `resumeMode: coordinator_handoff`, the conditional `status_change`, and exactly one `children_reattached` carrying the archived `TaskResult`, all before any `gap_detected`.

### - [ ] T-10.4.6 — `children_reattached` exactly-once-per-parent-resume guarantee not verified across the handoff/no-duplicate boundary [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The 'exactly once per parent resume' guarantee in [§7.2] is preserved: the synthesized frame counts as that one delivery for the reconstructing client; a client that was connected across the handoff and already observed a pre-handoff `children_reattached` receives no duplicate because its `resumeFromSeq` is past that frame's `SeqNum`." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:394)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/reattach_order_internal_test.go::TestEmitChildrenReattachedStreamsArchiveInSettlementOrder_spec_8_10_1062` and `TestEmitChildrenReattachedSuppressedWhenNoneActive_spec_8_10_1062` cover ordering and suppression-when-none. `TestEventsStreamHandoffSynthesisStreamsChildren_spec_10_4` covers a single reconstructing client. No test models the two-client case the spec calls out: a client whose `resumeFromSeq` is past a pre-handoff `children_reattached` (must receive no duplicate) versus a reconstructing client whose cursor predates it (must receive exactly one).
- **Gap:** The no-duplicate guarantee for a client connected across the handoff is the adversarial half of the exactly-once contract and is untested. A regression in the cursor comparison (`completion_seq > resumeFromSeq`) would re-deliver a settled child to a client that already saw it, which this finding's missing test would catch. Target tier4 component, modeling two cursors against the same handoff.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today against the in-process sessionserver with two stream connections at different cursors; tests/testinfra/sdkhelper helps drive the two readers.
- **Suggested test:** Add a case to `tests/tier3_contract/rest_sessions/events_gap_detected_test.go` or a new `handoff_children_dedup_test.go`: with an archived child whose `completion_seq` is fixed, open one stream with `resumeFromSeq` below it and a second with `resumeFromSeq` above it, then assert the first receives exactly one `children_reattached` and the second receives none.

### - [ ] T-10.4.7 — `streaming_reconnect` load scenario asserts only HTTP status and latency, not zero-loss/zero-duplicate [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "streaming_reconnect_under_load | 500 concurrent streaming sessions, periodic disconnects | Streaming reconnect latency P95 < 500ms; zero event loss" (TESTING.md:1180) and "Disconnect mid-stream and reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`; assert zero gaps and zero duplicates." (TESTING.md:1982)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/streaming_reconnect/main.js` is a k6 scenario whose `thresholds` block checks time-to-first-byte under the P95 budget and that at least 95% of reconnects return 200/206; its `check` calls assert only `r.status`. It synthesizes the `Last-Event-ID` from `__ITER - 1` rather than from observed sequence numbers, so it cannot detect a dropped or duplicated event. `tests/tier7b_load_kind/streaming_test.go` runs only `TestStreamingThroughput`. The declared `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/streaming_reconnect.go` (TESTING.md:1663) does not exist; the artifact is a `.js` k6 scenario (a path/format drift in TESTING.md).
- **Gap:** The "zero event loss" SLO that TESTING.md attaches to the load scenario is asserted nowhere; the scenario only measures latency and HTTP status. Under load the reconnect path is exactly where eviction and out-of-order delivery surface, so a load scenario that does not check sequence integrity gives false assurance. This is a partial-coverage finding (happy-path latency covered, correctness-under-load uncovered). Target tier7b/tier12 load with per-VU sequence tracking.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the k6 scenario to record per-VU received `SeqNum` sets and assert contiguity after reconnect; tests/testinfra/loadgen conventions apply. Buildable today by extending the existing scenario.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/streaming_reconnect/main.js` so each VU tracks the highest `SeqNum` it received, sends that real value as `Last-Event-ID` on reconnect, and adds a k6 `check` asserting the post-reconnect stream contains no gap below the cursor and no repeated `SeqNum`; correct the TESTING.md filename reference.

No Go test asserts the 512 default or the 64–4096 range bound (grep of `pkg`/`tests` for `sessionEventReplayBufferDepth` returns only the chart files and the spec). No `charts/lenny/tests` helm-unittest asserts the rendered flag value (`charts/lenny/tests/gateway-deployment_test.yaml` exists but carries no case for this flag).

The chart sets 512, so the running default is correct only because the chart always passes the flag, which makes the divergence latent rather than active. This is an assertion/naming-drift finding plus a missing chart unit test. Target tier1 for the range-clamp assertion (out of audit scope) and tier0/chart for the rendered value.

(spec/10_gateway-internals.md:388)

## §10.5 Upgrade and Rollback Strategy <a id="t-10.5"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/10_gateway-internals.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
Component coverage for §10.5 is uneven, though the two largest gaps identified at the 2026-06-03 audit have real, substantial code behind them now. Commit `9aa3b47e` ("F-10.5.1 progress") built the `RuntimeUpgrade` operator surface end to end: a durable per-pool record (Memory and Postgres backends), the `pkg/gateway/upgrade/runtimeupgrade.Manager` driving the linear `Pending→Expanding→Draining→Contracting→Complete` progression plus Pause/Resume/Rollback, the `POST/GET /v1/admin/pools/{name}/upgrade*` endpoints, the `lenny-ctl admin pools upgrade start|proceed|pause|resume|rollback|status` subcommand, and the `lenny_runtime_upgrade_state` gauge family feeding the §16.5 `RuntimeUpgradeStuck` alert. Commit `a6b8bee9` ("F-10.5.14") built the `lenny-sandboxtemplate-deletion-guard` admission webhook that enforces the §10.5 line 508 key safety invariant (old `SandboxTemplate` never deleted while a referencing pool has an active `RuntimeUpgrade`), fail-closed, with unit, tier5 Kind, and tier9 NetworkPolicy coverage landed via proposal 0022. What remains unbuilt is the part that turns the state machine's bookkeeping into an actual rollout: nothing calls into a controller or the warm-pool scaling path to expand the new pool, drain the old one, route a canary split, or auto-advance on a stabilization-window health check; `Rollback`'s "restore old pool" step is a state transition only, with no code that resets `minWarm` or session routing. The database-migration runbook keeps its Phase 1 nullable-column, round-trip, idempotency, rollback, and lenny-migrate-runner coverage, plus a tier8 dirty-flag recovery test on Kind, and the CRD schema-version preflight check is still unit-tested with a fake client. Real Phase 3 (`DROP COLUMN`) migrations now exist in the tree (0118, 0129, 0167 — the last from the §5.2 mode-collapse work), each fronted by the `DO $$` un-migrated-rows gate, but the gate's runtime abort behavior against a real Postgres is still exercised only as a static SQL scan. `migration_upgrade_test.go`, `migration_concurrent`, `pool_upgrade`, and `schema_migration` remain absent or no-op `t.Logf` scaffolds, and the two chaos scaffolds for a stuck rollout and an Expanding-phase rollback still cite controller packages (`pkg/controller/runtimeupgrade`, `pkg/controller/poolscaling`) that do not exist; the real package is `pkg/gateway/upgrade/runtimeupgrade`. The `drainFirst`/`schemaVersion` Phase-3 gating coupling, the expand-contract rolling-deploy with mixed-version replicas, and the controller startup CRD-mismatch hard stop are all still unverified at component tier or above.
Counts: 6 High, 5 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-10.5.1 — RuntimeUpgrade operator surface now exists; controller wiring that executes a rollout (pool scaling, session routing, auto-advance) is still absent, with no integration/e2e coverage [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The `RuntimeUpgrade` state machine is the required mechanism for production runtime upgrades. ... The state machine is surfaced via `GET /v1/admin/pools/{name}/upgrade-status` and managed by `lenny-ctl admin pools upgrade`." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:540, 468)
- **Existing tests:** Commit `9aa3b47e` built the CLI and endpoint this finding originally reported missing: `pkg/ctlcli/main.go` (moved from `cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go` in the pkg/ctlcli extraction) now dispatches `admin pools upgrade start|proceed|pause|resume|rollback|status`, and `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/routes.go` registers `POST/GET /v1/admin/pools/{name}/upgrade*`. `pkg/runtime/upgrade/state/state_test.go` still unit-tests the pure transition enum (unchanged from 2026-06-03). `pkg/gateway/upgrade/runtimeupgrade/runtimeupgrade_test.go` unit-tests the `Manager` (full lifecycle, start validation, pause/resume, rollback from Expanding/Draining, metrics emission) against an in-memory store. `pkg/gateway/upgrade/runtimeupgradestore/runtimeupgradestore_test.go` and `pgstore/pgstore_internal_test.go` cover the record round-trip and version guard (the pgstore test is a pure row-scan unit test, not a real-Postgres component test). `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/pool_upgrade_test.go::TestUpgradeAPI_fullLifecycle_spec_10_5` drives the HTTP surface through `start→proceed(×4)→upgrade-status` and asserts each phase, effectively pinning the `upgrade-status` response schema, but as an in-process handler test rather than a `tests/tier3_contract` case. `tests/tier3_contract/admin_conflict_codes/admin_conflict_codes_test.go` covers the 409 conflict mapping for a second concurrent `upgrade start`. `tests/spec-map.json` §10.5 still lists only the `pkg/runtime/upgrade/state` unit tests and has not been updated for any of the above. No test exists for the `pkg/ctlcli` `pools upgrade` subcommand itself (`grep` of `pkg/ctlcli/*_test.go` for `upgrade` finds only the unrelated §24.15 platform-upgrade and §24.20 answers-file tests). `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/crd_test.go::TestPoolUpgrade` still only asserts the pool-config-validator intercepts UPDATE.
- **Gap:** The state machine is now a real, tested record-and-API layer, but it is bookkeeping only: `Manager.Proceed` advances the stored phase with no check of `idlePodCount >= newPool.minWarm`, no `stabilizationWindowSeconds` wait, and no call into a warm-pool controller or scaling path; `Manager.Rollback`'s Expanding-phase branch is commented "Always allowed: set new pool minWarm 0, restore routing" but executes only a phase transition, not that restoration. `cmd/lenny-gateway/pool_upgrade.go`'s `poolSpecReader` only reads pool specs for the `previousPoolSpec` capture — nothing in the tree calls the `Manager` from a controller or drives real pod/session-routing changes off its state. So no test above the HTTP-handler unit exercises a real Pending→Expanding→Draining→Contracting→Complete rollout with actual new-pod ramp-up, canary session split, or old-pod drain. This is still the core capability of §10.5 unverified as a user journey and as a deployment behavior. Target tiers: tier1/2 for the `pkg/ctlcli` `pools upgrade` subcommand (currently untested), tier4 integration for an orchestration loop that does not yet exist, and tier5 e2e for a full rollout on Kind once that loop is built.
- **Dependencies:** The CLI, endpoint, and durable record now exist (built by `9aa3b47e`); what remains is the orchestration itself — a controller or gateway background loop that reads `Manager` state and drives `SandboxWarmPool.minWarm`, session routing, and the stabilization-window auto-advance check — which is a build task, not a test-only gap. The tier4 harness (`tests/testinfra/gateway`, `tests/testinfra/fakekube`) and the tier5 Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`, `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`) exist.
- **Suggested test:** Add a `pkg/ctlcli` test exercising `pools upgrade start|proceed|pause|rollback|status` against a stub admin API (mirroring the existing `pkg/ctlcli/operability_test.go` pattern for the §24.15 `upgrade` command) to close the untested-CLI gap immediately; once the orchestration loop lands, add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/runtime_upgrade_test.go` driving `lenny-ctl admin pools upgrade start --canary-percent 10` through `proceed` to `Complete` against a two-pool install, asserting new-pool routing and old-pool drain via sessiondriver.

### - [x] T-10.5.2 — RuntimeUpgrade safety invariant (old SandboxTemplate never deleted while upgrade active) is unverified [High] — RESOLVED a6b8bee9 (reconciled by proposal 0022, F-10.5.14)
- **Resolution:** Commit `a6b8bee9` ("F-10.5.14: build the §10.5 SandboxTemplate-deletion guard end to end") built `pkg/admission/webhook.SandboxTemplateDeletionGuard`, a fail-closed `ValidatingAdmissionWebhook` that lists every `SandboxWarmPool` referencing a deleted `SandboxTemplate`, queries the gateway's `GET /internal/runtime-upgrade/active` for each referencing pool, and denies the delete (409) when any pool has an active `RuntimeUpgrade`, or (503) when the reader or gateway probe is unreachable. `pkg/admission/webhook/sandboxtemplate_deletion_guard_test.go` unit-tests the block, allow, unreferenced-template, non-delete-op, and both fail-closed paths (probe error, reader unavailable), plus the multi-pool case. Proposal 0022 then wired the webhook's egress: `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/admission_test.go` (commit `bd5a14a9`) is a tier5 Kind negative-then-positive case that deletes a referenced `SandboxTemplate` and asserts the fail-closed webhook denies it until the `allow-deletion-guard-gateway-egress` NetworkPolicy restores the gateway probe path, and `tests/tier9_security/network_policy_test.go` (commit `c73bde55`) asserts sub-rule (c) narrows that egress to the deletion-guard pods alone. The webhook is deliberately kept in `pkg/preflight/webhooks.go`'s `implementationOnlyValidatingWebhooks` set rather than the §17.2 numbered catalogue (a documented, reviewed divergence, `F-10.5.14` comment at `webhooks.go:127-131,143`), which is an intentional design decision recorded in proposal 0022, not a remaining gap for this finding.

### - [ ] T-10.5.3 — Concurrent-migration advisory-lock guarantee has no component test (declared migration_concurrent suite absent) [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Migrations run as a Kubernetes Job ... The Job acquires a Postgres advisory lock to prevent concurrent migration runs. ... `golang-migrate` uses Postgres advisory locks to prevent concurrent migrations. The lock is released on completion or failure." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:408, 432)
- **Existing tests:** No test found. TESTING.md §13.1 still declares the `migration_concurrent` suite ("Two replicas attempt the same migration simultaneously; dirty-flag lock prevents duplicate apply", TESTING.md:1038) but grep across `tests/`, `pkg/`, and `cmd/` finds no test that runs two simultaneous migrations and asserts the advisory lock serializes them. `tests/tier2_component/migrations/migrations_test.go` still covers single-runner apply, idempotency, and rollback only. `tests/tier8_chaos/config_drift_test.go::TestSchemaMigrationDirtyFlag` still covers dirty-flag recovery but not concurrent contention.
- **Gap:** The advisory-lock serialization is a normative MUST that prevents two gateway replicas (or two migrate Jobs) from corrupting the schema during a rolling deploy. The behavior is exercised in no combination. This is a failure-path/concurrency gap. Target tier: tier2 component against a real Postgres container.
- **Dependencies:** None — buildable today. `tests/testinfra/containers` starts Postgres and the lenny-migrate runner is buildable from `cmd/lenny-migrate`.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier2_component/migrations/concurrent_lock_test.go` (build tag `component`) that launches two `lenny-migrate up` invocations against one Postgres container concurrently, asserts exactly one applies the migration and the other observes the lock or a no-op, and asserts the lock is released on both completion and a forced mid-migration failure.

### - [ ] T-10.5.4 — Full expand-contract rolling deploy with mixed-version replicas is untested (declared schema_migration suite absent) [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Mixed-version replicas must coexist during rollout. ... Phase 2 must not be deployed until all replicas are running Phase 1 code ... Phase 3 must not be deployed until every record that could have been written under the old schema has either been migrated or expired." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:403, 416)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier4_integration/scaffolds_test.go::TestMigrationUpgrade` is still a no-op `t.Logf` that asserts coverage lives in tier2 `prod_schema_test` and `migrations_test` plus tier8 dirty-flag, unchanged from 2026-06-03. TESTING.md §13.1 still declares the `schema_migration` suite (TESTING.md:1080) with no implementation. No test drives an old-version replica issuing `INSERT`s against a Phase 1 schema while a new-version replica writes both columns. Three real Phase 3 migrations now exist in the tree (0118, 0129, 0167), which sharpens rather than closes this gap: the mixed-version write-coexistence window these migrations' Phase 1/2 predecessors create is real and still has no runtime test.
- **Gap:** The mixed-version coexistence invariant is the central correctness property of expand-contract and is only asserted statically (the nullable-column linter in `nullable_columns_test.go`). No runtime test proves an old-version write path and a new-version write path coexist against the intermediate schema, nor that Phase 2 read-switch returns correct data while both code versions run. This is a real deployment-combination and user-journey gap. Target tier: tier4 integration through the compose stack with two gateway versions, or tier5 on Kind with a two-replica Deployment mid-rollout.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a fixture migration set modeling an expand/migrate/contract triple under `tests/testdata/migrations` and a way to run two gateway binaries (old and new) against one Postgres. The compose harness (`tests/testinfra/compose`) and `tests/testinfra/containers` exist; a two-version gateway fixture does not and is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/migration_upgrade_test.go` (the file change-graph.json already references) that applies Phase 1, runs an old-schema writer and a new-schema writer concurrently, applies Phase 2 and asserts reads, then applies Phase 3 and asserts the old column is gone with no data loss.

### - [ ] T-10.5.5 — Phase 3 preflight gate runtime behavior (abort on un-migrated rows, lock held during check) is unverified against Postgres [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Every Phase 3 migration file must begin with a preflight verification block ... aborts the migration with a non-zero exit code if the result is nonzero, emitting: `\"Phase 3 gate failed: <N> un-migrated rows remain ...\"` The advisory lock is held during this check so no concurrent Phase 3 run can bypass it." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:417)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier2_component/migrations/phase3_gate_test.go` is still a static SQL scan (no Postgres, no build tag) that asserts every Phase 3 (`DROP COLUMN`) migration in the tree drops idempotently and is fronted by a `DO $$` block. Unlike 2026-06-03, this is no longer a forward-looking guard against a hypothetical migration: `TestPhase3MigrationsAreGuarded_spec_10_5_417` now names three real Phase 3 migrations it checks (0118, 0129, and the §5.2 mode-collapse 0167), each carrying a `DO $$` gate that counts un-migrated rows (0167's gate is verified by inspection at `migrations/0167_runtime_definitions_execution_mode_service.up.sql:60-90`, gate-index `idx_sandbox_warm_pools_concurrency_style_unmigrated`). Still, no test executes a Phase 3 migration with un-migrated rows present against a real Postgres and asserts the `RAISE EXCEPTION` aborts with a non-zero exit and the documented message, and no test asserts the gate runs inside the same transaction as the DDL. `tests/tier2_component/migrations/prod_columns_test.go` asserts the post-migration column set for 0118/0167 but only on a clean (zero-un-migrated-row) apply, which never exercises the abort branch.
- **Gap:** The gate's runtime semantics (abort on nonzero count, exact error text, transactional non-skippability, lock held during check) are a normative MUST and are exercised only as a regex over SQL text, even though the tree now ships three live Phase 3 migrations this would apply to. This is a failure-path gap. Target tier: tier2 component against a real Postgres container.
- **Dependencies:** None — buildable today. The tree's own 0167 migration (or a small dedicated fixture) can seed a non-NULL `concurrency_style`-equivalent row and run the real up-migration; `tests/testinfra/containers` runs it.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier2_component/migrations/phase3_gate_runtime_test.go` (build tag `component`) that applies migrations through 0166, seeds a row that would trip the 0167 gate, runs 0167 via lenny-migrate, asserts a non-zero exit and the `"Phase 3 gate failed"` message, then migrates the row and asserts the same migration now succeeds and drops the column.

### - [ ] T-10.5.6 — Controller startup CRD schema-version mismatch hard stop is unverified end to end [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "each controller validates on startup that the installed CRD schema version ... matches the version the controller binary expects. If there is a mismatch, the controller logs a `FATAL` error ... and exits with a non-zero code, preventing the Deployment rollout from completing. ... Controllers validate the CRD schema version on startup and will refuse to start (non-zero exit, `CrashLoopBackOff`) if any CRD is still stale at this point." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:439, 451)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/preflight/crdschema_test.go` still unit-tests `CRDSchemaVersionCheck.Decide` against a controller-runtime fake client for pass, missing CRD, missing annotation, and mismatch. `cmd/lenny-controller/main.go` still calls `assertCRDSchemaVersion`, and its only test (`cmd/lenny-controller/main_test.go::TestBuildSchemeRegistersControllerTypes`) still does not exercise the mismatch-causes-exit path. No test starts the controller binary against a cluster carrying a stale CRD annotation and asserts a non-zero exit / `CrashLoopBackOff`; grep of `tests/tier5_e2e_kind` for `CrashLoopBackOff` or `assertCRDSchemaVersion` finds nothing.
- **Gap:** The startup hard stop is the §10.5 defense against silent stale-CRD field stripping during an upgrade, and the binary-level exit and the Deployment-rollout block are not verified. This is a failure-path and deployment-combination gap. Target tiers: tier2 component against envtest for the binary exit, plus tier5 on Kind for the `CrashLoopBackOff` rollout block.
- **Dependencies:** Requires installing a CRD with a deliberately stale `lenny.dev/schema-version` annotation. `tests/testinfra/envtest` and `tests/testinfra/kind` exist; no new infrastructure is required.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier2_component/controller/crd_version_gate_test.go` using `tests/testinfra/envtest` that installs a stale-annotation CRD, runs `assertCRDSchemaVersion` (or the controller `Run`), and asserts a non-zero exit with the line-439 runbook message; add a tier5 case asserting the controller pod enters `CrashLoopBackOff`.

### - [ ] T-10.5.7 — Chaos scaffolds for runtime-upgrade-stuck and pool-rollback still cite nonexistent controller packages; the alert and gauge substrate they need is now real [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "On timeout, remaining sessions are force-terminated with checkpoint. ... From `Expanding`: `lenny-ctl admin pools upgrade rollback` — sets new pool's `minWarm` to 0, restores full routing to old pool, transitions to `Paused`." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:482, 506)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier8_chaos/scaffolds_test.go::TestRuntimeUpgradeStuck` is still a no-op `t.Logf` that cites "pkg/controller/runtimeupgrade (the runtime-upgrade state machine substrate; Phase 3 Done per BUILD-PROGRESS)"; `pkg/controller/runtimeupgrade` still does not exist. The real substrate is `pkg/gateway/upgrade/runtimeupgrade` (built by `9aa3b47e`, see T-10.5.1), which now emits the `lenny_runtime_upgrade_state` gauge family on every durable commit and at startup (`Manager.EmitAll`) so the §16.5 `RuntimeUpgradeStuck` alert (`lenny_runtime_upgrade_state{state=~"expanding|draining|contracting"} == 1` for 10 minutes, `pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:1592-1599`) has a real, non-dead metric behind it, whereas at 2026-06-03 the catalog metric was never emitted. `tests/tier8_chaos/scaffolds_test.go::TestPoolUpgradeRollbackDuringExpanding` is still a no-op `t.Logf` citing "pkg/controller/poolscaling (pool-upgrade state machine)"; that package still has no Expanding/Draining/Contracting/upgrade/rollback logic (see T-10.5.1: `Manager.Rollback`'s Expanding branch is a phase transition only, with no code that resets `minWarm` or routing).
- **Gap:** TESTING.md §12.8 still lists "runtime upgrade stuck" and "pool upgrade rollback during expanding phase" as chaos scenarios. Both scaffolds cite package paths that were never accurate and remain stale even after the real substrate landed under a different path, so the scaffold comments continue to misstate where coverage lives. The live-fault-injection scenarios themselves (stall an Expanding rollout past `stabilizationWindowSeconds` and assert the alert fires; roll back mid-Expanding and assert routing actually reverts) still cannot be built because the alert-triggering "stuck" condition and the rollback's actual `minWarm`/routing reset are not implemented (see T-10.5.1). This is a declared-suite-is-a-scaffold gap with an incorrect citation, gated on T-10.5.1's orchestration work. Target tier: tier8 chaos on Kind once the orchestration lands.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the pool-scaling/session-routing wiring from T-10.5.1 (still absent) and a fault-injection hook to stall a drain. `tests/testinfra/chaos` and `tests/testinfra/kind` exist; building the orchestration is the blocking dependency.
- **Suggested test:** Correct the two scaffold comments to cite `pkg/gateway/upgrade/runtimeupgrade` instead of the nonexistent `pkg/controller/runtimeupgrade`/`pkg/controller/poolscaling`, noting the alert-metric half is now real; once T-10.5.1's orchestration lands, replace the scaffolds with `tests/tier8_chaos/runtime_upgrade_stuck_test.go` that stalls an Expanding rollout past `stabilizationWindowSeconds`, asserts the `RuntimeUpgradeStuck` alert fires, then runs `upgrade rollback` and asserts routing returns to the old pool and the machine reaches `Paused`.

### - [ ] T-10.5.8 — drainFirst / schemaVersion fields are now stored on the RuntimeUpgrade record but still enforce nothing; the Phase-3 gating coupling has no test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Set `drainFirst: true` on the `RuntimeUpgrade` — this forces the state machine to complete `Draining` ... before proceeding to `Contracting`. This ensures no old-schema pod is alive when Phase 3 (contract) runs. ... If `schemaVersion` is set, the gateway blocks Phase 3 migration attempts while `upgradeState != Complete` for the referenced pool." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:499, 502)
- **Existing tests:** No test found. Commit `9aa3b47e` added `DrainFirst` and `SchemaVersion` as stored fields on `runtimeupgradestore.Record` and `runtimeupgrade.Manager`'s `StartOptions`/`Snapshot` (`runtimeupgradestore.go:60-62`, `runtimeupgrade.go:128,141`), and `runtimeupgradestore_test.go` round-trips both fields through the store. But `Manager.Proceed` (`runtimeupgrade.go:224-246`) advances the phase unconditionally on any call regardless of `DrainFirst`, and no code anywhere in `pkg/gateway/upgrade`, `cmd/lenny-migrate`, or the schema-migration endpoints (`pkg/schemamigrate`) reads `SchemaVersion`/`upgradeState` before allowing a Phase 3 migration to proceed. Grep for "blocks Phase 3" and "upgradeState" across `tests/`, `pkg/`, and `cmd/` still returns nothing beyond the stored-field definitions.
- **Gap:** The interaction between a runtime upgrade and a schema migration is a normative coupling that prevents Phase 3 DDL from running while an old-schema pod is alive. The two fields it depends on are now durably stored and round-tripped, but neither is consulted anywhere: `drainFirst` does not force `Draining` to fully complete before `Contracting`, and `schemaVersion` does not block a Phase 3 migration attempt. This is a failure-path gap (running Phase 3 too early corrupts live old-schema pods) that is now closer to buildable than in 2026-06-03 since the fields it needs already exist. Target tiers: tier2 component for the gateway block, tier4 integration for the drainFirst ordering.
- **Dependencies:** Requires `Manager.Proceed` to consult `DrainFirst` before leaving `Draining`, and the Phase 3 migration path (`cmd/lenny-migrate` or `pkg/schemamigrate`) to query the gateway's `RuntimeUpgrade` state for `SchemaVersion`-tagged pools before applying; both are still unbuilt.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/upgrade_schema_gate_test.go` that registers a RuntimeUpgrade with `schemaVersion` set, attempts a Phase 3 migration while `upgradeState` is Draining, asserts the gateway rejects it, advances to Complete, and asserts Phase 3 then succeeds.

No test runs preflight, the `kubectl diff`/`apply`, `kubectl wait --for=condition=Established`, and `helm upgrade` in order against a cluster carrying stale CRDs.
