## §10.6 Environment Resource and RBAC Model <a id="t-10.6"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/10_gateway-internals.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The §10.6 primitives have strong unit coverage in `pkg/environment`, `pkg/gateway/environment/envaccess`, `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin`, `pkg/gateway/sessionserver`, `pkg/gateway/connectors/connectorauthz`, and `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcpruntimes`, plus one Postgres-backed component test (`tests/tier2_component/stores/environmentstore_test.go`) and one tier4 integration test that drives the admin CRUD surface and transparent filtering on the deny-all default. The proposal-0020 package regrouping (C3) relocated most of these packages under `pkg/gateway/environment`, `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric`, `pkg/gateway/externalapi`, `pkg/gateway/connectors`, and `pkg/gateway/runtime` without changing package names or test behavior; file-path citations below are updated to the current locations. Since generation, F-10.6.8 landed the OIDC `introspectionEnabled` real-time group-check subsystem end to end with a middleware-level test suite, closing T-10.6.9. The remaining gaps are unchanged: cross-environment delegation is an empty tier5 scaffold whose composite exercise is on the ops backlog, the declared `tests/tier9_security/rbac/environment_rbac_test.go` suite for OIDC-group member resolution does not exist, the `allow-all` fallback and its cross-tenant isolation guarantee are never exercised through the real gateway, and the `mcpRuntimeFilters` capability tool filtering and the explicit-environment endpoints across the four external interfaces have no component, integration, or wire-contract coverage beyond in-memory handler tests. The `delegation.isolation_violation` audit event with `cross_environment: true` is asserted nowhere and is not pinned against OCSF. Counts (open + resolved): 3 High, 4 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-10.6.1 — Cross-environment delegation has no integration or e2e test; the declared tier5 suite is an empty scaffold [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Effective cross-environment access requires both sides to permit it. Neither side can unilaterally grant the other access." plus the four-step "Gateway enforcement at delegation time" sequence ending in `target_not_in_scope` and `target_not_authorized` (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:627, spec/10_gateway-internals.md:631-637).
- **Existing tests:** The bilateral reachability primitive is unit-tested in `pkg/gateway/environment/envaccess/envaccess_test.go` (`TestCrossEnvironmentReachableBilateral`, `TestCrossEnvironmentReachableWildcardInbound`, `TestCrossEnvironmentUnreachableWithoutBothSides`), and the MCP tool handler that consults it is unit-tested in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/delegate_task_filtering_test.go` (`TestDelegateTaskCrossEnvironmentReachable`, `TestDelegateTaskEnvironmentScope`). The tier5 entry `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/scaffolds_test.go::TestCrossEnvironmentDelegation` (line 298) only calls `kind.InstallLenny(t)` and `t.Logf` that the composite exercise is "on the tier-5 ops backlog." TESTING.md:1796 declares `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/cross_environment_delegation_test.go` and states it is deferred. No tier4 test under `tests/tier4_integration/` exercises cross-environment delegation; `delegation_test.go` contains no environment scoping.
- **Gap:** The bilateral declaration enforcement (steps 2 and 3) and the resulting `target_not_in_scope` rejection are never driven through the real `cmd/lenny-gateway` binary with `lenny/delegate_task` dispatched from an agent pod. This is a real user journey (an agent in environment A delegating to a shared runtime in environment B) and an adversarial scenario (a caller whose environment lacks the outbound declaration, or whose target environment lacks the inbound declaration, attempting to reach a foreign runtime). Target tiers are tier4 integration and tier5 e2e.
- **Dependencies:** Requires `--agent-namespace` wiring on the e2e gateway so sessions land on agent pods, an agent runtime that issues `lenny/delegate_task` from inside the pod, and a seeded pair of environments with a bilateral `crossEnvironmentDelegation` declaration. The tier5 harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`) exists; the agent-namespace-enabled gateway fixture and the delegating runtime do not. Building them is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/cross_environment_delegation_test.go` driving alice in environment `team-a` delegating to a `shared:true` runtime owned by `team-b` through `lenny/delegate_task`, asserting success when both declarations permit it and `target_not_in_scope` when either side's declaration is absent, using `tests/testinfra/kind` and `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`. Add a companion tier4 negative case under `tests/tier4_integration/` that removes the inbound declaration mid-tree and asserts the next `delegate_task` is rejected.

### - [ ] T-10.6.2 — Environment-member RBAC with OIDC-group resolution has no tier9 security test; the declared suite is absent [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Member roles: viewer, creator, operator, admin." and "Identity: OIDC. Groups from LDAP/AD carried as JWT claims." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:605, spec/10_gateway-internals.md:661).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/environment/envaccess/envaccess_test.go` unit-tests `Membership` group and subject matching and highest-role-wins. `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/create_test.go` unit-tests explicit-environment non-member rejection, viewer rejection, and creator admission. `tests/tier9_security/rbac_test.go` exercises the §10.2/§12.9.7 platform role gate (platform-admin, tenant-admin, tenant-viewer) on `/v1/admin/environments` but its own header comment (lines 26-30) states the OIDC-verifier half is "not exercised here," and it does not test the §10.6 member roles at all. TESTING.md:1797 declares `tests/tier9_security/rbac/environment_rbac_test.go` for "OIDC-group resolution against the §10.6 members list" and marks it deferred; the directory `tests/tier9_security/rbac/` does not exist. The in-process OIDC stub added at `tests/testinfra/stubs/oidc` (predating this audit) is explicitly scoped to tier2/tier4 use (its own doc comment: "Use this when a tier-2 component or tier-4 integration test needs an authentication source") and cannot be reached from inside a Kind pod; it does not close this gap.
- **Gap:** The §10.6 member-role enforcement (a `viewer` cannot create a session in an environment, a `creator` can, role escalation by group membership) is verified only in handler unit tests against in-memory stores, never end to end against a real OIDC identity provider whose groups claim drives membership. This is a security control, so its absence at tier9 is a finding. The work is both a real user journey (alice in the `security-engineers` OIDC group reaching only her authorized environment) and an adversarial scenario (a caller forging or lacking the group claim).
- **Dependencies:** Requires a tier9 OIDC fixture that mints JWTs with a `groups` claim and is reachable from inside the Kind cluster (`tests/testinfra/tokenservice` mints tokens but the group-to-member resolution path is not wired into the Kind e2e gateway, which runs in dev mode; the referenced heavier alternative, `tests/testinfra/oidc-real/`, still does not exist). Building the OIDC-in-Kind fixture is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier9_security/rbac/environment_rbac_test.go` that installs Lenny on Kind with an OIDC provider, seeds an environment whose `members` grant `creator` to group `security-engineers`, and asserts a JWT bearing that group creates a session while a JWT lacking it is rejected, using `tests/testinfra/kind` and `tests/testinfra/tokenservice`.

### - [ ] T-10.6.3 — Cross-environment isolation monotonicity violation and its `cross_environment: true` audit event are untested and unpinned against OCSF [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Isolation monotonicity check: Verify the target pool's isolation profile is at least as restrictive as the calling session's minIsolationProfile ... Violation is rejected with ISOLATION_MONOTONICITY_VIOLATED and a delegation.isolation_violation audit event is emitted ... with cross_environment: true." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:636).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/delegate_task_filtering_test.go::TestDelegateTaskPoolIsolationMonotonicity` (lines 239-298) exercises the same-environment variant and explicitly asserts `cross_environment == false`. No test exercises the cross-environment variant. A search of `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/delegation/service_test.go`, `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/delegationpolicystore/`, and `tests/` for `cross_environment` together with `isolation` returns nothing new. `tests/tier3_contract/ocsf_audit/ocsf_audit_test.go` contains no reference to `delegation.isolation_violation` or `cross_environment`.
- **Gap:** The §10.6-specific path (a `sandboxed` session in environment A cross-environment-delegating to a `standard` pool in environment B) is rejected by no test, and the audit event it emits is never validated for the `cross_environment: true` field or pinned against the OCSF schema in the audit conformance suite. This is an adversarial scenario (relaxing isolation across an environment boundary) and a standards-conformance gap (OCSF audit shape). Target tiers are tier4 integration for the rejection and tier3 contract for the OCSF pin.
- **Dependencies:** The same cross-environment delegation fixture as T-10.6.1. The OCSF audit pin can reuse `tests/testinfra/audit` and the existing `tests/tier3_contract/ocsf_audit` harness; that part is buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Extend the cross-environment delegation tier4 test with a case where the target pool is weaker than the caller's `minIsolationProfile`, asserting `ISOLATION_MONOTONICITY_VIOLATED` and a `delegation.isolation_violation` event with `cross_environment: true`. Add a tier3 case under `tests/tier3_contract/ocsf_audit/` that maps that event to its OCSF class and validates required fields.

### - [ ] T-10.6.4 — The allow-all fallback and its cross-tenant isolation guarantee are never exercised through the gateway [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "allow-all: An authenticated user who is not a member of any environment can access any runtime owned by their own tenant ... Runtimes owned by other tenants are never exposed regardless of this setting. Cross-tenant runtime access is architecturally impossible." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:655-656).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/environment/envaccess/envaccess_test.go::TestAuthorizedRuntimesNoMembershipAllowAll` unit-tests the resolver returning all runtimes under allow-all, but the supplied slice is already tenant-scoped, so cross-tenant isolation is asserted by the caller, not the resolver. `tests/tier4_integration/environment_test.go::TestEnvironmentFiltering` starts the gateway with `--no-environment-policy deny-all` only (line 193) and asserts the deny-all path. Several other tier4 tests (`session_lifecycle_test.go`, `idempotency_test.go`, `policy_test.go`, `quota_test.go`, `tokenservice_cutover_test.go`) start the gateway with `--no-environment-policy allow-all` purely to bypass the environment gate as unrelated test setup; none of them seeds a second tenant or asserts a cross-tenant runtime stays hidden. No tier4 or tier5 test starts the gateway with `allow-all` and confirms a non-member sees their own tenant's runtimes while a runtime owned by a second tenant stays hidden.
- **Gap:** The allow-all branch of `noEnvironmentPolicy` and the "cross-tenant access is architecturally impossible" guarantee are not verified end to end. This is both a real user journey (a non-member in an allow-all tenant discovering runtimes) and an adversarial scenario (confirming a second tenant's runtimes are not leaked). Target tier is tier4 integration, ideally tier9 for the cross-tenant isolation assertion.
- **Dependencies:** None — buildable today. The tier4 gateway fixture (`tests/testinfra/gateway`) already supports `--no-environment-policy` and the bootstrap endpoint seeds runtimes for multiple tenants.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier4 case in `tests/tier4_integration/environment_test.go` that starts the gateway with `--no-environment-policy allow-all`, bootstraps runtimes for tenants `acme` and `globex`, and asserts a non-member acme caller sees only acme runtimes on `GET /v1/runtimes` and never a globex runtime.

### - [ ] T-10.6.5 — mcpRuntimeFilters capability-based tool filtering has no component or integration enforcement test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "mcpRuntimeFilters — capability-based tool filtering for type: mcp runtimes. Capabilities inferred from MCP ToolAnnotations ... Name collisions resolved by runtime:tool qualified reference in overrides." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:607).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcpruntimes/capability_filter_test.go` now drives the enforcement path through the real `mcpruntimes` HTTP handler (`h.ServeHTTP` against a `tools/call` JSON-RPC request), asserting a denied tool returns `403 TOOL_CAPABILITY_DENIED` before dispatch, an allowed tool dispatches, an unscoped or unmatched-runtime call is ungated, an unannotated tool fails closed to the admin default, and a `tools/list` call passes through ungated (landed pre-audit in F-10.6.2, commit `8e2788e0`). `pkg/gateway/environment/environmentstore/capability_filter_test.go` unit-tests the underlying `PermitCapabilities`/`PermitTool`/`MCPRuntimeFilterFor` evaluator. `pkg/gateway/runtime/capabilityinference/capabilityinference_test.go` unit-tests the annotation-to-capability inference. `tests/tier2_component/stores/environmentstore_test.go` round-trips the `MCPRuntimeFilters` field through Postgres but does not enforce it. None of these tests registers a real MCP runtime through a live component or integration fixture (all use an in-memory `runtimestore.Runtime` and an in-process handler), and no test exercises a `runtime:tool` qualified override resolving a name collision — that mechanism is unimplemented (a repo-wide search for `runtime:tool` qualified-override handling in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcpruntimes` and `pkg/gateway/environment/environmentstore` returns nothing).
- **Gap:** The enforcement path that maps inferred capabilities to an allow or deny decision on each MCP tool now has handler-level HTTP coverage, narrowing the original gap, but it is still exercised only against in-memory inputs rather than a live component or integration fixture, and the `runtime:tool` qualified-override collision resolution named in the spec has no implementation or test at any tier. This is a real user journey (an agent in the `security-team` environment seeing only `read`/`execute` tools on an MCP runtime) and an authorization boundary whose end-to-end behavior and collision-resolution behavior are unverified. Target tier is tier2 component against a real MCP runtime registration, or tier4 integration.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a `type: mcp` runtime stub that advertises tools with `ToolAnnotations` through a live component or integration fixture. `tests/testinfra/stubs` holds connector and runtime stubs (`tests/testinfra/stubs/runtime`); none currently advertises MCP tools. Building it, and building the `runtime:tool` override-resolution mechanism itself, is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier2_component/gateway_subsystems/mcp_runtime_filter_test.go` (or a tier4 case) that registers a `type: mcp` runtime advertising `read`, `write`, and `delete` tools through a live fixture, attaches an environment whose `mcpRuntimeFilters` deny `write` and `delete`, and asserts the discovered tool set is exactly `read`, plus a collision case resolved by a `runtime:tool` override (once that mechanism exists).

### - [ ] T-10.6.6 — Explicit-environment endpoints across the four external interfaces have no wire-contract test and no integration enforcement test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Explicit environment endpoint (opt-in) — dedicated paths across all external interfaces: /mcp/environments/{name}, /v1/environments/{name}/sessions, scoped model namespace on /v1/responses and /v1/chat/completions." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:557).

This is a standards-conformance gap on the OpenAI Chat Completions and Open Responses surfaces and an integration enforcement gap. Target tiers are tier3 contract for the wire pins and tier4 integration for enforcement.

This is an adversarial and operational scenario (an administrator tightening a bilateral declaration mid-tree). Target tier is tier4 integration, ideally tier5 for the multi-level tree.

### - [x] T-10.6.9 — introspectionEnabled real-time group checks have no component test confirming request-time introspection occurs [Low] — RESOLVED 58020a05
- **Resolution:** Commit `58020a05` ("F-10.6.8: §10.6 OIDC introspectionEnabled real-time group check") built the RFC 7662 introspection subsystem end to end and landed a request-time test suite: `pkg/gateway/middleware/auth/introspection_test.go` wraps the real auth middleware (`Wrap`) with a stub `GroupIntrospector` and asserts, per verified Bearer request, that an enabled tenant's real-time group set replaces the JWT `groups` claim (`TestIntrospectionReplacesJWTGroups_spec_10_6`), a disabled tenant keeps the JWT claim untouched (`TestIntrospectionDisabledKeepsJWTGroups_spec_10_6`), an inactive-token verdict rejects the bearer with 401 (`TestIntrospectionInactiveTokenRejects_spec_10_6`), a transport/config failure fails closed with 503 rather than falling back to the JWT claim (`TestIntrospectionFailsClosedOnError_spec_10_6`), and a nil introspector leaves the JWT-claim path unaffected (`TestNilIntrospectorLeavesGroups_spec_10_6`). This directly exercises the request-time behavior the original finding said was untested (only the storage/config round-trip had been verified before). `pkg/auth/introspection/introspection_test.go` separately covers the RFC 7662 client, the short-TTL config and group caches, and the array/delimited-string group-claim parsing. The suite is package-level (in-process `httptest`, stub introspector) rather than a tier2/tier4 fixture hitting a real introspection endpoint, but it verifies the behavioral effect the finding named, closing the gap.

## §10.7 Experiment Primitives <a id="t-10.7"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/10_gateway-internals.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The §10.7 experiment primitives have dense unit coverage in `pkg/experiment` (bucketing, validation, propagation, anonymous handling) and dense handler-level coverage in `pkg/gateway/sessionserver`, `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin`, `pkg/gateway/experiment/experimentsticky`, and `pkg/gateway/experiment/ofrep`, plus real-Postgres component tests (`evalstore_test.go`, and the newly landed `tests/tier2_component/evalaggregates/eval_aggregates_test.go` for the `lenny_eval_aggregates` materialized view). Coverage falls off sharply above the handler tier: the declared tier4 integration suite is a log-only scaffold, the only tier7b Kind exercise is `t.Skip`-ped, and no tier5, tier6, tier8, tier9, or tier10 test drives the experiment lifecycle, eval ingestion, OFREP targeting, or the isolation fail-closed path against a real cluster, real Redis outage, or a conforming runtime. The admin and eval REST surfaces still have no contract test pinning request and response bodies against the OpenAPI schema (the OpenAPI completeness test checks path presence only). The external-targeting integration (OFREP, LaunchDarkly, Statsig, Unleash) has no cloud-provider parity row and no live conformance check, and the adapter manifest `experimentContext` delivery is never verified through a runtime in the conformance battery. The §10.7 refactor under proposal 0020 relocated several backing packages (`pkg/gateway/admin` → `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin`, `pkg/gateway/ofrep` → `pkg/gateway/experiment/ofrep`, `pkg/gateway/openapi` → `pkg/gateway/externalapi/openapi`) without changing test substance; file-path citations below are updated to the new locations. The `lenny_eval_aggregates` materialized-view path (T-10.7.15) is now resolved by F-10.7.12's landed migration and tests.
Counts: 5 High, 7 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-10.7.1 — ExperimentRouter has no integration test through the live gateway; the declared suite is a log-only scaffold [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`ExperimentRouter` as built-in `RequestInterceptor`" and "When a session is enrolled in an experiment, its `experimentContext` ... is delivered to the runtime in the adapter manifest." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:682, 680)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/experimentrouter_test.go` exercises enrollment, OFREP, and multi-eligible-skipped, but it constructs the server with `memstore.New()` and `experimentstore.NewMemory()` (in-memory stores, no real backing services), so it runs at the unit tier. `tests/tier4_integration/scaffolds_test.go:176` `TestExperimentRouting` still only calls `t.Logf` and asserts nothing. TESTING.md:1806 still explicitly records `tests/tier4_integration/experiment_routing_test.go` as deferred. No test exercises the interceptor through the compose stack with Postgres-backed experiment and session stores.
- **Gap:** The ExperimentRouter interceptor wiring at PreRoute priority (the user journey where alice's session at acme is enrolled, routed onto a variant pool, and the `experimentContext` is written to the session record and adapter manifest) is unverified above the handler tier. This is a real user-journey gap at tier4. The declared suite is an empty scaffold, which is itself a reportable inconsistency.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier4 compose stack with real Postgres and the gateway binary (`tests/testinfra/inproc/gateway.go` or the compose harness). Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/experiment_routing_test.go` driving `POST /v1/admin/experiments` then `POST /v1/sessions` through the live gateway against real Postgres, asserting the session record carries the expected `experimentContext` and `RuntimeRef`/`PoolRef`, using `tests/testinfra/inproc` and `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`.

### - [ ] T-10.7.2 — No Kind or cloud end-to-end test routes a session to a real variant pod or exercises variant-pool lifecycle on status transition [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "PoolScalingController manages variant pool lifecycle automatically" and the transition table that sets variant pool `minWarm`/`maxWarm` to 0 on `paused`/`concluded` and restores them on re-activation. (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:1091, 1097-1103)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier7b_load_kind/experiment_test.go:45` `TestExperimentLoad` calls `kind.InstallLenny` then `t.Skip` with a phase-gate diagnosis; it never runs the bucketing or variant-pool path. `pkg/controller/poolscaling/variants_test.go` covers `ResolveVariantRoles` weight math at the unit tier with no Kubernetes. No tier5 or tier6 test creates an experiment, claims a variant pod, transitions the experiment, and asserts the `SandboxWarmPool` CRD `minWarm`/`maxWarm` and the base-pool recomputation against a real PoolScalingController.
- **Gap:** The core capability of routing real sessions onto a variant warm pool and the controller's drain-on-conclude and restore-on-reactivate behavior are unverified end to end. This is both a real user journey (an operator rolling out claude-worker-v2 to 10% of traffic) and a controller-reconciliation gap, targeted at tier5 (Kind) and tier6 (cloud).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`) with the runtime, pool, and experiment stores seeded, plus a registered variant pool referencing a real `SandboxTemplate`. The e2e overlay seeding an active experiment does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/experiment_lifecycle_test.go` that seeds an active experiment via the admin API, creates sessions until one lands on the variant pool, PATCHes the experiment to `paused` then `concluded`, and asserts the variant `SandboxWarmPool` CRD `minWarm` and `maxWarm` and the deletion-on-conclude using `tests/testinfra/kind` and `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`.

### - [ ] T-10.7.3 — Admin experiment and eval REST surfaces have no contract test pinning request and response bodies against the OpenAPI schema [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** The eval submission request body, the `EvalResult` schema, the Results API default response, and the `BreakdownResponse` schema. (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:911-927, 891-907, 955-1008, 1010-1085)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/externalapi/openapi/completeness_test.go:67` `TestDocumentMatchesRegisteredEndpoints` (moved from `pkg/gateway/openapi/openapi_test.go`'s former `TestDocumentMatchesEndpoints`) still asserts only that the registered route templates, including `/v1/sessions/{id}/eval`, `/v1/admin/experiments`, `/v1/admin/experiments/{name}`, and `/v1/admin/experiments/{name}/results`, appear in the served document (`documented[stripWildcard(route)]`) — path presence, not body schema. `tests/tier3_contract/rest_sessions/unexercised_endpoints_test.go:156` still only asserts the eval endpoint returns a backend-unavailable error. The aggregation, matview-routing, and breakdown response shapes are asserted only in `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/experiment_results_test.go` (moved from `pkg/gateway/admin/experiment_results_test.go`) against Go structs, not against the published OpenAPI schema.
- **Gap:** The wire format of the eval submission, the Results API aggregate response, and the `BreakdownResponse` is never validated against the OpenAPI document at tier3. A regression that diverges the served JSON from the documented schema would ship undetected. This is a standards-conformance gap against the gateway's own published contract.
- **Dependencies:** Requires an OpenAPI schema validator over live responses. `tests/testinfra/inproc` plus an OpenAPI validation helper; the validator does not exist as a shared building block yet and building it is part of this finding. (`cmd/lenny-compliance/schemavalidate_test.go` validates schema-battery output generically but is not wired to the experiment/eval endpoints.)
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/rest_admin/experiments_eval_test.go` that posts an eval and fetches `/results` (default and `breakdown_by`) through the in-process gateway and validates each request and response body against the schema component in `pkg/gateway/externalapi/openapi`.

### - [ ] T-10.7.4 — The adapter-manifest `experimentContext` delivery is never verified through a conforming runtime [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "its `experimentContext` (containing `experimentId`, `variantId`, and `inherited` flag) is delivered to the runtime in the adapter manifest" and "Runtimes can use this context to tag their traces with variant metadata." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:680)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/adapter/manifest_test.go:236` `TestWriteManifestWithExperimentContext` asserts the writer serializes the field at the unit tier. The tier10 conformance battery in `tests/tier10_conformance/scaffolds_test.go` and `cmd/lenny-compliance/full.go` exercise the MCP nonce handshake, lifecycle channel, checkpoint, and credential rotation, but no compliance check asserts that a runtime reads `experimentContext` from the manifest it is handed (no "experiment" reference exists anywhere in `cmd/lenny-compliance`).
- **Gap:** The runtime-adapter contract for experiment context delivery has no conformance test. The fidelity claim that runtimes receive `experimentId`/`variantId`/`inherited` is unverified against the three test runtimes and the nine reference runtimes. This is a runtime-adapter conformance gap at tier10.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a compliance check in `cmd/lenny-compliance` and a reference runtime that echoes the manifest `experimentContext` back over the lifecycle channel. The check and the echo behavior do not exist yet; building them is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add an `experiment_context_delivery` check to the Standard or Full battery in `cmd/lenny-compliance/full.go` that seeds a manifest with a populated `experimentContext`, runs delegation-echo, and asserts the runtime reports the same `experimentId`, `variantId`, and `inherited` it read.

### - [ ] T-10.7.5 — The `eval_results` RLS write-rejection and the Results API blinding rule have no security-tier test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Required for RLS ... The `lenny_tenant_guard` trigger validates this field on every INSERT." and "Implementers MUST NOT add fields (e.g., `first_enrolled_at`, `last_eval_at`) that expose per-variant temporal ordering." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:896, 1089)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier2_component/stores/evalstore_test.go:49` `TestEvalResultStoreContract` asserts cross-tenant reads do not leak (subtest "count and list are oldest-first and tenant-scoped"), but it does not drive a cross-tenant INSERT that the `lenny_tenant_guard` trigger must reject. `tests/tier9_security/tenant_isolation_test.go:50` `TestTenantIsolationCrossStore` probes the audit-events store reachable through the admin API but does not name `eval_results`. `tests/tier4_integration/rls_tenant_guard_test.go` exercises the missing-`SET LOCAL` rejection and a cross-tenant `SELECT` on the `sessions` table only, not `eval_results` and not a mismatched-`tenant_id` INSERT. No test asserts the Results API response omits temporal fields (`grep` for `first_enrolled_at`/`last_eval_at` across the repo returns no hits at all, including in tests).
- **Gap:** The security control that the `lenny_tenant_guard` trigger rejects a mismatched `tenant_id` on `eval_results` INSERT is unverified end to end at tier9, and the blinding invariant (a MUST NOT) that the Results API never leaks per-variant enrollment timing has no test. Both are adversarial gaps: a hostile or buggy caller writing across tenants, and an implementer adding a leaking field. Targeted at tier9.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier9 security harness with real Postgres and the RLS trigger applied (`tests/testinfra/security`, `tests/testinfra/envtest`). Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier9_security/eval_rls_test.go` that attempts an `eval_results` INSERT whose `tenant_id` differs from the transaction's `app.current_tenant` and asserts the trigger rejects it, plus a tier3 assertion that the `/results` response JSON contains no `first_enrolled_at` or `last_eval_at` key.

### - [ ] T-10.7.6 — No chaos test covers PoolScalingController-down during an experiment status transition [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "If the PoolScalingController is down during an experiment transition, the variant pool retains its pre-transition scaling parameters until the controller recovers and reconciles — the `PoolConfigDrift` alert ... fires in this scenario." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:1105)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier8_chaos/config_drift_test.go:48` `TestPoolConfigDrift` still exercises the `lenny-pool-config-validator` admission-webhook rejection of a `minWarm <= maxWarm` violation generally, but no chaos test transitions an experiment while the PoolScalingController is unavailable and asserts the variant pool retains its pre-transition `minWarm`/`maxWarm` and that `PoolConfigDrift` fires.
- **Gap:** The failure-path behavior on controller outage during a transition is unverified. This is a resilience and recovery gap at tier8 (an operator concludes an experiment while the controller is down and expects the pool to drain only after recovery).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier8 chaos harness able to pause the PoolScalingController and a seeded active experiment (`tests/testinfra/chaos`, `tests/testinfra/kind`). The experiment-seeding overlay does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier8_chaos/experiment_transition_controller_down_test.go` that scales the controller to zero, PATCHes an experiment to `concluded`, asserts the variant CRD parameters are unchanged and `PoolConfigDrift` fires, then restores the controller and asserts the drain completes.

### - [ ] T-10.7.7 — The OpenFeature targeting circuit breaker and fail-open hot path are not exercised under a real provider outage [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Under sustained failures, repeated 200ms waits at each session creation ... reduce throughput significantly. A per-tenant circuit breaker prevents this cascade" and "On OpenFeature client timeout or error ... no experiment assignment is made ... The session proceeds with the base runtime." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:834-838, 832)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/targetingbreaker_test.go` drives the breaker state machine with a `fakeClock` at the unit tier, and `experimentrouter_breaker_test.go:26` `TestExperimentTargetingCircuitBreakerSkipsOFREPWhenOpen_spec_10_7_835` asserts the router skips OFREP when the breaker is open using an `httptest` server. No integration or load test exercises session creation under a genuinely slow or down OFREP provider and asserts that throughput holds and sessions fall through to the base runtime. No `experiment_targeting_outage` (or similarly named) scenario exists under `tests/tier7a_load_local/scenarios/`.
- **Gap:** The throughput-protection behavior the circuit breaker exists to guarantee is verified only against a settable fake clock, not under a real failing dependency on the session-creation hot path. This is a failure-path and load gap at tier4 or tier7 (an OFREP outage at acme should not collapse session-creation throughput).
- **Dependencies:** Requires an OFREP stub that injects timeouts and a load generator on the session-creation path (`tests/testinfra/stubs`, `tests/testinfra/loadgen`). The fault-injecting OFREP stub does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier7a_load_local/scenarios/experiment_targeting_outage/scenario.go` that points a tenant at a stub OFREP endpoint returning 250ms+ delays, drives sustained session creation, and asserts the breaker opens, throughput stays above the floor, and every session runs the base runtime.

## §11.1 Admission and Fairness <a id="t-11.1"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/11_policy-and-controls.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§11.1 defines five admission and fairness controls (request rate limits, concurrent-session limits, active delegated children, concurrent uploads, and upload size) with named granularities, plus the normative `noEnvironmentPolicy` access-path default and its startup-validation requirement. The behavioral surface has dense unit and handler-level coverage in `pkg/gateway/middleware/ratelimit`, `pkg/gateway/sessionserver` (admission_ratelimit_test.go, concurrency_limits_test.go, create_test.go, upload_limits_test.go), and `cmd/lenny-gateway/main_test.go`, and the controls are fully wired into the gateway binary through flags. Coverage at tier2 and above is thin: the only tier2 component test (`tests/tier2_component/ratelimit/ratelimit_test.go`) exercises the bare Redis counter mechanics rather than the scope-keyed middleware, no tier3 contract test pins the `X-RateLimit-*` triplet or the `RATE_LIMITED` envelope across the REST, MCP, and OpenAI surfaces, no tier4 integration test drives the §11.1 request-rate or concurrency limits through the binary (the existing quota integration test covers §11.2 token budgets only), no tier5/tier6 e2e test exercises admission fairness on a real cluster, the `gateway-rate-limit-storm` chaos runbook entry maps to a generic store-outage test that asserts none of the §11.1 fail-open behavior, and the spec-map.json `pkg/policy/admission` package and the `tests/tier8_chaos/redis_down_during_policy_check.go` suite named in TESTING.md do not exist on disk. The deny-all admission default is verified only at the REST handler level and is never exercised as a security boundary end to end. Counts: 3 High, 5 Medium, 1 Low, 2 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-11.1.1 — §11.1 request-rate limit has no integration test through the gateway binary and no contract test for its wire surface [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Rate limits (requests/min) | Global, per-user, per-runtime, per-pool" (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:7), enforced by the §11.1 middleware that "increments a global, a per-user, and a per-tenant request counter on every API request and rejects with 429 RATE_LIMITED once a scope's count exceeds its configured per-minute limit" (pkg/gateway/middleware/ratelimit/ratelimit.go:3).
- **Existing tests:** The middleware is exercised only by in-process unit tests in `pkg/gateway/middleware/ratelimit/` (ratelimit_test.go, headers_test.go, hijack_test.go, failopen_integration_test.go — the last is in package `ratelimit_test` with no `//go:build` integration tag and uses a fake `togglingCounter`, so it is tier1). The single tier2 entry `tests/tier2_component/ratelimit/ratelimit_test.go` tests the bare `redisstore` counter (within-window accumulation, minute reset, atomic increment) and never constructs the middleware or its scopes. The middleware is wired into the binary at cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:4779 with `--rate-limit-global-per-min`, `--rate-limit-per-user-per-min`, and `--rate-limit-per-tenant-per-min` flags, but no tier4 test sets a limit and drives requests through `cmd/lenny-gateway`. spec-map.json §11.1 lists only `tests/tier2_component/ratelimit/...`. No tier3 contract test was found under tests/tier3_contract for the `RATE_LIMITED` envelope or the `X-RateLimit-*` triplet.
- **Gap:** The end-to-end request-rate admission path (counter increment, scope comparison, 429 emission, header triplet, Retry-After) is never verified through the running binary against real Redis, and the wire surface (the `RATE_LIMITED` error body and the `X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset` headers that §15.1 mandates) is never pinned as a contract. The work covers a real user journey (a client driven past its per-minute budget receives a well-formed 429 with backoff hints) and a wire-format conformance check. Target tiers: tier4 integration and tier3 contract.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The gateway-subprocess harness `tests/testinfra/gateway` and the Redis container helper `tests/testinfra/containers` already back the §11.2 quota integration test.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/ratelimit_test.go that starts `cmd/lenny-gateway` with `--rate-limit-per-user-per-min=2` against `tests/testinfra/containers.StartRedis`, drives three requests as one principal, and asserts the third returns 429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After` and the `X-RateLimit-*` triplet; add tests/tier3_contract/rest_ratelimit/ratelimit_test.go pinning the error envelope and header names.

### - [ ] T-11.1.2 — §11.1 fail-open admission behavior under Redis outage is unverified at tier2+ and the chaos runbook entry asserts none of it [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "A counter error fails open: §11.1 admission must not block traffic on a transient counter outage" (pkg/gateway/middleware/ratelimit/ratelimit.go:20); after the per-episode cap the middleware "switch[es] to fail-closed and rejects requests with 429 until the counter recovers" (pkg/gateway/middleware/ratelimit/ratelimit.go:53). The §11.1 controls back the §12.4 per-replica fail-open ceiling and cumulative timer.
- **Existing tests:** The fail-open and fail-closed edges are covered in-process by `pkg/gateway/middleware/ratelimit/failopen_integration_test.go` (tier1, fake counter). The `gateway-rate-limit-storm` chaos scenario in tests/tier8_chaos/runbook-map.yaml:327 maps to `TestRedisClusterDegraded` (tests/tier8_chaos/store_failure_test.go:81), whose helper `assertStoreOutageDegrades` (store_failure_test.go:312) asserts only generic store-outage degradation (health probe stays green, runbook ref `redis-failure`); a grep of tier8 chaos Go files for `rate`, `ratelimit`, `quota`, `failopen`, `429`, or `RATE_LIMITED` returns nothing. TESTING.md:1641 explicitly states `tests/tier8_chaos/redis_down_during_policy_check.go` "is deferred," and the file does not exist on disk.
- **Gap:** The security-relevant degraded-mode behavior (admission continues fail-open during a real Redis outage, the per-replica ceiling bounds drift, and the gateway transitions to fail-closed after `rateLimitFailOpenMaxSeconds`) is never exercised against a real Redis instance that the chaos harness disables and restores. The work is a failure-path and resilience scenario. Target tiers: tier8 chaos, with a tier2 component test against real Redis as a lower-cost precursor.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a Redis instance the chaos harness can take down. The Kind chaos harness `tests/testinfra/kind` and the store-outage helpers already exist; the deferred file TESTING.md names is the missing infrastructure and building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier8_chaos/rate_limit_redis_outage_test.go that drives steady request traffic, scales the Redis datastore to zero via `tests/testinfra/kind`, asserts requests keep admitting (fail-open) with the `lenny_rate_limit_failopen_active` gauge raised, holds the outage past the cap to observe the fail-closed 429, and asserts recovery on Redis restore; add tests/tier2_component/ratelimit/middleware_failopen_test.go wrapping the real `redisstore` counter and toggling the container.

### - [ ] T-11.1.3 — `noEnvironmentPolicy` deny-all admission gate is verified only at the REST handler level, never end to end as a security boundary or across the MCP and OpenAI surfaces [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Admission of a session that does not name an environment is governed by the tenant's `noEnvironmentPolicy` setting (platform default `deny-all` ...)." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:13)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/create_test.go:805-882` covers the deny-all rejection (403 FORBIDDEN with reason `no_environment_policy_deny_all`), the allow-all admission, the env-member admission, and the empty-tenant-policy default, all with `httptest` and `memstore` (tier1). `tests/tier4_integration/environment_test.go:173` (`TestEnvironmentFiltering`) starts the binary with `--no-environment-policy deny-all` but asserts only §10.6 discovery filtering of `GET /v1/runtimes`; it never issues a `POST /v1/sessions` under deny-all to assert the admission rejection through the binary. No MCP `lenny/create_session` or OpenAI session-creation test exercises the deny-all gate (no openai/responses session-create admission directory exists under pkg/gateway).
- **Gap:** The deny-all default is an authorization boundary, and its enforcement at session creation is never verified end to end through the running gateway, nor on the MCP and OpenAI surfaces that route through the same creation path. An adversarial journey (a caller with no environment membership is denied a session under the platform default) and a deployment-combination gap (REST verified at handler level only; MCP and OpenAI unverified) are both present. Target tiers: tier4 integration and tier9 security, with tier3 contract for the cross-surface envelope.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The `tests/testinfra/gateway` subprocess harness and the existing `environment_test.go` admin-bootstrap helpers cover the setup.
- **Suggested test:** Extend tests/tier4_integration/environment_test.go (or add admission_test.go) to start the gateway with `--no-environment-policy deny-all`, issue `POST /v1/sessions` with no environment as a non-member principal, and assert 403 FORBIDDEN with the policy reason; add an MCP `lenny/create_session` case driving the same rejection so the gate is confirmed surface-independent.

### - [ ] T-11.1.4 — Per-runtime and per-pool admission rate limits are tested only with an in-memory counter, never cross-replica against real Redis [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Rate limits (requests/min) | Global, per-user, per-runtime, per-pool" (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:7); the per-runtime and per-pool scopes "are enforced on the session-creation path where the runtime and pool are known (sessionserver requireAdmissionRateLimit, F-11.1.2)" (pkg/gateway/middleware/ratelimit/ratelimit.go:16).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/admission_ratelimit_test.go` covers per-runtime rejection, per-runtime isolation, per-pool rejection, fail-open, nil-counter pass-through, and empty-runtime skip, but every case constructs `rlcounter.NewMemory()` (admission_ratelimit_test.go:81) rather than the Redis-backed `redisstore`. The gateway wires `AdmissionRateLimitCounter` to the Redis counter at cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:3247 with `--rate-limit-per-runtime-per-min` and `--rate-limit-per-pool-per-min` flags.
- **Gap:** In an HA multi-replica deployment the per-runtime and per-pool caps are only meaningful when the counter is shared across replicas through Redis. That cross-replica counting is never exercised at tier2 or in integration; the in-memory counter masks any per-replica divergence. The work is a deployment-combination gap (HA multi-replica gateway with a shared Redis counter). Target tiers: tier2 component and tier4 integration.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. `tests/testinfra/containers.StartRedis` and the `redisstore` constructor are in place.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier2_component/ratelimit/admission_scopes_test.go that builds two `sessionserver.Server` instances sharing one `redisstore` counter, issues creates for the same runtime through both, and asserts the per-runtime cap binds across the two instances; mirror with a tier4 case starting two gateway subprocesses against one Redis container.

### - [ ] T-11.1.5 — Concurrent-session admission caps run their COUNT queries only against memstore, never against real Postgres at tier2 [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Concurrency limits (active sessions) | Global, per-user, per-team, per-runtime" (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:8); `requireConcurrencyLimits` enforces the global, per-user, and per-runtime scopes via `CountActiveSessions` / `CountActiveSessionsByUser` / `CountActiveSessionsByRuntime` (pkg/gateway/sessionserver/quota.go:132).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/concurrency_limits_test.go` covers the per-runtime, per-user, and global caps and the zero-is-unlimited case, all against `memstore.New()` (concurrency_limits_test.go:32). The pgstore implementations of these COUNT methods exist (pkg/gateway/sessionstore/pgstore/pgstore.go) but no tier2 component test drives the concurrency admission path against the real Postgres-backed counts.
- **Gap:** The admission decision depends on indexed COUNT queries that filter live (non-terminal) sessions; the memstore counts and the Postgres counts can diverge (index coverage, terminal-state filtering, tenant scoping). The Postgres-backed admission path is unverified at tier2. The work is a deployment-combination gap (single and HA Postgres backing the concurrency caps). Target tier: tier2 component.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The envtest or Postgres-container harness under `tests/testinfra/envtest` and `tests/tier2_component/stores` already back the sessionstore pgstore tests.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier2_component/stores/concurrency_admission_test.go that seeds running and terminal sessions in real Postgres, wires a `sessionserver.Server` to the pgstore, and asserts the per-user and per-runtime caps reject at the boundary while terminal rows do not count.

### - [ ] T-11.1.6 — Gateway readiness refusal when `noEnvironmentPolicy` is missing is unit-tested as a pure function but never verified as deployment behavior [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The platform-level value is a required configuration key: the gateway validates that `noEnvironmentPolicy` is set to either `deny-all` or `allow-all` during startup and refuses to become ready if the key is missing. ... This closes the misconfigured-Helm gap where an omitted value could otherwise leave admission under undefined behavior." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:13)

The Helm template renders `--no-environment-policy={{ .Values.global.noEnvironmentPolicy }}` unconditionally (charts/lenny/templates/gateway-deployment.yaml:327), and the helm unit test asserts the rendered flag value (charts/lenny/tests/gateway-deployment_test.yaml:63-81) — tier0. No test starts the binary with the key omitted to assert the process exits non-zero / refuses readiness, and no helm/tier5 test renders a chart with the value stripped to confirm the resulting empty flag fails startup rather than admitting under undefined behavior.

That refusal is never exercised end to end. The work is a failure-path deployment scenario. Target tiers: tier4 integration (process exits non-zero with the `LENNY_CONFIG_MISSING` marker) and tier5 e2e on Kind (the pod never becomes Ready when the chart value is stripped).
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. `tests/testinfra/gateway` can launch the binary with the flag omitted; the Kind harness `tests/testinfra/kind` covers the chart-render path.

- **Spec/Doc:** "Concurrent uploads | Per-session, global" and "Upload size | Per-file, per-session" (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:10-11). Whether the Lenny `RATE_LIMITED` envelope is correctly translated for those surfaces is a standards-conformance question that is unverified. ## §11.2 Budgets and Quotas <a id="t-11.2"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/11_policy-and-controls.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§11.2 has grown substantially since the 2026-06-03 audit. Three proposals landed against this unit: 0023 relocated the §8.6 budget-exhaustion lease-extension trigger into the gateway LLM Proxy and scoped it to proxy mode, changing the mid-session token-budget termination contract (T-11.2.5, T-11.2.13 rewritten to match); 0024 defined the direct-mode runtime-adapter usage frame and wired the gateway's usage poller plus the `lenny_gateway_token_usage_anomaly_total` detector, closing most of the untested-anomaly-metric half of T-11.2.3; and 0025 adopted a real per-tenant Postgres sequence with a length-bounded, safe-derived name for billing (and audit) sequencing, closing T-11.2.12 with a genuine concurrent-writer test. Independently, a `close-build-gaps` batch (commit `91b3f584`) implemented the previously wholly-absent billing event delivery sinks (webhook HMAC-SHA256, message queue) with solid unit coverage, resolving T-11.2.1, though the message-queue sink's broker driver is unwired in production (new finding T-11.2.17). A `pkg/gateway` reorganization (proposal 0020) moved several packages this section cites (`billingstore`→`billing/billingstore`, `correctionstore`→`billing/correctionstore`, `admin`→`externalapi/admin`, `storagequota`→`quota/storagequota`, `quotacheckpoint`→`quota/quotacheckpoint`, `treebudget`→`mcpfabric/delegationtree/treebudget`); findings citing the old paths are updated in place. The remaining open findings are largely unchanged in substance: the two-tier Redis-stream billing failover is still miniredis-only (T-11.2.2), the storage-quota GC-decrement ordering is still verified only with a fake releaser (T-11.2.4), the declared Kind and chaos quota suites are still absent (T-11.2.5, T-11.2.10), `TestQuotaRecovery` still pre-computes the MAX rule rather than exercising the gateway's own reconciler (T-11.2.6), soft-warning billing emission and the metering replay wire contract remain untested (T-11.2.7, T-11.2.11), billing-correction dual-control is still unit-only (T-11.2.8), the cloud billing-export scaffold still asserts nothing (T-11.2.9), delegation-budget reservation and recovery are still unverified through a real `delegate_task` call (T-11.2.14), the conditional-field wire contract is still verified only at the store layer (T-11.2.15), and spec-map.json still both undercounts and overclaims §11.2 coverage, now with a different set of undercounted tests (T-11.2.16).
Counts: 6 High, 7 Medium, 3 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [x] T-11.2.1 — Billing event delivery sinks (webhook HMAC-SHA256, message queue) have no implementation or component test [High] — RESOLVED 91b3f584
- **Resolution:** A `close-build-gaps` batch built the previously-absent §11.2.1 delivery-sink surface (BUILD-GAPS F-11.2.14, CLOSED). New `pkg/gateway/billing/billingsink` package: `WebhookSink` POSTs each event as JSON with an `X-Lenny-Signature: sha256=<hmac>` header (HMAC-SHA256 over the exact body), retries with exponential backoff, and dead-letters after the attempt budget is exhausted (`TestWebhookSink_SignsAndDelivers_spec_11_2_1_136`, `TestWebhookSink_RetriesThenSucceeds_spec_11_2_1_136`, `TestWebhookSink_DeadLettersOnExhaustion_spec_11_2_1_136` in `pkg/gateway/billing/billingsink/billingsink_test.go`); `QueueSink` publishes through an injected `QueuePublisher` with the same retry/dead-letter contract (`TestQueueSink_DeliversAndRetries_spec_11_2_1_137`); `Publisher` fans an event out to all configured sinks for the "Both" redundancy mode (`TestPublisher_FansOutToAllSinks_spec_11_2_1_138`). A `Publishing` store decorator (`pkg/gateway/billing/billingsink/publishing.go`) wraps the durable primary billing store so delivery fires only after the synchronous Postgres `Append` confirms and not at all on a failed write (`TestPublishing_PublishesAfterAppend_spec_11_2_1_137`, `TestPublishing_DoesNotPublishOnAppendError_spec_11_2_1_137`), verifying the Postgres-write-before-publish ordering the original gap named. `cmd/lenny-gateway/billingsink.go` wires the webhook sink from `billing.deliverySink.webhookURL` plus a `secretKeyRef` secret in production; the message-queue sink is a tested interface with no broker driver wired yet (tracked separately as T-11.2.17). The 17 unit tests use an injectable `httpDoer`/`QueuePublisher` rather than a live network stub, which is a lighter test double than the tier2/tier3 shape the original finding suggested, but they exercise the real HMAC computation, the real retry/backoff loop, and the real ordering decorator, closing the "no implementation or component test" gap this finding named.

### - [ ] T-11.2.2 — Two-tier billing failover (Redis stream consumer group, XAUTOCLAIM dedup) is tested only against miniredis, never real Redis plus Postgres [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "On Postgres write failure, the gateway publishes the billing event to the Redis stream via `XADD` ... A background flusher goroutine per tenant consumes the Redis stream via a consumer group ... the flusher uses `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, stream_entry_id) DO NOTHING` ... This prevents duplicate billing records from reclaimed entries." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:144)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/billing/billingstore/failover/failover_test.go` (moved from `pkg/gateway/billingstore/failover/` by the §11 pkg/gateway reorganization) exercises the tier-routing state machine with a `MemStream` fake (`TestFailoverRoutesToStreamTier`, `TestFailoverFallsThroughToBufferWhenStreamDown`, `TestStreamDrainReplaysToPrimary`). `pkg/gateway/billing/billingstore/failover/redisstream/purge_test.go` and `streammaxlen_test.go` use `miniredis`. None of these carry a `//go:build component` tag and none run against a real Redis stream consumer group or a real Postgres unique constraint.
- **Gap:** The billing-consistency mechanism that the spec calls out as eliminating the crash-during-failover gap is unverified end to end. No test drives `XADD` then `XREADGROUP` then `XAUTOCLAIM` against a real Redis container with two consumers (two replica identities), crashes one consumer after a flush but before `XACK`, and asserts the `ON CONFLICT` deduplication produces no duplicate billing row in real Postgres. This is the adversarial failure path (replica crash mid-failover) and a multi-replica concurrency scenario.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier2 real-Redis container (tests/testinfra/containers `StartRedis`) and the real-Postgres store harness already used by billingstore_test.go. None — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier2_component/billing_failover/redisstream_dedup_test.go starting a real Redis and Postgres, simulating a Postgres outage, writing events through two consumer identities, killing one mid-flush, and asserting `XAUTOCLAIM` plus `ON CONFLICT` yields exactly-once billing rows in `stream_seq` order.

### - [ ] T-11.2.3 — Proxy-mode authoritative accounting under a hostile under-reporting runtime is unverified end to end through a real gateway and Redis [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`ReportUsage` calls from the pod adapter are ignored for proxy-mode sessions; a malicious or misconfigured runtime cannot influence quota accounting by underreporting." and "the gateway pulls the incremental delta since its previous pull over the `ReportUsage` RPC at its direct-mode poll interval and increments Redis counters on each pull ... Deployers should monitor `lenny_gateway_token_usage_anomaly_total` (counter, labeled by `tenant_id` and `reason`: `zero_delta`, `implausibly_small`; `session_id` is intentionally excluded per the §16.1.1 high-cardinality attributes rule ...) — the gateway emits this metric when a session's pulled `ReportUsage` delta is zero (`zero_delta`) or implausibly small relative to LLM call frequency (`implausibly_small`)." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:41-42, reworded by proposal 0024, which also moved the direct-mode reporting mechanism from per-call to a cumulative-usage-frame pull)
- **Existing tests:** `cmd/lenny-gateway/llmproxy_usage_test.go::TestProxyUsageRecorderIgnoresDirectMode_Spec4_9_1468` and `TestProxyUsageRecorderAdvancesQuotaCounter_Spec11_2` still cover the proxy usage recorder in `package main` with fakes (unit tier). Proposal 0024 closed BUILD-GAPS F-11.2.20 and landed a real anomaly detector, `pkg/gateway/session/tokenanomaly.Detector`, with genuine tier9 coverage: `tests/tier9_security/token_usage_anomaly_test.go` (`TestDirectModeZeroTokenUnderReportingIsDetected_spec_11_2`, `TestDirectModeImplausiblySmallUnderReportingIsDetected_spec_11_2`, `TestDirectModeInterspersedNonZeroResetsZeroRun_spec_11_2`, `TestAnomalyIsIsolatedPerTenant_spec_11_2`, `TestAnomalyCounterLabelSetIsCompliant_spec_16_1_1`), plus `cmd/lenny-gateway/direct_usage_quota_integration_test.go::TestDirectModeUsageFlowsToQuotaCounter_spec_11_2` and the tier11 doc-consistency checks in `tests/tier11_docs/direct_usage_reportusage_consistency_test.go`. The direct-mode anomaly-metric half of the original gap is now closed.
- **Gap:** The remaining, more severe half of the original gap is untouched: no test drives a real proxy-mode session through the actual gateway binary with a real Redis counter and a misbehaving adapter that sends a fraudulent zero-token `ReportUsage` (which the gateway must ignore per spec), asserting the gateway-observed Redis counter is authoritative and unaffected by the adapter's report. This is the security-relevant adversarial scenario (a hostile or buggy proxy-mode runtime attempting to under-report) and remains verified only at unit tier with fakes.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier4 gateway harness (tests/testinfra/gateway), a real Redis (tests/testinfra/containers), and a fake LLM proxy upstream plus a misbehaving adapter stub in tests/testinfra/stubs. The under-reporting adapter stub does not exist; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/proxy_usage_authoritative_test.go driving a proxy-mode session whose adapter sends a fraudulent zero-token `ReportUsage` call and asserting the gateway-observed Redis counter (populated from the LLM Proxy's own extracted token counts, not the adapter's report) is authoritative and unaffected.

### - [ ] T-11.2.4 — Storage-quota GC-decrement Postgres-first ordering and the double-decrement crash hazard are verified only with a fake quota releaser [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Ordering requirement: The Redis decrement MUST be issued only after the Postgres `artifact_store` row has been durably committed with `deleted_at` set ... Issuing the decrement before the Postgres commit creates a double-decrement hazard ... On Redis restart, the gateway rehydrates per-tenant storage counters from the sum of `artifact_size_bytes` across active (non-deleted) artifacts in Postgres." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:37)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/blobstore/cataloging/cataloging_quota_test.go` (`TestSoftDeleteSessionReleasesStorageQuota`, `TestSoftDeleteSessionDecrementIsIdempotent`) uses a `fakeQuota` releaser and `MemoryStore`; it verifies the decrement fires and is idempotent against the catalog single-writer guard, not the Postgres-commit-before-Redis-decrement ordering. `pkg/gateway/quota/storagequota/recovery_internal_test.go::TestRecoveryReconcilerRehydratesOnRecoveryEdge_spec_12_4_210` (moved from `pkg/gateway/storagequota/` by the §11 pkg/gateway reorganization) verifies rehydration against a fake Postgres-sum source. Neither uses a real Redis and Postgres together.
- **Gap:** The normative MUST that the Redis decrement follows the Postgres commit, and the crash-recovery double-decrement hazard (crash after Redis decrement but before Postgres `deleted_at` commits, then rehydration plus a GC re-run), are not exercised against real stores. This is the data-integrity failure path for the storage counter and is currently unverified at component tier.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier2 real-Redis and real-Postgres harness (tests/testinfra/containers, the billingstore_test.go store harness) and a fault-injection point that crashes between the Redis decrement and the Postgres commit. The crash-injection seam is partially available via tests/testinfra/chaos; wiring it into the GC path is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier2_component/storagequota/gc_ordering_test.go that soft-deletes an artifact, forces a crash after the Redis decrement but before the Postgres commit, runs recovery rehydration plus a second GC sweep, and asserts the counter is decremented exactly once.

### - [ ] T-11.2.5 — No Kind end-to-end test for quota enforcement or quota recovery despite the declared tier5 suites [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "the gateway enforces budget limits against Redis counters (fast path). If a `deliveryMode: proxy` session exhausts its token budget, the gateway first attempts a §8.6 lease extension for the session ... it terminates the session only when the extension is terminal (`CEILING_REACHED` or `REJECTED`) or cannot be requested ... In `deliveryMode: direct` the gateway has no per-call LLM visibility, so a direct-mode session is not terminated in-path on budget breach; its over-run is bounded only by the gateway's next direct-mode `ReportUsage` poll interval ..." and "On Redis recovery, the gateway applies the MAX rule when restoring counters." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:44, reworded by proposal 0023, which relocated the §8.6 budget-exhaustion lease-extension trigger and scoped immediate in-path termination to proxy-mode sessions whose extension is terminal). TESTING.md §14 declares the tier5 scenarios `quota_enforcement` (TESTING.md:1035) and `quota_recovery` (TESTING.md:1036).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier4_integration/quota_test.go::TestQuotaEnforcement` enforces the per-tenant token budget through the real gateway binary against a Redis container and rejects session creation with `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` (admission-time, not mid-session). `tests/tier4_integration/quota_test.go::TestQuotaRecovery` exercises enforcement after recovery but computes `quota.ReconcileMax` in the test body and seeds Redis with the result (see T-11.2.6). No file under tests/tier5_e2e_kind/ references quota, `budget_exhausted`, or §11.2; the declared `quota_enforcement` and `quota_recovery` Kind scenarios are absent. The now-proxy-mode-scoped lease-extension mechanism itself has strong tier9 coverage (`tests/tier9_security/budget_extension_failclosed_test.go`), but that suite drives `leasecontrol.Service` and `sessionbudget.Enforcer` directly, not a Kind-deployed session hitting its budget through a real pod.
- **Gap:** The declared tier5 e2e suites do not exist on disk. Token-budget exhaustion driving a real proxy-mode session through the §8.6 lease-extension attempt to eventual termination, a real direct-mode session's bounded (not in-path-terminated) over-run, and Redis outage to fail-open to recovery with the MAX rule are never exercised on Kind with a real gateway deployment, real Redis, and a real runtime pod. This is the production user journey (a tenant hitting its budget mid-run, now mediated by lease extension) and the resilience journey (Redis bounce mid-session).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness (tests/testinfra/kind), a real Redis StatefulSet, and a runtime pod (the echo or delegation-echo test runtime). None beyond the existing Kind harness — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier5_e2e_kind/quota_enforcement_test.go driving a proxy-mode session past its `tokenQuotaPerWindow` with lease extension disabled or exhausted (asserting eventual termination) and a direct-mode session past budget (asserting it is NOT terminated in-path and instead over-runs bounded by the poll interval), and tests/tier5_e2e_kind/quota_recovery_test.go that bounces Redis mid-session and asserts the MAX-rule reconciliation keeps the budget enforced.

### - [ ] T-11.2.6 — TestQuotaRecovery asserts the arithmetic primitive rather than the gateway's MAX-rule recovery code path [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "On Redis recovery, the gateway applies the MAX rule when restoring counters: `restored_counter = MAX(in_memory_counter, postgres_checkpoint)` for each active session and tenant scope." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:44)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier4_integration/quota_test.go::TestQuotaRecovery` (lines 112-194) still computes `quota.ReconcileMax(accumulated, staleCheckpoint)` in the test and then calls `rd.Client.Set` to seed Redis with the result before asserting enforcement. The gateway never performs the reconciliation; the test verifies the pure function plus the downstream enforcement. `pkg/gateway/quota/quotacheckpoint/reconciler_internal_test.go::TestReconcilerTickEdge_spec_11_2` (moved from `pkg/gateway/quotacheckpoint/` by the §11 pkg/gateway reorganization) exercises the reconciler with fake stores at unit tier.
- **Gap:** No component-or-higher test drives the gateway's own recovery logic restoring the counter from the maximum of an in-memory value and a stale Postgres checkpoint after a real Redis outage. Because the test pre-computes the reconciled value, a regression that removed the MAX rule from the gateway's recovery path (for example reading the stale checkpoint directly) would not be caught. This is a spec-versus-test inconsistency that would let a regression ship.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier4 gateway harness plus a real Redis and real Postgres so the checkpoint and recovery both flow through the gateway. None — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Extend tests/tier4_integration/quota_recovery_test.go so the gateway writes a stale checkpoint to real Postgres, accumulates higher usage during a simulated Redis outage, restarts Redis, and asserts the gateway itself restores the higher value without the test computing ReconcileMax.

### - [ ] T-11.2.11 — Metering replay API (GET /v1/metering/events) has no wire-format contract test for the cursor envelope or since_sequence semantics [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Consumers detecting a gap in the `sequence_number` stream may request a replay via `GET /v1/metering/events?since_sequence={N}&limit={L}` — the gateway returns all events with `sequence_number > N` in ascending order, up to `limit` ... paginated using the standard cursor envelope." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:150)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/metering_test.go` covers role gating, ledger return, `since_sequence`, and pagination at unit tier with httptest. `tests/tier3_contract/rest_sessions/unexercised_endpoints_test.go::TestMeteringEventsRequiresViewUsagePermission` asserts only the 403 gate for an unauthenticated caller.
- **Gap:** The metering replay endpoint is a public REST surface, and no tier3 contract test pins its JSON cursor-envelope structure, the ascending `sequence_number > N` ordering, or the `limit`-plus-`hasMore` pagination wire format. The unit tests assert handler behavior, not the on-the-wire schema that external billing consumers depend on. This is a public-API wire surface with no conformance test.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier3 contract harness (the rest_sessions test server) and golden envelope fixtures (tests/testinfra/golden). None — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier3_contract/rest_metering/metering_events_test.go pinning the cursor-envelope JSON, the `since_sequence` ordering, and the pagination fields against a golden fixture for `billing-viewer`, `tenant-admin`, and `platform-admin` callers.

### - [x] T-11.2.12 — Billing sequence_number monotonicity under concurrent multi-replica writes is untested [Medium] — RESOLVED 80dd67cd
- **Resolution:** Proposal 0025 replaced the advisory-lock-plus-`MAX(sequence_number)+1` sequencing with a real per-tenant Postgres sequence (`billing_seq_` followed by the first 20 bytes of `SHA-256(tenant_id)` as 40 hex characters, keeping the identifier under the 63-byte Postgres limit; `audit_seq_` is the analogous distinct sequence for the audit log), closing BUILD-GAPS F-11.2.10. Billing `Append`/`InsertFromStream` now call `nextval` on the derived sequence instead of reading `MAX(sequence_number)` under an advisory lock. Commit `80dd67cd` ("0025 S5: switch billing Append/InsertFromStream to nextval") added `TestBillingSequenceConcurrentAppendNoCollision` to `tests/tier2_component/stores/billingstore_test.go`: 32 goroutines call `Append` concurrently against a real Postgres store for one tenant, and the test asserts every returned `sequence_number` is distinct (no duplicate, no lost write) — exactly the concurrency-correctness property this finding named as untested. Tier-11 doc tests (`tests/tier11_docs/billing_audit_sequence_docs_test.go`) additionally pin the two-sequence naming scheme.

### - [ ] T-11.2.13 — Mid-session token-budget enforcement (proxy-mode lease-extension-gated termination, direct-mode bounded over-run) is unverified at component tier [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "If a `deliveryMode: proxy` session exhausts its token budget, the gateway first attempts a §8.6 lease extension for the session ... it terminates the session only when the extension is terminal (`CEILING_REACHED` or `REJECTED`) or cannot be requested, and it terminates immediately, as before, when the lease is not extendable ... In `deliveryMode: direct` the gateway has no per-call LLM visibility, so a direct-mode session is not terminated in-path on budget breach; its over-run is bounded only by the gateway's next direct-mode `ReportUsage` poll interval and is reconciled against the parent's delegation budget at settlement ... During Redis unavailability (fail-open window), the gateway tracks usage in-memory per session and enforces the per-session budget locally using the per-replica ceiling formula." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:44, reworded by proposal 0023: proxy-mode termination is now gated behind a §8.6 lease-extension attempt, and direct-mode sessions are explicitly no longer terminated in-path at all)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/quota/quota_test.go::TestFailOpenCeilingFormula` and `TestPerUserFailOpenCeiling` cover the formulas. `pkg/gateway/storage/failopen/controller_test.go` (moved from `pkg/gateway/failopen/` by the §11 pkg/gateway reorganization) covers fail-open controller state with fakes. `tests/tier4_integration/quota_test.go::TestQuotaEnforcement` rejects new session creation at the admission boundary, not mid-session termination. The §8.6 lease-extension mechanism itself (the trigger, grant/ceiling/reject paths, and the fail-closed-on-CEILING_REACHED contract) has real tier9 coverage in `tests/tier9_security/budget_extension_failclosed_test.go`, but that suite drives `leasecontrol.Service`/`sessionbudget.Enforcer` directly rather than a real gateway HTTP session. No test drives an in-flight proxy-mode session past its budget through the real gateway and asserts it is terminated only once the lease extension resolves terminally, no test asserts a direct-mode session is NOT terminated in-path when it crosses budget (the new, more permissive contract), and none enforces the per-session budget locally against a genuinely unavailable Redis.
- **Gap:** Three distinct behaviors are unverified above unit/tier9-in-process tier: (1) a running proxy-mode session's termination gated behind a §8.6 lease-extension attempt, exercised through the real gateway HTTP path rather than the extension package directly; (2) the new direct-mode contract that a session crossing budget is NOT terminated in-path (only bounded and settled later) — a regression that reintroduced immediate direct-mode termination would not be caught by any current test; and (3) in-memory per-session enforcement during a real Redis outage using the per-replica ceiling. Admission-time rejection is covered, but these runtime-termination, direct-mode-non-termination, and degraded-mode enforcement paths are the operationally important ones.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier4 gateway harness, a runtime pod that consumes tokens, and a Redis container that can be made unavailable mid-session. None beyond the existing harness — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/quota_midsession_test.go with two cases: a proxy-mode session driven past budget with lease extension forced to a terminal outcome, asserting termination only after the terminal resolution; and a direct-mode session driven past budget, asserting the session is NOT terminated in-path and continues until the next `ReportUsage` poll. Add a fail-open case that takes Redis down and asserts the gateway enforces the per-replica ceiling locally.
