## §11.3 Timeouts and Cancellation <a id="t-11.3"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/11_policy-and-controls.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§11.3 defines a large timeout table, first-class cancellation for clients and parent agents, the `maxRequestInputWait` inter-agent blocking timeout with its `REQUEST_INPUT_TIMEOUT` error and `request_input_expired` parent event, and a `session_expiring_soon` / `DEADLINE_APPROACHING` pre-expiry warning. Since the 2026-06-03 audit, proposal 0002 collapsed the pool-level `runtime.maxIdleTimeSeconds` row into a `sessionPolicy.maxClientIdleSeconds` clock with a default equal to the effective `maxSessionAgeSeconds` and its own §6.2 pause table, and removed the `task_complete_acknowledged` row entirely (task mode is gone). Every BUILD-GAPS F-11.3.* implementation finding is now closed: the `session_expiring_soon` SSE event and the `DEADLINE_APPROACHING` adapter dispatch (F-11.3.5) and the `maxClientIdleSeconds` reclamation sweep (F-11.3.7) both landed with solid unit and tier2-component (real-Postgres) coverage, so the two former High findings that a live capability was completely missing while docs claimed otherwise are now narrowed to ordinary cross-tier coverage gaps and downgraded. The `pkg/gateway` reorg (proposal 0020) moved most cited packages (`watchdog` → `pkg/gateway/runtime/watchdog`, `mcptools` → `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools`, `inputwait` → `pkg/gateway/session/inputwait`, `interceptor` → `pkg/gateway/policy/interceptor`); all cited tests still exist at their new paths and this pass updates the pointers. Above unit tier the picture is largely unchanged: cancellation reaching a real pod, the `request_input_expired` wire event, the phase-specific interceptor timeouts, the elicitation per-hop timeout, and the per-runtime `maxSessionAge` resolution are still verified only in-process, with no tier4/tier5/tier10 test built since the last audit. The helm chart gained one relevant render test (`checkpointBarrierAckTimeoutSeconds`, F-11.3.15) but the rest of the §11.3 timeout-to-Helm-value table remains unpinned. Counts: 2 High, 6 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-11.3.1 — Cancellation reaching the runtime is never verified above unit tier; no e2e, chaos, or contract test confirms the pod actually drains [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Cancellation is first-class: clients and parent agents can cancel sessions/tasks cleanly." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:235)
- **Existing tests:** The clean-cancellation mechanism is unit-tested only. `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/cancel_release_test.go::TestCancelChildDrainsCancelledRuntimes_spec_11_3_1` (moved from `pkg/gateway/mcptools` in the §pkg/gateway reorg) and the sessionserver cascade tests (`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/cancel_release_test.go::TestCascadeCancelDrainsDescendantRuntimes_spec_11_3_9`) assert that `executor.ReleaseSession` is called against an in-process fake. `tests/tier3_contract/rest_sessions/sessions_test.go::TestDeleteCancelsSession` and `tests/tier4_integration/gateway_postgres_e2e_test.go` assert only that `DELETE` flips the row to `cancelled`; neither drives a live pod. `tests/tier4_integration/session_lifecycle_test.go:92` drives `interrupt → suspended` against the real gateway binary but asserts row state, not a runtime signal. `tests/spec-map.json` §11.3 now lists `pkg/gateway/runtime/watchdog/...`, `pkg/gateway/session/inputwait/...`, `pkg/session/state/...`, and a concrete `tests/tier2_component/watchdog/idle_pause_table_test.go::TestWatchdogIdleSweepPauseTable_spec_6_2` entry, but the `packages` list still names `pkg/policy/timeout`, which does not exist on disk. No tier5, tier8, or tier10 test asserts that DELETE, `/interrupt`, `lenny/cancel_child`, or a watchdog timeout produces the §11.4 line 258 `Terminate` RPC and the adapter SIGTERM/wait/SIGKILL sequence on a real pod.
- **Gap:** The core capability claim that cancellation reaches the runtime cleanly is verified only against an in-process executor double. A real user journey (alice cancels a running session and the pod is drained) and the cascade adversarial path (a parent cancels a subtree and every descendant pod terminates) are unexercised on Kind. Target tier5 e2e, with a tier8 chaos variant for cancel during pod disruption.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness (tests/testinfra/kind) with the gateway `--agent-namespace` flag wired so the §4.6 pod binder writes a SandboxClaim, plus tests/testinfra/sessiondriver to drive the session. `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/scaffolds_test.go` still records a skip when `--agent-namespace` is unset; the live-session infrastructure gap is unchanged since the last audit. Building the agent-namespace wiring is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier5_e2e_kind/cancellation_drain_test.go that drives a session to `running` via sessiondriver, issues `DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}`, and asserts the bound agent pod transitions claimed → draining → terminated within the graceful-shutdown window; add a cascade case that delegates a child and calls `lenny/cancel_child`, asserting both pods drain.

### - [ ] T-11.3.5 — `session_expiring_soon` and `DEADLINE_APPROACHING` are now implemented and unit-tested, but the wire event has no contract, schema, or conformance pin [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The gateway sends a `session_expiring_soon` event to the client and pod 5 minutes before `maxSessionAge` expires. [...] The agent receives a `DEADLINE_APPROACHING` signal via the adapter." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:239)
- **Existing tests:** BUILD-GAPS F-11.3.5 is CLOSED (commit `57784eb7`): the watchdog gained a `sweepExpiryWarning` pass (`pkg/gateway/runtime/watchdog/expiry_warning.go`, `expiry_warning_test.go`, 6 tests covering the window, dedup, resolver cap, and terminal-skip), `sessionserver.OnSessionExpiringSoon` performs both halves (`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/expiry_warning.go`, `expiry_warning_test.go`, `TestOnSessionExpiringSoonEmitsEventAndSignalsPod_spec_11_3_240` / `..._spec_11_3_240` without-binding variant), and the adapter side has 5 tests in `pkg/adapter/lifecycle_test.go` (`TestSignalDeadlineDeliversOverLifecycleChannel_spec_11_3_240` and siblings) plus a client-wrapper test. `docs/api/rest.md:288`, `docs/client-guide/wire-format.md:188`, and `docs/client-guide/streaming.md:69` now describe a live behavior rather than a documented-but-absent one. All of this coverage is unit-tier (in-process fakes); `grep -rln "session_expiring_soon"` over `tests/tier3_contract`, `tests/tier4_integration`, and `tests/tier10_conformance` returns nothing, and no `schemas/` entry defines the `session_expiring_soon` SSE payload.
- **Gap:** The prior High-severity defect (a documented capability with zero production emitter) is resolved: the emitter exists and is exercised at unit tier on both the SSE-event half and the adapter-signal half. What remains is the same class of gap as T-11.3.4: the wire-level `session_expiring_soon` SSE payload has no schema and no contract pin, and the `DEADLINE_APPROACHING` lifecycle-channel dispatch has no tier10 conformance case exercising a gateway-initiated `SignalDeadline` RPC end to end. Target tier4 integration for the SSE emit against a real gateway binary and tier10 conformance for the `DEADLINE_APPROACHING` dispatch.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today against the minimal gateway via tests/testinfra/gateway and tests/testinfra/clockstep or tests/testinfra/timectl to advance the session clock to `maxAge − 5min`. Adding a `session_expiring_soon` JSON schema under `schemas/` is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/session_expiry_warning_test.go that creates a session with a short effective `maxSessionAge`, advances the clock via clockstep, and asserts a `session_expiring_soon` SSE frame matching a new `schemas/` entry; add a tier10 conformance case in cmd/lenny-compliance asserting the runtime receives `DEADLINE_APPROACHING` from a gateway-initiated `SignalDeadline` dispatch.

### - [ ] T-11.3.7 — `maxClientIdleSeconds` reclamation is now implemented and tested against real Postgres, but the executor/pod-release side of expiry is still unverified [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Max client idle time | Effective `maxSessionAgeSeconds` (7200s default) | `sessionPolicy.maxClientIdleSeconds` | Yes (per pool)" (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:199)
- **Existing tests:** BUILD-GAPS F-11.3.7 is CLOSED (commit `2f970e91`, extended by `0002 S15`): proposal 0002 replaced the former pool-level `runtime.maxIdleTimeSeconds` knob with the single `sessionPolicy.maxClientIdleSeconds` clock and its own §6.2 pause table. `pkg/gateway/session/sessionidle/sessionidle_test.go` unit-tests the resolver (runtime/pool/playground min-wins, default-to-age-cap) and the activity `Stamper` (coalescing, terminal-skip, nil-safety) — 10 tests. `pkg/gateway/runtime/watchdog/idle_test.go` unit-tests the sweep itself (7 tests: expiry, default-is-age-cap, activity-anchor, resolver honoring, pause/run-state split, zero-resolver fallback). `tests/tier2_component/watchdog/idle_pause_table_test.go::TestWatchdogIdleSweepPauseTable_spec_6_2` exercises the full pause table (`running`/`input_required`/`awaiting_client_action` reclaimed, `suspended`/`resume_pending`/`resuming`/`finalizing` untouched) against a real Postgres container with the production migrations applied. None of this — unit or tier2 — wires a `TerminalHook`/executor double that asserts a pod-release call fires when the idle sweep expires a session; `tests/tier2_component/watchdog/idle_pause_table_test.go` constructs its watchdog with a `nil` hook.
- **Gap:** The reclamation clock itself (state transition, pause table, activity reset, per-pool/playground override resolution) is now solidly covered at unit and tier2-component tier against real Postgres. What remains is the release half of "reclaims warm pods from abandoned sessions": no test asserts that an idle-triggered `expired` transition actually invokes `executor.ReleaseSession` (or an equivalent pod-drain call) rather than only flipping the row. This is the same release-verification gap T-11.3.2 already names for the `maxSessionAge`/`maxAwaitingClientAction` sweeps; a single tier4 test covering both timers would close both.
- **Dependencies:** Requires tests/testinfra/clockstep or a short-deadline gateway configuration plus tests/testinfra/gateway to run the real binary; the watchdog clock injection T-11.3.2 already needs is the same missing piece here.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/idle_expiry_drain_test.go that opens a session against the real gateway binary, sends one message, advances the clock past the effective `maxClientIdleSeconds`, and asserts the session row becomes `expired` with `FailureReason = expired:idle` and the executor release path runs exactly once; assert a fresh message before the bound resets the idle timer and no expiry fires.

### - [ ] T-11.3.4 — `request_input` timeout error and `request_input_expired` parent event have no contract or conformance pin against the MCP/SSE wire format [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "the gateway resolves the blocked tool call with a `REQUEST_INPUT_TIMEOUT` error [...] the gateway emits a `request_input_expired` event on the parent's `lenny/await_children` stream: `{ \"type\": \"request_input_expired\", \"childId\": \"...\", \"requestId\": \"...\", \"expiredAt\": \"<ISO8601>\" }`" (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:237)
- **Existing tests:** Unit-only. `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/mcptools_test.go::TestRequestInputTimeoutSurfacesEnvelopeCode_spec_15_2_1_F_8_5_10`, `::TestRequestInputTimeoutCarriesExpiredAt_spec_11_3_238` (BUILD-GAPS F-11.3.23 additionally confirmed both `REQUEST_INPUT_TIMEOUT` and `ELICITATION_TIMEOUT` now carry a parsable `expiredAt`), and `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/limits_per_runtime_test.go::TestRequestInputExpiredPublishedToParentStream_spec_11_3_238` assert the envelope code and the parent-stream event in-process. `grep -rln "request_input_expired\|REQUEST_INPUT_TIMEOUT"` over `tests/**` still returns nothing, and `grep` over `schemas/` still returns no schema for either name. No tier3 contract or tier10 conformance test pins this output against the MCP Streamable HTTP or SSE wire format.
- **Gap:** The `request_input_expired` event and `REQUEST_INPUT_TIMEOUT` envelope are protocol surface delivered over the MCP `lenny/await_children` stream, and they have no wire-schema definition and no conformance check. This is a standards-conformance gap (MCP/JSON-RPC and SSE framing) and a failure-path delivery gap. Target tier3 contract across the REST and MCP surfaces, with a tier10 conformance pin.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today against the minimal gateway via tests/testinfra/gateway and tests/testinfra/sdkhelper, using a per-pool `maxRequestInputWaitSeconds` short enough to fire within the test. Adding a `request_input_expired` JSON schema under `schemas/` is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier3_contract/mcp_delegation/request_input_timeout_test.go that has a child call `lenny/request_input`, lets the timeout fire, and asserts the child receives a JSON-RPC tool-call error with `code: REQUEST_INPUT_TIMEOUT` and the parent's `await_children` stream carries a `request_input_expired` frame with `childId`, `requestId`, and an ISO8601 `expiredAt`, validated against the new schema.

## §11.4 User Invalidation <a id="t-11.4"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/11_policy-and-controls.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The §11.4 three-tier user invalidation is well covered at the unit tier. `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/users_invalidate_test.go` and `users_invalidate_fanout_test.go` (relocated from `pkg/gateway/admin` by the tier-0020 package reorganization) exercise soft_disable, hard_disable, and full_revoke against in-memory stores and fully faked fan-out dependencies, and the gate handlers under `pkg/gateway/sessionserver` and `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools` (relocated from `pkg/gateway/mcptools`) reject disabled and revoked principals on the session, interaction, and delegation paths. Proposal 0012 landed since the last review and rewrote the §11.4 step-5 wording and the trailing Note to match the implemented synchronous-local-plus-async-cross-replica contract, resolving the spec-vs-implementation ambiguity T-11.4.6 previously flagged; the Note now explicitly names credential deny-list entries as a third cross-replica pub/sub payload alongside the pod-Terminate request and the token revocations, which surfaces a new, previously uncovered gap (T-11.4.11) parallel to T-11.4.4's token-revocation angle. A repository-wide package move (`pkg/gateway/admin` → `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin`, `pkg/gateway/openapi` → `pkg/gateway/externalapi/openapi`, `pkg/gateway/mcptools` → `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools`, `pkg/gateway/adapterclient` → `pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterclient`, `pkg/gateway/revocation` and `pkg/gateway/credrenewal` → `pkg/gateway/credentials/...`, `pkg/gateway/issuedtokenstore` → `pkg/gateway/storage/issuedtokenstore`, `pkg/gateway/playground` → `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground`) left every existing test's content and line numbers intact but stale as file paths; those paths are corrected below. A new unit-level `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/user_invalidation_test.go` exercises the playground-session revocation primitive against a real Redis-backed session store via miniredis, and a new generic `TestOCSFTranslationCoversEveryEventType` (`tests/tier3_contract/ocsf_audit/ocsf_audit_test.go`) now runs `admin.user.invalidated` (registered in `pkg/audit/ocsf/mapping.go`) through the OCSF translator and asserts the structural shape, narrowing T-11.4.7's tier3 half; neither closes a finding outright. Coverage above the unit tier otherwise remains absent: no component (tier2) test drives full_revoke through the real pod-RPC terminator, the Postgres-backed issued-token store, the Redis-backed credential deny-list propagator, or the credential-lease store; the pipeline is asserted only against fakes. No contract (tier3) test pins the invalidate request body or the response envelope, and the OpenAPI document declares only a bare `200 OK` with no `mode` enum, no propagation-counter response schema, and no `USER_INVALIDATED` 403. No integration (tier4), Kind or cloud e2e (tier5/tier6), chaos (tier8), or security (tier9) test exercises user invalidation, so the security-critical full-revoke journey is unverified beyond the unit tier. spec-map.json's §11.4 `tests` glob was corrected to the new admin package path by the same reorganization, but its `packages` field still claims the nonexistent `pkg/auth/invalidate`.
Counts: 5 High, 4 Medium, 1 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-11.4.1 — Full-revoke propagation pipeline has no component test against real backing services [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Full revoke propagation mechanism: 1. Gateway looks up all active sessions for the user (via SessionStore). 2. For each session in the user's task tree: gateway sends a `Terminate` RPC to the pod with reason `USER_REVOKED`. ... 5. The user's issued tokens are revoked in the durable Postgres issued-token index (the authoritative revocation store; see [§13.3](13_security-model.md#133-credential-flow)), each revoked token id is pushed into the gateway's in-memory revocation cache, and the revocations are fanned out to peer replicas so every replica's cache rejects the tokens within seconds. 6. Credential leases held by the user's sessions are revoked (returned to pool). 7. Pending elicitations for the user are dismissed." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:253-261, reworded by proposal 0012)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/users_invalidate_fanout_test.go:25-108` (relocated from `pkg/gateway/admin`) defines `fakePodTerminator`, `fakeLeaseRevoker`, `fakeUserTokenRevoker`, and `fakePlaygroundRevoker`, and `newFullRevokeAdmin` wires `userstore.NewMemory()`, `memstore.New()` (`pkg/gateway/session/sessionstore/memstore`), `interactionstore.NewMemory()`, and a `fakeRevCache`. Every full_revoke assertion (`TestFullRevokeFansOutToPods`, `TestFullRevokeRevokesCredentialLeases`, `TestFullRevokeInvalidatesCachedAuth`, and the rest) runs against these fakes. The concrete adapters in `cmd/lenny-gateway/user_revocation.go` (`podTerminateFanOut`, `userLeaseRevoker`, `userTokenRevoker`) have a single unit test in `cmd/lenny-gateway/user_revocation_test.go`. A new `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/user_invalidation_test.go` adds real-Redis (miniredis) coverage of the playground-session-revocation fan-out step specifically, but still at the unit tier and not through the admin router. No test under tests/tier2_component wires the admin router's full_revoke handler to a real SessionStore, a real `credleasestore`, a real `issuedtokenstore.Store`, and a real revocation cache. Searched tests/tier2_component, tests/tier4_integration, tests/tier5_e2e_kind.
- **Gap:** The seven-step pipeline is verified only against mocks, so a divergence between a concrete adapter and the `admin.User*` interface it satisfies (for example `userTokenRevoker.RevokeUserTokens` calling `RevokeBySubject` with the wrong tenant scoping, or `userLeaseRevoker` failing to add the credential to the deny list) ships undetected. The work is a real component-level user journey: an operator full-revokes a user and the handler drives the real stores. Target tier2.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a Postgres container (tests/testinfra/containers `StartPostgres`) for `issuedtokenstore` (now `pkg/gateway/storage/issuedtokenstore`) and the credential-lease pgstore (`pkg/gateway/credentials/credleasestore/pgstore`), a Redis container or miniredis for the revocation cache and deny-list propagator, and a stub adapter for the pod-RPC `Terminate` call (a stub satisfying `adapterclient` from tests/testinfra/stubs, which does not exist yet for this path). Building the stub is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier2_component/gateway_subsystems/user_invalidate_test.go that wires `admin.NewRouter(...).WithUserRevocation(...).WithIssuedTokens(...).WithSessions(...)` to a real `issuedtokenstore.Store` over Postgres, a real `credleasestore`, and the real `revocation/propagator` (`pkg/gateway/credentials/revocation/propagator`), then issues a full_revoke and asserts the issued tokens are revoked by subject, the leases are dropped and deny-listed, and the response counters match.

### - [ ] T-11.4.2 — Full-revoke session-termination journey has no Kind or cloud end-to-end test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "| Full revoke | Terminate active sessions, invalidate cached auth, deny reconnects |" and "For each session in the user's task tree: gateway sends a `Terminate` RPC to the pod with reason `USER_REVOKED`. 3. The pod's runtime adapter initiates graceful shutdown (SIGTERM to agent, wait up to 10s, then SIGKILL)." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:251, 256-257)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterclient/client_test.go:585-653` (relocated from `pkg/gateway/adapterclient`) asserts that `cl.Terminate(..., "USER_REVOKED", 10s)` sends a Shutdown with the `USER_REVOKED` reason against an in-process gRPC stub. No tier5 or tier6 test creates a live session on a pod, revokes the owning user, and asserts the pod receives the `Terminate` RPC, performs the SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL graceful shutdown within 10s, and that the session moves to terminated. Searched tests/tier5_e2e_kind and tests/tier6_e2e_cloud for invalidate, USER_REVOKED, full_revoke; none found.
- **Gap:** The end-to-end full-revoke journey on a real cluster is unverified. The pod-RPC fan-out, the adapter's 10s graceful-shutdown window, and the SessionStore transition are never exercised together against a running pod under real NetworkPolicy and pod-to-gateway mTLS. This is the headline user journey for §11.4 and an operator-facing security control. Target tier5 (Kind), with a tier6 follow-on for at least one cloud provider.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness (tests/testinfra/kind) and the session driver (tests/testinfra/sessiondriver). `sessiondriver.Driver` exposes `CreateAndStart` and `Terminate` but has no admin `InvalidateUser` method; adding one is part of this finding. The delegation-echo or echo test runtime suffices for the pod side.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier5_e2e_kind/user_invalidation_test.go that uses `sessiondriver` to create and start a session for alice under acme, calls a new `Driver.InvalidateUser(ctx, "acme", "alice@acme.com", "full_revoke")`, then polls `GET /v1/sessions` until alice's session reports terminated and asserts a subsequent `CreateSession` for alice returns 403 `USER_INVALIDATED`.

### - [ ] T-11.4.3 — Invalidate endpoint has no contract test and the OpenAPI document omits the request and response schema [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "| Soft disable | Deny new sessions | Hard disable | Also block new delegated tasks; reject pending delegation approvals for the user | Full revoke | Terminate active sessions, invalidate cached auth, deny reconnects |" (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:249-251) and the handler's response body fields `podsTerminated`, `leasesRevoked`, `tokensRevoked`, and `elicitationsDismissed` (pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/users.go:562-566, relocated from `pkg/gateway/admin`).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/externalapi/openapi/openapi_test.go` (relocated from `pkg/gateway/openapi`) generically walks every OpenAPI path asserting `x-lenny-mcp-tool` and `x-lenny-scope` are present, which covers `/v1/admin/users/{userId}/invalidate` (the path parameter is now `{userId}`, not `{user_id}`) as one of many, but no longer hardcodes an assertion naming that path. The document itself (pkg/gateway/externalapi/openapi/openapi.json:1716-1730) declares only `"200": { "description": "OK" }` and a `404`, with no request-body schema, no `mode` enum constraining `soft_disable`/`hard_disable`/`full_revoke`, and no response schema for the propagation counters. No tier3 contract test exercises the endpoint; a grep of tests/tier3_contract for invalidate, soft_disable, full_revoke, USER_INVALIDATED, and podsTerminated returns nothing.
- **Gap:** A public admin REST surface and its MCP meta-tool projection (`x-lenny-mcp-tool: admin.invalidate_user`) have no wire-contract test. A handler change that renames `tokensRevoked`, accepts an unlisted mode, or drops a counter would not be caught, and the OpenAPI document does not pin the contract for SDK or MCP-shim generation. This is a contract-conformance gap on a public API. Target tier3.
- **Dependencies:** None, buildable today. The tier3 REST harness (tests/testinfra/gateway, used by tests/tier3_contract/rest_sessions) runs the minimal gateway in-process; the admin router is reachable through it.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier3_contract/rest_admin/users_invalidate_test.go that POSTs each of the three modes and asserts the response status and the JSON envelope fields against the documented schema, posts an unknown mode and asserts the 400 with the `mode must be one of soft_disable, hard_disable, or full_revoke` message, and extend openapi.json plus openapi_test.go to require the request-body `mode` enum and the propagation-counter response schema.

### - [ ] T-11.4.4 — Cross-replica cached-auth invalidation is not exercised through the full-revoke handler against real Redis [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "5. The user's issued tokens are revoked in the durable Postgres issued-token index ..., each revoked token id is pushed into the gateway's in-memory revocation cache, and the revocations are fanned out to peer replicas so every replica's cache rejects the tokens within seconds." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:259, reworded by proposal 0012) and the wiring contract that §11.4 step 6 must reach every replica's deny list, enforced by the `IsCrossReplicaPropagator()` marker (cmd/lenny-gateway/user_revocation.go:151-164).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier2_component/securitycaches/propagation_test.go:51-92` runs two `revocation/propagator` (`pkg/gateway/credentials/revocation/propagator`) instances over a real Redis container and asserts that `propA.Revoke("jti-a-to-b")` reaches `cacheB`. That test calls `Revoke` on the propagator directly; it does not drive the §11.4 full_revoke handler, so it never verifies that `runFullRevokeFanOut` pushes the JTIs returned by `RevokeUserTokens` into the cross-replica propagator. `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/users_invalidate_fanout_test.go:210-264` (`TestFullRevokeInvalidatesCachedAuth`, relocated from `pkg/gateway/admin`) asserts the push into a local `fakeRevCache`, with no Redis and no second replica.
- **Gap:** The end-to-end step-5 claim that a full_revoke on replica A invalidates the user's cached auth on replica B is not tested. The generic propagation test and the handler test cover the two halves separately, so a regression where the handler stops feeding revoked JTIs into the propagator (the `if r.revocationCache != nil` branch at pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/users_invalidate.go:175-179) would leave both tests passing while cross-replica invalidation silently breaks. This is a multi-replica deployment-combination gap on a security control. Target tier2, extendable to tier4 on the HA multi-replica gateway topology.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a Redis container (tests/testinfra/containers `StartRedis`) and two admin routers sharing one Redis through `revocation/propagator`, plus a real or stubbed `issuedtokenstore.Store` returning JTIs. None of this is missing; it is buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Extend tests/tier2_component/securitycaches/propagation_test.go (or add user_revoke_propagation_test.go) to build two admin routers, each `WithIssuedTokens` wired to a `revocation/propagator` over one Redis, issue a full_revoke on router A for alice, and assert router B's revocation cache reports each of alice's JTIs revoked within the propagation window.

### - [ ] T-11.4.5 — Hard-disable rejection of pending delegation approvals is not tested at component level [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "| Hard disable | Also block new delegated tasks; reject pending delegation approvals for the user |" (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:250)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/interactions_user_gate_test.go:21-52` asserts that `tool-use/{id}/approve` and elicitation `respond` are denied for a disabled user through the shared `requireActiveUserForAction` gate, using `memstore.New()` and `httptest`. `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/delegate_user_gate_test.go:57-129` (relocated from `pkg/gateway/mcptools`) asserts that `delegate_task` is rejected for a disabled or revoked owner. These are unit tests with in-memory stores and no real delegation tree.
- **Gap:** The spec calls out rejecting pending delegation approvals specifically for hard_disable. The unit tests cover the gate predicate, but no component or integration test stands up a real delegation parent-child tree with a pending approval, hard-disables the owner, and asserts the pending approval is rejected while the running session is left alone (since hard_disable does not terminate sessions). The interaction between hard_disable and an in-flight delegation approval is the failure-path scenario. Target tier2 or tier4.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the delegation harness used by tests/tier4_integration/delegation_test.go and an interaction store with a seeded pending approval; the interactionstore memory and pg implementations both exist. None missing for a tier4 build.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier4 case in tests/tier4_integration that creates a delegated task with a pending approval for alice, posts hard_disable for alice, and asserts the approval POST returns 403 `USER_INVALIDATED` while alice's already-running parent session remains running.

### - [ ] T-11.4.6 — Asynchronous propagation and GET /v1/sessions eventual consistency are untested [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Full-revoke propagation is two-tiered. On the handling gateway replica, the API performs the local effects synchronously before it returns ... The response body reports the per-effect counts and any partial-failure detail ... Because each local pod `Terminate` RPC is bounded, the call blocks for a bounded duration rather than returning immediately. Cross-replica propagation is asynchronous: the gateway publishes the step-2 `Terminate` request, the token revocations, and the credential deny-list entries on Redis pub/sub channels, and peer replicas apply them on their subscribers within seconds. ... The cancelled session state is committed to the central SessionStore before the call returns, so `GET /v1/sessions` reflects it on return; when read traffic is routed to a Postgres read replica ..., the cancellation becomes visible once it replicates, subject to the usual read-replica lag." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:263, rewritten by proposal 0012, replacing the prior "Invalidation is asynchronous — the API call returns immediately" Note)
- **Existing tests:** No test found. Searched tests/tier4_integration, tests/tier5_e2e_kind, and pkg/gateway for assertions on the synchronous-local/async-cross-replica timing behavior of invalidate; grep for `two-tiered`, `propagation completes`, and `read-replica lag` in *_test.go returns only unrelated erasure and limiter tests. `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/users.go` runs the local fan-out synchronously before responding, matching the rewritten Note, but no test asserts the cross-replica portion ("peer replicas apply them on their subscribers within seconds") converges within the documented window, nor the read-replica-lag-qualified `GET /v1/sessions` visibility.
- **Gap:** Proposal 0012 resolved the prior spec-vs-implementation ambiguity this finding originally flagged (the Note no longer claims the call "returns immediately"; it now states the synchronous-local, async-cross-replica contract the handler actually implements). The residual, still-untested behavior is narrower: no test measures that cross-replica effects (pod-Terminate fan-out, token revocation, credential deny-list) converge on a peer replica within the "within seconds" bound, and no test exercises the qualified `GET /v1/sessions` visibility claim under a configured Postgres read replica with induced lag. Target tier4 for the cross-replica convergence timing, tier5 or a dedicated read-replica-lag harness for the `GET /v1/sessions` clause.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the live gateway, a second replica sharing Redis/Postgres (see T-11.4.4's two-router fixture), and a SessionStore configured with a Postgres read replica for the lag-qualified assertion. The clock-step helper (tests/testinfra/clockstep, timectl) supports the within-seconds bound assertion.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier4 case that full-revokes a user on replica A, polls replica B's `GET /v1/sessions` and revocation-cache state until convergence, asserting it completes within the documented few-second window, and a follow-on case with `LENNY_PG_READ_DSN` pointed at a lagging read replica asserting the session read reflects cancellation only once replication catches up.

## §11.5 Idempotency <a id="t-11.5"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/11_policy-and-controls.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The REST idempotency surface for CreateSession has solid layered coverage: a tier2 Postgres store contract test, a tier3 wire contract suite, and a tier4 through-the-binary suite, all backed by thorough tier1 unit and property tests. Coverage thins sharply outside that one path. The MCP `idempotencyKey` surface that the spec names co-equal with the REST header is implemented in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/idempotency.go` (moved from `pkg/gateway/mcp/` by the proposal 0020 package reorganization) but is exercised only in tier1 unit tests, with no contract or integration test that pins the JSON-RPC wire behavior of the `idempotencyKey` field itself. The spec enumerates six critical operations; a tier4 test landed by proposal 0027 now drives one more of them, SpawnChild (`lenny/delegate_task`), through the client-facing `/mcp` edge with a same-key replay and a changed-body 422 case, but FinalizeWorkspace, StartSession, Approve/DenyDelegation, and Resume remain unexercised above unit level. That same proposal also spec-documents a boundary the failover finding must account for: the §11.5 mechanism runs only on the client-facing edge and is intentionally absent from the intra-pod platform-tool dispatch a restored parent session re-issues `delegate_task` over, so a pod-restore-induced duplicate child is an accepted at-least-once residual rather than a §11.5 defect. The spec's stated purpose, preventing duplicate sessions or children during gateway failover, still has no tier5 e2e or tier8 chaos test on the genuine failover path, and the atomic `Claim`/`Release` concurrency path that backs that guarantee is verified only against the in-memory mutex store, not the real Postgres `ON CONFLICT` statement. The scheduled GC sweeper (now in `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` and `workers.go` after the proposal 0020 file split) is untested, and `spec-map.json` still mis-attributes a credential-lifecycle load test to §11.5.
Counts: 2 High, 5 Medium, 1 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-11.5.1 — MCP `idempotencyKey` surface has no contract or integration test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Clients provide an idempotency key via the `Idempotency-Key` HTTP header (for REST) or the `idempotencyKey` field in the MCP tool input (for MCP)." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:276)
- **Existing tests:** The MCP idempotency hook in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/idempotency.go` (renamed from `pkg/gateway/mcp/idempotency.go` by the proposal 0020 `mcpfabric` package grouping; Claim/replay/in-flight/reuse/per-tool key namespacing) is exercised only by tier1 unit tests in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/idempotency_test.go` (TestMCPIdempotency_ReplaysCachedToolResult_spec_11_5, _ConcurrentRetryInFlight_, _DifferentBodyRejected_, _KeyNamespacing_, and siblings) that call the `mcp.Server` in-process. `tests/spec-map.json` §11.5 lists no MCP test at all. The tier3 contract directory `tests/tier3_contract/rest_idempotency/` and `tests/tier3_contract/rest_mcp_consistency/` contain no idempotency assertion, and `tests/tier4_integration/idempotency_test.go` posts only to the REST `/v1/sessions` path. Proposal 0027 landed `tests/tier4_integration/delegate_task_recovery_residual_test.go`, whose `testClientFacingMitigation` case does drive a real `tools/call` JSON-RPC body for `lenny/delegate_task` through the `/mcp` HTTP surface and asserts a same-key replay and a changed-body `422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`, but it uses the REST-style `Idempotency-Key` header rather than the MCP `idempotencyKey` tool-input field, covers only one tool, and asserts neither the in-flight 409 case nor per-tool key namespacing nor cross-transport non-collision, so it narrows but does not close this gap.
- **Gap:** The MCP transport is a public protocol surface and the spec applies §11.5 to it explicitly, so a JSON-RPC wire conformance test is still required. No test pins the `idempotencyKey` field (as opposed to the REST header) flowing through a real MCP `tools/call` request, the per-tool key namespacing (`mcp/<tool>/<caller>` that prevents a REST/MCP cross-transport replay), or the `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` / `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` ToolError mapping on the wire. This is both a standards-conformance gap (JSON-RPC) and a real user journey (an MCP client retrying `lenny/create_session` or `lenny/spawn_child`).
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The MCP server and the `idemmw.Store` MemoryStore are wired in-process today; the tier3 harness can drive `tools/call` over the JSON-RPC handler. For a tier4 form, `tests/testinfra/gateway` starts the binary with the MCP route mounted.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier3_contract/rest_mcp_consistency/idempotency_test.go that issues two identical `lenny/create_session` MCP `tools/call` requests with the same `idempotencyKey` tool-input field and asserts a replayed ToolResult, a third with a different argument body asserting `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`, and a concurrent pair asserting `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT`, plus a cross-transport case proving a REST `Idempotency-Key` and an MCP `idempotencyKey` of the same string do not collide.

### - [ ] T-11.5.2 — Failover de-duplication purpose has no e2e or chaos test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Prevents duplicate sessions or children during gateway failover or client retries." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:278)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier4_integration/idempotency_test.go::TestIdempotencyReplayThroughBinary` replays through a single steady-state gateway subprocess. `tests/tier7a_load_local/scenarios/idempotency_replay_race/scenario.go` drives `pkg/idempotency` pure logic under goroutines, and `tests/tier7a_load_local/scenarios/idempotency_cache_eviction/scenario.go` drives the in-process gateway with repeated same-key POSTs. No test in `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/`, `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/`, or `tests/tier8_chaos/` references idempotency; the only tier6 reference is an `Idempotency-Key` header attached to an unrelated session-lifecycle smoke (tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/session_lifecycle_test.go:96).
- **Gap:** The behavior that the spec advertises as the reason §11.5 exists, surviving a gateway failover without creating a duplicate session or child, is never exercised against a real multi-replica gateway with a shared Postgres `idempotency_keys` table. A tier8 chaos test that kills the serving replica after the inner handler commits but before the client receives the response, then has the client retry the same key against a surviving replica, is the failure-path test this requirement needs. The current load scenarios run against in-process or pure-logic targets and do not cross a replica boundary. Proposal 0027 clarifies a boundary this test must respect and not conflate: the client-facing failover/retry scenario this finding targets is distinct from the intra-pod pod-restore path, where §7.3/§8.10 now document an accepted at-least-once residual for `delegate_task` (the §11.5 hook does not run on the intra-pod platform-tool dispatch a restored parent re-issues, per `tests/tier4_integration/delegate_task_recovery_residual_test.go`). The chaos test suggested here must kill the *serving replica*, not the pod running the session, so it exercises genuine gateway failover rather than the documented-unmitigated pod-restore residual.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`) with an HA multi-replica gateway and a shared Postgres-backed store, and the tier8 chaos primitives (`tests/testinfra/chaos`) to kill a replica mid-request. The replica-kill-after-commit injection point may need a fault hook; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier8_chaos/idempotency_failover_test.go that drives a CreateSession with an `Idempotency-Key` against an HA gateway, kills the serving replica immediately after the session row is written, retries the same key against a surviving replica via `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`, and asserts a single session exists and the replayed status and body match.

### - [ ] T-11.5.3 — Four of the six critical operations are untested above unit level [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Critical operations support idempotency keys: CreateSession, FinalizeWorkspace, StartSession, SpawnChild, Approve/DenyDelegation, Resume" (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:267-274)
- **Existing tests:** Every component-and-above idempotency test in `tests/tier3_contract/rest_idempotency/idempotency_test.go` (lines 76, 102, 121, 139, 160) and `tests/tier4_integration/idempotency_test.go` (line 117) drives only CreateSession via `POST /v1/sessions`, and the tier2 store test uses synthetic keys with no operation binding (tests/tier2_component/stores/idempotencystore_test.go). Proposal 0027 added `tests/tier4_integration/delegate_task_recovery_residual_test.go::testClientFacingMitigation`, which drives SpawnChild (`lenny/delegate_task`) through the client-facing `/mcp` edge with an `Idempotency-Key` header, asserting a same-key replay (same child id, `nodeCount == 2`) and a changed-body `422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; this closes the SpawnChild gap this finding previously named. The gateway wiring in cmd/lenny-gateway/flags.go admits a `--idempotency-max-body-bytes` cap that names FinalizeWorkspace, StartSession, and Resume bodies (flags.go:1104-1106), confirming those endpoints are intended to be idempotent, yet no test posts an `Idempotency-Key` to a finalize, start, resume, or delegation-approve/deny endpoint.
- **Gap:** The replay and `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` behavior is now verified for two of the six enumerated operations (CreateSession and SpawnChild); FinalizeWorkspace, StartSession, Approve/DenyDelegation, and Resume still have no component or integration test proving a duplicate request replays rather than re-executes. Approve/DenyDelegation is the remaining delegation-path operation the spec singles out alongside SpawnChild, and Resume is the retry-after-disconnect path. This is a partial-coverage gap across the remaining four operations the spec normatively enumerates.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today for the REST forms. The session server and its finalize/start/resume handlers exist; delegation approve/deny endpoints are reachable through `tests/testinfra/gateway`.
- **Suggested test:** Extend tests/tier4_integration/idempotency_test.go with one replay-and-reuse case per remaining operation: FinalizeWorkspace (`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/finalize`), StartSession (`.../start`), Resume (`.../resume`), and Approve/DenyDelegation through the delegation surface, each asserting a single side effect and a matching replayed response.

### - [ ] T-11.5.4 — Atomic Claim/Release concurrency path is unverified against real Postgres [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Within this window, a duplicate request with the same key returns the cached response (same HTTP status and body) without re-executing the operation." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:276)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier2_component/stores/idempotencystore_test.go::TestIdempotencyStoreContract` exercises the Postgres-backed `pgstore` for Put, Get, replace-on-conflict, tenant isolation, the TTL read filter, and `DeleteExpired`, but never calls `Claim` or `Release` and runs no concurrent goroutines. The `Claim`/`Release` atomicity and the `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` 409 branch are tested only in tier1 against the in-memory mutex store (pkg/gateway/middleware/idempotency/idempotency_test.go::TestWrap_AtomicClaim_ConcurrentRetryGetsInFlight_spec_11_5 and _5xxReleasesPendingRow_).
- **Gap:** The production `pgstore.Claim` uses a CTE with `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, idempotency_key) DO UPDATE ... WHERE expired` (pkg/gateway/middleware/idempotency/pgstore/pgstore.go:122-159). That single statement is the entire concurrency-safety mechanism behind the no-double-execute guarantee, and it is verified only against a Go mutex, never against the real SQL under contention. A component test that fires concurrent `Claim` calls for the same `(tenant, key)` at the live Postgres container and asserts exactly one claimant wins is the failure-path test for the atomicity invariant.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The tier2 store harness (`startStore`, `freshTenant`) already brings up a Postgres container with production migrations.
- **Suggested test:** Add a subtest to tests/tier2_component/stores/idempotencystore_test.go that launches N goroutines calling `store.Claim(ctx, tenant, key, hash, now)` concurrently and asserts exactly one returns `claimed=true`, the rest observe the pending row, and a subsequent `Release` lets a fresh `Claim` win again.

### - [ ] T-11.5.5 — `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` 409 has no contract-tier wire test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "a duplicate request with the same key returns the cached response ... without re-executing the operation." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:276); the in-flight rejection is the implementation's enforcement of "without re-executing" (pkg/gateway/middleware/idempotency/idempotency.go:362-374).
- **Existing tests:** The 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT` envelope (code, `POLICY` category, `retryable: true`, `Retry-After` header) is asserted only at tier1 in pkg/gateway/middleware/idempotency/idempotency_test.go::TestWrap_AtomicClaim_ConcurrentRetryGetsInFlight_spec_11_5. The tier3 suite tests/tier3_contract/rest_idempotency/idempotency_test.go covers replay, 422 reuse, oversize-key 400, passthrough, and tenant scoping, but not the in-flight 409. `tests/spec-map.json` §11.5 lists no in-flight case.
- **Gap:** The in-flight rejection is a distinct wire outcome with its own status, error code, and `Retry-After` header that clients must handle, yet no contract test pins it on the wire. This is a missing negative-path contract assertion for a documented error envelope.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. A blocking inner handler (a channel the test releases) wrapped by the middleware is enough; this is the same wiring the tier1 test uses, lifted to the contract tier.
- **Suggested test:** Add TestIdempotencyConcurrentRetryReturns409InFlight to tests/tier3_contract/rest_idempotency/idempotency_test.go that holds the first request open, fires a second with the same key, and asserts HTTP 409, `code == IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_FLIGHT`, `retryable == true`, and a `Retry-After` header.

### - [ ] T-11.5.6 — Scheduled GC sweeper for `idempotency_keys` is untested [Medium] — OPEN

- **Existing tests:** The store-level `DeleteExpired` sweep is tested in tests/tier2_component/stores/idempotencystore_test.go ("DeleteExpired reclaims only rows past the TTL"). The scheduled job that drives it, `sweepIdempotencyKeys` (cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:2094, scheduled at cmd/lenny-gateway/workers.go:1455-1471 on the `--idempotency-gc-interval-seconds` cadence, itself defined at cmd/lenny-gateway/flags.go:1100-1102), has no test. The proposal 0020 reorganization split the former single `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` into `main.go`, `flags.go`, `workers.go`, and `httpsurface.go`; the sweeper function stayed in `main.go` but its flag and its scheduling loop moved. A repository-wide search for a test referencing the scheduler or its interval flag returns none.
- **Gap:** The periodic sweep that enforces "the key may be reused" after the window is wired into the gateway binary but is never exercised: no test proves the watchdog loop iterates tenants, calls `DeleteExpired`, recovers from a per-tenant sweep error (the function logs and continues, main.go:2098-2103), or that a key becomes reusable after the interval elapses. This is a SHOULD-level operational behavior with no component or integration coverage.

- **Existing tests:** Tenant scoping is asserted at tier3 with a MemoryStore (tests/tier3_contract/rest_idempotency/idempotency_test.go::TestIdempotencyTenantScoped), at tier4 through the binary (tests/tier4_integration/idempotency_test.go::TestIdempotencyTenantScopedThroughBinary), and at the store level for Put/Get (tests/tier2_component/stores/idempotencystore_test.go "keys are isolated per tenant"). - **Gap:** The body-cap rejection is a wire-visible error the middleware emits before hashing, and it interacts with the idempotency path specifically (the body must be buffered to hash it). It has no contract-tier assertion, leaving a single low-risk negative path unverified end to end.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The existing tier3 `post` helper can send an oversized payload after the middleware is wrapped with a small `MaxBodyBytes`.
- **Suggested test:** Add TestIdempotencyOversizeBodyRejected to tests/tier3_contract/rest_idempotency/idempotency_test.go wrapping the middleware with a small `MaxBodyBytes`, posting a larger body with an `Idempotency-Key`, and asserting HTTP 413 and `code == BODY_TOO_LARGE`.

## §11.6 Circuit Breakers <a id="t-11.6"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/11_policy-and-controls.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
Reconciliation against `d9074016..HEAD` found two real pieces of drift and one substantive landed feature. First, proposal 0032 (`spec: apply proposals/0032_fix_complete-the-12-4-canonical-redis-key-prefix-table-with-the-.md`, commit `6c0e97f4`) reconciled the pub/sub channel name divergence T-11.6.13 flagged: the spec's two occurrences (`circuit_breaker_events`) were rewritten to the code's literal `cb:events` across `spec/11_policy-and-controls.md` and `spec/12_storage-architecture.md`, so T-11.6.13 is now moot and RESOLVED. Second, `718d0f40` ("F-16.7.1: emit admission.circuit_breaker_cache_stale") landed the stale-serve counter and the sampled `admission.circuit_breaker_cache_stale` audit event T-11.6.3 found entirely unimplemented, with a dedicated unit suite (`pkg/gateway/middleware/circuitbreaker/cachestale_test.go`) pinning the fresh-cache no-op case, the admitted/rejected stale-serve emission, the per-`(replica, outcome)` sampling, and the CacheAge-absent disabled case, wired into the real gateway at `cmd/lenny-gateway/httpsurface.go:754`; T-11.6.3 is RESOLVED. Third, an unrelated code reorganization (proposal 0020, "decompose oversized functions and reorganize pkg/gateway") moved several files this section's findings cite by exact path: `pkg/gateway/admin` to `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin`, `pkg/gateway/gatewaymetrics` to `pkg/gateway/metrics/gatewaymetrics`, `pkg/gateway/breakerstore` to `pkg/gateway/middleware/circuitbreaker/breakerstore`, and the gateway's monolithic `main.go` was split so the `/readyz` handler and the auth-context read the RBAC finding cites now live in `cmd/lenny-gateway/httpsurface.go`. Those path/line references are corrected below (T-11.6.2, T-11.6.5, T-11.6.6, T-11.6.8, T-11.6.9) with no change to the underlying gap. A second, unrelated 1-line net spec edit earlier in the file (proposal 0002, commit `fe3956e8`) shifted every remaining §11.6 spec line citation down by exactly one; those are corrected too (T-11.6.1, T-11.6.2, T-11.6.4, T-11.6.5, T-11.6.6, T-11.6.7, T-11.6.8, T-11.6.9, T-11.6.11, T-11.6.12) with the quoted wording unchanged except where noted. Fourth, proposal 0019 ("close admin-API RBAC scope...") landed a real per-route `x-lenny-scope` enforcement gate (`SCOPE_FORBIDDEN`, commit `c4e80030`) and a generic tier9 regression proving it (`tests/tier9_security/admin_scope_enforce_test.go`), plus a unit test confirming the registry resolves `GET /v1/admin/circuit-breakers` to `tools:circuit_breaker:read` (`pkg/gateway/externalapi/openapi/openapi_test.go`); this closes the fail-open mechanism T-11.6.9 was implicitly worried about, but no test yet drives the breaker endpoints specifically with a scoped JWT, so T-11.6.9 is narrowed and stays OPEN. No other finding's suggested test or gap has landed: the cold-start readiness gate (T-11.6.2), the tier8 Redis-outage assertions (T-11.6.4), the audit-event contract/OCSF conformance test (T-11.6.5), the connector/delegation_depth/message_injection component coverage (T-11.6.6), the concurrent-storm and multi-replica sampling test (T-11.6.7), the pre-chain ordering test through a real gateway (T-11.6.8), the tier7a state-machine scaffold rewire (T-11.6.10), the multi-replica propagation test (T-11.6.11), and the health-service degraded-marking test (T-11.6.12) are all still absent from disk exactly as originally found.
Counts: 5 High, 5 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-11.6.1 — No integration or e2e test drives a real CIRCUIT_BREAKER_OPEN admission rejection through the gateway [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "If any open circuit breaker matches the request, it is rejected immediately with `CIRCUIT_BREAKER_OPEN` (HTTP 503, `retryable: false`); the error body includes `circuit_name`, `reason`, and `opened_at`." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:324)
- **Existing tests:** The tier3 contract test `tests/tier3_contract/rest_circuitbreaker/circuitbreaker_test.go` drives the middleware wrapped around the sessionserver via httptest against an in-memory `MemoryRegistry` (TestOpenOperationTypeBreakerRejects, TestFirstOpenMatchWins). The one tier4 test, `tests/tier4_integration/gateway_redis_e2e_test.go::TestGatewayRedisBreakerE2E`, opens a breaker through the admin API and then reads the `cb:{name}` key from Redis to confirm persistence; it never issues a session-creation request and never asserts a 503. No test searched under tests/tier4_integration, tests/tier5_e2e_kind, or tests/tier6_e2e_cloud asserts `CIRCUIT_BREAKER_OPEN` (grep for the literal returns only spec-map.json and the tier3 contract file).
- **Gap:** The end-to-end operator journey, an operator opening a breaker through the admin API and a subsequent session-creation request being rejected with the documented 503 envelope through the production Redis-backed cache, is unverified. This is a real user journey and the core capability of the subsection. The target tiers are tier4 (compose stack with a real gateway and Redis) and tier5 (Kind). The existing tier4 test exercises only the write side-effect and the tier3 test bypasses the Redis cache entirely.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The gateway harness `tests/testinfra/gateway` and the Redis container `tests/testinfra/containers` already back the existing tier4 test; the Kind harness `tests/testinfra/kind` backs a tier5 variant.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/gateway_circuitbreaker_reject_test.go` driving the real `cmd/lenny-gateway` against a Redis container: open a `runtime`-tier breaker scoped to `echo` through the admin API, then POST `/v1/sessions` with `runtimeRef: echo` and assert HTTP 503, `error.code == CIRCUIT_BREAKER_OPEN`, and the `circuit_name` / `reason` / `opened_at` body fields, using `tests/testinfra/gateway` and `tests/testinfra/containers`.

### - [ ] T-11.6.2 — Cold-start fail-closed readiness (CIRCUIT_BREAKER_CACHE_UNINITIALIZED) is unimplemented and untested [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The replica therefore **refuses readiness** until the startup Redis read succeeds at least once — `/readyz` returns 503 with failure reason `CIRCUIT_BREAKER_CACHE_UNINITIALIZED` and the replica is kept out of the Service load-balancer rotation." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:308)
- **Existing tests:** No test found. Searched pkg, cmd, and tests for `CIRCUIT_BREAKER_CACHE_UNINITIALIZED`, `CacheUninitialized`, and the readiness wiring; the string does not exist anywhere in code or tests. The gateway `/readyz` handler (moved by the 0020 reorganization from the former monolithic `main.go` to `cmd/lenny-gateway/httpsurface.go:645`) gates on `prestopHook.Draining()`, NTP drift, dual-store-down, and `HardDependencyStatus`, and the verdict function `cmd/lenny-gateway/readiness.go:52` does not consult the breaker cache. The `lenny_circuit_breaker_cache_initialized` gauge is set in `pkg/gateway/metrics/gatewaymetrics/gatewaymetrics.go` (moved from `pkg/gateway/gatewaymetrics`) but never feeds the readiness verdict.
- **Gap:** This is a security-relevant fail-closed control: a fresh replica that cannot read Redis at startup must refuse readiness so it does not silently fail-open against operator-declared incident breakers. The control is neither implemented nor tested, so a cold-started replica would be admitted to the Service rotation with an empty breaker cache and would admit every request that an open breaker should reject. The work covers an adversarial / failure scenario (Redis unreachable at replica startup during an active incident) and requires a tier5 Kind test plus a tier2 readiness-handler test. Building the readiness gate is part of this finding.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the readiness verdict to consult a cache-initialized signal (implementation work) and a Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`) able to start a gateway replica with Redis unavailable. Buildable with existing infrastructure once the gate exists.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/circuitbreaker_coldstart_readiness_test.go` that scales Redis to zero, starts a fresh gateway replica, and asserts `/readyz` returns 503 with reason `CIRCUIT_BREAKER_CACHE_UNINITIALIZED` and the pod stays out of the Service endpoints; add a tier2 `cmd/lenny-gateway` readiness test asserting the verdict returns 503 when the breaker cache reports uninitialized, using `tests/testinfra/kind`.

### - [x] T-11.6.3 — Running-replica stale-serve observability (gauge, counter, and audit event) has no emission point and no test [High] — RESOLVED 718d0f40
- **Resolution:** Commit `718d0f40` ("F-16.7.1: emit admission.circuit_breaker_cache_stale (residual 7→6)") wired the §11.6 stale-serve observability onto the admission gate: the breaker middleware (`pkg/gateway/middleware/circuitbreaker/circuitbreaker.go`) compares the `cachingstore` `LastRefresh` age against the 5 s budget on every decision, `AuditReporter.ReportCacheStale` (`pkg/gateway/middleware/circuitbreaker/audit.go`) emits the sampled `admission.circuit_breaker_cache_stale` audit event per `(replica, outcome)` window and increments the new `lenny_circuit_breaker_cache_stale_serves_total{outcome}` counter (`pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:309`, `pkg/observability/audit/catalog.go:44`), and `cmd/lenny-gateway/httpsurface.go:754` feeds the real `cachingstore` age into the gate. The dedicated unit suite `pkg/gateway/middleware/circuitbreaker/cachestale_test.go` (`TestCacheStaleFreshCacheNoEvent_spec_16_7`, `TestCacheStaleAdmittedServeEmits_spec_16_7`, `TestCacheStaleRejectedServeEmits_spec_16_7`, `TestCacheStaleServeIsSampled_spec_11_6`, `TestCacheStaleDisabledWithoutCacheAge_spec_16_7`) pins the fresh-cache no-op case, the admitted/rejected stale-serve emission with the correct `outcome` and `replica_service_instance_id` payload fields, the per-window sampling (5 serves collapse to 1 audit row while the counter still counts all 5), and the disabled-without-CacheAge case. This coverage is at the unit tier (an injected `CacheAge` function and a fake appender/metrics recorder) rather than the tier2-component-against-real-Redis test originally suggested, but it exercises the exact behavior the spec requires end to end through the real middleware and is wired into the production gateway, so the implementation-and-verification gap this finding raised is closed.

### - [ ] T-11.6.4 — The tier8 Redis-outage chaos test does not assert any §11.6 admission posture [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The cache's 5 s poll/TTL (above) expires but the replica continues to serve admission decisions against the last-known cache contents. Stale-serve duration is tracked in the `lenny_circuit_breaker_cache_stale_seconds` gauge (§16.1), and the `CircuitBreakerStale` alert (§16.5) fires when it exceeds 60 s." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:307)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier8_chaos/store_failure_test.go::TestRedisClusterDegraded` cites §11.6 in its diagnosis comment, but its assertions are confined to the §25.3 health report: the gateway liveness probe stays 200, the report flags the `redis` component unhealthy with the `redis-failure` runbook, and the report recovers after restore (the shared body is `assertStoreOutageDegrades`). It never opens a breaker, never issues an admission request during the outage, and never checks the stale gauge, the `CircuitBreakerStale` alert, or that an open breaker continues to reject while Redis is down.
- **Gap:** The distinctive §11.6 Redis-outage behavior, that an open breaker keeps rejecting against the in-process cache while Redis is down and the stale-serve gauge climbs toward the `CircuitBreakerStale` threshold, is asserted nowhere. The chaos tier verifies only that the process survives the outage. The work is a failure / resilience scenario at tier8 (chaos) and reuses the existing Kind store-outage injector. The current test name implies §11.6 coverage that the assertions do not provide.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The injector (`kubectl scale deploy lenny-redis --replicas=0`) and the gateway probe helpers already exist in `tests/tier8_chaos` and `tests/testinfra/kind`.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `tests/tier8_chaos/store_failure_test.go` (or add `circuitbreaker_redis_outage_test.go`) to open a `runtime`-scoped breaker before scaling Redis to zero, assert that session-creation for that runtime still returns 503 `CIRCUIT_BREAKER_OPEN` during the outage, and assert `lenny_circuit_breaker_cache_stale_seconds` rises above zero, using the existing `tests/testinfra/kind` injector.

### - [ ] T-11.6.5 — The breaker audit events have no contract or OCSF conformance test pinning their schema [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Every state change emits a `circuit_breaker.state_changed` audit event containing: `circuit_name`, `old_state`, `new_state`, `reason`, `limit_tier` ..., `scope` ..., `operator_sub`, `operator_tenant_id`, `timestamp`. Every request REJECTed by a tripped breaker emits an `admission.circuit_breaker_rejected` audit event containing: `circuit_name`, `reason`, `opened_at`, `limit_tier` ..., `replica_service_instance_id` ..., and the admission-time request snapshot ... §16.7 is the authoritative schema source for this event." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:328)
- **Existing tests:** The field set is asserted at the unit level by `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/breakers_test.go::TestOpenBreakerEmitsStateChangedAuditPayload_spec_16_7_673` (moved from `pkg/gateway/admin` by the 0020 reorganization) and `pkg/gateway/middleware/circuitbreaker/audit_test.go::TestReportWritesFullAuditRow`, both against in-process fakes. No test under tests/ references either event type; grep for `circuit_breaker.state_changed` or `admission.circuit_breaker_rejected` across tests returns nothing. The OCSF mapping at `pkg/audit/ocsf/mapping.go:116` (line shifted from :106) assigns activity classes to both events (and now also to `admission.circuit_breaker_cache_stale`, landed alongside T-11.6.3) but has no conformance test that emits a real event and validates the projected OCSF row against the schema.
- **Gap:** Both events are part of the persisted audit surface that SIEM operators query, and the spec ties their `limit_tier` vocabulary to the rejection metric for exact label correlation. There is no tier3 contract or tier10 conformance test that pins the on-the-wire JSON shape against the §16.7 catalogue or the OCSF projection, so a field rename or an OCSF class drift would ship unnoticed. The work is a standards-conformance check at tier3 (audit-row schema) and tier10 (OCSF fidelity).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the §16.7 audit-event schema fixtures and the OCSF mapping golden under `tests/testinfra/audit`. If those goldens do not yet enumerate the breaker events, adding them is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier3 audit-schema contract case that drives the gateway to emit `circuit_breaker.state_changed` and `admission.circuit_breaker_rejected`, then validates each row against the §16.7 field schema; add a tier10 OCSF case asserting the projected class for both events, using `tests/testinfra/audit`.

### - [ ] T-11.6.6 — The connector, delegation_depth, and message_injection admission tiers are never matched in a component-or-higher test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`limit_tier: 'connector'` / `scope: { 'connector': Z }` matches a connector invocation whose registered connector id equals `Z`; `limit_tier: 'operation_type'` / `scope: { 'operation_type': op }` matches an admission attempt for the named operation class (`uploads`, `delegation_depth`, `session_creation`, `message_injection`)." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:324)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/circuitbreaker/circuitbreaker_test.go` exercises `TestMatchConnectorTier` and `TestMatchOperationTypeTier` at the unit level. At the contract tier and above, only the `runtime`, `pool`, and `operation_type:session_creation`/`uploads` cases appear: `tests/tier3_contract/rest_circuitbreaker/circuitbreaker_test.go` uses only `TierOperationType` with `OpSessionCreation` and `OpUploads`, and `tests/tier2_component/breakers/*` uses only `TierRuntime` and `TierPool`. No component-or-higher test matches a `connector` breaker against a connector invocation, or a `delegation_depth` / `message_injection` breaker against the corresponding admission attempt. The gateway middleware `defaultExtract` (`pkg/gateway/middleware/circuitbreaker/circuitbreaker.go:196`, line shifted from :158) only maps `POST /v1/sessions` to `OpSessionCreation`.
- **Gap:** Half of the closed `operation_type` value set and the entire `connector` tier are exercised only by unit tests of the pure match function, not through the request path where the operation class and connector id are resolved from a real request. A breaker scoped to `connector` or to `delegation_depth` could fail to match at admission and the gap would not be caught. This is a deployment-combination and behavioral-tier gap at tier3 (contract) and tier4 (a real delegation or connector invocation).
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today for the operation-type cases. The connector and delegation-child cases need the delegation admission path and a connector invocation wired through the middleware extractor; the stub connector in `tests/testinfra/stubs` and the session driver in `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver` support this.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `tests/tier3_contract/rest_circuitbreaker/circuitbreaker_test.go` with `delegation_depth` and `message_injection` operation-type cases, and add a tier4 case that opens a `connector`-scoped breaker and asserts a connector invocation for that id is rejected with `CIRCUIT_BREAKER_OPEN`, using `tests/testinfra/stubs` and `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`.

### - [ ] T-11.6.7 — Sampling under breaker storms is verified only at unit level, never under concurrent load through the gateway [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "the **first** rejection per `(tenant_id, circuit_name, caller_sub)` tuple within any rolling 10-second window is written as a full audit row ...; subsequent rejections in the same window increment `lenny_circuit_breaker_rejections_suppressed_total` ... but do **not** write individual rows. ... The sampling window is tracked in **each gateway replica's in-memory admission-controller state** ... explicitly per-replica, no Redis or EventBus coordination." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:330)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/middleware/circuitbreaker/audit_test.go::TestReportSamplesPerTupleWithinWindow` verifies the per-tuple window, the suppression counter, and window expiry against an injected clock and an in-process fake appender. No test drives the sampling path under concurrent rejection volume through the real gateway, and no test asserts the per-replica locality property (that two replicas serving the same caller each write at most one row per window).
- **Gap:** The sampling discipline protects the per-tenant advisory-locked audit write path from a misbehaving client retry loop against a tripped breaker. That contention is a concurrency property the unit test cannot reproduce, and the per-replica locality claim is untested across replicas. The work is a failure / load scenario at tier7 (load) and a multi-replica tier4 or tier5 check. The current coverage is single-threaded and single-instance.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a load generator able to hammer a tripped breaker (`tests/testinfra/loadgen`) and a multi-replica gateway deployment for the locality check (`tests/testinfra/kind`).
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier7a_load_local/scenarios/circuit_breaker_rejection_storm` driving high-rate session-creation against an open breaker and asserting `lenny_circuit_breaker_rejections_total` greatly exceeds the audit rows written while `lenny_circuit_breaker_rejections_suppressed_total` accounts for the delta; add a tier5 two-replica case asserting at most one audit row per replica per window, using `tests/testinfra/loadgen` and `tests/testinfra/kind`.

### - [ ] T-11.6.8 — The pre-chain gate ordering (POL-014) is not asserted end to end through the gateway [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Circuit-breaker evaluation is a **pre-chain gate** ... It runs **after `AuthEvaluator` completes at `PreAuth`** and **before the `PostAuth` and `PreDelegation` interceptor chains run** ... so that the `admission.circuit_breaker_rejected` audit payload carries the authenticated caller identity (`caller_sub`, `caller_tenant_id`)." (spec/11_policy-and-controls.md:326)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/middleware/circuitbreaker/audit_test.go::TestMiddlewareEmitsAuditOnMatch` confirms the middleware emits a row with `caller_sub` from an injected snapshot, but the snapshot is supplied directly by the test rather than resolved from a real authenticated principal. The gateway wires the snapshot from `authmw.FromContext` at `cmd/lenny-gateway/httpsurface.go:738` (moved from the former monolithic `main.go:4735` by the 0020 reorganization). No test asserts the ordering invariant through the gateway: that an unauthenticated request is rejected by auth before the breaker gate runs, and that a breaker rejection of an authenticated request carries the real `caller_sub` / `caller_tenant_id` resolved by the auth middleware.
- **Gap:** The ordering is the rationale for the entire pre-chain placement, and it is the reason the rejection audit row can carry tenant-scoped accounting. A regression that moved the gate before auth would emit rejection rows with an empty caller identity, and no test would catch it. The work is a real adversarial-ordering check at tier3 or tier4 through the assembled gateway middleware stack.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The gateway harness `tests/testinfra/gateway` and the token service helper `tests/testinfra/tokenservice` provide an authenticated caller.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/circuitbreaker_prechain_order_test.go` that sends an unauthenticated request to an open-breaker route and asserts a 401 (auth wins) and then an authenticated request and asserts the 503 rejection plus an `admission.circuit_breaker_rejected` audit row carrying the authenticated `caller_sub` and `caller_tenant_id`, using `tests/testinfra/gateway` and `tests/testinfra/tokenservice`.

- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/breakers_test.go::TestBreakerEndpointsRequirePlatformAdmin` (moved from `pkg/gateway/admin` by the 0020 reorganization) asserts a tenant-admin principal receives 403 on all four endpoints, at the unit level against the in-memory router with dev-header roles rather than scoped JWTs. Since this finding was written, proposal 0019 ("close admin-API RBAC scope...", commit `c4e80030`) landed a real per-route `x-lenny-scope` enforcement gate (`scopeGate`, `403 SCOPE_FORBIDDEN`) ahead of every admin handler, proven generically at the security tier by `tests/tier9_security/admin_scope_enforce_test.go::TestAdminScopeGateRejectsNarrowedToken_spec_15_1_25_1` (using the `tools:audit:*` domain, not `circuit_breaker`), and a route-resolution unit test confirms `GET /v1/admin/circuit-breakers` resolves to `tools:circuit_breaker:read` in the canonical registry (`pkg/gateway/externalapi/openapi/openapi_test.go::TestRouteScopesResolvesCanonicalScope_spec_15_1_914`). What remains unverified is the breaker-domain-specific end-to-end path: a real `tools:circuit_breaker:read` token driven through the gate against the actual `open`/`close` write endpoints, and confirmation the generic mechanism engages correctly for this domain rather than only for `audit`.
