## §12.4 Redis HA and Failure Modes <a id="t-12.4"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/12_storage-architecture.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§12.4 has strong tier-2 component coverage for its arithmetic and key-isolation surface. The tenant-prefix Guard (`TestRedisTenantKeyIsolation`, and the new `pkg/gateway/storage/rediskeys` unit suite) covers all six mandated key classes plus the wrapper's own admit/reject decision, the fail-open controller and cumulative timer are exercised against fake counters, the Postgres advisory-lock leasestore runs against a real Postgres container, and AWS ElastiCache TLS, AUTH, eviction-policy, and cluster-mode are verified at tier-6. Since the 2026-06-03 audit, two things landed that resolve findings in this section. First, BUILD-GAPS F-12.4.24 (commit `2c5a4d59`) replaced the `TestRedisSentinelFailover` `t.Logf` scaffold with a real chaos test that kills a compose Sentinel-topology master and asserts automatic replica promotion and Sentinel-aware client failover, closing T-12.4.1 and making the `redis-sentinel-failover` runbook binding genuine. Second, proposal 0002 (the session/service execution-model rework) added a new §12.4 failure-behavior row — the session-mode slot counter's Postgres fallback under a per-pod advisory lock, bounded to `slotCounterPostgresFallbackMaxSeconds` before failing closed — and landed it with component and chaos coverage from the same commits that introduced it (`5fbda4c3`, `686e20f3`), so the new requirement is filed and resolved in the same pass (T-12.4.12). Separately, proposal 0032 completed the §12.4 canonical key-prefix table with several previously undocumented prefixes the gateway already wrote (`rl:`, `sq:`, `derive_lock:`, `lenny:events:`, the playground `pg:*` family, `conn:oauth:state:`) and rewrote the exception-class summary into two categories; the registry-completeness and summary-agreement claims are pinned by new tier-11 doc-consistency tests (`tests/tier11_docs/redis_key_prefix_registry_test.go`), and each new prefix's functional behavior is covered in its owning component (`pkg/gateway/storage/derivelock`, `pkg/connectoroauth`, `pkg/gateway/session/sessionevents`, `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground`), so no new gap is filed for the registry expansion itself. The remaining live-failure surface is unchanged and still weaker than the unit tier: the per-tenant and per-user fail-open ceilings, the cumulative fail-open financial-security control, and the `quota_failopen_started` audit emission are verified only against an in-process erroring counter, never against a genuine Redis outage at integration or security tier. The live Redis plaintext-rejection probe (TESTING.md §12.9.2) is still a skipped tier-9 scaffold, the cached-access-token AES-256-GCM ciphertext-at-rest format is asserted nowhere, the cluster-mode hash-tag slot co-location is verified only at unit level and only on AWS, and spec-map.json §12.4 still lists two packages (`pkg/store/lease`, `pkg/store/quota`) that do not exist on disk.
Counts: 3 High, 6 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info (across 12 findings, 2 resolved).

### Findings

### - [x] T-12.4.1 — Redis Sentinel automatic failover has no live chaos test and the runbook gate is satisfied by a skipped scaffold [High] — RESOLVED 2c5a4d59 (reconciled against BUILD-GAPS F-12.4.24)
- **Resolution:** BUILD-GAPS F-12.4.24 (commit `2c5a4d59`, "F-12.4.24: live Redis Sentinel failover chaos test; F-12.6.21 defer re-characterized") replaced the `t.Logf` stub with a real chaos exercise, `tests/tier8_chaos/redis_sentinel_failover_test.go::TestRedisSentinelFailover`. It brings up the compose Sentinel topology (one master, one replica, three sentinels, quorum 2), asserts the production `redisconn.NewClient` constructor builds a `FailoverClient` over the live sentinel addresses, seeds and replicates a canary key to the replica, `docker kill`s the master, asserts the sentinel quorum promotes the replica to master within the failover window, asserts the pre-failover canary survives on the promoted master, and drives an in-network client that resolves the master through the Sentinel protocol (`SENTINEL get-master-addr-by-name`, the exact resolution go-redis's `FailoverClient` performs) and writes/reads against the newly promoted node. `tests/tier8_chaos/runbook-map.yaml`'s `redis-sentinel-failover` binding now points at this real test, so the `TestRunbookMapCoverage` gate is satisfied by genuine master-kill-and-promotion coverage rather than a no-op. The finding's suggested Kind e2e overlay with a `--redis-sentinel-addrs` gateway install path was not built; the resolution instead exercises the topology through the existing compose Sentinel stack, which the finding had already identified as available and sufficient to prove automatic promotion and Sentinel-aware client failover end to end.

### - [ ] T-12.4.2 — Bounded fail-open and the cumulative financial-security control are never exercised against a real Redis outage [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Rate limit counters | Fail open with bounded window — allow requests for up to rateLimitFailOpenMaxSeconds (default: 60s), then fail closed" (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:216) and "quotaFailOpenCumulativeMaxSeconds is a financial security control ... the replica transitions to fail-closed for quota enforcement" (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:236).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/failopen/controller_test.go` and `cumulative_test.go` cover the controller, the per-user and per-tenant ceilings, the sliding-window cumulative timer, the state-file persistence, and the CrashLoopBackOff cold-start reset, all with a `fakeClock` and unit constructors. `pkg/gateway/middleware/ratelimit/failopen_integration_test.go` drives the middleware with an `erroringCounter`/`togglingCounter` that returns an error on every `Incr`, simulating an outage without a Redis backend. No test disables a genuine Redis instance and asserts the gateway transitions allow-then-429 at the bounded window, then fails closed after `quotaFailOpenCumulativeMaxSeconds`.
- **Gap:** The financial-exposure control (cumulative fail-open then fail-closed) is the security-relevant path and is verified only against an in-process fake. A regression in the wiring between the live Redis health signal and the controller's `Enter`/`Exit` edges would pass every existing test. This needs both a failure-path integration test (real Redis outage) and a security-tier verification that the cumulative cap bounds total overshoot. Target tier-8 chaos and tier-9 security. TESTING.md:1641 records `tests/tier8_chaos/redis_down_during_policy_check.go` as deferred for exactly this fail-open/fail-closed behavior under a disableable Redis.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a Redis instance the chaos harness can disable mid-run and a clock-injection seam wired through the live gateway so the cumulative window can be advanced without a 300s wall-clock wait (`tests/testinfra/timectl` or `clockstep`). The clock seam through the live binary does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding. (Note: `tests/tier8_chaos/slot_counter_redis_outage_test.go` now demonstrates the pattern of a disableable-Redis-plus-injected-clock chaos test for the adjacent slot-counter fallback (T-12.4.12); a similar harness shape is reusable here, though the live gateway binary itself is not yet wired through it.)
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier8_chaos/redis_failopen_bounded_test.go` driving the real `cmd/lenny-gateway` against a `tests/testinfra/containers` Redis: cut Redis, assert 200s during the bounded window, assert 429 after, advance the injected clock past the cumulative cap, and assert quota fails closed. Add a tier-9 companion asserting cluster-wide overshoot stays under `min(N × per_replica_hard_cap, ...)`.

### - [ ] T-12.4.3 — Live Redis plaintext-connection rejection is a skipped tier-9 scaffold [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Security: Redis AUTH (ACLs) and TLS are required." (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:208) and TESTING.md §12.9.2 "Plaintext connections to Postgres, PgBouncer, Redis ... are rejected." (TESTING.md:1246).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/tlsprobe/tlsprobe_test.go::TestRedisTLSEnforcement_spec_10_3_373` stands up loopback TLS-only and plaintext listeners and asserts the probe passes the first and fails the second (a unit-level probe, no real Redis). `pkg/redisconn/enforce_test.go` asserts the client constructor refuses a plaintext `redis://` URL. `tests/tier9_security/scaffolds_test.go::TestTLSPlaintextRejection` (line 111) is still skipped with the diagnosis that the e2e `datastores.yaml` runs plaintext for reachability, so the live probe has no TLS-configured store to assert against. The tier-9 `tls_test.go` covers only the §10.3 internal mTLS Certificate readiness, not Redis transit encryption.
- **Gap:** No test connects to a real in-cluster Redis over plaintext and asserts the connection is refused at the engine. The self-managed TLS-required control is verified end to end only on AWS ElastiCache (T-12.4.6), never on the self-managed Sentinel/single-node topology the spec's "required" applies to. This is a security control unverified end to end on the default deployment. Target tier-9 security.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a TLS-configured Redis fixture in the e2e overlay (a `redis-tls` variant of `tests/testinfra/k8s/datastores.yaml` with a cert and `--tls-port`). The current overlay runs plaintext for reachability; building the TLS variant and threading its CA to the probe is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add a TLS-configured Redis to the security overlay and convert `tests/tier9_security/scaffolds_test.go::TestTLSPlaintextRejection` into a live test that dials the Redis plaintext port from a probe pod (via `tests/testinfra/security`) and asserts a connection reset, then dials over TLS with AUTH and asserts a successful PING.

- **Spec/Doc:** "When a replica enters fail-open mode, it emits a quota_failopen_started audit event ... containing tenant_id, service_instance_id ... and timestamp, enabling billing consumers to detect and attribute overshoot windows." (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:236).

No integration or security test asserts the event reaches the §11.7 hash-chained audit log with the required `tenant_id` and `service_instance_id` attributes during a genuine fail-open episode.
- **Gap:** The audit emission is the billing-attribution control for fail-open overshoot windows, and the wiring from the controller's emitter to the persisted audit log is unverified end to end. A real user journey here is a billing consumer reconstructing an overshoot window from the audit stream. Target tier-4 integration (or fold into the tier-8 chaos test in T-12.4.2), asserting the event row with its attributes against the audit store.

### - [ ] T-12.4.5 — Cached access tokens are not asserted to be AES-256-GCM ciphertext at rest in Redis [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Cached access tokens are encrypted before storage in Redis (not stored as plaintext) ... using AES-256-GCM ... each cached token is stored as {nonce || ciphertext || tag}" (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:208).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/tokenservice/cache/cache_test.go::TestPutGetRoundtrip` round-trips claims through the envelope-encrypted cache against miniredis and asserts the decrypted subject and tenant. `New` is asserted to reject a nil KMS provider (encryption mandatory). No test reads the raw stored bytes and asserts they are not the plaintext claims, nor that the layout is the mandated `nonce || ciphertext || tag`.
- **Gap:** A round-trip test passes even if a future change stored the token in cleartext and read it back, because both sides use the same (broken) codec. The negative assertion (the stored blob is ciphertext, the plaintext token never appears) is the security-relevant check and is missing. Target tier-2 component, asserting the on-disk Redis value against the AES-256-GCM format.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today against the existing miniredis fixture in `pkg/tokenservice/cache`.
- **Suggested test:** Add `pkg/tokenservice/cache/atrest_test.go` that Puts a token, reads the raw value with the miniredis client, asserts the plaintext token string does not appear in the bytes, and asserts the prefix length matches the GCM nonce so the `nonce || ciphertext || tag` framing holds.

- **Spec/Doc:** "The t:{tenant_id}: key prefix convention ... ensures all keys for a given tenant hash to the same slot, preserving multi-key operation correctness for per-tenant Lua scripts." (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:275) and the delegation `{root_session_id}` hash tag "distributes different delegation trees across Redis Cluster slots while co-locating all keys for one tree on the same slot (required for multi-key Lua atomicity)" (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:195).

A multi-key Lua script that worked on Sentinel could raise CROSSSLOT on a real cluster, and no test would catch it. - **Suggested test:** Extend `TestCloudRedisClusterMode` (or add a sibling) to invoke the delegation-budget reserve script with multiple `{root}`-tagged keys against the multi-shard cluster and assert no CROSSSLOT error, confirming the hash-tag co-location holds on real sharding.

### - [ ] T-12.4.9 — Experiment sticky re-derivation on Redis outage is verified only at the cache layer, not at the gateway assignment path [Low] — OPEN

No test drives a session creation through the gateway with Redis down and asserts the variant is re-derived from the hash (rather than the request failing because the cache Get errored).

The spec's no-data-loss guarantee depends on the gateway swallowing the cache error and recomputing. ### - [x] T-12.4.12 — Session-mode slot counter's Redis-outage Postgres fallback (new §12.4 failure-behavior row) landed with chaos and component coverage from inception [Medium] — RESOLVED 686e20f3 (reconciled against proposal 0002)
- **Resolution:** Proposal 0002 (session/service execution-model rework) added the §12.4 failure-behavior table row for the session-mode slot counter (`lenny:pod:{pod_id}:active_slots`): on Redis unavailability the gateway gates intra-pod session capacity on `SessionStore.GetActiveSlotsByPod` under a per-pod Postgres advisory lock, bounded by `slotCounterPostgresFallbackMaxSeconds` (default 60s) before failing closed, with rehydration through the standard blocking-rehydration path on Redis recovery. The requirement landed with test coverage in the same change series rather than as a later-discovered gap: commit `5fbda4c3` ("0002 S19: per-pod occupancy claim claim-<podName>, Postgres-fallback slot gate, stop gateway Sandbox.status writes") added `tests/tier2_component/stores/reserve_slot_under_lock_test.go::TestReserveSlotUnderLock` against a real Postgres, asserting the gate admits below the bound counting only live sessions, rejects at the bound, and serializes concurrent admissions under the per-pod advisory lock so two racers cannot both observe the same free slot. Commit `686e20f3` ("0002 S28a: fail-closed slot release on nil counter, extract §12.4 Redis-outage Postgres fallback") added `tests/tier8_chaos/slot_counter_redis_outage_test.go::TestSlotCounterSurvivesRedisOutageAndRecovers`, which drives `pkg/gateway/storage/slotcounter` against real Postgres and Redis containers with an injected clock: it stops Redis and asserts the gate degrades to the Postgres fallback rather than rejecting all dispatch, asserts concurrent admissions during the outage do not overrun the per-pod bound, advances the injected clock past the 60s fallback window and asserts the gate fails closed, then restarts Redis and asserts the counter rehydrates from Postgres on the first post-recovery reservation and resumes enforcing the Redis-side cap. Both tests carry `// spec: 12.4` (or `3.2`/`6.57`/`5.2` cross-references) annotations. No further test is needed for this requirement; it is filed here so the audit records that the new failure-behavior row has coverage rather than showing as an unaudited gap.

## §12.5 Artifact Store <a id="t-12.5"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/12_storage-architecture.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§12.5 has dense unit and component coverage for the catalog lifecycle, the MinIO-backed blob store round-trip, the T4 SSE-KMS fail-closed write path, per-slot checkpoint rotation, the retention GC tick, the continuous T4 KMS probe, the bucket-lifecycle Helm render, the drain-readiness webhook posture and decision logic, the alert-rule presence, and the `node.drain.forced` OCSF event. The integration, e2e, chaos, and security tiers are thin. The MinIO-outage-to-Postgres-minimal-state durability journey is a `t.Skip` chaos scaffold, no checkpoint-to-resume journey exercises a real workspace restore, the S3, GCS, and Azure Blob backends run only against in-memory SDK fakes with every cloud parity-matrix row marked `planned`, the tenant-prefix isolation control has no security-tier adversarial test, the GC single-writer guarantee is never exercised under a real `lenny-gateway-leader` failover, and the eviction-rejection half of the drain webhook is explicitly deferred off Kind. The spec-map entry also points at a nonexistent package and a mismatched scaffold path. A `pkg/gateway` code-organization refactor since generation (proposal 0020, "group the storage cluster under `pkg/gateway/storage`" / "group the checkpoint store under `pkg/gateway/checkpoint`") moved several of the unit-tier packages this section cites; the underlying tests still exist and pass, only their paths changed. Counts: 3 High, 6 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-12.5.1 — MinIO-outage-during-checkpoint minimal-state fallback is a t.Skip chaos scaffold [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Prolonged MinIO unavailability degrades session durability — any pod eviction during an outage that exhausts all MinIO retries falls back to the Postgres minimal state record ... sessions resume with conversation context but workspace state is lost." (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:294)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier8_chaos/minio_outage_during_checkpoint_test.go:64` defines `TestMinIOOutageDuringCheckpoint` but its body is `t.Skip("tier-8 live exercise — requires toxiproxy + testcontainers MinIO ...")`. The fallback writer is covered at unit level only in `pkg/gateway/storage/evictionfallback/evictionfallback_test.go` (`TestWriteRetriesPostgresFailover`, `TestWriteExhaustsRetryBudgetThenDrivesTotalLoss`; package relocated from `pkg/gateway/evictionfallback` by the proposal-0020 storage-cluster regroup) and in `tests/tier2_component/stores/evictionfallback_test.go`. No tier4/5/8 test drives a real eviction into an unreachable MinIO and asserts the Postgres minimal-state record is written and the session resumes with conversation context.
- **Gap:** The central durability failure path of §12.5 is unverified above the unit tier. The work is an adversarial failure scenario: inject a MinIO outage mid-checkpoint, evict the pod, and assert the documented degraded-resume behavior plus `lenny_checkpoint_storage_failure_total` advancement. Target tier8 chaos with a tier4 integration companion.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a toxiproxy sidecar and a testcontainers MinIO in the chaos overlay (referenced in the scaffold but not built). The chaos building blocks live in `tests/testinfra/chaos`; the MinIO container helper is `tests/testinfra/containers`. Building the toxiproxy-fronted MinIO overlay is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Implement the body of `tests/tier8_chaos/minio_outage_during_checkpoint_test.go` using `tests/testinfra/chaos` toxiproxy plus `tests/testinfra/containers` MinIO to fail the bucket mid-write, then assert the `session_eviction_state` row carries the inline `last_message_context` and the session resumes; add a tier4 companion in `tests/tier4_integration/checkpoint_minimal_state_test.go` against the compose stack.

### - [ ] T-12.5.2 — No checkpoint-to-resume end-to-end journey restores a workspace from the artifact store [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Keep only the latest 2 checkpoints per active session. ... On pools with `sessionPolicy.maxConcurrentSessions > 1` ... checkpoints are per-slot — the 'latest 2' limit applies independently to each slot" (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:325) and the durability contract that a resumed session restores workspace state (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:294).
- **Existing tests:** Per-slot rotation is covered at component tier in `pkg/gateway/checkpoint/checkpointretention/checkpointretention_test.go:258` (`TestRotate_PerSlotIndependent`; package relocated from `pkg/gateway/checkpointretention` by the proposal-0020 checkpoint-store regroup). The MinIO round-trip is `tests/tier2_component/stores/miniostore_test.go:54`. TESTING.md:1683 records `tests/tier4_integration/checkpoint_resume_test.go` as deferred, and a filesystem search confirms no `checkpoint_resume` test exists at any tier. `tests/tier4_integration/session_lifecycle_test.go:35` drives REST create-to-terminate but never uploads, checkpoints, or restores a workspace artifact.
- **Gap:** The persona journey where alice's session is evicted, checkpointed to MinIO, and resumed on a new pod with the workspace restored is unverified end to end. This is a real user journey and the headline durability guarantee of the artifact store. Target tier5 e2e on Kind with a tier4 compose-stack companion.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`) with a MinIO-bearing datastore overlay and the session driver (`tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`). The Kind harness exists; the eviction-and-resume driver step is the new piece and is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/checkpoint_resume_test.go` driving create-to-upload-to-evict-to-resume via `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`, asserting the restored pod reads the workspace snapshot that the original pod wrote to MinIO; add `tests/tier4_integration/checkpoint_resume_test.go` for the compose-stack variant.

### - [ ] T-12.5.3 — Cloud-managed object-storage backends (S3, GCS, Azure Blob) are exercised only against in-memory SDK fakes [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Cloud-managed deployments should use the provider's native object storage (AWS S3, GCP Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage) ... Self-managed deployments use MinIO." (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:284)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/blobstore/s3/s3_test.go`, `pkg/blobstore/gcs/gcs_test.go`, and `pkg/blobstore/azureblob/azureblob_test.go` all construct in-process fakes (`newFakeS3`, `newFakeBlob`) rather than real backends or emulators. The `cloud_csi` parity-matrix entry (`tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml:70`) is `planned` for gke, eks, and aks. `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/cluster_assertions_test.go:379` (`TestMultiAZMinIO`) asserts only chart wiring (S3-or-MinIO, never both), not artifact round-trips against a live S3 bucket.
- **Gap:** The same interface is claimed to pass against every provider backend (TESTING.md:1114), but no validated cloud e2e exercises a real S3, GCS, or Azure Blob round-trip, SSE-KMS application, or tenant-prefix `DeleteByTenant` against a live bucket. This is a deployment-combination gap spanning three providers and a public capability claim with no cloud conformance. Target tier6 e2e cloud.
- **Dependencies:** Requires provisioned per-provider buckets and credentials via `scripts/cloud/<provider>/up.sh` and the `tests/testinfra/cloud` guard. The buckets and the `cloud_csi` test body do not exist yet; provisioning and writing them is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/cloud_csi_test.go` gated by `requireCloud`, running the shared blobstore contract (Put/Get/Stat, SoftDelete, DeleteByTenant, SSE-KMS) against the provider-native bucket for each of gke/eks/aks, and flip the `cloud_csi` parity-matrix rows to `validated` when green.

### - [ ] T-12.5.4 — Tenant-prefix isolation on the artifact store has no security-tier adversarial test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The `ArtifactStore` implementation validates the `tenant_id` prefix on every operation — no S3 call is issued unless the caller's authenticated `tenant_id` matches the path prefix. This validation lives at the interface boundary" (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:307)
- **Existing tests:** Cross-tenant `Copy` rejection is covered in `pkg/blobstore/fsstore_test.go:188` (`ErrCrossTenant`) and `DeleteByTenant` cross-tenant leak protection is in `pkg/blobstore/s3/s3_test.go:400`, `pkg/blobstore/gcs/gcs_test.go:333`, and `pkg/blobstore/azureblob/azureblob_test.go:288`, all at unit tier. The tier9 security suite `tests/tier9_security/tenant_isolation_test.go:50` (`TestTenantIsolationCrossStore`) covers only the Postgres-backed audit chain and contains no artifact, blob, or MinIO assertion.
- **Gap:** The §12.9.1-class control that one tenant cannot read or delete another tenant's checkpoints, workspace snapshots, or transcripts is unverified against a real object store from a hostile-caller position. This is an adversarial scenario and a security control. Target tier9 security.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the security store helpers (`tests/testinfra/security`, `tests/tier9_security/store_helpers_test.go`) plus a real MinIO container from `tests/testinfra/containers`. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier9_security/artifact_tenant_isolation_test.go` that seeds artifacts under `/acme/*` and `/globex/*` on a real MinIO, then asserts a caller authenticated as `globex` receives an authorization failure on Get, Stat, and DeleteByTenant against an `acme`-prefixed key, with no S3 call issued.

### - [ ] T-12.5.5 — Drain-readiness eviction rejection is never exercised end to end against a real pods/eviction on Kind [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "If the endpoint returns `503` or is unreachable, the webhook rejects the eviction with: 'Node drain blocked: MinIO health check failed — defer drain until MinIO is healthy (STR-006)'. The webhook is deployed with `failurePolicy: Fail`" (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:303)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/admission_featuregated_test.go:220` (`TestDrainReadinessWebhook`) asserts only webhook posture (failurePolicy, pods/eviction CREATE rule, caBundle, gateway callback URL) and its doc-comment explicitly states "the rejection half is covered by the tier-2/3 component suites." The decision logic is covered in `pkg/admission/drain_readiness/guard_test.go:27` and `pkg/admission/webhook/drain_readiness_test.go:92`. `tests/tier8_chaos/store_failure_test.go:101` (`TestMinIOUnavailable`) verifies the `/internal/drain-readiness` 503 transition but does not issue a `pods/eviction` and assert the API server rejects it.
- **Gap:** No test confirms that a real `CREATE pods/eviction` against the Kind API server is rejected by the deployed webhook while MinIO is unhealthy. The component test calls the decision function directly, bypassing the admission-webhook path. This is an adversarial failure scenario for the drain-blocking control. Target tier5 e2e on Kind.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`) and a way to drive the gateway probe to 503 without disrupting parallel suites (the existing test cites this as the blocker). The admission helpers live in `tests/testinfra/admission`. A scoped single-node Kind run isolates the probe state; building that isolation is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/drain_readiness_eviction_test.go` that scales MinIO to zero, issues a `policy/v1 Eviction` for a Ready agent pod via the client-go subresource, and asserts a 403 carrying the STR-006 rejection message, then restores MinIO and asserts the eviction succeeds.

## §12.6 Interface Design <a id="t-12.6"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/12_storage-architecture.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
Four of the five §12.6 scaling-extension interfaces have real coverage. StoreRouter, PodRegistry (both CRD and Postgres variants), EventBus, and CredentialGenerator carry tier2 component tests against real backing services plus a tier3 CloudEvents contract suite, and the scatter-gather bounds and retranscribe worker have thorough unit coverage. Since the 2026-06-03 audit, the fifth interface landed: `pkg/podregistry/clusterregistry.go` now implements `ClusterRegistry`/`RemotePodOperations`/`LocalClusterRegistry` with a unit suite covering the full v1 local contract, so TESTING.md's "v1 stub implementation" claim is now accurate; the cross-cluster mTLS security contract itself remains untested because no remote implementation exists to test against. Proposal 0033 also resolved the CloudEvents type-alias divergence by amending §12.6 to codify the native `Event` struct the code already ships, landing tier1/tier3/tier11 tests that pin the inline-OCSF wire form, marshaler determinism, and the alias-reintroduction guard. The `eventBus.duplicateInjectionFactor` Helm value and its re-send wrapper also landed with unit coverage, though the higher-level handler-idempotency-under-duplicate-delivery assertion is still missing. The remaining largest gaps are the EventBus publish-after-commit correctness path never being exercised against a real Redis outage at tier8, and the delegation-tree/session-lifecycle topics never being driven end to end through the gateway.
Counts: 1 High, 5 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-12.6.1 — ClusterRegistry's cross-cluster mTLS security contract has no test of any tier; the v1 local-registry gap is now closed [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Implementations of `ClusterClient` that return a remote `RemotePodOperations` ... MUST establish a mutually authenticated TLS connection ... the remote PodRegistry endpoint MUST validate that the caller's certificate SAN matches the expected gateway identity ... operations not in `RemotePodOperations` (`DeletePod`, `UpdatePodState`, `CreatePod`, `CountByState`, `WatchPods`) are prohibited over cross-cluster connections." (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:628)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/podregistry/clusterregistry.go` (landed 2026-06-04, commit 2a644535, "F-12.6.4: §12.6 ClusterRegistry/RemotePodOperations + v1 LocalClusterRegistry") now implements `ClusterRegistry`, `RemotePodOperations`, `ClusterInfo`, `ClusterSelectionRequest`, and the v1 `LocalClusterRegistry`. `pkg/podregistry/clusterregistry_test.go` covers the full v1 local contract at the unit tier: `ListClusters` returns the single local cluster with no endpoint/CA bundle (`TestLocalClusterRegistryListClusters_spec_12_6_586`), `GetCluster`/`ClusterClient` return `ErrClusterNotFound` for any non-local id, `SelectCluster` ignores every request field and always returns `LocalClusterID()`, and `ClusterClient` delegates the four `RemotePodOperations` methods to the in-process `PodRegistry`. TESTING.md:2644's "v1 stub implementation and well-defined contract" claim is accurate for `ClusterRegistry` as of this landing. No remote (cross-cluster) `ClusterRegistry`/`ClusterClient` implementation exists anywhere in the tree — a grep for a networked client/server pair returns none — so the mTLS transport security contract itself (SAN validation, the `CACertBundle` impersonation-prevention check, and the runtime rejection of a non-`RemotePodOperations` RPC over a cross-cluster connection) has no code to exercise and remains entirely unverified.
- **Gap:** The finding's original v1-local-registry gap is closed. What remains is the security contract that only becomes load-bearing once a remote `ClusterRegistry` implementation ships: the spec explicitly exempts `LocalClusterRegistry` from the mTLS requirement ("The `LocalClusterRegistry` (v1) is exempt — it returns an in-process `PodRegistry` reference ... with no network transport"), so there is currently no cross-cluster code path to test. This needs a tier9 security test (a compromised cluster signed by a different CA is rejected; a cross-cluster caller attempting `DeletePod` is refused at the remote endpoint) the moment a remote implementation lands.
- **Dependencies:** A remote `ClusterClient` implementation (a networked `RemotePodOperations` client/server pair) must exist first; v1 ships only the exempt in-process `LocalClusterRegistry`. The cross-cluster mTLS test needs a two-cluster harness with cert-manager CAs and a malicious-cluster stub, neither of which exists yet.
- **Suggested test:** When a remote `ClusterClient` implementation lands, add tests/tier9_security/cross_cluster_podregistry_test.go that stands up two cert-manager CAs, asserts a mismatched-SAN remote endpoint is rejected, and asserts a cross-cluster `DeletePod`/`UpdatePodState` RPC is refused at the remote endpoint.

### - [ ] T-12.6.2 — EventBus publish-after-commit replay buffer and retranscribe worker are never exercised against a real Redis outage [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "When `EventBus.Publish` returns an error after the durable commit ... the gateway: (a) increments `lenny_event_bus_publish_dropped_total{topic}` ...; (b) writes the serialized CloudEvents envelope to a bounded in-memory replay buffer ...; and (c) for audit-bearing topics, marks the source Postgres audit row with `eventbus_publish_state = 'failed'` ... On Redis reconnect, the replay buffer is drained in FIFO order ... The **correctness** layer ... is the retranscribe worker described next." (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:712)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/eventbus` moved to `pkg/gateway/storage/eventbus` (2026-06-30, commit 24c39afc, pure package relocation, "C3 group the storage cluster under pkg/gateway/storage"); the tests below are at the new path. The in-memory replay buffer drain, eviction, and serialization-skip paths are unit-tested in pkg/gateway/storage/eventbus/conformance_test.go (`TestReplayBuffer*` against a `recordingSender` fake). The retranscribe worker success/terminal/recovery transitions are unit-tested in pkg/gateway/storage/eventbus/eventbus_test.go against a `fakeRepublishStore`. The audit-row publish-state transition (failed→published) is exercised at tier2 in tests/tier2_component/stores/eventstore_test.go against real Postgres, but with `NewRedisEventBus(nil, nil)` (no real Redis and no induced outage). Since the audit, commit 805427b4 ("wire §12.6 EventBus retranscribe worker + eventBus.* Helm values") wired the retranscribe worker into the real gateway (`cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go`, gated on the durable-audit block) with `eventBus.retryInterval`/`eventBus.maxRetryAttempts` Helm values, but only added tier1 unit tests and a tier2 helm-unittest render check — no integration or chaos coverage. The tier8 chaos test tests/tier8_chaos/store_failure_test.go (`TestRedisClusterDegraded`) scales Redis to zero but asserts only gateway liveness and the §25.3 health report, not the EventBus drop counter, replay-buffer drain on reconnect, or retranscribe re-publish.
- **Gap:** No test drives the complete correctness path end to end against a real Redis outage and recovery: a gateway publishes an audit-bearing event while Redis is down, the audit row is marked `failed`, Redis is restored, and either the in-memory buffer drain or the leader-elected retranscribe worker re-publishes the byte-identical envelope and flips the row to `published`. This is the failure-path test for the §12.6 durability guarantee, and it is unchanged by the retranscribe worker now being wired into the real gateway. Target tier8 chaos (real Redis outage) with a tier4 supporting flow.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier8 Kind harness (tests/testinfra/kind) with a subscriber that records received envelopes, plus the ability to scale Redis down and back up mid-flow. The harness exists; the EventBus drop/drain assertions and the retranscribe-on-recovery wait are new. Buildable on the existing chaos infrastructure.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier8_chaos/eventbus_redis_outage_test.go that publishes audit-bearing events during a Redis scale-to-zero, asserts `lenny_event_bus_publish_dropped_total` rises and the audit rows show `eventbus_publish_state='failed'`, restores Redis, and asserts the rows transition to `published` via the retranscribe worker with a byte-identical CloudEvents `id`.

### - [x] T-12.6.3 — Event type diverges from the spec's go-sdk alias and CloudEvents conformance is self-asserted rather than pinned to the upstream v1.0.2 schema [Medium] — RESOLVED 4693160b (reconciled against proposal 0033)
- **Resolution:** Proposal 0033 ("Reconcile the §12.6 and §25.3 CloudEvents type-alias mandates with the shipped native envelope struct") converged on Direction A: reconcile the spec to the code rather than the code to the spec. Commit 4693160b amended §12.6 (and §25.3 in parallel) to replace `type Event = cloudevents.Event` with the native CloudEvents v1.0.2 structured-content struct the code already ships (`SpecVersion`, `ID`, `Source`, `Type`, `Time`, `DataContentType`, `Subject`, `Data json.RawMessage`, `Extensions`), with the rationale documented inline: the released go-sdk does not honor the RFC 6839 `+json` structured suffix in its content-type gate, so aliasing to `cloudevents.Event` would serialize `application/ocsf+json` data as an escaped JSON string and double-wrap the audit record, violating the section's own single-envelope inline model and the retranscribe byte-identical re-serialization contract. The proposal's S4 landed the tests the original finding asked for: commit 53fea64d added `TestCloudEventsInlineOCSFWireForm` to tests/tier3_contract/cloudevents/cloudevents_test.go, which decodes the top-level `data` key and asserts it is a JSON object (not an escaped string) carrying the OCSF record's `class_uid` field intact; commit d70721e6 added `TestEventMarshalIsDeterministic` to pkg/gateway/storage/eventbus/cloudevents_test.go, pinning that marshaling the same envelope twice produces byte-identical output (the property the retranscribe worker's byte-identity contract depends on); commit 7af540c6 added tests/tier11_docs/cloudevents_alias_reconciliation_test.go, a spec/code consistency guard that fails if either §12.6 or §25.3 ever re-introduces `= cloudevents.Event` while the code ships a native struct. The go-sdk remains absent from go.mod, which is now spec-conformant rather than a divergence.

### - [ ] T-12.6.4 — Delegation-tree and session-lifecycle EventBus topics are never driven through the gateway end to end [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Abstracts control-plane event distribution for delegation tree signals and session lifecycle events ... `TopicDelegationTree` ... budget signals, child completion, tree cancellation ... `TopicSessionLifecycle` ... state transitions, coordinator handoff notifications." (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:653)
- **Existing tests:** The EventBus interface, publish/subscribe round-trip, and tenant-prefixed channel are tested at tier2 against real Redis (tests/tier2_component/stores/eventstore_test.go TestEventBusContract) and at the unit level (pkg/gateway/storage/eventbus, moved from pkg/gateway/eventbus by commit 24c39afc). The tier4 delegation flow tests/tier4_integration/delegation_test.go spawns a child through `lenny/delegate_task` and asserts the REST tree, but it does not subscribe to or assert any `TopicDelegationTree` publish. tests/tier4_integration/session_lifecycle_test.go drives session state through the gateway without referencing the EventBus. A grep for `TopicDelegation`/`TopicSession`/`Publish`/`Subscribe` in both tier4 files returns no matches, unchanged since the 2026-06-03 audit.
- **Gap:** The two production topics are tested in isolation with synthetic events, but no integration test verifies that a real delegation child-completion or session state transition actually publishes the corresponding CloudEvents envelope on the tenant-prefixed channel and that a coordinating gateway replica's subscriber receives it. This is the real user-journey test for the EventBus (a parent session coordinating a delegation tree reacts to a child-completion signal). Target tier4 integration on the compose stack.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a subscriber attached to the gateway's Redis during the delegation flow. tests/testinfra/gateway and the existing compose stack provide the gateway; the subscriber wiring is new but small. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/eventbus_delegation_signal_test.go that subscribes to `t:{tenant}:evt:delegation_tree`, runs a delegate-then-complete flow, and asserts a `dev.lenny.delegation_tree_*` envelope arrives carrying `lennyrootsessionid`, plus a session-state-change case asserting a `dev.lenny.session_state_changed` envelope on `session_lifecycle`.

### - [ ] T-12.6.5 — Delivery-guarantee transition protocol: the duplicate-injection mechanism now exists and is unit-tested, but no test asserts handler idempotency under doubled delivery; redelivery-after-crash remains untested [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Before enabling a durable EventBus implementation in production, operators MUST execute the following validation sequence in a staging environment: 1. Duplicate-injection test. Configure the staging EventBus to publish every event twice (configurable via `eventBus.duplicateInjectionFactor: 2` test-only Helm value) ... 2. Redelivery-after-crash test. Kill a subscriber mid-handler (SIGKILL ...)." (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:727)
- **Existing tests:** Commit 805427b4 ("wire §12.6 EventBus retranscribe worker + eventBus.* Helm values") added the `eventBus.duplicateInjectionFactor` Helm value (charts/lenny/values.yaml:1428, default 1, wired through charts/lenny/templates/gateway-deployment.yaml:1131-1133) and a `WithDuplicateInjectionFactor` re-send wrapper on `RedisEventBus` (pkg/gateway/storage/eventbus/eventbus.go). pkg/gateway/storage/eventbus/duplicate_injection_test.go unit-tests the mechanism directly: `TestDuplicateInjectionFactor_spec_12_6_699` asserts a factor of N re-sends the envelope N times (with 0 and negative factors clamped to 1), and `TestDuplicateInjectionSkippedOnPrimaryFailure_spec_12_6_699` asserts the duplicate copies are skipped (and the replay buffer is not double-populated) when the primary send fails. No test exists at tier4 or above that runs a real handler (e.g., the delegation-tree completion path) under `duplicateInjectionFactor: 2` and asserts business-metric counters do not double — a grep for `duplicateInjectionFactor` across tests/ returns no matches. The redelivery-after-crash validation step (kill a subscriber mid-handler with SIGKILL) remains entirely untested, as before.
- **Gap:** The originally-reported absence — "the `duplicateInjectionFactor` Helm value does not exist" — is resolved: the value, its Helm wiring, and the re-send mechanism now exist and are unit-tested. What remains open is the higher-level assertion the spec's staging validation sequence actually calls for: that a real handler under doubled delivery does not produce doubled side effects. The spec still frames both steps as one-time staging validation rather than an ongoing CI obligation, so this stays a SHOULD-level gap rather than a MUST.
- **Dependencies:** none for the duplicate-injection integration assertion — buildable today using the now-existing `duplicateInjectionFactor` Helm value and a metrics scrape helper. The redelivery-after-crash test additionally needs a way to SIGKILL a subscriber process mid-handler and a second subscriber to observe redelivery; no such harness exists yet.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/eventbus_duplicate_injection_test.go that sets `duplicateInjectionFactor: 2`, runs the delegation flow, and asserts handler side-effect counters (e.g., delegation tree completion counts) reflect one state change per event rather than two.

### - [ ] T-12.6.6 — WatchPods and SessionShard latency budgets are declared as P99 SLOs but never asserted [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Implementations MUST deliver events within a bounded latency: 500 ms P99 for `CRDPodRegistry` ... 2 s P99 for a future `PostgresPodRegistry`" (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:494) and "`SessionShard` implementations MUST resolve within 5 ms P99 — this call is on the coordinator handoff hot path." (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:576)
- **Existing tests:** The WatchPods delivery contract (no initial snapshot, resync under backpressure, notify trigger) is asserted functionally in pkg/podregistry/crd_test.go and tests/tier2_component/stores/postgrespodregistry_test.go, and the `lenny_pod_registry_watch_lag_seconds` gauge is checked for emission, but no test asserts the 500 ms or 2 s P99 latency bound. The `SessionShard` co-location invariant is asserted in tests/tier2_component/stores/storerouter_test.go, but no load test asserts the 5 ms P99 resolution. The two tier7 matches for `SessionShard` (bulkhead_thread_pool_isolation, graceful_shutdown_drain) are unrelated scenarios. Unchanged since the 2026-06-03 audit.
- **Gap:** Both latency budgets are normative MUSTs expressed as P99 SLOs, and neither is verified. The WatchPods budget needs a tier7 load test measuring informer-to-channel delivery latency, and the SessionShard budget needs a tier7 microbenchmark on the coordinator-handoff hot path. These are SLO/performance gaps.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier7 load harness (tests/testinfra/loadgen, tests/testinfra/loadrunner) with a latency-histogram assertion against a P99 threshold. The harness exists; the specific scenarios are new. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/watchpods_propagation_latency to assert CRDPodRegistry WatchPods P99 under 500 ms, and a tier7a microbenchmark scenario asserting `SessionShard` resolution P99 under 5 ms.

This ensures tenant isolation is enforced at the interface boundary ... must be added to the canonical key table and to `TestRedisTenantKeyIsolation` coverage." (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:734)

The channel-name derivation is also covered at tier3 (cloudevents_test.go TestCloudEventsTenantPrefixedChannels). The tier4 subtest runs against a `guardedRedis` miniredis backend rather than a real Redis instance. Unchanged since the 2026-06-03 audit.
- **Gap:** The cross-tenant rejection is verified, so this is a deployment-combination gap rather than an absence. The guard is exercised against miniredis, not the real Redis cluster used in the tier2 EventBus contract. A real-Redis run would confirm the guard intercepts the actual `PUBLISH` command rather than a miniredis emulation. Target tier2 component (real Redis) to extend the existing isolation assertion.

(spec/12_storage-architecture.md:568)

Unchanged since the 2026-06-03 audit; v1 still ships only `SingleShardRouter`.

There is no component-or-higher gap to report while v1 ships only `SingleShardRouter`. This entry is recorded so that when a multi-shard router lands, a tier4 integration test must drive the concurrency batching, the `scatter_gather_shard_timeout` structured event, and the partial-result flag against multiple real shards.

## §12.7 Extensibility <a id="t-12.7"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/12_storage-architecture.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§12.7 is a five-bullet, non-normative design-guidance list (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:752-758) and is formally exempted from the per-section test rule in `tests/spec-map-exceptions.yaml:81` with the justification that it "states no behavior of its own." Four of the five bullets are design principles whose testable residue is covered indirectly: compile-time role-interface satisfaction is asserted in `tests/tier2_component/stores/erasure_interface_test.go`, the §12.6 scaling-interface contracts have suites, and the explicit/backend-specific migration framework is exercised in `tests/tier2_component/migrations/migrations_test.go`. The one concrete capability claim is the fifth bullet, "Token store module is separate ... allows future Vault/KMS migration." Its forward-migration capability is declared as the `cloud_secret_store` tier6 suite (TESTING.md:1117) yet that suite is marked `planned` for every provider in `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml`, and the only on-disk test (`TestCloudSecretStore` in `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/cluster_assertions_test.go`) is a negative guard that asserts v1 stays Postgres-backed and explicitly defers the swap-through-the-same-interface validation to a v2 follow-on. A documentation inconsistency also exists: TESTING.md frames cloud secret backends as alternative TokenStore backends "through the same interface" while the TokenStore role is interface-less for backend swap (per `pkg/gateway/storage/issuedtokenstore/issuedtokenstore.go:152-153` and the closed gap F-12.1.3, only the `Eraser` interface exists).
Counts: 0 High, 1 Medium, 1 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-12.7.1 — Token store Vault/KMS migration capability is asserted only by an unbuilt tier6 suite and a negative guard [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Token store module is separate even if initially backed by Postgres (allows future Vault/KMS migration)" (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:758). The corresponding suite is declared in TESTING.md: "cloud_secret_store | Native secret backend integration: Secret Manager (GCP), Secrets Manager (AWS), Key Vault (Azure) as alternative TokenStore backends through the same interface" (TESTING.md:1117).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/cluster_assertions_test.go:342` defines `TestCloudSecretStore`, which asserts the gateway pod carries no `LENNY_SECRETS_MANAGER_PROVIDER` or `AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_NAME` env and logs that "Secrets Manager / Key Vault routing is the v2 follow-on" (cluster_assertions_test.go:368). `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml:91-96` still marks `cloud_secret_store` as `planned` for gke, eks, and aks. The §12.6 contract suites in spec-map.json cover EventBus, StoreRouter, and EventStore; none exercise a TokenStore backend swap. The §14 TokenStore domain suite (TESTING.md:899) lists only KMS-envelope encryption, hash storage, revocation lookup, rotation, and RLS, with no backend-pluggability case. No test substitutes a non-Postgres token-store backend and asserts the platform behaves identically through the same interface; searched tiers tier2 (`pkg/gateway/storage/issuedtokenstore`, `pkg/gateway/connectors/connectorcredstore`, `pkg/tokenservice`), tier3 (`tests/tier3_contract/oauth_token`), tier4, and tier6.
- **Gap:** The forward-migration capability the bullet promises has no positive test. The only on-disk assertion is the negation that v1 does not wire a cloud secret backend, which verifies the absence of v2 rather than the swappability the bullet claims. This is a deployment-combination gap (Cloud KMS / AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault as the token-store backend, tier6 across GKE, EKS, and AKS) plus a missing role-interface contract test (tier2 or tier3) that pins the token store to a backend-agnostic contract a second backend can satisfy. A real operator journey (alice migrates acme's token store from Postgres to a provider secret manager and existing sessions continue to resolve tokens) is unexercised.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a second, non-Postgres token-store backend or a stub backend implementing the token-store role contract, which does not exist today (the role is interface-less for swap per F-12.1.3). It also requires the tier6 cloud harness (`tests/testinfra/cloud`) with provider secret-manager credentials, and for the contract-level test the `tests/testinfra/tokenservice` and `tests/testinfra/containers` building blocks. Building the second backend or a conformance stub is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier3 contract test `tests/tier3_contract/tokenstore/backend_swap_test.go` that runs a shared token-store contract suite against the Postgres backend and a stub secret-manager backend (built on `tests/testinfra/stubs`) to prove the interface boundary is backend-agnostic, and promote the `cloud_secret_store` parity-matrix row from `planned` to `validated` by implementing a tier6 `secret_store_test.go` (using `tests/testinfra/cloud`) that wires the provider secret manager as the token-store backend and asserts token issuance and resolution succeed against it.

### - [ ] T-12.7.2 — TESTING.md frames the TokenStore as having pluggable backends "through the same interface" while the role is interface-less for backend swap [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Token store module is separate even if initially backed by Postgres (allows future Vault/KMS migration)" (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:758) versus TESTING.md "as alternative TokenStore backends through the same interface" (TESTING.md:1117), contrasted with `pkg/gateway/storage/issuedtokenstore/issuedtokenstore.go:152-153`: "The full pluggable-backend role interface for the interface-less §12.2 stores is tracked separately (F-12.1.3)."
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier2_component/stores/erasure_interface_test.go` asserts only the mandatory-erasure `Eraser`/`tenantEraser` interface across stores; it does not assert a backend-swap role interface for the token store. No tier0 static check reconciles the TESTING.md "same interface" claim against the absence of a token-store backend role interface; searched tiers tier0 (`tests/tier0_static`) and tier2 (`tests/tier2_component/stores`).
- **Gap:** TESTING.md and §23.2 describe MemoryStore and SemanticCache as the pluggable stores, and the §14 domain-suite table marks only those two `pluggable`, yet TESTING.md:1117 separately frames cloud secret managers as token-store backends "through the same interface." The closed gap F-12.1.3 (BUILD-GAPS.md) records that the token store exposes only the `Eraser` interface, not a backend-swap role interface. Without a static reconciliation, a future change could ship a v2 secret-manager backend that diverges from the (currently nonexistent) token-store backend contract while the docs still assert parity, and CI would not catch the drift. This is a spec-versus-doc-versus-implementation inconsistency on a SHOULD-level (forward-compatibility) claim.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The tier0 validate-maps tooling (`cmd/lenny-test validate-maps`) already reads the parity-matrix and spec map.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier0 static assertion in `tests/tier0_static` (or extend `cmd/lenny-test validate-maps`) that any capability framed as backed "through the same interface" names a concrete role interface in `pkg/`, so the `cloud_secret_store` row cannot claim interface parity until a token-store backend role interface exists; pair it with a doc note aligning TESTING.md:1117 with the F-12.1.3 outcome.

### - [ ] T-12.7.3 — Module-separation structural property of the token store is unverified, and the §12.7 exemption is otherwise sound [Info] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Token store module is separate even if initially backed by Postgres" (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:758); design bullets "Define small role-based interfaces", "Start with Postgres + Redis", and "Keep migrations/schema explicit and backend-specific" (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:754-756); exemption recorded in `tests/spec-map-exceptions.yaml:81` ("Design-guidance list for the pluggable-storage interface boundary; states no behavior of its own").
- **Existing tests:** The token store lives in its own packages (`pkg/gateway/storage/issuedtokenstore`, `pkg/gateway/connectors/connectorcredstore`, `pkg/tokenservice`, `cmd/lenny-token-service`), so the separation holds structurally today. `tests/tier2_component/migrations/migrations_test.go` covers explicit/backend-specific migrations; `tests/tier2_component/stores/erasure_interface_test.go` and the §12.6 contract suites cover the interface-satisfaction principle; the full tier2 store suite runs against real Postgres and Redis, exercising the "start with Postgres + Redis" choice. No test asserts the separation invariant (for example that the token store package exposes no Postgres-specific type to its callers so the future swap remains feasible).
- **Gap:** The four design bullets carry no behavior to verify and are reasonably exempted; this finding records that conclusion explicitly so a later reviewer does not re-open them. The one structural property worth a guard is that the token store stays a swappable module, which today is enforced only by package layout and not by any test. This is an observation rather than a blocking gap, given the exemption and the indirect coverage above.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today, using `go/packages` import analysis.
- **Suggested test:** Optionally add a tier0 architectural check in `tests/tier0_static` that the token-store packages' exported API does not reference `pgx`, `pgxpool`, or other Postgres-specific types, so the module-separation claim that enables a future Vault/KMS swap is mechanically protected; otherwise treat §12.7 as covered indirectly per the existing exemption.

## §12.8 Compliance Interfaces <a id="t-12.8"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/12_storage-architecture.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§12.8 is one of the largest behavioral subsections in the spec, covering legal hold and checkpoint-rotation suspension, GDPR Article 17 erasure with a twenty-step dependency-ordered deletion sequence, Article 18 processing restriction, OCSF dead-letter PII redaction with signed RedactionReceipts, the tenant deletion lifecycle (now with an explicit Phase 3.5 legal-hold segregation/escrow step and a Phase 4a KMS-destruction step) with region-scoped legal-hold escrow, multi-region data residency and per-region backup pipelines, and DSAR primitives. Since the 2026-06-03 audit, proposal 0028 reconciled the step-14 redaction language (dropping the phantom `audit_log.user_id` column and restating the chain re-seal as the shipped receipt-authorized discontinuity) and proposal 0025 reconciled the Phase-4 teardown so the per-tenant billing/audit sequence is no longer dropped (the `lenny_erasure` role holds no `DROP` privilege) — both are spec-text-only rewordings that keep the underlying findings' gaps intact, so their Spec/Doc citations are updated below rather than resolved. Separately, the Phase 3.5 legal-hold escrow segregation — spec text that already existed at generation time with no implementation or test — has since been built end to end (controller phase, `force-delete` admin endpoint, region-scoped escrow migrator, Postgres-backed escrow record store, and release/GC path) with component-tier tests against real Postgres and gateway-level integration tests, resolving T-12.8.3. That work leaves a narrower residual (no test exercises the escrow migration against a real MinIO/KMS backend or the CMP-058 platform-Postgres residency-routing failure), captured as a new finding. Coverage above unit otherwise remains thin in the same places as before: the tier8 chaos scaffolds for §12.8 are still `t.Logf`-only, no tier4 integration test drives the twenty-step `DeleteByUser` sequence or the six/seven-phase `DeleteByTenant` sequence against real backends, there is no e2e, conformance, or security coverage for data-residency enforcement, the OCSF erasure-notification classes, cross-tenant erasure-job leakage, or the backup-resurrection control, and the `erasure.requested` external-sink propagation remains unimplemented. Counts: 6 High (1 resolved), 8 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-12.8.1 — spec-map.json lists skip-only chaos scaffolds as the §12.8 test surface [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Erasure jobs must complete within the tier-specific deadlines defined in Section 12.9: T3 data within 72 hours, T4 data within 1 hour. ... If the job has not completed by the deadline, the `ErasureJobOverdue` alert ... fires." (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:797) and the legal-hold-override and mid-sequence-failure behaviors at lines 823-825 and 766.
- **Existing tests:** `tests/spec-map.json:1488-1493` lists `tests/tier8_chaos/chaos_helpers_test.go`, `component_failure_test.go`, `config_drift_test.go`, `live_session_test.go`, and `store_failure_test.go` as the §12.8 tests. The §12.8-specific chaos functions live in `tests/tier8_chaos/scaffolds_test.go`: `TestErasureJobFailureMidSequence` (line 313), `TestLegalHoldOverrideFlow` (line 327), and `TestT3T4SLABreach` (line 340) each only call `t.Logf` and return without asserting anything. The store-failure files cover Postgres/Redis/MinIO outage, not erasure or legal hold.
- **Gap:** The chaos suite that spec-map.json presents as the §12.8 coverage is an empty scaffold. A dashboard query for §12.8 reports green while the erasure-job-failure recovery, the legal-hold override escrow path, and the SLA-breach alert are never exercised. This is a spec-versus-test inconsistency that lets a regression in the erasure runner, the override path, or the deadline sampler ship undetected. The target tier is tier8 chaos for the failure-injection scenarios plus a corrected spec-map.json that points at the real unit and component suites rather than the scaffolds.
- **Dependencies:** The live mid-sequence fault injection needs a store-fault layer that pauses or fails one store mid-`DeleteByUser`; build it under `tests/testinfra/chaos` and `tests/testinfra/stubs`. Clock injection for the SLA breach exists at `pkg/clockinject`. The infrastructure is partly present and partly buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Replace the three `t.Logf` scaffolds in `tests/tier8_chaos/scaffolds_test.go` with implemented tier8 tests under `tests/tier8_chaos/erasure_chaos_test.go` driving an erasure job that fails at the artifact-store step, asserting the job lands in `failed` with `failure_phase=store_delete`, `processing_restricted` stays set, and `lenny_erasure_job_failed_total` increments; and correct `tests/spec-map.json` §12.8 to list the real suites.

### - [ ] T-12.8.2 — No integration test drives the twenty-step DeleteByUser sequence through real stores with FK ordering [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The `DeleteByUser(user_id)` erasure job executes store deletions in the following dependency order. ... Foreign-key and referential constraints dictate that child/referencing stores are deleted before parent/referenced stores." (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:821) with the explicit edges at lines 836-837 and 860-861.
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/erasure/order_test.go` validates `canonicalRank` and `fkMustPrecede` statically over store names. `pkg/gateway/erasurejob/runner_test.go` drives the runner with a fake orchestrator. `tests/tier2_component/stores/erasure_interface_test.go:78` smoke-calls each store's `DeleteByUser`/`DeleteByTenant`, but every store it constructs is the in-memory variant (`memstore.New()`, `userstore.NewMemory()`, `evalstore.NewMemory(...)`, and so on), so no foreign-key constraint is in play. TESTING.md §14.10 (line 1933) and the suite table at line 1044 both claim a Tier 4 `erasure_job` suite running "the 19-step sequence in order"; no such file exists under `tests/tier4_integration/`.
- **Gap:** The dependency ordering is the spec's stated reason the sequence cannot be reordered, and it is only enforceable against a real Postgres where the `EvalResult.session_id`, `session_tree_archive.root_session_id`, and other foreign keys reject an out-of-order delete. The static rank test cannot catch a wiring that deletes `sessions` before `eval_results` against a real database, and the in-memory component test has no constraints to violate. This is a missing real-user-journey integration test (alice requests erasure; every store the spec lists is purged in FK-safe order against live backends) and a declared-suite-is-absent inconsistency. Target tier is tier4 integration.
- **Dependencies:** Needs the full set of Postgres-backed stores plus Redis and MinIO wired through `erasure.Orchestrator`, available via `tests/testinfra/containers` (StartPostgres, StartRedis) and the MinIO container helper. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/erasure_job_test.go` that seeds a user with rows in every erasure-scope store against real Postgres/Redis/MinIO, runs the orchestrator's `DeleteByUser`, and asserts each store returns zero rows and the FK-parent `sessions` is deleted last without a constraint error, using `tests/testinfra/containers`.

### - [x] T-12.8.3 — Tenant deletion Phase 3.5 legal-hold escrow has no implementation and no test [High] — RESOLVED 07f4420e
- **Resolution:** The Phase 3.5 legal-hold segregation/escrow step named in the spec at generation time (unchanged in substance since; spec/12_storage-architecture.md:901, 907-918) has since been implemented and tested end to end. `pkg/controller/tenantdeletion/lifecycle.go` and `controller.go` add `PhaseLegalHoldSegregation` to the phase order (commit `07f4420e`, "§12.8 Phase 3.5 legal-hold escrow core + controller override path"), wired into the gateway by `65df24ad` ("wire the §12.8 tenant-deletion lifecycle in the gateway"). The `force-delete` admin endpoint (`pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/forcedelete.go`) and the region-scoped escrow migrator (`pkg/legalholdescrow/{escrow,migrator,release}.go`) landed via `0acbdfef` and `24ff7280` ("gateway escrow-migrator integration tests"), and the release/GC path via `839f9772` ("build §12.8 legal-hold escrow GC/release"). Tests now cover: the block-without-override path and the override-authorizes-Phase-3.5 path at the controller level (`pkg/controller/tenantdeletion/legalhold_test.go`, `legalhold_override_test.go`); the HTTP-level `force-delete` endpoint including the unheld-tenant happy path, the blocked-without-override 409, the override with/without justification, and the tenant-admin-forbidden case (`pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/forcedelete_test.go`); the region-resolution and re-encryption logic including the unresolvable-region abort and the actual re-encryption of a held artifact (`cmd/lenny-gateway/legalholdescrow_test.go`); and the escrow record store's round-trip, tenant isolation, and `MarkReleased` idempotency against a real Postgres container with the production migrations applied (`tests/tier2_component/legalholdescrow/pgstore_test.go`, migration 0166). This closes the "neither implemented nor tested" gap the finding named. The residual — no test exercises the escrow migration against a real MinIO/KMS backend, and the CMP-058 platform-Postgres residency-routing failure path (`PLATFORM_AUDIT_REGION_UNRESOLVABLE`) has no test — is captured as T-12.8.17.

### - [ ] T-12.8.4 — No security-tier test for cross-tenant erasure-job leakage or Article 18 bypass [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "all session creation endpoints (`POST /v1/sessions` and `POST /v1/sessions/start`) are rejected with `403 ERASURE_IN_PROGRESS` for the affected `user_id`" (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:793) and the cross-tenant non-leakage of erasure jobs implied by the handler's "reads as not-found so its existence is not leaked across the tenant boundary" guard.
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/user_gate_test.go` covers the 403 gate at the handler level. `pkg/gateway/admin/erasure_test.go` and `erasure_retry_test.go` cover the cross-tenant not-found guard at the handler level. `tests/tier9_security/` contains tenant_isolation, rbac, audit_integrity, ssrf, and credential_leakage suites; none reference erasure, `processing_restricted`, or legal hold (grep returns only `audit_integrity_test.go`, which covers the audit chain, not erasure).
- **Gap:** The processing-restriction gate and the cross-tenant erasure-job confidentiality boundary are security controls (a tenant-admin for globex must not enumerate or clear acme's erasure jobs, and the Article 18 restriction must hold end to end through the gateway). They are verified only as handler-level unit assertions with mocks, never end to end against a real gateway with real auth and a real UserStore under a tier9 security harness. This is a missing adversarial-path test for a critical control. Target tier is tier9 security.
- **Dependencies:** Needs the tier9 gateway harness with OIDC/JWT auth (`tests/testinfra/gateway`, `tests/testinfra/tokenservice`) and a real Postgres UserStore. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier9_security/erasure_isolation_test.go` asserting that a tenant-admin token for globex receives 404 on `GET /v1/admin/erasure-jobs/{acme_job}` and on the retry and clear-restriction endpoints, and that a user with `processing_restricted` set is rejected with `403 ERASURE_IN_PROGRESS` on both session-creation endpoints through the live gateway, using `tests/testinfra/gateway` and `tokenservice`.

### - [ ] T-12.8.5 — OCSF erasure-notification classes are not pinned against the external schema in a conformance test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "the erasure job MUST emit a structured `gdpr.erasure_deadletter_downstream_notified` audit event ... mapped to OCSF class 5001 Entity Management with `activity_id: 4` (`Delete`) and `category_uid: 5`" (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:858) and the dead-letter redaction event family at line 839.
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/audit/ocsf/erasure_recovery_test.go:36` asserts the class is `ClassEntityManagement` for erasure-recovery event types, and `pkg/audit/ocsf/ocsf_test.go` checks class/activity for several event types and the class-2004 dead-letter receipt. These are Go-internal assertions against the package's own constants, not a conformance check that pins the emitted JSON against the published OCSF 1.x schema. The tier10 conformance directory holds only `README.md`, `scaffolds_test.go`, and two unrelated conformance suites (`concurrent_slot_conformance_test.go`, `recycle_scrub_conformance_test.go`).
- **Gap:** The spec applies a specific external standard (OCSF) to compliance events so that SIEM rulesets recognize them. A conformance test that validates the serialized event against the OCSF schema for class 5001 (Entity Management, Delete) and class 2004 (Application Security Finding) is required by the audit's standards-conformance rule, and its absence is a finding. The internal constant checks would not catch a divergence between the project's notion of class 5001 and the actual OCSF field set (for example a missing `category_uid` or `metadata.version`). Target tier is tier10 conformance.
- **Dependencies:** Needs an OCSF schema fixture (the relevant class JSON schemas) under `tests/testinfra` and a JSON-schema validator. The schema fixtures do not exist yet; vendoring them is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier10_conformance/ocsf_gdpr_events_test.go` that marshals `gdpr.erasure_deadletter_downstream_notified` and `gdpr.erasure_deadletter_redacted` through the OCSF translator and validates the output against the vendored OCSF class 5001 and class 2004 schemas, asserting `class_uid`, `activity_id`, `category_uid`, and `metadata.version`.

- **Spec/Doc:** "The erasure job publishes an `erasure.requested` event to all configured billing and audit sinks, carrying the `user_id` (or `tenant_id`) and a deadline. ... The erasure receipt records which sinks were notified and their acknowledgment status." (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:924)
- **Existing tests:** A grep for `erasure.requested`, `erasure_requested`, and `ErasureRequested` across all non-test Go files returns no matches, so the propagation is not implemented. No test references it either.
- **Gap:** A normative MUST behavior (notify external SIEM and billing sinks of an erasure request and record acknowledgment in the receipt) has neither an implementation nor a test. The receipt's `which sinks were notified` field that compliance auditors rely on cannot be produced. This is a missing capability with no component-or-higher coverage, and it spans the SIEM and billing-webhook sink integrations. Target tier is tier4 integration once the implementation lands.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the propagation implementation plus the SIEM sink stub and billing webhook receiver in `tests/testinfra/stubs`; the implementation and the stubs are part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/erasure_sink_propagation_test.go` that registers a stub SIEM sink and a stub billing webhook, runs a user erasure, and asserts an `erasure.requested` event reaches both sinks with `user_id` and a deadline, and that the `gdpr.erasure_completed` receipt records each sink's acknowledgment, using `tests/testinfra/stubs`.

### - [ ] T-12.8.7 — Data residency enforcement chain has no e2e or integration coverage [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "the gateway restricts pod allocation — including delegation targets — to pools whose `region` label matches. A delegation that would route to a pool in a non-matching region is rejected with `REGION_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATED`. ... The gateway validates that at least one pool and one storage backend are available for the requested region before accepting a session. If not, session creation fails with `REGION_UNAVAILABLE`." (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:942, 944)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/admission/webhook/data_residency_validator_test.go` and `pkg/admission/data_residency_validator/validator_test.go` cover the admission webhook's region-rejection logic. `pkg/storerouter/storerouter_test.go` and `tests/tier2_component/stores/storerouter_test.go` cover the v1 `SingleShardRouter` (single region) only. `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/admission_featuregated_test.go` references the residency validator feature gate. No test exercises pod-pool region routing rejecting a delegation, the session-creation `REGION_UNAVAILABLE` gate, or the multi-region `StorageRouter` directing writes to a region-local backend.
- **Gap:** The three-level residency enforcement (pod routing, storage routing, session-creation validation) is verified only for the admission webhook and the single-region router. The delegation `REGION_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATED` path, the transitive inheritance through a delegation tree, and the `REGION_UNAVAILABLE` session gate are deployment-combination gaps with no integration or e2e coverage. This is a partial-coverage finding spanning a real user journey (alice's EU-pinned session and its children stay in eu-west-1) and an adversarial path (a delegation that would cross a region is rejected). Target tiers are tier4 integration for the storage-routing and session-gate paths and tier5 e2e for the pod-pool delegation rejection.
- **Dependencies:** Needs a two-region pool fixture and per-region storage endpoints. The fakekube and scenkit harnesses (`tests/testinfra/fakekube`, `tests/testinfra/scenkit`) can model the pools; the multi-region storage routing needs a second Postgres/MinIO/Redis trio in `tests/testinfra/containers`. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/data_residency_test.go` asserting that a tenant with `dataResidencyRegion=eu-west-1` and no eu pool fails session creation with `REGION_UNAVAILABLE`, and `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/data_residency_delegation_test.go` asserting a delegation to a non-matching-region pool is rejected with `REGION_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATED` and emits `DataResidencyViolationAttempt`, using `tests/testinfra/scenkit`.

### - [ ] T-12.8.8 — OCSF dead-letter PII redaction and RedactionReceipt chain reseal lack a security-tier verification [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "the erasure job redacts the PII-bearing payload fields in place ... The verifier sets the row's `chainIntegrity` state to `redacted_gdpr` ... The erasure job persists a signed `RedactionReceipt` ... Chain verifiers that encounter a `redacted_gdpr` row without a signature-verifying `RedactionReceipt` MUST raise `broken` and fire `AuditRedactionReceiptMissing`." (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:839; proposal 0028 restated the same paragraph's chain-reseal language as the shipped receipt-authorized discontinuity rather than a physical re-seal — the missing-receipt-raises-`broken` requirement this finding targets is unchanged)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/audit/chain_test.go` exercises the `Chain` verifier with `RedactionReceipt` maps, and `pkg/audit/ocsf/erasure_recovery_test.go` covers the OCSF class for redaction events. `tests/tier11_docs/audit_gdpr_erasure_reconciliation_test.go` pins the reconciled spec prose (`TestErasureStep14DescribesReceiptDiscontinuityNotReseal`, `TestReceiptCheckSurfacesDropChainRewriteBoundary`) as a documentation-consistency check, not a runtime verification. `tests/tier9_security/audit_integrity_test.go` (`TestAuditChainContinuity`, `TestAuditSequenceMonotonicity`) verifies the hash chain against real Postgres but does not cover a `redacted_gdpr` discontinuity or a missing-receipt tamper.
- **Gap:** The redaction reseal is a security control: a verifier must accept an authorized GDPR redaction (signed receipt present) and reject a tamper that clears `payload` without a valid receipt (`broken` plus `AuditRedactionReceiptMissing`). This is verified only as a package-internal unit test with synthetic rows and a doc-consistency test pinning the reconciled spec wording, never end to end against a real audit store under the tier9 harness, and the missing-receipt adversarial branch is the security-relevant path. This is a missing adversarial verification for a fail-closed integrity control. Target tier is tier9 security.
- **Dependencies:** Needs the tier9 audit harness with real Postgres (`tests/testinfra/audit`, `tests/testinfra/containers`) and the KMS signing fixture for the receipt signature. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier9_security/audit_gdpr_redaction_test.go` that redacts a dead-lettered row through the erasure path against real Postgres, verifies the chain accepts the `redacted_gdpr` discontinuity with the signed receipt, then deletes the receipt and asserts the verifier reports `broken` and the `AuditRedactionReceiptMissing` alert predicate fires, using `tests/testinfra/audit`.

### - [ ] T-12.8.10 — Per-region backup pipeline residency enforcement has no integration or chaos coverage [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "If a shard's resolved region has no corresponding `backups.regions.<region>` entry, or if the region's MinIO endpoint is unreachable ... `lenny-ops` MUST abort the backup with error code `BackupRegionUnresolvable` ... the `BackupFailed` alert fires, and a `DataResidencyViolationAttempt` audit event is emitted." (spec/12_storage-architecture.md:965) and the runtime residency preflight for continuous replication at line 967.
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/ops/backup/region_test.go` covers region resolution logic, and `pkg/ops/opsserver/backup_internal_test.go` and `pkg/ops/backup/k8slauncher/k8slauncher_test.go` cover backup-job launching. `pkg/blobstore/replication/replication_test.go` and `pkg/gateway/admin/artifact_replication_test.go` cover replication state. These are unit-level. No test exercises a multi-region backup that aborts on an unreachable region endpoint, or the continuous-replication residency preflight suspending replication on a jurisdiction-tag mismatch.
- **Gap:** The fail-closed `BackupRegionUnresolvable` abort and the runtime residency preflight (`ARTIFACT_REPLICATION_REGION_UNRESOLVABLE`, suspend on tag mismatch or DNS rebinding) are compliance controls that prevent cross-border transfer. They are verified only as unit logic, never against a backup job hitting an unreachable or mistagged destination. This is a failure-path and deployment-combination gap. - **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/backup_region_residency_test.go` asserting a backup aborts with `BACKUP_REGION_UNRESOLVABLE`, fires `BackupFailed`, and emits `DataResidencyViolationAttempt` when a shard's region has no `backups.regions` entry, plus a tier8 case that rebinds the replication destination to a mistagged bucket and asserts replication suspends with `suspended_residency_violation`, using `tests/testinfra/containers`.
