- **Existing tests:** TESTING.md §12.5 states the Kind harness uses Calico (TESTING.md:1059) while tests/tier9_security/network_policy_test.go documents the CNI under test as kindnet (network_policy_test.go:16). All live NetworkPolicy enforcement runs on a single CNI on Kind. The tier6 cloud parity matrix (tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml) governs per-provider capability coverage, but no test asserts NetworkPolicy egress enforcement specifically on a managed CNI (AWS VPC CNI or Azure CNI) augmented with Calico in policy-only mode, which is the recommended production configuration on EKS/AKS/GKE.
- **Gap:** Egress enforcement is verified on one CNI in one topology. The spec recommends the managed-CNI-plus-Calico-policy-only configuration for production managed Kubernetes, and that combination's egress enforcement (the property the entire §13.2 posture depends on) is unexercised. This is a deployment-combination observation. Target tier6 cloud (per provider).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier6 cloud harness (tests/testinfra/cloud) with the provider's native CNI plus Calico in policy-only mode installed, plus an agent-egress probe. Standing up the policy-only-mode CNI in the cloud overlay is part of this observation.
- **Suggested test:** Add a row to tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml for NetworkPolicy egress enforcement under the managed-CNI-plus-Calico configuration, and a tier6 test that repeats the T-13.2.1 agent-egress denial assertions on each provider's policy-only-mode cluster, using tests/testinfra/cloud.

### - [x] T-13.2.16 — NET-068 sub-rule (c) gateway-egress narrowing for the sandboxtemplate-deletion-guard webhook is enforced live [Medium] — RESOLVED c73bde55 (reconciled by proposal 0022)
- **Resolution:** Proposal 0022 added the `lenny-sandboxtemplate-deletion-guard` webhook to the §13.2 admission-webhook table row and introduced a new NET-068 egress sub-rule (c): the gateway's internal HTTP port (default 8080, `GET /internal/runtime-upgrade/active`) is reachable only from pods carrying the paired `lenny.dev/component: admission-webhook` + `lenny.dev/webhook-name: sandboxtemplate-deletion-guard` labels, not from every admission-webhook pod. This was a new testable requirement that did not exist at the 2026-06-03 audit. It landed with rendered-manifest coverage (charts/lenny/tests/sandboxtemplate-deletion-guard-webhook_test.yaml, charts/lenny/tests/admission-webhooks_test.yaml), a doc-consistency test (tests/tier11_docs/admission_webhook_alert_bijection_test.go), and — closing the live-enforcement gap this section otherwise tracks for every other egress rule — a tier9 cluster test, `TestDeletionGuardGatewayEgressLeastPrivilege` in tests/tier9_security/network_policy_test.go (added in commit c73bde55), which schedules a positive-control probe carrying both labels and asserts it reaches the gateway's internal port, and a negative-control probe carrying only the canonical `lenny.dev/component: admission-webhook` label and asserts its egress to that port times out (curl exit 28) under the live `lenny-system` default-deny plus the new sub-rule (c) allow.

## §13.3 Credential Flow <a id="t-13.3"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/13_security-model.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The RFC 8693 token-exchange invariants in §13.3 carry strong unit and tier-3 contract coverage in `pkg/tokenexchange` and `tests/tier3_contract/oauth_token`, the write-before-issue Postgres transaction is exercised at tier-2 against a real database, and cross-replica revocation propagation has a tier-2 component test over a real Redis. The proxy-mode pod-isolation guarantee has a tier-9 Kind probe, and the credential-lease gRPC surface has a tier-2 component test. Since the 2026-06-03 audit, proposal 0021 (F-CTL-1) added the gateway-mediated bootstrap admin-credential rotation ordering — the persist-before-revoke Secret/Postgres sequence and the crash-window-closing named-predecessor reclaimer, revoke-before-overwrite, and per-subject-serialization rules (spec/13_security-model.md:599-607) — and this landed with tier-2 component coverage against a real Postgres-backed issued-token store and audit chain (`tests/tier2_component/stores/admintoken_rotation_test.go`), so that requirement is resolved as T-13.3.13. The remaining gaps concentrate in the security-critical failure and adversarial paths the spec describes but no test exercises above unit tier: the no-grace-period revocation race on a live two-replica gateway (for the general `/v1/oauth/token` self-rotation grant, distinct from the now-covered bootstrap path), the §13.3 rate-limit and audit-sampling behavior on the actual `/v1/oauth/token` wire, the clock-drift self-eviction and `503 token_validation_unavailable` behavior, the Postgres-outage `503 token_store_unavailable` fail-closed behavior, the actor-token-revoked race during concurrent rotation, and the bootstrap OIDC-ID-token authentication path on the token endpoint. The proxy-mode end-to-end runtime path (agent pod presenting a lease token to the proxy and receiving an upstream response with credential injection) is exercised only as a unit-tier handler test and is documented as a deferred scaffold at tier-4. Counts: 5 High, 6 Medium, 1 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-13.3.1 — No-grace-period token revocation has no live cross-replica e2e or adversarial race test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "There is **no grace period** during which the old token continues to validate. Every token validation on every replica consults the in-memory revocation cache; on a cache miss ... the replica falls through to a direct `SELECT revoked_at FROM issued_tokens WHERE jti = $1` against Postgres." (spec/13_security-model.md:609) and "The general admin and service-principal token rotation grant ... is **atomic and immediate**: inside the write-before-issue transaction that creates the new token, the Token Service also writes `revoked_at = now()` on the previous token's `issued_tokens` row." (spec/13_security-model.md:597)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier2_component/securitycaches/propagation_test.go::TestTokenRevocationPropagation` proves that a `Revoke` on one in-memory `revocation.Cache` reaches a peer cache over real Redis pub/sub, but it operates on the cache primitive directly and never mints, rotates, or validates a token. `pkg/tokenservice` unit tests cover the in-process exchange. `spec-map.json` §13.3 lists the propagation test and the contract tests. No test rotates a token on replica A, then presents the old token to replica B and asserts `401 token_revoked`, and no test exercises the Postgres-fallback path on a cache miss or the worst-case `401 token_expired_or_revoked` transient window.
- **Gap:** The end-to-end revocation guarantee that a rotated token stops validating on every replica with no grace period is unverified above the cache primitive. The work is both a real user journey (alice rotates her admin token via `lenny-ctl` and the prior token immediately stops working everywhere) and an adversarial scenario (an attacker presents a freshly revoked token to a replica that has not yet seen the EventBus message, exercising the `SELECT revoked_at` fallback). Target tiers are tier4 (compose two-replica gateway plus Postgres plus Redis) and tier5 (Kind multi-replica).
- **Dependencies:** Requires a two-replica gateway harness wired to a shared Postgres and Redis (`tests/testinfra/gateway`, `tests/testinfra/containers`, `tests/testinfra/tokenservice`) and a way to drop or stall the EventBus on one replica to force the Postgres fallback. The EventBus-partition control does not exist in `tests/testinfra/chaos` for this path; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/token_revocation_no_grace_test.go` that mints a token, rotates it on replica A through `/v1/oauth/token`, presents the old `jti` to replica B and asserts `401 token_revoked`, then severs replica B's Redis subscription and asserts the `SELECT revoked_at` fallback still rejects the old token.

### - [ ] T-13.3.2 — Rate limiting and audit sampling on `/v1/oauth/token` have no contract or component test on the wire [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Default limits are 10 requests/second and 300 requests/minute per `(tenant_id, sub)` tuple — excess requests return `429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After`." (spec/13_security-model.md:617) and "the first rejection per `(tenant_id, sub)` tuple within any rolling 10-second window is written as a full `token.exchange_rate_limited` audit event ... subsequent rejections in the same window increment the `lenny_oauth_token_rate_limited_sampled_total` counter ... but do NOT write individual audit rows." (spec/13_security-model.md:619)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/tokenservice/audit_test.go::TestHandlerRateLimitedReturns429AndAudits` asserts the 429 plus the sampled-audit and counter behavior, but it is a package-internal unit test (`package tokenservice`, no build tag), and `pkg/tokenservice/ratelimit.go` is the in-process limiter. `tests/tier3_contract/oauth_token/oauth_token_test.go` carries no rate-limit case, and a grep for `429`, `RateLimit`, or `Retry-After` across `tests/tier3_contract/` returns nothing. The `GatewayRateLimitStorm` alert and the per-replica sampling-window locality are not exercised by any test above unit tier.
- **Gap:** The §13.3 rate-limit response contract (`429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After`), the per-tenant global limit, the limit-tier label vocabulary, and the audit-sampling write-before-error discipline are unverified on the actual HTTP surface. This is both an adversarial scenario (an attacker brute-forcing `subject_token` validation is contained and produces exactly one audit row per window) and a standards-adjacent contract check (the RFC 6749 error object plus `Retry-After`). Target tier is tier3 contract, with the per-replica sampling-locality claim at tier4.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The `tokenservice.NewServer` harness in `tests/tier3_contract/oauth_token/oauth_token_test.go` accepts `RateLimitOptions`, and `tests/testinfra/clockstep` or `tests/testinfra/timectl` can drive the rolling-window boundary deterministically.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/oauth_token/rate_limit_test.go` that configures `CallerPerSecond: 2`, fires three exchanges in one window, asserts the third returns `429 rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header, and asserts exactly one `token.exchange_rate_limited` audit row plus a `lenny_oauth_token_rate_limited_sampled_total` increment for the subsequent rejection.

### - [ ] T-13.3.3 — Postgres-outage fail-closed token issuance (`503 token_store_unavailable`) and revocation-validation fail-closed (`503 token_validation_unavailable`) are untested above the fake recorder [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "During a Postgres outage (primary unreachable or in failover), token issuance is unavailable by design — callers receive `503 token_store_unavailable` and the alert `TokenStoreUnavailable` fires; the platform does not fall back to issuing tokens without audit coverage." (spec/13_security-model.md:591) and "A gateway replica that cannot reach Postgres refuses to validate tokens — it returns `503 token_validation_unavailable` rather than accepting potentially-revoked tokens from its stale in-memory cache." (spec/13_security-model.md:611)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier3_contract/oauth_token/oauth_token_record_test.go::TestTokenServiceRefusesOnRecordFailure` injects a `fakeRecorder{err: ...}` and asserts `500` with no token, which exercises the generic record-failure branch but asserts `500` rather than the documented `503 token_store_unavailable` for an outage, and uses a fake rather than a real-Postgres outage. `tests/tier8_chaos/store_failure_test.go::TestPostgresUnavailable` exercises a live Postgres-down gateway but asserts the session-store and drain-readiness behavior, not token issuance or validation. No test asserts the `503` status code, the `token_store_unavailable` or `token_validation_unavailable` reason, or that the `TokenStoreUnavailable` alert fires.
- **Gap:** The fail-closed discipline under a real Postgres outage is the security-relevant guarantee that the platform never issues or validates a token it cannot audit or prove un-revoked. Both the issuance path (`503 token_store_unavailable`) and the validation path (`503 token_validation_unavailable`) are unverified end to end. Target tiers are tier4 (compose Postgres outage against a live Token Service) and tier8 (chaos recovery), and the scenario is a failure-path test.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a live Token Service plus gateway wired to a Postgres container that can be paused mid-run (`tests/testinfra/containers`, `tests/testinfra/tokenservice`, the `tests/tier8_chaos` pause primitives). The Postgres-pause-then-exchange wiring for the token path does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier8_chaos/token_store_failclosed_test.go` that pauses the Postgres container, issues a `/v1/oauth/token` exchange and asserts `503 token_store_unavailable`, presents an existing token for validation and asserts `503 token_validation_unavailable`, then unpauses and asserts both paths recover.

### - [ ] T-13.3.4 — Proxy-mode end-to-end credential flow (agent pod to proxy to upstream, real key out of the pod) has no component-or-higher test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Real API key never enters the AGENT pod and is never written to disk or tmpfs — it lives only in the gateway process's memory ... On lease expiry/revocation: LLM Proxy subsystem immediately rejects requests before the translator is invoked." (spec/13_security-model.md:649) and the proxy-mode flow block "Agent pod sends OpenAI- or Anthropic-shaped LLM requests to proxy URL with lease token ... Translator ... reads real key from the in-memory cache, forwards over TLS." (spec/13_security-model.md:646)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/llmproxy/handler_test.go` covers credential injection (`TestHandlerProxiesAndInjectsTheRealCredential` asserts the lease token is not forwarded upstream and the real key is injected) and lease rejection on missing, unknown, expired (`LEASE_EXPIRED`), revoked (`CREDENTIAL_REVOKED`), and SPIFFE-mismatch (`LEASE_SPIFFE_MISMATCH`) leases, but all of these run as package-internal unit tests against an `httptest` mock upstream. `tests/tier4_integration/scaffolds_test.go::TestLLMProxyAnthropic` is a `t.Logf` scaffold that explicitly defers the composite check to the unit handler test and a release smoke test. `tests/tier9_security/credential_leakage_test.go` probes the pod environment, filesystem, and egress capture on Kind but skips when no `cred-shell-echo` pod is present.
- **Gap:** The full proxy-mode runtime path through the live gateway binary, where an agent presents a lease token to the proxy URL and the gateway injects the real upstream credential while keeping it out of the pod, is exercised only at unit tier and is a documented tier-4 scaffold. The lease-expiry and lease-revocation rejection-before-translation branch (a security control) is also unit-only. The work is both a real user journey (alice's agent makes an LLM call in proxy mode and the upstream sees the real key) and an adversarial scenario (a revoked lease is rejected before the translator forwards anything). Target tiers are tier4 (live gateway with the proxy wired to a stub upstream) and tier5 (Kind with a real agent pod).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the gateway binary serving the proxy route plus a stub upstream provider (`tests/testinfra/gateway`, `tests/testinfra/stubs/llmprovider`) and, for tier5, an agent pod with a minted lease. The live-gateway proxy wiring in the tier-4 harness does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Convert `tests/tier4_integration/scaffolds_test.go::TestLLMProxyAnthropic` into a real test that boots the gateway with a proxy-mode pool, sends an Anthropic-shaped request to the proxy URL with a valid lease token against `tests/testinfra/stubs/llmprovider`, asserts the upstream received the injected key and not the lease token, then revokes the lease and asserts the next request is rejected with `CREDENTIAL_REVOKED` before any upstream forward.

### - [ ] T-13.3.5 — Actor-token-revoked race during concurrent rotation has no test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "For delegation child minting with `actor_token`, the Token Service reads the `actor_token`'s `jti` against the revocation cache **inside** the same advisory-locked transaction that issues the child. If the parent was rotated between the client's exchange submission and the Token Service's cache check ... the exchange is rejected with `invalid_grant` reason `actor_token_revoked`." (spec/13_security-model.md:615)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/tokenexchange/tokenexchange_test.go::TestValidateRejectsExpiredActor` and `tests/tier3_contract/oauth_token/oauth_token_test.go::TestExpiredSubjectRejected` cover the expired-actor and expired-subject cases. A grep for `actor_token_revoked` across `tests/` returns nothing. No test mints a child with an actor token whose `jti` has been revoked and asserts `invalid_grant` reason `actor_token_revoked`.
- **Gap:** The race-elimination guarantee that a stale parent token cannot mint a child that outlives the parent's legitimate lifetime is unverified. This is an adversarial scenario (a client races a revoked parent token against rotation to mint a long-lived child). Target tier is tier3 contract for the rejection-reason wire behavior, with the in-transaction revocation-check race at tier4 against real Postgres and Redis.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today for the contract case. The tier3 `oauth_token` harness can seed a revoked `jti` into a revocation-cache stub; the in-transaction race at tier4 reuses `tests/testinfra/containers` and `tests/testinfra/tokenservice`.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/oauth_token/actor_token_revoked_test.go` that marks the actor token's `jti` revoked, submits a child-minting exchange with that actor token, and asserts `400 invalid_grant` with reason `actor_token_revoked` and no issued token.

### - [ ] T-13.3.6 — Gateway clock-drift self-eviction and `503 token_validation_unavailable` above 5s drift are untested [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "absolute drift above 500ms triggers `GatewayClockDrift` at `warning` severity; above 2s at `critical` severity; and above 5s the replica removes itself from the Service endpoints (`/healthz` reports degraded) and returns `503 token_validation_unavailable` on every exchange rather than issue or validate tokens whose `exp` it cannot trust." (spec/13_security-model.md:595)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier3_contract/rest_auth/auth_test.go::TestExpiredTokenReturns401` and `tests/tier7a_load_local/scenarios/clock_skew_admission/scenario.go` exercise the ±1s skew tolerance on the `exp` check at the `jwt.Verify` level (an expired token is rejected, a fresh one accepted). Neither drives the drift thresholds, the `/healthz` degraded transition, the self-removal from Service endpoints, or the `503 token_validation_unavailable` response above 5s drift. A grep for `token_validation_unavailable` across `tests/` returns nothing.
- **Gap:** The drift-driven fail-closed behavior, where a replica with an untrustworthy clock removes itself and refuses to validate or issue tokens, is unverified. This is a failure-path test for a replica whose NTP synchronization has degraded. Target tiers are tier4 (a gateway with an injected clock offset) and tier8 (chaos NTP-drift injection), with the alert-firing assertion at the metrics layer.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a way to inject a controlled clock offset into a running gateway replica (`tests/testinfra/timectl` or `tests/testinfra/clockstep`) and to read `lenny_time_drift_seconds` plus `/healthz`. The drift-injection hook for the gateway binary does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier8_chaos/gateway_clock_drift_test.go` that advances a replica's offset past 5s, asserts `/healthz` reports degraded and the replica leaves the Service endpoints, asserts every `/v1/oauth/token` call returns `503 token_validation_unavailable`, then restores the clock and asserts recovery.

### - [ ] T-13.3.7 — Bootstrap authentication on `/v1/oauth/token` via an upstream OIDC ID token has no contract test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The bearer token is either (a) an upstream OIDC ID token from the tenant's configured IdP (the **bootstrap** credential — first interaction with Lenny; Lenny verifies the token's signature against the IdP's JWKS and derives `tenant_id` via the tenant's OIDC-claim-mapping configuration), or (b) a previously issued Lenny access token ... `/v1/oauth/token` is reachable without a pre-existing Lenny-issued token." (spec/13_security-model.md:623)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier3_contract/oauth_token/oauth_token_test.go::TestMissingCallerRejected` asserts a `401` when no `Authorization` header is present, and the happy-path tests use a Lenny-minted bearer as the caller token. No test presents an upstream OIDC ID token verified against an IdP JWKS as the bootstrap caller credential, and no test asserts that `tenant_id` is derived from the tenant's OIDC-claim-mapping. The `tests/testinfra/stubs/oidc` stub exists but is not wired into the `oauth_token` contract suite.
- **Gap:** The bootstrap path, where a first-time caller authenticates to the token endpoint with an IdP ID token and no pre-existing Lenny token, is unverified. This is a real user journey (alice's first interaction exchanges her IdP ID token for a Lenny access token) and a standards-conformance check (signature verification against the IdP JWKS and OIDC-claim mapping). Target tier is tier3 contract.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. `tests/testinfra/stubs/oidc` provides a JWKS-serving IdP stub that the `tokenservice.NewServer` harness can be pointed at.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/oauth_token/bootstrap_oidc_test.go` that mints an ID token from the OIDC stub, presents it as the `Authorization` bearer with no prior Lenny token, and asserts the exchange succeeds and the issued token carries the `tenant_id` derived from the configured claim mapping.

### - [ ] T-13.3.8 — `token.exchanged` audit payload secret-exclusion is not asserted; only the event type and chain linkage are checked [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Token contents — `access_token`, `subject_token`, `actor_token` — are NEVER written to audit payloads; only claim identifiers (`sub`, `jti`) and metadata (`scope`, `audience`, `delegation_depth`) are recorded." (spec/13_security-model.md:587) and "any `tenant_mismatch` rejection is itself audited with `policy_result: \"rejected:tenant_mismatch\"`." (spec/13_security-model.md:585)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier2_component/auditstore/write_before_issue_test.go` asserts the `token.exchanged` row is written atomically with the `issued_tokens` row, chains correctly, and rolls back on a duplicate `jti`, but it constructs the audit payload itself in the test and never asserts that the production exchange handler excludes `access_token`, `subject_token`, and `actor_token` from the payload. `pkg/tokenservice/audit_test.go::TestHandlerEmitsRejectionAuditOnInvalidScope` checks the rejection event type. No test asserts that a rejected exchange carries `policy_result: "rejected:tenant_mismatch"` (or the analogous reason) and that no token material appears in the payload.
- **Gap:** The audit-payload secret-exclusion guarantee and the rejection `policy_result` vocabulary are unverified against the production handler. This is an adversarial-adjacent control (a misconfigured handler that logs raw tokens leaks credentials into the SIEM). Target tier is tier2 component or tier3 contract against the live handler audit emission.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The `pkg/tokenservice` handler harness with an in-memory auditor (used by `audit_test.go`) can be promoted to a tagged component test that inspects the emitted payload.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier2_component/auditstore/token_exchanged_payload_test.go` that drives an accepted and a tenant-mismatch-rejected exchange through the handler and asserts the emitted `token.exchanged` payload contains `sub`, `jti`, `scope`, `audience`, and `delegation_depth`, contains no `access_token`, `subject_token`, or `actor_token`, and that the rejection carries `policy_result: "rejected:tenant_mismatch"`.

### - [ ] T-13.3.9 — Connector-credential isolation (gateway holds downstream OAuth tokens, pod never receives them) has no pod-side verification test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Gateway holds all downstream OAuth tokens → Pod receives: session context + projected SA token → Pod never receives: client tokens, downstream OAuth tokens." (spec/13_security-model.md:544) and "Connector credentials (OAuth tokens for external tools and agents) are used by the gateway on behalf of pods (pods never see them)." (spec/13_security-model.md:656)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier4_integration/connector_oauth_test.go::TestOAuthConnector` drives the §9.3 authorize-callback flow and asserts the gateway completes the code exchange and stores the connector token, plus anti-CSRF state single-use. `tests/tier9_security/credential_leakage_test.go` probes for LLM-provider credential prefixes (`sk-ant-`, `ghp_`, and similar) in the pod environment and filesystem, which incidentally covers connector OAuth token prefixes like `ghp_`, but the probe targets the `cred-shell-echo` pool and skips when absent, and it is not framed as a connector-token isolation assertion. No test verifies that a pod running an MCP tool call against a connector receives only the session context and projected SA token while the gateway holds the downstream OAuth token.
- **Gap:** The connector-credential isolation boundary, the upper half of the §13.3 credential model, is verified only indirectly through the credential-leakage prefix scan and is never asserted as a property of a connector-driven session. This is both a real user journey (alice's agent invokes a GitHub MCP tool and the gateway injects the OAuth token without exposing it to the pod) and an adversarial scenario (a pod attempts to read the downstream OAuth token and cannot). Target tier is tier5 e2e on Kind with a registered connector and a live agent pod.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a Kind cluster with a registered OAuth connector and an agent pod making a tool call (`tests/testinfra/kind`, the connector fixtures from `tests/tier4_integration/connector_oauth_test.go`). The connector-token pod-side probe does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/connector_token_isolation_test.go` that registers an OAuth connector, runs a session that invokes a connector tool, and asserts from inside the pod (environment, mounts, and the gateway-injected request) that the downstream OAuth token never appears in the pod while the tool call still succeeds through the gateway.

### - [ ] T-13.3.10 — Token Service mTLS caller authentication and certificate rotation are unverified end to end [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Per [RFC 6749 §2.3], token endpoints authenticate clients. Lenny's token endpoint treats every caller as a **public client** and authenticates via the `Authorization: Bearer <caller_token>` header." (spec/13_security-model.md:623) combined with the §13.3 requirement, recorded in `tests/tier9_security/reviews/credential-review.md` Finding 1, that "the Token Service [must] authenticate callers over mTLS" so subject, actor, and minted tokens do not traverse the network in clear text.
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier9_security/reviews/credential-review.md` Finding 1 (High, tracked to Phase 12a) records that `cmd/lenny-token-service/main.go` serves plaintext HTTP with no `TLSConfig`, no client-certificate verification, and no SPIFFE peer check, so the mTLS rotation property cannot hold and there is no test for it. `tests/tier4_integration/tokenservice_cutover_test.go` boots the Token Service and gateway as subprocesses and references the mTLS gRPC link in its doc comment but asserts only that the gRPC dial succeeds and the gateway boots, not that mTLS terminates or that the client certificate is verified. `tests/tier9_security/tls_test.go` covers gateway TLS, not the Token Service endpoint.
- **Gap:** The Token Service mTLS termination, gateway client-certificate verification, and rotation-without-dropping-in-flight-leases property are unverified and currently unimplemented. This is a security-control verification (the token endpoint must not accept callers over an unauthenticated, unencrypted transport). Target tiers are tier9 security (the mTLS control) and tier5 (cert-manager-issued material with a certificate roll).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the Phase 12a Token Service that terminates mTLS, plus cert-manager wiring on Kind (`tests/testinfra/kind`, `tests/testinfra/security`). The implementation and the rotation-aware key provider do not exist yet; the missing implementation is recorded in `credential-review.md` Finding 1 and building the test is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier9_security/tokenservice_mtls_test.go` that asserts a plaintext or wrong-client-certificate connection to the Token Service is refused, a valid gateway client certificate is accepted, and a certificate rotation completes without failing an in-flight exchange.

### - [ ] T-13.3.11 — Per-dialect cap matrix for `lenny-ops` and `llm-proxy` audiences is only partially exercised [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`audience` | The target audience: `lenny-gateway` (default), `lenny-ops` (operability-scope tokens), `llm-proxy` (credential-lease tokens)." (spec/13_security-model.md:564) and "Response `expires_in` | Seconds until expiry; constrained by upstream lifetime caps (lease TTL, delegation tree TTL, user session max, etc.)." (spec/13_security-model.md:567)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier3_contract/oauth_token/oauth_token_test.go::TestPerDialectCapCapsExp` exercises the `lenny-gateway` 24h cap and `TestPerDialectCapCapsExpForMultiValueAudience` exercises the tightest-cap selection across `lenny-gateway` plus `lenny-ops`. The single-audience `llm-proxy` cap (lease tokens) and the single-audience `lenny-ops` cap (operability tokens) are not each asserted in isolation, and the `pkg/tokenexchange/tokenexchange_test.go::TestValidateExpRespectsPerDialectCap` unit test covers the arithmetic but not the per-audience wire response.
- **Gap:** Two of the three documented audiences lack a single-audience contract assertion that the cap is applied to the wire `expires_in`. This is a single missing edge case per audience on an otherwise covered behavior. Target tier is tier3 contract.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The existing `tokenservice.NewServer` harness accepts a `PerDialectCap` map keyed by audience.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `tests/tier3_contract/oauth_token/oauth_token_test.go` with single-audience cases for `lenny-ops` (1h) and `llm-proxy` (1h) that request an over-cap `expires_in` and assert the response is capped to the audience ceiling.

### - [ ] T-13.3.12 — Recursive child revocation on a parent revocation request is documented in §13.3 but covered only in the §8.3 delegation suite [Info] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Delegation child tokens minted from a parent that is later rotated continue to validate on their own `jti` until their own `exp` (children are not transitively revoked by parent rotation unless the rotation is specifically a revocation request — `grant_type=...:token-exchange` with `scope=\"\"` and `requested_token_type=...:access_token:revoked` triggers recursive child revocation, see [§8.3])." (spec/13_security-model.md:613)
- **Existing tests:** `spec-map.json` routes the recursive-revocation behavior to §8.3 (`pkg/delegation/lease`), and the §13.3 entry does not list a test for it. The §13.3 contract suite (`tests/tier3_contract/oauth_token`) does not exercise the `access_token:revoked` requested-token-type or assert that children continue to validate on their own `jti` after an ordinary parent rotation.
- **Gap:** This is an observation about coverage location rather than a missing test. The recursive-child-revocation behavior is referenced from §13.3 but its coverage, if any, lives under §8.3. A reviewer auditing §13.3 in isolation cannot confirm the behavior is tested, and the distinction between an ordinary rotation (children survive) and a revocation request (children are recursively revoked) should be exercised at the token-exchange wire to close the §13.3 surface.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today against the `oauth_token` contract harness once the delegation-tree revocation handler is wired into the exchange path.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier3 case in `tests/tier3_contract/oauth_token` (or a cross-referenced entry in the §8.3 delegation suite) that rotates a parent normally and asserts a previously minted child still validates, then issues the `access_token:revoked` revocation request and asserts the child's `jti` is revoked, and record the coverage under §13.3 in `spec-map.json`.

### - [x] T-13.3.13 — Gateway-mediated bootstrap admin-credential rotation ordering and its crash-window closure (named predecessor, revoke-before-overwrite, per-subject serialization) had no test [High] — RESOLVED 628b4d95 (reconciled against proposal 0021)
- **Resolution:** Proposal 0021 (F-CTL-1) added the §13.3 gateway-mediated bootstrap admin-credential rotation ordering as new normative spec text (spec/13_security-model.md:599-607): the bootstrap `lenny-admin` Secret rotation is a gateway-direct in-process mint, distinct from the general `/v1/oauth/token` self-rotation grant, that must persist the new token to the Secret before durably revoking the prior one, and it names three rules (a leader-gated periodic reclaimer keyed on a named predecessor slot in the Secret, revoke-before-overwrite of that slot, and per-subject Postgres advisory-lock serialization) that close the resulting persist-before-revoke crash window. Commit `628b4d95` ("0021 S11: rewrite admin-rotation ordering with audit, durable revoke, prevJtiKey, and the advisory lock (C7, F-CTL-1)") implements the ordering, and `2ab309df` ("0021 S12: register the leader-gated admin-token reclaimer sweep (C7 crash recovery)") wires the reclaimer sweep into the gateway. The requirement now has tier-2 component coverage against a real Postgres-backed issued-token store and audit chain in `tests/tier2_component/stores/admintoken_rotation_test.go`: `TestAdminRotationEmitsExchangeAndRevokeAudit` and `TestAdminRotationDurablyRevokesOldTokenAndGatesCache` assert the persist-then-revoke ordering and audit emission; `TestAdminRotationSecretPatchFailureLeavesOldTokenLive` asserts a Secret-patch failure leaves the prior token live; `TestAdminRotationConcurrentLeavesNoLiveSupersededToken` exercises the per-subject advisory-lock serialization under concurrent rotations; and `TestReclaimerRevokesOrphanedPredecessorAfterCrash`, `TestReclaimerMidRotationDoesNotRevokeSuccessor`, `TestReclaimerLeavesFlow2SelfRotatedTokenAlive`, and `TestReclaimerTwoCrashRetryRotationsRevokeBothPredecessors` exercise the leader-gated reclaimer's crash-window closure, including the two-consecutive-crash-then-retry case and the guarantee that the general self-rotation grant's token is never named as a predecessor. Package-level unit tests in `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admintoken/admintoken_test.go` (e.g. `TestRotateOrderingUnderLock_spec_13_3_599`, `TestRotateRevokesOrphanedPredecessorBeforeOverwrite_spec_13_3_601`) and `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admintoken/reclaimer/reclaimer_test.go` cover the same ordering and sweep logic in isolation. All are registered under `tests/spec-map.json` §13.3.

## §13.4 Upload Security <a id="t-13.4"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/13_security-model.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
Since generation, archive extraction moved from the pod adapter into the gateway (`F-7.4.1`/`F-13.4.1`/`F-7.4.11`, commit `b7721eab`), closing the trust-boundary divergence T-13.4.4 reported and giving `lenny_upload_extraction_aborted_total` a real production emitter (T-13.4.3). A wire-contract test now proves one §13.4 sub-code (`max_entry_count`) surfaces as `UPLOAD_ARCHIVE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` through the real HTTP handler (commit `83f6bf7d`), and the archive-validator unit suite (now `pkg/upload/archive/archive_test.go`) covers every attack class the spec names. What remains open is narrower than at generation time but still real: the other eight §15.1 sub-codes and MCP-surface parity are unproven at the wire level, no tier9 security test drives a hostile archive against a live surface, the symlink opt-in's CRD-to-extraction wiring (now implemented) has no end-to-end test, the TESTING.md-claimed `tests/tier2_component/workspace_plan/` archive-bomb suite still does not exist, and no deployment combination beyond the in-process envtest harness (tier4 compose/MinIO, tier5 Kind, tier6 cloud) exercises upload security. A checked-in hostile-archive fixture corpus (`tests/testdata/uploads/archives`) predates the audit and remains unwired to any test. Counts: 4 High, 4 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-13.4.1 — No component/integration/e2e test drives a hostile archive through the real upload pipeline [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Path traversal protection: reject `..` components, absolute paths, and symlinks whose canonicalized target escapes the workspace root. Canonicalization is a normative requirement: every extracted or uploaded path is resolved (`filepath.Clean` + absolute-root prefix check) before the file is written." (spec/13_security-model.md:664) and the archive-validator ceilings (spec/13_security-model.md:667-675).
- **Existing tests:** Extraction moved gateway-side since generation (`F-7.4.1`/`F-13.4.1`/`F-7.4.11`, commit `b7721eab`). `pkg/upload/archive/archive_test.go` is now the primary extractor suite (`TestExtract_PathEscapesRoot_spec_13_4`, `TestExtract_MaxEntryCount_spec_13_4`, `TestExtract_MaxPathDepth_spec_13_4`, `TestExtract_MaxPathLength_spec_13_4`, `TestExtract_DecompressionRatio_spec_13_4_659`, and the rest of the §13.4 attack-class list), still tier1 unit (`package archive_test`, in-memory byte slices). `pkg/upload/upload_test.go` retains the validator-function unit tests cited at generation. Two envtest-backed tests now drive a hostile archive through the real HTTP-to-adapter pipeline end to end: `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start_pod_test.go::TestFinalizeRejectsOverLimitArchiveAsNonRetryable_spec_13_4` posts a session create + finalize referencing an over-`MaxEntryCount` archive blob through the real `sessionserver.Handler()`, a real envtest kube-apiserver, and a real in-process adapter gRPC server, and asserts the 413 rejection; `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/binder_archive_test.go::TestBindUploadArchiveAbortRecordsMetric` does the same for a hardlink entry. `pkg/adapter/workspace/symlink_test.go` asserts the pod-side adapter now fail-closed rejects `uploadArchive`/`gitClone` sources rather than decompressing them. No test yet exercises path traversal, symlink escape, decompression-ratio bombs, or path-depth/length overflow through this same component-tier HTTP-to-adapter path (only `max_entry_count` and `non_regular_entry` are proven there), and `tests/tier4_integration`, `tests/tier5_e2e_kind`, `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud`, and `tests/tier9_security` still contain no upload-archive test of any kind.
- **Gap:** The trust-boundary inversion this finding originally reported (extraction ran in the pod) is fixed, and two attack classes are now proven end to end at tier2 (envtest + real adapter). The remaining gap is narrower than at generation time: the other seven §13.4 sub-codes are asserted only against the in-memory `archive.Extract` function, not through the HTTP-to-adapter path, and no tier4 (real MinIO/compose), tier5 (Kind), tier6 (cloud), or tier9 (security) test exists at all. Target tier2 to round out the remaining sub-codes on the existing envtest harness, then tier4/tier5 for the compose-stack and Kind runs.
- **Dependencies:** The tier2 harness now exists (envtest helpers in `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession`, httptest helpers in `pkg/gateway/sessionserver`) and needs only new hostile-archive fixtures wired in to cover the remaining sub-codes. A hostile-archive fixture corpus already exists on disk at `tests/testdata/uploads/archives` (`bomb-deep.tar`, `bomb-count.tar`, `path-traversal.tar`, `setuid.tar`, `clean.tar.gz`, generated by `scripts/regen-upload-fixtures.sh`) but is referenced by no Go test in the repository — wiring it in is part of this finding rather than new fixture work. The tier4/tier5 runs still require the compose stack with real MinIO and a pod-session binder driver (tests/testinfra/sessiondriver); that infrastructure does not exist yet.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start_pod_test.go` (or a new `upload_archive_security_test.go` alongside it) with one case per remaining §13.4 sub-code using the existing envtest+adapter harness and the `tests/testdata/uploads/archives` fixtures, then add `tests/tier4_integration/upload_archive_security_test.go` and `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/upload_archive_test.go` repeating the full corpus against the compose stack and Kind using tests/testinfra/sessiondriver.

### - [ ] T-13.4.2 — `UPLOAD_ARCHIVE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and its `details.reason` sub-codes have no contract test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Validator violations surface to clients as `UPLOAD_ARCHIVE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` with `details.reason` carrying the specific sub-code (see [§15.1](15_external-api-surface.md#151-rest-api) error reference)." (spec/13_security-model.md:676)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/externalapi/errorclassify/errorclassify.go:360` still registers the code as a permanent, non-retryable error. Since generation, commit `83f6bf7d` ("0018 S3: emit UPLOAD_ARCHIVE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED for archive-validation failures") landed a genuine wire-contract test: `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start_pod_test.go::TestFinalizeRejectsOverLimitArchiveAsNonRetryable_spec_13_4` posts a real HTTP finalize request through `sessionserver.Handler()`, decodes the JSON error envelope, and asserts `error.code == "UPLOAD_ARCHIVE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED"`, `error.category == "PERMANENT"`, `retryable == false`, `details.reason == upload.ReasonMaxEntryCount`, and the absence of `Retry-After`. This covers exactly one of the nine §15.1 sub-codes. A grep for the other eight sub-code constants (`ReasonPathEscapesRoot`, `ReasonSymlink`, `ReasonNonRegularEntry`, `ReasonMaxDecompressedSize`, `ReasonMaxDecompressionRatio`, `ReasonMaxEntrySize`, `ReasonMaxPathDepth`, `ReasonMaxPathLength`) across `tests/` and `pkg/gateway` turns up only the `pkg/upload/archive` unit suite, not a wire-level assertion, and no test asserts the mapping is stable on the MCP surface (`pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools`).
- **Gap:** The client-facing wire contract is no longer entirely unpinned — one sub-code (`max_entry_count`) is now asserted end to end through the real HTTP handler. The other eight documented sub-codes and the REST/MCP parity claim remain unverified at the wire level. A refactor that broke the mapping for any sub-code other than `max_entry_count`, or that diverged the MCP surface from REST, would not be caught. Target tier3 contract (or the same tier2 envtest harness already in place) for the remaining sub-codes, plus an MCP-surface assertion.
- **Dependencies:** The httptest-driven gateway upload handler now exists and is proven with a real envtest+adapter harness (`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start_pod_test.go` helpers); extending it to the other sub-codes needs one crafted archive fixture per remaining sub-code — `tests/testdata/uploads/archives` already has fixtures that can seed several (`bomb-deep.tar` for `max_path_depth`, `path-traversal.tar` for `path_escapes_root`) — plus an MCP-equivalent request path, which does not exist yet.
- **Suggested test:** Parameterize the `TestFinalizeRejectsOverLimitArchiveAsNonRetryable_spec_13_4` pattern (or extract it into a table test) over the remaining eight §13.4 sub-codes using the `tests/testdata/uploads/archives` fixtures, and add a parallel MCP-surface assertion via tests/testinfra/gateway so the two surfaces agree on `details.reason`.

### - [x] T-13.4.3 — `lenny_upload_extraction_aborted_total{error_type}` is declared but never emitted, and no test asserts emission [High] — RESOLVED b7721eab
- **Resolution:** Commit `b7721eab` ("F-7.4.1/F-13.4.1/F-7.4.11: move archive extraction into the gateway") gave `lenny_upload_extraction_aborted_total` a real producer: `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession.Binder.ExtractionAbort` is invoked with the §13.4 sub-code on every extraction abort, and `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/uploadmetrics.go`'s `PromUploadMetrics.AddExtractionAbort` increments the cataloged counter against a real Prometheus registry, asserted by `TestPromUploadMetrics_EmitsCatalogedNames` in `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/uploadmetrics_test.go` (reads the value back with `testutil.ToFloat64`). `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/binder_archive_test.go::TestBindUploadArchiveAbortRecordsMetric` drives a real hardlink archive through `Bind` and asserts the callback fires with `error_type=non_regular_entry`. Commit `fe86fab9` wires `w.podBinder.ExtractionAbort = uploadMetrics.AddExtractionAbort` in `cmd/lenny-gateway`, so the counter moves in the production binary rather than only in tests.

### - [x] T-13.4.4 — "Pod trusts only the gateway" and the gateway-side-extraction claim are unverified, and the implementation diverges from the spec [High] — RESOLVED b7721eab
- **Resolution:** Commit `b7721eab` ("F-7.4.1/F-13.4.1/F-7.4.11: move archive extraction into the gateway") closed the spec-vs-code divergence this finding reported. Archive decompression and path canonicalization now run in the gateway's `pkg/upload/archive` extractor inside the shared §4.1 `uploadSubsystem` gate (`Binder.UploadGate`), invoked from `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession.Binder.stageWorkspace`, and the pod-side adapter's `materializeSource` fail-closed rejects `uploadArchive` and `gitClone` sources (`pkg/adapter/workspace/materialize.go:491-507`: "uploadArchive sources are extracted by the gateway; the adapter must not decompress archives"). Both directions are now tested: `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/binder_archive_test.go::TestBindExtractsUploadArchive` proves the gateway performs the extraction, and `pkg/adapter/workspace/symlink_test.go` proves the pod refuses to. The residual — a live-channel probe confirming a non-gateway-mediated write cannot introduce archive bytes into a pod — is narrower than the original finding and is tracked separately as T-13.4.11.

### - [ ] T-13.4.5 — No adversarial security-tier test for the archive-validator attack classes [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`hardlink`, `character-device`, `block-device`, `FIFO`, and `socket` entries rejected outright." and the decompression-ratio, entry-count, and per-entry-size ceilings (spec/13_security-model.md:668-675).
- **Existing tests:** The validator and extractor now live in `pkg/upload/archive/archive_test.go` (`TestExtract_NonRegularEntry_Hardlink_spec_7_4_457`, `TestExtract_MaxEntryCount_spec_13_4`, `TestExtract_MaxPathDepth_spec_13_4`, `TestExtract_MaxPathLength_spec_13_4`, `TestExtract_MaxEntrySize_StreamingOverrun_spec_13_4`, `TestExtract_DecompressionRatio_spec_13_4_659`, `TestExtract_SymlinkRejectedByDefault_spec_7_4_458`, `TestExtract_SymlinkEscapeRejected_spec_13_4_665`), all tier1 unit against in-memory archive bytes. `tests/tier9_security/scaffolds_test.go` still lists no upload/archive check among the implemented tier9 suites (network policy, mTLS, admission, tenant isolation, audit integrity, RBAC, SSRF), and `tests/tier7a_load_local/scenarios/oversized_request_rejection_recovery/scenario.go` still calls the validator as a pure function under concurrency rather than through a live gateway endpoint. No tier9 test drives any of these archive classes against a running upload surface.
- **Gap:** Every attack class is now exercised more completely at unit tier (the ratio, entry-count, and hardlink defenses the extraction loop previously lacked are implemented and unit-tested), but the security tier still has no adversarial exercise of the live surface. This is an adversarial-path gap. Target tier9 security.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the `tests/testdata/uploads/archives` corpus (already checked in but currently unreferenced by any Go test — see T-13.4.1) and a live or compose upload surface (tests/testinfra/security, tests/testinfra/sessiondriver, or the envtest+adapter harness already built in `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession`). Wiring the existing fixtures into a tier9 test is the remaining work.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier9_security/upload_archive_test.go` that drives one archive per attack class (each forbidden entry kind, ratio bomb, entry-count flood, oversized entry, over-length and over-depth paths) against the live upload surface and asserts rejection with the §13.4 sub-code, reusing the `tests/testdata/uploads/archives` corpus.

- **Spec/Doc:** "Symlinks rejected by default; if a Runtime opts in via `allowSymlinks: true`, the target must canonicalize inside `/workspace/current` and must not traverse `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev`, or `/run/lenny`. Post-promotion symlink re-validation applies." (spec/13_security-model.md:675)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/upload/upload_test.go::TestValidateEntrySymlinkOptInWorkspaceLocalTarget` and `TestValidateEntrySymlinkRejectsEscape` still cover the validator functions. - **Suggested test:** Add a case to `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/binder_archive_test.go` (or a new `tests/tier4_integration/upload_symlink_test.go`) that sets `ArchivePolicy.AllowSymlinks: true` on the bound Runtime, materializes an internal symlink under it, then a second archive whose symlink resolves inside staging but escapes `/workspace/current` after promotion, and asserts the documented promotion rollback.
