### - [ ] T-13.4.10 — `pkg/upload` extraction tests are unit-tier despite asserting component-relevant behavior [Info] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Staging → validation → promotion pattern." (spec/13_security-model.md:666)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/upload/archive/archive_test.go` (gateway-side extraction, `package archive_test`) and `pkg/adapter/workspace/promotion_internal_test.go`, `promotion_test.go` (pod-side staging-to-current promotion, `package workspace_test`) exercise the staging, validation, and promotion steps — the extractor against in-memory archive bytes, the promotion step against `t.TempDir()`. `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/binder_archive_test.go` adds a stronger harness (envtest kube-apiserver + real adapter gRPC server over the wire) but still does not mount a real pod's `/workspace/staging`. They provide strong logic coverage but still run without a real blob store or a pod-mounted staging volume.
- **Gap:** No coverage is missing at the logic level; this is an observation that the staging→validation→promotion pattern is verified only against in-memory bytes and the local filesystem, not against the real staging directory a pod mounts. The component-tier verification is captured by T-13.4.1 and T-13.4.6, and has moved closer to tier2 (the envtest+adapter harness now exists) without yet reaching a pod-mounted staging directory. Target tier2.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today once the T-13.4.1 harness is extended to mount a real staging volume.
- **Suggested test:** When the T-13.4.1 harness is extended, promote the staging-and-promotion assertions to a tier2 component test that runs against a pod-mounted `/workspace/staging` so the pattern is verified in its deployed context.

### - [ ] T-13.4.11 — No test proves a non-gateway-mediated write cannot introduce archive bytes into a pod's workspace [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Pod trusts only the gateway (not arbitrary clients)." (spec/13_security-model.md:663)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/adapter/transport.go`'s `TLSServerOption` sets `ClientAuth: tls.RequireAndVerifyClientCert`, confirmed constructed correctly by `pkg/adapter/server_test.go::TestTLSServerOptionConfiguresMutualTLS` and `TestTLSServerOptionRejectsUnusableClientCA`, but no test dials the adapter's gRPC server with an untrusted or self-signed client certificate and asserts the live connection is rejected — the mTLS tests all stop at config construction. `tests/tier9_security/tls_test.go` covers admission-webhook CA bundle readiness, not the adapter link. No test attempts to write directly into a pod's `/workspace/staging` or invoke `FinalizeWorkspace` outside the gateway-mediated `podsession.Binder` path.
- **Gap:** The trust-boundary claim's runtime enforcement (mTLS on the adapter link) has never been exercised end to end with a live rejected connection, so a regression that weakened `ClientAuth` to `RequestClientCert` or dropped verification would pass every existing test. This is the narrower residual left after T-13.4.4 closed the code-vs-spec divergence on which component performs extraction. Target tier9 security.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a test TLS client certificate not signed by the trusted CA (tests/testinfra/security or a locally generated throwaway cert) and a running adapter server instance (`adapter.New` plus `TLSServerOption`, already used in `pkg/adapter/server_test.go`) — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier9 test (or extend `pkg/adapter/server_test.go`) that starts the adapter's gRPC server with `TLSServerOption` and mTLS configured, dials it with a client certificate signed by an untrusted CA, and asserts the handshake fails, then dials with the trusted gateway client certificate and asserts success — pinning the "pod trusts only the gateway" boundary at the transport level rather than only at config-construction level.

## §13.5 Delegation Chain Content Security <a id="t-13.5"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/13_security-model.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The seven §13.5 mitigations have strong unit and package-level coverage. The maxInputSize cap, the PreDelegation `DelegationPolicyEvaluator`, the PreMessageDelivery message scan, the PreExportMaterialization file scan, the messaging rate limits, the messagingScope reachability rules, and the external `RequestInterceptor` gRPC client are each exercised in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools`, `pkg/gateway/policy/interceptor`, `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/delegation/export`, and `pkg/gateway/policy`, and the Postgres-backed `DelegationPolicy` registry has a tier2 component contract in `tests/tier2_component/stores/delegationpolicystore_test.go`. Coverage thins out above tier2: the tier4 `TestDelegation` covers only the §8.2 spawn-and-tree contract and `TestPolicyGate` covers §11.2 quota, so no integration test drives the content-security phases through the wired gateway binary; there is no tier3 contract test pinning the `INPUT_TOO_LARGE` or `EXPORT_FILE_SCAN_*` envelopes across REST and MCP; the external interceptor gRPC SPI is never pinned against the published proto at tier3 or tier10; tier5/tier6 and tier8 carry nothing for this surface; and the tier9 security suite has no adversarial prompt-injection, `CLAUDE.md`-export-injection, or multi-sibling-flooding scenario. The spec-map.json §13.5 entry lists a package `pkg/delegation/security` that does not exist on disk and names no concrete tier2+ test. A repository-wide package regroup (proposal 0020: `pkg/gateway/mcptools` → `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools`, `pkg/gateway/interceptor` → `pkg/gateway/policy/interceptor`, `pkg/gateway/delegation` → `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/delegation`) relocated every package this section cites; the §13.5 spec text itself is unchanged since the 2026-06-03 audit, and none of the moved tests closed a gap on its own. A new package-level test (`pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/content_policy_scoped_test.go`, landed with the F-13.5.2 per-policy `interceptorRef` resolution) adds finer-grained fake-chain coverage of scoped scanner selection on the `send_message` path, but it does not reach the wired gateway binary and so does not close T-13.5.9. Counts: 3 High, 5 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-13.5.1 — Delegation content-security phases are never exercised through the wired gateway binary at integration tier [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`contentPolicy.maxInputSize` ... enforces a hard byte-size cap on delegation input" and "`contentPolicy.interceptorRef` invokes a `RequestInterceptor` at the `PreDelegation` phase ... before any delegation is processed." (spec/13_security-model.md:682-683)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/delegate_max_input_size_test.go` (`TestDelegateTaskInputTooLargeSurfacesCanonicalCode_spec_8_3_157`) and `delegate_integration_test.go` (same package) exercise the PreDelegation evaluator and a PreDelegation rewrite against an in-process MCP server with a fake chain. The tier4 `tests/tier4_integration/delegation_test.go` (`TestDelegation`) covers only the §8.2 spawn-and-tree lineage and registers no content policy. `tests/tier4_integration/policy_test.go` (`TestPolicyGate`) exercises the §11.2 QuotaEvaluator on session creation, not the delegation content phases. No tier4 test starts `cmd/lenny-gateway` with a configured `maxInputSize` and drives an over-cap `lenny/delegate_task` to assert `INPUT_TOO_LARGE` and that no child session is created.
- **Gap:** The PreDelegation enforcement that `cmd/lenny-gateway/policychain.go` wires (the `DelegationPolicyEvaluator` registered at line 77, relocated there from `main.go` by the proposal-0020 package regroup) is never verified through the running binary against a real store. This is both a real user journey (alice delegates a task whose input exceeds the cap and receives a rejection) and a failure-path test. Target tier4, with a tier5 follow-on for the on-cluster path.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. Uses `tests/testinfra/gateway` (`StartWith`) and `tests/testinfra/containers` for Redis/Postgres, following the `TestDelegation` and `TestPolicyGate` patterns already in the package.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/delegation_content_policy_test.go` starting the gateway with `LENNY_DELEGATION_MAX_INPUT_SIZE` set low, driving an over-cap `delegate_task` through the MCP shim, asserting the `INPUT_TOO_LARGE` envelope and an absent child via `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/tree`, plus a within-cap case that proceeds.

### - [ ] T-13.5.2 — Opt-in exported-file content scanning has no integration or e2e test of the wired enforce path [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`contentPolicy.scanExportedFiles` ... routes each file enumerated by `delegate_task.fileExport` through the same `contentPolicy.interceptorRef` at the `PreExportMaterialization` phase ... before the file is persisted into the child's workspace. This covers the delegation-mediated file-injection vector (e.g., a compromised parent writing adversarial text into a runtime-recognized instruction file such as `CLAUDE.md` before exporting it)." (spec/13_security-model.md:685)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/policy/interceptor/export_test.go` and `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/delegation/export/export_test.go` (`TestMaterializeScanRejectFailsClosed_spec_8_7`, `TestMaterializeScanModifyPersistsRewritten_spec_8_7`, `TestMaterializeScanEnabledWithoutChainFailsClosed_spec_8_7`) cover the scan logic with a fake interceptor and a fake sink. `tests/tier2_component/stores/delegationpolicystore_test.go` covers the policy-storage validation that `scanExportedFiles` requires an `interceptorRef`. No integration, e2e, or security-tier test exports a real file with adversarial content (for example a `CLAUDE.md`) through the running gateway under `scanExportedFiles: true` and asserts the file is rejected before it reaches the child workspace.
- **Gap:** The delegation-mediated file-injection vector named in the spec is the security-relevant path and is verified only in isolated package tests with fakes. The full enforce path (parent export, PreExportMaterialization scan, rejection, no persistence into the child) is unverified end to end. The work covers both an adversarial scenario (a compromised parent exporting an adversarial instruction file) and a real deployer journey (acme enabling `scanExportedFiles` with a classifier). Target tier4 for the wired path and tier9 for the adversarial framing.
- **Dependencies:** Requires an external `RequestInterceptor` classifier stub. `tests/testinfra/stubs` has `kms`, `llmprovider`, `oidc`, `runtime`, and `siem` but no interceptor/classifier stub; building one is part of this finding. The `external_test.go` bufconn fake interceptor in `pkg/gateway/policy/interceptor` is a starting point.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/export_scan_enforce_test.go` and a `tests/testinfra/stubs/interceptor` gRPC stub that rejects any payload matching an injection signature; delegate a `fileExport` carrying a `CLAUDE.md` with adversarial text, assert `EXPORT_FILE_SCAN_REJECTED` and that the child workspace never receives the file.

### - [ ] T-13.5.3 — No adversarial prompt-injection scenario in the tier9 security suite [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Delegation chains introduce a prompt injection attack surface: a compromised or manipulated parent agent can craft adversarial `TaskSpec.input` payloads — or adversarial **exported workspace files** — targeting child agents. Lenny provides layered mitigations." (spec/13_security-model.md:680)
- **Existing tests:** "no test found." Searched `tests/tier9_security/` (all `*_test.go`), `tests/tier8_chaos/`, `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/`, and `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/`. The only matches for prompt injection are prose in `tests/tier9_security/reviews/full-system-review.md` (Finding 9), which records the advisory framing as a documented design acceptance and asserts no end-to-end verification. The tier9 suite contains `elicitation_tamper_test.go`, `ssrf_test.go`, `credential_leakage_test.go`, and (new since the last audit) `injection_gate_failclosed_test.go`, but that last file exercises the unrelated §5.1 secret-injection fail-closed gate, not delegation content security; nothing in the suite drives a hostile parent against a child through the delegation content path.
- **Gap:** §13.5 is a security control surface whose adversary (a compromised parent) is explicit, yet no security-tier test plays that adversary against the layered mitigations end to end. This is the missing adversarial journey: a compromised parent (bob) crafts an over-cap input and an adversarial exported file targeting a child (carol), and the gateway blocks both under a configured classifier while admitting benign content. Target tier9, with the enforce path reused from T-13.5.2.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the interceptor/classifier stub from T-13.5.2 and the tier9 live-session harness (`tests/tier9_security/live_session_test.go` pattern, `tests/testinfra/security`). The classifier stub does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier9_security/delegation_injection_test.go` registering a signature-matching classifier at `PreDelegation` and `PreExportMaterialization`, then assert that an adversarial `TaskSpec.input` and an adversarial `CLAUDE.md` export are both rejected while a benign delegation from the same parent proceeds.

### - [ ] T-13.5.4 — Content-policy error envelopes are not pinned across REST and MCP at contract tier [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "the MCP shim surfaces the evaluator's canonical INPUT_TOO_LARGE code (not the generic INTERCEPTOR_REJECTED) so REST and MCP envelopes share the same (category, retryable) pair" (pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/delegate_max_input_size_test.go:14-18, asserting the §8.3/§15.1/§15.2.1 cross-surface requirement); export codes `EXPORT_FILE_SCAN_REJECTED`, `EXPORT_FILE_SCAN_SIZE_EXCEEDED`, and `EXPORT_FILE_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE` are defined in `pkg/gateway/policy/interceptor/export.go:27-44`.
- **Existing tests:** The canonical-code assertion lives only in the in-process MCP shim unit test. `tests/tier3_contract/rest_mcp_consistency/` has grown since the last audit (`message_input_union_test.go`, `error_matrix_test.go`, `inbox_unavailable_test.go`, `lifecycle_pagination_test.go`, `scaffolds_test.go`), but none of the new files touch delegation content-policy codes — they pin §15.4 message-input union parity, the §15.2.1 adapter error-matrix lockstep, inbox-unavailable receipts, and lifecycle/pagination parity. Searching `tests/tier3_contract/` for `INPUT_TOO_LARGE`, `EXPORT_FILE_SCAN_REJECTED`, `EXPORT_FILE_SCAN_SIZE_EXCEEDED`, and `EXPORT_FILE_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE` still returns no matches. The §15.1 error reference for these codes is not pinned in a wire-format contract test.
- **Gap:** §13.5 mechanism 3 states the same content policy applies across the delegation and message paths, and the implementation comment asserts REST and MCP must carry the same `(category, retryable)` pair. No contract test pins the on-the-wire envelope for these codes across both surfaces, so a divergence between the REST and MCP error mapping (for example an HTTP status or `retryable` drift on `EXPORT_FILE_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE`, which the spec maps to TRANSIENT/503) could ship undetected. This is a standards-conformance and cross-surface contract gap. Target tier3.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. Uses `tests/tier3_contract/rest_mcp_consistency` and the existing REST/MCP contract harnesses.
- **Suggested test:** Add cases to `tests/tier3_contract/rest_mcp_consistency/` that trigger `INPUT_TOO_LARGE`, `EXPORT_FILE_SCAN_REJECTED`, `EXPORT_FILE_SCAN_SIZE_EXCEEDED`, and `EXPORT_FILE_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE`, and assert the error code, HTTP status, category, and retryable flag match between the REST envelope and the MCP `lenny/error` block.

### - [ ] T-13.5.5 — The external `RequestInterceptor` gRPC SPI is not pinned against its published proto at contract or conformance tier [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`contentPolicy.interceptorRef` invokes a `RequestInterceptor` at the `PreDelegation` phase ... Deployers wire in external classifiers (prompt injection detectors, content safety APIs) here." (spec/13_security-model.md:683)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/policy/interceptor/external_test.go` exercises the gRPC client over an in-memory bufconn fake (`TestExternalAllowThroughGRPC`, `TestExternalRejectThroughGRPC`, `TestExternalModifyRewritesPayload`, `TestExternalFailClosedRejectsOnTransportError`, `TestExternalTimeoutFailClosed`). Searching `tests/tier3_contract/` and `tests/tier10_conformance/` for `lenny-interceptor`, `RequestInterceptor`, and `InterceptorService` returns no matches.
- **Gap:** The `RequestInterceptor` SPI is the documented integration point for deployer-supplied classifiers and is a public protocol surface (`pkg/proto/interceptor/v1`). It is verified only against an in-package fake server, so the request payload shape, the MODIFY immutability contract, and the action enum are never pinned against the published proto in a way an external implementer can rely on. This is a standards/SPI conformance gap. Target tier3 contract or tier10 conformance.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The proto is in `pkg/proto/interceptor/v1`; the bufconn fake from `external_test.go` can be promoted into `tests/testinfra/stubs/interceptor`.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/interceptor_spi/` that serves a reference `RequestInterceptor` implementation against the generated proto, drives PreDelegation, PreMessageDelivery, and PreExportMaterialization requests, and asserts the wire payload fields and the immutable-field rejection match the published schema.

### - [ ] T-13.5.6 — Fail-open behavior of the content interceptor under classifier outage is not exercised as a chaos scenario [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Under fail-open the same timeout/error conditions admit the file and emit delegation.export_scan_failed_open instead" and the parallel `CodeExportFileScanUnavailable` TRANSIENT/503 fail-closed branch (pkg/gateway/policy/interceptor/export.go:38-44); §13.5 mechanism 4 routes exported files through the interceptor, whose FailPolicy governs the outage response.
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/policy/interceptor/failopenskip_test.go` and `pkg/gateway/policy/policy/exportscanobserver_test.go` cover the fail-open admit-and-emit logic at the package level; `pkg/gateway/policy/interceptor/external_test.go` covers fail-closed-on-transport-error and timeout-fail-closed against a bufconn. The tier8 chaos suite (`component_failure_test.go`, `store_failure_test.go`, and the others) has no scenario that kills a configured classifier mid-delegation. Searching `tests/tier8_chaos/` for interceptor and fail-open returns no matches.
- **Gap:** The behavior under a failing dependency (the deployer's classifier becoming unreachable) determines whether delegations and file exports are admitted or rejected, and is verified only in package unit tests with synthetic transport errors. No chaos test drives a real interceptor stub, kills it during a delegation, and asserts the fail-closed branch returns `EXPORT_FILE_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE` (503) while the fail-open branch admits and emits `delegation.export_scan_failed_open`. This is a failure-path and resilience gap. Target tier8.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the interceptor/classifier stub (shared with T-13.5.2 and T-13.5.5) made killable, plus the tier8 fault-injection harness in `tests/testinfra/chaos`. The stub does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier8_chaos/interceptor_outage_test.go` that registers a killable classifier, issues a delegation with a file export, terminates the classifier, and asserts the fail-closed FailPolicy yields the TRANSIENT 503 envelope while a fail-open policy admits and records the failed-open audit and metric.

### - [ ] T-13.5.7 — The maxInboundPerMinute multi-sibling flooding defense is not exercised as a multi-sender adversarial scenario [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The `maxInboundPerMinute` aggregate limit caps total inbound messages to any single session regardless of the number of senders, preventing N compromised siblings from flooding a target at N × the per-sender rate." (spec/13_security-model.md:686)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/messaging_internal_test.go` (`TestMessagingLimiterInboundExceeded`) verifies the aggregate cap counts across senders at the limiter unit level, and `messaging_handler_test.go` (`TestSendMessageRateLimitedReceipt_spec_7_2_371`) verifies a single-sender `RATE_LIMITED` receipt through the MCP handler. No integration or security test drives multiple distinct sibling sessions concurrently against one target to confirm the aggregate cap holds across senders through the running gateway.
- **Gap:** The spec frames `maxInboundPerMinute` as the defense against N compromised siblings, which is a multi-sender adversarial property. It is verified only by a single-process limiter test that increments a counter; the concurrent multi-sender behavior through the gateway and store is unverified. This is an adversarial and deployment-combination gap (the limiter must hold under concurrent senders, including the concurrent execution mode where siblings share a pod). Target tier4 or tier9.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. Uses `tests/testinfra/gateway`, `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`, and the `mcpClient` helper from the tier4 package.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/messaging_inbound_flood_test.go` that creates several sibling sessions under `siblings` scope and a low `maxInboundPerMinute`, sends from all siblings concurrently to one target, and asserts the target's accepted-inbound count never exceeds the aggregate cap and that excess sends return `RATE_LIMITED`.

### - [ ] T-13.5.8 — spec-map.json §13.5 names a nonexistent package and no concrete tier2+ test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** spec-map.json §13.5 lists `"packages": ["pkg/delegation/security"]` and four package globs under `"tests"` (`pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/delegationpolicystore/...`, `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/...`, `pkg/delegation/lease/...`, `pkg/gateway/policy/interceptor/...`), with `"blocked_until_phase": "10"` (tests/spec-map.json:1864-1877). The proposal-0020 package regroup rewrote the four glob paths to their post-move locations, but left the dangling `packages` entry untouched.
- **Existing tests:** The package `pkg/delegation/security` does not exist on disk; `find pkg -type d -path "*delegation*security*"` returns nothing, and `pkg/delegation` contains only `tracing`, `recovery`, `cycle`, and `lease`. The four glob entries point at directories that exist but name no specific test function, so the map does not assert any concrete §13.5 behavior. `tests/spec-map-exceptions.yaml` has no entry for §13.5. The tier0 spec-map validator (`cmd/lenny-test/cmd_validate.go`) checks that glob paths resolve on disk but has no check on the `packages` field, so the dangling `pkg/delegation/security` entry passes validation silently.
- **Gap:** The coverage map references a package that was never created and lists only directory globs for a security-critical subsection, so a dashboard query for §13.5 reports coverage that cannot be traced to a named test, and the dangling package reference would not catch a regression. This is a spec-versus-map inconsistency. The fix is to remove the nonexistent `pkg/delegation/security` entry and list the concrete tier2+ tests once they exist (T-13.5.1 through T-13.5.3).
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. Edit `tests/spec-map.json` and confirm against the tier0 spec-map validator.
- **Suggested test:** Extend the tier0 spec-map consistency check (`tests/tier0_static`) to fail when a `packages` entry names a directory absent from disk, and update the §13.5 entry to cite concrete test functions rather than directory globs.

### - [ ] T-13.5.9 — The PreMessageDelivery content scan is verified only with a fake chain, never through the wired gateway [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`contentPolicy.maxInputSize` and `contentPolicy.interceptorRef` apply to `lenny/send_message` payloads via the `PreMessageDelivery` interceptor phase ... providing the same content policy enforcement as delegation inputs." (spec/13_security-model.md:684)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/mcptools_test.go` (`TestSendMessageRejectedByInterceptor`, lines 507-525) registers a fake interceptor at `PhasePreMessageDelivery` and asserts a REJECT becomes a tool error, and `pkg/gateway/policy/interceptor/interceptor_test.go:235` (`TestPhaseChainsAreIndependent`) confirms phase isolation. Since the last audit, `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/content_policy_scoped_test.go` (landed with the F-13.5.2 per-policy `interceptorRef` change) added finer-grained fake-chain coverage of the same phase: `TestSendMessage_maxInputSize_spec_4_8_1040`, `TestSendMessage_runsOnlyNamedScanner_spec_8_3_157`, `TestSendMessage_nullRef_runsNoScanner_spec_8_3_157`, and `TestSendMessage_unresolvableRef_failsClosed_spec_4_8_1032`. The wiring lives in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/mcptools_register.go:395-467` (relocated there from `mcptools.go` by the proposal-0020 package regroup). No integration test drives `lenny/send_message` through the running gateway with a configured message-scanning interceptor.
- **Gap:** The inter-session message-scanning path — including the newer per-policy scoped-scanner selection — is verified at the package level with fake chains but not through the wired binary against a real store, so the production path that mechanism 3 promises is unexercised at integration tier. This is a happy-path-plus-rejection integration gap that overlaps the harness built for T-13.5.1. Target tier4.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. Reuses the gateway harness and the classifier stub once T-13.5.2 builds it; a built-in rejecting interceptor is sufficient otherwise.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `tests/tier4_integration/delegation_content_policy_test.go` with a `lenny/send_message` case under a configured `PreMessageDelivery` interceptor that rejects a flagged body and admits a benign one, asserting the delivery receipt status in each case.

### - [ ] T-13.5.10 — The residual-risk runtime-layer hardening (ignoreInstructionFiles allowlist) is referenced by the spec but absent from code and tests [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Deployers who leave `scanExportedFiles: false` are responsible for treating all workspace files received via delegation as untrusted input and for applying runtime-layer hardening (e.g., a runtime `ignoreInstructionFiles` allowlist)." (spec/13_security-model.md:692)
- **Existing tests:** "no test found." Searching `pkg/`, `cmd/`, and `tests/` for `ignoreInstructionFiles` and `IgnoreInstructionFiles` returns no matches, and no runtime adapter test exercises ignoring an exported instruction file.
- **Gap:** The spec names a runtime-layer mitigation as the deployer's responsibility when export scanning is off, but no runtime adapter implements or tests an `ignoreInstructionFiles` allowlist, so the documented residual-risk control is unverified. If this is a forward-looking deployer guidance rather than a platform feature, that should be confirmed; if any reference runtime is expected to honor it, the conformance suite should pin it. Target tier10 conformance, or reclassify as deployer guidance.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a runtime adapter that recognizes the allowlist and the tier10 conformance harness (`cmd/lenny-compliance`). The feature does not exist yet; confirming intent is the first step of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** If the control is in scope, add a tier10 conformance case asserting a runtime configured with `ignoreInstructionFiles` does not load a delegation-exported `CLAUDE.md`; otherwise record the spec language as deployer guidance with no platform test obligation.

### - [ ] T-13.5.11 — Content-security controls are unexercised across execution modes, isolation backends, and client protocols [Info] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** The §13.5 mitigations apply to every delegation regardless of execution mode (session, task, concurrent), isolation backend (runc, gVisor, Kata, Confidential Containers), and client protocol (REST, MCP, OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Open Responses). (spec/13_security-model.md:678-692)
- **Existing tests:** The existing package tests run a single in-process configuration. There is no matrix coverage of the content-security phases across execution modes or client protocols, and no e2e run under gVisor or on a cloud provider.
- **Gap:** Once the integration and e2e tests from T-13.5.1 through T-13.5.3 exist, the content-security controls should be exercised in more than one deployment combination, in particular the concurrent execution mode (siblings sharing a pod, relevant to the inbound-flood defense) and at least one cloud provider for the export-scan enforce path. This is a deployment-combination observation rather than a standalone missing test, recorded so the matrix is not forgotten when the higher-tier tests land.
- **Dependencies:** Requires `tests/testinfra/matrix` for the combination sweep and `tests/testinfra/kind`/`tests/testinfra/cloud` for the e2e legs; depends on T-13.5.1, T-13.5.2, and T-13.5.7 landing first.
- **Suggested test:** After the base tests exist, add a `tests/testinfra/matrix` dimension covering execution mode and client protocol for the maxInputSize and PreMessageDelivery cases, and run the export-scan enforce path on one cloud provider under tier6.

## §14 Workspace Plan Schema <a id="t-14"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/14_workspace-plan-schema.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The §14 schema validation surface has strong unit and component coverage at the parser (`pkg/workspaceplan`), the materializer (`pkg/adapter/workspace`), and the gateway ingress (`pkg/gateway/sessionserver`) layers, plus a tier0 JSON Schema test that validates the published `workspaceplan-v1.json` against canonical examples and a tier3 wire-contract suite. The gateway-ingress tests for gitClone ref-resolution, gitClone auth-host binding, the env blocklist, runtimeOptions validation, and callback SSRF validation are thorough but all run against stub resolvers, in-memory stores, and httptest servers. The gaps are concentrated above the component tier: the gitClone clone-and-materialize flow, the webhook callback delivery, the per-slot concurrent-workspace materialization, and the §14.1 schema-version rollback rejection are never exercised through real backing services, a Kind or cloud cluster, or a chaos drill, and two documented contracts (the built-in runtimeOptions published-schema URLs and the §14 session-terminal CloudEvents event types) have no conformance test pinning them against their external schema. TESTING.md §14.2 declares a `tests/tier2_component/workspace_plan/` suite that does not exist on disk. Counts: 3 High, 6 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-14.2 — Declared tier2 component suite `tests/tier2_component/workspace_plan/` does not exist [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`tests/tier2_component/workspace_plan/` and `tests/tier3_contract/workspaceplan/` together cover the workspace plan schema. Every source type (`inlineFile`, `uploadFile`, `uploadArchive`, `mkdir`, `gitClone`) has positive and adversarial cases" (TESTING.md:1848)
- **Existing tests:** The tier3 contract directory `tests/tier3_contract/workspaceplan/sources_test.go` exists and is populated. The companion `tests/tier2_component/workspace_plan/` directory is absent; `ls tests/tier2_component/` lists auditintegrity, auditstore, breakers, controllers, coordination, gateway_subsystems, healthchecks, leases, migrations, observability, opsaudit, preflight, quota, ratelimit, rls, securitycaches, storagequota, stores, and translators, with no workspace_plan entry. The materializer coverage that the component tier would own lives in `pkg/adapter/workspace/*_test.go` as plain in-package unit tests with no build tag and no real backing services.
- **Gap:** TESTING.md declares a tier2 component suite that is not implemented. The component tier is the level at which a real workspace tree is materialized against a real staging directory and a real blob store, where the unit tests use temp dirs and in-memory archives. This is a spec-versus-test inconsistency: the testing plan claims a suite that does not exist, so a reviewer reading TESTING.md would believe `gitClone` and `uploadArchive` materialization are covered at tier2 when they are not.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier2 component harness with a real MinIO blob store (tests/testinfra/compose or tests/testinfra/stubs) and a git-server stub (does not exist yet under tests/testinfra/stubs; building it is part of this finding).
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier2_component/workspace_plan/materialize_test.go` that materializes a plan containing each source type against a real staging directory and a MinIO-backed blob store, asserting on-disk file modes, the strip-components skip warnings, and the path-collision last-writer-wins outcome, referencing tests/testinfra/compose for MinIO.

### - [ ] T-14.3 — gitClone clone-and-materialize flow has no integration or e2e test against a real git server [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Clone a Git repository into the workspace at materialization time. The gateway performs the clone using its network path, not the pod's, so the runtime never sees raw credentials." (spec/14_workspace-plan-schema.md:91) and "the gateway then performs the clone with a short-lived HTTPS bearer/basic token scoped to the repository, and the `git` client inside the pod uses an in-pod HTTPS credential helper that calls the gateway's token endpoint" (spec/14_workspace-plan-schema.md:95)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/adapter/workspace/gitclone_test.go` materializes a gzip-tar archive that a helper fabricates in place of a real clone (`TestMaterializeGitClone`, `TestMaterializeGitCloneMissingArchive`, `TestGitCloneStagingRef`). `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/gitclone_pin_test.go` drives the ref-resolution and auth-host binding through httptest with a `pinStubResolver` and a `stubVCSCreds`. `pkg/workspaceplan/refresolve_test.go` tests the resolver against a stub. No test under tests/tier4_integration, tests/tier5_e2e_kind, or tests/tier6_e2e_cloud references gitClone, resolvedCommitSha, or ls-remote; a grep across those three directories returns nothing.
- **Gap:** The end-to-end gitClone journey is never exercised. The credential-lease-to-clone path (the gateway obtaining a short-lived token from §4.9, cloning over its own network path, and the in-pod HTTPS credential helper resolving subsequent operations against the gateway token endpoint) is a core capability with a security boundary (the runtime never sees raw credentials) and has no integration or e2e coverage. This is a real user journey (alice creates a session that clones a private repository) and the security-relevant credential-isolation claim is unverified.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a git-server stub or fixture serving HTTPS clone over the gateway network path (no such stub exists under tests/testinfra/stubs today; building it is part of this finding), the tier4 compose stack with the §4.9 credential-leasing service wired, and for the e2e variant the tier5 Kind harness (tests/testinfra/kind).
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/gitclone_materialize_test.go` that registers a github-shaped VCS credential pool, creates a session whose plan clones a private repo from a git-server stub, and asserts the workspace contains the repo contents at the pinned `resolvedCommitSha` while the pod never received the raw token, referencing tests/testinfra/stubs for the git server and tests/testinfra/compose for the credential service.

### - [ ] T-14.108 — Webhook callback delivery has no integration or e2e test and no security-tier SSRF delivery test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Gateway POSTs a CloudEvents v1.0.2 envelope with session-terminal event data when the session reaches a terminal state" (spec/14_workspace-plan-schema.md:108) and the SSRF mitigations "The callback `http.Client` uses a custom `DialContext` that connects directly to the pinned IP at the TCP level ... This prevents DNS rebinding attacks" (spec/14_workspace-plan-schema.md:110)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/sessioncallback/delivery_test.go` covers the retry schedule, fresh-signature-per-attempt, pinned-client dial, and redirect refusal with an httptest target. `pkg/gateway/sessioncallback/validate_test.go` covers HTTPS-only, private-IP rejection, metadata blocklist, and the domain allowlist. `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/callback_test.go::TestTerminalCallbackDelivered_spec_14_108` drives a terminal delivery through httptest+memstore. No test under tests/tier4_integration, tests/tier5_e2e_kind, or tests/tier6_e2e_cloud delivers a callback end to end (a grep for callbackUrl, OnSessionTerminal, or session_completed across those directories returns nothing), and the tier9 `tests/tier9_security/ssrf_test.go` is scoped to the §9.3 connector registry HTTPS check, not the §14 callbackUrl path.
- **Gap:** The webhook delivery path is verified only at the unit level. The DNS-rebinding defense, the RFC 1918 / RFC 6598 rejection, and the cloud-metadata-hostname blocklist are SSRF security controls that §14 calls out explicitly, and they are never verified through the running gateway against an adversarial target. This is both a real user journey (a CI system at acme receives the terminal CloudEvents webhook with a valid HMAC) and an adversarial scenario (a client supplies a callbackUrl that re-resolves to an internal IP); both are absent above the unit tier.
- **Dependencies:** For the integration variant, none beyond the tier4 compose stack plus an HTTP receiver stub. For the security variant, the tier9 Kind harness (tests/testinfra/kind) plus an internal target to attempt the rebind. Buildable today for tier4.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/webhook_delivery_test.go` that creates a session with a callbackUrl and callbackSecret, drives it to a terminal state, and asserts the receiver got a CloudEvents envelope with a valid `X-Lenny-Signature` and the documented `data` body; add `tests/tier9_security/callback_ssrf_test.go` that submits a callbackUrl whose hostname re-resolves to a pod-network IP after registration and asserts the dispatcher refuses to connect, referencing tests/testinfra/security and tests/testinfra/kind.

### - [ ] T-14.1.326 — §14.1 schema-version rollback rejection (older gateway reads newer plan) has no integration or chaos test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "If the gateway encounters a `schemaVersion` higher than it understands (e.g., a plan written by a newer gateway version is read by an older one during a rollback), it MUST NOT proceed with workspace materialization — instead it MUST reject the operation with error code `WORKSPACE_PLAN_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED` (HTTP 422), including `details.knownVersion` and `details.encounteredVersion`." (spec/14_workspace-plan-schema.md:326)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/adapter/workspace/schemaversion_test.go::TestCheckSchemaVersion_spec_14_1_326` covers the version comparison at unit level. `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/create_test.go::TestCreateRejectsUnsupportedSchemaVersion_spec_14_1_326` and `tests/tier3_contract/workspaceplan/sources_test.go::TestParserRejectsUnsupportedSchemaVersion` cover the rejection at session-creation ingress. No test exercises the reconciliation read-back path where a downgraded gateway resumes or retries a session whose stored plan carries a higher schemaVersion. A grep for WORKSPACE_PLAN_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED, knownVersion, or encounteredVersion across tests/tier8_chaos returns nothing.
- **Gap:** The spec frames this as a rollback scenario (a newer gateway writes the plan, an older gateway reads it during a deployment rollback while replaying setup for a resumed or retried session). That live-consumer read-back path is distinct from the create-time ingress check and is never exercised through the gateway reconciliation loop. This is a failure-path and deployment-combination gap (rolling downgrade) and is the appropriate subject of a chaos or integration test.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier4 compose stack with a Postgres-backed session store seeded with a plan at a higher schemaVersion, or the tier8 chaos harness to model a replica downgrade. Buildable today against the compose stack.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/schemaversion_rollback_test.go` that persists a session whose stored WorkspacePlan carries `schemaVersion` above the gateway's known maximum, triggers a resume or retry that replays workspace setup, and asserts the gateway returns 422 WORKSPACE_PLAN_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED with both detail fields, referencing tests/testinfra/gateway and tests/testinfra/clockstep.

### - [ ] T-14.139 — callbackSecret KMS-envelope encryption at rest and write-only API behavior has no component test against real Postgres and KMS [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The secret is stored in the `sessions` table as KMS-envelope-encrypted ciphertext using the same KMS backend as credential pool secrets ... The `lenny_app` database role can `SELECT` the ciphertext column, but only the gateway process with KMS `Decrypt` permission can recover the plaintext. The plaintext is never returned by any API endpoint — `callbackSecret` is a write-only field." (spec/14_workspace-plan-schema.md:139)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/sessionstore/pgstore/envelope_test.go::TestRequestEnvelopeCallbackRoundTrip_spec_14_108` is a plain in-package unit test that round-trips a bundle carrying an already-sealed `CallbackSecret` byte slice through the JSONB serialization helpers; it does not encrypt or decrypt and does not touch a real database. `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/callback_test.go::TestTerminalCallbackDelivered_spec_14_108` asserts the secret column is cleared after delivery via memstore. No tier2 component test under tests/tier2_component/stores exercises the KMS-envelope ciphertext column against a real Postgres and a KMS provider, and no test asserts the plaintext is absent from any API response.
- **Gap:** The encryption-at-rest claim for T3-classified data is verified only at serialization-helper level. The component tier should confirm that the stored column holds ciphertext (not the plaintext secret), that recovery requires the KMS Decrypt path, and that no read endpoint surfaces the plaintext. This is a security control with no component-or-higher verification.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier2 component store harness with a real Postgres (tests/testinfra/envtest or tests/testinfra/compose) and the KMS stub (tests/testinfra/stubs/kms, which exists). Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier2_component/stores/sessionstore_callback_secret_test.go` that creates a session with a callbackSecret against real Postgres and the KMS stub, SELECTs the raw ciphertext column to confirm it does not equal the plaintext, recovers it through the KMS Decrypt path, and asserts GET /v1/sessions/{id} never echoes the plaintext, referencing tests/testinfra/stubs/kms and tests/testinfra/envtest.

### - [ ] T-14.137 — §14 session-terminal CloudEvents event types and per-event data schemas have no conformance test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`type` is `dev.lenny.<short_name>` where `<short_name>` matches the event-type catalog in §16.6" with the per-event data schemas for `session_completed`, `session_failed`, `session_terminated`, `session_cancelled`, `session_expired`, `session_awaiting_action`, and `delegation_completed` (spec/14_workspace-plan-schema.md:137-148)
- **Existing tests:** The tier3 CloudEvents contract suite `tests/tier3_contract/cloudevents/cloudevents_test.go` asserts the envelope shape for `delegation_tree_completed`, `session_state_changed`, and `operation_progressed` only. The §14 webhook-specific terminal event types are referenced in unit tests (`pkg/gateway/sessionserver/callback_test.go`, `pkg/gateway/sessioncallback/delivery_test.go`) but only the `type` string is checked; no test pins the per-event `data` body (for example `session_failed` carrying `error.code`, `delegation_completed` carrying `parent_session_id` and `childSessionId`) against a CloudEvents schema.
- **Gap:** §14 delivers webhook payloads over an external standard (CloudEvents v1.0.2) and defines a distinct `data` schema per terminal event type. No conformance test pins these event types or their `data` schemas against the CloudEvents envelope, so a regression that drops a required `data` field or renames an event type would not be caught at the contract tier. The absence of a standards-conformance check on a wire surface is a finding.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a CloudEvents validator and per-event-type `data` schemas under schemas/ (the lifecycle-events schema exists; per-terminal-event data schemas may need to be added). Buildable today using tests/testinfra/golden for the per-event fixtures.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `tests/tier3_contract/cloudevents/cloudevents_test.go` (or add `webhook_events_test.go` alongside it) to generate one of each §14 terminal event type, validate the envelope against the CloudEvents v1.0.2 schema, and assert each `data` body matches the documented per-event field set, referencing tests/testinfra/golden.

### - [ ] T-14.300 — Built-in runtimeOptions published-schema URLs have no artifact on disk and no conformance test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "All built-in runtime schemas above are published at `https://schemas.lenny.dev/runtime-options/<runtime-name>/v1.json` ... Reference runtimes in §26 declare their `runtimeOptionsSchema` field as a `$ref` to these URLs rather than inlining the schema body, so the canonical schema lives in one place." (spec/14_workspace-plan-schema.md:300)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier0_static/schemas_test.go::TestPhase1SchemasParse` validates `schemas/workspaceplan-v1.json` but no runtime-options schema. There is no `schemas/runtime-options/` directory on disk (an `ls` returns no such directory). `pkg/gateway/admin/runtimes_test.go` covers the derived-runtime property-subset rule (`INVALID_DERIVED_RUNTIME`) and `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/envelope_test.go` covers `RUNTIME_OPTIONS_INVALID` and the `RuntimeOptionsUnschematized` warning, but neither validates the published built-in schemas or the §26 `$ref` indirection.
- **Gap:** §14 commits to a published JSON Schema per built-in runtime at a stable URL, and §26 reference runtimes are documented to `$ref` those URLs. The schema artifacts do not exist under schemas/, and no tier0 or tier3 test parses them, validates a sample runtimeOptions document against each, or confirms the §26 `$ref` resolves. This is a published-contract surface with neither an artifact nor a conformance test, in contrast to the workspace-plan schema which has both. A drift between the inline §14 schema body and any published artifact would ship undetected.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the runtime-options schema artifacts to be committed under schemas/runtime-options/ (do not exist yet; producing them is part of this finding) and the schematest helper (tests/testinfra/schematest, which exists). Buildable today once the artifacts exist.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier0_static/runtime_options_schemas_test.go` that compiles each `schemas/runtime-options/<name>/v1.json`, validates the documented example options for each built-in runtime against its schema, and asserts that every §26 reference-runtime `runtimeOptionsSchema` `$ref` resolves to a committed artifact, referencing tests/testinfra/schematest.

(spec/14_workspace-plan-schema.md:5)

That tier5 test does not exist: a find for `concurrent_modes` under tests returns nothing. `tests/tier12_load_cloud/concurrent_workspace_test.go::TestCloudConcurrentWorkspaceSlotClaim` stresses slot-claim throughput but does not assert per-slot workspace materialization content.

The tier4 test covers admission only, the referenced tier5 test is absent, and the tier12 test measures throughput rather than per-slot content. This is a deployment-combination gap (concurrent execution mode with concurrencyStyle workspace) for a core materialization behavior.

- **Spec/Doc:** "At minimum, the gateway's `NetworkPolicy` `except` clauses on the external HTTPS egress rule (Section 13.2) block callback traffic from reaching cluster-internal CIDRs (pod network, service network, node metadata endpoints)." (spec/14_workspace-plan-schema.md:111)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/sessioncallback/validate_test.go` and `delivery_test.go` cover the application-layer IP pinning and rejection at unit level. `tests/tier9_security/network_policy_test.go` exists for the §13.2 NetworkPolicy posture. No test connects the §14 callback worker egress path to the §13.2 NetworkPolicy `except` clauses, that is, no test confirms that even if the application-layer validator were bypassed, the NetworkPolicy still blocks callback egress to pod-network, service-network, and metadata CIDRs.

That network-layer boundary specific to callback traffic is not verified end to end on a cluster. (spec/14_workspace-plan-schema.md:100)

These are all unit-level tests.

A component test that extracts a real tar.gz and zip with leading path segments to be stripped, in the materializer against a real staging directory, would confirm the format-independent behavior the spec promises for all three formats. ### - [ ] T-14.105 — env blocklist is a security control with no security-tier or integration-tier enforcement test [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The platform ships a default blocklist that operators can extend but not reduce in multi-tenant mode." and "any env var whose name matches any entry (exact or glob) is rejected with `400 ENV_VAR_BLOCKLISTED`" (spec/14_workspace-plan-schema.md:105)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/envblock/envblock_test.go` covers the matcher (exact, glob, case-sensitivity, deployer-extension-cannot-reduce) at unit level. `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/envelope_test.go` covers the gateway returning `ENV_VAR_BLOCKLISTED` for a blocked env var through httptest. No security-tier test confirms that the default blocklist cannot be reduced in multi-tenant mode through the running gateway, and no integration test confirms a blocklisted secret-bearing env var (for example `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`) is rejected end to end before it reaches a pod.
- **Gap:** The env blocklist prevents secret-bearing variables from being injected into a session, which §14 frames as a multi-tenant security guarantee (operators cannot reduce the default blocklist). The cannot-reduce guarantee under multi-tenant mode is verified only at the matcher unit level, not through the gateway against a tenant attempting to reduce it. This is a low-risk negative-path gap because the matcher unit test is strong, but the multi-tenant policy enforcement is unverified above the unit tier.
- **Dependencies:** None beyond the tier4 compose stack or the tier9 substrate. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier9_security/env_blocklist_test.go` that, in multi-tenant mode, attempts to register a tenant policy that removes a default-blocklist entry and asserts the reduction is refused, then creates a session with a blocklisted env var and asserts 400 ENV_VAR_BLOCKLISTED, referencing tests/testinfra/security and tests/testinfra/gateway.

### - [ ] T-14.1.328 — Durable-consumer (audit/analytics) forward-read of unknown WorkspacePlan.schemaVersion coverage is observational [Info] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Audit pipelines, compliance exporters, and analytics queries that read session records containing embedded `WorkspacePlan` objects are durable consumers and MUST apply the forward-read rule from Section 15.5 item 7: process all fields they understand and preserve unknown fields verbatim. They MUST NOT reject session records solely because the embedded `WorkspacePlan.schemaVersion` is unrecognized." (spec/14_workspace-plan-schema.md:328)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/workspaceplan/plan_test.go` and `pkg/workspaceplan/refresolve_test.go::TestMarshalPreservesUnknownSourceType` confirm the parser preserves unknown source-type fields verbatim on round trip. The §15.5 forward-read rule itself is the subject of §15.5 coverage, and the §15.5 spec-map exception (tests/spec-map-exceptions.yaml:89) defers the schemaVersion mechanism's verification to §14. No test exercises an audit or analytics consumer reading a session record whose embedded plan carries an unrecognized schemaVersion and confirming the record is not rejected.
- **Gap:** This is an observation rather than a hard gap. The durable-consumer forward-read obligation is a §15.5 cross-cutting rule applied to §14 objects; the verbatim-preservation primitive is unit-tested in pkg/workspaceplan, but no audit-pipeline test reads a future-schemaVersion plan through the audit or analytics read path. Coverage of the §15.5 rule against a §14-embedded object would close the loop; this note records where that coverage would live so it is not assumed under §14.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier4 audit-pipeline harness (tests/tier4_integration/audit_pipeline_test.go exists) seeded with a session record whose embedded plan carries a future schemaVersion. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add a case to `tests/tier4_integration/audit_pipeline_test.go` that ingests a session record whose embedded WorkspacePlan carries an unrecognized schemaVersion and an unknown source type, and asserts the audit consumer processes the record and preserves both unknown fields verbatim rather than rejecting it, referencing tests/testinfra/audit.

## §15.1 REST API <a id="t-15.1"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/15_external-api-surface.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The §15.1 REST surface is large: session lifecycle, derive and replay, the user-credential endpoints, the comprehensive admin CRUD plane, the OpenAPI document and its MCP-extension CI contract, scoped-token enforcement, ETag optimistic concurrency, cursor pagination, dry-run, and a large error-code catalog. Since the 2026-06-03 baseline, the §4–17 layout refactor (0020 S12) moved the admin, OpenAPI, error-classifier, and pagination packages under `pkg/gateway/externalapi/`, and three of the original findings closed: the OpenAPI document is now reconciled against the live route mux by a dedicated completeness test (T-15.1.2, landed 2026-06-25), the gateway-side per-route `x-lenny-scope` enforcement landed with its own tier-9 regression (T-15.1.3, ADM-1, landed 2026-06-29), and the circuit-breaker `dryRun` simulation shape gained a dedicated unit suite (T-15.1.11, landed 2026-06-04). Substantial new unit-tier coverage also landed for cursor pagination (a shared `pkg/gateway/externalapi/pagination` package plus per-endpoint tests across sessions, logs, transcript, metering, pools, and the new `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events` endpoint) and for ETag optimistic concurrency (dedicated `_etag_test.go` files for nearly every admin resource type), though both remain below their originally targeted tier3/tier4 level, and `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/artifacts` still returns no `cursor`/`hasMore` envelope at all despite being one of the spec's named cursor-paginated endpoints. The assembled admin REST plane against real OIDC and Postgres, the real OIDC/PKCE/RFC 9068 admin auth path, the derive/replay tier4 happy path, the isolation-downgrade override and its audit event, and the pool-drain backpressure's integration/rate-limiting arm remain unverified above unit tier.

Counts: 4 High, 6 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-15.1.1 — Assembled admin REST plane has no component/integration test with real OIDC and role-ceiling middleware against Postgres [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "All operational configuration is API-managed." plus the admin endpoint table and "Runtime and pool records are platform-global ... Tenant-scoped visibility is enforced at the application layer via `runtime_tenant_access` and `pool_tenant_access` join tables. `platform-admin` callers receive unfiltered results; `tenant-admin` and `tenant-viewer` callers receive results filtered to the access-table entries for their tenant." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:758, 770)

- **Gap:** No component-or-higher gap for the error envelope or rate-limit headers per se; the catalog is centralized and unit-tested (including the error codes added since the baseline) and the wire envelope is sampled at tier3. This entry records that the large error-code catalog (the conditions under which each code is returned) is not individually exercised end to end, which is acceptable because each producing handler asserts its own code at unit tier. No new suite is required beyond the per-feature findings above (for example T-15.1.3 for `SCOPE_FORBIDDEN` and T-15.1.7 for `POOL_DRAINING`).
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** No standalone suite required; ensure each per-feature integration test added under the findings above asserts the specific error code and HTTP status from the catalog rather than only the status family.

## §15.2 MCP API <a id="t-15.2"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/15_external-api-surface.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
This unit was left unreconciled after the fan-out pass's transient failure; this pass reconciles it against commit range `d9074016..c3014435`. Since the 2026-06-03 baseline, the §4–17 layout refactor (0020 S12) moved this unit's packages from `pkg/gateway/mcp`, `pkg/gateway/mcptools`, and `pkg/gateway/adapterregistry` to `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp`, `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools`, and `pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterregistry` respectively, and `OutputPart` was renamed to `MessagePart` throughout (proposal 0018 S15); neither changes a requirement this unit tracks, only the citations below. Four findings closed on real landed work: the MCP Streamable-HTTP SSE transport — `attach_session`, `resumeFromSeq`/`Last-Event-ID` replay, `gap_detected`, and the 20s keepalive — is implemented and pinned at tier1 (T-15.2.1, T-15.2.2; commits `cbe7fce2`, `936710ae`), the per-kind wire projection this transport carries closes the outstanding unknown-notification well-formedness gap (T-15.2.12), and the §15.2.1 state-transition-sequence and pagination equivalence sub-contracts gained real REST/MCP parity tests (T-15.2.9; commit `70716b06`). The remaining findings are substantially unchanged in substance, though several gained partial coverage worth recording: the §15.2.1 consistency matrix still covers only the REST/MCP built-in pair, with translation-fidelity tests for the OpenAI Chat/Responses adapters but no behavioral-equivalence (error/retryable/state/pagination) coverage for either (T-15.2.3); new tests reuse the `RegisterAdapterUnderTest` name for that REST/MCP-only matrix, but the spec's pluggable third-party `RegisterAdapterUnderTest(ExternalProtocolAdapter)` entry point still does not exist (T-15.2.4); the production adapter-validate gate still runs the §15.4 runtime-binary battery rather than the §15.2.1 matrix, though the routing-exclusion half of the gate is now a machine-enforced `Status.Routable()` predicate (T-15.2.5); the MCP-transport coordinator-handoff reattach still falls back to a generic frame with no dedicated projection or test, even though the REST-side reattach machinery it depends on gained heavy coverage (T-15.2.6); no test pins MCP output against the published MCP 2025-03-26 schema (T-15.2.7); two-version negotiation itself landed, but the deprecation-window session-lifetime exception and the preflight drain gauge remain dormant (T-15.2.8; commit `1f613abd`); the declared contract suite still carries by-design no-op stand-ins and a stale TESTING.md path (T-15.2.10); and the client-facing tool catalog gained one new membership check (`attach_session`) but still has no completeness assertion against the full table (T-15.2.11).
Counts: 7 High, 4 Medium, 1 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [x] T-15.2.1 — MCP streaming transport (`attach_session`, SSE frames, per-kind wire projection) is unimplemented and untested [High] — RESOLVED cbe7fce2, 936710ae
- **Resolution:** Commit `cbe7fce2` (F-15.2.2) built the transport this finding named absent: `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/stream.go` upgrades a `tools/call` for the new `lenny/attach_session` tool sent with `Accept: text/event-stream` to a per-session SSE stream sourced from the §15.1 `sessionevents.Bus`, with `SeqNum` on the SSE `id:` line and an `Authorize` gate rejecting a missing/foreign session as `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`. Commit `936710ae` (F-15.2.13/F-15.2.14) then built the per-kind wire projection (`pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/projection.go`): a classifier lifts live bus event types onto the closed `SessionEventKind` enum and projects each to the table's named frame — `notifications/tasks/statusUpdate` for `state_change`, streaming content frames for `output`, `elicitation/create` for `elicitation` and the approval-required `tool_use` requested phase, `notifications/lenny/toolCall` for the remaining `tool_use` phases, `notifications/lenny/error` for `error`, and the MCP Tasks final-state frame for `terminated`. Tests: `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/stream_test.go` (backlog+live streaming, missing-sessionId, Authorize rejection, non-SSE fallthrough) and `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/projection_test.go` (one case per table row plus `TestEveryProjectedFrameIsValidJSONRPC_spec_15_2_1374`), plus `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/attach_session_test.go::TestAttachSessionInToolList_spec_15_2` (tool discoverable in `tools/list`). Commit `42b157e4` added the equivalent push over the playground WebSocket leg (F-27.4.7). Residual, not reopening this finding: the streaming path is implemented directly in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp` rather than through the `pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterregistry.MCPAdapter.OutboundChannel` abstraction the spec's Go snippet names (`MCPAdapter` still declares `OutboundCapabilities()` but does not override `OpenOutboundChannel`) — an architecture-consistency question for BUILD-GAPS, not a test-coverage gap, since the observable wire behavior is now implemented and tested. No tier4 (real gateway process) or tier5 (Kind) end-to-end test exists yet; `tests/tier4_integration/gateway_full_e2e_test.go` still only smoke-checks `initialize`.

### - [x] T-15.2.2 — Event-stream resume (`resumeFromSeq`, `gap_detected`, keepalive, `Last-Event-ID`) has no MCP-surface test [High] — RESOLVED cbe7fce2
- **Resolution:** Commit `cbe7fce2` built the resume contract this finding named untested, in the same transport as T-15.2.1. `resumeFromSeq` (with SSE `Last-Event-ID` as the implicit fallback) replays buffered events with `SeqNum` greater than the cursor before switching to live delivery; a `notifications/lenny/gapDetected` stream-control frame carrying `{lastSeenSeq, nextSeq}` (no `id:` line) precedes the backlog when the cursor sits below the buffer's oldest retained sequence; and a `:keepalive\n\n` SSE comment line is written after 20s of frame silence. Tests in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/stream_test.go`: `TestAttachStreamsBacklogThenLive_spec_15_2`, `TestAttachResumeFromSeqReplaysOnlyNewer_spec_15_2`, `TestAttachLastEventIDResume_spec_15_2`, `TestAttachGapDetected_spec_15_2`, `TestAttachKeepalive_spec_15_2`, `TestWriteMCPSessionEventCarriesSeqOnIDLine`, and `TestWriteMCPGapDetectedHasNoIDLine`; the WebSocket leg's equivalent (`TestWebSocketAttachGapDetected_spec_15_2`) landed with commit `42b157e4`. The buffer depth is the operator-tunable `gateway.sessionEventReplayBufferDepth` (default 512, range `[64,4096]`), already wired per F-10.4.5. No tier4/tier5 test drives this over a real gateway process or Kind yet — the same residual T-15.2.1 records.

### - [ ] T-15.2.3 — §15.2.1 consistency suite does not cover the OpenAI Completions or Open Responses adapters [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "CI includes contract tests that call the REST endpoint and **every built-in external adapter** (MCP, OpenAI Completions, Open Responses) for every overlapping operation and assert both structural and behavioral equivalence of responses." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:1397)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier3_contract/rest_mcp_consistency/` now has real REST/MCP behavioral-equivalence coverage (`error_matrix_test.go`, `lifecycle_pagination_test.go`, landed `70716b06`; see T-15.2.4/T-15.2.9), but nothing extends that matrix to the OpenAI adapters. `tests/tier3_contract/rest_openai_chat/scaffolds_test.go` and `tests/tier3_contract/rest_openai_responses/scaffolds_test.go` are no longer empty — they carry a real Translation Fidelity Matrix suite (`TestRESTOpenAIChatFidelityMatrix`, `TestRESTOpenAIChatDroppedFieldsContract`, `TestRESTOpenAIChatPreservedFieldsContract` and the Responses equivalents) asserting the §15 field-fidelity table — but this predates the 2026-06-03 baseline (commit `ba60f275`, an ancestor of it) and tests translation correctness, not the §15.2.1 rule-5 behavioral-equivalence contract this finding names: a grep for `retryable`, `errorclassify`, or `category` in either file still returns nothing.
- **Gap:** The contract's "every built-in external adapter" scope is still unmet for two of the three named surfaces on the behavioral-equivalence axis (error `code`/`category`/`retryable`, authz denials, state-transition results, pagination), even though translation fidelity is now well covered. This is a wire-protocol consistency gap. Target tier3 contract, extending the `rest_mcp_consistency`-style harness to the OpenAI adapters.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the OpenAI Chat Completions and Open Responses adapters to be mountable in a consistency harness alongside the shared `memstore` and `EchoExecutor`; `pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterregistry` already models them as `ExternalProtocolAdapter`s, so wiring is buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `tests/tier3_contract/rest_mcp_consistency/` (or a sibling per-adapter package) into a per-adapter table and run the `error_matrix_test.go`/`lifecycle_pagination_test.go` equivalence assertions against the OpenAI Chat and Responses adapters too, asserting the same `code`/`category`/`retryable` triple and the same session state after each fixed operation sequence.

### - [ ] T-15.2.4 — `RegisterAdapterUnderTest(ExternalProtocolAdapter)` consistency matrix harness does not exist [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The contract test harness exposes a `RegisterAdapterUnderTest(adapter ExternalProtocolAdapter)` entry point so that third-party adapter authors can run the suite against their implementation. The test matrix covers the full operation set of overlapping endpoints" including "All error classes: `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, `RATE_LIMITED`, ... `TENANT_SUSPENDED`" and "All state transition sequences" and "Pagination" and "Event-stream resume" and "Coordinator-handoff reattach". (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:1415-1421)
- **Existing tests:** Commit `70716b06` (F-15.2.5) added `tests/tier3_contract/rest_mcp_consistency/error_matrix_test.go` and `lifecycle_pagination_test.go`, whose test names reuse "RegisterAdapterUnderTest" (`TestRegisterAdapterUnderTestErrorMatrixLockstep`, `TestRegisterAdapterUnderTestErrorMatrixEndToEnd`, `TestRegisterAdapterUnderTestStateSequence`, `TestRegisterAdapterUnderTestPaginationParity`) for a fixed, in-process REST-vs-MCP harness: the error-class lockstep check covers the full §15.2.1 list plus the §15.4 rejection family against the shared `errorclassify` table, with three codes (`VALIDATION_ERROR`, `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION`) exercised end to end; the state-sequence and pagination tests cover a `create→terminated` sequence and a single-page/empty-result list. None of this exposes the spec's actual entry point — a function or interface accepting an arbitrary `ExternalProtocolAdapter` so a third-party author can run the suite against their own implementation still does not exist. The only `RegisterAdapterUnderTest` symbol in the tree remains `pkg/compliance/compliance.go:184`, the unrelated §15.4 runtime-adapter-binary battery. `tests/testinfra/matrix` (added since the baseline) is a generic §12.3.1 dimension cross-product test helper for unrelated contract suites, not this harness.
- **Gap:** The third-party adapter conformance entry point the spec mandates is still absent; what exists is a meaningful but fixed REST-vs-MCP built-in subset (error lockstep, a two-step state sequence, single-page pagination) rather than a pluggable matrix. The full three-sequence state-transition list, multi-page cursor traversal, event-stream resume, and coordinator-handoff reattach entries are still unverified for any adapter (event-stream resume is now covered on the REST transport per T-10.4's gap-detect work, but not through this matrix or the MCP transport specifically). Target tier3 contract plus tier10 conformance for the pluggable entry point.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the new harness keyed on `ExternalProtocolAdapter`, extending the canonical triggering inputs `error_matrix_test.go` already has for a subset of codes. The MCP transport (T-15.2.1/T-15.2.2) and the built-in matrix (this batch) are no longer blocking prerequisites; the harness itself does not exist yet.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier10_conformance/external_adapter_matrix_test.go` exposing `RegisterAdapterUnderTest(ExternalProtocolAdapter)` and asserting, per adapter, identical `code`/`category`/`retryable`/status for each catalogued error code, the three state-transition sequences, and pagination cursor and total-set identity, reusing the triggering inputs from `tests/tier3_contract/rest_mcp_consistency/error_matrix_test.go` and referencing `tests/testinfra/matrix` for the per-adapter table.

### - [ ] T-15.2.5 — Production external-adapter validate gate runs the §15.4 runtime battery instead of the §15.2.1 consistency matrix [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`POST /v1/admin/external-adapters/{name}/validate` runs the `RegisterAdapterUnderTest` suite in a sandboxed environment against the registered adapter and transitions the adapter to `status: active` on success or `status: validation_failed` ... Third-party adapters that do not pass this full matrix **must not be enabled in production**." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:1423)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/external_adapters_test.go` (moved from `pkg/gateway/admin`) still drives the validate handler with a `fakeValidator` returning a canned `compliance.Report`. The real `AdapterValidator.Validate` (`pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/external_adapters.go:45`) still calls `compliance.RunSuite`, which shells out to `cmd/lenny-compliance` and runs the §15.4 runtime-adapter binary battery — unchanged. Commit `70716b06` (F-15.2.5) added `pkg/gateway/runtime/externaladapterstore.Status.Routable()`, a machine-enforceable predicate that only a `status: active` adapter routes traffic (`TestStatusRoutable`), closing the "excluded from all traffic routing" half of the gate, and added the `rest_mcp_consistency` matrix tests from T-15.2.4/T-15.2.9 — but nothing wires that matrix into the validate handler itself.
- **Gap:** The machine-enforceable production gate the spec describes still validates the wrong contract: it checks §15.4 runtime-binary conformance, not §15.2.1 REST/MCP behavioral equivalence, even though the routing-exclusion consequence of a failed validation is now typed and tested. An external protocol adapter that diverges on error `category`, `retryable`, pagination, or event-stream resume would still pass the gate and reach production traffic. Target tier4 (the validate handler running the real §15.2.1 matrix) and a tier9 security framing (an adapter that silently flips `retryable` must be blocked).
- **Dependencies:** Depends on T-15.2.4 (the pluggable matrix harness must exist). Once it exists, the validate handler must invoke it; the handler-level test is buildable with the existing `fakeValidator` seam.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/external_adapter_validate_gate_test.go` registering a deliberately divergent adapter (one that returns `retryable: true` for a `VALIDATION_ERROR`), calling `POST /v1/admin/external-adapters/{name}/validate`, and asserting the adapter transitions to `validation_failed` and (per `Status.Routable()`) is excluded from routing.

### - [ ] T-15.2.6 — Coordinator-handoff reattach synthesized state-frame sequence is untested [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "a client reattaching with `resumeFromSeq < lastSeqBeforeHandoff` after a coordinator handoff MUST receive a synthesized state-frame sequence reconstructing session, delegation-tree, and elicitation state from durable Postgres state BEFORE any `gap_detected` frame is emitted. The test asserts: (a) the frame set includes exactly one `session.resumed` with `resumeMode: \"coordinator_handoff\"` ... (e) `gap_detected`, if emitted, follows the synthesized frames" (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:1421)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/projection.go` classifies a `children_reattached` bus event as `kindUnclassified`, so it falls back to the generic `notifications/lenny/sessionEvent` frame rather than a dedicated per-kind projection, and no test in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp` asserts the five (a)-(e) sub-contracts over the MCP `attach_session` transport. The REST-side reattach machinery this depends on gained substantial coverage since the baseline — `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/reattach_order_internal_test.go`, `resumed_event_test.go`, `resume_metrics_audit_test.go`, and `tree_archive_test.go` — but none of it exercises the MCP transport. `tests/tier8_chaos/scaffolds_test.go` still does not cover MCP reattach.
- **Gap:** The handoff-recovery sequence is a MUST with five enumerated sub-assertions and remains unverified on the MCP surface specifically. After a coordinator failover, an MCP client reattaching would receive the generic fallback frame rather than the synthesized `session.resumed`/`children_reattached` sequence the matrix requires, with no test to catch the divergence. Target tier8 chaos plus tier4 for the deterministic frame-ordering assertions, now buildable directly against the existing `attach_session` transport.
- **Dependencies:** T-15.2.1/T-15.2.2 (streaming and resume) are resolved, removing that prerequisite. Still requires a coordinator-handoff fault injector (`tests/testinfra/chaos`) and the MCP-transport synthesized-frame producer, neither of which exists yet; building them is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier8_chaos/mcp_coordinator_handoff_reattach_test.go` that seeds a parent with two completed children past `resumeFromSeq`, forces a coordinator handoff, reattaches via `attach_session` with `resumeFromSeq < lastSeqBeforeHandoff`, and asserts exactly one `session.resumed{resumeMode:"coordinator_handoff"}`, a conditional `children_reattached`, monotonic `SeqNum`s, and that any `gap_detected` follows the synthesized frames.

### - [ ] T-15.2.7 — MCP Streamable-HTTP / JSON-RPC 2.0 output is not pinned against the MCP 2025-03-26 schema [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Target MCP spec version: MCP 2025-03-26 (latest stable at time of writing). All MCP features used by Lenny are gated on this version or later." and "tool schemas, error formats, and streaming behavior conform to the negotiated version." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:1317, 1324)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/mcp_test.go` asserts Lenny-internal field expectations (`serverInfo.name == "lenny-gateway"`, JSON-RPC error codes, `tools/list` shape) using ad-hoc `map[string]any` decoding. No test validates an `initialize` result, a `tools/list` entry, or a `tools/call` result against the published MCP 2025-03-26 JSON schema. TESTING.md §12.3 lists MCP under "Wire-format equivalence across surfaces" but the only MCP conformance against an external schema is the §15.4 *intra-pod* adapter JSONL schema (`tests/tier3_contract/adapter_jsonl/`), which is unrelated to the gateway-edge MCP protocol. No schema fixtures exist anywhere in the tree (`schemas/` has only `lenny-adapter.proto`, `lenny-adapter-jsonl.schema.json`, and `messagepart.schema.json`).
- **Gap:** The external-standard conformance test the audit charter requires for MCP is still absent. Lenny could drift from the MCP 2025-03-26 envelope (capabilities object, `tools/list` `inputSchema` shape, JSON-RPC error object, and now the new SSE/notification frames from T-15.2.1) without any test failing. This is a standards-conformance gap. Target tier3 contract / tier10 conformance pinning output against the MCP schema for both the current and previous negotiated versions.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the MCP 2025-03-26 (and 2024-11-05) JSON schema fixtures vendored under `schemas/` or `tests/testinfra/stubs`. The schema fixtures are not in the tree yet; vendoring them is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/mcp_protocol/conformance_test.go` that drives `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call` (success and error), and the new `attach_session` SSE frames, validating each against the negotiated MCP version's JSON schema, asserting the negotiated version pins the serialization (current versus previous).

### - [ ] T-15.2.8 — Deprecation-window session-lifetime exception and `lenny-preflight` drain gauge are untested above the negotiation unit [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "any `MCPAdapter` connection that completed `initialize` handshake before the deprecation deadline is permitted to continue for the duration of its session ... the `lenny-preflight` Job emits a warning if any sessions older than 1 hour are active on the deprecated version (`lenny_mcp_deprecated_version_active_sessions` gauge)." and "If a post-handler-removal defect ... forces early termination ... the session closes with a structured close carrying a `mcp_protocol_version_retired` degradation annotation". (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:1328, 1331, 1332)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/version_internal_test.go` and `version.go` (commit `1f613abd`, F-15.2.1) now implement concurrent two-version support (`2025-03-26` current, `2024-11-05` previous), the structured `MCP_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED`/`MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION_RETIRED` errors with `details.supportedVersions`, and the `X-Lenny-Mcp-Version-Deprecated` header on both the POST and WebSocket `initialize` paths — closing the sibling version-negotiation gap this finding sits beside. But per that commit's own note, the session-lifetime-exception drain machinery it did not touch "stays dormant": `retiredVersions` remains `[]string{}` in v1, so the retired path is still exercised only by temporarily monkey-patching the package variable (`TestNegotiateVersion_retired_spec_15_2`), and no test exercises a mid-session connection surviving a version-support removal, the `lenny_mcp_deprecated_version_active_sessions` gauge, the preflight drain warning, or the `mcp_protocol_version_retired` `MessageEnvelope` annotation.
