An upgrade that drops a version could terminate mid-session connections or fail to surface the drain gauge without a test catching it. Target tier4 for the gauge and the mid-session continuation, tier3 for the `mcp_protocol_version_retired` annotation schema.
- **Dependencies:** Requires per-connection `negotiatedVersion` tracking wired to dispatch (now present per `version.go`), a way to simulate handler removal at runtime, and the `lenny-preflight` Job surface. The preflight gauge wiring is not exercised by any test today; building the harness is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/mcp_version_deprecation_test.go` that establishes a session on the previous version, simulates the version exiting the deprecation window, asserts the existing connection continues to dispatch on its `negotiatedVersion` while a new `initialize` on that version is rejected with `MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION_RETIRED`, and asserts the `lenny_mcp_deprecated_version_active_sessions` gauge reflects the live session.

### - [x] T-15.2.9 — REST/MCP state-transition-sequence and pagination equivalence is not asserted [Medium] — RESOLVED 70716b06

### - [ ] T-15.2.11 — The client-facing MCP tool catalog is not asserted complete against the §15.2 table [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** The §15.2 client-facing tool table lists `create_session`, `create_and_start_session`, `upload_files`, `finalize_workspace`, `start_session`, `attach_session`, `send_message`, `interrupt_session`, `get_session_status`, `get_task_tree`, `get_session_logs`, `get_token_usage`, `list_artifacts`, `download_artifact`, `terminate_session`, `cancel_session`, `resume_session`, `list_sessions`, and `list_runtimes`. (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:1293-1315)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/mcp_test.go::TestToolsList` registers and lists a single synthetic tool. `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/attach_session_test.go::TestAttachSessionInToolList_spec_15_2` (new since the baseline, part of T-15.2.1's transport) closes the one specific catalog gap the original finding named as most at risk — `attach_session`'s presence in `tools/list` is now asserted — but no test asserts the served catalog contains the full §15.2 client-facing tool set end to end against the production `mcptools.Register`, nor that each entry carries the `x-lenny-stability` label and an `inputSchema`. `TestToolsListStampsStabilityTier_spec_15_5_2447` still checks the stability default on two synthetic tools only.
- **Gap:** A regression that drops `resume_session` or `list_runtimes` from the catalog, or that ships a tool without an input schema, would still not be caught (unlike `attach_session`, now guarded). This is a capability-completeness gap on the public tool surface. Target tier2/tier3 against the real `mcptools.Register` output.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the `mcptools.Register` catalog to be near-complete; it is substantially more complete than at the baseline (T-15.2.4/T-15.2.9's shared session-creation service, `attach_session`). The catalog-completeness assertion is buildable against whatever is registered today and tightened as tools land.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/rest_mcp_consistency/tool_catalog_test.go` that stands up the gateway MCP server with the production `mcptools.Register`, calls `tools/list`, and asserts every §15.2 client-facing tool name is present, identity-filtered for `list_runtimes`, and that each entry carries a non-empty `inputSchema` and an `x-lenny-stability` value.

### - [x] T-15.2.12 — `notifications/lenny/*` unknown-notification tolerance has no test [Low] — RESOLVED 936710ae
- **Resolution:** Commit `936710ae`'s per-kind wire projection (the same work that closed T-15.2.1) ensures every `notifications/lenny/*` frame is a well-formed MCP notification. `TestProjectToolUseNotification_spec_15_2_1364` (`pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/projection_test.go`) asserts the `notifications/lenny/toolCall` frame carries no JSON-RPC `id` for the `approved`/`denied`/`completed` phases, and `TestEveryProjectedFrameIsValidJSONRPC_spec_15_2_1374` asserts every projected frame (including `notifications/lenny/error`) carries `jsonrpc:"2.0"` and a `method`. Together these pin the exact frame shape — method set, `id` absent — a conforming client needs to ignore an unrecognized `notifications/lenny/*` method without interrupting the stream, which is the gap this finding named.

### - [ ] T-15.2.13 — MCP idempotency, dispatch-tool lockstep, and result-interceptor paths are covered at the unit level [Info] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Building the adapter over the existing gateway services keeps the REST and MCP surfaces in lockstep per the §15.2.1 REST/MCP consistency contract." (pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/mcp.go:18; spec/15_external-api-surface.md:1389, 1395)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/idempotency_test.go`, `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/dispatchtool_test.go`, `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/mcp_test.go` (result-interceptor and transport-error-envelope cases), and `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/environment_scope_test.go` (the §10.6 `/mcp/environments/{name}` scope) give solid in-package coverage of the single-shot dispatch, the §11.5 idempotency Claim/Replay/Finalize path, the §9.1 `DispatchTool`/`Catalog` intra-pod lockstep seam, and the §4.8 `PreToolResult` interceptor — unchanged in substance since the baseline, only relocated under `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/`.
- **Gap:** No component-or-higher gap on these specific single-shot paths; they are well covered. This entry records that the audit found adequate coverage here so a reader does not mistake the absence of a High/Medium finding for an unexamined area. The streaming, cross-surface, and harness gaps above remain the load-bearing ones.
- **Dependencies:** None — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** No new test required for the single-shot paths. If desired, promote one idempotency case to the tier4 `gateway_full_e2e` walk so the §11.5 collapse is observed through the real gateway process rather than only in-package.

### - [ ] T-15.2.14 — OpenAI Chat / Open Responses error envelopes omit the `category` and `retryable` fields required for the §15.2.1 rule 5(d) cross-surface field-identity contract [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** §15.2.1 rule 5(d) requires that "the retryable flag and error category must be identical across REST and all adapter surfaces" (spec/15_external-api-surface.md, §15.2.1 rule 5(d)).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier3_contract/rest_mcp_consistency/error_matrix_test.go` asserts `code`/`category`/`retryable` parity between the REST and MCP transports, but no test asserts the same field-level parity for the OpenAI Chat or Open Responses adapters (see also T-15.2.3). A grep for `retryable` or `category` in the OpenAI adapter contract suites returns nothing.
- **Gap:** `pkg/gateway/environment/translator/openai_chat.go:381` (`writeOpenAIError`) encodes only `OpenAIErrorBody{Type, Message}`, and that same symbol is reused by the Open Responses handler (`pkg/gateway/environment/translator/open_responses.go`). Neither OpenAI-family adapter surface exposes the lenny error `category` or the `retryable` flag at the wire level, so the strict cross-surface field-identity in §15.2.1 rule 5(d) is unsatisfiable for these two adapters as written. This may be intentional OpenAI-native-format fidelity, but the spec text carves out no exception; it reads as a code-vs-spec mismatch on the error-envelope contract for the OpenAI-family surfaces.
- **Dependencies:** Overlaps with T-15.2.3 (behavioral-equivalence coverage for the OpenAI adapters). Resolving the field-identity assertion requires a design decision on whether the OpenAI-native error format is a sanctioned exception to rule 5(d) or whether the adapters must surface `category`/`retryable`.
- **Suggested test:** Add a contract case asserting `code`/`category`/`retryable` field-level parity across REST and MCP, plus behavioral reject-the-same-input parity for the OpenAI Chat and Open Responses surfaces (the same input rejected with an equivalent error envelope), until the rule-5(d) exception question for the OpenAI-native format is settled.

## §15.3 Internal Control API (Custom Protocol) <a id="t-15.3"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/15_external-api-surface.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§15.3 is a pointer paragraph that defines the internal control API as "Gateway ↔ Pod communication over gRPC + mTLS" and incorporates the full RPC surface from §4.7 and the wire contract from §15.4 by reference. The paragraph's text is unchanged since the 2026-06-03 audit (`git diff d9074016 HEAD -- spec/15_external-api-surface.md` touches nothing in the §15.3 span). The RPC behaviors themselves are exercised at component level in `pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterclient/client_test.go` (moved from `pkg/gateway/adapterclient` since generation), but every one of those tests, plus every other direct dial against `adapter.NewGRPCServer` added across tier3 and tier4 since generation, still dials with `insecure.NewCredentials()`, so the integrated gRPC-over-mTLS transport that is the sole normative claim of this subsection is still never exercised at tier2 or above. A new tier3 contract test (`tests/tier3_contract/embedded_gatewaycallback/callback_reachability_test.go`, landed with proposal 0013 S6) does exercise a live mTLS handshake and a fail-closed unverified-client rejection citing §15.3, but on the adjacent GatewayControl callback channel (pod → gateway), not the gateway → pod adapter-RPC direction this section's findings target, so it does not close the gap. The TESTING.md tier-9 `mtls_enforcement` suite is still declared and named at the same two places in TESTING.md but its real implementation is still absent on disk; the tier5 and tier9 `tls_test.go` checks still only assert that cert-manager Certificates report Ready, and the live plaintext-rejection probe is still an explicit no-op scaffold. The cloud parity matrix still carries no internal-control or gateway-pod mTLS row, and the chaos gateway-to-pod partition scenario is still a structural-only scaffold. The spec-map entry for §15.3 still points at a package, `pkg/gateway/internal`, that exists nowhere in the tree.
Counts: 2 High, 2 Medium, 1 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-15.3.1 — Gateway↔pod gRPC mTLS handshake and plaintext rejection are unverified at component level or above [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Gateway ↔ Pod communication over gRPC + mTLS." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:1427). The §4.7 contract restates this: "Contract (internal gRPC/HTTP+mTLS API — gateway ↔ adapter)" (spec/04_system-components.md:641). TESTING.md names the suite: "mtls_enforcement | Gateway ↔ pod gRPC over mTLS; plain text rejected; cert auto-renewal at 2/3 lifetime" (TESTING.md:1073) and "gateway-to-pod gRPC ... are rejected. mTLS handshakes require both certificates." (TESTING.md:1246).
- **Existing tests:** The gateway-side RPC client is exercised in `pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterclient/client_test.go` (moved from `pkg/gateway/adapterclient` since generation; NegotiateVersion, PrepareWorkspace, FinalizeWorkspace, RunSetup, AssignCredentials, Interrupt, Attach, Shutdown, Terminate, RotateCredentials), but every test still dials with `grpc.WithTransportCredentials(insecure.NewCredentials())` (client_test.go:85, :590, and a third site at :1378 added since generation). The same insecure-dial pattern has since proliferated into tier3/tier4 tests that also drive `adapter.NewGRPCServer` directly: `tests/tier4_integration/concurrent_workspace_test.go:369`, `tests/tier4_integration/eager_claim_lifecycle_test.go:201`, `tests/tier4_integration/recycle_scrub_path_test.go:217`, and `tests/tier3_contract/adapter_usage_wired/wired_reportusage_test.go:123` — none of these upgrade the transport to mTLS either. SPIFFE peer verification and the TLS server/client option builders are still unit-tested only, in `pkg/mtls/spiffe/verify_test.go` and `pkg/adapter/transport_mods_test.go`, both tagged to §10.3, none wired into a live `adapter.NewGRPCServer` plus `adapterclient.Dial` round trip. A new tier3 contract test, `tests/tier3_contract/embedded_gatewaycallback/callback_reachability_test.go` (landed with proposal 0013 S6, `TestEmbeddedCallbackReachableMTLS` and `TestEmbeddedCallbackMTLSRejectsUnverifiedClient`), does drive a live mTLS handshake and a fail-closed unverified-client rejection and cites §15.3 in its diagnosis comment, but it exercises the GatewayControl callback channel (pod calling back into the gateway's `ListPlatformTools`), which is the opposite direction from the gateway-dials-pod-adapter RPCs this finding names, so it does not close this gap. The tier9 scaffold `TestTLSPlaintextRejection` (tests/tier9_security/scaffolds_test.go:111) is still a `t.Logf` no-op that defers the live plaintext probe to "the ops backlog" and points at store overlays, not the gateway↔pod gRPC link. No test found that asserts an RPC succeeds with a valid client cert and is rejected over plaintext or with a wrong-identity peer cert against the gateway→pod adapter server; searched tests/tier2_component, tests/tier3_contract, tests/tier4_integration, tests/tier5_e2e_kind, tests/tier9_security, pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterclient, and pkg/adapter.
- **Gap:** The mutual-authentication handshake that §15.3 names as the only transport guarantee for the internal control API has no component, integration, or e2e coverage on the gateway-dials-pod-adapter direction. This is both a missing standards-conformance check (mTLS mutual auth on the gateway↔pod gRPC surface) and a missing adversarial scenario (a hostile or misconfigured pod presenting no cert, a plaintext peer, or a cert from a foreign trust domain must be refused before any RPC dispatches). Target tiers: tier2 component for the in-process server-plus-client mTLS round trip and rejection, and tier9 security for the end-to-end plaintext-rejection probe on the gateway↔pod path.
- **Dependencies:** The tier2 case is buildable today: `adapter.NewGRPCServer` with `adapter.TLSServerOption` wired to the `pkg/mtls/spiffe` agent peer verifier, an in-process listener, and `adapterclient.Dial` (`pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterclient`) with `adapter.TLSClientOption`, using the self-contained CA/leaf-minting helper pattern now demonstrated in `tests/tier3_contract/embedded_gatewaycallback/callback_reachability_test.go`. The tier9 live probe needs the tier5 Kind harness (tests/testinfra/kind) with cert-manager wiring and a way to attempt a plaintext dial against a pod adapter port; the gateway binary and the `kind.InstallLenny` path already exist, so the remaining work is the plaintext-dial assertion.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier2_component/adapter_mtls/handshake_test.go` that stands up `adapter.NewGRPCServer` behind the SPIFFE agent verifier and asserts a valid-cert `adapterclient.Dial` completes `NegotiateVersion` while an insecure dial and a foreign-trust-domain cert are both refused, plus a tier9 `tests/tier9_security/mtls/gateway_pod_test.go` that attempts a plaintext gRPC dial against a live pod adapter on Kind and asserts the handshake fails.

### - [ ] T-15.3.2 — Declared tier-9 `mtls_enforcement` suite is absent on disk; cert auto-renewal at 2/3 lifetime is exercised only by unit logic [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "mtls_enforcement | Gateway ↔ pod gRPC over mTLS; plain text rejected; cert auto-renewal at 2/3 lifetime" (TESTING.md:1073). The suite is in the PR critical-path subset: "Critical-path subset (runs on PR): warm_pool, sandbox_claim, pod_lifecycle, mtls_enforcement, ..." (TESTING.md:1088). The deferral note names the missing files: "tests/tier5_e2e_kind/mtls_enforcement_test.go and tests/tier9_security/mtls/ are deferred." (TESTING.md:1544).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/mtls_enforcement_test.go` still does not exist and `tests/tier9_security/mtls/` still does not exist (confirmed by directory listing). The tier5 `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/mtls_test.go` and tier9 `tests/tier9_security/tls_test.go` still only assert that the §10.3 cert-manager Certificate and Issuer resources report `Ready=True`; neither drives a gRPC RPC over the issued certs, asserts plaintext rejection, nor exercises renewal. Cert renewal logic is still unit-tested only, in `pkg/mtls/rotation_test.go` (CA-rotation state machine) and `pkg/mtls/certreload/certreload_test.go` (`TestReloaderPicksUpRenewedCert_spec_10_3_338`), both at unit level against §10.3, with no integrated gateway↔pod renewal scenario.
- **Gap:** A named suite that sits in the PR critical-path subset still has no implementation, so the dashboard and the gate count a green where no test runs. Two of its three asserted behaviors (plaintext rejection on the gateway↔pod link, cert auto-renewal at 2/3 lifetime observed across a live RPC) remain unverified above unit level. The renewal half is specifically a real operational journey: a long-lived session whose pod adapter cert crosses 2/3 of its lifetime must hot-reload the renewed leaf without dropping the gRPC connection. Target tiers: tier5 e2e on Kind for the renewal-without-disconnect journey, and tier9 security for plaintext rejection (shared with T-15.3.1).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness with cert-manager (tests/testinfra/kind, already used by mtls_test.go) plus a mechanism to force or fast-forward a Certificate renewal (a short-lived `duration`/`renewBefore` on a test Certificate, or `cmctl renew`). No external credentials needed; buildable on the existing harness once the renewal-trigger fixture is added.
- **Suggested test:** Create `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/mtls_enforcement_test.go` that issues a gateway↔pod Certificate with a short lifetime, drives a live session RPC across the 2/3 renewal boundary via the sessiondriver harness (tests/testinfra/sessiondriver), and asserts the connection survives the leaf swap; pair it with the tier9 plaintext-rejection case so the named `mtls_enforcement` suite has a real backing implementation.

### - [ ] T-15.3.3 — Internal control API mTLS link is unvalidated on every cloud provider (GKE, EKS, AKS) [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Gateway ↔ Pod communication over gRPC + mTLS." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:1427). The cloud parity matrix is the per-provider coverage ledger: "A capability that the spec claims but is missing from this matrix fails the Tier 0 static gate." (tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml:7-8).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml` still lists gvisor_isolation, kata_isolation, firecracker_isolation, multi_zone_dr, managed_ingress, cloud_csi, cloud_kms, cloud_oidc, cloud_secret_store, multi_az_minio, cloud_observability, and cloud_billing_export. It still contains no row for the internal control API, gateway-pod mTLS, or SPIFFE peer verification. No test found that exercises the gateway↔pod gRPC handshake on GKE, EKS, or AKS; searched the parity matrix and tests/tier6_e2e_cloud.
- **Gap:** The mTLS transport is asserted to hold across the cloud topologies in the deployment matrix (GKE/EKS/AKS, where workload identity, IRSA, or WIF mints the pod identity), but no cloud capability row exercises it, so the link is verified in zero of the three cloud combinations. This is a deployment-combination gap: cert issuance and SPIFFE identity binding differ per cloud CA integration, and a provider-specific handshake regression would ship undetected. Target tier: tier6 e2e on cloud.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier6 cloud harness (tests/testinfra/cloud) and live GKE/EKS/AKS clusters with cert-manager and the cloud CA integration configured. Clusters and cloud credentials are external; building the capability row and the assertion is buildable once a cloud cluster is reachable.
- **Suggested test:** Add a `mtls_internal_control` capability to `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml` (spec_section "15.3") with a backing tier6 test under tests/tier6_e2e_cloud that drives one session RPC over the gateway↔pod link on each provider and asserts the handshake mutually authenticates, marking the cell `validated` per provider as the harness lands.

### - [ ] T-15.3.4 — Gateway-to-pod partition resilience for the control API is a structural-only chaos scaffold [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Gateway ↔ Pod communication over gRPC + mTLS." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:1427), exercised under failure per TESTING.md tier-8: "Network failures: gateway-to-pod partition, agent-to-LLM-provider partition, network-policy drift, cross-zone partition." (TESTING.md:1216).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier8_chaos/scaffolds_test.go:170` still carries a "§12.8 gateway-to-pod partition — covered structurally by" comment block; there is still no executing chaos test that severs the gateway↔pod gRPC link mid-session and asserts recovery. No partition test found that operates on the internal control API; searched tests/tier8_chaos.
- **Gap:** The failure path for the internal control API (a gRPC partition between the gateway and a running pod adapter) is named in the chaos tier but is only structurally referenced. This is a missing failure-path scenario: when the control channel drops, the session must surface a defined state (reconnect, suspend, or orphan-reconcile) rather than hang. Target tier: tier8 chaos.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the chaos harness (tests/testinfra/chaos) with a network-fault injector against the pod adapter port and a live or compose-backed session. The fault-injection layer is the missing infrastructure; recording and building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier8_chaos/gateway_pod_partition_test.go` that drives a session via sessiondriver, injects a gateway↔pod gRPC partition with the chaos harness, and asserts the session transitions to the documented post-partition state and recovers when the link is restored.

### - [ ] T-15.3.5 — spec-map.json §15.3 points at a nonexistent package `pkg/gateway/internal` [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Gateway ↔ Pod communication over gRPC + mTLS." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:1427). The spec-map §15.3 entry declares `"packages": ["pkg/gateway/internal"]` with `"tests": []` (tests/spec-map.json:2084-2095); the §15 umbrella entry repeats the same package (tests/spec-map.json:1989).
- **Existing tests:** No package `pkg/gateway/internal` exists on disk (confirmed by directory listing; the only references to the path are the two spec-map.json lines). The gateway-side adapter client now lives in `pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterclient` (moved from `pkg/gateway/adapterclient` since generation) and the in-pod adapter gRPC server lives in `pkg/adapter` (root-level, not under `pkg/gateway/`); `pkg/gateway/runtime/adapter` is a distinct package holding only the §15/§9.1 `Capabilities` struct and is not the RPC server this section is about.
- **Gap:** The spec-map mapping for §15.3 is still an inconsistency: it claims a package that does not exist and lists no tests, so any coverage dashboard reading this entry reports a phantom package and zero tests for the internal control API. This is a spec-versus-map drift that masks the real (and partial) coverage in `pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterclient` and `pkg/adapter`. Target tier: tier0 static (the map-validation gate).
- **Dependencies:** None — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Correct the §15.3 and §15 entries in `tests/spec-map.json` to reference `pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterclient` and `pkg/adapter`, and extend the `cmd/lenny-test validate-maps` tier0 gate to fail when a spec-map `packages` entry names a directory absent from the module so future phantom-package drift is caught.

### - [ ] T-15.3.6 — §15.3 is classified non-normative, but its mTLS transport claim has no owning normative test in §4.7 or §15.4 coverage [Info] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** The spec-map exception records: "section 15.3 ... reason: non-normative ... Pointer paragraph stating gateway-to-pod transport is gRPC over mTLS; the RPC surface is normative in §4.7 and §15.4." (tests/spec-map-exceptions.yaml:84-86).
- **Existing tests:** §15.4 coverage (tests/spec-map.json) and the §4.7 RPC behaviors (`pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterclient/client_test.go`) exercise the RPC payloads and the JSON-Lines and MessagePart wire formats, all over insecure transport. The mTLS transport claim is still delegated to §10.3, whose tests verify cert issuance and SPIFFE parsing at unit level (see T-15.3.1 and T-15.3.2). The new `tests/tier3_contract/embedded_gatewaycallback/callback_reachability_test.go` (see T-15.3.1) supplies a normative mTLS-handshake test, but only for the opposite-direction GatewayControl callback channel, so it does not fill the seam this note describes for the gateway→pod adapter RPC direction.
- **Gap:** This is an observation rather than a missing test. The non-normative classification is defensible because the RPC surface is owned by §4.7 and §15.4, but the specific "+ mTLS" transport assertion in §15.3 falls between the §4.7 RPC tests (insecure) and the §10.3 PKI tests (cert issuance only), so no single normative test asserts that the §4.7 RPC surface runs over a mutually authenticated channel. Findings T-15.3.1 through T-15.3.3 close that seam; this note records that the seam is a cross-section coverage boundary rather than a §15.3-local omission.
- **Dependencies:** None — buildable today (the closure is the tier2 mTLS round-trip test proposed in T-15.3.1).
- **Suggested test:** Once T-15.3.1 lands, add the tier2 `adapter_mtls` round-trip test to the §4.7 or §15.4 spec-map entry so the RPC-over-mTLS assertion has an explicit normative owner, and keep the §15.3 exception as documentation of the pointer relationship.

## §15.4 Runtime Adapter Specification <a id="t-15.4"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/15_external-api-surface.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The adapter↔binary JSON Lines protocol, the lifecycle channel, the Standard-level MCP nonce handshake, and the OpenAI Completions and Open Responses translators have genuine coverage at the unit, component (`pkg/adapter`), contract (`tests/tier3_contract/adapter_jsonl`), and conformance (`tests/tier10_conformance` against the three bundled runtimes) tiers. The gaps concentrate where the spec applies a behavior across deployment combinations, external protocols, or failure paths. No test exercises the adapter protocol or the conformance harness against a runtime deployed on Kind or a cloud cluster, so the production sidecar transport plus NetworkPolicy plus mTLS path is unverified end to end. The Translation Fidelity Matrix conformance check covers only the OpenAI Completions and Open Responses columns and leaves the MCP, REST, and A2A columns plus the adapter `lenny-blob://` dereference obligation untested at component or conformance tier. The adversarial conformance fixtures exist on disk but are wired into no negative-path battery, the nine reference runtimes are checked only structurally, and several spec-map-listed tier3 tests are no-op stubs. Since the 2026-06-03 audit, proposal 0018 renamed `OutputPart` to `MessagePart` (and `OUTPUTPART_*` error codes to `MESSAGEPART_*`) across this section, proposal 0020 regrouped the gateway package tree (`pkg/gateway/outputpartfidelity` → `pkg/gateway/externalapi/outputpartfidelity`, `pkg/gateway/adapterclient` → `pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterclient`, `pkg/gateway/mcptools` → `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools`, `sdks/runtime/go/outputpart` → `sdks/runtime/go/messagepart`), and proposal 0002 deleted task mode and its between-task `task_complete`/`task_ready` lifecycle signaling outright, replacing it with the `session`/`service` execution-mode model and pool-level pod recycling. Two findings are resolved this pass: the concurrent-workspace `slotId` dispatch loop (T-15.4.1.7) now has thorough component and conformance coverage via the new `echo-concurrent` reference runtime, and the task-mode pod-reuse cycle (T-15.4.3.1) is moot because task mode no longer exists. A third (T-15.4.1.5, adapter-local path-traversal rejection) is resolved on discovering pre-existing unit coverage in `pkg/adapter/localtools` that the original audit missed. Counts: 5 High, 8 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-15.4.1 — Adapter↔binary protocol and conformance harness are never exercised on Kind or a cloud cluster [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Platform testing: Validates the full session lifecycle (pod claim → workspace setup → message → response → teardown) without requiring a real agent runtime or LLM credentials." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2162); the §4.7 sidecar model runs the adapter and runtime in separate containers.
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/adapter/socketruntime_e2e_test.go::TestSidecarSocketTransportDrivesTheEchoRuntime` drives the real `cmd/runtimes/echo` binary over the socket transport in one process. `tests/tier10_conformance/scaffolds_test.go` runs the conformance batteries against the bundled runtimes through the fake adapter. `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/pod_lifecycle_test.go::TestPodLifecycle` inspects pod container topology and `runtimeClassName` only; it never sends a `message` or asserts a `response`. No tier5 or tier6 test sends a `message` envelope through a deployed adapter sidecar and asserts the `response` round-trips over the real gRPC `Attach` stream under NetworkPolicy and pod-to-gateway mTLS.
- **Gap:** The end-to-end adapter transport (gateway → adapter gRPC → stdin/stdout JSON Lines → runtime → response) is verified only in-process and against fakes. The real user journey, where alice creates a session on a Kind or GKE cluster and the runtime echoes her input back through the production sidecar, has no e2e test. Target tiers: tier5 (Kind) and tier6 (cloud). This is a core-capability user-journey gap.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`) and the tier6 cloud harness (`tests/testinfra/cloud`) with the echo runtime image published to the cluster registry. The Kind harness exists; an in-cluster echo image build step is the missing piece and is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/adapter_protocol_test.go` that deploys the echo runtime, creates a session via `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`, sends a `message`, and asserts the echoed `response` arrives over the real adapter transport; mirror it as a tier6 case keyed off `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml`.

### - [ ] T-15.4.6.1 — Reference-runtime conformance is asserted structurally only; no reference runtime is actually exercised [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "CI for first-party reference runtimes ... invokes `lenny runtime validate` on every push and fails the release if any test category regresses." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2391); "This suite runs against every test runtime and every reference runtime." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:996, TESTING.md)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier10_conformance/scaffolds_test.go::TestReferenceCatalogNightly` reads `pkg/compliance.ReferenceCatalog()` and asserts the catalog manifest lists claude-code, gemini-cli, codex, cursor-cli, chat, langgraph, mastra, openai-assistants, and crewai at their declared levels. The image-pull half is gated behind `LENNY_REFERENCE_IMAGE_REGISTRY` and the test logs and returns without running any battery when it is unset.
- **Gap:** No reference runtime is run through `lenny-compliance` at any tier. The nightly conformance run that the spec requires for the nine reference runtimes does not exist on disk; only the catalog table shape is checked. Target tier: tier10 conformance (nightly), with the image-pull execution path. This is a standards-conformance gap for the runtime-adapter contract across the reference catalog.

### - [x] T-15.4.1.7 — Concurrent-workspace `slotId` multiplexing over the binary protocol is unexercised across execution modes [Medium] — RESOLVED 228ac6a2 (proposal 0002/0035 groundwork)
- **Resolution:** The `slotId`-keyed dispatch loop is now thoroughly covered. Integration tier: `tests/tier4_integration/concurrent_workspace_test.go::TestConcurrentWorkspacePerSlotExecution_spec_5_2` drives two concurrent sessions through the real gateway→adapter→runtime path and asserts per-slot workspace isolation and response `slotId` tagging. Conformance tier: `tests/tier10_conformance/concurrent_slot_conformance_test.go::TestConcurrentSlotDispatchConformance` (commit `228ac6a2`) drives the new bundled `cmd/runtimes/echo-concurrent` reference runtime — which did not exist at audit time and closes the "no bundled runtime declares concurrent-workspace mode" dependency this finding recorded — with two interleaved `slotId`s plus a no-`slotId` frame, and asserts per-slot response tagging, per-slot cwd derivation, and the no-`slotId` whole-pod path. The session-mode/task-mode "never carry `slotId`" invariant is covered by `TestNoSlotIDKeepsBasePath_spec_6_4`. The terminology this finding used ("concurrent-workspace mode") was retired by proposal 0002 in favor of `sessionPolicy.maxConcurrentSessions > 1`; the underlying dispatch contract and its test coverage are unaffected by the rename.

### - [x] T-15.4.3.1 — Task-mode between-task signaling (`task_complete` / `task_ready`) has no pod-reuse cycle test against a real runtime [Medium] — RESOLVED fe3956e8 (reconciled against proposal 0002)
- **Resolution:** Proposal 0002 deleted task mode and its between-task lifecycle signaling outright (commit `fe3956e8`, "spec: apply 0002 session/service execution model and per-pod occupancy claims"; adapter-side removal in commit `2084f114`, "remove adapter between-task lifecycle surface (task_complete/task_ready/task_lifecycle)"). The `task_complete`, `task_complete_acknowledged`, and `task_ready` lifecycle-channel frames, the `task_lifecycle` capability, the `LifecycleChannel` `taskMode`/`taskCompleteAckTimeout` fields, `RequestTaskComplete`, and `SignalTaskReady` no longer exist anywhere in the spec or the adapter; the `task_complete_ack_timeout` metric is deleted; and the corresponding `TestLifecycleChannelTaskCompleteRoundTrip_spec_4_7` test was removed in the same change as orphaned. The `session` and `service` execution modes replace `session`/`task`/`concurrent-workspace`: pod recycling under `sessionPolicy.recycle` now runs uniformly across whole sessions with no runtime cooperation and no between-task lifecycle exchange, and is explicitly "not a level-sensitive capability" (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:545). There is no longer a between-task pod-reuse cycle for this finding's suggested test to exercise; the successor recycle-boundary behavior (whole-session scrub-and-reuse, `ReportSessionScrub`/`ReportPodScrub`) is covered under the §5.2/§6.2 units by proposal 0035's conformance work (e.g. `tests/tier10_conformance/recycle_scrub_conformance_test.go`), outside this §15.4 unit's scope.

## §15.5 API Versioning and Stability <a id="t-15.5"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/15_external-api-surface.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§15.5 carries a dense set of normative requirements: the REST `/v1`→`/v2` 6-month sunset rule, the MCP two-version deprecation window, the runtime-adapter protocol version selection, the CRD graduation path with a conversion-webhook deployment ordering, the bifurcated live-versus-durable `schemaVersion` forward-read rules, the distinct degradation-annotation catalog, and the 90-day durable-consumer migration SLA. Coverage today is almost entirely tier0/tier1: the `pkg/degradation` annotation constructors, the `pkg/gateway/middleware/deprecation` header stamper, the `pkg/preflight` and `pkg/admission/webhook` conversion checks, and the `pkg/embedded/crds` preserve-unknown-fields assertions are unit tests, and the helm-unittest suite covers the chart flag wiring. The `tests/spec-map.json` entry for §15.5 lists no tests and points at a `pkg/api/version` package that does not exist on disk, while `tests/spec-map-exceptions.yaml` classifies the whole subsection as non-normative even though it contains multiple MUST and MUST NOT clauses. No tier2 component, tier4 integration, tier5/tier6 e2e, tier9 security, or tier10 conformance test exercises the durable forward-read MUST against a real store, the deprecation header through the real gateway router, the conversion webhook on a real API server, or the MCP version-retirement degradation path. Counts: 3 High, 4 Medium, 1 Low, 2 Info.

Proposal 0018 (F-MS5/S5, applied 2026-06-25) renamed `OutputPart` to `MessagePart` throughout the spec, including the two references inside this subsection (the degradation-annotation-catalog table row and the closing `TaskRecord` forward-read paragraph). This is a pure identifier rename with no change to the normative behavior: every MUST/MUST NOT clause in §15.5 reads identically before and after, and the section's content is otherwise unchanged since the 2026-06-03 audit (confirmed by diffing the section text verbatim against the pre-rename revision). The rename, combined with unrelated insertions earlier in the spec file, shifted every quoted line number in this section's findings by a constant +8; the quotes below are updated to the current line numbers. No finding in this section resolves on that basis alone, and no new testable requirement was introduced by the rename.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-15.5.1 — Durable-consumer forward-read MUST is unverified above unit tier against any real persisted store [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Durable consumers MUST forward-read records with unrecognized `schemaVersion`. ... Durable consumers MUST process all fields they understand and preserve all unknown fields verbatim (pass-through). If a durable consumer cannot safely pass through unknown fields ... it MUST emit a `durable_schema_version_ahead` structured error to an operator alert channel and queue the record for manual review rather than dropping it. ... Durable consumers MUST NOT silently discard records based solely on an unrecognized `schemaVersion`." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2480-2482)
- **Existing tests:** The forward-read obligation is exercised only at unit tier. `pkg/degradation/annotations_test.go` asserts the field shapes of the three annotation bodies. `pkg/workspaceplan/plan_test.go::TestParseRejectsUnsupportedHigherSchemaVersion` covers the workspace-plan reject path (a live-consumer behavior, not the durable pass-through). `pkg/adapter/mcpruntime_schemaversion_internal_test.go` asserts a `MessagePart` producer schemaVersion is hoisted intact. The tier2 store suites assert only writes at the default version: `tests/tier2_component/stores/billingstore_test.go:67` asserts `SchemaVersion == 1` and `tests/tier2_component/stores/sessionstore_test.go:182` writes `"schemaVersion":1`. A grep across tests/tier2_component, tests/tier3_contract, tests/tier4_integration, tests/tier8_chaos, and tests/tier9_security for `durable_schema_version_ahead`, "manual review", "operator alert", or a record read at schemaVersion ≥ 2 returned no match (no test found).
- **Gap:** No tier2 component test reads a persisted `TaskRecord`, billing event, audit event, session record, checkpoint, or `MessageEnvelope` at a `schemaVersion` higher than the reader understands and asserts the three durable behaviors: known fields parse, unknown fields are preserved verbatim, and a schema-strict sink emits `durable_schema_version_ahead` to an operator channel with the record queued instead of dropped. This is the strongest normative clause in §15.5 and is the compliance-critical path for the 13-month billing and regulatory audit retention windows. The missing test is both a real user journey (a durable analytics or compliance reader processing a record written by a newer gateway) and an adversarial scenario (a schema-strict sink that must not drop data).
- **Dependencies:** Requires a forward-version record fixture (a row written at schemaVersion=N+1 with an unknown field) in tests/testdata or via tests/testinfra/fixtures/generators, plus a schema-strict-sink stub under tests/testinfra/stubs and the real Postgres-backed store harness used by tests/tier2_component/stores. The forward-version fixture and the strict-sink stub do not exist yet; building them is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier2_component/stores/schemaversion_forward_read_test.go that inserts billing, audit, and session records at schemaVersion=N+1 with an extra unknown JSONB field, reads them back through the real store, and asserts unknown fields survive a round-trip; add a strict-sink case asserting `durable_schema_version_ahead` is emitted and the record is queued, using tests/testinfra/audit and tests/testinfra/stubs.

### - [ ] T-15.5.2 — REST `/v1`→`/v2` deprecation header and 6-month sunset have no component, integration, or e2e coverage [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "REST API: Versioned via URL path prefix (`/v1/`). Breaking changes require a new version (`/v2/`). ... The previous version is supported for at least 6 months after a new version ships." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2435)
- **Existing tests:** The `Deprecation`-header middleware is covered only by unit and helm-unittest tiers. `pkg/gateway/middleware/deprecation/deprecation_test.go` exercises `Wrap` directly (`TestStampsHeaderOnDeprecatedPath_spec_15_5_124`, `TestSkipsHeaderOnLiveVersion_spec_15_5_124`, `TestNoOpWhenSetEmpty_spec_15_5_124`). The chart wiring is asserted in `charts/lenny/tests/gateway-deployment_test.yaml` (renders `--deprecated-api-versions=v1,v2`). The middleware is wired into the gateway at `cmd/lenny-gateway/httpsurface.go:902` (moved from `main.go` since the audit; wiring is unchanged in substance). A grep across tests/tier2_component, tests/tier3_contract, tests/tier4_integration, and tests/tier5_e2e_kind for `Deprecation` or `DeprecatedAPIVersion` returned no match (no test found at tier2 or above).
- **Gap:** No tier4 integration test starts the real gateway with `--deprecated-api-versions=v1` set and asserts that a `/v1/...` response carries the `Deprecation` header while a `/v2/...` or unversioned response does not. No tier5 Kind e2e test exercises the operator journey of shipping `/v2`, adding `v1` to `gateway.deprecatedAPIVersions`, and confirming clients on `/v1` continue to receive responses with the deprecation signal through the full ingress path. The header is a public REST contract surface and is unverified end to end. This is a real user journey (alice keeps her `/v1` integration working through a `/v2` rollout).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the running gateway harness in tests/testinfra/gateway with the deprecated-version flag set; for the Kind variant, tests/testinfra/kind. None — buildable today for the tier4 case.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/api_deprecation_header_test.go that boots the gateway with `v1` deprecated, issues requests to `/v1/sessions` and `/v2/sessions`, and asserts the `Deprecation` header presence and value via tests/testinfra/gateway; add a tier5 follow-up driving the same through Kind ingress.

### - [ ] T-15.5.3 — CRD conversion-webhook deployment ordering and multi-version coexistence is verified only with a fake client, never on a real API server [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The conversion webhook (`lenny-crd-conversion`) must be deployed before adding a new served version to any CRD — the API server begins routing conversion requests to the webhook as soon as `spec.conversion.strategy: Webhook` is set, and a missing webhook causes all CRD operations to fail. ... The `lenny-preflight` Job validates conversion webhook availability as a preflight check and will fail the upgrade if the webhook Service is absent or not ready." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2443-2446)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/preflight/conversionwebhook_test.go` (`TestCheckConversionWebhook_spec_15_5_2438`, `TestRunConversionWebhookReady_spec_15_5_2438`, `TestRunConversionWebhookUnready_spec_15_5_2438`) uses `fake.NewClientBuilder()` to assert the preflight check passes or fails on a synthetic Service/Deployment state. `pkg/admission/webhook/crd_conversion_test.go` exercises the conversion handler over `httptest` with `ConversionReview` bodies. `pkg/embedded/crds/crds_test.go::TestEmbeddedCRDsPreserveUnknownFields_spec_10_437` asserts the CRD schema declares `x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields`. A grep across tests/tier4_integration and tests/tier5_e2e_kind for `conversion`, `v1alpha1`, `v1beta1`, or "served" returned no CRD-version match (no real-API-server test found).
- **Gap:** No envtest or Kind test installs two served CRD versions, runs the `lenny-crd-conversion` Deployment, and validates the spec ordering: that applying a new served version with the webhook absent or unready fails CRD operations, that the preflight Job blocks the upgrade in that state, and that re-applying stored objects triggers storage migration once both versions are served. The "missing webhook causes all CRD operations to fail" branch is the failure-path requirement and is never exercised against a real API server, where conversion routing and admission actually occur. This combines a deployment-combination gap (upgrade topology) with an adversarial failure scenario (webhook absent during a served-version add).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the envtest harness in tests/testinfra/envtest with a real API server and the conversion webhook served, or the tier5 Kind harness in tests/testinfra/kind with the chart's conversion-webhook Deployment installed. The two-served-version envtest fixture does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier5_e2e_kind/crd_conversion_upgrade_test.go that installs a CRD at one served version, deploys `lenny-crd-conversion`, adds a second served version, exercises a stored-object re-apply migration, and asserts CRD operations fail when the webhook Service is deleted, driving the preflight Job via tests/testinfra/kind and tests/testinfra/envtest.

### - [ ] T-15.5.4 — spec-map.json claims no §15.5 tests and points at a non-existent package while real F-15.5 tests exist [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "§15.5 ... tests: []; packages: [pkg/api/version]; blocked_until_phase: 5 ... The REST/MCP version-negotiation contract ... is a Phase 5 deliverable; tests land alongside the API implementation." (tests/spec-map.json:2160-2168)
- **Existing tests:** The spec-map entry lists an empty `tests` array, yet multiple tests tagged `F-15.5.*` and `spec_15_5_*` exist on disk: `pkg/degradation/annotations_test.go`, `pkg/gateway/middleware/deprecation/deprecation_test.go`, `pkg/preflight/conversionwebhook_test.go`, `pkg/embedded/crds/crds_test.go`, `pkg/adapter/mcpruntime_schemaversion_internal_test.go`, and `pkg/task/record_test.go::TestReconcileSchemaVersion_spec_8_8_825`. The package the entry names, `pkg/api/version`, does not exist (the only `pkg/api` subtrees are `pkg/api/v1` and `pkg/api/v1/session`).
- **Gap:** The spec-to-test map is inconsistent with the codebase in two ways: it claims zero coverage where partial unit coverage exists, and it points the package list at a directory that was never created. A dashboard query for §15.5 reports it as entirely unbuilt and blocked on Phase 5, which hides the existing degradation, deprecation, preflight, and CRD coverage and prevents a reviewer from noticing the tier2-and-above gaps recorded in T-15.5.1 through T-15.5.3. This inconsistency could let a regression in the existing F-15.5 unit tests ship unnoticed because the map does not track them under §15.5.
- **Dependencies:** None — buildable today. The fix is to populate the §15.5 `tests` and `packages` arrays with the on-disk F-15.5 tests and correct or remove the `pkg/api/version` entry.
- **Suggested test:** Update tests/spec-map.json §15.5 to list the existing `pkg/degradation`, `pkg/gateway/middleware/deprecation`, `pkg/preflight`, and `pkg/embedded/crds` F-15.5 tests, correct the package path, and add a tier0 guard in tests/tier0_static that fails when a spec-map `packages` entry names a directory absent from the module.

### - [ ] T-15.5.5 — Live-consumer forward-read with the `schema_version_ahead` annotation is unverified on any real streaming path [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Live consumers ... MAY reject an unrecognized `schemaVersion` — but SHOULD forward-read ... When a live consumer chooses to forward-read, it MUST surface a `schema_version_ahead` annotation on the enclosing `MessageEnvelope` (fields: `knownVersion`, `encounteredVersion`) so the caller is informed of potential incompleteness." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2465-2466)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/degradation/annotations_test.go::TestSchemaVersionAheadFieldShape_spec_15_5_2465` asserts the annotation body carries `knownVersion` and `encounteredVersion`. No higher-tier test produces this annotation through a real streaming session. A grep across tests/tier2_component, tests/tier3_contract, and tests/tier4_integration for `schema_version_ahead` or `SchemaVersionAhead` returned no match (no test found above unit tier).
- **Gap:** No tier4 integration test drives a streaming session in which a `MessageEnvelope` arrives at a `schemaVersion` the live consumer does not recognize and asserts the consumer either rejects with the documented session failure or forward-reads while stamping `schema_version_ahead` on the enclosing envelope. The streaming forward-read SHOULD/MUST pair is the live half of the bifurcated rule and is exercised only as a constructor unit test. This is a real user journey (bob's streaming client receives a newer-schema event during a rolling gateway upgrade) and a degradation-signalling path.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a streaming session harness in tests/testinfra/sessiondriver and a forward-version envelope injector in tests/testinfra/stubs. The forward-version envelope injector does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/schema_version_ahead_streaming_test.go that injects a `MessageEnvelope` at schemaVersion=N+1 into a live streaming session and asserts the `schema_version_ahead` annotation appears with the correct `knownVersion`/`encounteredVersion`, using tests/testinfra/sessiondriver.

### - [ ] T-15.5.6 — 90-day durable-consumer migration window SLA has no test asserting old-version readability after retirement [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Migration window SLA: When a new `schemaVersion` is introduced, all durable consumers MUST be upgraded to understand the new version within 90 days of the version's release. After 90 days, the previous schema version may be retired from active write paths, but persisted records at the old version remain readable for the full retention period of each record type." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2483)
- **Existing tests:** TESTING.md references the rule in the SDK compatibility matrix ("validated against the two most recent minor gateway versions ... per spec/15.5", TESTING.md:1991) and the TaskRecord domain suite ("old readers can pass through unknown fields per forward-read rule", TESTING.md:1883), but a grep across the test tiers for "90 day", "migration window", or a retired-write-path-with-readable-old-records scenario returned no match (no test found).
- **Gap:** No test asserts the post-retirement invariant: after the previous schemaVersion is removed from the active write path, persisted records still written at that version remain decodable for the record type's full retention period (13 months for billing, regulatory periods for audit). The retention-readability guarantee after write-path retirement is untested, and a regression that prunes the old deserialization path would silently break compliance reads. This is a deployment-and-time-evolution gap best exercised with a multi-version corpus.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a corpus of records at version N and N-1 in tests/testdata or via tests/testinfra/fixtures/generators and the real store harness; clock control via tests/testinfra/clockstep or tests/testinfra/timectl to model the 90-day boundary. The mixed-version corpus does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier2_component/stores/schema_retention_readability_test.go that writes billing and audit records at version N-1, simulates retirement of the N-1 write path, and asserts the records still decode through the store after the 90-day window using tests/testinfra/clockstep.

### - [ ] T-15.5.7 — `mcp_protocol_version_retired` degradation path is unit-only, with no tier2+ or adversarial coverage [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`mcp_protocol_version_retired` | Old writer → new reader | An active MCP session whose negotiated `protocolVersion` has been removed from the gateway is forced to terminate by a post-handler-removal defect ... `retiredVersion`, `currentVersions`. ... These annotations MUST NOT be conflated." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2475-2477)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/degradation/annotations_test.go::TestMcpProtocolVersionRetiredFieldShape_spec_15_5_2467` and `TestAnnotationKeysAreDistinct_spec_15_5_2469` assert the body fields and the distinctness of the three annotation keys at unit tier. MCP version negotiation and the retired-version handshake rejection are covered at unit tier by `pkg/gateway/mcp/version_internal_test.go::TestNegotiateVersion_retired_spec_15_2` (attributed to §15.2). A grep across tests/tier4_integration and tests/tier9_security for `mcp_protocol_version_retired`, "retired", or a version-downgrade adversarial case returned no match (no test found above unit tier).
- **Gap:** No tier4 integration test holds an active MCP session whose negotiated protocol version is then removed from the gateway and asserts the session is terminated with the `mcp_protocol_version_retired` annotation carrying `retiredVersion` and `currentVersions`. No tier9 security test exercises a hostile client attempting to pin a retired version or to conflate the retirement signal with a forward-compat signal. The session-lifetime retirement behavior is a protocol-conformance and resilience path and is unverified end to end. This is both a failure scenario (a live MCP session surviving a gateway upgrade that drops its version) and a standards-conformance check against the negotiated MCP protocol version.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the MCP session harness in tests/testinfra/gateway with a runtime-time version-retirement hook and a long-lived MCP connection driver in tests/testinfra/sessiondriver. The version-retirement hook does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/mcp_version_retirement_test.go that negotiates the previous MCP version, retires it on the gateway mid-session, and asserts the termination emits `mcp_protocol_version_retired` with the documented fields, using tests/testinfra/gateway and tests/testinfra/sessiondriver.

### - [ ] T-15.5.8 — Runtime-adapter protocol version selection at INIT lacks a §15.5-attributed conformance assertion [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Runtime adapter protocol: Versioned independently ... The adapter advertises a protocol version at INIT; the gateway selects a compatible version. Major version changes are breaking." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2439)
- **Existing tests:** Adapter INIT negotiation is exercised by the proto `NegotiateVersion` RPC and the conformance suite under tests/tier10_conformance/scaffolds_test.go (`TestBasicAdapterProtocol`, `TestStandardLevel`, `TestFullLevel`), but these are attributed to §15.4.x and do not include a negative case that asserts the gateway refuses an adapter advertising an incompatible major version. The version-handling unit coverage lives in pkg/adapter alongside the lifecycle tests; `pkg/adapter/server_test.go::TestNegotiateVersionReportsIncompatibleWhenNoOverlap` covers the no-overlap rejection at unit tier only, still not through the tier10 conformance harness this finding targets.

This is a single negative-path edge on an already-covered surface, so the risk is low, but the breaking-change guarantee for the adapter protocol is not pinned by a conformance assertion.

- **Suggested test:** Add a negative case to tests/tier10_conformance covering an adapter that advertises an incompatible major protocol version at INIT and asserting the gateway refuses the session with the documented error, run via cmd/lenny-compliance.

### - [ ] T-15.5.9 — §15.5 is classified non-normative in spec-map-exceptions despite multiple MUST and MUST NOT clauses [Info] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "section: \"15.5\"; reason: non-normative; justification: API-versioning and stability policy; the schemaVersion mechanism it cites is verified under §14 and §11.2.1." (tests/spec-map-exceptions.yaml:87-89)
- **Existing tests:** The exception delegates §15.5 coverage to §14 (workspace-plan schema) and §11.2.1 (billing event stream). Those sections cover the workspace-plan reject path (`pkg/workspaceplan/plan_test.go`) and the billing schemaVersion write (`tests/tier2_component/stores/billingstore_test.go`), but neither covers the durable forward-read MUST, the 90-day SLA, the conversion-webhook ordering, the deprecation header, or the annotation non-conflation rule that are normative inside §15.5 itself.
- **Gap:** The non-normative classification is inaccurate. §15.5 contains explicit MUST clauses (durable forward-read, preserve unknown fields, emit `durable_schema_version_ahead`, upgrade within 90 days, deploy the conversion webhook before adding a served version) and MUST NOT clauses (do not silently discard, do not conflate annotations). Treating the subsection as a policy pointer suppresses the tier2-and-above requirements catalogued in T-15.5.1 through T-15.5.7. This is recorded as Info because it is a classification observation rather than a missing test, but it is the root cause of the empty spec-map entry in T-15.5.4.
- **Dependencies:** None — buildable today. The fix is to reclassify §15.5 as normative (or to split the exception so only the introductory paragraph is non-normative) and to attribute the existing and proposed F-15.5 tests to it.
- **Suggested test:** No runtime test; update tests/spec-map-exceptions.yaml to remove or narrow the §15.5 non-normative exception and link the durable-consumer and conversion-webhook requirements to the tests proposed in T-15.5.1 and T-15.5.3.

### - [ ] T-15.5.10 — Stability-tier semantics (stable/beta/alpha) and the "breaking change" definition have no enforcement test [Info] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Stability tiers: `stable` ... `beta`: May change between minor releases with deprecation notice. `alpha`: May change without notice." and "Definition of \"breaking change\": Removing a field, changing a field's type, changing the default behavior ... removing an endpoint/tool, or changing error codes for existing operations." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2453-2458)
- **Existing tests:** No test found. A grep across the test tiers for stability-tier enforcement or a breaking-change diff gate returned only the deprecation-header and schemaVersion tests already catalogued above.
- **Gap:** These two items are governance definitions rather than runtime behaviors, so they are not directly testable as a user journey. A useful guard would be a tier0 static check that diffs the published OpenAPI document and the MCP tool schemas against the previous release and fails when a field is removed, a type changes, or an error code changes without a version bump. The absence of such a gate is an observation; the breaking-change policy is enforced today only by review.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a stored previous-release OpenAPI snapshot and tool-schema snapshot in tests/testdata and a schema-diff helper. The snapshots and the diff helper do not exist yet.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier0_static/api_breaking_change_diff_test.go that compares the current `pkg/gateway/openapi` document and MCP tool schemas against a checked-in previous-release snapshot and fails on a removed field, changed type, or changed error code absent a version bump.

## §15.6 Client SDKs <a id="t-15.6"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/15_external-api-surface.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The client SDKs have a single tier of coverage: the tier3 contract suite under `tests/tier3_contract/sdks/` drives the Go, Python, and TypeScript SDKs against an in-process `sessionserver` backed by `memstore`. That suite exercises wire-format round-trips, a single-connection streaming reconnect, webhook signature verification, tenant propagation, idempotency, the error envelope for three codes, pagination, the MCP create/send path, and cross-language equivalence. Since the 2026-06-03 audit, the Go SDK gained real `UploadArchive`/`UploadFile`/`FinalizeWorkspace` methods with tier1 unit coverage (`sdks/client/go/lenny/upload.go`, `upload_test.go`, landed in `9fb5e241` for F-24.17.4/F-26.2.4), but the tier3 contract file upload test remains an unmodified no-op placeholder that still asserts the SDK "has no upload helper yet" — a claim that itself is now stale — and the Python and TypeScript SDKs still have no upload surface at all. The compatibility matrix is still a no-op placeholder, retry-with-backoff is still excluded from the contract by design and covered only by tier1 unit tests, and the SDK authentication surface (OIDC bearer, API key, token refresh) is never exercised against an auth-enforcing gateway. No tier4 compose, tier5 Kind, or tier6 cloud SDK test exists as such, although a tier4 CLI smoke test (`tests/tier4_integration/embedded_mode_smoke_test.go`) now drives the Go SDK's MCP `create_session` path indirectly through `pkg/embedded/localcli`, and `pkg/ctlcli/install_smoke.go` drives it through the install-wizard smoke phase; neither exercises the SDK as a first-class subject (no assertions target SDK behavior, no other language, no OpenAPI operation matrix), so TESTING.md §14.13's declared tier4/5/6 cadence and publication smoke tests remain unimplemented. A spec-versus-implementation inconsistency persists: §15.6 names only Go and TypeScript as v1 client SDKs while a Python client SDK, its test, and its spec-map entry are present.
Counts: 4 High, 6 Medium, 1 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-15.6.1 — File upload (multipart, archive, gitClone, progress, resumable) is unimplemented and the only test is a no-op placeholder [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "SDKs encapsulate session lifecycle management, MCP streaming with automatic reconnect-with-cursor, file upload multipart handling, webhook signature verification, and error handling with retries" (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2489). TESTING.md §14.13 item 3: "File upload. Multipart upload, tar/tar.gz/zip archive upload via `uploadArchive`, gitClone source materialization. Progress callbacks fire monotonically. Resumable upload (if supported by the language client) survives a connection drop." (TESTING.md:1983)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier3_contract/sdks/go_client_test.go:425` still defines `TestGoClientFileUpload` with a body that is a single `t.Logf("non-skip — documented follow-on: §15.6 Go client file upload — sdks/client/go has no upload helper ...")` (go_client_test.go:426) and asserts nothing; this claim is now inaccurate. `9fb5e241` ("F-24.17.4/F-26.2.4: workspace upload binding") added real `UploadArchive`, `UploadFile`, and `FinalizeWorkspace` methods to the Go SDK (`sdks/client/go/lenny/upload.go:61`, `:89`, `:120`) with tier1 unit tests (`sdks/client/go/lenny/upload_test.go`: `TestUploadArchivePostsRawBodyWithToken`, `TestUploadFileTargetsPlainUpload`, `TestUploadArchiveRejectsMissingInputs`, `TestUploadArchiveSurfacesAPIError`, `TestFinalizeWorkspacePostsPlan`, `TestFinalizeWorkspaceNilPlanIsNoBody`). No `gitClone` helper, progress-callback hook, or resumable-upload path exists in any SDK. The Python and TypeScript contract files and SDK sources still contain no upload method or upload test of any kind.
- **Gap:** The tier1 unit tests confirm the Go SDK's upload request construction (raw body plus `X-Lenny-Upload-Token`/`X-Lenny-Content-Hash` headers, error decoding) but do not touch the tier3 contract or tier4 integration surface this finding targets: no test drives `UploadArchive`/`FinalizeWorkspace` against a real gateway and asserts the `/workspace` materialization round trip, no test exists for Python or TypeScript at any tier, and `gitClone`, progress callbacks, and resumable upload remain wholly untested (and, for `gitClone` and resumable upload, unimplemented in the SDK surface) in every language. The missing test is a real user journey (alice uploads a workspace archive through the SDK, the gateway materializes it into `/workspace`, the seal-and-export checkpoint is uploaded back) and an adversarial/failure scenario (a connection drop mid-upload, a malformed archive, a stale `uploadToken`). Target tiers are tier3 contract for the multipart and archive request format and tier4 integration for the materialization round trip.
- **Dependencies:** The Go upload helper now exists; the tier3 contract test needs only to be rewritten against it. Python and TypeScript still need the upload helper built before a test can drive it. The tier4 round trip needs the compose stack and an artifact store (MinIO) from `tests/testinfra/stubs` or the compose profile.
- **Suggested test:** Replace the `TestGoClientFileUpload` placeholder in `tests/tier3_contract/sdks/go_client_test.go` with a case driving `UploadArchive`/`FinalizeWorkspace` against the in-process gateway and asserting the returned `uploadRef` binds at finalize; add the equivalent upload helper and contract test to the Python and TypeScript SDKs; add a tier4 case in `tests/tier4_integration/sdk_upload_test.go` that uploads a tar.gz, asserts monotonic progress callbacks, and forces a mid-upload disconnect to verify resumable behavior, using the compose artifact store.

### - [ ] T-15.6.2 — SDK authentication (OIDC bearer, API key, token refresh) is never exercised against an auth-enforcing gateway [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "SDKs encapsulate ... error handling with retries — logic that is complex and error-prone to re-implement from the protocol specs alone." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2489). TESTING.md §14.13 item 5: "Authentication. OIDC bearer, service-account token, API key (per the chosen mode). Token refresh before expiry. Multi-tenant context (`tenant_id` claim) honored." (TESTING.md:1985)
- **Existing tests:** `TestGoClientAuthentication` (go_client_test.go:495), `TestTypeScriptClientAuthentication` (typescript_client_test.go:624), and `TestPythonClientAuthentication` (python_client_test.go:390) assert only that the `LENNY_TENANT_ID=acme` env value propagates to the gateway as a tenant stamp. The in-process `newGateway` (go_client_test.go:129) enforces no authentication. The SDK implements `BearerToken`, `APIKey`, and `RefreshingToken` (`sdks/client/go/lenny/auth.go:32`, `:49`, `:79`), none of which the contract suite drives. No SDK test references `BearerToken`, `RefreshingToken`, RFC 9068 scopes, OIDC, or PKCE; searched tiers 3 through 6.
- **Gap:** The credential-attachment and token-refresh logic is unverified end to end. The bearer and API-key authenticators are never asserted to set the `Authorization` or `X-Lenny-API-Key` header against a gateway that rejects an unauthenticated or expired request, and the token-refresh-before-expiry hook is never driven. The missing work is a real user journey (alice's SDK presents a valid OIDC bearer token and is admitted, refreshes it before expiry, and continues) and an adversarial scenario (a missing, malformed, expired, or wrong-scope token is rejected). Target tiers are tier3 contract for header attachment and tier4 integration for token-refresh against the real auth middleware.
- **Dependencies:** Requires an auth-enforcing gateway fixture and a token minter. `tests/testinfra/tokenservice` and `tests/testinfra/gateway` provide these building blocks; a clock-stepping fixture (`tests/testinfra/clockstep` or `timectl`) is needed to drive token expiry deterministically.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/sdks/auth_test.go` asserting each SDK attaches the bearer and API-key headers and that a missing or expired credential yields the documented `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED` envelope, plus a tier4 case in `tests/tier4_integration/sdk_token_refresh_test.go` that uses `tokenservice` and `clockstep` to verify `RefreshingToken` fetches a new token before expiry against the real JWT/RFC 9068 middleware.

## §15.7 Runtime Author SDKs <a id="t-15.7"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/15_external-api-surface.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The runtime-author SDKs have genuine protocol coverage at the contract tier: `tests/tier3_contract/sdks/runtime_sdk_test.go` runs `cmd/lenny-compliance` against SDK-built example runtimes (echo at Basic, delegate at Standard, lifecycle at Full) for Go, Python, and TypeScript, and the tier10 conformance suite re-runs the batteries against the bundled reference runtimes. Coverage stops there. The runtime-author SDK is exercised in no tier4 integration, tier5 Kind, tier6 cloud, tier8 chaos, or tier9 security suite, so every SDK capability that depends on a real pod (manifest-nonce handshake under `SO_PEERCRED`, credential rotation against the live leasing service, abstract-Unix-socket dialing under default-deny NetworkPolicy) is verified only against in-process fakes. Several capabilities the spec attributes to the SDKs have no automated assertion at all: the workspace materialization and checkpoint-upload helpers, the Prometheus/OpenTelemetry telemetry surface, and the `runtime-sdk testserver` test double are stubbed in the contract suite as `t.Logf` follow-ons or are absent from disk. The declared scaffold-to-running-session quick-start journey (`make image`, `lenny runtime publish`, session creation against the new runtime) is asserted only through offline file checks, and the SDK-version-negotiation guarantee is untested. Counts: 4 High, 5 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-15.7.1 — Runtime-author quick-start is never exercised as a running scaffold-to-session journey [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Third-party runtimes get the same code path at release time: `lenny runtime init <name>` produces a repository identical in structure to the first-party reference runtimes." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2706) and "Runtime author quick-start works: `lenny runtime init my-agent --language go --template coding`, `make image`, `lenny runtime publish` (against a local mock registry), session creation against the new runtime." (TESTING.md:2101)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier11_docs/time_to_hello_world_test.go::TestRuntimeAuthorQuickStart` runs `lenny runtime init` and `lenny runtime validate`, but its `make_image` subtest only greps the Makefile for a `docker build` line and logs when Docker is absent, its `publish_to_local_registry` subtest substitutes `runtime validate` for the actual publish, and its `session_against_new_runtime` subtest only asserts that `lenny session new` rejects a missing `--runtime` flag. No test builds the scaffolded image, pushes it, registers the runtime, and runs a session against it.
- **Gap:** The end-to-end runtime-author journey that the spec and TESTING.md §16 item 9 promise is unverified; a scaffolded SDK runtime could fail to build, fail to register, or fail to serve a session and every existing check would still pass. The work is a real user journey (the persona alice scaffolds a runtime, builds the image, publishes it, and runs a session) that belongs at tier5 on Kind. Target tiers: tier5 e2e (and a tier4 variant against the compose stack with a local registry).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`), a Docker or buildkit builder for the `make image` step, a local OCI registry, and `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver` to run the session. The registry-on-Kind fixture is the missing infrastructure; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/runtime_author_quickstart_test.go` that runs `lenny runtime init alice-agent --language go --template coding`, executes `make image`, pushes to an in-cluster registry, runs `lenny runtime publish`, then drives a session against `alice-agent` via `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver` and asserts a non-empty response.

### - [ ] T-15.7.2 — "Every reference runtime is built on the SDK" claim is unverified; conformance runs against non-SDK bundled runtimes [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Every reference runtime in [§26] — `claude-code`, `gemini-cli`, `codex`, `cursor-cli`, `chat`, `langgraph`, `mastra`, `openai-assistants`, `crewai` — is built on top of the Runtime Author SDKs above, using the scaffolder output as the starting point." (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2706)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier10_conformance/scaffolds_test.go` builds and conformance-tests `cmd/runtimes/echo`, `cmd/runtimes/streaming-echo`, and `cmd/runtimes/delegation-echo`, which are hand-written test runtimes rather than SDK-scaffolded reference runtimes. `TestReferenceCatalogNightly` asserts only the catalog manifest (name, level) and skips the image-pull half unless `LENNY_REFERENCE_IMAGE_REGISTRY` is set. The tier3 SDK suite runs the SDK example runtimes (`sdks/runtime/go/example/*`), not the §26 reference runtimes.
- **Gap:** No test asserts that any of the nine §26 reference runtimes actually imports the runtime-author SDK or passes conformance as an SDK-built artifact, so the central structural claim of §15.7 is unchecked. The work is both a structural conformance check (each §26 runtime image links the SDK and clears its declared level) and a deployment-combination gap (SDK-built runtime versus the test runtimes that stand in for it today). Target tiers: tier10 conformance, with the image-pull path wired in.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the §26 reference-runtime OCI images published to a reachable registry (the `github.com/lennylabs/runtime-templates` deliverable) and the image-driven mode of `lenny-test conformance --image`. The published images and the image runner are the missing infrastructure.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `tests/tier10_conformance/scaffolds_test.go` with a nightly case that pulls each §26 image, runs `lenny-compliance --image` at the runtime's declared level, and asserts the image manifest or a build-provenance label records the runtime-author SDK dependency.

### - [ ] T-15.7.3 — SDK conformance is never run in a real pod (Kind or cloud) against live sockets, NetworkPolicy, and the leasing service [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Pre-release: SDK conformance against the production-grade chart on Tier 5 (Kind) and Tier 6 (cloud)" (TESTING.md:2028) and "Intra-pod authentication. The manifest-nonce handshake described in [§15.4.3] ... paired with the adapter-side `SO_PEERCRED` UID check" (spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2525)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier3_contract/sdks/runtime_sdk_test.go` runs the Standard and Full batteries entirely in-process: `cmd/lenny-compliance/standard.go` and `full.go` open a fake socket and write a synthetic manifest. No tier5 or tier6 suite references `sdks/runtime` (grep across `tests/tier5_e2e_kind` and `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud` returns zero files), so the SDK never dials a real `@lenny-platform-mcp` or `@lenny-lifecycle` socket inside a pod, never passes the `SO_PEERCRED` UID check enforced by the real adapter, and never runs under the default-deny NetworkPolicy.
- **Gap:** The intra-pod handshake and socket-dialing behavior is the security-relevant integration the SDK exists to encapsulate, and it is verified only against fakes. The pre-release cadence that TESTING.md declares (tier5 and tier6) has no implementation. The work is a real user journey (an SDK runtime starting inside a sandboxed pod and completing the nonce handshake) and a deployment-combination gap across isolation profiles and topologies. Target tiers: tier5 e2e on Kind and tier6 e2e on cloud.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`), the production-grade Helm chart, a registered SDK-built runtime image, and `tests/testinfra/gateway` to assert the adapter-side handshake. The SDK runtime image fixture is the missing piece.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/runtime_sdk_pod_handshake_test.go` that deploys an SDK-built Standard-level runtime, runs a session, and asserts via the audit log and gateway metrics that the nonce handshake and `SO_PEERCRED` check succeeded inside the real pod under NetworkPolicy.

(spec/15_external-api-surface.md:2531) and "Workspace helpers. `read_file`, `write_file`, `list_dir`, `delete_file` confined to `/workspace/current` and `/workspace/output`. Path traversal blocked." (TESTING.md:1998)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier3_contract/sdks/runtime_sdk_test.go::TestRuntimeSDKWorkspaceHelpers` is a non-skip `t.Logf` placeholder that states `cmd/lenny-compliance` has no path-traversal corpus and defers to the SDK unit tests. No tier2/tier4/tier5 test drives the workspace helpers against a real `/workspace` mount, and no test asserts that the checkpoint-upload helper produces a sealed artifact through the §7.1 seal-and-export path.

The path-traversal confinement is an adversarial security control (a runtime author attempts to escape `/workspace/current` to read `/run/lenny/credentials.json`) with no negative-path test. The checkpoint-upload helper has no integration test that confirms the artifact reaches the store. Target tiers: tier9 security for the path-traversal corpus and tier4 integration for the checkpoint upload.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a path-traversal corpus in `tests/testinfra/stubs/runtime` or the conformance harness, a real `/workspace` mount fixture, and the artifact store (`tests/testinfra` MinIO) for the checkpoint half. The adversarial-path corpus is the missing infrastructure.
