## §16.1 Metrics <a id="t-16.1"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/16_observability.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§16.1 defines the platform metric catalog and §16.1.1 defines the attribute-naming rules, including the MUST-NOT-as-label high-cardinality denylist and the OTel-to-Prometheus mapping. Existing coverage is concentrated at tier0/tier1: `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog_test.go` checks the catalog for name and type completeness against the §16.1 table, and `pkg/observability/metrics/metrics_test.go` checks the `Validate` function against the forbidden-label list in isolation. The catalog records only name, type, and help, so no test verifies that each metric carries the labels the spec mandates or excludes the labels it forbids, and the spec-named CI enforcer `pkg/metrics/lint` does not exist. The only tier2-and-above coverage claimed in spec-map.json is a name/type cross-check that is effectively static plus a tier6 OTLP test that passes vacuously when no gateway pod or OTLP endpoint is present, so the OTel semantic-convention mapping, the repo-wide label-hygiene CI gate, runtime metric emission under real backing services, and failure-path metric emission under chaos are all unverified at component tier or higher.
Counts: 3 High, 4 Medium, 1 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-16.1.1 — The §16.1.1 forbidden-label CI gate is not enforced repo-wide; six production packages register metrics through raw Prometheus constructors that bypass the validator [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`session_id`, `operation_id`, `root_session_id`, `credential_id`, `user_id`, `lease_id`, and `request_id` ... MUST NOT be used as Prometheus metric labels. ... Any new metric introduced by a PR that includes one of these attributes as a label is a CI failure (enforced by the `pkg/metrics/lint` validator that scans metric registrations for label-name membership in a denylist)." (spec/16_observability.md:309)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/observability/metrics/metrics_test.go::TestValidateRejectsForbiddenLabels` and `TestForbiddenLabelsCatalog` exercise the `Validate` function and the `ForbiddenLabels` slice in isolation (tier1 unit). The spec-named package `pkg/metrics/lint` does not exist on disk (verified by `find`/`ls`); the validator lives at `pkg/observability/metrics` and is opt-in through the `NewCounter`/`NewGauge`/`NewHistogram` wrappers. The gateway metrics package that hosted the raw registrations at generation time has since moved to `pkg/gateway/metrics/gatewaymetrics` (was `pkg/gateway/gatewaymetrics`); most files in the new location have migrated to the validated wrappers, but `gatewaymetrics_audit.go`, `gatewaymetrics_orphan.go`, `gatewaymetrics_quota.go`, and `gatewaymetrics_retention.go` still register metrics through raw `prometheus.New{Counter,CounterVec,Histogram}` calls (unlabeled or non-forbidden labels today, but unchecked against the denylist by construction). The remaining five bypass sites are unchanged: `pkg/alerting/alertingmetrics/alertingmetrics.go`, `pkg/loadctl/metrics.go`, `pkg/ops/metrics/querymetrics.go`, `cmd/lenny-ops/locks.go`, and `cmd/lenny-ops/gatewayclient.go` all still call raw `prometheus.New*` constructors directly. No tier0 static test scans the repository's metric registrations for denylisted label names; `tests/tier0_static/` still contains no label-hygiene check (verified: no `label`/`forbidden`/`metriclabel` file under that tree).
- **Gap:** The normative MUST-NOT rule has no enforcement that covers all metric registrations. A regression that adds `user_id` or `session_id` as a label on any metric declared through the raw constructors ships without a test failing, contradicting the spec's "CI failure" guarantee. The missing test is a tier0 static analyzer (a real CI gate) that parses every metric registration in `pkg/` and `cmd/` and asserts no label name is on the §16.1.1 denylist regardless of which constructor created it.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. A `go/ast` or `golang.org/x/tools/go/packages` walk over `pkg/**` and `cmd/**` finds `prometheus.New*Vec` and `*.NewCounter`/`NewGauge`/`NewHistogram` calls and inspects the label string-slice literal argument.
- **Suggested test:** Add tier0 `tests/tier0_static/metriclabels/forbidden_labels_test.go` that walks all non-test Go packages, extracts the label-name literals passed to every Prometheus metric registration, and fails when any equals an entry in the §16.1.1 denylist; seed it from `pkg/observability/metrics.ForbiddenLabels` so the list cannot drift.

### - [ ] T-16.1.2 — No component/integration test verifies §16.1 metrics are actually emitted at runtime with their spec-mandated labels [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Token usage (`lenny_tokens_consumed_total`, counter labeled by `tenant_id`, `runtime_class` ... `user_id` is intentionally excluded because it is on the forbidden-label list)" and the full §16.1 table of metric definitions with mandated labels. (spec/16_observability.md:23, table spec/16_observability.md:6-282)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog_test.go::TestMetricCatalogIsCompleteAgainstSpec161` and `TestMetricCatalogHasNoUnspecifiedMetrics` assert the catalog contains exactly the §16.1 metric names and valid types (the table has grown since generation — `lenny_warmpool_reserved_pods`, the split `lenny_gateway_pod_retirement_total`/`lenny_controller_pod_retirement_total` pair, `lenny_gateway_token_usage_anomaly_total`, `lenny_pool_security_degraded`, and the renamed `lenny_pod_session_reuse_count` are all present and asserted by name/type). `MetricSpec` still carries only `Name`, `Type`, and `Help` (verified in `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go`), so the catalog encodes no labels and the completeness check still cannot assert label sets. One genuine component-tier emission test has since landed: `tests/tier2_component/watchdog/expiry_counter_test.go::TestWatchdogSessionExpiryCounter_spec_16_1` drives a real Postgres-backed watchdog, scrapes the real Prometheus `/metrics` endpoint, and asserts `lenny_session_expiry_total{pool, reason}` is exported with the correct `max_idle_time`/`max_session_age` reason vocabulary — this is the first component-tier proof that a §16.1 metric is emitted end to end with its labels. It covers one metric family only. `tests/tier4_integration/gateway_full_e2e_test.go:171-179` still scrapes `/metrics` but asserts only `lenny_gateway_requests_total`, which is not a §16.1 catalogued metric. The new `lenny_gateway_token_usage_anomaly_total` metric is exercised close to production code by `tests/tier9_security/token_usage_anomaly_test.go` (drives the real detector, asserts the `{tenant_id, reason}` label set against a real registry) but that test builds its own local registry rather than scraping a running gateway's `/metrics` endpoint. No test claims a session, drives token usage, scrapes `/metrics`, and asserts `lenny_tokens_consumed_total{tenant_id, runtime_class}`, `lenny_session_creation_duration_seconds{phase}`, or `lenny_gateway_active_sessions{runtime, pool, state, tenant}` are present with their exact label keys; grep confirms no non-catalog file references `lenny_session_creation_duration_seconds` or `lenny_pod_state_transition_duration_seconds` at all, so those two histograms have no label-emitting code path yet, let alone a test for one.
- **Gap:** The core capability of §16.1, that a running gateway, controller, and token service expose the catalogued metric series with the documented labels, remains unverified above unit tier for the representative slice this finding names. No component test claims a session, drives token usage, scrapes `/metrics`, and asserts `lenny_tokens_consumed_total{tenant_id, runtime_class}` is present with those exact label keys and no forbidden label. This is a real user-journey gap (an operator scraping the gateway after alice runs a session) at tier2/tier4.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The compose `observability` profile (TESTING.md §11) provides Prometheus and the gateway; `tests/testinfra/scenkit` and `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver` drive a session.
- **Suggested test:** Add tier4 `tests/tier4_integration/metrics_emission_test.go` that drives a session through the gateway on the compose stack, scrapes `/metrics`, and asserts a representative slice of §16.1 series (`lenny_tokens_consumed_total`, `lenny_session_creation_duration_seconds`, `lenny_gateway_active_sessions`) are exported with exactly their spec-mandated label keys and with no denylisted label, using `tests/testinfra/scenkit` and `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`.

### - [ ] T-16.1.1.3 — No conformance test pins metric/attribute names against OpenTelemetry semantic conventions or the dot-to-underscore Prometheus mapping [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Metric labels and trace/log attributes follow the OpenTelemetry semantic conventions where a convention exists ... OTel dotted attribute names map to Prometheus labels by replacing dots with underscores (per OTel's Prometheus interop rules); both forms refer to the same attribute. This table is the single source of truth for attribute names ... A label/attribute must not appear anywhere in the spec unless it is in this table or documented as a local-only extension." (spec/16_observability.md:288-290, mapping table spec/16_observability.md:292-303)
- **Existing tests:** no test found. Searched tier1 (`pkg/observability/**`), tier2 (`tests/tier2_component/observability/`), tier3 (`tests/tier3_contract/`), and tier10 (`tests/tier10_conformance/`). The `tests/tier2_component/observability/integration_test.go` asserts span/log correlation attributes (`tenant_id`, `runtime_class`, `pool`) but does not assert the OTel dotted form (`k8s.pod.name`, `service.instance.id`) maps to the Prometheus underscore form. The `tests/testinfra/mocks/otelcollector` mock records spans only and has no metric receiver (verified: `otelcollector.go` exposes `Spans()` and no metric API). `tests/tier10_conformance/` still contains nothing for metrics, OTLP, or semantic conventions.
- **Gap:** §16.1.1 touches an external standard (OpenTelemetry semantic conventions and the OTel Prometheus interop mapping). The spec's requirement that, for example, OTel `k8s.pod.name` and Prometheus `k8s_pod_name` denote the same attribute, and that no label appears anywhere outside the §16.1.1 single-source-of-truth table, has no conformance test pinning emitted attribute names against the external convention. This is a standards-conformance gap at tier10.
- **Dependencies:** Requires an OTLP metric-receiving stub. The existing `tests/testinfra/mocks/otelcollector` only records spans; extending it to capture exported OTLP metrics (or adding an OTLP metric collector under `tests/testinfra/mocks`) is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tier10 `tests/tier10_conformance/observability/semconv_attribute_test.go` that exports a representative metric and span through the OTLP exporter, captures them at the metric-receiving stub, and asserts each resource/label attribute either matches its OTel semantic-convention name with the documented dot-to-underscore mapping or is a §16.1.1-table Lenny-specific name, failing on any attribute absent from the table.

### - [ ] T-16.1.4 — The tier6 cloud observability test for OTLP delivery passes vacuously and never verifies a metric reaches the provider-native collector [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "OTLP delivery to provider-native collectors (Cloud Trace and Cloud Logging on GCP, X-Ray and CloudWatch on AWS, Application Insights and Log Analytics on AKS)" claimed for §16.1 in spec-map.json and "cloud_observability | OTLP delivery to the provider-native collector ..." in TESTING.md. (tests/spec-map.json:2283, TESTING.md:1119)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/cluster_assertions_test.go::TestCloudObservability` (now lines 416-443; spec-map.json's package/test list has drifted to cite a non-existent `scaffolds_test.go` for the same test name, but the function still lives in `cluster_assertions_test.go`) is the only tier6 test spec-map.json §16.1 lists. It lists gateway pods, and when none are running it logs `"no gateway pod running"` and returns, and when the pod has no `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` it logs a "to unblock" hint and returns. When the env var is present it logs the endpoint and returns without asserting anything. No path fails on missing delivery, and no path scrapes the provider-native collector to confirm a metric series arrived. Unchanged behaviorally since generation.
- **Gap:** The declared cloud-observability coverage is a soft no-op that asserts only an env var is set on one path and passes on every path. OTLP metric delivery to the provider-native collector on GKE/EKS/AKS is therefore unverified. ## §16.2 Key Latency Breakpoints <a id="t-16.2"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/16_observability.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
Section 16.2 requires instrumenting four per-session timestamps (pod claimed, workspace prep done, session ready, and first event/token emitted) so operators can decompose startup latency into pod allocation, file upload, session start, and runtime cost. The four breakpoints are realized on disk as `lenny_pod_claim_duration_seconds`, the `WorkspaceMaterialization` phase of `BindTimings` (now at `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/binder.go`), `lenny_session_startup_duration_seconds`, and `lenny_session_time_to_first_token_seconds`, and the emission logic is wired into `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go`. Coverage is unit-tier only for the four metrics as a set — `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/binder.go`, `pkg/gateway/sessionserver`, and `pkg/gateway/metrics/gatewaymetrics` (moved from `pkg/gateway/gatewaymetrics`) carry tests tagged §6.3 and §16.1 — but proposal 0006 has since landed a real load-tier consumer: `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go` (`TestStartupLatencyPodWarm`, `TestStartupLatencySDKWarm`) and `tests/tier12_load_cloud/session_startup_latency_test.go` now drive `POST /v1/sessions/start` against a real gateway and Kind/cloud cluster and scrape the `lenny_session_startup_duration_seconds` histogram from `/metrics`, replacing the echo-adapter process-start microbenchmark that T-16.2.4 flagged. No component, integration, or e2e test scrapes `/metrics` and asserts all four breakpoint series together with `pool`/`runtime_class`/`isolation_profile` labels, and the load scenarios that decompose latency into pod-claim vs. workspace-materialization vs. runtime attribution (as opposed to reading the single session-ready aggregate) still do not exist. The `tests/spec-map.json` entry for §16.2 still lists zero tests and marks the section deferred to Phase 14.5 even though the instrumentation and a real load-tier consumer both ship.
Counts: 1 High, 2 Medium, 1 Low, 1 Info. (1 Medium resolved this pass.)

### Findings

### - [ ] T-16.2.1 — The four latency-breakpoint metrics are never asserted to emit through a real session at component tier or above [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Instrument four timestamps per session: 1. Pod claimed 2. Workspace prep done 3. Session ready 4. First event/token emitted" (spec/16_observability.md:313-318)
- **Existing tests:** Unit-tier only for the four-breakpoint set. `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/binder.go` (moved from `pkg/gateway/podsession/binder.go`) populates `BindTimings{PodClaim, WorkspaceMaterialization, ..., AgentSessionStart}`. `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/startupmetrics_internal_test.go::TestRecordStartupPhases_spec_6_3` and siblings (renamed from `TestRecordStartupMetrics_spec_6_3`) exercise the per-phase observation against in-memory callbacks. `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/ttft_test.go::TestMessagesObservesTTFTOnFirstResponse_spec_6_3_F_6_3_3` covers the first-token observation against `memstore`. `pkg/gateway/metrics/gatewaymetrics/gatewaymetrics_elicitation_test.go::TestSessionStartupMetricsExposed_spec_6_3` and `TestSessionTimeToFirstTokenExposed_spec_6_3_F_6_3_3` (moved from the single `pkg/gateway/gatewaymetrics/gatewaymetrics_test.go`, which no longer exists as that package was split into `pkg/gateway/metrics/gatewaymetrics`) scrape the Prometheus text exposition for `lenny_session_startup_duration_seconds` and `lenny_session_time_to_first_token_seconds` against a hand-driven registry. All of these remain package-level unit tests (no `//go:build component` tag). Since generation, proposal 0006 (commit 766f1f5f) landed `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go::TestStartupLatencyPodWarm` / `TestStartupLatencySDKWarm` and `tests/tier12_load_cloud/session_startup_latency_test.go`, which drive real `POST /v1/sessions/start` calls against a Kind or cloud gateway and scrape `lenny_session_startup_duration_seconds` via `tests/testinfra/load/startup_histogram.go` — the first real-session, real-cluster consumer of one of the four breakpoints. No test anywhere reads `lenny_pod_claim_duration_seconds` or the workspace-materialization phase of `lenny_session_creation_duration_seconds`, and no test above unit reads `lenny_session_time_to_first_token_seconds` (verified by grep across tests/tier2_component, tests/tier3_contract, tests/tier4_integration, tests/tier5_e2e_kind, tests/tier6_e2e_cloud, tests/tier7a_load_local, tests/tier7b_load_kind, and tests/tier12_load_cloud).
- **Gap:** No component-or-higher test drives `POST /v1/sessions` plus `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/messages` against a real gateway with real backing stores and then scrapes `/metrics` to assert that all four breakpoint series are present with non-zero observation counts and the documented `pool` / `runtime_class` / `isolation_profile` labels, in one flow. The tier7b/tier12 tests added under proposal 0006 close part of this gap for the session-ready aggregate at load tier, but they read only `lenny_session_startup_duration_seconds`, they run at tier7b/tier12 (load) rather than component or integration tier, and they do not touch `lenny_pod_claim_duration_seconds`, the workspace-materialization phase, or `lenny_session_time_to_first_token_seconds`. This is the core capability of the section (operators decomposing startup latency) and it is unverified end to end below the load tier. The work is a real user journey: an operator inspecting the latency breakdown for a session alice started. Target tier: tier2 component against the compose stack, promoted to tier4 for the full gateway-plus-controller flow.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. Use the compose observability profile (tests/testinfra/compose, `--profile observability`), tests/testinfra/sessiondriver to create a session and send a first message, and tests/testinfra/gateway plus a Prometheus text-format scrape against the gateway `/metrics` endpoint.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/latency_breakpoints_test.go that starts a session through sessiondriver, sends one prompt, scrapes `/metrics`, and asserts `lenny_pod_claim_duration_seconds`, `lenny_session_startup_duration_seconds`, and `lenny_session_time_to_first_token_seconds` each recorded one observation with matching `pool`/`runtime_class`/`isolation_profile` labels, plus that the per-phase `lenny_session_creation_duration_seconds{phase="pod_claim"}` and the workspace-materialization phase are recorded.

### - [ ] T-16.2.2 — spec-map.json marks §16.2 deferred with zero tests although the instrumentation already ships and is wired into the gateway [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Instrument four timestamps per session" (spec/16_observability.md:313); the §16.1 metric table binds each breakpoint to a concrete metric, e.g. `lenny_pod_claim_duration_seconds` is "a subcomponent of end-to-end session creation latency used for diagnosing pod-allocation bottlenecks per §16.2" (spec/16_observability.md:19).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/spec-map.json:2285-2292` still records `"16.2"` with `"tests": []`, `"packages": []`, and `"blocked_until_phase": "14.5"`, with the note that "Phase 14.5 lands the production baseline and the SLO package; the packages list is intentionally empty until then." `tests/spec-map-exceptions.yaml:90-92` repeats the deferral: "Per-session latency-breakpoint instrumentation is added in Wave 7 (Phase 14.5)." The instrumentation is present on disk now: `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podsession/binder.go` defines `BindTimings`, `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/start.go` records the startup phases, and `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` wires `ObserveTimeToFirstToken: gwMetrics.ObserveSessionTimeToFirstToken`. Since generation, proposal 0006 also landed a real load-tier consumer (`tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go`, `tests/tier12_load_cloud/session_startup_latency_test.go`) that neither map file references.

A regression that silently stops emitting one of the four breakpoint series would not be caught, and the stale deferral hides the absence of the component-level test in T-16.2.1 and the existence of the tier7b/tier12 load-tier test. This is a spec-versus-test inconsistency that would let a regression ship. The fix is to land T-16.2.1, then replace the empty `tests`/`packages` arrays with the real test pointers (including the already-landed tier7b/tier12 scenario) and remove or re-scope the deferral.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. Requires the test from T-16.2.1 to populate the map entry fully; the tier7b/tier12 pointers can be added immediately.
- **Suggested test:** After adding tests/tier4_integration/latency_breakpoints_test.go (T-16.2.1), update `tests/spec-map.json` §16.2 to list it plus the gatewaymetrics, podlifecycle/podsession, and tier7b_load_kind/tier12_load_cloud packages, and either remove the `16.2` entry from tests/spec-map-exceptions.yaml or change its reason from `deferred` to a coverage pointer; add a tier0 assertion in tests/tier0_static that the §16.2 map entry is non-empty.

### - [ ] T-16.2.3 — Load scenarios measure wire-level request latency, not the breakpoint decomposition the section exists to provide [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "This lets operators identify whether bottlenecks are in pod allocation, file upload, session start, or the agent runtime itself." (spec/16_observability.md:320)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/pod_claim_latency/main.js:44` asserts `http_req_duration{name:claim_pod} p(99)<100`, and `tests/tier12_load_cloud/scenarios/session_pod_claim/main.js` and `tests/tier12_load_cloud/scenarios/session_streaming_throughput/main.js:33` assert `http_req_duration` percentiles. This is real progress: it is the first load scenario to read a breakpoint histogram rather than only `http_req_duration`. `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/gateway_capacity_calibration/main.js:123` still confirms the general pattern for the remaining scenarios: the in-replica metric "must be scraped from /metrics out-of-band," which no harness besides `startup_latency` does.
- **Gap:** The four breakpoints exist so an operator can attribute a slow start to one of pod allocation, upload, session start, or runtime, but the newly landed scrape only reads the single `lenny_session_startup_duration_seconds` aggregate; no load or SLO test scrapes the per-phase histograms (`lenny_pod_claim_duration_seconds`, the workspace-materialization phase, or `lenny_session_time_to_first_token_seconds`) to verify the decomposition is correct — for example, that a deliberately slow upload shows up under workspace materialization and not under pod claim. The diagnostic value is the SHOULD-level behavior of the section and it is exercised in zero combinations that vary upload size or isolate the phases from each other. This is a deployment-combination and capability gap rather than a pure user journey.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today for the scrape harness; `tests/testinfra/load/startup_histogram.go` (landed by proposal 0006) already exposes the scrape-and-P95-delta primitive the new scenario needs to extend. The gVisor pod-warm arm on Kind and the Phase 2 exit-gate ADR benchmark are carried forward as follow-up in the same commit message, tracked separately from this finding's README-accuracy concern.

### - [ ] T-16.2.5 — The first-token breakpoint observation fires on the in-process echo executor only, never across a real adapter or a non-REST client surface [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "4. First event/token emitted" (spec/16_observability.md:318); §16.1 binds it to `lenny_session_time_to_first_token_seconds`, "wall-clock time from session start request to first streaming event emitted to the client" (spec/16_observability.md:17).

Since generation, `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go` and `tests/tier12_load_cloud/session_startup_latency_test.go` (proposal 0006) added real-session load-tier coverage for `lenny_session_startup_duration_seconds`, but neither scrapes or asserts on `lenny_session_time_to_first_token_seconds`, so the first-token breakpoint's cross-surface coverage is unchanged.

A path that emits the first agent event without routing through the REST `response` frame would not observe the histogram, and that negative case is untested above unit. Target tier: tier4 (compose) for the streaming-echo adapter path, with one tier3 contract case per non-REST surface confirming the first streamed token still triggers the observation.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. Use the streaming-echo runtime under tests/testinfra/runtimes and tests/testinfra/sdkhelper for the OpenAI surfaces; scrape the gateway `/metrics`.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier4 case to tests/tier4_integration that starts a streaming-echo session, opens the SSE stream, and asserts `lenny_session_time_to_first_token_seconds` records exactly one observation; add a tier3 contract assertion that the same observation fires when the first token is delivered over the OpenAI Chat Completions streaming surface.

## §16.3 Distributed Tracing <a id="t-16.3"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/16_observability.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§16.3's spec text is unchanged since generation (`git diff d9074016 HEAD -- spec/16_observability.md` shows the §16.3 body byte-identical; it only shifted down 6 lines because §16.1 gained a metric row earlier in the file). Production code moved dramatically, though: commit `51e44ff0` (BUILD-GAPS F-16.3.1/F-16.3.6) wired production emit sites for 21 of the 22 catalog spans across the gateway and the in-pod `lenny-adapter`, each with a dedicated per-package `tracetest.SpanRecorder` test covering the happy and error paths; `coordinator.handoff` remains the sole span with no call site, though the §10.1 handoff protocol it instruments (`pkg/gateway/coordination/coordfence`, `pkg/gateway/coordination/barrier`) has since been built, so the span is now buildable rather than blocked. `credential.assign`/`rotate`/`fallback_chain`/`proxy_request` are now opened as their own spans (not just attribute labels), and `delegation.budget_reserve`/`budget_return` carry all four mandated attributes, both verified by dedicated tests. What is still missing is unchanged in kind: no test propagates one trace id end to end through real running binaries (tier4/tier5), the tier-4 scaffold still misrepresents `tracingContext` coverage, tail-based sampling and cloud OTLP delivery are still unverified against a real collector or backend, no conformance test pins the W3C/OTLP wire format, and `tests/spec-map.json` §16.3 now under-reports coverage more severely than before given the dozens of new tests it does not list. A new gap surfaces from the emission work itself: no test checks a span's actual component locus against the spec table's "Component" column, and `session.claim_pod` is now a confirmed mismatch (documented "Controller", emitted gateway-side).
Counts: 5 High, 4 Medium, 2 Low, 2 Info.

### Findings

### - [x] T-16.3.1 — Most of the §16.3 span catalog is never emitted by any binary and has no emission test [High] — RESOLVED 51e44ff0
- **Resolution:** Commit `51e44ff0` (BUILD-GAPS F-16.3.1/F-16.3.6) wires production `tracer.Start` call sites for 21 of the 22 catalog spans: gateway-side `session.create` (`sessionserver.createSession`), `session.claim_pod` (`podclaim.Claimer.Claim`), `session.upload`, `session.prompt`, `session.seal_and_export` (`sessionserver`), `delegation.spawn_child` (`mcpfabric/delegation.Service.Delegate`), `delegation.await_child` + `mcp.elicitation` (`mcpfabric/mcptools`), `delegation.budget_reserve`/`budget_return` (`mcpfabric/delegationtree/treebudget`, with `outcome`/`tenant_id`/`root_session_id`/`lua_queue_wait_ms`), `mcp.external_tool_call` (`connectors/connectorinvoke`, fixing a nil-tracer default), `credential.assign` (`credentials/credassign`), `credential.rotate` (`credentials/credentialserver`), `credential.fallback_chain`/`credential.proxy_request` (`llmproxy`); pod-side (in `lenny-adapter`) `session.start`, `session.run_setup`, `session.finalize_workspace`, `session.tool_call` (per invocation), plus the pod halves of `session.upload` and `session.checkpoint`. Each has a dedicated per-package test using an SDK `tracetest.SpanRecorder` over the global provider, covering a happy path and an error path (for example `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/delegation/span_test.go::TestDelegateEmitsSpawnChildSpan_spec_16_3`, `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/delegationtree/treebudget/span_test.go::TestReserveEmitsBudgetReserveSpan_spec_16_3`, `pkg/gateway/credentials/credassign/span_test.go::TestAssignEmitsCredentialAssignSpan_spec_16_3`, `pkg/gateway/llmproxy/llmproxy/fallback_span_internal_test.go::TestDriveFallbackEmitsExhaustedSpan_spec_16_3`, `pkg/adapter/tracing_external_test.go` and `tracing_internal_test.go`). The one residual, `coordinator.handoff`, has no host call site because the §10.1 3-step handoff protocol was unimplemented at the time; that protocol has since landed (`pkg/gateway/coordination/coordfence`, `pkg/gateway/coordination/barrier`, BUILD-GAPS F-10.1.7/F-11.3.14, both CLOSED) with no tracing integration, so the residual is carried forward as T-16.3.8 rather than reopening this finding. The tier-2/tier-5 cross-binary and Kind-tree assertions this finding originally asked for were not built as named files; the per-package unit tests substantively close the "never emitted, no test" defect this finding raised.

### - [ ] T-16.3.2 — Tier-1 trace-context propagation chain has no integration or e2e test through real binaries [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Tier 1 trace context flows through: Client → Gateway (HTTP headers); Gateway → Pod (gRPC metadata); Pod → Gateway (delegation tool calls carry parent trace context); Gateway → Child Pod (inherited trace context); Gateway → External MCP tools (HTTP headers)" (spec/16_observability.md:330-336)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/middleware/correlation/tracing_propagation_test.go` checks the Client to Gateway HTTP hop with an `httptest` handler. `pkg/gateway/runtime/adapterclient/tracing_propagation_test.go::TestGRPCTraceContextPropagatesGatewayToPod_spec_16_3_327` checks the Gateway to Pod gRPC hop over a `bufconn` listener using the `otelgrpc` client/server stats handlers wired by BUILD-GAPS F-16.3.3 (commit `bc7b973a`). `pkg/gateway/connectors/connectorinvoke/tracing_propagation_test.go` checks the Gateway to External MCP HTTP hop with a fake `http.Doer`. All three remain in-process unit tests with locally installed propagators (paths moved under the 0020 mcpfabric/connectors reorganizations but the tests themselves are unchanged in scope). `pkg/adapter/gatewaycontrol/gatewaycontrol.go` now wires `otelgrpc.NewClientHandler` on the pod's dial to the gateway's `GatewayControl` server (per the F-16.3.3 resolution note), but no test exercises that Pod to Gateway hop specifically, and no test exercises the Gateway to Child Pod inherited-context hop. No tier-4 or tier-5 test propagates one trace id end to end across the compose stack or Kind so the whole delegation tree shares a root.
- **Gap:** The unit tests prove each propagator is wired in isolation, and the code-level wiring for all five documented hops now exists (it did not for two of them at generation time), but a single trace id surviving Client to Gateway to Pod to Child to a re-entrant delegation tool call is still never asserted against running binaries, and the Pod to Gateway and Gateway to Child Pod hops still have no dedicated test at any tier. The missing work is an integration test (tier4) that issues a request with a known `traceparent`, runs a delegation through the live gateway and a pod, collects spans from an OTLP collector, and asserts every span carries the inbound trace id. This is a real user journey for an operator debugging a delegation latency spike.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the OTLP-over-gRPC receiver deferred in TESTING.md §13.4 (the current `tests/testinfra/mocks/otelcollector` is an in-process recorder with no receiver, and `tests/testinfra/compose/compose.go::OTLPEndpoint` returns a fixed address with no OTel collector service in the compose stack backing it), plus the compose observability profile wired to a real collector. The receiver does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/trace_propagation_test.go` that starts the gateway via `tests/testinfra/gateway`, sets a fixed `traceparent` on a session-create request, drives a `delegate_task` through the platform MCP server, and asserts via the OTLP receiver that the gateway, pod, and child spans all share the inbound trace id.

### - [ ] T-16.3.3 — Tier-2 runtime `tracingContext` propagation has no end-to-end or conformance test across the delegation boundary [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Runtimes register tracing identifiers via `lenny/set_tracing_context` (MCP) or `set_tracing_context` (JSONL), and the gateway attaches them to child delegation leases automatically. Child runtimes receive the parent's `tracingContext` in the adapter manifest and use it to stitch their native traces into the parent's trace tree." (spec/16_observability.md:328)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/delegation/service_test.go::TestDelegatePropagatesTracingContext` asserts the child lease inherits the parent's `tracingContext` using fakes. `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/mcptools_test.go` covers the `lenny/set_tracing_context` tool (merge, sensitive-key rejection, URL rejection, oversize rejection, terminal-session rejection) at the handler level. `pkg/adapter/manifest_test.go::TestWriteManifestWithTracingContext` checks the manifest carries the context. BUILD-GAPS F-16.3.11 (verify-closed, Info) confirms the full code chain is wired end to end (`pkg/delegation/tracing/`, `mcptools.go:663`, `delegation/service.go:430 copyTracingContext`, `sessionserver/start.go:978/996/1563`, `adapterclient/client.go:76/95/334/385`, `adapter/manifest.go:116/251`), but that is a code-wiring confirmation, not a test. The tier-4 scaffold (`tests/tier4_integration/scaffolds_test.go:34-35`) still states the §8.3 `tracingContext` propagation is exercised in `delegation_test.go`; `tests/tier4_integration/delegation_test.go::TestDelegation` still asserts only tree node count and lineage and contains no `tracingContext` reference. `tests/tier3_contract/sdks/runtime_sdk_test.go:426-427` is still a non-skipping log recording that `cmd/lenny-compliance` has no OTel context-propagation check (confirmed: `cmd/lenny-compliance` has no telemetry- or tracing-named check file today).
- **Gap:** The full path (parent runtime sets `tracingContext` via the platform tool, gateway attaches it to the child lease, child reads it from the manifest) is fully wired in code but still never exercised end to end against running binaries, and the tier-4 scaffold claim is still inaccurate. There is also still no tier-10 conformance check that a runtime forwards its tracing identifiers through `delegate_task` to a child, which the §14 conformance domain lists as "Telemetry pass-through" (TESTING.md:2002 area). The missing work is both an integration user journey (an eval platform stitching a child runtime's trace into the parent) and a standards-style conformance check via `cmd/lenny-compliance`.
- **Dependencies:** Requires `delegation-echo` (a reference runtime that sets a `tracingContext`) and the live gateway from `tests/testinfra/gateway`. For the conformance arm, `cmd/lenny-compliance` needs a new check at the Full level; that check does not exist yet and is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add a `tracingContext` assertion to `tests/tier4_integration/delegation_test.go` (set a context on the parent, read it back from the child's manifest), correct the tier-4 scaffold claim, and add a Full-level check in `cmd/lenny-compliance/full.go` driven by `tests/tier3_contract/sdks/runtime_sdk_test.go::TestRuntimeSDKTelemetryPassThrough` asserting the child runtime receives the parent's `tracingContext`.

### - [ ] T-16.3.4 — Tail-based sampling behavior is unverified against a running Collector [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The gateway emits 100% of traces to the OpenTelemetry Collector; the Collector applies tail-based sampling ... 100% sampling is applied for errors (any span with error status), slow requests (session creation exceeding 500ms ...), and delegation trees (all spans in a tree are sampled if the root is sampled ...)." (spec/16_observability.md:365)
- **Existing tests:** `charts/lenny/tests/otel-collector_test.yaml` (now 8 helm-unittest cases, up from the original set, per BUILD-GAPS F-16.3.4 commit `5da00bd6`) asserts the rendered `templates/otel-collector.yaml` ConfigMap text contains the `tail_sampling` processor, the `threshold_ms: 500` latency policy, the `errors` policy, the `sampling_percentage` derived from `global.traceSamplingRate` (now defined in `values.yaml`, default `0.1`), the NET-046 `observability.otlpPodLabel`, and the gateway OTLP-endpoint fallback/override. `pkg/observability/tracing/provider.go` configures the gateway-side sampler as `ParentBased(AlwaysSample())` (100% head sampling), and `TestInitProviderInstallsSDKProviderAndPropagator_spec_16_3` confirms `InitProvider` installs a real SDK `TracerProvider` and W3C propagator, though no test directly asserts the sampler type. No test runs the rendered collector config against a real Collector and asserts an error trace is kept, a sub-500ms non-error trace is dropped at the configured rate, or a delegation tree is sampled as a unit.
- **Gap:** The chart helm-unittest pins the static config more thoroughly than before, but the runtime sampling decision (errors kept, slow kept, trees kept together, the rest probabilistic) is still never exercised against a live Collector. The missing work is a component-or-integration test that feeds spans through an actual OpenTelemetry Collector configured from the chart output and asserts the keep/drop decisions. This is both an operator user journey (an error trace must always be retained for debugging) and a failure-path assertion.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a real OpenTelemetry Collector container in the compose observability profile (`tests/testinfra/compose`) plus an OTLP receiver or backend stub to observe which traces were exported. The chart now ships an opt-in in-cluster collector (`tracing.collector.enabled`), but the compose stack still has no collector container (`compose.go::OTLPEndpoint` is a fixed address with nothing behind it); building the compose-side collector and backend stub is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/trace_sampling_test.go` that renders the chart collector config, runs it in a Collector container, emits one error span, one slow span, and a batch of fast non-error spans, and asserts the error and slow traces are always exported while the fast traces are sampled near `global.traceSamplingRate`.

- **Spec/Doc:** "The backend is deployer-configured — Jaeger, Tempo, Zipkin, or cloud-native options (Cloud Trace, X-Ray) are all supported." (spec/16_observability.md:365) and the §14 cloud suite "cloud_observability | OTLP delivery to the provider-native collector (Cloud Trace and Cloud Logging on GCP, X-Ray and CloudWatch on AWS, Application Insights and Log Analytics on Azure)" (TESTING.md:1119)

It still never emits a span or queries Cloud Trace, X-Ray, or Application Insights to confirm a trace was received. `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml` still contains no trace or OTLP entry.

The missing work is a per-provider e2e (tier6) that emits a known trace and reads it back from the provider-native trace backend, and a parity-matrix row recording which providers are covered. This is a deployment-combination gap across GKE, EKS, and AKS.

These credentials and the per-provider trace-query helpers do not exist yet; building them is part of this finding.

### - [ ] T-16.3.6 — No conformance test pins span output against the W3C trace-context and OTLP schemas [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "OpenTelemetry trace ID propagation through the entire delegation tree." and "the platform emits OTLP traces and the collector handles sampling, batching, and export." (spec/16_observability.md:326, 365)
- **Existing tests:** The propagation unit tests construct `traceparent` strings by hand (for example `pkg/gateway/middleware/correlation/tracing_propagation_test.go:45` builds `00-<trace>-<span>-01`) and parse them with the OTel propagator, which is a round-trip against the library rather than a conformance assertion against the W3C `traceparent` grammar. No test pins the emitted OTLP payload against the OpenTelemetry proto schema, and no test asserts the gateway accepts and rejects `traceparent` and `tracestate` values per the W3C specification (version byte, malformed flags, oversize `tracestate`).
- **Gap:** §16.3 names OpenTelemetry and OTLP as external standards, so a conformance test that pins both the inbound `traceparent`/`tracestate` parsing and the outbound OTLP message against the published schemas is required, and its absence is a finding. The missing work is a tier-3 contract test exercising the W3C trace-context grammar (valid and malformed inputs) and validating the OTLP export against the OpenTelemetry proto.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the OpenTelemetry collector proto definitions or a schema validator and the OTLP receiver from the testinfra collector (deferred per TESTING.md §13.4). The receiver does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/tracing/w3c_trace_context_test.go` with a table of valid and malformed `traceparent`/`tracestate` headers asserting the gateway's extract behavior, plus an OTLP export validation that decodes the emitted spans against the OpenTelemetry proto.

### - [ ] T-16.3.8 — `coordinator.handoff` span and its attributes are unverified [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`coordinator.handoff` Gateway (attributes: `pool`, `outcome`, `generation` — covers the 3-step coordinator handoff protocol ...)" (spec/16_observability.md:363)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/observability/tracing/tracing.go` defines `SpanCoordinatorHandoff` and the `AttrGeneration` constant (declared alongside the budget attributes under F-16.3.5), and `pkg/observability/tracing/tracing_test.go::TestSpanNamesCatalogMatchesSpec163Table` confirms the constant matches the spec row. A grep of `pkg/gateway/coordination/coordfence`, `pkg/gateway/coordination/barrier`, and the rest of `pkg/`/`cmd/` shows no production call site for `SpanCoordinatorHandoff` anywhere outside its own declaration, so the §10.1 coordinator handoff path still opens no span and the `pool`, `outcome`, and `generation` attributes are never recorded. No tier-2 or higher test asserts the handoff emits its span.
- **Gap:** The coordinator handoff is the HA gateway leadership-transfer path, and its trace span is the operator's view into a 3-step protocol failure, yet the span is still not instrumented and not tested. Unlike at generation time, the §10.1 handoff protocol itself is no longer the blocker: `CoordinatorFence`/`CheckpointBarrier` (BUILD-GAPS F-10.1.7, CLOSED) and the `coordfence.Fencer`/`barrier.Coordinator` gateway-side drivers (F-11.3.14, CLOSED) are now implemented and wired into the resume re-bind path (`sessionserver.resumeOnPod`), so this finding is buildable today rather than blocked on protocol work. The missing work is a component test that runs the gateway in dev mode and confirms a span reaches the stdout exporter. This is a low-risk developer-experience assertion.

The BUILD-GAPS F-16.3.1 resolution note states directly: "the spec marks this 'Controller' but this implementation claims the idle pod gateway-side, so the span is emitted there" — `session.claim_pod` is opened by `pkg/gateway/podlifecycle/podclaim.Claimer.Claim`, which runs inside the gateway process (`cmd/lenny-gateway`), not inside `cmd/lenny-controller`.

No test catches a component-column drift like this (the parity test checks only span names), so a future span whose emitting component moves would go undetected the same way. This is a documentation-accuracy and observability-usability gap rather than a missing-span gap.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today; the emitting component for every wired span is now known from the F-16.3.1 batch.

## §16.4 Logging <a id="t-16.4"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/16_observability.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§16.4's spec text is unchanged since the 2026-06-03 audit (byte-identical from "Structured JSON logs..." through the SIEM-responsibility-split paragraph), so no finding in this section is resolved by a spec rewording. Two commits since the audit closed real gaps this section had flagged, however: `0ddce6a9` wired the `lenny_audit_partition_drop_blocked` gauge the `AuditPartitionDropBlocked` alert reads (T-16.4.5, now RESOLVED — the pruner produces and clears the per-partition signal under tier1 and tier2 tests, though a live rule-evaluation test is still missing and is now tracked separately as T-16.4.13), and `61cea725` (BUILD-GAPS F-16.4.6) closed the "EventStore tables are not partitioned" gap by adding `session_logs` and `stream_cursors` as natively range-partitioned tables (migration 0149) plus the leader-gated `pkg/gateway/storage/partitionmaint` background job that creates and drops their partitions. That new component has zero coverage above tier1 string/logic tests — no test runs it against real Postgres, and no code path anywhere inserts a row into either table — so it is captured as a new High finding, T-16.4.12. A cluster of §20-refactor package moves (`pkg/gateway/auditstore` → `pkg/gateway/audit/auditstore`, `pkg/gateway/auditretention` → `pkg/gateway/audit/auditretention`, `pkg/gateway/admin` → `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin`, `pkg/gateway/gatewaymetrics` → `pkg/gateway/metrics/gatewaymetrics`) left several findings' file citations stale; those are corrected in place without changing their analysis. The credential-sensitive-RPC span-attribute gap (T-16.4.1), the cross-binary `operation_id` join (T-16.4.2), the `spec-map.json` under-listing (T-16.4.3), the `AuditRetentionLow` startup-emission gap (T-16.4.4), the fake-store-only `Pruner`/`Run`-loop orchestration gap (T-16.4.6), the force-drop REST contract gap (T-16.4.7), the setup-output EventStore persistence gap (T-16.4.8), the missing e2e/chaos coverage of the audit-retention sweep (T-16.4.9), the custom-retention-days edge case (T-16.4.10), and the retention-SQL attribution note (T-16.4.11) all remain open and were re-verified against the current tree with no change in substance. Counts: 3 High, 6 Medium (1 resolved), 3 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-16.4.1 — Credential-sensitive RPC exclusion from OTel trace span attributes is implemented but never asserted by a test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "**Credential-sensitive RPCs** (`AssignCredentials`, `RotateCredentials`) are excluded from payload-level logging, gRPC access logs, and OTel trace span attributes. Only RPC name, lease ID, provider type, and outcome are recorded." (spec/16_observability.md:376)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/adapter/credredact_test.go` covers the gRPC access-log surface: `TestCredentialRedactionInterceptorRedactsPayload_spec_16_4_376`, `TestCredentialRedactionInterceptorRecordsErrorOutcome_spec_16_4_376`, and `TestCredentialRedactionInterceptorPassesThroughNonSensitive_spec_16_4_376` assert that the redacted log line carries only `lease_ids`, `providers`, `operation`, and `outcome` and never the secret payload. The span-attribute branch of `credentialRedactionInterceptor` (`pkg/adapter/credredact.go:128`, guarded by `span.IsRecording()`) is never reached because none of these tests install a recording span on the context. No test in tier2, tier3, or tier9 inspects the exported span attributes for the `credential.assign` / `credential.rotate` spans. BUILD-GAPS F-16.4.8 (CLOSED) confirms the interceptor now stamps the safe field set onto the active otelgrpc span as part of the same seam, but the test file cited there is the identical `credredact_test.go` suite named above — the span assertion still does not exist.
- **Gap:** The OTel span-attribute surface is one of three the spec names as a credential leak vector, and it is the one that reaches the external trace backend. The implemented redaction is unverified, so a regression that set the raw `AssignCredentialsRequest` payload as a span attribute would ship green. This is an adversarial / leak-prevention scenario. Target tier2 (a real recording span via the tracetest recorder) and tier9 (a security assertion that the exported span carries no payload bytes).
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The tracetest SpanRecorder is available via `tests/testinfra/mocks/otelcollector` and the OTel SDK `tracetest` package; the interceptor and `SafeCredentialFields` already exist.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier2 case in `pkg/adapter/credredact_test.go` (or `tests/tier2_component/observability/credential_span_test.go`) that opens a recording span via `tests/testinfra/mocks/otelcollector`, runs `credentialRedactionInterceptor` for `AssignCredentials` and `RotateCredentials` with a secret payload, and asserts the recorded span attributes contain only the lease IDs, provider types, and outcome and never the payload bytes; mirror it as a tier9 leak assertion.

### - [ ] T-16.4.2 — No contract or cross-binary test pins the log-line JSON schema or the `operation_id` join between gateway and `lenny-ops` [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "**Agent-operability correlation fields** (all components, §25.4): every log line MUST include `ts` (RFC 3339 UTC), `level`, `msg`, `component`, and — when present on the originating request — `operation_id` (from the `X-Lenny-Operation-ID` header) and `agent_name` (from `X-Lenny-Agent-Name`). This shape is shared between the gateway and `lenny-ops` so a single orchestrated agent task can be joined across both binaries via `operation_id`." (spec/16_observability.md:372)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/observability/logging/logging_test.go::TestHandlerProjectsCorrelationFieldsFromContext` asserts the handler projects `operation_id` and `agent_name` from a `correlation.Fields` value in-process. `pkg/ops/opsserver/correlation_fallback_test.go` asserts `lenny-ops` HTTP handlers fall back to the `X-Lenny-Operation-ID` header for lock and escalation requests. `tests/tier3_contract/cloudevents/cloudevents_test.go` asserts `operation_id` lands on the CloudEvents `lennyoperationid` extension. No test runs the real gateway and the real `lenny-ops` binary, drives one orchestrated task carrying a single `operation_id`, and asserts both binaries emit JSON log lines carrying that same `operation_id` so the task can be joined across the two log streams. No contract test pins the required-key JSON schema against an external or fixed schema.
- **Gap:** The MUST is a cross-binary log-correlation contract, and the join is the operability promise §25.4 depends on. The shared-shape claim is asserted only at the single-binary primitive level. This is both a standards-style schema-conformance gap (a fixed log-record schema is never pinned) and a multi-component integration gap. Target tier4 (both binaries on the compose stack sharing one `operation_id`) and tier3 (a log-record schema conformance check).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the `lenny-ops` binary running alongside the gateway on the compose stack. `lenny-ops` exists (`cmd/lenny-ops`) and installs `logging.Setup`. The compose `observability` profile and `tests/testinfra/gateway` exist; a log-capture helper that parses both binaries' stderr into structured records is the missing fixture and is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/log_correlation_test.go` that issues a request carrying `X-Lenny-Operation-ID` and `X-Lenny-Agent-Name` through the gateway, triggers a `lenny-ops` action on the same operation, captures both binaries' JSON logs, and asserts every line carries the required keys and the two streams share the `operation_id`; add a tier3 fixture that validates one captured record against a pinned log-record schema.

### - [x] T-16.4.5 — `AuditPartitionDropBlocked` alert firing when the GC holds a partition past TTL is untested [Medium] — RESOLVED 0ddce6a9
- **Resolution:** Commit `0ddce6a9` ("F-16.4.6: activate dormant AuditPartitionDropBlocked alert (SIEM-lag gauge)") wires the signal the alert reads. `auditstore.SIEMHeldCount` (real Postgres, `tests/tier2_component/auditstore/auditstore_test.go::TestSIEMHeldCount`) counts non-`gdpr.*` rows past the retention cutoff withheld because their sequence number exceeds the SIEM forwarder's high-water mark, including the empty-tenant and zero-cutoff rejection paths. `auditretention.Pruner.Tick` now reads that count each sweep and drives the §16.1-cataloged `lenny_audit_partition_drop_blocked{partition}` gauge (1 when held, cleared to 0 exactly once on recovery, never emitting a series for a partition that was never blocked), covered against a fake store by `pkg/gateway/audit/auditretention/auditretention_test.go::{TestTickSetsPartitionDropBlockedGauge, TestTickClearsPartitionDropBlockedOnRecovery, TestTickSkipsGaugeWhenSIEMUnconfigured, TestTickHeldCountErrorLeavesGaugeUntouched}` — the last of which asserts a held-count read error leaves the prior gauge state untouched rather than flipping it. `pkg/gateway/metrics/gatewaymetrics/gatewaymetrics_test.go::TestAuditPartitionDropBlockedGauge` confirms the gauge is registered and exposed, and the gauge is wired into `cmd/lenny-gateway` via the `auditRetentionMetrics` sink. This falsifies the finding's core claim ("the signal the alert evaluates is never produced by the tested pruner path"): the signal is now produced and its production is unit-tested end to end from a real-Postgres-verified count through the pruner's gauge-setting logic. The originally suggested tier2-pruner-against-live-Postgres variant and the tier7b rule-evaluation pairing were not built as such (the pruner test uses a fake store rather than a live one, and no rule-evaluation test exists); the residual rule-evaluation gap is tracked separately as T-16.4.13 so it is not lost in this resolution.

### - [ ] T-16.4.6 — The `auditretention.Pruner` orchestration and its leader-gated `Run` loop are only unit-tested against a fake store [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "A background job drops partitions beyond the retention window ... Production runs this under the §10.1 leader lease so a single replica owns the destructive sweep" (spec/16_observability.md:378; pkg/gateway/audit/auditretention/auditretention.go:352-356, wired at cmd/lenny-gateway/auditpipeline.go:194-210). File paths moved from `pkg/gateway/auditretention` and `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` in the §20 S12 C3 audit-package regroup; the quoted comment and wiring are otherwise unchanged.
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/audit/auditretention/auditretention_test.go` covers `Tick`, the no-window no-op, the per-tenant error stop, `ForceDrop`, and (since `0ddce6a9`) the `AuditPartitionDropBlocked` gauge set/clear/skip/error cases, all against a `fakeStore`. The real per-tenant `PruneRetention` SQL and the real `SIEMHeldCount` SQL are covered separately in tier2. No test wires the `Pruner` (its multi-tenant `Tick` loop, its `Run` ticker, and the §16.7 `audit.partition_drop_forced` emit-before-delete ordering) to a real Postgres audit store, and no test exercises the leader-gated `Run` loop under a multi-replica gateway to confirm a single replica owns the destructive sweep.
- **Gap:** The orchestration layer (iterate tenants, emit the force-drop audit row before deleting, run on the leader only) is verified only against fakes, so a bug in the tenant iteration, the emit ordering against a real append, or a missing leader gate that lets two replicas delete concurrently would not be caught. This is both a real operator journey (the scheduled sweep prunes the platform's audit table) and a deployment-combination gap (single-replica versus HA multi-replica gateway). Target tier4 (Pruner over real Postgres) and tier8 (leader-failover during a sweep).
- **Dependencies:** Real Postgres via `tests/testinfra/containers` plus the §10.1 leader-lease test harness. The leader-failover primitive lives in `tests/testinfra/chaos`; a fixture that runs the Pruner under a contended lease does not exist yet and is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/audit_retention_sweep_test.go` that seeds multiple tenants with aged rows, runs `auditretention.Pruner.Tick` against a live Postgres store, and asserts each tenant's rows past the window are deleted while gdpr.* and SIEM-held rows survive; add a tier8 case using `tests/testinfra/chaos` that kills the lease holder mid-sweep and asserts only one replica deletes.

## §16.5 Alerting Rules and SLOs <a id="t-16.5"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/16_observability.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
Coverage for §16.5 is concentrated in static and unit tiers. `pkg/alerting/rules` ships the typed alert catalog with a PromQL validator, completeness checks against the spec, and dual-window burn-rate structure, and the tier2 `catalog_crosscheck_test.go` asserts the rendered chart `PrometheusRule` matches the catalog with no drift. That coverage proves the catalog and its rendering are internally consistent, but it does not prove a single alert fires when its condition holds, that any SLO holds under load, or that the rendered artifacts conform to their external schemas. Since the 2026-06-03 audit, commit `9adff965` (F-25.13.6) replaced the gateway's `NoopExprEvaluator{}` wiring with `pkg/alerting/inproceval`, a real `ExprEvaluator` backed by the gateway's own Prometheus registry, so `gateway.healthTracker.useCompiledRules: true` (the default) now drives a genuine in-process evaluation of the instant-vector subset of the §16.5 catalog rather than a no-op; T-16.5.1 is rewritten below to reflect that the spec-versus-implementation divergence it originally reported is fixed, while the remaining gap (no test drives the real gateway HTTP/metrics surface end to end to a firing assertion) persists at a lower severity. TESTING.md declares that chaos tests assert "alert fires"/"alert clears" and that the SLO load scenarios assert their targets, but the implemented chaos tests assert component health status rather than named-alert firing, and every tier7b/tier12 SLO-validation entry is `t.Skip`-gated or scaffolded. The security-relevant alerts (residency violation, elicitation tamper, plaintext egress, credential compromise) have catalog rules and unit-tested counters but no end-to-end firing assertion; a new tier9 `elicitation_tamper_test.go` landed since the audit but only exercises the enforcement-mode admin API, not tamper detection itself. A new F-SH-1 `OpsClockSkewExceeded` alert landed with the same unit-only, backlog-parked pattern as the other design-invariant scaffolds. Counts: 3 High, 7 Medium, 2 Low, 2 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-16.5.1 — In-process §16.5 evaluator now uses a real backend, but no test drives it end to end against the live gateway to a firing assertion [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "the gateway compiles the rules into an in-process evaluator used as a fallback when Prometheus is unreachable ... When `gateway.healthTracker.useCompiledRules: true`, the gateway evaluates the bundled rules against its in-process metric registry and against Prometheus through the `MetricReader` interface when available." (spec/16_observability.md:575)
- **Existing tests:** Commit `9adff965` ("F-25.13.6: in-process ExprEvaluator backed by the registry, wired into gateway") replaced the `evaluator.NoopExprEvaluator{}` construction this finding originally reported with `inproceval.New(w.gwMetrics.Gatherer())` (`cmd/lenny-gateway/runserver.go:90`, gated by `--health-tracker-use-compiled-rules`, default `true`); the gateway now runs a real per-replica fallback evaluator against its own metric registry. `pkg/alerting/inproceval/inproceval_test.go` unit-tests the instant-vector subset (selectors, aggregations, scalar RHS, division, unsupported-expr preserve-state, absent-metric-as-inactive) against a fresh `prometheus.Registry` built to mirror the gateway's, and `TestEvaluatorStateMachineFires_spec_25_13_4676` drives the state machine to firing. `cmd/lenny-gateway/health_alert_overlay_test.go` still exercises the health-source mapping with a synthetic `staticExpr`, not `inproceval`. `pkg/alerting/evaluator/emit_test.go::TestEvaluatorWithNoopExprFiresNothing` remains a generic unit test of `NoopExprEvaluator`'s own no-op contract, unrelated to gateway wiring now that the gateway no longer constructs one by default. No test starts the actual `lenny-gateway` binary (or its component-level harness), pushes a real metric increment through its HTTP/session surface past a §16.5 threshold, and asserts the in-process tracker reports the alert firing. Searched tiers: tier2 `pkg/alerting/inproceval`, tier2 `tests/tier2_component/observability`, tier4 `tests/tier4_integration`, tier5 `tests/tier5_e2e_kind` — none reference `inproceval` or `--health-tracker-use-compiled-rules`.
- **Gap:** The original divergence (the binary wired a no-op regardless of the spec's fallback requirement) is fixed: the default posture now evaluates a real registry-backed expression engine. The residual gap is narrower — `inproceval` only supports the instant-vector subset (selectors, aggregations, scalar comparisons); expressions needing `rate()`/`increase()`/`histogram_quantile()` (for example `WarmPoolExhausted`, most burn-rate alerts) resolve to `ErrUnsupportedExpr` and never fire from this fallback, which is by design but is asserted only at the unit level against a synthetic registry, not against the real gateway's live metric surface. No component or integration test proves the wiring holds when the gateway is actually running and driving requests. This is still a real operator journey (the on-call sees an in-process-evaluable alert, e.g. `DualStoreUnavailable`, when Prometheus is down) that lacks an end-to-end proof.
- **Dependencies:** Buildable today against the real gateway binary or its component harness; `inproceval` and its `MetricReader`-independent registry adapter already exist. `tests/testinfra/inproc` and `tests/testinfra/gateway` provide the in-process gateway substrate.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier2_component/observability/inprocess_alert_eval_test.go` starting the real gateway wiring with `--health-tracker-use-compiled-rules=true` and Prometheus unreachable, driving a session-store failure or another in-process-evaluable §16.5 condition (e.g. `DualStoreUnavailable`) through the gateway's real metric registry, and asserting the named alert transitions to firing and clears, using `tests/testinfra/clockstep` to advance the `for` window deterministically.

### - [ ] T-16.5.2 — No chaos test asserts §16.5 alerts fire or clear despite TESTING.md declaring it [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Assert the documented behavior: alert fires, fallback engages, audit trail records the event ... Assert recovery: alert clears, system returns to healthy." (TESTING.md:1227) covering the §16.5 critical alerts `DualStoreUnavailable`, `SessionStoreUnavailable`, `RedisUnavailable`, and `MinIOUnavailable` (spec/16_observability.md:431, 415, 416, 418).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier8_chaos/store_failure_test.go` injects a dual-store outage and asserts `/v1/admin/health` flags `postgres` and `redis` `unhealthy`/`degraded` and returns to `healthy` on recovery (`TestDualStoreUnavailable`, `TestPostgresUnavailable`, `TestRedisClusterDegraded`, `TestMinIOUnavailable`). It asserts component health status, not the named alerts. No assertion checks `lenny_dual_store_unavailable`, `lenny_quota_redis_fallback_total`, or `lenny_artifact_upload_error_total{error_type="minio_unreachable"}`, and none checks the named alert transitions to firing then clears. Searched tiers: tier8 `tests/tier8_chaos`, tier2 `tests/tier2_component/observability`.
- **Gap:** The chaos pattern TESTING.md prescribes (alert fires on injection, clears on recovery) is unimplemented for every store-outage alert. Health-component status is a weaker proxy than the named alert that pages on-call; a regression that breaks the alert metric or its threshold would not fail any chaos test. The store-outage alerts are the page-on-call signals for the platform's most severe degradation modes and need a failure-path test that asserts firing and clearing.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the in-process evaluator firing path from T-16.5.1, or a Prometheus deployed in the Kind chaos overlay so the rendered `PrometheusRule` can be evaluated and queried. The Kind overlay does not currently deploy Prometheus. Building that overlay or the in-process firing path is part of this finding. `tests/testinfra/kind` and `tests/testinfra/chaos` provide the injection harness.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `tests/tier8_chaos/store_failure_test.go` (or add `tests/tier8_chaos/alert_firing_test.go`) so each store-outage case asserts the named §16.5 alert is firing during the outage and clears on recovery, querying either the gateway in-process tracker or a Prometheus deployed by `tests/testinfra/kind`.

### - [ ] T-16.5.3 — SLO targets and multi-window burn-rate alerts have no executed load validation [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Before GA, load tests must demonstrate that all SLOs below hold at sustained Tier 2 load ... Phase 14.5 re-validates all SLOs with full security hardening active — Phase 14.5 is the final GA gate for SLO compliance." (spec/16_observability.md:614) and the burn-rate table `SessionCreationSuccessRateBurnRate`, `SessionAvailabilityBurnRate`, `GatewayAvailabilityBurnRate`, `TTFTBurnRate` (spec/16_observability.md:640-646).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier7b_load_kind/post_hardening_test.go::TestPostHardeningSLO` calls `t.Skip("phase-gated ...")`. `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go` carries `t.Skip` on `TestFullSystemLoadBaseline`, `TestFullSystemWithHardeningLoad`, `TestGateway10kSessions`, and others. `tests/tier7b_load_kind/experiment_test.go::TestExperimentLoad` (the only §16.5-mapped tier7 test in spec-map.json) is `t.Skip`-gated. The `startup_latency` and `checkpoint_duration` scenarios persist percentiles but assert no SLO threshold in the committed test code. `pkg/alerting/rules/rules_test.go::TestBurnRateRulesAreDualWindow` checks structure only. Searched tiers: tier7a `tests/tier7a_load_local`, tier7b `tests/tier7b_load_kind`, tier12 `tests/tier12_load_cloud`.
- **Gap:** No executed test demonstrates that any §16.5 SLO target holds at Tier 2 load, and no test asserts a burn-rate alert fires when the error budget is being burned at 14x or 3x. The provisional SLO values therefore have no behavioral floor in CI, and the burn-rate alert math is verified only as PromQL structure. This is the GA SLO-compliance gate (Phase 14.5) and is the load and SLO journey for the platform; the burn-rate firing is a failure-path scenario.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the Phase 14.5 hardened-cluster load harness and committed Tier 2 baseline JSON, which the skip messages state do not yet exist. A burn-rate firing test needs synthetic error injection (a fault sink that drives `lenny_session_creation_error_ratio` upward). Building the harness and the fault sink is part of this finding. `tests/testinfra/load`, `tests/testinfra/loadgen`, and `tests/testinfra/kind` provide the substrate.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier7b_load_kind/slo_burnrate_test.go` that runs the Tier 2 session-creation load, asserts P99 < 500ms and success >= 99.5%, then injects a controlled error rate and asserts `SessionCreationSuccessRateBurnRate` (fast window) fires; pair with a tier12 cloud run for sustained Tier 2/3 validation.

### - [ ] T-16.5.4 — Security-relevant alerts (residency, tamper, plaintext egress, credential compromise) have no end-to-end firing test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`DataResidencyViolationAttempt` ... Fires immediately on the first occurrence (`lenny_data_residency_violation_total > 0`)." (spec/16_observability.md:433); "`ElicitationContentTamperDetected` ... `increase(lenny_elicitation_content_tamper_detected_total{enforcement_mode="enforce"}[5m]) > 0`." (spec/16_observability.md:443); "`OTLPPlaintextEgressDetected` ... any non-zero rate is an active confidentiality regression." (spec/16_observability.md:441); "`CredentialCompromised` ... still has active leases alive against it, indicating revocation propagation failure." (spec/16_observability.md:422).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier9_security/scaffolds_test.go` documents that the elicitation-tamper alert metric and audit envelope are unit-tested in `gatewaymetrics_test.go` and that a live per-hop content-tamper e2e is "post-v1 work" filed as a bead by proposal 0030 (F-9.2.1), because in v1 the gateway resolves the elicitation chain server-internally and no intermediate pod re-emits, so there is no per-hop re-emission wire path to drive the tamper condition at all. A new `tests/tier9_security/elicitation_tamper_test.go` landed since the 2026-06-03 audit and drives `/v1/admin/tenants/{id}/elicitation-content-integrity` against a real Kind cluster (`TestElicitationTamperEnforceMode`, `TestElicitationTamperDetectOnlyMode`, `TestElicitationPlatformFloor`), but it only asserts the enforcement-mode resolver and wire contract (`storedMode`/`effectiveMode`), not a tamper event, the `lenny_elicitation_content_tamper_detected_total` metric, or the alert firing. TESTING.md:1288 declares the `ElicitationContentIntegrityPermissiveTamper` alert is "recorded" under `detect-only`. No tier9 test asserts the residency, plaintext-egress, or credential-compromise alerts fire end to end. Searched tiers: tier9 `tests/tier9_security`, tier4 `tests/tier4_integration`, tier8 `tests/tier8_chaos`.
- **Gap:** These alerts are the confidentiality and integrity tripwires whose steady-state value is zero, and the spec says any non-zero increment is an active regression. The security controls behind them are exercised (NetworkPolicy, elicitation enforce mode, OTLP TLS), but no test confirms the alert metric increments and the alert fires when the hostile condition is reached. Each is an adversarial scenario (a tampering intermediary, a cross-border write attempt, a plaintext exporter, a leaked-after-revocation credential) plus a standards-conformance touchpoint for the OCSF/MCP origin-binding invariant. The tamper case specifically remains architecturally blocked in v1 (no per-hop re-emission wire path), which the newly landed config-level test does not change.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier9 Kind security overlay with an active elicitation-tamper intermediary stub (blocked on the post-v1 per-hop re-emission producer proposal 0030 files as F-9.2.1), a cross-region `StorageRouter` fixture, a plaintext OTLP collector, and a credential-revocation injector. The plaintext-collector stub is noted as not yet built. Building the non-tamper pieces is part of this finding; the tamper piece is blocked on the post-v1 bead. `tests/testinfra/security`, `tests/testinfra/stubs`, and `tests/testinfra/audit` provide reusable pieces.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier9_security/alert_firing_test.go` driving each hostile condition that is buildable today (a cross-region write; a plaintext OTLP export; a revoked credential with a live lease) and asserting the corresponding §16.5 alert metric increments and the named alert fires, correlating with the paired audit event; track the tamper-firing case against the F-9.2.1 backlog bead rather than blocking this finding on it.

### - [ ] T-16.5.5 — Rendered PrometheusRule is not validated against the prometheus-operator CRD schema or run through promtool [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "the chart renders the rules into a `PrometheusRule` CRD (when `monitoring.format: prometheusrule`) and/or a ConfigMap (`configmap`)." (spec/16_observability.md:574)

- **Gap:** The rendered artifact is the wire surface deployers consume, and a contract or conformance test pinning it against the external prometheus-operator CRD schema is absent. A rule that is catalog-consistent but malformed against the CRD (or that promtool would reject) would render and pass the crosscheck yet fail to load in a real Prometheus. This is a standards-conformance gap for the prometheus-operator schema.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the prometheus-operator `PrometheusRule` JSON schema fixture and `promtool` on PATH (or a vendored validator). Neither is currently wired. Building the schema fixture and a promtool invocation is part of this finding. `tests/testinfra/schematest` and `tests/testinfra/helm` provide the validation and render harness.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/prometheusrule_schema/prometheusrule_schema_test.go` that renders the chart `PrometheusRule`, validates it against the `monitoring.coreos.com/v1` schema, and runs every expr through `promtool check rules`.

- **Spec/Doc:** "The §16.5 latency and availability SLOs are authored once in pkg/alerting/rules (SLODefinitions); burnRateAlerts and RenderOpenSLO both derive from that single catalog." (tests/spec-map.json:2438, §16.10 notes) and the SLO targets table (spec/16_observability.md:620-630).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/alerting/rules/openslo_test.go::TestRenderOpenSLOEmitsThreeDocsPerSLO` and `::TestRenderOpenSLOObjectivesMatchCatalog` check internal consistency. `charts/lenny/tests/openslo-configmap_test.yaml` asserts the ConfigMap renders, has the right name, and lands in the monitoring namespace. No test validates the rendered OpenSLO documents against the published OpenSLO v1 JSON schema (`apiVersion`, `kind: SLO`/`AlertPolicy`, `spec.objectives`, `spec.indicator`). Searched: `pkg/alerting/rules`, `charts/lenny/tests`, `tests/testinfra/schematest`.
- **Gap:** OpenSLO is an external standard that downstream SLO tooling parses, and the absence of a conformance test pinning the export against the OpenSLO v1 schema is a finding. The internal consistency checks would pass even if the emitted documents were not valid OpenSLO. This is a standards-conformance gap.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the OpenSLO v1 JSON schema fixture, which is not present. Building it is part of this finding. `tests/testinfra/schematest` provides the JSON-schema validation helper.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/openslo_schema/openslo_schema_test.go` that renders the OpenSLO documents from `pkg/alerting/rules` and validates each against the OpenSLO v1 schema, asserting the objective targets match the §16.5 SLO table.
