## §17.4 Local Development Mode (lenny-dev) <a id="t-17.4"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/17_deployment-topology.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
Proposal 0017 ("re-architect §17.4 Embedded Mode to run the full production stack in-cluster") landed in full (spec commit `89f66d71`, code merged at `b6828cf3`) since the 2026-06-03 audit, on top of proposals 0013 (cross-platform Docker-backed k3s launcher) and 0016 (pod-deployable echo runtime). Embedded Mode no longer runs the gateway as a host process with embedded-Postgres/miniredis/OIDC-pod backends: the gateway and controllers now run as pods inside the embedded k3s cluster, rendered from the production chart under a development profile, with ephemeral in-process-in-memory Postgres/Redis/KMS/blob stores, a dev bearer-trust hook (`pkg/embedded/devauth`, replacing the old `pkg/embedded/oidc` provider) instead of a separate embedded OIDC pod, and a loopback-only host-side TLS-terminating forwarder in front of the in-cluster plaintext gateway. This closed most of the High-severity findings in this section: a real tier4 smoke test now drives `lenny up` → `lenny session new` → `lenny down --purge` end to end (T-17.4.1), the Compose Mode bundle and its credentials/observability/smoke profiles exist and are contract-tested (T-17.4.3, T-17.4.4, T-17.4.8), the `EMBEDDED_MODE_LOCAL_ONLY` fail-closed guard is now proven through the operator-facing `lenny up` path rather than only the internal function (T-17.4.6), the "same production code path" claim is now literally true and asserted by a pod-placement smoke test (T-17.4.10), and the non-suppressible production banner is asserted against real `lenny up` stdout (T-17.4.11). What remains open: the gateway's fail-closed `LENNY_DEV_MODE` startup assertion is still verified only as a pure function, never against the real `cmd/lenny-gateway` binary (T-17.4.5); the `dev.local` audience refusal has no contract test against the RFC 9068 schema and no end-to-end foreign-audience-rejected test against a running gateway (T-17.4.7); the Source Mode SQLite substitution now has a real restart-durability test, but the in-memory-cache and filesystem-artifact substitutions are still unverified in combination (T-17.4.9); the Source-Mode `:9090/metrics` endpoint and the credentials-profile cert-regeneration-on-delete behavior remain untested (T-17.4.12); and the §17.4 spec-map entry, while much improved, still names a non-existent `cmd/lenny-dev` package and omits the tier4 smoke tests that are the section's best coverage (T-17.4.13). Three new findings track testable surface the 0017 rewrite introduced: the placeholder-pinned §26 reference-runtime session-creation failure path (T-17.4.14), the absence of an automated Go-driven Compose Mode live round trip (T-17.4.15), and the untested "local isolation fidelity" degradation claims (T-17.4.16). Counts: 4 High, 8 Medium, 2 Low, 2 Info (13 resolved-or-open across the section; 7 resolved this pass, 3 new).

### Findings

### - [x] T-17.4.1 — Embedded Mode `lenny up` → session → `lenny down` has no end-to-end test [High] — RESOLVED c5ebc95e (extended c37f5b6e, 72e0bfe0)
- **Resolution:** `tests/tier4_integration/embedded_mode_smoke_test.go` (`//go:build smoke`) now carries `TestEmbeddedModeSmoke_spec_17_4_18`, which builds the real `cmd/lenny` binary, runs `lenny up`, waits for every control-plane pod (gateway, controller, `lenny-ops`) to reach Ready, drives `lenny session new` against the seeded echo runtime across the §5.2 `PoolWarmingUp` initial-fill window, asserts a session response, then runs `lenny down --purge` and asserts the state directory is removed, logging the bring-up wall-clock via `time.Since`. Landed originally in commit `c5ebc95e` (closing BUILD-GAPS F-17.4.18) and substantially extended by proposal 0017 (commits `c37f5b6e`, `72e0bfe0`) to also assert real pod placement (see T-17.4.10) and a custom-sidecar-runtime leg. The test is gated behind `embedded.SkipUnlessAvailable` (a Docker-backed or Linux k3s substrate must be reachable), the test-coverage tier-5/6 escape hatch for hardware/substrate-dependent tests; it skips with a stated dependency rather than failing when unavailable.

### - [ ] T-17.4.5 — Dev-mode hard startup assertion is verified only as a pure function, never against the real gateway binary [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The gateway refuses to start with TLS disabled unless the environment variable `LENNY_DEV_MODE=true` is explicitly set. Any other value, or absence of the variable, causes an immediate fatal error at startup. This ensures a misconfigured staging or production deployment cannot silently run without encryption." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:279, unchanged wording; renumbered from line 268 by the 0017/0020 edits above it)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/deployment/devmode/devmode_test.go:15` (`TestResolveStartupGate_spec_17_4_268`) is a white-box unit test of the `ResolveStartupGate(devMode, tlsTerminatedUpstream)` pure function; the package moved from `pkg/gateway/devmode` to `pkg/gateway/deployment/devmode` under the unrelated proposal 0020 package-reorganization refactor (commit `a752838b`), with no change to the function or its coverage. The tier4 gateway harness `tests/testinfra/gateway/gateway.go:104-106` (path unchanged) still unconditionally sets `LENNY_TLS_TERMINATED_UPSTREAM=true` so the gate always passes; no component test starts the real `cmd/lenny-gateway` binary with neither dev mode nor upstream acknowledgment and asserts it exits fatally. Searched tiers tier2, tier4, and tier9; no `gateway_tls_startup_gate_test.go` or equivalent exists anywhere in `tests/`.
- **Gap:** The fail-closed branch is the security-critical assertion that a misconfigured production gateway cannot run without encryption. It is exercised only as a function call, so a regression in `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go`'s wiring (for example reading the wrong env var, or defaulting the flag to true) would ship undetected. This is an adversarial/failure-path gap at the process level, unchanged by the §17.4 rearchitecture since it lives in `cmd/lenny-gateway` rather than the embedded-mode substrate. Target tier4 component or tier9 security.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The `tests/testinfra/gateway` helper builds and spawns the real binary; the test passes a custom env that omits both `LENNY_DEV_MODE` and `LENNY_TLS_TERMINATED_UPSTREAM`.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/gateway_tls_startup_gate_test.go` that spawns `cmd/lenny-gateway` with no dev-mode and no upstream-termination env, asserts a non-zero exit, and asserts the stderr carries the `LENNY_TLS_REQUIRED` diagnosis, then a positive case that sets `LENNY_DEV_MODE=true` and confirms startup.

### - [x] T-17.4.3 — Compose Mode (`docker compose up`) full local stack is unbuilt and untested [High] — RESOLVED afc9d673
- **Resolution:** A top-level `docker-compose.yml` now provisions `postgres`, `redis`, `minio`, a `migrate` one-shot, and a `gateway` service (built from the production `Dockerfile`, `BINARY=lenny-gateway`) running the §17.4 line 262 built-in echo runtime as the single agent; the gateway runs the controller simulation and echo agent in-process, the same substitution Source Mode makes. `tests/tier3_contract/compose_mode/compose_mode_test.go` (`TestComposeDefaultProfileServices_spec_17_4_216`, `TestComposeGatewayWiring_spec_17_4_168`) asserts every default-profile service exists, carries no profile tag, and that the gateway service builds `lenny-gateway`, wires the Postgres/Redis/MinIO DSNs, passes `--dev-mode --agent-runtime=echo`, and depends on `migrate`/`minio-setup` completing and Postgres/Redis being healthy before starting. The live round trip is exercised by `compose/smoke-test.sh` rather than by a Go-driven `compose.Up` test (see new finding T-17.4.15 for that residual gap).

### - [x] T-17.4.4 — Credential-testing profile (`make compose-tls`, `credentials`) and mTLS dev path are untested [High] — RESOLVED afc9d673
- **Resolution:** `make compose-tls` now runs `scripts/dev-certs.sh ./lenny-data/certs` (an idempotent openssl CA+leaf generator) and then `LENNY_DEV_TLS=true docker compose --profile credentials up`; the `credentials` profile carries a `dev-certs` service running the same script in-container, and the gateway reads `LENNY_DEV_TLS`. `tests/tier3_contract/compose_mode/compose_mode_test.go::TestComposeCredentialsProfile_spec_17_4_245` asserts the `dev-certs` service is profiled under `credentials`, the gateway service reads `LENNY_DEV_TLS`, and `scripts/dev-certs.sh` exists, defaults to `./lenny-data/certs`, and emits `ca.crt`. This is a wire-contract/config-render level test rather than a live mTLS handshake or a negative test that real credentials over plain HTTP are gated; that residual gap is folded into new finding T-17.4.15.

### - [x] T-17.4.6 — EMBEDDED_MODE_LOCAL_ONLY non-loopback rejection is unit-tested only and never exercised through `lenny up` [Medium] — RESOLVED 72e0bfe0 (built on 8e534807, c37f5b6e)
- **Resolution:** Proposal 0017 added a fixed gateway NodePort (`stack.GatewayNodePort`) published only on host loopback (Linux: `--kube-proxy-arg=nodeport-addresses=127.0.0.1/32`; Docker-backed launcher: `-p 127.0.0.1:<nodePort>:<nodePort>`), on top of the pre-existing loopback-only TLS-terminating forwarder. `tests/tier9_security/embedded_gateway_loopback_test.go::TestEmbeddedGatewayDockerBackedSecurityLegs_spec_17_4` runs a real `lenny up`, then its `gateway_nodeport_unreachable_on_non_loopback` subtest dials the fixed gateway NodePort on the host's primary non-loopback IPv4 address and asserts the dial fails or times out, proving the operator-facing bind path — not just `startTLSProxy`'s internal function — fails closed per `EMBEDDED_MODE_LOCAL_ONLY`. The companion `TestEmbeddedForwarderLegsFailClosedOnNonLoopback_spec_17_4` covers the forwarder leg in-process. Both are gated behind `embedded.SkipUnlessAvailable`.

### - [ ] T-17.4.7 — Embedded OIDC dev.local audience refusal lacks a contract/conformance test against the JWT/RFC 9068 schema and an end-to-end gateway-rejection test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The in-cluster gateway runs in dev mode and trusts the dev bearer the CLI mints from the persisted dev key through its dev-mode bearer-trust hook; it refuses any token whose `aud` claim is not `dev.local` even when the token is signed by the trusted dev key, and it rejects externally-issued tokens." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:193; restates the same requirement previously at line 182, reworded by proposal 0017 to describe the dev-bearer-trust hook rather than a separate embedded OIDC provider)
- **Existing tests:** The standalone `pkg/embedded/oidc` provider package was removed by proposal 0017 (commit `051e1efc`, "remove the host-process control plane and the in-process backend legs"); the audience-issuance/verification logic now lives in `pkg/embedded/devauth/devauth_test.go`, which carries `TestVerifyRejectsForeignAudience` (added by commit `a405ea2c`, "pin the dev.local audience-rejection invariant lost in the oidc->devauth move") alongside the pre-existing `cmd/lenny-gateway/embedded_audience_test.go:37-79` (`TestEmbeddedHMACVerifierRejectsForeignAudience_spec_17_4_182`, `TestEmbeddedAudienceCompositionMatchesGateway_spec_17_4_182`, unchanged file and line range). Both remain package-internal unit tests (`devauth`, `main`), with no running gateway. No tier3 contract test pins the issued token against the RFC 9068 access-token claim schema, and no tier4/tier5/tier9 test presents an externally-issued (foreign-audience) bearer to the running in-cluster gateway — including the new `tests/tier9_security/embedded_gateway_loopback_test.go` suite, whose `cli_bearer_authenticates_end_to_end` subtest only exercises the accepted `dev.local` path. Searched tiers tier3, tier4, tier5, and tier9.
- **Gap:** The spec references an external standard (OIDC/JWT with RFC 9068 scopes), so the absence of a contract test pinning the issued token against the schema, and of an end-to-end rejection test for a foreign-audience token against the now-in-cluster gateway, is a conformance and adversarial-path finding. A hostile actor presenting a valid-signature token with a `lenny-gateway` audience is the relevant scenario. Target tier3 contract plus a tier9 negative case alongside the existing Docker-backed security legs.
- **Dependencies:** The tier9 `embedded_gateway_loopback_test.go` harness (`embedded.Build`/`embedded.Run`) and `tests/testinfra/tokenservice` can mint a foreign-audience token against the running embedded stack; buildable for the contract piece today without any additional infrastructure.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/embedded_oidc/audience_test.go` pinning the `devauth`-issued token's claims against the RFC 9068 schema, plus a subtest in `TestEmbeddedGatewayDockerBackedSecurityLegs_spec_17_4` that presents a foreign-audience token signed under the persisted dev key to the running in-cluster gateway and asserts a 401.

## §17.5 Cloud Portability <a id="t-17.5"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/17_deployment-topology.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§17.5 is a four-bullet portability statement that spec-map.json labels non-normative, but each bullet makes a verifiable capability claim that TESTING.md §12.6 backs with named tier-6 suites (`cloud_csi`, `cloud_kms`, `cloud_oidc`, `cloud_secret_store`) and a provider parity matrix. The implementation seams exist (`pkg/blobstore/providerflags`, `pkg/kms/providerflags`, and per-provider adapters under `pkg/blobstore/{s3,gcs,azureblob}` and `pkg/kms/{aws,gcp,azure}`) with unit-level fake-backed tests, and the gateway wires the provider switch in `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go`. Component-and-above coverage of the portability claim is thin: the only real-backend round-trips (`TestCloudCSI`, `TestCloudKMS`) run against AWS alone and early-return for GCP and Azure, the entire tier-6 harness is gated behind `//go:build e2e_cloud` with a README that states it "is not yet implemented", and the parity matrix lists every cloud capability as `planned` with zero `validated` providers. The matrix file header and TESTING.md both assert that "every capability has at least one validated provider" is enforced, yet the validator in `cmd/lenny-test/cmd_validate_yaml.go` deliberately discards that invariant (`_ = hasValidated`), so the spec-claimed gate does not fire. The pluggable-backend switch itself has no integration test that boots the gateway against a non-default provider. The four §17.5 bullets themselves are unchanged since the 2026-06-03 audit; only the line numbers of the spec quotes shifted (an earlier §17.4 embedded-mode CRD-apply worked example grew by 35 lines). Since the audit, the tier-6 harness gained more scaffolded suites (`cluster_assertions_test.go`, `behavior_test.go`, `managed_elasticache_test.go`, `managed_rds_test.go`, `session_lifecycle_test.go`), including a `TestManagedIngress` case now cross-referenced from `tests/spec-map.json`'s §17.5 entry, but every one of them remains gated behind `requireCloud`/`e2e_cloud` and so still does not run in any regular CI cadence — the existing findings on that gap stand unchanged.
Counts: 1 High, 4 Medium, 1 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-17.5.1 — Storage-backend pluggability is round-tripped against AWS only; GCS and Azure Blob portability is unverified at every tier above unit [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Storage backends are pluggable" (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:386). TESTING.md operationalizes the bullet as a multi-provider check: "`ArtifactStore` against the provider's native object storage: GCS on GKE, S3 on EKS, Azure Blob Storage on AKS. The same interface tests pass against every backend" (TESTING.md:1114).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/aws_resources_test.go:135` (`TestCloudCSI`) round-trips `pkg/blobstore/s3.Store` (Put, Get, Stat, SoftDelete) against a real S3 bucket, but it begins with `if p != "aws" { t.Logf(...); return }` so GCS and Azure Blob never execute. Unit tests under `pkg/blobstore/{gcs,azureblob}/*_test.go` use in-process fakes (`fakeGCS`, an in-memory Azure stand-in) and do not exercise a real or emulated backend. `pkg/blobstore/providerflags/providerflags_test.go` resolves the `gcs`/`azure` provider names but only asserts config-required errors, never a round-trip. The tier-2 `tests/tier2_component/stores/miniostore_test.go` round-trips MinIO only.
- **Gap:** The portability claim asserts the same interface passes against every backend, and the cross-backend equivalence is the substance of the claim. No component-or-higher test round-trips the GCS or Azure Blob adapter against its native (or emulated) object store, so a behavioral divergence in either adapter ships unverified. The work is a real user journey (an operator on GKE or AKS storing and retrieving a session artifact) and a deployment-combination gap (the `objectStorage.provider=gcs|azure` combinations are unexercised).
- **Dependencies:** Requires GKE and AKS clusters with provisioned buckets plus the tier-6 cloud harness (`tests/testinfra/cloud`), or a fakegcs-server and Azurite emulator wired into a hermetic tier-2 suite. The emulator fixtures do not exist in `tests/testinfra` yet; building a `tests/testinfra/containers/{fakegcs,azurite}.go` pair is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Lift the provider gate in `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/aws_resources_test.go::TestCloudCSI` to run the same round-trip for `gcp` (via `pkg/blobstore/gcs`) and `azure` (via `pkg/blobstore/azureblob`); in parallel add `tests/tier2_component/stores/cloudstore_contract_test.go` that runs one table-driven Store contract against MinIO, fakegcs-server, and Azurite using `tests/testinfra/containers`.

### - [ ] T-17.5.2 — Cloud KMS pluggability (Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault) is round-tripped against AWS KMS only [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Storage backends are pluggable" (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:386), extended by the parity matrix `cloud_kms` capability and TESTING.md: "T4 per-tenant keys against the provider's native KMS: Cloud KMS on GKE, AWS KMS on EKS, Azure Key Vault on AKS. KMS probe, key rotation, key-unavailable fail-closed validated for each" (TESTING.md:1115).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/aws_resources_test.go:71` (`TestCloudKMS`) wraps and unwraps a DEK against a real AWS KMS alias and asserts cross-alias rejection, but it early-returns with `if p != "aws"` so the GCP Cloud KMS and Azure Key Vault providers are never exercised. `pkg/kms/{gcp,azure}/*_test.go` use in-process fakes. `pkg/kms/providerflags/providerflags_test.go` registers `aws`/`gcp` provider names through `Bind` but performs no provider round-trip.
- **Gap:** The matrix names KMS probe, key rotation, and key-unavailable fail-closed as the per-provider assertions, and none of those run against Cloud KMS or Azure Key Vault at the component tier or above. The fail-closed path (provider unavailable) is a security-relevant branch and is the adversarial scenario here; the wrap-unwrap round-trip is the user journey (an operator on GKE or AKS provisioning per-tenant envelope keys).
- **Dependencies:** Requires GKE and AKS clusters with provisioned KMS keys, or GCP Cloud KMS and Azure Key Vault emulators. No KMS emulator fixture exists in `tests/testinfra`; the key-unavailable case can be exercised today against the real provider by pointing at a revoked or non-existent key.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/aws_resources_test.go::TestCloudKMS` (or add `gcp_resources_test.go` and `azure_resources_test.go`) so the wrap-unwrap-and-cross-alias-reject sequence runs against `pkg/kms/gcp` and `pkg/kms/azure`, and add a per-provider key-unavailable case asserting the documented fail-closed error.

### - [ ] T-17.5.3 — Parity matrix declares every cloud capability `planned` and the validator that should require a `validated` provider is disabled [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Every capability has at least one `validated` provider." (tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml:16) and "CI fails if a capability is claimed in the spec or chart but missing from the matrix." plus the stronger reading at TESTING.md:1122. Every capability row in the matrix is `planned` or `skip` (parity-matrix.yaml:27-118).
- **Existing tests:** `cmd/lenny-test/cmd_validate_yaml.go:310` (`validateParityMatrixYAML`) tracks `hasValidated` per capability but discards it: line 375 reads `_ = hasValidated` with the comment "`planned` everywhere is acceptable today". `cmd/lenny-test/cmd_validate_yaml_test.go` covers unknown-provider, skip-without-reason, empty-status, and empty-providers cases (`TestValidateParityMatrixHappy/UnknownProvider/SkipRequiresReason/UnknownState/EmptyStatus/EmptyProviders/Absent`), but no test asserts the at-least-one-validated invariant the matrix header promises.
- **Gap:** The matrix file and TESTING.md both state an invariant that the implementation deliberately does not enforce, so a regression that leaves a capability with zero validated providers ships silently while the documents claim CI guards against it. This is a spec-versus-test inconsistency that lets the unvalidated state persist undetected. The fix is a tier-0 static assertion plus a documentation reconciliation.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add a `cmd/lenny-test/cmd_validate_yaml_test.go` case (`TestValidateParityMatrixRequiresValidated`) that fails a matrix with every cell `planned`, and either enforce the invariant in `validateParityMatrixYAML` or amend the matrix header and TESTING.md:1122 to state the invariant is deferred until the first cloud run lands.

### - [ ] T-17.5.4 — The tier-6 cloud harness is unimplemented, so no §17.5 cloud claim runs in any regular CI cadence [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The design avoids baking in cloud-specific assumptions" (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:384) with the nightly critical-path subset named at TESTING.md:1125 ("`gvisor_isolation`, `cloud_csi`, `cloud_kms` per provider").
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/README.md:10` still states "The tier-6 harness is not yet implemented." Every tier-6 file, including the suites added since the 2026-06-03 audit (`cluster_assertions_test.go`, `behavior_test.go`, `managed_elasticache_test.go`, `managed_rds_test.go`, `session_lifecycle_test.go`), carries `//go:build e2e_cloud` and starts with `requireCloud(t)`, which calls `cloud.SkipUnlessAvailable` (`tests/testinfra/cloud/cloud.go:171`) and `t.Fatalf`s when `LENNY_CLOUD_PROVIDER` is unset. `tests/testinfra/cloud/cloud.go:215` still reports the provisioning scripts as a "Phase 13+ deliverable" that is "not present". The suite therefore neither runs nor produces a pass in standard CI.
- **Gap:** The portability bullets are exercised against a live provider only through the tier-6 suite, and that suite has no implemented harness, no provisioning scripts, and no scheduled cadence, so the cloud portability claim has no executed component-or-higher coverage today. This is a deployment-combination gap spanning all three managed providers (GKE, EKS, AKS) and is the prerequisite that T-17.5.1 and T-17.5.2 depend on.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the `scripts/cloud/{aws,gcp,azure}/up.sh` provisioners, the Terraform modules under `deploy/terraform/cloud`, and reachable GKE/EKS/AKS clusters with credentials. None of the provisioning scripts exist yet; building them is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Land the `tests/testinfra/cloud` provisioning scripts and a nightly CI job that runs `lenny-test --tier e2e_cloud` against at least one provider, flipping `cloud_csi` and `cloud_kms` for that provider from `planned` to `validated` in `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml`.

### - [ ] T-17.5.5 — The object-storage provider switch has no integration test that boots the gateway against a non-default backend [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Storage backends are pluggable" (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:386); `pkg/blobstore/providerflags` documents itself as the §17.5 bullet-1 wiring seam exposing the `minio | s3 | gcs | azure` selector (providerflags.go header).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/blobstore/providerflags/providerflags_test.go` unit-tests `Resolve` for each provider name (returning a Store or a config error). `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go:1303` calls `blobproviderflags.Resolve` at boot. The helm-unittest suites `charts/lenny/tests/gateway-deployment_test.yaml` and `charts/lenny/tests/preflight-job_test.yaml` assert the rendered `objectStorage.provider` values. No tier-2 or tier-4 test boots the gateway with a selected provider and asserts that an artifact written through the live `/v1` surface lands in the chosen backend.
- **Gap:** The unit test proves `Resolve` returns the right Store type, and the helm test proves the value renders, but the end-to-end wiring (gateway boots with `objectStorage.provider=minio` or `=s3` and routes a real artifact to that backend through the request path) is unverified at the integration tier. A regression that resolves the wrong Store or fails to thread the resolved Store into the artifact handler would not be caught below tier-6. This is an integration-flow gap for the supported non-default-provider combinations.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the compose stack (`tests/testinfra/compose`) plus a MinIO container (`tests/testinfra/containers`) for the in-cluster case; the AWS path needs LocalStack or the tier-6 harness. The MinIO container fixture exists; a LocalStack fixture still does not.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/object_storage_provider_test.go` that starts the gateway with `objectStorage.provider=minio` against a MinIO container, writes an artifact through the live REST surface, and asserts the object exists in the MinIO bucket; parameterize over `memory` and `filesystem` to cover the other locally-buildable selectors.

### - [ ] T-17.5.6 — No test asserts the chart installs no cloud-specific CRDs [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "No cloud-specific CRDs required" (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:389).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/crd_test.go` asserts the Lenny CRDs `sandboxwarmpools.lenny.dev`, `sandboxtemplates.lenny.dev`, and `sandboxclaims.lenny.dev` are Established (the latter also checking the `lenny-sandboxclaim-guard` webhook scope), but it does not assert the absence of any non-`lenny.dev` (cloud-provider) CRD dependency. The helm-unittest suites under `charts/lenny/tests` validate individual CRD manifests without asserting the CRD set is provider-neutral.
- **Gap:** The bullet is a negative invariant (the chart depends on no provider-specific CustomResourceDefinition), and no test enforces it, so a future chart edit that introduces a dependency on, for example, a `crd.k8s.aws` or `cloud.google.com` resource would not be flagged. This is a low-risk negative-path assertion suited to the static or chart tier.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier-0 or helm-unittest assertion that every `CustomResourceDefinition` the chart renders carries the `lenny.dev` group, and that the chart's templated resources reference no `apiVersion` outside the Kubernetes core, the documented standard add-ons, and `lenny.dev`.

### - [ ] T-17.5.7 — NetworkPolicy "standard Kubernetes" claim is covered on Kind but not across CNIs at the cloud tier [Info] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Network policies are standard Kubernetes" (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:387).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/ingress_test.go:46` (`TestGatewayIngressPolicy`) enforces the NET-038 `allow-gateway-ingress` policy on Kind under kindnet, and TESTING.md:1113 records that the policy is validated on Kind in tier 5. `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/eks_platform_test.go:78` (`TestCloudVPCCNIPodIPFromVPC`) confirms pod IPs come from the VPC subnet under the AWS VPC CNI, which is the precondition for the allow-list policies to match. `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/cluster_assertions_test.go::TestManagedIngress` (new since the audit) confirms the gateway Service stays ClusterIP and any operator-supplied Ingress routes to it, but that is the managed-LB-ingress claim, not a NetworkPolicy enforcement check, and it is still gated behind `requireCloud`.
- **Gap:** The standard-Kubernetes claim is exercised under kindnet on Kind and the VPC-CNI IP precondition is checked on EKS, but no test enforces a NetworkPolicy denial on a cloud CNI (Calico, Cilium, Azure CNI). NetworkPolicy enforcement is CNI-dependent, so the cross-CNI portability of the policies is an observed gap rather than a normative miss. The tier-5 coverage is adequate for the standard-Kubernetes assertion; this entry records the cloud-CNI enforcement gap for the parity backlog.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier-6 harness on GKE and AKS with a policy-enforcing CNI; depends on T-17.5.4.
- **Suggested test:** When the tier-6 harness lands, add a per-provider negative case that asserts a default-deny NetworkPolicy actually drops disallowed traffic under the provider's CNI, reusing the tier-5 NET-038 assertion structure.

## §17.6 Packaging and Installation <a id="t-17.6"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/17_deployment-topology.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§17.6 specifies the Helm chart install path, the `lenny-preflight` validation Job (a matrix of roughly forty checks), the idempotent `lenny-ctl bootstrap` seed mechanism, the initial admin-credential Secret, the `values.schema.json` enforcement, the interactive `lenny-ctl install` wizard, the CRD upgrade and recovery procedure, and a Day-0 walkthrough from empty cluster to first echo session. Unit and chart-render coverage is dense: `pkg/preflight/*_test.go` exercises every check with a fake Kubernetes client and fake probers, `pkg/chart/values/schema_test.go` covers schema acceptance and rejection, the `pkg/ctlcli` tests (the CLI logic and its tests moved out of `cmd/lenny-ctl` under the F-24.0.1/F-17.4.9 `lenny`/`lenny-ctl` surface unification) cover bootstrap and install flag handling, the chart `helm-unittest` suites render every Job and template, and the krew binary-naming CI invariant is implemented in `.github/workflows/release.yml`. The initial `lenny-admin` user and `lenny-admin-token` Secret mechanism is implemented (a gateway-side `admintoken.Provisioner`, wired into `cmd/lenny-gateway/adminrouter.go`, with chart-rendered RBAC and env vars) and has dense unit coverage, including a create-or-preserve idempotency test and, since the 2026-06-03 audit, a real-Postgres component test for rotation ordering (proposal 0021) — this was already true when the audit was generated and the original finding's "unimplemented, no test" framing was stale from the start; it is corrected below. The component-and-above coverage still has substantial gaps: the `lenny-preflight` Job is never run against real backing services with a fail-closed assertion, the Day-0 walkthrough is never exercised end-to-end on Kind or cloud, the admin-credential mechanism's create-or-preserve idempotency and Day-0 retrieval are verified only against fakes, the CRD stale-upgrade recovery procedure has only a no-op scaffold, the interactive wizard's full apply flow is never driven against a live cluster, and the cloud-provider install path is unexercised. Counts: 3 High, 6 Medium, 3 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-17.6.1 — Admin-credential mechanism is implemented and unit-tested; create-or-preserve idempotency and Day-0 retrieval remain untested against a real store or live cluster [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The bootstrap Job creates an initial `platform-admin` user (username: `lenny-admin`) with a generated API token. The token is written to a Kubernetes Secret `lenny-system/lenny-admin-token`" (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:490); the Day-0 walkthrough step 5 retrieves it: "kubectl get secret lenny-admin-token -n lenny-system -o jsonpath='{.data.token}' | base64 -d" (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:666-667); the rotation procedure was reworded since the 2026-06-03 audit to move minting and Secret-patching to the gateway: "the gateway mints the new token in process, records it, patches the `lenny-admin-token` Secret with the new token value, and then durably revokes the prior token — the CLI does not mint the token or patch the Secret" (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:507).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admintoken/admintoken_test.go` (moved from `pkg/gateway/admintoken` in the proposal-0020 `externalapi` regroup) unit-tests the full mechanism against fakes: `TestProvisionFirstRunCreatesSecretAndUser_spec_17_6_455` and `TestProvisionIsIdempotent_spec_17_6_459` cover first-run creation and the create-or-preserve idempotency the Day-0 walkthrough depends on, and `TestRotateMintsAndRevokesPrevious_spec_13_3` plus the ordering/reclaimer tests cover the gateway-mediated rotation the reworded spec text now describes. `charts/lenny/templates/gateway-deployment.yaml` (not the bootstrap Job) renders the `LENNY_ADMIN_TOKEN_SECRET_NAME`/`LENNY_ADMIN_TOKEN_TENANT` env vars and a Secret-scoped Role/RoleBinding for the gateway ServiceAccount, wired to `admintoken.New` in `cmd/lenny-gateway/adminrouter.go` (F-17.6.3); `charts/lenny/tests/` renders these at helm-unittest tier. `pkg/ctlcli/users_test.go` (moved from `cmd/lenny-ctl/users_test.go`) now asserts `rotate-token` calls the dedicated gateway route (`TestRotateTokenCallsGatewayEndpoint`) rather than patching a Secret itself, matching the reworded spec. Since the 2026-06-03 audit, `tests/tier2_component/stores/admintoken_rotation_test.go` (proposal 0021, landed 2026-07-01; the sole entry now in `tests/spec-map.json` §17.6) drives the real `admintoken.Provisioner` against a real Postgres-backed issued-token store and audit chain for `Rotate` (`TestAdminRotationDurablyRevokesOldTokenAndGatesCache` and siblings) — but it fakes the Kubernetes Secret (`memSecrets`) and exercises `Rotate` only, not the first-run `Provision` create-or-preserve path. No component or e2e test drives `Provision` against a real Postgres user store, and no tier5 Kind test asserts the `lenny-admin-token` Secret exists after a live install or is preserved across a second `helm upgrade`.
- **Gap:** The mechanism this finding originally reported as unimplemented was already implemented (gateway-side provisioner, chart RBAC, CLI wiring) and unit-tested before the 2026-06-03 audit was generated; the audit's "no test found, neither implemented in the chart nor the CLI" claim was inaccurate from the start rather than a product of subsequent drift, and is corrected here. The residual, still-real gap is narrower: `Provision`'s create-or-preserve idempotency and the Day-0 retrieval/re-run guarantee are verified only against fakes, and the real-Postgres component test that landed since the audit covers `Rotate` durability, not `Provision`. Target tier2 component (extend the real-Postgres harness to `Provision`) and tier5 Kind (fold into the T-17.6.4 Day-0 walkthrough test).
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. `tests/tier2_component/stores/admintoken_rotation_test.go` already stands up the real Postgres/audit harness `Rotate` needs; extending it to `Provision` needs no new infrastructure. The tier5 Kind assertion is the same harness T-17.6.4 already depends on.
- **Suggested test:** Add a `Provision` case to `tests/tier2_component/stores/admintoken_rotation_test.go` (or a sibling `admintoken_provision_test.go`) that runs `Provision` against the real Postgres-backed `userstore` twice and asserts the second run returns the same `token`/`jti` (byte-identical, per spec line 459 idempotence) rather than regenerating; extend the tier5 Day-0 test proposed in T-17.6.4 to assert `kubectl get secret lenny-admin-token -n lenny-system` returns a non-empty `token`, then re-run `helm upgrade` and assert the Secret is unchanged.

### - [ ] T-17.6.2 — `lenny-preflight` Job is never run against real backing services with a fail-closed assertion [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The Helm chart includes a `lenny-preflight` Job (`helm.sh/hook: pre-install,pre-upgrade`, `helm.sh/hook-weight: "-10"`) that validates all infrastructure prerequisites before any Lenny component is deployed. The Job runs to completion and blocks the install/upgrade if any check fails." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:513); "Exit code 1: One or more checks failed — Helm aborts." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:565).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/preflight/run_test.go` and the per-check `*_test.go` files exercise every check against a fake controller-runtime client (`sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/client/fake`) and the infra probers against fakes (`pkg/preflight/infra/infra_test.go` defines `fakePostgres`, `fakeRedis`, `fakeMinIO`). `tests/tier2_component/preflight/minio_sse_test.go` is the only component-tier preflight test and it uses a fake-MinIO prober plus a fake Kubernetes client. `charts/lenny/tests/preflight-job_test.yaml` is a `helm-unittest` that asserts rendered Job args only. On Kind, `tests/testinfra/kind/e2e-values.yaml` sets `global.devMode: true`, so per spec line 568 the Job skips MinIO encryption, cert-manager, CNI, and PgBouncer checks and validates only Postgres and Redis connectivity; no tier5 test asserts the preflight Job passed or that a misconfiguration aborts the install.
- **Gap:** The core capability (preflight blocks a misconfigured install) is verified only with fakes. The real prober behavior against live Postgres, PgBouncer, Redis, and MinIO, and the fail-closed exit-1 path that aborts a `helm install`, are unexercised end to end. The work is both a real operator journey (preflight passes on a correctly provisioned cluster) and an adversarial or failure scenario (preflight aborts when PgBouncer `pool_mode` is not `transaction`, when MinIO SSE is absent, or when a CNI lacks NetworkPolicy support). Target tiers are tier4 integration for the prober-against-real-backends path and tier5 Kind for the install-abort path.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a tier4 harness that stands up real Postgres or PgBouncer, Redis, and MinIO containers (tests/testinfra exposes compose-stack building blocks) and a tier5 Kind path that installs with a deliberately broken value and asserts the release never reaches `deployed`. The deliberately-misconfigured-values fixture does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/preflight_real_backends_test.go that runs `preflight.Run` with `infra.RealProbers()` against compose-stack Postgres/Redis/MinIO and asserts pass plus a fail case (PgBouncer in session mode), and tests/tier5_e2e_kind/preflight_abort_test.go that runs `helm install` with a bad `kubeApiServerCIDR` or absent MinIO SSE and asserts the pre-install hook fails and the release status is not `deployed`.

### - [ ] T-17.6.3 — CRD stale-upgrade detection and recovery procedure has only a no-op scaffold [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Controllers validate the installed CRD schema version on startup ... and will refuse to start if CRDs are stale." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:415); "the Helm chart includes a `lenny-crd-validate` Job (`helm.sh/hook: post-upgrade`...) that runs after `helm upgrade` completes. ... If any CRD is stale, the Job fails" (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:420); the recovery procedure (apply CRDs, rollout restart, verify) at lines 422-428.
- **Existing tests:** `charts/lenny/tests/crd-validate-job_test.yaml` is a `helm-unittest` that renders the Job. `pkg/ctlcli/preflight_test.go` (moved from `cmd/lenny-ctl/preflight_test.go`) exercises the CRD version check with a fake client. The tier8 chaos `runbook-map.yaml` maps `crd-upgrade` to `TestCRDUpgradeImmutableFieldChange`, but `tests/tier8_chaos/scaffolds_test.go:420` is a no-op: it only logs "CRDs ship at v1 only (conversion strategy None); multi-version exercise is a v2 follow-on." No test installs an old CRD, runs `helm upgrade` without applying new CRDs, observes a controller `CrashLoopBackOff` with the schema-mismatch message, and drives the documented recovery to a healthy state.
- **Gap:** A normative MUST (controllers refuse to start on stale CRDs) and the operator recovery journey are unverified end to end, and the runbook-mapped test is an empty scaffold standing in for a real suite. The work is a failure-path and recovery scenario on Kind. Target tier is tier5 Kind, with a tier8 chaos variant for the recovery runbook.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness (tests/testinfra/kind) plus a fixture pair of CRDs at two schema-version annotations so the test can install the stale one and upgrade. The two-version CRD fixture does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Replace the `tests/tier8_chaos/scaffolds_test.go` no-op with tests/tier5_e2e_kind/crd_stale_upgrade_test.go that installs CRDs annotated with an old `lenny.dev/schema-version`, runs `helm upgrade` without re-applying CRDs, asserts a controller pod logs the schema-mismatch FATAL and the post-upgrade `lenny-crd-validate` hook fails, then applies the current CRDs, runs `kubectl rollout restart`, and asserts the control plane returns to Ready.

### - [ ] T-17.6.4 — Day-0 walkthrough (empty cluster to first echo session) is never exercised end to end; the declared `bootstrap_first_install` smoke is unmet [High] — OPEN

No test exercises the bootstrap seed interaction: a fresh install with the default `deny-all` and no seeded environment, then a `user`-role principal receiving `403 FORBIDDEN`, and the same install with Option A (`allow-all` in the bootstrap seed) granting access. The bootstrap `rbacConfig` field is not asserted in `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/bootstrap_test.go`.
- **Gap:** The documented Day-1 access gap and its two resolutions are a deployment-configuration behavior with no integration coverage, so a regression that drops the bootstrap `rbacConfig` plumbing or flips the default would not be caught. The work is both a failure scenario (a denied user) and a deployment-combination gap (the two bootstrap remediation options). Target tier is tier4 integration, with a tier5 variant on Kind.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The tier4 gateway harness (tests/testinfra/gateway) supports dev-header role injection and the bootstrap admin endpoint.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/bootstrap_noenvpolicy_test.go that bootstraps a tenant with default `deny-all` and asserts a `user`-role request to a runtime returns `403 FORBIDDEN`, then bootstraps with `rbacConfig.noEnvironmentPolicy: allow-all` (Option A) and asserts the same request succeeds, and a variant that seeds an environment with the user as a member (Option B).

## §17.7 Operational Runbooks <a id="t-17.7"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/17_deployment-topology.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§17.7 mandates a bundled set of operational runbooks with a three-part Trigger/Diagnosis/Remediation structure, a machine-consumable form served at `/v1/admin/runbooks/*` (delegating the format to §25.7), and an `issueRunbooks` health-API lookup table. The static and unit layers are strong: tier11 linters validate front-matter and section structure, the alert-to-runbook and runbook-to-alert cross-maps resolve against the §16.5 catalog, the `pkg/ops/runbooks` parser and `pkg/gateway/operability/health` Path B lookup carry direct unit tests, and a tier3 contract suite pins the index and `/steps` wire format. The component-and-above coverage is thin and partly illusory. The tier3 contract suite drives a single hardcoded stub runbook rather than the bundled set, the production `LoadRunbookDir` loader that scans `docs/runbooks/` has no test, and the TESTING.md §15.2 promise that "every operational runbook is executable end-to-end ... Each has a Tier 8 chaos test that triggers the condition, executes the remediation through the API, and asserts return to healthy" is unmet because the chaos scenarios are `t.Logf` scaffolds and the `TestRunbookMapCoverage` gate only checks that a YAML key resolves to a file. The spec-map entry for the related §25.7 surface lists test paths and a package that do not exist on disk. Since the 2026-06-03 audit, an unrelated §04/§11 refactor (proposal 0020) relocated the `issueRunbooks` implementation from `pkg/gateway/health/runbook_links.go` to `pkg/gateway/operability/health/runbook_links.go` and dropped the spec's parenthetical file-path citation; the bundled runbook count grew from 109 to 113 (`token-usage-anomaly.md`, `node-isolation-violation.md`, and others); and two more runbooks (`ops-clock-skew`, `token-usage-anomaly`) were added to `runbook-map.yaml`, one of them (`token-usage-anomaly`) again sharing a chaos scaffold with an unrelated runbook (`agent-to-llm-partition`), reinforcing rather than resolving T-17.7.2. None of this changes any finding's disposition; the surface remains coverage-thin above tier3.
Counts: 3 High, 4 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-17.7.1 — TESTING.md §15.2 "every runbook executable end-to-end through a Tier 8 chaos test" is unmet; chaos scenarios are no-op scaffolds [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "§spec/17.7 mandates that every operational runbook (`docs/runbooks/`) is executable end-to-end through the platform's APIs rather than ad-hoc `kubectl` commands. ... Each has a Tier 8 chaos test that: 1. Triggers the runbook's condition. 2. Confirms the documented alert fires. 3. Executes the runbook's documented remediation through the API (not kubectl). 4. Asserts the system returns to healthy. 5. Confirms the audit trail records the operator action and any required justification." (TESTING.md:2065-2070)
- **Existing tests:** The chaos tests named in `tests/tier8_chaos/runbook-map.yaml` resolve to `tests/tier8_chaos/scaffolds_test.go`, where every function (`TestPostgresFailover`, `TestGatewayClockDrift`, `TestRuntimeUpgradeStuck`, `TestEmergencyRevocationDuringActiveSession`, and the rest) is a single `t.Logf(...)` that asserts nothing and defers the live exercise to "the ops backlog." A handful of real chaos tests exist (`tests/tier8_chaos/store_failure_test.go`, `component_failure_test.go`, `concurrency_test.go`, `audit_chain_test.go`, `live_session_test.go`, and the newer `nonce_only_degradation_test.go`), but none of them executes a runbook's documented remediation through the admin API, asserts return-to-healthy, or checks the audit trail for the operator action; they exercise the failure mode in isolation. No test under any tier performs the five-step runbook execution the spec describes for any runbook.
- **Gap:** The single most important normative claim of the runbook surface, that each runbook is an executable end-to-end recovery procedure, has no real test for any runbook. This is the missing user journey (an operator or agent following a runbook from alert to recovery through the API) and the missing failure-path verification (return-to-healthy plus audited operator action). Target tier8 chaos for the trigger/remediate/recover loop, with tier4 integration covering the API-driven remediation step against the compose stack where a Kind cluster is not required.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a fault-injection overlay the scaffolds note is absent (HA store topologies, KMS adapters, clock injection via `pkg/clockinject`, and a network-traffic injector). Reuse `tests/testinfra/chaos`, `tests/testinfra/kind`, `tests/testinfra/audit` for hash-chain assertions, and `tests/testinfra/clockstep`/`timectl` for the time-driven runbooks. The overlay knobs do not exist yet; building them is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier8_chaos/runbook_execution_test.go` that, for at least the P0 core runbooks (postgres-failover, redis-failure, warm-pool-exhaustion, gateway-replica-failure, minio-failure), triggers the condition, confirms the §16.5 alert fires, drives the documented `lenny-ctl`/REST remediation, asserts the health API returns to healthy, and asserts the audit trail (via `tests/testinfra/audit`) records the operator action.

### - [ ] T-17.7.2 — TestRunbookMapCoverage gate validates only key existence, not that the named test exists or exercises the runbook [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The mapping between runbook and test lives in `tests/tier8_chaos/runbook-map.yaml` and is validated by `lenny-test validate-maps`: every runbook has a matching test, and every test names its runbook." (TESTING.md:2072); "§12.8 says every runbook in docs/runbooks/ implies at least one chaos test." (tests/tier8_chaos/runbook-map.yaml:5-6)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/testinfra/chaos/runbook_map_test.go` `TestRunbookMapCoverage` walks `docs/runbooks/`, and for each alert-driven runbook it asserts only that a YAML key is present in `runbook-map.yaml` and that every mapped slug resolves to an existing `.md` file (runbook_map_test.go:121-154). It never resolves the `test:` value to a Go test function, never checks that the function exists, and never checks that the function does anything. The map itself binds dozens of distinct runbooks to the same unrelated scaffold: `warm-pool-exhaustion` → `TestPoolUpgradeRollbackDuringExpanding`, `etcd-operations` → `TestPostgresFailover`, `gateway-rate-limit-storm`/`circuit-breaker-open`/`billing-stream-backlog` → `TestRedisClusterDegraded`, and the F-17.7.4 block openly maps eight residency/audit/ops runbooks to whichever scaffold is "closest". A newly added entry continues the pattern: `token-usage-anomaly` (added since the 2026-06-03 audit) shares `TestAgentToLLMProviderPartition` with the unrelated `agent-to-llm-partition` runbook.
- **Gap:** The coverage gate that is supposed to enforce the §12.8/§17.7 "every runbook has a chaos test" contract is a structural placeholder. It produces a green signal while the underlying tests are no-ops and the mappings are arbitrary, so a regression that deletes or breaks a real chaos test would not be caught through the map. This is a spec-versus-test inconsistency that lets a regression ship. Target tier0/tier1 for the map validator hardening (resolve `test:` to a symbol and reject mapping multiple unrelated runbooks to one generic scaffold) and tier8 for the real scenarios.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today for the validator hardening (parse the tier8 test files and assert each `test:` value names a declared `func Test...`). The real per-runbook scenarios share the fault-injection dependency from T-17.7.1.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `tests/testinfra/chaos/runbook_map_test.go` to load the AST of `tests/tier8_chaos/*_test.go`, assert every `runbook-map.yaml` `test:` value resolves to a declared test function, and flag any test function bound to more than one runbook slug as an unverified shared scaffold.

### - [ ] T-17.7.3 — spec-map §25.7 entry names test files and a package that do not exist on disk [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The runbooks below are consumed by both humans and agents. For agent parsing, the structure is formalized in §25.7 ... served as structured JSON at `/v1/admin/runbooks/{name}/steps`. The `issueRunbooks` lookup table maps health-API issue codes to runbook names ..." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:776). Note: proposal 0020's gateway reorganization (commit f34e15a3) dropped the spec's former parenthetical citation of the maintaining file and, separately, moved the actual implementation from `pkg/gateway/health/runbook_links.go` to `pkg/gateway/operability/health/runbook_links.go` — the spec-map drift this finding describes has gotten worse, not better.
- **Existing tests:** `tests/spec-map.json` §25.7 (lines 3064-3077) lists `pkg/ops/runbooks/runbooks_test.go`, `pkg/ops/runbooks/steps_test.go`, and `pkg/ops/opsserver/runbooks_test.go` as the tests, and `pkg/operability/runbooks` as the package. On disk `pkg/ops/runbooks/runbooks_test.go` does not exist (the real file is `pkg/ops/runbooks/index_test.go`), and neither `pkg/operability` nor `pkg/operability/runbooks` exists at all. The §17.7 entry (spec-map.json:2551-2561) lists only `tests/tier11_docs/runbooks_test.go`, omitting the tier3 contract suite and the `pkg/gateway/operability/health/runbook_links_test.go` Path B coverage that actually exercise the surface.
- **Gap:** The spec-to-test traceability map points at a non-existent test file and a non-existent package for the runbook surface, so a dashboard query for §25.7 reports coverage that is not there, and the §17.7 entry undercounts the real coverage. A reviewer trusting the map would conclude the surface is tested by files that cannot run. This is a spec-versus-map inconsistency. Target tier0 static (the map is consumed by a tier0 cross-check).
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier0 assertion in `tests/tier0_static` that every path in `tests/spec-map.json` `tests[]` exists on disk and every `packages[]` entry is a real directory, then correct the §25.7 and §17.7 entries to the on-disk paths (`pkg/ops/runbooks/index_test.go`, `pkg/ops/runbooks/steps_test.go`, `tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/mcp_test.go`, `pkg/gateway/operability/health/runbook_links_test.go`).

### - [ ] T-17.7.4 — Runbook index/steps contract suite exercises one hardcoded stub, not the bundled docs/runbooks set [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The index is built at startup by scanning the bundled `docs/runbooks/*.md` files and parsing their front matter. No Postgres storage — runbooks are read-only artifacts shipped with the binary." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:3188); "GET /v1/admin/runbooks/{name}/steps — structured representation" (spec/25_agent-operability.md:3063)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/mcp_test.go` (`TestRunbookIndexContract`, `TestRunbookIndexFilterContract`, `TestRunbookStepsContract`, `TestRunbookStepsNotFoundContract`, lines 195-279) and `pkg/ops/opsserver/runbooks_test.go` both build the server with a `stubRunbookSource` that returns a single fabricated `warm-pool-exhaustion` runbook (helpers_test.go:82-127). The production `LoadRunbookDir` loader (`pkg/ops/opsserver/runbooks.go:34`) that reads the real `docs/runbooks/` directory has no test anywhere: a search for `LoadRunbookDir` or `DirRunbookSource` across `_test.go` files returns nothing.
- **Gap:** The wire-format contract is pinned, but the actual bundled-runbook scan that ships in the binary is never exercised. A runbook whose front matter fails to parse, whose `### ` step headings carry no `<!-- access: -->` marker, or that the loader silently drops would not be caught by the contract suite because the suite never sees the real files. This is a deployment-combination gap (the production loader path is the one operators run) and a missing failure-path test (a malformed bundled runbook). Target tier2 component (loader over the real directory) and tier3 contract (server backed by `LoadRunbookDir` rather than a stub).
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The real `docs/runbooks/` directory is the fixture; reuse `pkg/ops/opsserver.LoadRunbookDir` directly.
- **Suggested test:** Add `pkg/ops/opsserver/runbooks_loader_test.go` that calls `LoadRunbookDir("../../../docs/runbooks")`, asserts every bundled runbook parses and produces at least one structured step, then re-run the tier3 `mcp_test.go` runbook cases against a server constructed with the directory-backed source so the index and `/steps` contract is verified against the shipped set.

### - [ ] T-17.7.5 — No integration or e2e journey: agent receives alert_fired, fetches the linked runbook, and follows Path A/B/C discovery [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "This closes the loop for the most common automated path: agent calls health API → sees degraded component with suggested action → fetches the linked runbook for full context → executes the appropriate steps." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:3221); "alert_fired events ... include a `runbook` field when the alert's `runbook` annotation is set." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:3240)
- **Existing tests:** Path B is unit-tested in isolation: `pkg/gateway/operability/health/runbook_links_test.go` pins `RunbookForIssue` for the eight §17.7 line 741 issue codes and the aggregator back-fill of `suggestedActions[].runbook`. The discovery filters are unit-tested in `pkg/ops/runbooks/index_test.go`. No test connects the pieces: there is no test where a health probe reports a degraded component, the agent reads the `runbook` field, calls `GET /v1/admin/runbooks/{name}` and `/steps`, and selects the access path matching its capability. A search for runbook references across `tests/tier4_integration` returns nothing.
- **Gap:** The end-to-end discovery loop that the spec calls "the most common automated path" is unverified above the unit tier. The individual links are tested, but the chain from alert/health signal to runbook fetch to step selection is not. This is a missing real user journey (an operator agent diagnosing a degraded platform). Target tier4 integration against the compose stack with the gateway health API and `lenny-ops` runbook index both live.
- **Dependencies:** Requires `lenny-ops` and the gateway running together in the compose stack with the bundled runbook index loaded. Reuse `tests/testinfra/gateway`, `tests/testinfra/stubs` for an unhealthy-component probe, and `tests/testinfra/sdkhelper` for the agent caller. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/runbook_discovery_test.go` that forces a component into the `WARM_POOL_EXHAUSTED` state, reads `GET /v1/admin/health`, extracts `suggestedActions[].runbook`, then fetches `/v1/admin/runbooks/{name}` and `/steps` and asserts the returned step exposes the `api` access path the agent would execute.

### - [ ] T-17.7.6 — Machine-consumable runbook surface has no authenticated/authorization-scoped access test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "served as structured JSON at `/v1/admin/runbooks/{name}/steps`." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:776); "Diagnostic endpoints are read-only. ... It deliberately omits write scopes on `runtime`, `pool`, ... the playground never needs to mutate platform configuration." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:52, 113)
- **Existing tests:** The runbook handlers are tested only through the unauthenticated `opsserver.New(...).ServeHTTP` path in `pkg/ops/opsserver/runbooks_test.go` and the tier3 contract suite, which constructs the server with no auth middleware. `pkg/ops/opsserver/auth_test.go` exists for the auth layer generally, but no test asserts that `GET /v1/admin/runbooks` and `/steps` require a read-capable operability scope, or that a token without the operability read scope is rejected. No security-tier test covers the runbook endpoints.
- **Gap:** The runbook index and steps endpoints are part of the `/v1/admin` operability surface that the spec scopes to operability read capability, yet there is no test that the endpoints enforce that scope. An over-broad or missing scope check would expose the index to callers that should not reach it, and a regression would ship unnoticed. This is a missing adversarial/security path. Target tier9 security (scope enforcement on the operability read surface) with a tier3 negative case for the unauthorized response envelope.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the ops-server auth middleware and a token minter. Reuse `tests/testinfra/tokenservice` and `tests/testinfra/security`. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier9 case under `tests/tier9_security` (or extend `pkg/ops/opsserver/auth_test.go`) that calls `GET /v1/admin/runbooks` and `/v1/admin/runbooks/{name}/steps` with a token lacking the operability read scope and asserts a 403 with the §25.2 error envelope, and with the correct scope asserts 200.

### - [ ] T-17.7.7 — Runbook-as-procedure validation is absent for the multi-step admin-API remediations (drift-snapshot tail, stuck-finalizer, legal-hold quota, feature-flag downgrade) [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Treat this step as a permanent tail of every hotfix runbook entry in this section." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:868, drift-snapshot-refresh); "Remove the finalizer: `kubectl patch sandbox ... '/metadata/finalizers'` ... Do not remove the finalizer until the claim is resolved." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:838-841, stuck-finalizer); the legal-hold decision tree paths A and B (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:873); the feature-flag downgrade remediation (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:878).
- **Existing tests:** The underlying mechanisms have unit/component coverage: `POST /v1/admin/drift/snapshot/refresh` is tested in `pkg/ops/opsserver/drift_test.go` and `tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/drift_test.go`; finalizer removal logic in `pkg/controller/sandbox/finalizer_internal_test.go`; legal-hold quota alert in `pkg/alerting/rules/rules_test.go`; the feature-flag downgrade acknowledgement event in `pkg/observability/audit/catalog_test.go`. None of these assembles the runbook's ordered procedure: there is no test that the drift-snapshot refresh is invoked as the documented tail after a hotfix remediation, that the stuck-finalizer guard (active `SandboxClaim` or non-terminal Postgres state) actually blocks removal, or that the legal-hold path-B freeze rejects new checkpoint writes with `STORAGE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` while retaining held checkpoints.
- **Gap:** The spec describes these as ordered, safety-gated procedures with explicit "do not proceed" conditions, but only the isolated endpoints are tested. The decision logic and the safety gates that protect against data loss or spoliation are unverified as procedures. This is a partial-coverage finding (the happy-path primitive is tested, the guarded procedure is not) and a missing failure path (the "do not remove" / freeze branches). Target tier4 integration for the API-driven procedures and tier8 chaos for the stuck-finalizer guard under a live terminating Sandbox.

## §17.8 Capacity Planning and Defaults <a id="t-17.8"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/17_deployment-topology.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The static and Helm-unit layers cover §17.8 well: `charts/lenny/tests/tier-presets_test.yaml` asserts the per-tier replica counts, ResourceQuota rows, ops self-health cadence, stream MAXLEN, billing stream MAXLEN, and the Tier 3 podAntiAffinity, `tests/tier0_static/core_deployment_inventory_test.go` fail-closes on a missing mandatory `lenny-ops` resource, and `pkg/controller/poolscaling/*_test.go` pins the tier-default `safety_factor`, the scaling formula, and bootstrap-stays-at-static behavior at unit level. Since the 2026-06-03 audit, the §17.8.2 cold-start bootstrap convergence state machine and the operator-facing `bootstrap-override` admin API — previously wholly unimplemented — landed in full (F-17.8.3, commit `2b745ebb`), with a component-level admin-router test, a convergence-evaluator unit suite, and controller-side bootstrap/converge/hold tests; T-17.8.2.1 is resolved. Proposal 0002 also renamed the §5.2 execution-mode terminology this section's delegation-sizing formula depends on (task-mode/concurrent-mode → `recycle.enabled`/`maxConcurrentSessions`), and the renamed model now has reconciler-level (fake-client) tests driving `Sync()` end to end for cold-start, converged, bounded, and error-fallback mode-factor paths; T-17.8.2.5 is rewritten to reflect this but stays open because no envtest-backed component test or delegation-echo-driven integration test exists yet. A new §25.8 registry/upgrade-watchdog Helm-unit case now covers `lenny-ops` `platform.registry.url` resolution, narrowing T-17.8.6.1 and T-17.8.6.2 to the still-uncovered `lenny-backup` component and the still-absent `--skip-preflight` flag and `docs/deployment/air-gap.md` file. Component, integration, e2e, and chaos coverage above the unit/Helm layer otherwise remains thin exactly as before: the `failover_claims_served_fraction ≥ 0.99` SLO is never exercised under a real failover, the tier capacity targets still run only as health-rate smoke checks, the ResourceQuota-block and PDB-drain failure paths are still unexercised at runtime, the tier-promotion go/no-go workflow still has no integration or e2e test, and `tests/spec-map.json` for §17.8.4 still references tier names and files that do not exist. Counts: 3 High open (1 High resolved), 6 Medium, 2 Low, 2 Info.

### Findings

### - [x] T-17.8.2.1 — Bootstrap convergence state machine and operator override API are unimplemented and untested [High] — RESOLVED 2b745ebb (closes BUILD-GAPS.md F-17.8.3)
- **Resolution:** Commit `2b745ebb` ("F-17.8.3: §17.8.2 cold-start bootstrap admin API + status signaling") implements the full §17.8.2 step 3/4 procedure and its tests. `pkg/gateway/poolstore` gained a nullable `BootstrapMinWarm` override with a Postgres/Memory round-trip (migration `0137`, `migrations/pool_bootstrap_min_warm_test.go`); `pkg/gateway/admin/pools.go` (now re-exported under `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin`) added `PUT {bootstrapMinWarm}`, an idempotent `DELETE /v1/admin/pools/{name}/bootstrap-override`, and a `GET` response carrying the `bootstrapStatus` object (`active`, `bootstrapMinWarm`, `hoursOfData`, `estimatedConvergenceAt`), exercised end to end against the router in `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/pools_bootstrap_test.go` (for example `TestPutBootstrapMinWarmAndGetStatus_spec_17_8_2`). `SandboxWarmPoolStatus` gained `scalingMode` (`bootstrap`/`formula`) and `bootstrapHoursOfData`. The new `pkg/controller/poolscaling/convergence` package implements and unit-tests all four exit criteria (≥48h data, 2-hour/20%-variance stability tracker, no `WarmPoolLow` in 6h, 3× bootstrap-override cap with the `PoolBootstrapUnderprovisioned` warning) across fourteen cases in `convergence_test.go` (for example `TestConverged_AllCriteriaMet_spec_17_8_2`, `TestConverged_BlockedByInstability_spec_17_8_2`, `TestConverged_BlockedByWarmPoolLow_spec_17_8_2`, `TestUnderprovisioned_Boundary_spec_17_8_2`). `pkg/controller/poolscaling/bootstrap_meter.go` emits `lenny_pool_bootstrap_mode`, `lenny_pool_bootstrap_target_min_warm`, and `lenny_pool_bootstrap_min_warm_override`, tested in `bootstrap_mode_test.go`. The operator journey (deploy a pool, accumulate traffic, confirm or force convergence) is now covered by unit and component-level (in-process HTTP router) tests; the gap this finding named is closed.

### - [ ] T-17.8.2.2 — Failover-warm-serve SLO (the validation gate for `safety_factor`) is never exercised under a real failover [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Failover-warm-serve SLO (validation gate for `safety_factor`). Production deployments SHOULD measure `lenny_warmpool_failover_claims_served_fraction` ... The target is ≥ 0.99 ... If this SLO is not met over a rolling 30-day window containing at least one observed failover event (or a chaos-drill synthetic failover ...), the `safety_factor` is under-sized ... and MUST be increased." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1047)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog.go:198` defines the `lenny_warmpool_failover_claims_served_fraction` gauge and `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog_test.go:73` asserts the metric is registered. No test in `tests/tier8_chaos/` injects a warm-pool controller failover and asserts the served fraction stays at or above 0.99; the chaos suite (`tests/tier8_chaos/store_failure_test.go`, `leader_election_test.go`, `component_failure_test.go`, `pod_disruption_test.go`) still covers Postgres, Redis, MinIO, leader-election failover, and pod disruption but not the warm-pool claim-serve fraction during a controller failover window.
- **Gap:** The spec names this metric the explicit validation gate for the per-tier `safety_factor` and the Tier 3 1.2 multiplier, yet no chaos drill produces a failover and measures whether claims continue to be served from the warm pool. This is the adversarial or failure scenario for the entire warm-pool sizing model; without it the 1.2 / 1.5 factors are asserted only as arithmetic at unit level and never validated against the failure mode they exist to cover.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier8 chaos harness (`tests/testinfra/chaos`) to kill the active WarmPoolController leader during a sustained claim load, the `tests/testinfra/loadgen` building block to drive the claim rate, and the `tests/testinfra/clockstep` or metric-scrape helper to compute the served fraction over the `failover_seconds + pod_warmup_seconds` window. The leader-kill primitive exists in `leader_election_test.go`; the claim-serve-fraction measurement does not.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier8_chaos/warmpool_failover_serve_fraction_test.go` that drives a steady claim rate against a tier-sized pool, kills the WPC leader, and asserts `lenny_warmpool_failover_claims_served_fraction` remains ≥ 0.99 across the post-failover window, reusing `tests/testinfra/chaos` and `tests/testinfra/loadgen`.

### - [ ] T-17.8.2.3 — Per-tier capacity targets are run as health-rate smoke checks, not capacity assertions [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Gateway replicas (min / max) ... 5 / 30 ... Stream Proxy maxConcurrent ... 20,000 ... maxSessionsPerReplica ... 400" and the Tier 3 ResourceQuota of `pods: 15000` sized for "up to 10,000 active session pods". (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:954-969, 1093, 1106)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier12_load_cloud/session_mode_test.go` and `task_mode_test.go` still run scenarios such as `session_pod_claim` and `session_streaming_throughput`, each ending in `assertScenarioRan` (`tests/tier12_load_cloud/scaffolds_test.go:196`), which only fails when the request error rate exceeds 10% and otherwise logs the p99 as a captured baseline. `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go:488 TestFullSystemLoadBaseline` remains `t.Skip`-ped as phase-gated ("captured at the Phase 13.5 release gate ... not from a PR-cadence Kind smoke run"). No test asserts that a tier-sized deployment actually sustains the tier's concurrent-session ceiling, the per-replica session capacity, or the warm-pool claim rate within the published latency SLO.
- **Gap:** The §17.8.2 tier numbers (10,000 sessions at Tier 3, 400 sessions per replica, 30 max replicas) are the load-bearing capacity claims of the entire section and are exercised only as a "the gateway did not error out" smoke check. The deployment-combination gap is that no tier (1, 2, or 3) has a load test that pins the published capacity target as a pass criterion. This is the user journey of operating a tier at its stated ceiling.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the cloud-load cluster (`tests/testinfra/cloud`) sized to the tier, the `tests/testinfra/loadgen` scenarios already present, and a tightening of `assertScenarioRan` (or a new assertion helper) that compares sustained concurrent sessions and claim-queue-wait p99 against the tier target rather than only the error rate. The cloud cluster and loadgen exist; the capacity assertion does not.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `tests/tier12_load_cloud/session_mode_test.go` with a `TestTier3SessionCeiling` that holds the Tier 3 concurrent-session target and asserts `lenny_pod_claim_queue_wait_seconds` p99 < 2s and zero OOMKills, using `tests/testinfra/cloud` and the existing `session_pod_claim` scenario at full volume.

- **Spec/Doc:** "Air-gapped deployments mirror all Lenny-published images into a private registry, set `platform.registry.url` to that registry, and rely on `--skip-preflight` for environments where the preflight Job cannot reach the mirrored registry ... The procedure is documented in `docs/deployment/air-gap.md`. The chart's `ImageResolver` ... composes every image reference ... ensuring the gateway, `lenny-ops`, controllers, `lenny-backup`, and the warm-pool controller all honor the same registry configuration." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1369)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/common/registry/resolver_test.go` covers the resolver at unit level (override-wins, digest enforcement, URL composition). `charts/lenny/tests/gateway-deployment_test.yaml:494`, `controller-deployment_test.yaml:279`, and `pool-scaling-controller_test.yaml:171` assert `platform.registry.url` resolution at Helm-unit level for the gateway, controller, and PSC, and `charts/lenny/tests/ops-deployment_test.yaml:124` ("passes a runtime registry override and pull secret to §25.8 lenny-ops") now asserts the same for `lenny-ops`, closing half of the two-component gap this finding originally raised. There is still no end-to-end air-gap install test, the `--skip-preflight` flag is still absent from `cmd/`, `pkg/`, and `charts/` (the chart instead implements `preflight.skipNetworkProbes`, asserted in `charts/lenny/tests/preflight-job_test.yaml` and `composition-dimensions_test.yaml`), `docs/deployment/air-gap.md` still does not exist (the `docs/deployment/` directory is absent), and no `backup-job_test.yaml` case asserts that `lenny-backup` resolves its image from `platform.registry.url`.
- **Gap:** The spec still asserts a behavior across five components and a documented air-gap procedure, but the install path is never exercised end to end, the cited `--skip-preflight` flag still does not exist (an unreconciled spec-versus-implementation inconsistency), and `lenny-backup` — the one remaining component of the five named in the registry-resolution claim — still has no registry-resolution assertion at any tier. This is both a deployment-combination gap (air-gapped topology) and a spec-versus-test inconsistency that would let a regression in `lenny-backup` image resolution ship silently.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a Kind harness with a local registry mirror and outbound egress blocked (`tests/testinfra/kind` plus a mirror-registry fixture that does not yet exist), and reconciliation of the spec wording with the implemented `preflight.skipNetworkProbes` value or addition of the `--skip-preflight` flag. The Helm-unit assertion for `lenny-backup` is buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add a Helm-unit case to `charts/lenny/tests/backup-job_test.yaml` asserting `platform.registry.url` resolution for `lenny-backup` (mirroring the new `ops-deployment_test.yaml` case), and add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/airgap_install_test.go` that installs the chart against a local mirror with egress blocked and confirms every Lenny pod pulls from the mirror, building the mirror fixture under `tests/testinfra/kind`.

### - [ ] T-17.8.2.5 — Delegation-adjusted minWarm and the mode_factor divisors are exercised at reconciler level with a fake client, but not against a live controller under delegation load [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Formula for delegation-adjusted `minWarm`: ... `minWarm >= adjusted_claim_rate * safety_factor * (failover_seconds + pod_warmup_seconds) / mode_factor + adjusted_burst_claims * pod_warmup_seconds / burst_mode_factor` ... This formula assumes a one-session-per-pod pool (`maxConcurrentSessions: 1`, `recycle.enabled: false`) when `mode_factor = 1.0` ... For delegation child pools that recycle pods (`recycle.enabled: true`) or serve concurrent sessions (`maxConcurrentSessions > 1`), apply the `mode_factor` and `burst_mode_factor` derivations from [Section 5.2] ... Omitting these divisors for a recycling pool with `recycle.maxSessionsPerPod: 50` would over-provision by up to 50x." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1053-1063; reworded by proposal 0002 from the retired task-mode/concurrent-mode terminology, commit `fe3956e8`)
- **Existing tests:** Proposal 0002 renamed the §5.2 execution-mode surface (task-mode/concurrent-mode → `recycle.enabled`/`maxConcurrentSessions`), and the strategy- and controller-level tests were renamed and expanded to match: `pkg/controller/poolscaling/strategy/strategy_test.go` now covers `TestComputeModeFactorReducesSteady` and `TestComputeServiceModeReducesBothTerms` at unit level (formerly `TestComputeTaskModeReducesSteady` / `TestComputeConcurrentModeReducesBothTerms`), and `pkg/controller/poolscaling/controller_test.go` gained a `fakeModeFactor` source and five reconciler-level tests that drive `Reconciler.Sync()` against a controller-runtime fake client end to end — `TestSyncServiceModeUsesMaxConcurrent_spec_5_2`, `TestSyncRecyclingPoolColdStartUsesBaseModeFactor`, `TestSyncRecyclingPoolNilSourceUsesBaseModeFactor`, `TestSyncRecyclingPoolConvergedUsesObservedMedian`, `TestSyncRecyclingPoolMedianBoundedByMaxSessionsPerPod`, `TestSyncRecyclingPoolSourceErrorFallsBackToColdStart`, and `TestSyncSessionPoolConcurrentBurstFactor`. These assert the divisor-adjusted `minWarm` for cold-start, converged, ceiling-bounded, and error-fallback mode-factor paths, which is materially more than "pure arithmetic." No delegation-echo-driven or `tests/testinfra/envtest` (real kube-apiserver) test exists; the `Sync()` tests above still run against the controller-runtime fake client rather than a live API server or a real delegation demand source.
- **Gap:** The mode-factor divisors are the guard against a 50× over-provision and are now validated at reconciler level (fake client) for every convergence branch, closing most of the original "pure arithmetic only" gap. What remains untested is the true component/integration path: a task-mode or concurrent-mode delegation child pool sized under the tier's concurrent-delegation cap, driven by an actual delegation demand source against a real (envtest or Kind) API server, converging to the divisor-adjusted `minWarm`.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the `tests/testinfra/envtest` API server with a delegation demand source wired into the PoolScalingController, plus the `delegation-echo` test runtime to generate child sessions. The envtest harness and the delegation-echo fixtures exist under `tests/testinfra/envtest` and `tests/testinfra/fixtures`.
- **Suggested test:** Add `pkg/controller/poolscaling/delegation_modefactor_test.go` (component, envtest) that drives a recycling pool with `recycle.maxSessionsPerPod: 50` under the Tier 3 concurrent-delegation cap via a real delegation demand source and asserts the computed `minWarm` matches the divisor-adjusted formula rather than the un-divided value.
