- **Spec/Doc:** "GO — all of the following must be true: Phase 13.5 load tests passed all four checks ... LLM Proxy ... below 0.3:1 ... `lenny_gateway_gc_pause_p99_ms` ... below 50 ms ... KEDA is deployed and validated ... etcd ... sufficient for ~800 CRD status writes/s. NO-GO — any of the following blocks promotion ..." and Step 3 applies the Tier 3 Helm values, Step 4 monitors for 24 hours. (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1305-1344)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/controller/poolscaling/controller_test.go` and `charts/lenny/tests/tier-presets_test.yaml` confirm the Tier 3 column renders correctly. No test exercises the promotion as a sequence: apply Tier 2 values, run the four gate checks, apply the Tier 3 column, and confirm the post-promotion alerts (`EtcdWriteLatencyHigh`, `WarmPoolLow`, `GatewaySessionBudgetNearExhaustion`) stay quiet. `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go:488 TestFullSystemLoadBaseline`, which would back the Phase 13.5 gate, remains `t.Skip`-ped as phase-gated.
- **Gap:** The promotion guide is a procedural operator workflow with concrete pass and block criteria, and none of the gate checks or the apply-then-validate sequence is exercised against a running deployment. This is the operator journey of promoting acme from Tier 2 to Tier 3. The spec-map-exceptions classifies §17.8.3 as non-normative procedural guidance, but the gate metrics and the Helm value transition are concrete and testable.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a tier6 cloud cluster (`tests/testinfra/cloud`) able to reach Tier 2 peak load, the load generator (`tests/testinfra/loadgen`), and a metric-scrape helper to evaluate the GC-pause, proxy-ratio, and etcd-write-latency gates. The cloud harness exists; a promotion-orchestration driver does not.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/tier_promotion_test.go` that brings a Tier 2 deployment to peak, evaluates the four go-criteria metrics, applies `charts/lenny/presets/values-tier3.yaml`, and asserts the Step 4 post-promotion alerts do not fire within the monitoring window, using `tests/testinfra/cloud` and `tests/testinfra/loadgen`.

### - [ ] T-17.8.2.6 — PDB-bound gateway scale-down and node-drain serialization are untested at runtime [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The flat `maxUnavailable: 1` PDB on the gateway Deployment ... caps concurrent voluntary evictions at one across all tiers. The effective scale-down floor is therefore `1 / pod_termination_seconds` ... Operators observe the PDB-bound scale-down floor via `lenny_pdb_blocked_evictions_total` ... worst_case_single_node_drain_time = pods_on_node × terminationGracePeriodSeconds". (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:971-981)
- **Existing tests:** `charts/lenny/tests/gateway-deployment_test.yaml` and `charts/lenny/tests/autoscaling-gateway_test.yaml` assert the rendered PDB `maxUnavailable: 1` and the HPA `1 pod / 60s` scale-down policy at Helm-unit level. `tests/tier8_chaos/pod_disruption_test.go` exists for pod disruption, but a search shows no test that drains a node hosting multiple gateway pods and asserts the PDB serializes evictions to one at a time or that `lenny_pdb_blocked_evictions_total` increments during the drain.
- **Gap:** The PDB-bound scale-down floor and the node-drain serialization formula are operational safety properties (they bound the CheckpointBarrier fan-out), and they are verified only as rendered YAML. The runtime behavior, that a `kubectl drain` of a node with two or three gateway pods serializes through the PDB and surfaces the blocked-evictions metric, is unexercised. This is the failure scenario of a node-image patch or autoscaler consolidation at Tier 3.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier8 chaos harness (`tests/testinfra/chaos`) on a Kind or cloud cluster with multiple gateway replicas co-located on one node, plus a metric-scrape helper for `lenny_pdb_blocked_evictions_total`. The chaos and Kind harnesses exist; a multi-pod-per-node placement fixture is needed.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier8_chaos/gateway_pdb_drain_test.go` that schedules two gateway pods onto one node, runs `kubectl drain`, and asserts evictions occur one at a time and `lenny_pdb_blocked_evictions_total` rises during the drain, using `tests/testinfra/chaos`.

## §17.9 Deployment Answer Files <a id="t-17.9"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/17_deployment-topology.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
Static and unit coverage for §17.9 is strong: `pkg/chart/values/schema_test.go` lints every shipped catalog answer file against `values.schema.json` and asserts the full nine-file catalog is present, `pkg/ctlcli` unit tests exercise answer-file parsing and cluster-type suggestion, and Helm unit suites cover the composition-dimension NOTES summary, the backend-invariant env wiring, the MinIO lifecycle Job, and the cloud-managed PgBouncer omission. Since the 2026-06-03 audit, BUILD-GAPS finding F-17.9.2 (commit `b1e340b3`) built the previously-absent §17.9.3 cloud-managed-pooler sentinel-trigger preflight check, closing the highest-severity gap this section carried; the residual real-Postgres component-test gap for that check is split out as new finding T-17.9.3.3. `tests/tier4_integration/embedded_mode_smoke_test.go` (landed 2026-06-04, F-17.4.18, and extended through proposal 0017's embedded-mode re-architecture) now drives the full embedded-backend combination end to end, closing T-17.9.6.1. Proposal 0017 also reconciled §17.9.6/§17.9.7 to describe Embedded Mode's in-process in-memory stores (replacing the retired embedded-Postgres/local-disk-artifact-storage model), which reworded the §17.9.7 RLS-checkout-defense passage; T-17.9.7.1's quote is updated accordingly and the finding stays open. The §17.9.4 cloud object-storage lifecycle mandate remains fail-closed only for AWS S3; GCS and Azure still degrade to an advisory warning with no wired prober, and the real S3 SDK prober still has no component-level test — T-17.9.4.1 is unchanged. No integration, Kind, or cloud test installs a curated catalog answer file and verifies the resulting deployment, and the §17.9.3 cloud-managed-omission combination, the §17.9.2 air-gapped install, and the §17.9.7 exactly-one RLS defense per backend remain untested combinations.
Counts: 2 High, 6 Medium, 1 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [x] T-17.9.3.1 — Preflight does not verify the `lenny_tenant_guard` trigger exists for cloud-managed poolers, and no test covers it [High] — RESOLVED b1e340b3
- **Resolution:** BUILD-GAPS finding F-17.9.2 closed this gap. Commit `b1e340b3` (2026-06-08, "F-17.9.2: build the §17.6 preflight cloud-pooler sentinel defense check") adds `pkg/preflight/cloud_pooler_sentinel.go` (`CloudPoolerSentinelCheck` / `PoolerSentinelProber`), wires it into `pkg/preflight/run.go`'s check set, and rewires `cmd/lenny-preflight/main.go` to read a real `--postgres-dsn` flag and probe `integrity.TenantGuardCoverageGaps` (reused from `pkg/audit/integrity`) instead of discarding `--connection-pooler`. The check no-ops when `connectionPooler` is not `external`, defers to the gateway's runtime `LENNY_POOLER_MODE` defense when no DSN is wired, and fails closed when the live probe reports any tenant-scoped table lacking the trigger. `pkg/preflight/cloud_pooler_sentinel_test.go` and `pkg/preflight/run_test.go` unit-test every branch (skip-when-not-external, defer-when-no-DSN, pass-when-covered, fail-closed-with-gaps, fail-closed-on-query-error) against a fake `PoolerSentinelProber`, and `charts/lenny/tests/preflight-job_test.yaml:310-345` asserts the Job wires `--postgres-dsn` from the chart's Postgres-credentials Secret. The normative MUST this finding flagged as unimplemented now has a real fail-closed implementation with unit coverage of every decision branch. The residual gap — no test exercises the check against a real Postgres connection rather than a fake prober — is tracked as new finding T-17.9.3.3.

### - [ ] T-17.9.4.1 — Cloud object-storage lifecycle check is fail-closed only for S3; GCS and Azure have no wired prober and no component test exercises the real SDK readers [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Cloud-managed object storage buckets must be configured with the same lifecycle rules ... bucket versioning ... and delete-marker / noncurrent-version expiration ... the deployer must apply equivalent rules before installation; the preflight Job validates them." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1455) and "S3 `GetBucketVersioning` + `GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration`; GCS `storage.buckets.get` (lifecycle field); Azure `BlobServiceProperties.IsVersioningEnabled` + `ManagementPolicy` GET." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:529)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/preflight/cloud_object_storage_test.go` exercises `CloudObjectStorageLifecycleCheck.Decide` with an in-memory fake prober for the S3 and GCS decision branches and a prober-error fail-closed case. `cmd/lenny-preflight/main.go:264` wires `cloudLifecycleProber` so that only `s3` returns a real SDK reader; the comment at line 261 states "gcs/azure route through the advisory path (nil prober)." The matching test case at `pkg/preflight/cloud_object_storage_test.go:57` ("nil prober is advisory pass") asserts a cloud provider with no prober returns a `WARNING` rather than failing. The real S3 SDK prober (`s3LifecycleProber` in `cmd/lenny-preflight/main.go:149`) has no component test against a fake S3 endpoint; `cmd/lenny-preflight/main_test.go` covers only flag parsing, and `minio_sse_test.go` runs a real fake-MinIO prober for a different check.
- **Gap:** The spec mandates the lifecycle rules for all three cloud providers and documents the specific GCS and Azure SDK calls, but for `gcs` and `azure` the check silently degrades to an advisory warning, so the `gke-production.yaml` and `aks-production.yaml` answer files cannot actually validate their object storage before install. The S3 path is wired but unverified at the SDK level. The missing work is a standards-conformance and failure-path gap: a component test that the real provider readers parse versioning and lifecycle responses correctly and fail closed on a non-compliant bucket, for each of S3, GCS, and Azure. The GCS and Azure probers must be implemented first.
- **Dependencies:** Requires GCS and Azure lifecycle probers in `cmd/lenny-preflight`, plus fake provider endpoints. A fake-S3 server exists via the MinIO fixture in `tests/testinfra` (see `minio_sse_test.go`); GCS and Azure fakes or recorded-response stubs in `tests/testinfra/stubs` do not exist yet and building them is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier2_component/preflight/cloud_lifecycle_provider_test.go` running each provider's real prober against a fake endpoint that returns compliant and non-compliant lifecycle configurations, asserting pass and fail-closed respectively, referencing the MinIO fixture for S3 and new GCS/Azure stubs in `tests/testinfra/stubs`.

### - [ ] T-17.9.2.1 — No integration, Kind, or cloud test installs a curated catalog answer file and verifies the resulting deployment [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The chart ships with the following curated answer files under `deploy/helm/lenny/answers/`. ... operators layer them with `helm install -f base.yaml -f answer-file.yaml -f values-tierN.yaml -f overrides.yaml`." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1395, 1375)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/chart/values/schema_test.go:103` lints each catalog file against the schema and `pkg/ctlcli/install_test.go:807` (`TestCatalogAnswerFilesAreValid`) validates each file parses (this test moved from `cmd/lenny-ctl/install_test.go` to `pkg/ctlcli/install_test.go` under the F-24.0.1/F-17.4.9 `lenny`/`lenny-ctl` command-surface unification; same line number). `tests/tier11_docs/time_to_hello_world_test.go:295` runs `lenny-ctl install --non-interactive --answers <f> --dry-run` but writes an ad-hoc `environment: local` file and stops before invoking helm. No Helm unit suite layers a curated catalog file as a values fragment; `charts/lenny/tests/composition-dimensions_test.yaml` and `preflight-job_test.yaml` use `set:` on individual dimension values and mention the catalog only in comments.
- **Gap:** The catalog files are validated as static documents, but no test renders or installs a real catalog file (`eks-small-team.yaml`, `gke-production.yaml`, `aks-production.yaml`, `openshift-self-managed.yaml`, `bare-metal-self-managed.yaml`) layered with a tier preset and asserts the composed deployment matches its declared dimensions end to end. This is a deployment-combination gap and a real operator user journey: alice installing acme on EKS following the documented `helm install -f` layering should produce a working cloud-managed deployment.
- **Dependencies:** A Helm-render combination test is buildable today with `tests/testinfra/helm`. A self-managed end-to-end install is buildable on Kind via `tests/testinfra/kind`; cloud-managed end-to-end installs need the tier6 cloud harness (`tests/testinfra/cloud`) with managed-backend credentials.
- **Suggested test:** Add `charts/lenny/tests/catalog-render_test.yaml` (or a Go render test under `tests/tier2_component`) that layers each catalog file with its typical tier preset and asserts the rendered manifests match the declared cluster, backends, environment, and isolationProfile, plus a tier5 `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/selfmanaged_answerfile_install_test.go` that installs the bare-metal self-managed catalog file and drives one session.

### - [ ] T-17.9.3.2 — No render test asserts the complete cloud-managed omission set (PgBouncer, Sentinel, and MinIO) for a single cloud-managed answer file [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Answer files whose backends dimension is `cloud-managed` omit PgBouncer, Redis Sentinel, and MinIO resources and reference provider-native endpoints instead." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1417)
- **Existing tests:** `charts/lenny/tests/pgbouncer-deployment_test.yaml:8` asserts the PgBouncer Deployment renders nothing when `pgbouncer.deploy` is false, mapped to §12.3. `charts/lenny/tests/minio-bucket-lifecycle_test.yaml:6` asserts the MinIO lifecycle Job is skipped when MinIO is unconfigured. `charts/lenny/tests/datastore-secret_test.yaml:212` asserts Sentinel AUTH renders when `redis.provider=sentinel`. These are three separate per-resource suites driven by individual `set:` values.
- **Gap:** No single test renders a cloud-managed configuration (for example `backends: cloud-managed` with `connectionPooler: external`, `redis.provider: external`, `objectStorage.provider: s3`) and asserts that PgBouncer, Redis Sentinel, and MinIO are all absent together while the provider endpoints are wired. The §17.9.3 behavior is a combination property of the cloud-managed dimension, and verifying each omission in isolation does not prove the combined posture. This is a deployment-combination gap at the Helm-unit tier.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today with `tests/testinfra/helm`.
- **Suggested test:** Add a suite to `charts/lenny/tests/composition-dimensions_test.yaml` (or a new `cloud-managed-omission_test.yaml`) that sets the cloud-managed dimension once and asserts `hasDocuments: count: 0` for the PgBouncer Deployment, the Redis Sentinel StatefulSet, and the MinIO StatefulSet in the same render.

### - [ ] T-17.9.2.2 — The air-gapped answer file has no end-to-end install test against a private mirror with network probes skipped [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`answers/airgap-self-managed.yaml` | cluster=`vanilla`, backends=`self-managed`, `platform.registry.*` set to a private mirror, `preflight.skipNetworkProbes: true` | ... requires operator to set mirror details" (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1407)
- **Existing tests:** `charts/lenny/tests/composition-dimensions_test.yaml:43` asserts the NOTES summary notes the air-gap posture when `preflight.skipNetworkProbes` is true. `charts/lenny/tests/preflight-job_test.yaml:47` asserts the Job succeeds with no egress when `skipNetworkProbes=true`. A repo-wide grep for `airgap`, `air-gap`, or `skipNetworkProbes` across `tests/` returns only `spec-map.json`; no integration or e2e test exists.
- **Gap:** The air-gap combination (private registry mirror plus skipped network probes plus self-managed backends pulling images only from the mirror) is verified only at the Helm-unit posture level. No test confirms a deployment that pulls every image from the configured `platform.registry.*` mirror succeeds while external egress is blocked. This is a deployment-combination and adversarial-environment gap: the air-gap path is exactly where a missed external reference fails silently in production.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a Kind cluster configured with a private mirror and default-deny external egress. The tier5 Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`) exists; an in-cluster registry-mirror fixture does not yet exist and building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/airgap_install_test.go` that installs the air-gap catalog file with `platform.registry.*` pointed at an in-cluster mirror and external egress denied, then asserts all pods reach Ready by pulling solely from the mirror.

### - [ ] T-17.9.7.1 — The exactly-one RLS checkout defense invariant is not verified per backend [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "RLS checkout defense: Either `connect_query` sentinel (self-managed PgBouncer) **or** per-transaction tenant validation trigger (cloud-managed poolers without `connect_query` support) — exactly one must be active per deployment ... Embedded Mode runs the in-memory Postgres-compatible store, which carries no RLS trigger." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1576)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier4_integration/rls_tenant_guard_test.go:35` asserts the `lenny_tenant_guard` trigger fires against real Postgres (mapped to §12.3). `charts/lenny/tests/pgbouncer-config_test.yaml` covers the `connect_query` ConfigMap for the self-managed PgBouncer path. No test asserts the exactly-one property: that the self-managed backend activates the sentinel and the cloud-managed backend activates the trigger, and that the two are not both active or both absent for a given deployment.
- **Gap:** The §17.9.7 invariant is a backend-invariant correctness property that ties each backend dimension to exactly one checkout defense. The two defenses are tested in isolation, but no test exercises the per-backend selection or the mutual-exclusivity guard. This is a failure-path and deployment-combination gap: a misconfiguration that leaves neither defense active (or activates both) is the regression this invariant exists to prevent.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today with `tests/testinfra/helm` for the render selection and the tier2 real-Postgres harness in `tests/tier2_component/rls` for the active-defense assertion.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier2 test under `tests/tier2_component/rls` that, for `backends=self-managed`, asserts the sentinel is active and the trigger path is not relied upon, and for `backends=cloud-managed` asserts the trigger is the active defense, plus a Helm-unit guard that a configuration leaving both inactive fails the render.

### - [x] T-17.9.6.1 — Embedded-mode backends are not exercised as an end-to-end combination [Medium] — RESOLVED c5ebc95e
- **Resolution:** `tests/tier4_integration/embedded_mode_smoke_test.go` (`TestEmbeddedModeSmoke_spec_17_4_18`, added at commit `c5ebc95e` on 2026-06-04 as F-17.4.18 and subsequently extended through proposal 0017's embedded-mode re-architecture, notably `c37f5b6e` "embedded: tier-4 in-cluster smoke legs and the Docker-backed tier-9 security legs") drives the real `lenny` binary through `lenny up` → `lenny status` → `lenny session new` → `lenny down --purge`, asserting the embedded Kubernetes substrate reports healthy (the real-cluster path rather than a controller-simulator fallback), the gateway/controller/lenny-ops control-plane Deployments each reach Ready, and a session against the auto-seeded echo runtime places on a pod in the embedded cluster over the real §4.7 adapter boundary. This exercises the embedded-backend combination end to end, which is what this finding asked for. Proposal 0017 (commit `89f66d71` applying the spec edits) also replaced the finding's original "embedded Postgres (single-node bundle), in-process Redis, local-disk artifact storage" framing with in-process in-memory stores inside the gateway pod, so the original Suggested test's "artifact upload lands on local disk and session state persists in embedded Postgres" framing is superseded; the reconciled §17.9.6 no longer names those stores. The tier-2 component bring-up (`tests/tier2_component/embedded/bringup_test.go`) and tier-3 contract suite pin the CRD-install and pod-IP-dial legs the tier-4 smoke composes.

### - [ ] T-17.9.4.2 — The provider parity matrix omits cloud object-storage lifecycle, cloud-managed backend, and connection-pooler capability rows [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "the deployer must apply equivalent rules before installation; the preflight Job validates them." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1455) and the cloud-managed backend table (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1419-1424).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml` enumerates per-provider capabilities (gvisor_isolation, kata_isolation, multi_zone_dr, managed_ingress, cloud_csi, cloud_kms, and others), each currently marked `planned`. There is no row for object-storage lifecycle validation, cloud-managed backend selection, or the external connection pooler. `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/cluster_assertions_test.go:379` (`TestMultiAZMinIO`) mentions a per-release S3 bucket provisioned with versioning but only logs and does not assert the §17.9.4 lifecycle rules are present.
- **Gap:** The §17.9.4 lifecycle requirement and the §17.9.3 cloud-managed backend wiring are per-provider behaviors with no parity-matrix entry, so the documented cloud capability surface and the matrix have drifted. The matrix is the tier6 source of truth for which cloud capabilities are validated per provider, and the absence of these rows means the gap is invisible to the tier0 parity-matrix gate. This is an observation about coverage tracking rather than a missing assertion on its own.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today by editing `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml`; promoting the rows to `validated` requires the tier6 cloud harness and managed-backend credentials.
- **Suggested test:** Add `object_storage_lifecycle`, `cloud_managed_backend`, and `external_connection_pooler` capability rows (spec_section `17.9`) to `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml`, and extend `cluster_assertions_test.go` `TestMultiAZMinIO` to assert the bucket's versioning and noncurrent-version expiration rules are actually present when the S3 backend is active.

- **Spec/Doc:** "Each catalog fragment is linted against `charts/lenny/values.schema.json` by `pkg/chart/values.TestCatalogAnswerFilesConformToSchema` (§17.9.2 line 1374)" (charts/lenny/answers/README.md:60-62), tracking spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1409 ("The chart CI lints every shipped answer file against `values.schema.json`").

The README and `BUILD-GAPS.md` reference it as `TestCatalogAnswerFilesConformToSchema` without the `_spec_17_9_2_1374` suffix. A second valid lint, `pkg/ctlcli/install_test.go:807` (`TestCatalogAnswerFilesAreValid`, moved from `cmd/lenny-ctl/install_test.go` under F-24.0.1/F-17.4.9), also covers the catalog. The lint behavior itself is present and asserts the full nine-file catalog conforms.

- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Update the `charts/lenny/answers/README.md:62` reference to the full function name `TestCatalogAnswerFilesConformToSchema_spec_17_9_2_1374`, or add a documentation cross-reference assertion in `tests/tier11_docs` that the named test function exists.

### - [ ] T-17.9.3.3 — `CloudPoolerSentinelCheck` / `TenantGuardCoverageGaps` has no component test against a real Postgres connection [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The preflight Job verifies this trigger exists when `connectionPooler = external`." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:1422) and "Cloud-managed pooler sentinel defense | When `postgres.connectionPooler = external`: connect to Postgres, verify the per-transaction tenant validation trigger exists on tenant-scoped tables (query `pg_trigger` for the `lenny_tenant_guard` trigger). If absent, fail." (spec/17_deployment-topology.md:523)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/preflight/cloud_pooler_sentinel_test.go` (`TestCloudPoolerSentinelCheck_spec_17_6_488`) and `pkg/preflight/run_test.go:417` exercise `CloudPoolerSentinelCheck.Decide` entirely against an in-memory `PoolerSentinelProbeFunc` fake. `pkg/audit/integrity/pooler_test.go` exercises `TenantGuardCoverageGaps`'s `pg_trigger` catalog query against a fake `pgx.Rows` implementation (`fakeRows`), not a real connection. A grep across `tests/tier2_component`, `tests/tier4_integration`, and `tests/testinfra` for `TenantGuardCoverageGaps`, `CloudPoolerSentinelCheck`, or `PoolerSentinelProber` returns only the two unit-test files above; no test runs the query against a live Postgres instance with the `lenny_tenant_guard` trigger present on some tables and absent on others.
- **Gap:** F-17.9.2 (commit `b1e340b3`) built the check and unit-tested every decision branch with a fake prober, but the catalog query itself (`pg_trigger` join logic in `integrity.TenantGuardCoverageGaps`) has never run against a real Postgres schema. A syntax error, a wrong join condition, or a Postgres-version-specific `pg_trigger` column difference would pass every existing unit test (which only stub the `pgx.Rows` interface) yet fail or silently misreport against a real database, defeating the fail-closed guarantee this is the sole programmatic defense for. This is a component-tier gap on a security-relevant install check.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today with the tier2 real-Postgres harness already used by `tests/tier2_component/rls` (the same migrated schema `lenny_tenant_guard` triggers onto).
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier2_component/preflight/tenant_guard_trigger_test.go` that runs `integrity.TenantGuardCoverageGaps` against a real migrated Postgres with the trigger present on all tenant-scoped tables (expect empty gaps) and with the trigger dropped from one table (expect that table named in the gaps), then drives `CloudPoolerSentinelCheck.Decide` end to end against the same connection for both cases.

## §24.0-24.4 lenny-ctl: Install, Bootstrap, Preflight, Runtime and Pool Management <a id="t-24.0-24.4"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/24_lenny-ctl-command-reference.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
Every command in §24.0 through §24.4 has tier1 unit coverage under `pkg/ctlcli` (the CLI now delegates from a thin `cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go` shim to `pkg/ctlcli` per the code-best-practices cmd/-stays-thin rule; all subcommand tests moved with it) that asserts HTTP request shaping, exit codes, and flag validation against `httptest` stubs and fake Kubernetes clients, and the gateway-side handlers for bootstrap, runtimes, and pools carry handler-level unit tests under `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin` (moved from `pkg/gateway/admin` by the 0020 S12 external-API-surface refactor). Since the 2026-06-03 audit, three previously-flagged absences were substantially built out: `lenny-ctl doctor` / `doctor --fix` now has a full implementation (`pkg/ops/doctor`, `cmd/lenny-ops/doctorremediator.go`) with unit coverage of every guardrail and the operation-ID audit trail; the §10.5 RuntimeUpgrade operator surface (durable Postgres-backed record, manager, and admin API) landed with a solid unit/handler-level test layer alongside the pre-existing `pkg/runtime/upgrade/state` enum tests; and `exit-bootstrap` plus `circuit-breaker` gained both CLI and handler tests. A new `admin runtimes register --manifest <f>` command was also added to §24.3 and has CLI unit coverage. The component, integration, and e2e tiers remain almost entirely absent. TESTING.md §15.1 still promises that every §24 subcommand has at least one tier4 integration test against the compose stack plus a tier5 Kind test for cluster-affecting commands, but no tier4 or tier5 test invokes any `lenny-ctl` command, the declared suites `admin_bootstrap` (tier4), `bootstrap_first_install` (tier5, named in the PR critical-path subset), and `pool_upgrade` (tier5) still do not exist on disk, and the tier4 bootstrap scaffold still points readers at a non-existent `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/bootstrap_test.go`. The standalone preflight mode is still never exercised against real Postgres, Redis, or MinIO; the §24.3 runtime tenant-access endpoints have handler-level coverage but still no integration test proving a grant gates session creation; the new `admin pools upgrade start/proceed/pause/resume/rollback/status` CLI dispatch has zero test coverage at any tier despite the underlying state machine's improved unit layer; and the §24.0 krew, `kubectl-lenny`, and cosign-signed-binary packaging claims are still not verified by any test.
Counts: 6 High, 3 Medium, 4 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-24.0-24.4.1 — spec-map lists a package glob instead of real tests for every §24.0–24.4 section, and TESTING.md §15.1 claims tier4/tier5 coverage that does not exist [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Every documented subcommand in §spec/24 (sections §spec/24.0–§spec/24.20) has at least one Tier 4 integration test against the compose stack and, for cluster-affecting commands, a Tier 5 Kind test." (TESTING.md:2040). spec-map.json entries §24.0 through §24.4 each still list `"cmd/lenny-ctl/..."` as the only test and `packages: ["cmd/lenny-ctl"]` (tests/spec-map.json, `sections["24.0"]`–`sections["24.4"]`).
- **Existing tests:** The spec-map glob `cmd/lenny-ctl/...` is now doubly stale: it was already a package-path placeholder rather than a test pointer, and since the F-24.0.1/F-17.4.9 unification (commit fd2d69ee, 2026-06-08) `cmd/lenny-ctl` contains no subcommand test files at all — every §24 CLI test moved to `pkg/ctlcli` (`pkg/ctlcli/main_test.go`, `pkg/ctlcli/preflight_test.go`, `pkg/ctlcli/quota_pools_cli_test.go`, `pkg/ctlcli/tenant_access_test.go`, `pkg/ctlcli/runtime_test.go`, `pkg/ctlcli/ops_test.go`), so the glob no longer even resolves to the right directory. No tier4 or tier5 test invokes a `lenny-ctl` command; grep across tests/tier4_integration, tests/tier5_e2e_kind, and tests/tier6_e2e_cloud finds no reference to the CLI binary or its subcommands beyond the deferred scaffolds.
- **Gap:** The declared integration and e2e coverage layer for the entire CLI surface in scope is missing, and the spec-map records a glob that cannot be validated against a requirement and now points at the wrong package entirely, so a regression in any §24.0–24.4 command ships without a component-or-higher test failing. This is a spec-versus-test inconsistency and an integration-tier gap.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier4 compose harness (tests/testinfra/compose plus tests/testinfra/gateway) that already backs tests/tier4_integration/environment_test.go, and the tier5 Kind harness (tests/testinfra/kind). Both exist today.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/lenny_ctl_test.go that builds the `cmd/lenny-ctl` binary and drives bootstrap, `admin pools list/get`, and `admin runtimes list-access` against the real cmd/lenny-gateway binary on the compose stack, then update tests/spec-map.json §24.0–24.4 to cite `pkg/ctlcli` (not `cmd/lenny-ctl`) and the resulting test functions.

### - [ ] T-24.1.1 — `lenny-ctl bootstrap` idempotent re-run and dry-run diff have no integration or Kind test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`lenny-ctl bootstrap --from-values <file>` | Apply seed configuration (runtimes, pools, tenants, users) using upsert semantics" and "`--dry-run` ... Validate seed file and report what would be created/updated without making changes" (spec/24_lenny-ctl-command-reference.md:34-35). The §14 suite `admin_bootstrap` requires "idempotent re-run succeeds; dry-run shows accurate diff" (TESTING.md:1039).
- **Existing tests:** pkg/ctlcli/main_test.go (moved from cmd/lenny-ctl/main_test.go by commit fd2d69ee; TestBootstrapAppliesJSONSeedFile, TestBootstrapAppliesYAMLSeedFile, TestBootstrapDryRunAndForceUpdateQuery_spec_24_1_35, TestBootstrapExitCodeMapping_spec_17_6_420) assert the CLI emits POST /v1/admin/bootstrap with the right body, query, and exit code against an `httptest` stub. pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/bootstrap_test.go and bootstrap_tier_test.go (moved from pkg/gateway/admin by the 0020 S12 refactor) assert upsert, skip-on-identical, force-update, and dry-run no-persist at the handler level with an in-memory tenantstore. TESTING.md §13.9 still records `tests/tier4_integration/admin_bootstrap_test.go` as deferred (TESTING.md:1596) and the file is still absent. The tier4 scaffold TestAdminBootstrap (tests/tier4_integration/scaffolds_test.go:54) still logs that the composite flow is exercised by `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/bootstrap_test.go`, which still does not exist.
- **Gap:** No test drives `lenny-ctl bootstrap` against a live gateway over real Postgres, runs the same seed file twice to prove the second run reports skips rather than errors, or asserts the dry-run output reports the same create/update set the apply run would produce. The idempotency and accurate-diff guarantees that operators rely on for repeated installs are unverified end to end. This is a real user journey (an operator re-seeding Day-1 state) and an integration-tier gap.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier4 compose harness with real Postgres (tests/testinfra/compose, tests/testinfra/gateway). The note in TESTING.md §13.9 that "lenny-ctl does not yet implement the bootstrap subcommand" is stale; `pkg/ctlcli` now implements it. None — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/admin_bootstrap_test.go that runs `lenny-ctl bootstrap --from-values` twice against the compose gateway, asserts the first run creates and the second run reports `skippedCount` for unchanged resources, then runs `--dry-run` and asserts the previewed diff matches the apply outcome.

### - [ ] T-24.2.1 — `lenny-ctl doctor` and `doctor --fix` now have a full implementation with solid unit coverage, but no component or e2e test exercises a real remediation [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`lenny-ctl doctor` | Run a richer diagnostic pass combining `preflight` checks with the server-side diagnostic endpoints ... Outputs a remediation report." and "`lenny-ctl doctor --fix` | Run `lenny-ctl doctor` and apply the auto-remediations ... Each remediation is logged with the corresponding operation ID." (spec/24_lenny-ctl-command-reference.md:44-45).
- **Existing tests:** This finding is substantially superseded by commit d4aaeb12 (2026-06-03, hours after this audit was generated: "F-25.6.2/F-24.2.3: §25.6 doctor fix=true auto-remediation + lenny-ctl doctor"), which built the command end to end. pkg/ctlcli/ops_test.go (TestDoctorReadOnly, TestDoctorFixSetsQuery, TestDoctorFindingsFlag) asserts the CLI POSTs to `/v1/admin/diagnostics/run[?fix=true]` with the parsed `--findings` list. pkg/ops/doctor/doctor_test.go (13 test functions) unit-tests the orchestrator: read-only detection, fix-mode apply-and-emit, the `maintenanceMode` guard, the `allowedFixes` guard, the per-fix opt-out, apply-error handling, manual-remediation reporting for non-fixable and requested-but-not-detected findings, and the `doctor-` operation-ID prefix, including that `fix_started` carries `operationId`/`findings`/`principal`. cmd/lenny-ops/doctorremediator_test.go (8 test functions) exercises the production `k8sDoctorRemediator` against a fake Kubernetes clientset (`k8s.io/client-go/kubernetes/fake` and `dynamic/fake`) for both fixable-finding codes named in the spec (`coreDnsStuckEndpoint`, `certManagerExpiring`), including the not-detected and opt-out branches. No test exercises the remediator against a real (envtest or Kind) apiserver, and no test induces a real degraded CoreDNS or cert-manager and confirms `lenny-ctl doctor --fix` against a live cluster actually restores it.
- **Gap:** The command and its `--fix` auto-remediation are now implemented and heavily unit-tested with fake Kubernetes objects, including the audited operation-ID trail the spec requires. The remaining gap is verification against a real cluster: no component-tier test proves the CoreDNS restart or cert-manager reissuance actually executes against a live apiserver rather than a fake clientset's in-memory objects, and no tier5 Kind test induces a genuine fault, runs the CLI, and observes recovery end to end. This is now a component/e2e verification gap rather than a missing capability.
- **Dependencies:** A tier2 test needs an envtest apiserver (already used elsewhere under tests/tier2_component). The `--fix` tier5 case needs a Kind environment with a degradable CoreDNS or cert-manager (tests/testinfra/kind plus tests/testinfra/chaos to induce the fault).
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier2_component/ops/doctor_remediation_test.go driving `k8sDoctorRemediator` against a real envtest apiserver with a stuck CoreDNS Deployment and an expiring cert-manager Certificate, asserting the live restart/reissuance; add tests/tier5_e2e_kind/doctor_fix_test.go that induces the same faults on a Kind cluster, runs `lenny-ctl doctor --fix`, and asserts the cluster recovers and an operation-ID audit event is written (tests/testinfra/audit).

- **Spec/Doc:** "In standalone mode ... the CLI embeds the full preflight check logic and probes infrastructure directly from the caller's machine — no running Lenny deployment is required. ... The §14 domain-suite line names "Preflight: DSN precedence ... probe timeouts respected." (TESTING.md:2043).

This is a component-tier gap on the primary use case of the command.

### - [ ] T-24.3.1 — Runtime tenant-access grant, list, and revoke have handler-level coverage but still no integration test proving a grant gates session creation [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`lenny-ctl admin runtimes grant-access --runtime <name> --tenant <id>` | Grant a tenant access to a runtime" with the matching list-access and revoke-access rows mapping to `/v1/admin/runtimes/{name}/tenant-access` (spec/24_lenny-ctl-command-reference.md:54-56; shifted by one line from 53-55 by the new `admin runtimes register` row inserted above it). The §14 line names "Runtime management: grant-access, revoke-access, list-access." (TESTING.md:2044).
- **Existing tests:** pkg/ctlcli/tenant_access_test.go (moved from cmd/lenny-ctl/tenant_access_test.go by commit fd2d69ee) asserts the CLI emits POST, GET, and DELETE to the tenant-access paths against an `httptest` stub. pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/tenant_access_test.go (moved from pkg/gateway/admin by the 0020 S12 refactor) does carry handler-level coverage the original audit missed: TestGrantRuntimeTenantAccess, TestGrantTenantAccessIdempotent, TestListRuntimeTenantAccess, TestRevokeRuntimeTenantAccess, TestPoolTenantAccess, the tenant-scoped list/get variants, the 404-on-missing-runtime/pool cases, the §16.7 audit-event-naming assertion, and an RBAC-required-platform-admin case — this file was already present at audit time (pre-dating 2026-06-03) and the original finding's grep against `pkg/gateway/admin/runtimes_test.go` alone missed it. No tier4 or tier5 test grants access through the CLI and then verifies the gate against a real session request.

What remains missing is the integration-level proof the finding's title names: that a tenant without a grant is denied a session on the runtime, a grant admits it, and a revoke removes the access, driven through the real `lenny-ctl` CLI and a real gateway. A handler regression is now caught at tier1; an authorization-effect regression in how the grant actually gates a session is not caught anywhere. This is a missing user journey and a missing adversarial path, narrower than originally scoped.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier4 compose harness with the real gateway and a tenant store (tests/testinfra/gateway, tests/testinfra/sessiondriver to attempt the gated session). None — buildable today.

TESTING.md §13.10 still records `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/pool_upgrade_test.go` as deferred (TESTING.md:1543); the file is still absent. The tier8 scaffold for "pool upgrade rollback during expanding" (tests/tier8_chaos/scaffolds_test.go:157, TestPoolUpgradeRollbackDuringExpanding) still logs that the live rollback exercise is on the backlog. The prior citation of pkg/ops/upgradeservice/pgstore/pgstore_test.go as covering "the persistence layer" was a mischaracterization even at audit time — that package implements the unrelated §25.8 platform-upgrade orchestrator (`lenny-ctl upgrade`, not `admin pools upgrade`) and is not part of this command's surface.

This is a missing user journey and a missing failure-path (rollback) test, plus a newly-introduced CLI-unit gap.

- **Spec/Doc:** "`lenny-ctl admin pools exit-bootstrap --pool <name>` | Remove the bootstrap `minWarm` override and switch to formula-driven scaling immediately, regardless of the 48-hour convergence window." mapping to DELETE /v1/admin/pools/{name}/bootstrap-override (spec/24_lenny-ctl-command-reference.md:65; shifted by one line from 64 by the new `admin runtimes register` row in §24.3 above).
- **Existing tests:** This finding is substantially superseded since the audit. pkg/ctlcli/main_test.go (TestAdminPoolsExitBootstrap, TestAdminPoolsExitBootstrapRequiresPool, added by commit 67c648af "F-24.4.1: wire the missing §24.4 admin pools CLI subcommands", 2026-06-08) asserts the CLI emits DELETE /v1/admin/pools/{name}/bootstrap-override and exits 2 without `--pool`. pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/pools_bootstrap_test.go (present since commit 2b745ebb, 2026-06-04, one day after the audit) covers the handler: TestDeleteBootstrapOverride_spec_17_8_2 (clears the stored override and confirms GET no longer carries a `bootstrapStatus` object, plus an audit event), TestDeleteBootstrapOverrideIdempotent_spec_17_8_2 (a repeat DELETE is a 200 no-op), and TestDeleteBootstrapOverrideMissingPool_spec_17_8_2 (404 on an unknown pool).
- **Gap:** The command, the DELETE endpoint, its idempotency, its 404 case, and its audit emission are now tested at the CLI and handler tiers. What is not tested anywhere is the substantive behavior the spec names: that clearing the override actually switches the pool's effective `minWarm` to the formula-computed value before the 48-hour convergence window closes. The handler test only asserts the stored `BootstrapMinWarm` field becomes nil; no test drives the PoolScalingController to observe the resulting scaling decision. This is now a narrow integration-verification gap rather than a missing-coverage gap.
- **Dependencies:** The integration assertion needs the tier4 compose gateway with the PoolScalingController and a pool carrying a bootstrap override (tests/testinfra/gateway). None — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier4 case in tests/tier4_integration/pool_ops_test.go that sets a bootstrap override via the admin API, calls `lenny-ctl admin pools exit-bootstrap`, and asserts the pool's effective `minWarm` (as observed via `admin pools get` or the PoolScalingController's applied CRD spec) follows the formula rather than the cleared override.

## §24.5-24.10 lenny-ctl: Credentials, Quota, Breakers, Adapters, Users, Tenants <a id="t-24.5-24.10"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/24_lenny-ctl-command-reference.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The `lenny-ctl` command surface for credentials, quota, breakers, adapters, users, and tenants has unit-level CLI mapping tests (each asserts the subcommand resolves to the correct HTTP method, path, and body against a `httptest` fake gateway) plus gateway-side handler tests (component-style, with faked revokers, validators, and reconcilers). The proposal-0020 refactor moved both surfaces: the CLI logic now lives in `pkg/ctlcli` (`cmd/lenny-ctl/main.go` is a thin wrapper that delegates to it), and the gateway admin handlers moved from `pkg/gateway/admin` to `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin`; every file:line reference below is updated to the current location. Two substantive changes landed since the prior review: (1) proposal 0021 replaced `admin users rotate-token`'s client-driven RFC 8693 token-exchange-plus-CLI-Secret-patch with a dedicated, gateway-internal `POST /v1/admin/users/{user}/rotate-token` route that mints, patches the Secret, and durably revokes the superseded token with **no grace period** (F-CTL-1), which inverts the "graceful handoff" premise this section's T-24.9.8 finding tested for and is now thoroughly unit/component-tested (T-24.9.8 resolved below); (2) the §12.8 Phase 3.5 legal-hold force-delete path (F-12.8.2/F-24.10.2) landed end to end — CLI subcommand, gateway handler, controller override branch, escrow migrator, and audit/alert wiring all exist with component tests — narrowing T-24.10.1 to its still-missing Tier 4/Tier 8 layers. The section still lacks the Tier 4 integration coverage that TESTING.md §15.1 mandates ("Every documented subcommand in §spec/24 has at least one Tier 4 integration test against the compose stack and, for cluster-affecting commands, a Tier 5 Kind test"): no test drives the `lenny-ctl` binary against a live gateway plus real backing services for any of these six command groups, and no Tier 5 Kind test exercises any of them. The Tier 8 chaos scenarios for emergency credential revocation and the legal-hold override flow remain skipped scaffolds. The §24.7 circuit-breaker `open` command's CLI parser still does not validate the `--limit-tier` enum or the `operation_type` closed-set scope values client-side (the server-side `pkg/circuitbreaker` validator does, and is unit-tested, but the CLI-to-gateway propagation of an invalid value is untested end to end). The schema-driven assertion generation behind §24.8 `external-adapters validate` (now citing `messagepart.schema.json` after the OutputPart→MessagePart rename) is exercised only through a faked validator at the gateway and through the separate runtime-author harness, never against the three published schemas through the admin endpoint.
Counts: 4 High, 6 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-24.10.1 — Tenant force-delete with legal-hold override: core path now implemented and unit/component-tested, but the Tier 4 and Tier 8 layers remain untested [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`lenny-ctl admin tenants force-delete <id> --acknowledge-hold-override --justification <text>` Force-delete a tenant despite active legal holds. … Phase 3.5 legal-hold segregation resolves the tenant's `dataResidencyRegion` … re-encrypts held evidence under the region-scoped platform `legal_hold_escrow_kek` … `POST /v1/admin/tenants/{id}/force-delete`" (spec/24_lenny-ctl-command-reference.md:130). TESTING.md §15.1 promises "Tenant management: delete; force-delete with legal-hold override." (TESTING.md:2051)
- **Existing tests:** BUILD-GAPS.md's F-12.8.2/F-24.10.2 closed this out (commits `07f4420e`, `0acbdfef`, `8ce68b17`, `24ff7280`): the CLI now wires `force-delete` (`pkg/ctlcli/main.go:994` dispatch, `cmdTenantsForceDelete` at `pkg/ctlcli/main.go:1026`), the gateway handler exists (`handleForceDeleteTenant`, `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/forcedelete.go:45`) and is registered in `pkg/gateway/externalapi/openapi/openapi.json`, the controller's Phase 3.5 override branch and region-resolution/escrow migrator live in `pkg/legalholdescrow` and `pkg/controller/tenantdeletion` (`legalhold_override_test.go`), and CLI (`pkg/ctlcli/main_test.go:296-453`, five cases including the no-override rejection and the justification requirement), gateway-handler (`pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/forcedelete_test.go`, six cases including `TestForceDeleteHeldTenantWithOverride_spec_12_8_880` and the platform-admin-only check), and controller-level tests (`pkg/controller/tenantdeletion/legalhold_override_test.go`: `TestPhase35OverrideEscrowsAndProceeds_spec_12_8_880`, `TestPhase35OverrideUnresolvableRegionPauses_spec_12_8_883`) all pass. `pkg/legalholdescrow/escrow_test.go` unit-tests the migrator's happy path, the fail-closed unresolvable-region abort, and idempotency. The Tier 8 scenario `TestLegalHoldOverrideFlow` (tests/tier8_chaos/scaffolds_test.go:320) is unchanged since the prior review: still a `t.Logf` scaffold, and runbook-map.yaml:183 still points the `legal-hold-override` runbook at it.
- **Gap:** The remaining gap is narrower than previously recorded: no Tier 4 integration test drives `lenny-ctl admin tenants force-delete` against a live gateway with a real Postgres-backed tenant and controller (the CLI-mapping and handler/controller tests above use faked stores and an in-memory controller harness), and the Tier 8 chaos exercise for the escrow-region-unresolvable fail-closed path against real (or realistically faulted) region-scoped escrow infrastructure is still an unimplemented scaffold. This is a missing real user journey (operator force-deletes a held tenant end to end and watches the escrow-then-destroy sequence complete against live stores) and a missing adversarial/failure-path exercise (the escrow region becoming unresolvable under real fault injection), rather than a missing implementation.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a Postgres container, a region-scoped escrow bucket fixture, and the `tests/testinfra/clockstep` and `tests/testinfra/audit` helpers to assert the audit chain at Tier 4. The Tier 8 chaos exercise needs a region-scoped escrow KMS/bucket fault-injection stub, which does not exist yet (the production code is real, but a faultable stand-in for the exercise is not built).
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/tenant_force_delete_test.go driving `lenny-ctl admin tenants force-delete` against the live gateway: assert the no-flag rejection (`TENANT_DELETE_BLOCKED_BY_LEGAL_HOLD`), the flag-present Phase 3.5 escrow migration against a real Postgres-backed tenant row, and the two audit events; add a Tier 8 case in tests/tier8_chaos that makes the escrow region unresolvable and asserts `LEGAL_HOLD_ESCROW_REGION_UNRESOLVABLE` plus the `LegalHoldEscrowResidencyViolation` alert, converting the `TestLegalHoldOverrideFlow` scaffold.

### - [ ] T-24.5-24.10.2 — No Tier 4 integration test drives the lenny-ctl binary against a live gateway for any of these six command groups [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Every documented subcommand in §spec/24 (sections §spec/24.0–§spec/24.20) has at least one Tier 4 integration test against the compose stack and, for cluster-affecting commands, a Tier 5 Kind test." (TESTING.md:2040)
- **Existing tests:** no test found at Tier 4 for the CLI binary. The proposal-0020 refactor moved the CLI logic and its tests from `cmd/lenny-ctl` to `pkg/ctlcli` (`cmd/lenny-ctl` now holds only `main.go`, a thin wrapper, plus the `runtimescaffold` subpackage). The `pkg/ctlcli/*_test.go` suites (credential_pools_test.go, quota_pools_cli_test.go, external_adapters_test.go, users_test.go, main_test.go, and others) are unit tests that run `run(...)` against an in-process `httptest` fake gateway via `runAgainstGateway` (pkg/ctlcli/main_test.go:170); they assert method, path, and body, never the server-side effect. The only Tier 4 reference to `lenny-ctl` is in tests/tier4_integration/scaffolds_test.go (a documentation scaffold, still present unchanged). Server-side handler tests, now under `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin` (moved from `pkg/gateway/admin` by the same refactor), use fakes (`fakePoolRevoker`, `fakeValidator`, `fakeQuotaReconciler`). The compose harness exists at tests/testinfra/compose.
- **Gap:** The mandated end-to-end path (operator runs the real CLI, the request crosses the wire to a real gateway backed by real Postgres and Redis, the documented state change occurs) is unverified for credential-pools, quota reconcile, circuit-breakers, external-adapters validate, users rotate-token, and tenants. The CLI mapping tests and the handler tests can both pass while the wire contract between them drifts — the rotate-token wire-contract change since the prior review (client-side token-exchange replaced by a dedicated gateway route) is exactly the kind of drift this Tier 4 gap would have caught mechanically rather than requiring a manual spec/test audit. This is a missing real user journey for the entire operator credential and tenant toolchain.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the compose stack (tests/testinfra/compose) or the gateway subprocess harness (tests/testinfra/gateway) plus Postgres and Redis containers (tests/testinfra/containers), and a built `lenny-ctl` binary invoked as a subprocess. None — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/lennyctl_admin_test.go that builds `cmd/lenny-ctl`, points `--api-url` at a `gateway.StartWith` subprocess wired to Redis and Postgres, and runs `admin credential-pools list`, `admin quota reconcile --all-tenants`, `admin circuit-breakers open/close`, `admin external-adapters validate`, `admin users rotate-token`, and `admin tenants delete`/`force-delete`, asserting each documented server-side effect (Redis `cb:{name}` key, credential store state, tenant deletion-lifecycle state, the `lenny-admin-token` Secret patched by the gateway).

### - [ ] T-24.5.3 — Emergency credential revocation terminating active leases has no end-to-end or chaos test with a real lease [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`lenny-ctl admin credential-pools revoke-credential --pool <name> --credential <id> --reason <r>` Emergency revocation of a single credential; terminates all active leases." (spec/24_lenny-ctl-command-reference.md:92). TESTING.md §15.2 requires each runbook to have a Tier 8 test that triggers the condition, executes the remediation through the API, and asserts return to healthy (TESTING.md:2063).
- **Existing tests:** The gateway handler test `TestRevokeCredentialMarksRevokesAndAudits` (pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/credential_pool_revocation_test.go:96, moved from `pkg/gateway/admin` by the proposal-0020 refactor; line unchanged) asserts the store flips to revoked, the audit event carries `active_leases_terminated`, and a `fakePoolRevoker` is called, but the revoker is a stub so no lease is actually terminated. The Tier 8 scenario `TestEmergencyRevocationDuringActiveSession` (tests/tier8_chaos/scaffolds_test.go:215) is unchanged since the prior review: still a `t.Logf` scaffold, now noting "cred-shell-echo wired in 3aa580b" but still stating the live e2e exercise is "on the ops backlog," and runbook-map.yaml:141 still maps the P0 `emergency-credential-revocation` runbook to it. The tier4 `credential_test.go` exercises the end-user `/v1/credentials` surface, not the admin `/v1/admin/credential-pools/.../revoke` surface.
- **Gap:** The security-critical effect (an active session holding a leased credential loses it when an operator revokes that credential) is unverified end to end. The handler test proves the store mutation and the audit row; nothing proves the lease is torn down at a running pod or that the cross-replica deny-list propagation reaches the holder. This is a missing adversarial or failure-path test for a P0 runbook and a missing real journey for an operator responding to a suspected leak.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a session with a live credential lease (the spec scaffold references `cred-shell-echo`, now wired per the scaffold comment), the `tests/testinfra/kind` harness, and the Redis EventBus for cross-replica propagation. The fault-injection wiring for live revocation does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier8_chaos/credential_revocation_test.go (or convert the scaffold) that starts a session leasing a pool credential on Kind, runs `lenny-ctl admin credential-pools revoke-credential`, and asserts the lease is terminated at the holder within the propagation window, the `credential.revoked` audit event fires with the terminated count, and a subsequent lease draw on that credential fails.

### - [ ] T-24.8.4 — external-adapters validate has no conformance test pinning the schema-driven suite against the three published adapter schemas through the admin endpoint [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Run the `RegisterAdapterUnderTest` compliance suite against a registered adapter. The suite is **schema-driven**: assertions are generated from the published `schemas/lenny-adapter.proto`, `schemas/lenny-adapter-jsonl.schema.json`, and `schemas/messagepart.schema.json` artifacts … rather than hand-coded against prose." (spec/24_lenny-ctl-command-reference.md:114). The schema filename changed from `outputpart.schema.json` to `messagepart.schema.json` when commit 611f6b1f (0018 S15) renamed OutputPart to MessagePart across the content model; the requirement itself is unchanged.
- **Existing tests:** The gateway handler tests (`TestValidateExternalAdapterPasses`, `TestValidateExternalAdapterFails`, pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/external_adapters_test.go:126,151 — moved from `pkg/gateway/admin` and shifted a few lines by the refactor) drive `POST /v1/admin/external-adapters/{name}/validate` but inject a `fakeValidator` (pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/external_adapters_test.go:23) whose `Validate` returns a canned report, so no schema is consulted. The Tier 10 conformance suite (tests/tier10_conformance/scaffolds_test.go) runs the separate runtime-author harness (`cmd/lenny-compliance`) against bundled runtimes and exercises `compliance.RegisterAdapterUnderTest` (`TestBasicAdapterProtocol`, line 203), but that is the runtime-conformance path, not the admin `external-adapters validate` endpoint that §24.8 maps to. The schemas are validated as wire shapes in tests/tier3_contract/adapter_jsonl/messages_test.go via `schematest`, independently of the validate endpoint.
- **Gap:** The claim that the validate suite's assertions are generated from the three published schemas is unverified at the admin-endpoint level. No test feeds a known-good and a known-bad adapter binary through `POST /v1/admin/external-adapters/{name}/validate` and asserts the validation report cites the specific schema assertion that failed, nor that the failing assertion traces to `lenny-adapter.proto`, `lenny-adapter-jsonl.schema.json`, or `messagepart.schema.json`. This is a missing standards-conformance check for the adapter contract surface, distinct from the runtime-author harness already covered in Tier 10.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the real `ComplianceValidator` (pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/external_adapters.go:40) wired against a sample adapter binary that emits a known schema violation, plus the published schemas under `schemas/`. None — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier10_conformance/admin_adapter_validate_test.go that registers an adapter, runs `lenny-ctl admin external-adapters validate --name <n>` against a live gateway with the real validator, and asserts a conformant binary transitions to `active` while a binary emitting an out-of-schema `messagepart` transitions to `validation_failed` with a report citing the violated schema assertion.

### - [x] T-24.9.8 — rotate-token graceful-handoff (old token valid through the handoff) is unverified end to end [Medium] — RESOLVED 715381ce (reconciled by proposal 0021)
- **Resolution:** Proposal 0021 (F-CTL-1) replaced the documented mechanism this finding tested for: `admin users rotate-token` no longer calls `/v1/oauth/token` with an RFC 8693 token-exchange grant and no longer patches the Secret client-side from the CLI. It now calls a dedicated `POST /v1/admin/users/{user}/rotate-token` route the gateway serves in process (`pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/admin_token.go:81`), which mints the replacement token, patches the `lenny-admin-token` Secret server-side, and then durably revokes the superseded token's jti with **no grace period** — the opposite of the "old token valid through graceful handoff" property this finding asked to verify (spec/24_lenny-ctl-command-reference.md:120: "immediately invalidates the superseded token (no grace period; see §17.6)"). The new no-grace-period, crash-safe invariant is thoroughly component-tested: `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admintoken/admintoken_test.go` (`TestRotateMintsAndRevokesPrevious_spec_13_3`, `TestRotateOrderingUnderLock_spec_13_3_599`, `TestRotateRevokesOrphanedPredecessorBeforeOverwrite_spec_13_3_601`, `TestRotateAbortsWhenOrphanRevokeFails_spec_13_3_601`, `TestRotatePatchFailureLeavesOldTokenLive_spec_13_3_599`, `TestRotatePostPatchRevokeFailureSurfaces_spec_13_3_599`) prove the revoke-before-overwrite ordering and every crash-window failure mode; the route itself is proven in `TestRotateTokenRoute_spec_17_6` (pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/admin_token_test.go:111, including the reject-any-other-user 404 branch); and the leader-gated reclaimer sweep that durably revokes an orphaned predecessor after a crash between the Secret patch and the durable revoke is unit-tested in `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admintoken/reclaimer/reclaimer_test.go` (`TestSweepRevokesNamedPredecessor` and the other sweep/interval/lifecycle cases in that file). TESTING.md §14's `token_rotation` suite entry (TESTING.md:1085) still reads "old token valid through graceful handoff" and has not been updated to match the reworded spec; that is a documentation-drift item for TESTING.md itself; it does not reopen this finding because the platform's actual and now-tested contract is the opposite property (immediate, no-grace-period invalidation), which this section's tests already pin.

### - [ ] T-24.9.9 — lenny token print clustered-rejection is asserted at unit level only, never as the documented end-to-end refusal [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Print a short-lived dev bearer token minted locally from a persisted dev key, which the in-cluster gateway trusts in dev mode through its `--bearer-trust-hmac-key-file` bearer-trust hook … The token is scoped to the local embedded gateway and rejected by any clustered deployment (the dev key is not trusted in clustered installs)." (spec/24_lenny-ctl-command-reference.md:121). Proposal 0017 replaced the mechanism this finding described (an "embedded OIDC provider" minting the token) with the persisted-dev-key/`--bearer-trust-hmac-key-file` design as part of the §17.4 embedded-mode re-architecture (commit 89f66d71); the rejected-by-clustered-deployment requirement itself is unchanged.
- **Existing tests:** `TestLennyCtlDelegatesTokenPrint_spec_24_9_120` (pkg/ctlcli/main_test.go:1130, path moved and line shifted by the refactor) asserts only that `token print` exits `3 EMBEDDED_MODE_REQUIRED` outside Embedded Mode. `TestEmbeddedHMACVerifierRejectsForeignAudience_spec_17_4_182` (cmd/lenny-gateway/embedded_audience_test.go:37, unchanged) asserts the gateway verifier rejects a foreign-audience token at the verifier level. `TestPersistedKeyFileLoadableByGatewayVerifier` (pkg/embedded/devauth/devauth_test.go:238) proves the accepted side of the contract: a token the persisted-key signer mints verifies through the same `jwt.LoadHMACKeyFile` path the in-cluster gateway's `--bearer-trust-hmac-key-file` hook uses. No test mints a real `lenny token print` token from the persisted dev key and presents it to a clustered gateway (one configured with a different, or no, trust anchor for that key) to confirm the documented rejection.
- **Gap:** The security claim that a dev-key-minted token is rejected by a clustered deployment because the dev key is untrusted there is not exercised end to end. The existing tests cover the local exit guard, the audience check, and the accepted (embedded-gateway) verification path in isolation; the cross-boundary refusal (dev-key token presented to a clustered install that does not trust that key) is a missing adversarial journey.
- **Dependencies:** Requires an embedded-mode binary to mint the token (`pkg/embedded/devauth` or `pkg/embedded/localcli`) and a clustered gateway configured with a different trust anchor (tests/testinfra/gateway). None — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/embedded_token_clustered_rejection_test.go that mints a token via `pkg/embedded/devauth` and presents it to a clustered-configured gateway (no `--bearer-trust-hmac-key-file` pointed at that key), asserting a 401/403 with the documented untrusted-signer reason.

## §24.11-24.14 lenny-ctl: Session Investigation, Erasure, Migration, Policy <a id="t-24.11-24.14"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/24_lenny-ctl-command-reference.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The four subsections are thin CLI wrappers over REST Admin API endpoints, and coverage is concentrated at the lowest two tiers. Since the 2026-06-03 baseline, `cmd/lenny-ctl` moved to `pkg/ctlcli`, `pkg/gateway/admin` moved to `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin`, and `pkg/gateway/delegationpolicystore` moved to `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/delegationpolicystore` (package regroup under proposal 0020); the file-path and line citations below are updated to the moved locations, with no change in test substance. Proposal 0018 (C2) closed the two High findings that tracked missing OpenAPI coverage: the served document now carries `/v1/admin/sessions/{id}`, `/v1/admin/sessions/{id}/force-terminate`, `/v1/admin/erasure-jobs/{jobId}/retry`, and `/v1/admin/erasure-jobs/{jobId}/clear-processing-restriction` with full `x-lenny-*` extensions, and the old hardcoded `expected[]` allowlist test was replaced with a live-mux-enumerating completeness test that cannot silently omit a registered route again. Commit F-24.13.4 (76b06e14, one day after the baseline) built the `schema_migration_phase` overlay storage and wired `buildStatus` to surface a Job-recorded `phase`/`gateCheckResult`/`appliedAt`/`migrationJobName` when one exists, with new unit and embedded-Postgres tests; the production writer (`cmd/lenny-migrate`'s `RecordRun`) still only ever stamps `phase=complete`/`gateCheckResult=not_run` for every version, including the three real Phase 3 migrations (0118, 0129, 0167) that now ship with a working `DO $$` gate block, so the documented `phase1_applied`/`phase2_deployed`/`phase3_applied`/`gateCheckResult=pass|fail:<N>_rows` values remain unobserved by any operator-facing path. The remaining gaps are unchanged in substance: no component (tier2), integration (tier4), e2e (tier5/tier6), chaos (tier8), security (tier9), or contract (tier3) test runs the session-investigation, erasure-job, migration, or policy-audit admin surfaces against a real Postgres or live gateway; `tests/tier4_integration/scaffolds_test.go` and `tests/tier8_chaos/scaffolds_test.go` are still `t.Logf` placeholders; the `migration_upgrade_test.go` named in `tests/change-graph.json` still does not exist; and the `erasure_job` and `schema_migration` domain suites named in TESTING.md §14 still have no implementation.
Counts: 2 High, 5 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-24.11.1 — Session investigation and force-terminate have no integration or e2e test through a real pod release [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`lenny-ctl admin sessions force-terminate <id>` Force-terminate a session that is stuck or unresponsive. The session transitions immediately to `failed` and the assigned pod is released to the pool." (spec/24_lenny-ctl-command-reference.md:137)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/ctlcli/session_ops_test.go` (TestAdminSessionsForceTerminate, line 38) asserts the CLI sends `POST /v1/admin/sessions/{id}/force-terminate` against an `httptest` fake, which is tier1 (moved from `cmd/lenny-ctl/session_ops_test.go`). `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/sessions_test.go` (TestAdminForceTerminate_Transitions_spec_24_11, line 121) drives the handler against a `fakeSessionAdmin` in-memory double and asserts the `failed` transition plus the `session.force_terminated` audit event (moved from `pkg/gateway/admin/sessions_test.go`). No test exercises the operator path against a real session row in Postgres, and no test asserts the assigned pod is actually released back to the warm pool.
- **Gap:** The spec's core promise (`the assigned pod is released to the pool`) is never verified end to end. The missing test is a real user journey: operator alice runs `lenny-ctl admin sessions force-terminate <id>` against a stuck session occupying a pod, and the pod returns to the warm pool for reuse. Target tiers are tier4 integration (CLI to live gateway subprocess with real Postgres) and tier5 e2e on Kind (force-terminate releases the Kubernetes pod and the pool replenishes).
- **Dependencies:** tier4 needs the live-gateway harness in `tests/testinfra/gateway` plus a real Postgres from `tests/testinfra/containers`; tier5 needs `tests/testinfra/kind` and a session driver (`tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`) that parks a session on a pod. Buildable today with existing infrastructure.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/admin_session_force_terminate_test.go` driving `lenny-ctl admin sessions force-terminate` against a stuck Kind session and asserting the pod is released and the pool warm count recovers, plus a tier4 case in `tests/tier4_integration/admin_sessions_test.go` asserting the Postgres row reaches `failed`.

### - [x] T-24.11.2 — Session-investigation REST endpoints are absent from the published OpenAPI document and the contract test does not catch it [High] — RESOLVED 1fa4eee4 (reconciled by proposal 0018)
- **Resolution:** Proposal 0018 finding W1 confirmed the served `openapi.json` covered roughly 73 of the ~113 mux-registered admin path templates and that the guard test (`TestDocumentMatchesEndpoints`, then in `pkg/gateway/openapi/openapi_test.go`) checked presence against a hardcoded `expected[]` allowlist rather than the live mux, so an admin route could ship undocumented with no test failure. Commit `1fa4eee4` ("0018 S11: complete openapi.json and replace the allowlist guard with a mux-enumerating completeness test (W1 / C2)") added the absent admin templates — including `/v1/admin/sessions/{id}` (`GET`, `x-lenny-scope: tools:sessions:read`) and `/v1/admin/sessions/{id}/force-terminate` (`POST`, `x-lenny-scope: tools:sessions:write`), both carrying `x-lenny-required-role: platform-admin` — and rewrote the completeness test (now `pkg/gateway/externalapi/openapi/completeness_test.go`, package moved by the 0020 externalapi regroup) to enumerate the live serve mux and assert every registered template, admin and non-admin, is present in the document, so a future omission fails the build rather than passing under a stale allowlist. `TestAdminEndpointsCarryMCPExtensions_spec_15_1_933` (`pkg/gateway/externalapi/openapi/openapi_test.go:149`) independently confirms both routes carry `x-lenny-mcp-tool`, `x-lenny-scope`, `x-lenny-required-role`, and `x-lenny-category`. Merged via `9df646f3`.

### - [x] T-24.12.1 — Erasure retry and clear-processing-restriction REST endpoints are absent from the published OpenAPI document [High] — RESOLVED 1fa4eee4 (reconciled by proposal 0018)

No test exercises the actual production path end to end: `cmd/lenny-migrate`'s `Manager.RecordRun` (`pkg/schemamigrate/schemamigrate.go:180`) unconditionally stamps every advanced version with `Phase: PhaseComplete` and `GateCheckResult: GateNotRun`, so no code path ever writes `phase1_applied`, `phase2_deployed`, `phase3_applied`, `pass`, or `fail:<N>_rows` in production, and the `GatePass` constant (`schemamigrate.go:80`) has zero non-definition references anywhere in the tree.

An operator reading the status output cannot distinguish a Phase 1 migration from a fully complete one, and cannot confirm a Phase 3 gate result at all. The missing work is a component test pinning the status projection to the documented value set once a real multi-phase migration's gate result is captured and recorded (the capture logic itself does not exist and is part of this finding, distinct from the overlay/storage plumbing F-24.13.4 already built). Target tier is tier2 component.
- **Dependencies:** the gate-check-result capture logic (parsing or wrapping the `DO $$` block's outcome into a `pass`/`fail:<N>_rows` `PhaseRow` write) does not exist in `cmd/lenny-migrate` or `schemamigrate`; building it is part of this finding. ## §24.15-24.20 lenny-ctl: Agent-Ops, Discovery, Session Ops, Scaffolding, Local Stack, Wizard <a id="t-24.15-24.20"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/24_lenny-ctl-command-reference.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
Every command in §24.15 through §24.20 has in-process unit coverage, now in `pkg/ctlcli/*_test.go` (moved from `cmd/lenny-ctl/*_test.go` by commit fd2d69ee, which extracted the dispatcher into an importable package so both the `lenny` and `lenny-ctl` binaries share one command surface) and `pkg/embedded/localcli/*_test.go`, that asserts CLI-to-HTTP request mapping against an `httptest` fake, scaffolder file emission, and exit codes. Since the 2026-06-03 audit, proposal 0017 re-architected §17.4 Embedded Mode so `lenny up` renders the production chart under a development profile and runs the gateway, controllers, and `lenny-ops` as in-cluster pods on the embedded k3s instead of host child processes, and `tests/tier4_integration/embedded_mode_smoke_test.go` now drives the real `lenny` binary through that boot sequence end to end, closing the two highest-severity findings from the prior pass (T-24.19.1, T-24.19.1.2) and the krew-parity finding (T-24.0.1, closed by the same dispatcher-unification commit). The broader gap the prior audit found is otherwise unchanged: none of the agent-operability command groups (`operations`, `events`, `audit`, `upgrade`, `restore`) has a Tier 4 integration test against the compose stack's gateway and `lenny-ops`, and the MCP-based session verbs, the `lenny-ctl install` helm-plus-bootstrap-plus-smoke flow, and `lenny runtime validate` against a running runtime remain unverified end to end. The re-architecture also introduced two new live-cluster surfaces with no test beyond fakes: the `lenny restart` Kubernetes Deployment rollout-restart and `lenny logs` pod-log streaming. Counts across open and resolved findings: 6 High, 8 Medium, 3 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-24.15-24.20.1 — No Tier 4 integration test for any §24.15-24.20 subcommand despite a declared per-subcommand obligation [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Every documented subcommand in §spec/24 (sections §spec/24.0–§spec/24.20) has at least one Tier 4 integration test against the compose stack and, for cluster-affecting commands, a Tier 5 Kind test." (TESTING.md:2040)
- **Existing tests:** All coverage for the operability groups (`pkg/ctlcli/ops_test.go`, `pkg/ctlcli/ops_groups_test.go`, `pkg/ctlcli/operability_test.go`; moved from `cmd/lenny-ctl/` by fd2d69ee), session ops (`pkg/embedded/localcli/session_verbs_test.go`), discovery (`pkg/ctlcli/ops_test.go:284` `TestOpsAutoDiscoveryFromGateway`), scaffolding (`pkg/ctlcli/runtime_test.go`, `cmd/lenny-ctl/runtimescaffold/scaffold_test.go`, which stayed under `cmd/lenny-ctl` since it is still imported by the moved `runtime.go`), local stack (`pkg/embedded/localcli/localcli_test.go`), and install (`pkg/ctlcli/install_test.go`) runs in-process via `run()` / `cmdSession()` against `httptest` servers or stubs. `tests/tier4_integration/embedded_mode_smoke_test.go` now builds and drives the real `lenny` binary end to end, but only for the §24.19 local-stack bring-up sequence (`up`/`status`/`session new`/`image import`/`down`); it does not drive `operations`, `events`, `audit`, `upgrade`, or `restore` against a compose-stack gateway and `lenny-ops`. `tests/tier4_integration/` still contains no file that drives any agent-operability command against the compose stack. spec-map.json §24.15-24.20 still lists only the `cmd/lenny-ctl/...` glob (tests/spec-map.json:2869-2945).
- **Gap:** The declared tier4 obligation is unmet for the agent-operability command groups. The unit tests assert request shape against a fake; they do not confirm the gateway and `lenny-ops` accept the emitted requests, that the responses render correctly, or that the discovery/routing split resolves a real `opsServiceURL`. This is a spec-versus-test inconsistency that would let a CLI-to-server contract regression ship. Target tier4 integration against the compose stack.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the compose stack (tests/testinfra/compose) with both gateway and `lenny-ops` reachable, plus a binary-build helper. The `tests/testinfra/inproc` gateway exists; the `tests/testinfra/embedded` binary-build helper the Docker-backed smoke test added (`embedded.Build`) is a candidate to adapt for a compose target; a `lenny-ops` compose service still needs wiring.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/lennyctl_ops_groups_test.go that builds `pkg/ctlcli` (via `cmd/lenny-ctl`), points `--api-url`/`--ops-server` at the compose gateway and ops service, and exercises `operations list`, `events buffer`, `audit query`, `drift report`, `backup list`, and `me` against the live services, asserting non-error exit and a parseable JSON envelope.

### - [x] T-24.19.1 — `lenny up` embedded stack is never booted end to end in any tier [High] — RESOLVED c5ebc95e (extended through 1802e63b)
- **Resolution:** `tests/tier4_integration/embedded_mode_smoke_test.go` (`TestEmbeddedModeSmoke_spec_17_4_18`), added the day after the audit was generated (c5ebc95e, F-17.4.18) and substantially extended through proposals 0013, 0016, and 0017 (through 1802e63b), now drives the real `lenny` binary through `up` → `status` → `session new` → `down --purge` against the live embedded substrate (a Docker-backed k3s container on non-Linux hosts, a host child process on Linux). It asserts the gateway URL is printed, the embedded cluster (rather than the retired controller-simulator fallback) is up, every in-cluster control-plane Deployment (gateway, controller, `lenny-ops`) reaches Ready, a session against the auto-seeded echo runtime places successfully across the §5.2 warm-up window, a warm (non-`--purge`) down/up cycle reuses the persisted substrate (the idempotency claim), and `--purge` removes the state directory. Proposal 0017 re-architected the underlying bring-up (production chart under a dev profile, in-cluster pods rather than host processes for gateway/controller/`lenny-ops`, no separate Postgres/Redis/KMS/OIDC process; spec/24_lenny-ctl-command-reference.md:261), and this test is the end-to-end verification of that new architecture, not only of the original claim. The test is gated behind `LENNY_EMBEDDED_SMOKE` plus a Docker/Linux prerequisite (`tests/testinfra/embedded.SkipUnlessAvailable`) and is wired into `make test-smoke-embedded`.
