- **Spec/Doc:** "`lenny restart [<component>]` | Roll out a restart of one of the pod-backed components (`gateway`, `controller`, `ops`) as a Kubernetes Deployment rollout-restart through the embedded kubeconfig, without tearing down the rest of the stack." and "`lenny logs [<component>] [--follow]` | Tail merged logs, or filter to one of `gateway`, `controller`, `ops`, the k3s substrate, or `runtime-<name>`." (spec/24_lenny-ctl-command-reference.md:264-265)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/embedded/localcli/restart_test.go` (`TestCmdRestartRequiresComponent_spec_24_19_264`, `TestCmdRestartRejectsUnknownComponent_spec_24_19_264`, `TestCmdRestartNoStack`) asserts the argument validation and the "no stack running" guard, and `pkg/embedded/localcli/localcli_test.go` (`TestRunLogsNoStack`) asserts the missing-stack diagnostic for `lenny logs`; neither drives a live in-cluster Deployment. `tests/tier4_integration/embedded_mode_smoke_test.go` and `tests/tier2_component/embedded/bringup_test.go` bring up the real in-cluster gateway/controller/ops Deployments but neither calls `lenny restart` or `lenny logs` against them.
- **Gap:** Proposal 0017 changed `lenny restart` from a host-process restart to a Kubernetes Deployment rollout-restart issued through the embedded kubeconfig, and changed `lenny logs` from tailing host-process/child-process log files (including the retired `postgres`/`redis`/`kms`/`oidc` components) to streaming in-cluster pod logs for the pod-backed components. Neither the rollout-restart call against a real Deployment (does the rollout actually happen, does the pod recycle, does a subsequent `lenny status` show it recovers) nor the pod-log streaming against a real pod is exercised beyond the argument-validation unit tests. Target tier2 component (envtest) or a tier4 addition to the embedded smoke test.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a running embedded k3s with the gateway/controller/ops Deployments up (the tier2 bring-up test or the tier4 smoke test already provision this); driving `lenny restart <component>` and `lenny logs <component>` against that live cluster and asserting the rollout/log output needs adding.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `tests/tier4_integration/embedded_mode_smoke_test.go` (or add a sibling test reusing its bring-up) to run `lenny restart gateway` against the live cluster, assert the gateway Deployment's pod is replaced (a new pod name or restart count) and `lenny status` reports it `ok` again after the rollout completes, and run `lenny logs gateway` asserting non-empty log output naming the gateway container.

### - [ ] T-24.19.3 — `lenny image list`/`lenny image rm` and the real-socket `K3S_UNAVAILABLE` path remain unverified against a live embedded containerd [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`4 K3S_UNAVAILABLE` when the embedded containerd socket cannot be reached (typically because `lenny up` is not running or the cluster is mid-startup — retry after `lenny status` reports `gateway: healthy`)." (spec/24_lenny-ctl-command-reference.md:283)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/embedded/localcli/image_test.go` unit-tests the `K3S_UNAVAILABLE` diagnostic against a seeded fake k3s binary and an empty `containerd.sock` file (`TestCmdImageImportRequiresEmbeddedStack_spec_24_19_1`, `TestCmdImageListUnavailableStack_spec_24_19_1`, `TestCmdImageRmUnavailableStack_spec_24_19_1`). `tests/tier4_integration/embedded_mode_smoke_test.go`'s custom-sidecar-runtime leg (T-24.19.1.2, resolved) now runs `lenny image import --file` against a live embedded containerd as part of the walkthrough, but the smoke test never calls `lenny image list` or `lenny image rm` against that live store, and no test triggers the `K3S_UNAVAILABLE` path against a real (rather than a stub) containerd socket that has genuinely gone away mid-command.
- **Gap:** With the primary import-and-place walkthrough now covered end to end (T-24.19.1.2), the residual gap is narrower: confirming a freshly imported image is listed and removable through the live store, and confirming the documented retry guidance holds when the real embedded cluster is mid-startup or torn down under a concurrent `image` call. Target tier4, extending the existing embedded smoke harness rather than building a new one.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the same Docker/Linux embedded-stack prerequisite as `TestEmbeddedModeSmoke_spec_17_4_18` (tests/testinfra/embedded); no new harness is needed beyond extending that test.
- **Suggested test:** Extend the custom-sidecar-runtime leg of `tests/tier4_integration/embedded_mode_smoke_test.go` to run `lenny image list` after the import and assert the imported reference appears, then `lenny image rm` and assert it no longer appears; add a case that runs `lenny image import` immediately after `lenny down` (before a subsequent `lenny up`) and asserts exit `4` with the `K3S_UNAVAILABLE` diagnostic.

## §25.1-25.2 Agent Operability: Design Philosophy and Architecture <a id="t-25.1-25.2"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/25_agent-operability.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The §25.1 scoped-token machinery (RFC 8693 exchange, RFC 9068 space-separated `scope` claim, `tools:<domain>:<action>` matching, the playground intersection invariant) and the §25.2 API conventions (canonical error envelope, dry-run/confirm pattern, pagination, progress envelope, degradation envelope) have strong unit and tier3 contract coverage. The contract suites run entirely in-process through `httptest` against in-memory stores, so no integration, e2e, or chaos test exercises the operability surface end to end. The two headline architectural claims of §25.1 and §25.2 are unverified at runtime: the external-only `lenny-ops` boundary (no internal cluster workload, including agent pods, can reach the operational control plane) is asserted only at chart-render time by helm-unittest, and the bootstrap-problem claim (an external agent observes a partially-down platform and falls back to the gateway health summary) has no chaos test. The tier6 cloud suite carries no operability coverage at all. The negative-render half of the §25.1 "mandatory in every tier" claim is now enforced by a chart-validation `fail` guard (F-17.8.12) and is resolved; the cloud-topology presence half remains untested (T-25.2.3). Proposal 0021 moved the audit log query API (§25.9) from `lenny-ops` to the gateway because its data plane is gateway-resident; the component-model quote in this unit is updated accordingly, and the integration-coverage gap in T-25.2.1 is otherwise unaffected. Proposal 0029 widened the §25.2 canonical degradation envelope to cover in-process-history starvation (not just external-dependency unavailability); the new state transition is pinned at the unit level but carries no contract or integration coverage (new finding T-25.2.5). Correlation-header propagation to audit events is unit-tested but never traced end to end through a live audit pipeline. RFC 9068 scope narrowing is enforced in-process but has no live-cluster (tier-5) coverage because the e2e install carries no scoped-token issuer (new finding T-25.1.7).
Counts: 3 High, 6 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [x] T-25.1.1 — `lenny-ops` external-only boundary has no runtime adversarial test from an agent pod [High] — RESOLVED 56ad5a16b15c76abcb6e6106abb3e95e3aea24f5
- **Resolution:** Added tier-9 security test tests/tier9_security/ops_agent_pod_boundary_test.go::TestOpsUnreachableFromAgentPod_spec_25_1, which schedules a §13.1-compliant probe pod in the lenny-agents (tenant-code) namespace and asserts the CNI drops its connection to lenny-ops:8090 (curl exit 28), with an Ingress-controller positive control that reaches lenny-ops (exit 0) proving the deny is selective. This pins the specific lateral-movement path §25.1/§25.2 forbid (agent pods cannot reach the operational control plane) under live CNI enforcement, which the existing default-namespace tests did not exercise. The test passed against unmodified product code, confirming the chart's lenny-ops-deny-all-ingress boundary is correctly enforced.

### - [x] T-25.2.1 — `lenny-ops` operability surface has no integration test against real backing services [High] — RESOLVED a136d080394f305c4be2503aba52ea89bff6d7af
- **Resolution:** Added a tier4 integration test (tests/tier4_integration/ops_escalations_e2e_test.go::TestOpsServiceEscalationStoreBackedE2E) that boots the real cmd/lenny-ops binary against real Postgres and Redis and drives the §25.4 escalation surface end to end: create lands durable-postgres records (201 + X-Lenny-Persistence header, cross-checked in ops_escalations), GET returns the §25.2 items/pagination envelope populated from the store, ?severity= and ?status= filters and the ?limit= cap resolve against the live store, and a PUT status update round-trips through Postgres and is reflected on a subsequent filtered list. It passed against unmodified product code.

### - [x] T-25.1.2 — Bootstrap-problem / external-agent-survives-failure claim has no chaos test [High] — RESOLVED bf9488be3910ccdc03a18de68b9d074b347aa684
- **Resolution:** Added tests/tier8_chaos/ops_survives_gateway_test.go with two tier-8 chaos tests. TestOpsSurvivesGatewayOutage scales the gateway Deployment to zero and asserts lenny-ops stays Ready with a stable restart count (no crash-loop) throughout, then restores the gateway. TestGatewayHealthSummarySurvivesOpsOutage scales lenny-ops to zero (Service endpoints drained) and asserts the gateway GET /v1/admin/health/summary heartbeat keeps returning 200, then restores lenny-ops. Both passed against unmodified product code, confirming the §25.1 independent-failure-domain guarantee holds in both directions; the gap was missing coverage, not a defect.

### - [ ] T-25.2.2 — Gateway-side ops endpoints have only a happy-path health smoke at integration tier [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Ops-facing endpoints on the admin API: GET /v1/admin/health... /v1/admin/recommendations... /v1/admin/platform/version... /v1/admin/platform/config... /v1/admin/events/buffer" and "Health API ... reads `prometheus.Registry` directly, works when Prometheus is down." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:140, spec/25_agent-operability.md:180)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier4_integration/gateway_full_e2e_test.go:163` and `tests/tier4_integration/gateway_postgres_e2e_test.go:180` issue `GET /v1/admin/health` against the gateway subprocess and assert `status == "healthy"` only. `pkg/gateway/health/service_test.go` covers the degradation envelope and `thresholdSource` at tier2. No integration test exercises `/v1/admin/recommendations`, `/v1/admin/platform/version`, `/v1/admin/platform/config`, or `/v1/admin/events/buffer` against the live gateway, and none asserts the §25.2 split-criterion claim that the Health API serves from the in-process registry when Prometheus is unavailable.
- **Gap:** The integration coverage of the gateway-side operability surface is a single happy-path field check. The recommendations, version, config, and event-buffer endpoints have no live-gateway assertion, and the "works when Prometheus is down" claim is never exercised against a real gateway with Prometheus removed. This is partial coverage (happy path only) and a degradation-path gap. Target tier4 for the endpoint round-trips and tier8 for the Prometheus-down path.
- **Dependencies:** The gateway subprocess harness (`tests/testinfra/gateway`) already serves these endpoints, so the round-trip assertions are buildable today. The Prometheus-down path needs a deployment with a removable Prometheus, shared with the chaos infrastructure in T-25.1.2.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `tests/tier4_integration/gateway_full_e2e_test.go` to assert `/v1/admin/recommendations`, `/v1/admin/platform/version`, `/v1/admin/platform/config`, and `/v1/admin/events/buffer` each return their documented envelopes; add a tier8 case that stops Prometheus and asserts `/v1/admin/health` still returns 200 with a `degradation` envelope carrying `thresholdSource: compiled-in-defaults`.

### - [ ] T-25.1.3 — Agent correlation-header propagation to the audit trail is unit-tested but never traced end to end [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Agents may pass an `X-Lenny-Operation-ID` header to correlate multi-step remediations in the audit trail... All audit events produced during the request include this ID... They are propagated to audit events and included in operational metrics labels (`agent_name`)." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:54, spec/25_agent-operability.md:121, spec/25_agent-operability.md:124)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/admin/audit_sink_correlation_test.go` asserts the audit-event builder carries `operation_id`, `caller_kind`, and `agent_name`. `pkg/gateway/middleware/correlation/correlation_test.go` and `pkg/ops/opsserver/middleware_test.go` assert the headers land on the request context and the structured log line. These are unit tests on the builder and middleware; none drives a mutating request with `X-Lenny-Operation-ID` and `X-Lenny-Agent-Name` through a live gateway or `lenny-ops` and then reads the persisted audit event from Postgres (or the OCSF/SIEM projection) to confirm the correlation survives the full pipeline.
- **Gap:** The header-to-persisted-audit-event journey crosses the middleware, the admin handler, the audit hash chain, and the OCSF translator, and is asserted only at the first hop. A regression that drops the header between the context and the persisted row would pass every unit test. This is an end-to-end propagation gap for a documented audit behavior. Target tier4 (compose, audit pipeline) building on `tests/tier4_integration/audit_pipeline_test.go`.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the audit-pipeline integration harness (real Postgres plus the fake SIEM endpoint) already present in `tests/tier4_integration/audit_pipeline_test.go`, plus the `tests/testinfra/audit` helpers. None blocking — buildable today against the gateway subprocess.
- **Suggested test:** Add a case to `tests/tier4_integration/audit_pipeline_test.go` that issues a mutating admin request with `X-Lenny-Operation-ID` and `X-Lenny-Agent-Name`, then reads the persisted audit event and asserts both fields are present on the row and on the OCSF projection.

### - [x] T-25.1.4 — `lenny-ops` mandatory-in-every-tier claim is unverified [Medium] — RESOLVED b00fbe72
- **Resolution:** `templates/ops-deployment.yaml` now carries a top-of-file `fail` guard rejecting both `ops.enabled: false` (the §17.8.5 mandatoriness violation this finding named) and `ops.enabled: true` (an unsupported key), landed as build-gaps finding F-17.8.12 (commit `b00fbe72`, 2026-05-28). `charts/lenny/tests/ops-deployment_test.yaml` pins both cases — "rejects ops.enabled=false at chart validation per §17.8.5" and "rejects ops.enabled=true at chart validation per §17.8.5" — asserting `failedTemplate` with the documented error message. This closes the tier1 negative-render half of this finding's Suggested test: the chart now fails to render rather than silently accepting a disable override. The cloud-topology presence assertion (that `lenny-ops` is deployed across the dev/single-node/cloud topologies) was explicitly deferred by this finding's own Suggested test and remains open, tracked under T-25.2.3.

### - [ ] T-25.2.3 — Operability surface is absent from the tier6 cloud e2e suite and parity matrix [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "DevOps agents... can deploy, configure, monitor, troubleshoot, upgrade, and maintain a Lenny installation entirely through APIs... `lenny-ops` ... Connects to: Postgres, Redis, K8s API, MinIO, Prometheus, Gateway admin API." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:3, spec/25_agent-operability.md:169)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/` contains `eks_platform_test.go`, `managed_rds_test.go`, `managed_elasticache_test.go`, and `session_lifecycle_test.go`. A grep of `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml` for operability, health, diagnostics, drift, audit, escalation, or `lenny-ops` returns nothing. The cloud suite neither deploys nor exercises the operability control plane.
- **Gap:** Per-provider capability coverage (the parity matrix) omits the operability surface entirely, so the agent-operability story is unverified on GKE, EKS, and AKS, including the managed-store and workload-identity combinations that §25.4 connects `lenny-ops` to. This is a deployment-combination gap across the cloud providers. Target tier6 (cloud e2e), with parity-matrix rows added.
- **Dependencies:** Requires `lenny-ops` deployed in the tier6 cloud install and the cloud harness (`tests/testinfra/cloud`). The cloud install does not currently deploy `lenny-ops` for the operability path; adding it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/ops_surface_test.go` asserting `lenny-ops` is Ready and answers a health/diagnostics request against managed RDS and ElastiCache on at least one provider, and add operability rows to `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml`.

### - [ ] T-25.1.5 — Idempotency-Key on remediation endpoints is verified only in-process, not over the wire against a real store [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Remediation endpoints are idempotent and accept an optional `Idempotency-Key` header (Section 25.4)." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:52)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/ops/opsserver/idempotency_test.go` and `pkg/ops/opsidem/*_test.go` cover the idempotency store and handler at the unit/tier2 level, including a `pgstore` contract. `tests/tier3_contract/rest_idempotency/idempotency_test.go` and `tests/tier4_integration/idempotency_test.go` exercise idempotency on the gateway `/v1/sessions` path (`gateway.Start(t)`), not on any `lenny-ops` remediation endpoint. No integration test replays a remediation mutation (for example a lock acquire or a drift reconcile) with a repeated `Idempotency-Key` against a deployed `lenny-ops` and asserts the second call is a no-op served from the Postgres-backed idempotency store.
- **Gap:** The remediation-endpoint idempotency guarantee is the safety property that lets an agent retry without double-applying, and it is exercised end to end only on the gateway session path, never on the operability remediation path against a real store. This is a partial-coverage gap on a §25.1 safe-by-default control. Target tier4 (compose), reusing the idempotency assertion pattern.
- **Dependencies:** Depends on the `lenny-ops` compose service from T-25.2.1 and the `tests/testinfra/scenkit` idempotency helpers. Building the `lenny-ops` compose wiring is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add a case to `tests/tier4_integration/ops_endpoints_test.go` (the suite proposed in T-25.2.1) that replays a remediation mutation with a repeated `Idempotency-Key` and asserts the second response is the recorded first result, served from the Postgres idempotency store.

### - [ ] T-25.2.4 — Pagination gap-detection and cursor-opaqueness across a source transition are unit/contract-only [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Agents MUST NOT parse cursors. A cursor produced by one `actualSource` may be invalid at a different source — agents treat cursor incompatibility as a gap... When the provided cursor cannot be honored... the response includes `"gapDetected": true`." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:261, spec/25_agent-operability.md:263)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/ops/conventions/conventions_test.go` covers `ParsePageParams` (limits, time windows, malformed rejection). `tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/conventions_test.go` covers the pagination envelope, the limit cap, and malformed-parameter rejection. TESTING.md §15.3 names "gap detection on cursor eviction" for the tier4 event-stream suite. No test presents a cursor minted by one `actualSource` (for example a Redis-stream cursor) to a different source (the gateway buffer after a Redis outage) and asserts `gapDetected: true` with `oldestAvailableCursor` and `suggestedAction: resync`.
- **Gap:** The cross-source gap-detection path is the documented recovery contract for the degraded event stream and is exercised only as a same-source unit case. This is a single missing negative path on a MUST-level cursor-opaqueness rule. Target tier4 (event stream), aligned with TESTING.md §15.3.
- **Dependencies:** Depends on the `lenny-ops` event-stream integration harness with a togglable Redis (shared with T-25.2.1) and the `tests/testinfra/stubs` Redis-outage control. Building the source-transition harness is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add a case to the proposed `tests/tier4_integration/ops_endpoints_test.go` event-stream path that pages with a Redis-stream cursor, induces a Redis outage so the response falls back to the gateway buffer, and asserts the next page carries `gapDetected: true`, `oldestAvailableCursor`, and `suggestedAction: resync`.

### - [ ] T-25.1.6 — Scope-enforcement coverage is thorough at unit and contract tiers; no live-deployment enforcement test [Info] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Scopes are enforced in three places: Admin API middleware... MCP tool invocation... `/v1/admin/me/authorized-tools`." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:92)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/common/scopes/scopes_test.go` (parse and match), `pkg/gateway/openapi/openapi_test.go::TestAdminScopesFollowDocumentedSyntax_spec_15_1_933` (every `x-lenny-scope` follows the documented syntax), `pkg/ops/mcp/server_test.go::TestToolsCallScopeForbidden` and `tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/mcp_test.go` (-32001 SCOPE_FORBIDDEN), `tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/locks_test.go` (403 LOCK_SCOPE_FORBIDDEN), `pkg/gateway/admin/me_test.go` and `pkg/ops/me/service_test.go` (authorized-tools filtering), and `pkg/gateway/playground/playground_test.go` (the §25.1 `intersection(subject, playground_allowed_scope)` invariant). All three enforcement points are covered, though only in-process.
- **Gap:** No deployment-combination gap rises to a Medium here: the matching logic, the MCP rejection, the admin-API rejection, and the authorized-tools pre-filter are each pinned. The observation is that none of these run against a deployed gateway or `lenny-ops` with a real OIDC-issued token, so the enforcement is verified at the handler boundary rather than through the full auth middleware chain. Recording this as an Info; if T-25.2.1 lands a live `lenny-ops` integration harness, a single live SCOPE_FORBIDDEN assertion would close the residual gap cheaply.
- **Dependencies:** Would reuse the live `lenny-ops` harness from T-25.2.1 and a real OIDC token from `tests/testinfra/tokenservice`. None blocking — buildable once the harness exists.
- **Suggested test:** When the T-25.2.1 harness lands, add one tier4 assertion that a narrowly-scoped real token (for example `tools:health:read` only) receives 403 SCOPE_FORBIDDEN when calling a pool-scale endpoint on the deployed `lenny-ops`, using `tests/testinfra/tokenservice` to mint the token.

### - [ ] T-25.2.5 — Widened canonical degradation envelope (in-process-history trigger) has no contract or integration coverage of the healthy/degraded transition [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Any response whose data quality depends on the availability of an external dependency, or on in-process history having accumulated (for example the capacity-recommendation ring buffers, which start empty after a gateway restart, Section 25.3), includes a top-level `degradation` object with a uniform schema... Endpoints serving from their primary source omit `degradation` entirely (or return `"level": "healthy"`...), except that an endpoint whose data quality also depends on in-process history reports `"level": "degraded"` while it holds no history at all and returns to `"level": "healthy"` once any of its rules records a sample." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:205, spec/25_agent-operability.md:233)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/operability/recommendations/service_test.go::TestGetRecommendationsEmptyWhenNoData`, `::TestGetRecommendationsHealthyEnvelopeWhenBelowThreshold`, and `::TestGetRecommendationsHealthyWhenCategoryFilterStarvedRuleHasData` pin the degraded-while-empty and healthy-once-populated behavior at the unit level, landed by proposal 0029 (commit `15dc2d80`) reconciling build-gaps finding F-25.3.16. `tests/tier11_docs/recommendations_post_restart_reconciliation_test.go` asserts the two reconciled spec passages are textually self-consistent — a documentation check, not a runtime behavior check. A grep of `tests/tier3_contract` and `tests/tier4_integration` for `/v1/admin/recommendations` or "recommendations" returns no matches: no contract or integration test exists for this endpoint at all.
- **Gap:** Proposal 0029 widened the §25.2 canonical degradation envelope's trigger from "external dependency unavailable" to also cover "insufficient in-process history," and the one endpoint that exercises the new branch (`/v1/admin/recommendations`) has zero contract or integration coverage — this is the same endpoint T-25.2.2 already flags as missing from live-gateway testing generally, but the specific new state-machine behavior (degraded-while-empty, flips to healthy on first sample) is a distinct, more recent gap. A wire-level regression — `omitempty` swallowing `"level"` on marshal, or the HTTP handler failing to propagate the service's `Degradation` field — would ship undetected by the unit suite alone, since that suite calls the service directly rather than through JSON marshaling or a live HTTP round trip. Target tier3 (httptest contract) for the wire shape and tier4 (gateway subprocess) for the observed restart-to-populated transition.
- **Dependencies:** Reuses the existing `tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints` httptest harness and the `tests/tier4_integration/gateway_full_e2e_test.go` gateway-subprocess harness; both already exist and need no new infrastructure. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/recommendations_test.go` asserting a `GetRecommendations` response over `httptest` with an empty `WindowStore` carries `degradation.level == "degraded"` and a warning, and that a populated store carries `"healthy"`; extend `tests/tier4_integration/gateway_full_e2e_test.go` to call `/v1/admin/recommendations` immediately after gateway start (empty ring buffers) and assert the degraded envelope, then again after driving traffic that records a sample and assert it flips to healthy.

### - [ ] T-25.1.7 — RFC 9068 scope narrowing has no end-to-end (tier-5) coverage on a live cluster; only in-process (tier-9) coverage exists [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** The §25.1 scoped-token machinery (RFC 8693 token exchange, RFC 9068 space-separated `scope` claim, `tools:<domain>:<action>` matching) and the admin-API scope gate that narrows an exchanged token's authority. (spec/25_agent-operability.md, §25.1)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier9_security/admin_scope_enforce_test.go:11-21` exercises the §25.1 scope gate in-process only; its own comment records that the scope-narrowing boundary is not reachable on the e2e Kind cluster. No tier5 test drives the scope gate against a live gateway.
- **Gap:** On the e2e Kind cluster the scope-narrowing boundary is never reachable end to end. The install runs `global devMode: true` (`tests/testinfra/kind/e2e-values.yaml:309`), so dev-header auth carries no `scope` claim and there is no OIDC provider to issue a scoped token. Minting a scoped token via `/v1/oauth/token` from the gateway admin bearer is also blocked: the running gateway and lenny-token-service deployments both pass `--kms-provider=local` with independent ephemeral keys, so the token service cannot verify the gateway-signed `subject_token`, and a probe exchange request timed out. The RFC 9068 narrowing enforcement is therefore verified only at the in-process (tier-9) layer.
- **Dependencies:** Closing this needs the e2e install to add an in-cluster OIDC stub or a shared gateway/token-service signing key so a scope-narrowed token can be minted and presented on a live cluster. This is the same RFC 9068 scoped-JWT-narrowing dependency already flagged on T-DEP.8 and the T-JRN.11 escalation. Building that infrastructure is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier5 Kind test that mints a scope-narrowed token (via an in-cluster OIDC stub or a shared gateway/token-service signing key), presents it to the deployed gateway, and asserts an out-of-scope admin call is rejected with the documented scope error while an in-scope call succeeds.

## §25.3 Gateway-Side Ops Endpoints <a id="t-25.3"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/25_agent-operability.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The §25.3 subsystems (Platform Health API, Capacity Recommendations, Version and Config Introspection, Event Emission, Gateway Event Buffer) have thorough unit coverage in `pkg/gateway/operability/health`, `pkg/gateway/operability/recommendations`, and `pkg/events`/`pkg/gateway/eventbuffer` (the package tree moved under the proposal-0020 `pkg/gateway` reorganization: `pkg/gateway/health` → `pkg/gateway/operability/health`, `pkg/gateway/recommendations` → `pkg/gateway/operability/recommendations`, `pkg/gateway/events` split into the gateway-neutral `pkg/events` vocabulary and the concrete `pkg/gateway/eventbuffer` ring buffer, and `pkg/gateway/admin` → `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin`), and the store-outage degradation path is exercised end to end on Kind by the tier8 chaos suite for Postgres, Redis, and MinIO. Above the unit tier the coverage still thins sharply: only `/v1/admin/health` is touched by integration and chaos tests, while `/v1/admin/recommendations`, `/v1/admin/events/buffer`, `/v1/admin/platform/version`, and `/v1/admin/platform/config` still have no contract, integration, or end-to-end test anywhere on disk. The spec-mandated admin-role requirement (line 410) is still contradicted by an unauthenticated health handler with no test pinning the spec's behavior, the `lenny_ops_endpoints` integration suite declared in TESTING.md §12.4/§14.6 still does not exist, the Prometheus-unreachable health-accuracy claim is still unverified at every tier, and the cross-replica `eventKey` deduplication over the headless Service is still exercised only with in-process fakes. Two proposals landed against this unit since the 2026-06-03 audit: proposal 0029 reconciled a self-contradictory post-restart recommendations contract (dropping the per-item `confidence: 0.0` reading in favor of the canonical §25.2 `degradation` envelope, now backed by new unit tests in `pkg/gateway/operability/recommendations/service_test.go`) and proposal 0033 replaced the spec's `OperationalEvent = cloudevents.Event` alias mandate with the native structured-content struct the code already shipped, adding byte-level inline-OCSF wire-form tests in `pkg/events/auditbearing_test.go` and `tests/tier3_contract/cloudevents/cloudevents_test.go`. Neither proposal changed runtime behavior, and neither closes any of the ten tracked findings outright — the underlying tier2-and-above gaps they touch (T-25.3.6, T-25.3.7, T-25.3.10) are narrower than before but still open. The `tests/spec-map.json` entry for §25.3 now lists the two new unit tests plus the tier11 doc-consistency tests the two proposals added, alongside the still-placeholder `tests/tier2_component/healthchecks/...` path.
Counts: 3 High, 5 Medium, 3 Low, 0 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-25.3.1 — Health endpoints are served unauthenticated, contradicting the spec's admin-role requirement, with no test pinning either behavior [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "These endpoints live on the existing admin API, served from the gateway's main port. They require `platform-admin` or `tenant-admin` role (same as the rest of the admin API)." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:410)
- **Existing tests:** The chaos suite probes `/v1/admin/health` with no credentials and the helper comment states it hits "the unauthenticated §25.3 /v1/admin/health endpoint" (tests/tier8_chaos/chaos_helpers_test.go:501, 507). The tier4 integration tests call health with an empty role argument (tests/tier4_integration/gateway_full_e2e_test.go:180, tests/tier4_integration/gateway_postgres_e2e_test.go:181). The implementation mounts the health handler directly on the gateway's top-level mux ahead of the `/v1/admin/` catch-all and never wraps it with an admin-role check (cmd/lenny-gateway/httpsurface.go:256-257), with a code comment asserting the endpoints are "unauthenticated-readable per §25.3" (pkg/gateway/operability/health/handler.go:17, package moved from `pkg/gateway/health` under the proposal-0020 reorganization). No test asserts the role requirement that the spec states. Searched tiers 2 through 9 under tests/ and the gateway admin router, now `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin`.
- **Gap:** The spec and the implementation still disagree on whether the health endpoints require an admin role. No test encodes the spec's requirement, so a regression in either direction ships silently, and the existing chaos infrastructure actively depends on the unauthenticated behavior. This is a security-control inconsistency on a public admin surface. The work needs an adversarial test (an unauthenticated and an under-privileged caller) plus a spec-or-implementation reconciliation. Target tiers are tier3 contract and tier9 security.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a token-minting helper for an authenticated admin caller and an under-scoped caller. tests/testinfra/tokenservice and tests/testinfra/security provide token issuance; buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/health_auth_test.go asserting that `GET /v1/admin/health`, `/health/summary`, and `/health/{component}` return the documented status code for an unauthenticated caller, an admin caller, and a non-admin caller, and reconcile spec line 410 with the handler. Use tests/testinfra/tokenservice to issue the admin and non-admin tokens.
- **Needs human input (as of 2026-07-12):** §25.3 line 410 requires platform-admin/tenant-admin role on the gateway health endpoints, but the gateway serves /v1/admin/health, /v1/admin/health/summary, and /v1/admin/health/{component} unauthenticated (deliberately, per the handler comment), and tier-8 chaos tests depend on that anonymous access. Which artifact is authoritative: (a) fix the code to gate /v1/admin/health* behind platform-admin/tenant-admin (401 for anonymous, 403 for non-admin, 200 for admin) and switch the tier-8 chaos probes to authenticated calls, or (b) amend §25.3 via a proposal to make at least the summary/heartbeat endpoint explicitly public (§25.4 line 45 describes it as an unauthenticated-feeling fallback heartbeat and line 422 labels summary "for synthetic health checks"), leaving the implementation as-is? A faithful role-gating contract test is committed but skipped pending this decision.

- **Resolution:** Added a tier-3 contract suite (tests/tier3_contract/gateway_ops/endpoints_test.go) that drives the gateway admin Router via httptest and pins the wire format of the four §25.3 read endpoints (recommendations, events/buffer, platform/version, platform/config) plus the UNKNOWN_RECOMMENDATION_CATEGORY 400 and RECOMMENDATIONS_UNAVAILABLE 503 error envelopes against the §25.2 canonical schema. ### - [ ] T-25.3.5 — Cross-replica event-buffer fan-out and `eventKey` deduplication over the headless Service is exercised only with in-process fakes [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "When `lenny-ops` uses the buffer fallback, it discovers all gateway pod IPs via the headless Service `lenny-gateway-pods` (see below) and polls each replica individually. Deduplication across replicas uses `eventKey`, not a content hash." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:759) and "lenny-ops uses DNS SRV lookup (`lenny-gateway-pods.{namespace}.svc`) to discover all gateway pod IPs." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:761)
- **Existing tests:** The fan-out is unit-tested with three httptest servers behind a `StaticDiscovery` (pkg/ops/gateway/client_test.go:128, TestFanOutGet_Discovery) and the buffer dedup-by-eventKey is unit-tested in pkg/ops/events. The chart renders the headless Service and a helm unit test asserts it (charts/lenny/tests/gateway-deployment_test.yaml:892, moved from line 700 as the chart test file grew). No test runs two real gateway replicas, induces a Redis outage so lenny-ops falls back to the buffer, and asserts the merged stream is deduplicated by `eventKey` across replicas. A grep for `lenny-gateway-pods` across tests/ still returns only chart/inventory hits (tests/integration/core_deployment_inventory_test.go, tests/tier0_static/core_deployment_inventory_test.go), neither of which drives fan-out traffic. Searched tiers 4, 5, and 6.
- **Gap:** The buffer fallback is the resilience path that keeps operational events observable when Redis is down, and its correctness across replicas depends on real DNS SRV discovery and per-replica `eventKey` uniqueness. The behavior is verified only with fakes and a single process, so the cross-replica collision class the spec calls out (two replicas emitting `alert_fired` for the same alert in the same second) is never reproduced against real pods. The work is a failure-path deployment-combination test (HA multi-replica gateway plus Redis outage). Target tiers are tier5 e2e on Kind or tier6 cloud.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a two-replica gateway install on Kind, a Redis scale-to-zero injection, and SRV resolution of `lenny-gateway-pods`. tests/testinfra/kind and the tier8 chaos store scale helpers provide the parts; the multi-replica install value still does not have an e2e fixture and building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier5_e2e_kind/event_buffer_fanout_test.go that installs the gateway with two replicas, scales Redis to zero, drives both replicas to emit a same-second `alert_fired`, polls the buffer through lenny-ops, and asserts the merged result deduplicates by `eventKey` with no duplicate alert.

### - [ ] T-25.3.6 — Only two of the health checkers had a real-backing component test; MinIO, K8s API, cert-manager, and connector probes now have verdict/issue-code unit coverage but still no tier2 test with a real or stub backend [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Lightweight dependency probes. TCP connect + single-query probes against Postgres (`SELECT 1`), Redis (`PING`), MinIO (`HeadBucket`), K8s API server (`/healthz`), cert-manager (certificate status), and registered connectors. Each probe has a hard timeout of 2 seconds." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:440)
- **Existing tests:** The component suite tests/tier2_component/healthchecks/backends_test.go still covers only the Postgres and Redis checkers against real containers and against unreachable backends (unchanged: TestPostgresChecker, TestRedisChecker). Since 2026-06-03, the package-level pkg/gateway/operability/health/backends/backends_test.go (moved from `pkg/gateway/health/backends`) gained fake-backed verdict and issue-code tests for the four previously-uncovered checkers: TestObjectStoreHealthy/Unhealthy_spec_25_3_441, TestAPIServerHealthy/Unhealthy_spec_25_3_441, TestConnectorsHealthy/Unhealthy_spec_25_3_441, and TestCertManagerHealthy/DegradedWhenExpiringSoon/UnhealthyWhenExpired/UnhealthyWhenUnreadable_spec_25_3_441 (lines 126-235). These assert the `health.StatusHealthy/Degraded/Unhealthy` verdict and the stamped issue code (`MINIO_UNREACHABLE`, `CERT_EXPIRY_IMMINENT`, etc.) against fake probes and a fake `CertReader`, but none is a tier2 component test against a real or stub backend, and none asserts the 2-second probe timeout. The `ObjectStore`, `APIServer`, `CertManager`, and `Connectors` checker functions still live at the same lines (pkg/gateway/health/backends/backends.go:240, 268, 299, 342, package now `pkg/gateway/operability/health/backends`). Searched tier1 unit, tier2 component, and tier8 chaos.
- **Gap:** The healthy/degraded/unhealthy verdicts and issue codes for four of the six probes are now pinned at the unit tier with fakes, narrowing the finding from "no test at all" to "no test at the tier the spec-derived probe behavior — a real MinIO HeadBucket, a real or fake `/healthz` responder, a real certificate file, a real connector registry — actually needs". The cert-manager probe in particular governs the `CertExpiryImminent` degraded window, which is a security-relevant signal, and its unit test uses a synthetic `time.Now().Add(...)` fixture rather than a certificate file inside its expiry window. No test anywhere asserts the spec's 2-second hard probe timeout for any of the four checkers. The work now covers the tier2 real-backend case and the timeout case specifically. Target tier is tier2 component, with the cert-expiry case also suited to tier9.
- **Dependencies:** The MinIO probe needs a MinIO container (tests/testinfra/containers, already used by the Postgres/Redis tier2 tests). The API-server probe needs a fake `/healthz` responder, the cert-manager probe needs a certificate fixture inside its expiry window, and the connectors probe needs a connector-registry stub; none of these three exist yet on disk and building them is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Extend tests/tier2_component/healthchecks/backends_test.go (or add objectstore_certmanager_test.go) to drive `backends.ObjectStore` against a real MinIO container, and `backends.APIServer`, `backends.CertManager`, and `backends.Connectors` against stub backends, asserting the status verdict, the stamped issue code, and the 2-second probe timeout for each.

### - [ ] T-25.3.7 — The operational-event CloudEvents and OCSF wire format served by the buffer has no conformance test reading from the buffer itself [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Every emitted event is a CloudEvents v1.0.2 JSON record ... Audit-bearing events carry the OCSF record directly in the CloudEvents `data` field with `datacontenttype: application/ocsf+json` ... Non-audit operational events use `datacontenttype: application/json` and carry an event-specific JSON payload in `data` whose schema is documented per `type` in the catalogue." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:650, 652)
- **Existing tests:** The tier3 cloudevents contract test pins the CloudEvents v1.0.2 envelope produced by `pkg/gateway/storage/eventbus` and the audit-bearing `application/ocsf+json` discriminator generically (tests/tier3_contract/cloudevents/cloudevents_test.go:34, 159), and it references `operation_progressed` only inside a generic type-list assertion (line 35). Since 2026-06-03, proposal 0033 reconciled the spec's `OperationalEvent = cloudevents.Event` alias mandate to the native struct the code already shipped and added a byte-level inline-OCSF wire-form assertion for both envelope types: TestCloudEventsInlineOCSFWireForm (tests/tier3_contract/cloudevents/cloudevents_test.go:195) for the eventbus `Event`, and the parallel TestOperationalEventInlineOCSFWireForm (pkg/events/auditbearing_test.go:72) for the §25.3 `OperationalEvent` specifically — this closes the finding's prior observation that no-double-wrapping was "asserted only on the generic eventbus path, not on the §25.3 emitter output". No test still reads an actual `dev.lenny.alert_fired`, `pool_state_changed`, or `operation_progressed` record from `GET /v1/admin/events/buffer` and validates it against the CloudEvents v1.0.2 schema or the per-type payload schema in the §16.6 catalogue. The catalogue unit test confirms each short name maps to a `dev.lenny.*` type (pkg/events/catalog_test.go, moved from pkg/gateway/events/catalog_test.go). Searched tiers 3 and 10.
- **Gap:** The remaining gap is narrower than in the prior audit: the inline-OCSF single-envelope rule is now pinned for both the transport-level eventbus `Event` and the §25.3 `OperationalEvent` at the byte level. What is still missing is a conformance test that reads records back out through the buffer query surface (`GET /v1/admin/events/buffer`) and validates them against the CloudEvents v1.0.2 schema or the per-type payload contract from the §16.6 catalogue — the byte-level tests marshal an envelope directly rather than round-tripping through the buffer's HTTP surface. Target tiers are tier3 contract or tier10 conformance.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a CloudEvents v1.0.2 schema validator and the per-type payload schemas from the §16.6 catalogue. tests/tier3_contract/cloudevents already loads the envelope and now asserts the inline-data byte form; the per-type payload schemas and the buffer-read harness may need to be added and building that fixture set is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier3_contract/cloudevents/ops_events_buffer_test.go that emits each §25.3 event type through the emitter, reads them via the buffer query surface, validates the envelope against the CloudEvents v1.0.2 schema, and asserts `datacontenttype` is `application/ocsf+json` for audit-bearing types and `application/json` for the rest.

## §25.4 The lenny-ops Service <a id="t-25.4"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/25_agent-operability.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
§25.4 specifies the mandatory `lenny-ops` Deployment and its full operational surface: identity discovery (`/v1/admin/me`), the operations inventory, remediation locks with a tiered Postgres/Redis/memory store and epoch-based split-brain resolution, idempotency with tier-dependent enforcement, tiered escalations, self-monitoring, leader-elected singletons, the `GatewayClient` with TLS-default internal transport (NET-070), Prometheus-with-fan-out aggregation, and three rendered NetworkPolicies. Unit coverage in `pkg/ops/**` is dense, the helm-unittests in `charts/lenny/tests/ops-*` pin the rendered manifests, and a tier3 contract suite (`tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints`) pins the wire shapes through `httptest` with stub stores. Coverage falls off sharply above the unit and static tiers: there is no tier4 compose-stack exercise of any `lenny-ops` endpoint against real backing services, no tier2/tier8 exercise of the lock tier-transition and split-brain reconciliation against real Postgres and Redis, the tier9 RBAC and NetworkPolicy suites never drive the live `lenny-ops` service, the tier5/tier6 e2e coverage stops at "Deployment Ready," and no harness pins any `lenny-ops` response against the `/v1/openapi.json` schema. Several deployment combinations (multi-replica `memoryTier` rejection, Tier-1 vs Tier-2/3 idempotency enforcement, Prometheus-down fan-out, air-gapped) are unexercised end to end. Proposal 0021 moved the audit log query API fully to the gateway (Section 25.9) and re-hosted `/v1/openapi.json` on the gateway as well (still covering `lenny-ops`'s own routes via the F-COV-3 document merge); this reassigns wording throughout §25.4 but does not remove any of the findings below. Proposal 0019's F-SH-1 fix wired a real producer for the previously-inert `lenny_ops_clock_skew_seconds` gauge, which is a new self-monitoring surface with only fake-clock unit coverage (T-25.4.15).
Counts: 6 High, 10 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [x] T-25.4.1 — Remediation-lock tier transition and split-brain resolution have no real-store or chaos test [High] — RESOLVED 12bc5a55cdc9bcab773526802351f24270908243
- **Resolution:** Added a tier2 component test (tests/tier2_component/coordination/tier_transition_test.go) that wires the real pgstore + redisstore through the tiered coordination Service across a Postgres-down-then-up transition: it drives the Redis-side outage-epoch increment, post-outage Tier 2 acquisitions stamped with that epoch, and the single-transaction advisory-lock reconciliation reading the live Redis store, then asserts the MAX(redis,postgres) epoch written to both stores, the pre-outage-wins and Redis-wins split-brain resolutions, a copied Redis-only scope, and the ops_lock_conflicts / split-brain-metric / audit trail. Also filled the previously uncovered "Postgres wins when the Redis lock is expired" resolution branch in the pgstore reconcile tests. Both pass against unmodified product code.

### - [x] T-25.4.2 — No tier4 integration test drives any lenny-ops endpoint against the real compose stack [High] — RESOLVED 703996a1e4ebc5df019d93b9524f6ad084baa357
- **Resolution:** The tier-4 lenny-ops remediation-lock persistence journey (GET /v1/admin/me -> operations inventory -> POST/DELETE /v1/admin/remediation-locks against the running cmd/lenny-ops binary on the real Postgres/Redis compose stack) was already committed but had been rejected for lacking the required tier-2+ // diagnosis: annotation. Added a // diagnosis: comment immediately above TestOpsServiceRemediationLockPersistenceE2E stating that a failure means the lenny-ops composition root did not thread the live Postgres Tier-1 store through to the remediation-lock surface. Test re-run green (5.59s) against real Postgres/Redis; validate-maps clean.

### - [x] T-25.4.3 — lenny-ops RBAC, scope-narrowing, and lock-scope authorization are not verified against the live service [High] — RESOLVED 867c61c218bbbf0d890b72862b0fb1fe8c6ae5e2
- **Resolution:** The six lenny-ops RBAC tests in tests/tier9_security/ops_rbac_test.go were rejected only for missing // diagnosis: comments (required on tier-2+ tests) and a comment that referenced the ephemeral audit finding rather than the endpoints. Added a // diagnosis: line above each of the six test functions stating what a failure means, and reworded the opsReadEndpoints comment to name the lock, escalation, and operations families directly. Tests still pass against unmodified product code; spec-map registration and validate-maps are clean.

### - [x] T-25.4.4 — lenny-ops NetworkPolicies and the internal mTLS/plaintext transport are not exercised live [High] — RESOLVED 84a05db689e02754de07affde7800945238e93c6
- **Resolution:** Added tests/tier9_security/ops_network_policy_test.go: five live tier9 tests that install the control plane on Kind and drive in-cluster curl probes to confirm the CNI enforces the §25.4 lenny-ops NetworkPolicies. They assert the deny-all-ingress/ingress-controller/egress policies are applied with the correct selectors and NET-070 default ports (8443 TLS, not 8080 plaintext); an app=lenny-ops probe reaches the gateway internal TLS port but is dropped reaching the token-service (bound egress) and dropped reaching a cluster pod IP on port 443 (SSRF except block); a default-namespace probe is dropped reaching the lenny-ops admin port 8090 (deny-all-ingress, with a CoreDNS positive control isolating ingress from source egress); and the live lenny-ops metrics record no plaintext admin-API handshake. All five pass against current code.

### - [ ] T-25.4.5 — Idempotency Postgres-outage 503 and tier-dependent enforcement have no real-store or deployment-combination test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Endpoints requiring idempotency keys return `503 IDEMPOTENCY_STORE_UNAVAILABLE`. This is stricter than most ops endpoints ... silently proceeding without it would violate the contract." and "The following endpoints **require** `Idempotency-Key` at Tier 2/3 ... At Tier 1 (dev), the key is optional" (spec/25_agent-operability.md:2048, 2037)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/ops/opsserver/idempotency_test.go` covers `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`, replay through the chain, and the optional-endpoint pass at the handler level. `pkg/ops/opsidem/opsidem_test.go`, `memory_test.go`, and `opsidem/pgstore/pgstore_test.go` cover the store. `tests/tier2_component/stores/idempotencystore_test.go` exercises the §11.5 **gateway** `pkg/gateway/middleware/idempotency/pgstore`, not the §25.4 `ops_idempotency_keys` table. No test takes Postgres down against a real `lenny-ops` to assert `503 IDEMPOTENCY_STORE_UNAVAILABLE`, and none asserts the Tier-1-optional vs Tier-2/3-required behavior across the two tier presets.
- **Gap:** The fail-closed 503 (which prevents multi-replica split-brain) and the tier-conditioned requirement are both untested above the in-process layer. The 503 path is a failure scenario; the tier difference is a deployment-combination gap (`values-tier1.yaml` vs `-tier2.yaml`).
- **Dependencies:** Requires real Postgres (`tests/testinfra/containers`) for the outage case and the two tier presets for the combination case. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier2_component/opsidem/outage_test.go` wiring the Postgres-backed ops idempotency store and asserting `IDEMPOTENCY_STORE_UNAVAILABLE` when the pool is closed; add a tier4 case parameterized over `platform.tier` that asserts `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED` at tier2 and acceptance at tier1 for `POST /v1/admin/backups type:full`.

### - [ ] T-25.4.6 — Escalation tiered persistence and exactly-once emission are not exercised against real stores under outage [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`POST /v1/admin/escalations` attempts storage tiers in order ... `201 Created`/`durable-postgres` ... `201 Created`/`durable-redis` ... `202 Accepted`/`buffered-memory`" and "The event stream receives exactly one `escalation_created` event per escalation, regardless of how many times the escalation is written or flushed across tiers." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:2384, 2406)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/ops/escalation/tiered_test.go`, `escalation_test.go`, `pgstore/pgstore_test.go`, and `redisstore/redisstore_test.go` cover the tiered create path and stores. `tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/escalations_test.go` pins the wire shape through `httptest`. `tests/tier8_chaos/escalation_retry_test.go::TestEscalationEmissionRetryAfterDualDestinationRecovery` (landed for F-REL-1, the emission-retry path previously had no production caller) drives `escalation.Service.RetryEmission` against a fake dual-destination emitter and confirms exactly-once re-publish on recovery, but it does not use real Postgres, real Redis, or a real event stream — the "dual outage" it models is an in-process emitter flag, not the tiered-store outage this finding names. No test drives a real `lenny-ops` through a Postgres-down (Tier 2 Redis), then dual-down (Tier 3 memory), then recovery sequence, asserting the `X-Lenny-Persistence` header transitions, `created_at` preservation across flush, the 30s reconciliation flush, and a single `escalation_created` event on the stream.
- **Gap:** The reconciliation goroutine, the emission exactly-once invariant across tier flushes, and the `requireDurable:true` fail-fast (`503 ESCALATION_NO_DURABLE_STORE`) are unverified end to end with real stores and a real event stream. This is a failure-path and durability-contract gap.
- **Dependencies:** Requires real Postgres, real Redis, and the gateway event emitter (`tests/testinfra/compose`, `tests/testinfra/audit`). Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier8_chaos/ops_escalation_tiers_test.go` that creates escalations while toggling Postgres and Redis availability, asserts the persistence-tier progression and single emission, and asserts `ESCALATION_NO_DURABLE_STORE` under dual outage when `requireDurable:true`, using `tests/testinfra/chaos` and `tests/testinfra/audit`.

### - [ ] T-25.4.7 — No conformance test pins lenny-ops responses against the published /v1/openapi.json schema [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The canonical API contract is exposed as an OpenAPI 3.1 document served by the gateway" and "Full OpenAPI 3.1 document (JSON) for the entire operability surface — both the gateway admin-API endpoints and `lenny-ops`'s own endpoints" (spec/25_agent-operability.md:4515, 4519)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/*` assert individual field presence (for example `locks_test.go` checks `id, scope, operation, acquiredBy, ...`) but do not validate any response against a JSON Schema or the OpenAPI document. `pkg/gateway/externalapi/openapi/completeness_test.go::TestDocumentMatchesRegisteredEndpoints` (landed for F-COV-3, the gateway/lenny-ops document merge) asserts every registered route — gateway and `lenny-ops` alike, via `pkg/ops/opsserver.RouteSchemas()` — appears in the served `openapi.json`, but this is a route-inventory completeness check, not a response-body schema-conformance check. `tests/testinfra/schematest/helpers.go` provides a jsonschema wrapper, but no `lenny-ops` test uses it, and no test under `tests/tier10_conformance` references `openapi.json`.
- **Gap:** The `lenny-ops` REST surface is a public protocol surface for DevOps agents. Proposal 0021 moved `/v1/openapi.json` hosting from `lenny-ops` to the gateway (it still documents `lenny-ops`'s own routes via the F-COV-3 merge), and removed the `/v1/openapi/{endpoint-id}` fragment route entirely; the document-completeness gap this finding originally named is now covered by `completeness_test.go`, but there is still no conformance check that a `lenny-ops` response's actual JSON body validates against the corresponding schema component in the (now gateway-served) `/v1/openapi.json`, so a response-schema regression (a renamed or dropped field, a wrong type) would ship. The standards-conformance pin on response bodies is absent.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the gateway-served OpenAPI document to be a fetchable test fixture (it now already is, per `completeness_test.go`) and the `schematest` helper (present). Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/openapi_conformance_test.go` that fetches `/v1/openapi.json` from the gateway, then validates live `lenny-ops` responses for `/v1/admin/me`, `/v1/admin/operations`, lock, and error-envelope endpoints against the matching schema components using `tests/testinfra/schematest`.

### - [ ] T-25.4.8 — Multi-replica memoryTier rejection and leader-elected singleton failover are unexercised [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Default behavior in multi-replica mode (`ops.locks.memoryTier: \"single-replica-only\"`) **rejects** in-memory locks during dual-storage outages, returning `503 REMEDIATION_LOCK_NO_COORDINATION`." and "Webhook delivery (background goroutine per subscription runs only on leader) ... the lease expires (15s by default) and the new pod elected as leader on a different node." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:1545, 1343, 1331)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/ops/coordination/gate_test.go` and `service_test.go::TestServiceMemoryTier*` cover the gate logic in-process. `tests/tier8_chaos/leader_election_test.go::TestControllerLeaderElectionDisruption` exercises the **controller** Lease failover, not `lenny-ops-leader`. `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/lifecycle_test.go::TestLennyOpsFirstDeploy` only asserts the Deployment reaches Ready. No test scales `lenny-ops` to two replicas to assert `REMEDIATION_LOCK_NO_COORDINATION` under dual outage, and none kills the `lenny-ops` leader to assert singleton failover (webhook delivery, backup cron) onto a surviving replica.
- **Gap:** The multi-replica safety default (the central trade-off of §25.4 Multi-Replica Scaling) and the `lenny-ops-leader` failover are both deployment-combination gaps verified only in-process. Singleton failover is a resilience scenario; the memoryTier rejection is a failure-path scenario.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a Kind deployment of `lenny-ops` at `replicas: 2` with node anti-affinity, plus the chaos harness to kill the leader pod and the store-outage harness. `tests/testinfra/kind` and `tests/testinfra/chaos` exist. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier8_chaos/ops_leader_failover_test.go` reading `lenny-ops-leader` `holderIdentity`, deleting the leader, and asserting failover plus continued webhook delivery; add a tier8 case at `replicas:2` that takes both stores down and asserts `REMEDIATION_LOCK_NO_COORDINATION` on lock acquire.

### - [ ] T-25.4.9 — Prometheus-down fan-out fallback and the unreachable definition are unverified end to end [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Prometheus is considered unreachable when any of the following holds for longer than `ops.prometheus.unreachableThreshold` (default 10s) ... Used when Prometheus is unreachable. `lenny-ops` queries each replica's health endpoint and merges: worst-of status per component, union of suggested actions. Cached for 10s. Circuit breakers skip unresponsive replicas." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:1936, 1968)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/ops/metrics/source_test.go` and `duration_test.go` cover the `MetricSource` and query-duration metric in-process. `pkg/ops/gateway/breaker_test.go`, `discovery_test.go`, and `client_test.go` cover the circuit breaker and headless-service discovery in isolation. No test exercises the `PrometheusWithFallback` path against a real gateway fleet over the headless Service with Prometheus made unreachable, and `replica-fanout`/`gateway-scrape` `actualSource` values are not asserted in any tier4+ test.
- **Gap:** The whole "survive a Prometheus outage" story (health worst-of merge, recommendations aggregate-before-evaluate, pool-bottleneck `gateway-scrape` fallback, partial-aggregation degradation warning, `disableOnPrometheusOutage` returning `503 RECOMMENDATIONS_UNAVAILABLE`) is unverified end to end. This is a failure-path and deployment-combination gap (with-Prometheus vs without). (The §25.4 "Why required at Tier 2/3" table's capacity-recommendations row was reworded from a bare `confidence: 0.0` claim to the `degradation.level` transition the gateway's recommendations engine actually implements; that recommendations-engine behavior is gateway-resident (§25.3) and is tracked there rather than duplicated in this lenny-ops finding.)
- **Dependencies:** Requires a multi-replica gateway reachable via the headless Service and a Prometheus stub that can be made unreachable (`tests/testinfra/stubs`, `tests/testinfra/gateway`). A controllable Prometheus stub may need adding; record it as part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/ops_prometheus_fallback_test.go` that points `lenny-ops` at an unreachable Prometheus, asserts health and recommendations fall back to `replica-fanout` with the partial-aggregation warning, and asserts `RECOMMENDATIONS_UNAVAILABLE` when `disableOnPrometheusOutage:true`.

- **Spec/Doc:** "The same NetworkPolicy that allows the operator's Prometheus to scrape Lenny components ... also allows `lenny-ops` egress to the configured Prometheus URL." and "Cloud-managed Redis (ElastiCache, Memorystore, Azure Cache) causes the chart to substitute an `ipBlock` egress rule resolved at render time." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:1466, 1205)

- **Gap:** The `ipBlock` egress substitution for cloud-managed Postgres/Redis/object storage, workload-identity/IRSA/WIF token acquisition by `GatewayClient`, and the managed-ingress SSE hold for `lenny-ops` are unverified on GKE/EKS/AKS. The mandatory service has no tier6 coverage and no parity-matrix accounting, which is a deployment-combination gap across all cloud providers.
