A search for `helm.sh/release` and a CRD-version source across `pkg/ops/upgradeservice` and `cmd/lenny-ops` finds no implementation, so `GET /v1/admin/platform/version/full` silently omits CRD and Helm drift.

## §25.9-25.10 Audit Log Query API and Config Drift Detection <a id="t-25.9-25.10"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/25_agent-operability.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The §25.9 audit query API and the §25.10 drift detection API both have dense handler-level and unit-level coverage: `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/audit_query_filter_test.go` (moved from `pkg/gateway/admin` by the 0020 `externalapi` regrouping) and `pkg/ops/driftservice/driftservice_test.go` pin nearly every documented filter, error code, severity classification, and envelope field against in-memory backends, and `pkg/ops/driftservice/pgstore/pgstore_test.go` exercises the snapshot store against an embedded Postgres. Since the original audit, the platform-admin cross-tenant scatter-gather read, its result cache, and the 207 `AUDIT_PARTIAL_RESULTS` degradation are now built and tested at component/handler level (F-25.9.11), the §25.10 running-state collector is now wired to a real gateway-backed reader in every chart deployment (F-25.10.4), and the upgrade-time target-snapshot write/promote lifecycle is built and unit/contract tested. Coverage still thins out above the component tier: the §25.9 query endpoints (`GET /v1/admin/audit-events`, `/summary`, `/{seq}`, `/retranslate`, `/republish`) are never driven against a real Postgres `auditstore.Store`, the declared tier4 `lenny_ops_endpoints` compose-stack suite for audit query and drift detection is absent, and neither the gateway-backed drift collector nor the target-snapshot promotion has been exercised through a real integration or e2e run. The production scatter-gather cache is in-memory rather than the spec-mandated Redis, and the `audit.query_executed` audit event still hardcodes its cache/shard fields. Several other normative behaviors (`chainIntegrity: rechained_post_outage` reconciliation, drift reconcile against the real gateway, drift cross-tenant isolation) remain unverified at component level or above, and the spec-map's `packages` field still points at directories that do not exist on disk.
Counts: 4 High, 8 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-25.10.1 — Drift report's gateway-backed running-state collector has no integration or e2e test against a live gateway [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`GET /v1/admin/drift` compares: 1. Running state — read via `GatewayClient` calls to `GET /v1/admin/runtimes`, `GET /v1/admin/pools`, etc. 2. Desired state — read from `bootstrap_seed_snapshot` table in Postgres." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:3773)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/ops/driftservice/driftservice_test.go` (TestReportDetectsDriftAgainstSnapshot and peers) and `pkg/ops/opsserver/drift_reconcile_test.go` drive the service with a `fixedRunning` stub. `tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/drift_test.go` (TestDriftReportContract) uses `driftservice.NewMemSnapshotStore()` plus a `fixedRunningState` stub. `pkg/ops/driftservice/gatewayreader/gatewayreader.go` plus `gatewayreader_test.go` (F-25.10.4, commit 28777027) now build and unit-test a real `RunningStateReader` that reads the four gateway admin LIST endpoints (`/v1/admin/runtimes`, `/pools`, `/tenants`, `/credential-pools`) through the `pkg/ops/gateway.Client` `AdminGetter` seam and normalizes the results into the snapshot's resource-keyed structure. `cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go:1256` wires `gatewayreader.New(gwClient)` whenever a gateway client is configured, falling back to `emptyRunningState{}` (line 1256/1367) only when `--gateway-url` is unset; the shipped chart always sets `--gateway-url` (`charts/lenny/templates/ops-deployment.yaml:120,123`). No tier2-or-higher test drives the reader through `gateway.Client`'s real HTTP transport against a live or containerized gateway; `gatewayreader_test.go` exercises the reader against a hand-written `fakeAdmin` that implements `AdminGetter` directly, bypassing HTTP entirely.
- **Gap:** The production drift report is no longer permanently wired to an empty running state — every chart-deployed `lenny-ops` now collects the real running state via the gatewayreader collector — so the original "reports every desired field as removed" failure mode no longer applies to a standard deployment. The remaining risk is narrower: no test exercises the collector through `gateway.Client`'s actual HTTP transport against a real gateway, and no tier4/tier5 test drives the full operator journey (alice queries `GET /v1/admin/drift` after a manual pool edit and sees the actual drift), so a regression in the HTTP layer or in the four admin LIST endpoints' JSON shape would not be caught by any existing test. Target tiers: tier4 integration and tier5 e2e.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the compose stack with a real gateway and Postgres (`tests/testinfra` compose harness), and for tier5 the Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`). The `RunningStateReader` implementation itself (`pkg/ops/driftservice/gatewayreader`) is no longer a dependency; it exists and is unit-tested.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/drift_report_test.go` that starts `lenny-ops` with `--gateway-url` pointed at a real gateway plus Postgres, mutates a pool through the admin API, and asserts `GET /v1/admin/drift?scope=pools` reports exactly that field as drifted with the documented severity; add a tier5 `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/drift_test.go` driving the same flow on Kind.

### - [x] T-25.9.1 — §25.9 query endpoints have no component-or-higher test against a real Postgres audit store [High] — RESOLVED 1df42ad3998bb56e8381378118cec3b5aa27bf3f
- **Resolution:** Added tests/tier2_component/auditstore/admin_query_test.go, a tier-2 component test that wires the production admin router (admin.NewRouter(...).WithAuditLog(auditstore.New(pg.Router(t)))) to a real Postgres audit store and drives the §25.9 GET /v1/admin/audit-events, /{seq}, and /summary endpoints. It asserts the OCSF envelope (ocsfVersion, translatorVersion, per-item lenny_chain), the chainIntegrityReport verified tally, eventType and actorId+resourceType AND filters, cursor pagination that walks every row exactly once across pages, the 24h default time window excluding older rows, per-tenant RLS isolation, and the summary groupBy eventType/actorId counts against the actual Postgres rows.

### - [ ] T-25.9.2 — Scatter-gather and result caching are implemented in-memory rather than Redis, and the audit trail misreports cache/shard state [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Scatter-gather caching: platform-admin cross-tenant queries that use `AllAuditShards()` cache their results in Redis for 5 minutes ... Set `?fresh=true` to bypass the cache." and "When only some audit shards are reachable (partial-shard outage), the endpoint returns 207 `AUDIT_PARTIAL_RESULTS` with the canonical `degradation` envelope listing the missing shards." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:3713, 3720)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/audit_scatter_test.go` (TestListAuditEventsCrossTenantMergesShards_spec_25_9_3668, TestListAuditEventsCrossTenantCachesResults_spec_25_9_3709, TestListAuditEventsCrossTenantFreshBypassesCache_spec_25_9_3709, TestListAuditEventsCrossTenantCacheOptOut_spec_25_9_3709, TestListAuditEventsCrossTenantPartialShard_spec_25_9_partial, TestListAuditEventsCrossTenantTotalOutage_spec_25_9_503, TestMemScatterGatherCacheTTL) drives the platform-admin cross-tenant path with a `fakeScatterReader` and asserts the cache-hit, `?fresh=true`, opt-out, 207-partial, and 503-total-outage behaviors at the handler level. `tests/tier2_component/auditstore/scatter_gather_test.go` (TestScatterGatherRowsMergesAllTenants_spec_25_9_3668) exercises the underlying `auditstore.ScatterGatherRows` against a real multi-tenant Postgres. Production wiring (`cmd/lenny-gateway/auditpipeline.go:164`) constructs `admin.NewMemScatterGatherCache(nil)` — an in-memory cache, not Redis — and no test asserts the cache against a real Redis backend or across multiple gateway replicas. `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/audit_query.go:809` (`emitAuditQueryExecuted`) still hardcodes `cacheHit: false` and `shardsTouched: 1` in the `audit.query_executed` event regardless of whether the cross-tenant scatter path actually hit the cache or fanned out.
- **Gap:** The scatter-gather fan-out, the 5-minute result cache with `?fresh=true` bypass and opt-out, and the 207 `AUDIT_PARTIAL_RESULTS` degradation envelope are now built and tested at component/handler level (F-25.9.11) — the original "single-shard, no cache, unimplemented" premise no longer holds. Two narrower gaps remain: (1) the spec mandates a Redis-backed cache so results are consistent across `lenny-ops`/gateway replicas, but production uses an in-memory `MemScatterGatherCache` with no test pinning the documented Redis behavior or flagging the divergence, so a multi-replica deployment silently gets per-replica cache incoherence; (2) the `audit.query_executed` event's `cacheHit`/`shardsTouched` fields are hardcoded false/1 even on the cross-tenant scatter path, so an operator auditing query costs from the audit trail sees values that do not reflect the real cache hit or shard fan-out. Target tiers: tier2 component (Redis-backed cache implementation and test) plus a handler-level fix and test for the audit event fields.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a Redis-backed `ScatterGatherCache` implementation (the interface exists; only `MemScatterGatherCache` is wired) and a Redis container (`tests/testinfra/containers`). The audit-event field fix requires no new infrastructure; buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add a Redis-backed `ScatterGatherCache` implementation and `tests/tier2_component/auditstore/scatter_redis_cache_test.go` asserting a platform-admin cross-tenant query's cached result is visible to a second `admin.Router` instance sharing the same Redis (simulating a second replica); fix `emitAuditQueryExecuted` to thread the real cache-hit/shard count through from the scatter path and extend `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/audit_scatter_test.go` to assert the emitted `audit.query_executed` event carries the accurate `cacheHit`/`shardsTouched` values.

### - [ ] T-25.9.3 — Degraded-mode deferred-write reconciliation producing chainIntegrity rechained_post_outage has no integration test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Deferred writes are applied to `audit_log` during reconciliation in original-timestamp order. The chain hash is re-computed for the affected range, which intentionally breaks `chainIntegrity: verified` for those events to `chainIntegrity: rechained_post_outage` so operators can distinguish tamper-broken chains from legitimately-rechained ones." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:3697)
- **Existing tests:** `migrations/audit_log_deferred_writes_test.go` asserts the `audit_log_deferred_writes` DDL only (now migration `0125_audit_log_deferred_writes`). `pkg/audit/chain_test.go` covers the `gap_suspected` classification (including the newly added `nextval_rollback`-vs-outage distinction, TestVerifyRowsNextvalRollbackGapIsAdvisoryNotAlarming) and the `redacted_gdpr` classification (TestVerifyRowsLawfulRedaction) at unit level. No test found that writes deferred rows, runs the reconciliation, and asserts the affected range is classified `rechained_post_outage` while a tamper-broken row remains `broken`; `grep -rl audit_log_deferred_writes` outside tests turns up only a comment in `pkg/audit/audit.go` describing the reconciliation as future work — the reconciliation driver itself does not exist in code yet. Searched tier4 (`tests/tier4_integration`), tier8 (`tests/tier8_chaos/audit_chain_test.go` covers gap detection only), and `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin`.
- **Gap:** The reconciliation that rehashes deferred writes and the resulting `rechained_post_outage` classification is the operator-facing signal that distinguishes a legitimate post-outage rechain from tampering. Neither the reconciliation driver nor a test for it exist above the unit tier, and the `lenny_audit_chain_rechained_post_outage_total` counter is never asserted to fire from a real reconciliation. The work is a failure-recovery scenario (Postgres outage then reconciliation). Target tiers: tier4 integration and tier8 chaos.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a real Postgres (`tests/testinfra/containers`), the `lenny-ops` deferred-write reconciliation path (not yet built — building it is part of this finding), and a way to seed `audit_log_deferred_writes` rows with original timestamps.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/audit_deferred_reconcile_test.go` that seeds deferred writes, runs reconciliation, and asserts the rehashed range is `rechained_post_outage` via `GET /v1/admin/audit-events` while a separately tampered row is `broken`, and that the rechained counter incremented.
- **Needs human input (as of 2026-07-12):** Building the §25.9 deferred-write post-outage reconciliation driver is a new lenny-ops subsystem (an outage-time deferred-write writer, a reconciler that applies audit_log_deferred_writes into per-tenant audit_log chains in original-timestamp order and re-hashes the affected range, per-row rechained_post_outage persistence surfaced by GET /v1/admin/audit-events, and the counter wiring), which the spec-map explicitly defers to phase 14 / lenny-ops. The spec pins the observable contract but not the mechanism, and several mechanics are under-specified: (a) how the platform-scoped audit_log_deferred_writes table (no tenant column) maps onto the per-tenant audit_log hash chains; (b) how "the affected range" is re-hashed when later rows are already committed above the insertion point (does reconciliation rewrite subsequent rows' prev_hash, and how are sequence numbers assigned for out-of-order inserts?); (c) how the rechained_post_outage state is persisted so the query API's per-row verifier reports it (classifyRow currently cannot). Should this driver be built here as part of test-gap closure, or should it go through the change-proposal/implement-proposal pipeline first to resolve (a)-(c), leaving this finding open with the skipped spec-faithful test committed? If it is to be built here, an approved answer to (a)-(c) is a prerequisite.

### - [ ] T-25.10.2 — Drift reconcile against the real gateway admin API has no integration or e2e test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`POST /v1/admin/drift/reconcile` calls admin API `PUT` endpoints via `GatewayClient` to apply the desired state. Each call goes through full RBAC, validation, and audit on the gateway side." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:3846)
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/ops/opsserver/drift_reconcile_test.go` (TestDriftReconcileConfirm_spec_25_10, TestDriftReconcilePartial207_spec_25_10, TestDriftReconcileDryRun_spec_25_10, TestDriftReconcileNoApplier503_spec_25_10) drives reconcile with an in-memory `labelApplier`. The `pkg/ops/driftservice.ResourceApplier` interface (`pkg/ops/driftservice/reconcile.go`) is now defined with a documented `DRIFT_RECONCILE_UNAVAILABLE` fail-closed path when no applier is configured, but `cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go` never calls `Service.SetApplier` with a `GatewayClient`-backed implementation, so a confirmed reconcile in every real deployment still fails closed rather than applying. No test routes reconcile through a real `GatewayClient` to real gateway admin `PUT` endpoints. Searched tier4 (`tests/tier4_integration`), tier5 (`tests/tier5_e2e_kind`), and tier6 (`tests/tier6_e2e_cloud`).
- **Gap:** Reconcile is specified to apply desired state through the gateway admin API under RBAC, validation, and audit, but no `ResourceApplier` implementation is wired in production, so a `confirm: true` reconcile always returns `DRIFT_RECONCILE_UNAVAILABLE` today; the RBAC, validation, and audit interaction on the gateway side is entirely unverified, as is the `operation_progressed` event firing per resource and the Operations Inventory `drift_reconciliation` entry. This is a real operator journey (carol reconciles a drifted pool) plus a partial-failure path (HTTP 207). Target tiers: tier4 integration and tier5 e2e.
- **Dependencies:** Requires building and wiring a `GatewayClient`-backed `ResourceApplier` in the binary (the interface exists; no implementation is wired — related to T-25.10.1's gatewayreader precedent), the compose stack with a real gateway and Postgres, and for tier5 the Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`).
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/drift_reconcile_test.go` that seeds a drifted pool, calls `POST /v1/admin/drift/reconcile` with `confirm:true`, asserts the pool converges via the gateway admin API, and asserts a `drift.resource_reconciled` audit event and an `operation_progressed` event per resource.
- **Needs human input (as of 2026-07-12):** This finding requires building a GatewayClient-backed ResourceApplier (a production component) and wiring it into cmd/lenny-ops, which is beyond a test-gap fix. Should this go through the change-proposal / implement-proposal pipeline? Two design decisions the spec (§25.10 Reconciliation) leaves open must be settled before an applier can be written and a tier4 test can assert against it: (1) how the applier acquires the required If-Match ETag for each admin PUT at reconcile time (GET-then-PUT per resource? the ops gateway client's PutJSON does not currently set If-Match at all); and (2) how the gatewayreader-normalized desired-state subtree maps onto each resource type's full-replace PUT request body. The spec says "calls admin API PUT endpoints via GatewayClient to apply the desired state" but does not specify either mechanism.

### - [x] T-25.9.4 — Declared tier4 lenny_ops_endpoints suite for audit query and drift detection is absent [High] — RESOLVED 4b3184748a0a25a2f01a43e92758a70d34bf8c96
- **Resolution:** Added tests/tier4_integration/ops_endpoints_test.go, the declared TESTING.md §12.4 lenny_ops_endpoints suite. TestOpsDriftEndpointsAgainstPostgresE2E drives the §25.10 drift surface against the real cmd/lenny-ops binary and a live Postgres: POST /v1/admin/drift/snapshot/refresh (verified persisted to bootstrap_seed_snapshot), POST /v1/admin/drift/validate (match and diverged verdicts), and GET /v1/admin/drift (desiredStateSource resolved from the stored snapshot). TestGatewayAuditQueryEndpointsE2E drives the §25.9 audit query surface against the real cmd/lenny-gateway binary: GET /v1/admin/audit-events (OCSF envelope with ocsfVersion 1.1.0 and chainIntegrityReport) and GET /v1/admin/audit-events/summary (grouped aggregate counts in descending order, plus the unsupported-groupBy 400 boundary). Both pass against current product code; registered in tests/spec-map.json under §25.9 and §25.10.

### - [ ] T-25.9.5 — §25.9 OCSF query envelope has no conformance test pinning records against the external OCSF v1.1.0 schema [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "All endpoints in this subsection return audit records as [OCSF v1.1.0](https://schema.ocsf.io/1.1.0/) JSON objects per the Wire Format in §11.7. The `items[]` array in paginated responses is an array of OCSF records." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:3657)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier3_contract/ocsf_audit/admin_audit_envelope_test.go` asserts a fixed set of structural keys (`class_uid`, `category_uid`, `metadata`, `unmapped`, etc.) and `metadata.version`, but it checks key presence rather than validating each record against the published OCSF v1.1.0 JSON Schema. `pkg/audit/ocsf/ocsf_test.go` covers the translator at unit level.
- **Gap:** §25.9 binds the query envelope to an external standard (OCSF v1.1.0). The contract test verifies a hand-picked key list, not conformance against the OCSF schema, so a record that satisfies the key list but violates an OCSF type, enum, or required-field constraint would pass. A standards-conformance test pinning the records against the OCSF v1.1.0 schema is required. Target tier: tier3 contract (and tier10 conformance for the fidelity matrix).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the OCSF v1.1.0 schema fixtures vendored into the repository and a JSON-Schema validator helper. The schema fixtures are not present; vendoring them is part of this finding.

### - [ ] T-25.10.3 — Drift cross-tenant isolation is named in the §12.9.1 matrix but unexercised [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "for each store and each operation, attempt cross-tenant reads and writes through every code path (REST, MCP, OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, admin API, MCP management server, audit query, drift detection, lenny-ops endpoints). Every attempt must fail with the documented isolation error." (TESTING.md:1242)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier9_security/tenant_isolation_test.go` (TestTenantIsolationCrossStore) covers the audit-events list and verify endpoints cross-tenant, and `tests/tier9_security/rbac_test.go` covers RBAC, but neither exercises the §25.10 drift endpoints. A `grep` for `drift` in `tenant_isolation_test.go` returns zero matches.

### - [ ] T-25.9.12 — All lenny-ops audit events store the operation id as camelCase operationId, so the §25.9 ?operationId= query (snake operation_id) never returns any lenny-ops audit row [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** §25.9 defines the audit query API's `?operationId=` correlation filter, which the gateway resolves against the audit payload's `operation_id` field to return the audit rows for an operation across subsystems (spec/25_agent-operability.md).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/audit_query_test.go` covers the §25.9 query filters, but no test asserts that a lenny-ops-emitted audit row (backup, upgrade, drift, doctor, diagnostics) is retrievable by `?operationId=`.
- **Gap:** The gateway §25.9 audit query filters on `payload.operation_id` (snake): `pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/audit_query_filter.go:172` `stringFrom(payload, "operation_id")`. But every lenny-ops audit emitter writes camelCase `operationId`: `pkg/ops/backup/audit.go:121`, `cmd/lenny-ops/deps.go:1005` (diagnostics), `:1343` (drift), `:1711` (upgrade), `pkg/ops/doctor/doctor.go:356/379/464/483/494`, `pkg/ops/driftservice/reconcile.go:209/237/264`, `pkg/ops/opsserver/opsaudit.go:35` (me/inventory). Gateway admin rows correctly use snake `operation_id` (`audit_sink.go:133`). Post-incident `?operationId=` correlation across backup/restore, upgrade, drift-reconcile, doctor-fix, and diagnostics audit trails therefore silently returns nothing. This is a product defect (a key-casing mismatch between emitter and query), not only a test gap, and it is broader than the §25.17 lock case tracked by T-25.17.1. Discovered while closing T-25.17.1. Target tiers are tier4 integration through the audit query API and tier1 for the emitter key casing.
- **Dependencies:** Requires aligning the lenny-ops emitters' payload key (`operationId` to `operation_id`) with the gateway query filter before the correlation query can be verified.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier4 integration case that drives a lenny-ops operation (for example a backup or upgrade), captures its operation id, then queries `GET /v1/admin/audit-events?operationId=<id>` and asserts the emitted audit rows are returned; add a tier1 case pinning each lenny-ops emitter's payload key to `operation_id`.
- **Needs human input (as of 2026-07-13):** Should the canonical lenny-ops AUDIT-PAYLOAD correlation key be normalized to snake_case operation_id across all lenny-ops audit emitters (backup/restore, upgrade, drift, doctor, diagnostics, me/inventory — ~8 emission sites plus the tests that assert the camelCase form), matching the gateway admin sink and the §25.9 filter — OR should the §25.9 query filter instead be taught to accept both operation_id and operationId? The fix must not touch the client-facing camelCase operationId wire fields (the ?operationId= query param, the operations-inventory response, and the MCP tool input schema), which are spec-correct per §25.6/§25.7; only the internal audit-payload emission key is the defect. This is the same cross-service convention decision escalated under T-25.17.1(b), now scoped to the full emitter set rather than the §25.17 lock case alone.

## §25.11 Backup and Restore API <a id="t-25.11"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/25_agent-operability.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The spec text this unit covers barely moved since the 2026-06-03 audit: the only edits are proposal 0021's SEC-BACKUP-2 reconciliation of the `ops_backups`/`Backup.Status` enum (adding `pending`, `verifying`, `verification_failed`, `expired` to the documented enum to match the code) and the accompanying note that `POST /v1/admin/backups/{id}/verify` persists `status: "verifying"` before the Job runs; both are now pinned by a new tier-11 doc-consistency test (`tests/tier11_docs/backup_status_enum_test.go`) and a component assertion in `pkg/ops/backup/orchestrator_test.go`, so neither is a gap. Everything else in this section shifted by exactly four lines from unrelated edits earlier in the file; those references are corrected below with no change to the finding text. Two findings materially improved from other, non-proposal work that landed the day after the audit (`F-17.3.6`, BUILD-GAPS): the `lenny-backup` binary's encryption, SHA-256 checksum, and column-redaction pipeline are now exercised end to end at the component tier with a fake `pg_dump` binary (`pkg/ops/backup/runner/redact_exec_test.go`, `exec_test.go`), and the test-restore sampled-HEAD logic, its 99% floor (including the at-floor boundary), and its gauge/counter emission are now fully unit- and component-tested (`pkg/ops/backup/runner/restoretest_test.go`, `cmd/lenny-ops/restore_test_metrics_test.go`). T-25.11.2 is downgraded from High to Medium and rewritten to name the narrower remaining gap (the real `MinIOUploader`/`MinIODownloader` network wrappers and a full binary run against real Postgres and MinIO are still untested); T-25.11.10 is downgraded from Medium to Low and rewritten to note that only the tier5 CronJob-on-Kind dispatch layer remains unexercised, which is already the subject of T-25.11.1's broader gap. No finding in this section is resolved outright, and no new gap was introduced by the drift: the SEC-BACKUP-1 config/CRD exporter work (`pkg/ops/backup/runner/export.go`, `export_test.go`) that also landed under proposal 0021 already carries thorough fake-clientset and fake-Postgres coverage and closes no open finding by itself. The remaining eleven findings (tier3 contract, tier4 integration, tier5 Kind round trip, tier6 cloud replication residency, tier8 chaos degradation, tier9 isolation, the unimplemented `WORKSPACE_SNAPSHOT_MISSING` error path, the spec-map inaccuracy, the OCSF per-event pinning gap, the lock-steal journey, and the leader-election/retention-cron HA path) are all unchanged on disk and remain open exactly as audited.
Counts: 4 High, 7 Medium, 3 Low, 2 Info.

### Findings

### - [x] T-25.11.1 — Backup and restore round trip against real Postgres and MinIO is deferred; tier5 Kind test only renders templates [High] — RESOLVED 6fce1921a3e2cf7ccdcfc263c9a637f65142871e
- **Resolution:** Added tier-4 integration test TestBackupRestoreRoundTrip (tests/tier4_integration/backup_restore_test.go) that drives the production lenny-backup runner surfaces end to end against a real Postgres 15 container and a real MinIO container: it seeds a row, runs a full backup (ExecDumper pg_dump per shard, TarGzArchiver client-side AES-256-GCM, MinIOUploader SSE-S3 upload), downloads and decrypts the archive (TarGzOpener), restores it with pg_restore into a fresh scratch database (ExecScratchRestorer), and asserts the seeded row reappears; it also asserts the recorded checksum matches the uploaded bytes and that a wrong data key fails to open the archive. The test passed against unmodified product code on the first run. The MinIO test-container helper gained an Env option so the built-in KMS can be enabled for SSE-S3.

### - [ ] T-25.11.2 — `lenny-backup` data path now has solid component coverage (encryption, redaction, checksum, test-restore); MinIO upload/download and a full binary run remain untested [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Encrypts the archive client-side with AES-256-GCM using a data key wrapped by the KMS key", "Computes SHA-256 checksum of the encrypted archive", "Uploads to MinIO at `backups/{type}/{id}/{timestamp}.tar.gz.enc`", and the redaction filter "`pg_dump` output is piped through a sed filter that replaces matched columns with `'[REDACTED]'`" (spec/25_agent-operability.md:4005-4007, 4020). Test-restore "actually restores the backup to a temporary namespace ... runs smoke tests" (spec/25_agent-operability.md:4260).
- **Existing tests:** This is now substantially more covered than at the 2026-06-03 audit. `pkg/ops/backup/runner/exec_test.go` (`TestTarGzArchiverWithKeyEncrypts`, `TestDecryptAESGCMRejectsWrongKey`, `TestHashReader`) exercises the real AES-256-GCM archive encryption and SHA-256 checksum against the real `ExecDumper`. `pkg/ops/backup/runner/redact_exec_test.go` and `redact_internal_test.go` (`TestDumpPostgresRedactsPlainFormat_spec_25_11_4012`, `TestArchiveManifestRecordsRedactedColumns_spec_25_11_4012`, plus the `COPY`-stream parsing cases) drive the real `pg_dump`-output redaction sed-equivalent against a fake `pg_dump` script, landed post-audit (`148cb77d`, F-25.11.12). `pkg/ops/backup/runner/restoretest_test.go` (added `e3aa5ee4`, F-17.3.6) covers the test-restore smoke path end to end over fakes. `cmd/lenny-backup/main_test.go` still covers only flag parsing for the binary entry point itself. No test exercises `pkg/ops/backup/runner/minio.go` (`MinIOUploader.Upload`) or `miniodownload.go` (`MinIODownloader.Download`) — the real network-facing MinIO client wrappers — against a real or containerized MinIO, and no test runs the `lenny-backup` binary end to end against a real Postgres and MinIO target. Searched cmd/lenny-backup, pkg/ops/backup/runner.
- **Gap:** The data-correctness logic (encryption, checksum, redaction, and the test-restore smoke path) is now exercised at the component tier with fakes standing in for `pg_dump` and the object store, closing the original finding's core concern that a regression here would ship undetected. What remains untested is the thin but real network-facing layer: whether `MinIOUploader.Upload`/`MinIODownloader.Download` correctly round-trip against an actual MinIO endpoint, and whether the full `lenny-backup` binary — wiring the real `ExecDumper`, `MinIOUploader`, and Postgres client together — produces a correct archive end to end. Target tier2 (the binary against a real Postgres and a MinIO container) and tier4 (the full Job).
- **Dependencies:** Requires a real Postgres with a seeded schema and an S3-compatible target (MinIO container or the tests/testinfra/stubs equivalent). Buildable today using `pkg/embedded/postgres` and a MinIO test container.
- **Suggested test:** Add `pkg/ops/backup/runner/minio_test.go` that runs `MinIOUploader.Upload` and `MinIODownloader.Download` against a MinIO test container and asserts a byte-exact round trip and correct SSE settings, and add `cmd/lenny-backup/run_test.go` (or `tests/tier4_integration/backup_pipeline_test.go`) that runs the binary in `--mode=full` against an embedded Postgres with a `secrets`-shaped table and a `redactColumns` entry, downloads the uploaded object from the same MinIO container, and asserts the SHA-256 matches the recorded checksum, the ciphertext decrypts with the data key, and the redacted columns are absent from the archive.

### - [x] T-25.11.3 — Backup and restore admin endpoints have no tier3 wire-format contract test [High] — RESOLVED 394ddbb1d49ddbfc42052c908edbd7acfbc37da4
- **Resolution:** Added tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/backup_test.go, a tier3 contract suite over the in-memory BackupService that pins the §25.11 public wire format: the Backup field set (create and detail), the RestorePreview field set including artifactReplicationLagSeconds/estimatedOrphanArtifactRows, the safety-check body with its nested dataLossEstimate and compatibility objects, the RestoreState field set (after executing a restore against a safe backup), and the §25.2 canonical error envelope carrying the canonical BACKUP_NOT_FOUND / RESTORE_NOT_FOUND codes (404, PERMANENT, retryable:false) on the documented not-found failures. All seven tests pass against unmodified product code. A field rename in any pinned response would now fail the suite.

### - [x] T-25.11.4 — Degradation failure paths (Postgres down, MinIO down, K8s API down, Jobs continue independently) have no tier8 chaos coverage [High] — RESOLVED c16e8a664c112a9ca98bf84c8c6829e182ff44cf
- **Resolution:** Added tier-4 integration tests (tests/tier4_integration/backup_degradation_test.go) that drive the production backup.Service, pgstore, k8slauncher, and lenny-backup runner against real Postgres and MinIO containers stopped mid-test: Postgres down yields BACKUP_STORAGE_UNREACHABLE (503) on create/list/schedule, an unreachable Kubernetes API yields BACKUP_JOB_CREATION_FAILED (503), and MinIO down fails the runner's upload and records the failed status. This replaces the previous fakes-only tier-2 coverage of the §25.11 dependency-down 503 paths with assertions against genuinely unavailable dependencies. New Stop() helpers on the Postgres and MinIO container fixtures inject the outage (the testcontainers analogue of the tier-8 scale-to-zero injection).

### - [ ] T-25.11.5 — Backup-Job isolation (SELECT-only Postgres role, scoped MinIO key, restricted ServiceAccount, egress NetworkPolicy) is not verified at runtime in tier9 [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** The Job pod has "a dedicated `lenny-backup` Postgres role with `SELECT` on shard tables and no write access", "a dedicated `lenny-backup` access key with `s3:PutObject`, `s3:GetObject` ... and `s3:DeleteObject` ... on the backup bucket only", "a dedicated ServiceAccount `lenny-backup-sa` with `get`/`list` on CRDs ... No Pod, Deployment, or Secret read access", and "NetworkPolicy: egress permitted to Postgres Service, MinIO Service, and K8s API only" (spec/25_agent-operability.md:3994-3998).
- **Existing tests:** `charts/lenny/tests/backup-job_test.yaml` and `ops-network-policies_test.yaml` render the ServiceAccount, the security context, and the `lenny-backup-job` NetworkPolicy (no ingress, storage egress). These are chart-render assertions. `pkg/ops/backup/k8slauncher/k8slauncher_test.go` asserts the rendered pod spec carries the security context and the label the NetworkPolicy selects. No tier9 test verifies the controls are enforced at runtime: that the backup role cannot write, that the access key cannot reach a non-backup bucket, that the ServiceAccount cannot read Secrets, or that egress to a non-allowlisted endpoint is dropped. Searched tests/tier9_security (rbac_test.go and network_policy_test.go contain no backup reference).
- **Gap:** The backup Job runs with credentials and network reach that, if mis-scoped, would let a compromised backup image exfiltrate secrets or write to arbitrary buckets. The rendered-manifest tests prove the chart asks for the right scope; they do not prove the cluster enforces it. This is a security control that is unverified end to end. Target tier9 (security).
- **Dependencies:** Requires a Kind cluster with the backup RBAC, the MinIO bucket policy, and the NetworkPolicy applied, plus an attacker pod or a forced backup-pod exec to attempt the denied operations (tests/testinfra/kind, tests/testinfra/security). Buildable on the existing tier9 Kind harness.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier9_security/backup_isolation_test.go` that, using the `lenny-backup-sa` token and the `lenny-backup` MinIO key, asserts an INSERT against a shard table is denied, a PutObject to a non-backup bucket is denied, a Secret GET in `lenny-system` is denied, and an egress connection to an out-of-policy host times out under the rendered NetworkPolicy.

### - [ ] T-25.11.8 — Runtime residency-preflight periodic tick (drift detection between batches) is never exercised live [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "the preflight runs before every replication batch ... and, independently, on a periodic tick every `minio.artifactBackup.residencyCheckIntervalSeconds` (default 300s / 5 min) so that long idle gaps between batches cannot hide a silent redirection." and the controller "suspends replication for the affected source region" when a destination tag drifts after load time (spec/25_agent-operability.md:4066-4068, 4077).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/blobstore/replication/replication_test.go` verifies `Preflight` and `Resume` once; `cmd/lenny-gateway/replication_wiring_test.go::TestRunReplicationControllerStops` and `TestRunReplicationControllerMeasuresLag` cancel the loop before the first tick, so the periodic re-check is never observed firing on a tag that drifts after startup. The new `TestReplicationControllerEndToEnd` (added since the audit) exercises `Configure`/`Preflight` called directly with a fixed mismatching-then-fixed tag, not the controller's own periodic-tick loop, so it does not close this gap. No test changes the destination tag while the loop is running and asserts the next tick suspends the region. Searched pkg/blobstore/replication and cmd/lenny-gateway.
- **Gap:** The tick that catches a post-load DNS rebinding or tag drift, the distinguishing value of the runtime preflight over the startup check, is not exercised. A regression that runs the preflight only before batches (and never on the idle tick) would pass every current test. This is the adversarial drift scenario. Target tier2 (controller with a clock-stepped loop) and tier8 (live tag drift).
- **Dependencies:** Requires a clock-injectable controller loop (tests/testinfra/clockstep or tests/testinfra/timectl) and a FakeDriver whose jurisdiction tag is mutated between ticks. Buildable today against the FakeDriver.
- **Suggested test:** Add `cmd/lenny-gateway/replication_tick_test.go` that starts `runReplicationController` with a stepped clock, lets the startup preflight pass, mutates the FakeDriver tag to a mismatching jurisdiction, advances the clock past `residencyCheckIntervalSeconds`, and asserts the region transitions to `suspended_residency_violation` and emits `DataResidencyViolationAttempt` without any batch submission.

The steal-and-resume handoff is a real day-2 scenario (alice's restore stalls, bob steals the lock and resumes) and would benefit from a tier4 integration test against the real lock store, though the core semantics are unit-covered. Target tier4 (integration).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the real remediation-lock store (§25.4) and two operator identities against the compose stack (tests/testinfra/gateway). Buildable once a tier4 backup harness exists (see T-25.11.6).

### - [ ] T-25.11.15 — The lenny-backup container image lacks pg_dump/pg_restore/psql, so the §25.11 backup/restore Job cannot run as built [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** The §25.11 backup/restore Job dumps each shard with `pg_dump`, uploads the encrypted archive, and restores it with `pg_restore`/`psql` (spec/25_agent-operability.md, backup and restore procedure).
- **Existing tests:** The tier-5 Kind test honest-skips the round trip and TESTING.md:1761 defers it; the component-tier data-path tests substitute a fake `pg_dump` binary (see T-25.11.2), so no test runs the packaged image.
- **Gap:** The `lenny-backup` image is built from the generic `./Dockerfile` whose runtime stage is `FROM gcr.io/distroless/static:nonroot` (`Dockerfile:23`) with no shell and no Postgres client tools, and `tests/testinfra/kind/install.sh:192` builds it with `docker build --build-arg BINARY=lenny-backup`. But `pkg/ops/backup/runner/exec.go:70-73` (`ExecDumper.DumpPostgres`) defaults to shelling out to `pg_dump` on PATH, and `pkg/ops/backup/runner/restoreexec.go` (`ExecScratchRestorer`/`ExecDumpInspector`) shell out to `pg_restore` and `psql`. A backup Job run from the built image would fail with `pg_dump: executable file not found in $PATH`. This is why the tier-5 test honest-skips the round trip. The feature is non-functional in the packaged image: a packaging defect that the tier-5 skip masks.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a `lenny-backup` image whose runtime stage includes the Postgres client tools (`pg_dump`, `pg_restore`, `psql`), which is a build and packaging change; the round-trip test then becomes runnable on Kind.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier5 (or image-smoke) test that runs the built `lenny-backup` image and asserts `pg_dump`, `pg_restore`, and `psql` are on PATH and that a full backup-then-restore round trip completes on the real cluster, replacing the current honest-skip.
- **Needs human input (as of 2026-07-13):** The lenny-backup image must ship pg_dump/pg_restore/psql for the §25.11 backup and restore Jobs to run, but the fix is a production packaging/supply-chain decision the spec does not settle. Decide: (1) which runtime base image the lenny-backup image should use (a dedicated non-distroless Dockerfile, e.g. alpine + postgresql-client like cmd/runtimes/cred-shell-echo/Dockerfile, vs debian-slim, vs the official postgres image) given the Dockerfile's stated §13.1 distroless/non-root/read-only-rootfs posture that a Postgres-client base weakens; (2) which Postgres client major version to pin, since pg_dump refuses a server newer than the client and the spec pins no server version (test infra uses PG16); and (3) whether to introduce a per-image Dockerfile override and wire it through all four build paths (tests/testinfra/kind/install.sh build_image, .github/workflows/release.yml `file:`, scripts/cloud/aws/build-images.sh `--file`, Makefile). Because this changes the production release image and touches the release CI, it should likely go through the change-proposal pipeline rather than be decided in a test-gap batch. The spec-faithful tier5 assertion (TestBackupImageProvidesPostgresClientTools) is committed in a held/skipped state to un-skip once the packaging is fixed.

### - [ ] T-25.11.16 — GET /v1/admin/restore/{id}/status omits the §25.11-mandated canonical progress envelope [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "the restore-status response includes the canonical `progress` envelope (totalSteps = shard count + 1, currentStep, etaSeconds via linear_extrapolation + historical_p50)" (spec/25_agent-operability.md:4198).
- **Existing tests:** T-25.11.3's tier3 `tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/backup_test.go` pins the `RestoreState` field set after executing a restore, but it does not assert any `progress` envelope on the restore-status response.
- **Gap:** The wire type `RestoreState` (`pkg/ops/backup/service.go:351-384`) has no progress field, and `handleRestoreStatus` (`pkg/ops/opsserver/backup.go:373-384`) serializes the `RestoreState` row directly with no progress object. `conventions.Progress` (`pkg/ops/conventions/conventions.go:272`) exists and is used elsewhere (for example `platform_upgrade.go:298`) but not on this endpoint. Implementing `etaSeconds` (linear_extrapolation over completed shards plus historical_p50 for the gateway-restart phase) is a substantive feature beyond a wire-format pin. This is a missing wire field plus the ETA computation behind it.
- **Dependencies:** Requires adding the progress envelope and the `etaSeconds` computation to the restore-status handler (a product change), then a contract test. The implementation gap is a prerequisite this finding records.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier3 contract case asserting `GET /v1/admin/restore/{id}/status` returns a canonical `progress` envelope with `totalSteps` = shard count + 1, a `currentStep`, and an `etaSeconds` derived from linear_extrapolation over completed shards plus the historical p50 for the gateway-restart phase.

## §25.12 MCP Management Server <a id="t-25.12"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/25_agent-operability.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The §25.12 management MCP server has unit coverage (`pkg/ops/mcp/server_test.go`), an in-process component test (`pkg/ops/opsserver/mcp_test.go`), and a `//go:build contract` tier3 suite (`tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/mcp_test.go`) that all drive an httptest handler over an in-memory backing. Proposal 0021 (F-MCP-1/F-COV-3, landed 2026-07-01) built the build-time `openapi-to-mcp` generator and a Tier-0-equivalent drift guard (`pkg/ops/mcp/generated_tools_drift_test.go`), replacing the hand-authored `buildToolset()` literal with a generated inventory (`pkg/ops/mcp/generated_tools.go`) derived from the now-complete gateway OpenAPI document, which resolves T-25.12.1. The inventory now spans the full admin-API surface (~164 platform-management tools alongside the 58 lenny-ops operability tools), but the tool names for the admin-API half follow an `admin.{action}_{noun}` convention rather than the spec's stated `lenny_{domain}_{action}` pattern, an untested divergence captured in the new T-25.12.16. No test drives `/mcp/management` over the compose stack (tier4), over Kind or cloud (tier5/tier6), through the security controls end to end (tier9), or against an external MCP/JSON-RPC schema (tier3 wire conformance or tier10). The gateway-proxy routing path (T-25.12.3) remains unbuilt, so while the platform-management tools now exist in the registry, invoking one against a gateway-owned endpoint still has no dispatch path; the two security-model CI sweeps (no-role and scope-restricted, iterated over every tool) and the SSE-via-MCP `notifications/subscribe` method also remain unimplemented and untested. spec-map.json and spec-map-exceptions.yaml both still record stale metadata that masks the gap. Counts: 7 High, 7 Medium, 4 Low, 2 Info.

### Findings

### - [x] T-25.12.1 — No build-time OpenAPI-to-MCP generation and no Tier-0 divergence guard despite an explicit claim [High] — RESOLVED 06675d38 (reconciled against proposal 0021)
- **Resolution:** Proposal 0021 (F-MCP-1, decided 2026-06-30, applied to spec 2026-07-01) built the `cmd/openapi-to-mcp` build-time generator (`pkg/ops/mcp/mcptoolgen`) that derives the `/mcp/management` tool inventory directly from the served `openapi.json`, and replaced the hand-authored `buildToolset()` literal in `pkg/ops/mcp/tools.go` with the generated `generated_tools.go` (`generatedToolset()`, 2696 lines, 222 tools). Commit `06675d38` ("0021 S9: build the openapi-to-mcp generator and derive the /mcp/management inventory (F-MCP-1)") landed the generator and `pkg/ops/mcp/generated_tools_drift_test.go::TestGeneratedToolsMatchOpenAPI_spec_25_12`, which re-runs `mcptoolgen.Generate` over the live document and fails the build if the committed `generated_tools.go` is not byte-identical to a fresh regeneration — the Tier-0-class divergence guard the spec and TESTING.md:2085 require. A same-day follow-up, `53232353` ("0021 S9 fix: emit an MCP tool per admin-API endpoint..."), corrected the generator to emit one tool per documented endpoint rather than the operability subset; `TestGeneratedInventoryCoversEveryDocumentedEndpoint_spec_25_12` now pins that every non-null `x-lenny-mcp-tool` in the served document has a corresponding registry tool and vice versa (an exact-set equality check), closing the reconciliation gap this finding named. The F-COV-3 companion lift merged the 63 previously gateway-absent `lenny-ops` route schemas into the single served OpenAPI document so the generator covers the "entire operability surface" claim. The residual naming-convention divergence this finding also flagged (`admin.create_tenant` vs. the spec's stated `lenny_{domain}_{action}` pattern) is untested and is spun off as T-25.12.16 rather than left folded into this now-resolved generation/drift-guard finding.

Since the T-25.12.1 generator landed, `pkg/ops/mcp/registry.go::NewRegistry()` now derives from `generatedToolset()`, which does include the platform-management tools (`admin.create_tenant`, `admin.create_pool`, `admin.create_connector`, `admin.list_circuit_breakers`, and ~160 more, pinned by `generated_tools_drift_test.go::TestGeneratedInventoryCoversEveryDocumentedEndpoint_spec_25_12`). This is a missing user journey (an MCP-first platform-admin provisioning a tenant or scaling a pool) and a core-capability coverage gap at tier3/tier4, still blocked on the gateway-proxy routing (T-25.12.3).

Once T-25.12.3's routing exists, also add a `pkg/ops/mcp` unit test asserting `FilterForList({Scope: "admin"})` returns the platform-management tools rather than the current hard-coded empty result.

This is itself the separate open High finding T-25.12.3, and it rests on an undesigned decision: how should the invoker decide, per generated tool, whether tools/call dispatches to the local lenny-ops mux or proxies to the gateway? The spec names the split ("gateway-owned endpoints (all platform management plus health and recommendations)" vs "ops-owned endpoints") but supplies no mechanical marker — the generated mcp.Tool carries only method/path, the served OpenAPI has no x-lenny-owner extension, and §25.12 is still a deferred/Wave-4 (Phase 13) exception in spec-map-exceptions.yaml. Questions for a human: (1) Should T-25.12.2 be built together with T-25.12.3 (they are inseparable — the dispatch path is the feature)? (2) What is the sanctioned routing predicate — a new x-lenny-owner OpenAPI extension plus generator change, a tool-name-prefix heuristic (admin.* -> gateway, lenny_* -> ops), or a static path routing table? (3) Does this belong in the change-proposal/build pipeline given the Wave-4 deferral, rather than the test-gaps track?

### - [ ] T-25.12.3 — Gateway-proxied tool routing through GatewayClient is unimplemented and untested [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Tool invocations are routed transparently to either: ... `lenny-ops` handlers ... Gateway admin API via `GatewayClient` — for gateway-owned endpoints (all platform management plus health and recommendations). The routing is invisible to the MCP client — all tools appear in a single tool inventory." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:4368)
- **Existing tests:** no test found. `pkg/ops/opsserver/mcp.go` implements `opsInvoker`, which still replays the tool's request against the local ops mux only (its own doc comment at `mcp.go:15-21` states plainly: "the v1 management server exposes the ops-owned operability tools" and names `GatewayClient` only as the architecture's stated dual-routing target, not as something wired in). There is no `GatewayClient` field on the adapter and no proxy branch. `pkg/ops/gateway/client.go` defines a `GatewayClient` used by `configservice` and `driftservice`, but the MCP invoker does not hold or call one. Searched pkg/ops, pkg/ops/opsserver, and tests/ for `GatewayClient` proxying from the MCP adapter; none found.
- **Gap:** The spec's dual-routing model (ops-owned tools local, gateway-owned tools proxied) is still half-built and untested for the proxy half, and the gap is now more consequential than when this finding was written: the generator (T-25.12.1) populates `tools/list` with ~164 gateway-owned admin-API tools that have no invocation path at all, so `tools/call` against any of them 404s against the lenny-ops mux rather than reaching the gateway. No test asserts a gateway-owned tool reaches the gateway admin API transparently, and no test asserts the routing is invisible (single inventory) across both sources. This is a core-architecture coverage gap at tier4.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a gateway stub or the real gateway in the compose stack (tests/testinfra/gateway, tests/testinfra/stubs). The GatewayClient proxy code does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/mcp_management_gateway_routing_test.go that stands up lenny-ops with a gateway behind it (tests/testinfra/gateway), invokes a gateway-owned tool (e.g. `admin.create_pool`) through `/mcp/management`, and asserts the request arrived at the gateway admin API with the propagated identity, while an ops-owned tool (e.g. `lenny_lock_acquire`) stays local.
- **Needs human input (as of 2026-07-12):** Building the §25.12 gateway-proxy routing requires two design decisions the spec does not resolve; please decide before implementation. (1) Identity-forwarding transport: §25.12 "Headers and Correlation" requires forwarding the caller's authenticated identity as the Authorization header on gateway calls and returning the gateway's raw status/body (including 4xx RBAC denials) to the MCP client, but the §25.4 GatewayClient is service-account-authed and JSON-decodes/errors on 4xx. Should the MCP gateway proxy (a) extend GatewayClient with a per-call identity override plus a raw status+body passthrough method, or (b) introduce a separate identity-forwarding proxy component, leaving the §25.4 GatewayClient unchanged for its drift/health fan-out role? (2) Dev-mode propagation: the scaffold and local/dev path carry identity via X-Lenny-Role dev headers (no bearer), but the spec's propagation model names only the Authorization header. Which headers should the proxy forward to the gateway in dev-mode so caller RBAC is enforced gateway-side (AllowDevHeaders)? A secondary, lower-stakes choice: use opsserver.RouteSchemas() as the ops-vs-gateway routing predicate (recommended — no generator/OpenAPI drift-guard changes), or add an explicit per-tool owner marker to the OpenAPI/generator? Given the scope (opsInvoker + opsserver.Options/Server + cmd/lenny-ops wiring + possibly pkg/ops/gateway/client.go) and that a prior author already left the tier4 scaffold skipped citing an "undesigned routing predicate," this likely warrants a change-proposal rather than an in-line fix.

### - [x] T-25.12.4 — The two security-model CI sweeps (no-role 403, scope-restricted 403 over every tool) do not exist [High] — RESOLVED 14dab239

### - [ ] T-25.12.16 — Generated admin-API tool names diverge from the spec's stated `lenny_{domain}_{action}` naming convention, untested [Medium] — OPEN

- **Existing tests:** no test found. The T-25.12.1 generator (`pkg/ops/mcp/mcptoolgen/mcptoolgen.go::buildTool`) takes the tool name verbatim from the OpenAPI document's `x-lenny-mcp-tool` field (`name := *op.MCPTool`) rather than deriving or validating it against a naming pattern. `grep -c` over `pkg/gateway/externalapi/openapi/openapi.json` shows 164 `x-lenny-mcp-tool` values following an `admin.{action}_{noun}` convention (`admin.create_tenant`, `admin.list_users`, `admin.create_pool`, ...) against 58 following the spec's stated `lenny_{domain}_{action}` convention (the pre-existing lenny-ops operability tools: `lenny_lock_acquire`, `lenny_backup_create`, ...). `pkg/gateway/externalapi/openapi/openapi_test.go` asserts every `x-lenny-mcp-tool` value is present and non-empty on documented admin-API endpoints but does not assert any naming pattern on the value itself.

An agent that assumes `lenny_{domain}_{action}` naming to predict a tool name for a platform-management action (e.g., guessing `lenny_tenant_create` instead of `admin.create_tenant`) will get a tool-not-found error tools/list would have prevented. This is a spec-versus-implementation naming inconsistency, uncovered at tier1 (a unit assertion on the naming pattern) and tier11 (the spec's naming claim is unreconciled documentation).

### - [x] T-25.12.17 — lenny-ops MCP management invoker drops the caller principal on internal replay, breaking tool invocation whenever the §25.4 auth gate is configured [High] — RESOLVED f35a3635d35f0c13f6c16854f166c305310cd897
- **Resolution:** The §25.12 MCP management invoker replayed each mapped tool request as a fresh, principal-less HTTP request through the full lenny-ops handler chain, so the §25.4 role gate rejected the replay (401/403) whenever an auth gate was configured, breaking every management tool invocation in production even for an authorized platform-admin caller. The product-code fix: the invoker now inherits the caller's already-verified principal, scope claim, and correlation context from the originating /mcp/management request (via a new ctx parameter on the Invoker interface) and replays against the post-authentication chain (role gate + scope gate, without re-verifying a bearer that is not forwarded in-process), so an authorized call is admitted as the real caller and a non-admin caller is still rejected 403. The spec makes the fix unambiguous — §25.12 Security Model, layer 3 (REST-layer RBAC): "Every MCP tool invocation that passes the scope check is translated into a REST call against `lenny-ops` or the gateway admin API. That REST call passes through the standard OIDC/JWT middleware and role-based authorization check. An agent with a `tenant-admin` role receives `403` from the underlying REST endpoint when calling a tool that requires `platform-admin`, regardless of what its scopes declare (scopes narrow; they don't elevate)." The CI-sweep paragraph adds the positive control: an authorized platform-admin caller must reach the endpoint rather than be rejected. The test now pins both directions via two new tests in pkg/ops/opsserver/mcp_test.go (authorized platform-admin replay reaches the endpoint; non-admin caller still 403).

### - [ ] T-25.12.18 — Spec's §25.12 no-role CI sweep (403 for every tool at the underlying REST call) contradicts §25.4 for the self-identity tools [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** `spec/25_agent-operability.md:4543` mandates a 403 for every MCP tool called with a no-role token, but `spec/25_agent-operability.md:1668` states "Any authenticated caller may call `/v1/admin/me` and its sub-endpoints."
- **Existing tests:** the no-role sweep landed under T-25.12.4 (`14dab239`). The generated tools `admin.me` and `admin.me_authorized_tools` (`pkg/ops/mcp/generated_tools.go:1220,1232`, `RequiredRole "user"`) map to `/v1/admin/me`.
- **Gap:** `/v1/admin/me`'s handler (`pkg/gateway/externalapi/admin/me.go:27`, "every authenticated caller can read it, no role gate") returns 200 for a role-less token, so a per-underlying-endpoint no-role sweep asserting "403 from the underlying REST call" would fail on `admin.me` and `admin.me_authorized_tools`. The spec's blanket "every MCP tool -> 403" rule needs to carve out the self-identity endpoints or state that the sweep runs at the `/mcp/management` transport gate. This is a spec-versus-spec contradiction, uncovered at tier1 (the sweep assertion) and tier11 (the unreconciled spec text).
- **Dependencies:** none; resolving the contradiction requires a spec amendment via the proposal pipeline (either the §25.12 sweep rule or the §25.4 self-identity carve-out).
- **Suggested test:** Once the spec contradiction is resolved, pin the no-role behavior of `admin.me` and `admin.me_authorized_tools` to whichever rule the spec settles on (a transport-gate 403 or a 200 self-identity carve-out).

### - [ ] T-25.12.19 — tools/list never intersects the capability filter with the caller's scope claim (permittedScopes hard-coded nil) [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** §25.12 states "Filtering is ALWAYS intersected with the caller's scope claim (tools not permitted by scope are filtered out regardless of capability declaration)."
- **Existing tests:** no test found exercising scope intersection on the HTTP `tools/list` path.

A scope-restricted caller therefore sees tools its scope does not permit in the `tools/list` display. `requestScopes(r)` already exists (`server.go:313`) to supply the scope set but is not used by `handleToolsList`.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add a `pkg/ops/mcp` unit test that drives `tools/list` for a scope-restricted caller and asserts tools outside the caller's scope claim are filtered out of the response even when the capability declaration would otherwise include them.

## §25.13-25.14 Bundled Alerting Rules and lenny-ctl Extensions <a id="t-25.13-25.14"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/25_agent-operability.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The §25.13 alerting-rules surface has strong static and chart-template coverage: `pkg/alerting/rules` is unit-tested for catalog hygiene and PromQL validation, the tier2 `catalog_crosscheck_test.go` asserts the rendered chart PrometheusRule matches the compiled catalog, and `charts/lenny/tests/prometheusrule_test.yaml` plus `gateway-deployment_test.yaml` cover format gating, `alertOverrides`, `alertThresholds`, and the `useCompiledRules` flag at the helm-unit level. The §25.14 `lenny-ctl` extensions have thorough request-shaping coverage against fakes in `pkg/ctlcli` (moved from `cmd/lenny-ctl` after the audit was generated; see F-24.0.1/F-17.4.9, `fd2d69ee`), including auto-discovery and the rule-3 fallback. Proposal 0021 (F-COV-2, landed `715381ce`) reassigned the audit-events surface from `lenny-ops` to the gateway; the §25.14 Routing table now lists `audit` alongside `health` and `recommendations` as gateway-targeted, and `pkg/ctlcli/operability_test.go` already pins every `audit` subcommand to the gateway (`runAgainstGateway`), so this reassignment did not open a new coverage gap. A second reconciliation: T-25.14.2's suggested tier3 contract test already existed at audit time (`tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/mcp_test.go`, landed pre-audit in `3f76ea9f`) and drives the real `lenny-ops` MCP management server through `initialize`, `tools/list`, and `tools/call` (including the dry-run mapping and the `-32001 SCOPE_FORBIDDEN` error shape); the original audit missed it, and it is resolved here. The remaining gaps are concentrated above tier1: no component test confirms the gateway `/metrics` endpoint actually exposes the `lenny_alerting_*` series with chart-driven values; the "single source of truth" claim is only half-verified because no test compares the gateway in-process evaluator against the catalog; the `thresholdSource: operator-customized` value is dead code and the operator-customized aggregation path is unexercised; TESTING.md §15.1 declares tier4 and tier5 coverage for every `lenny-ctl` operability subcommand that does not exist; and no chaos or e2e test asserts a bundled alert actually fires under its triggering condition. Counts: 2 High, 5 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info (across open and resolved findings).

### Findings

### - [x] T-25.14.1 — lenny-ctl operability extensions have no tier4 or tier5 coverage despite TESTING.md declaring it mandatory [High] — RESOLVED 3db46ffd880bf18fc99a743e8d1c9c7e97678951
- **Resolution:** Added tests/tier4_integration/lenny_ctl_ops_test.go, which drives the lenny-ctl operability command groups (runbooks list, diagnose connectivity, escalations create/resolve, backup list) through ctlcli.Run against the real cmd/lenny-ops binary backed by Postgres and Redis. It exercises the full CLI path — global-flag parsing, §25.14 dispatch, §24.16 --ops-server routing, dev-header propagation, and JSON decode — and cross-checks the escalations create/resolve mutation against the ops_escalations Postgres table, closing the gap that these groups were only exercised at unit level against httptest fakes.

### - [x] T-25.13.1 — The §25.13 single-source-of-truth invariant is only half-tested: the gateway in-process evaluator is never compared against the catalog [High] — RESOLVED 92b0a49f2edd317da4b629316580848c380cf943
- **Resolution:** Added a tier2 case, TestGatewayEvaluatorTracksCatalogAndRenderedChart, in tests/tier2_component/observability/catalog_crosscheck_test.go. It constructs the gateway in-process alert evaluator the same way cmd/lenny-gateway/runserver.go does (evaluator.New over rules.Catalog() with the inproceval backend), enumerates the rule names it tracks via State(name), and asserts that set equals both the distinct rules.Catalog() names and the rendered chart PrometheusRule's alert names. This ties the third §25.13 surface (the gateway evaluator) to the catalog and rendered manifest that the pre-existing crosscheck tests already compared, so a filtered or hand-maintained evaluator subset now fails. Passes against current code; a mutation feeding the evaluator a subset was confirmed to fail. lenny-test validate-maps is clean. Spec basis (spec/25_agent-operability.md §25.13 "Single Source of Truth"): "**The gateway binary** — the in-process alert state tracker (Section 25.3, Health API) evaluates these expressions against the in-process metric registry. This is the per-replica fallback used when Prometheus is unreachable" and "This avoids the two-source-of-truth problem: the rule definitions cannot drift between what the gateway evaluates and what Prometheus loads. A change to a threshold expression updates both the compiled-in evaluator and the rendered manifests in lockstep."

### - [ ] T-25.13.2 — The §25.13 alerting metrics are never observed on a live gateway /metrics scrape [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`lenny_alerting_rules_bundled` | Gauge | `format` | 1 if rules are rendered in the given format ... `lenny_alerting_rule_overrides` ... Count of operator-overridden rules ... `lenny_alerting_rule_eval_duration_seconds` | Histogram | `rule` ... These metrics let operators verify their bundling configuration is in effect and detect evaluation cost issues." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:4836-4840).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/alerting/alertingmetrics/alertingmetrics_test.go` unit-tests the registration and the `SetBundledFormats`/`SetOverrideCount`/`ObserveRuleEvalDuration` setters. `charts/lenny/tests/gateway-deployment_test.yaml` asserts the chart renders `LENNY_ALERTING_BUNDLE_FORMATS` and `LENNY_ALERTING_OVERRIDE_COUNT`. `cmd/lenny-gateway/main.go` reads those env vars and calls the setters. No test scrapes a running gateway and asserts the three series appear with values matching the chart's `monitoring.format` and `len(monitoring.alertOverrides)`.
- **Gap:** The unit test proves the setter works in isolation and the helm test proves the env var is rendered, but nothing closes the loop that the env value flows through `cmd/lenny-gateway` startup to a real `/metrics` exposition with the correct gauge values. A regression in env parsing (for example `LENNY_ALERTING_BUNDLE_FORMATS=both` not splitting to two label series) would not be caught. This is a missing component-level user journey (an operator scraping `/metrics` to confirm bundling) at tier2.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. A gateway started in-process with the alerting env vars set plus a Prometheus text scrape of its `/metrics` is sufficient.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier2_component/observability/alerting_metrics_exposition_test.go that starts the gateway with `LENNY_ALERTING_BUNDLE_FORMATS=prometheusrule,configmap` and `LENNY_ALERTING_OVERRIDE_COUNT=2`, scrapes `/metrics`, and asserts `lenny_alerting_rules_bundled{format="configmap"}==1` and `lenny_alerting_rule_overrides==2`.

### - [ ] T-25.13.3 — The operator-customized threshold-source value is dead code and its aggregation path is untested [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "In all three cases, `lenny-ops` health aggregation reflects the operator's view because it queries Prometheus's alerts API. If an operator has decided that queue depth >5 is critical instead of warning, agents see that severity. There is no second set of thresholds in `lenny-ops`." (spec/25_agent-operability.md:4791); the envelope value `"operator-customized"` is defined at pkg/ops/conventions/conventions.go:120-122.
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/operability/health/service_test.go::TestReportStampsThresholdSource_spec_25_13_4848` and `pkg/gateway/operability/recommendations/service_test.go` assert the gateway always stamps `thresholdSource=compiled-in-defaults` (these files moved from `pkg/gateway/health` and `pkg/gateway/recommendations` under the proposal 0020 §12 reorganization). A repository-wide grep shows `ThresholdSourceOperatorCustomized` is assigned nowhere in production code (only the const definition exists), and no test under `tests/` references `thresholdSource` at all.
- **Gap:** The spec promises that when `lenny-ops` serves from the Prometheus alerts API the response reflects the operator-customized rule set, which would correspond to `thresholdSource: operator-customized`. That value is never produced and no component or integration test exercises a `lenny-ops` health response derived from Prometheus's `/api/v1/alerts` with an operator-customized severity. This is both a spec-versus-implementation inconsistency (a documented envelope value that can never appear) and a missing tier2/tier4 coverage of the primary aggregation path.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a Prometheus stub or mock that serves `/api/v1/alerts` with a customized severity (tests/testinfra/stubs or tests/testinfra/mocks). A Prometheus-alerts mock does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier2_component/ops/health_threshold_source_test.go that points `lenny-ops` at a Prometheus mock returning a firing `GatewayQueueDepthHigh` at `severity=critical`, then asserts the aggregated health response carries `thresholdSource: operator-customized` and the critical severity, and add the missing assignment in the ops aggregation code.

- **Spec/Doc:** "| Universal | `WarmPoolExhausted`, `SessionStoreUnavailable`, `DualStoreUnavailable`, `CertExpiryImminent`, `BackupOverdue`, `PlatformUpgradeStuck` | Fixed values (e.g., warm pool == 0 for >60s). Same at any scale. |" (spec/25_agent-operability.md:4731); TESTING.md:2067 requires every runbook chaos test to "Confirm the documented alert fires."
