## §27.3 Web Playground: Authentication <a id="t-27.3"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/27_web-playground.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The playground authentication surface has dense unit-and-component coverage in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground` (regrouped from `pkg/gateway/playground` by proposal 0020's MCP Fabric consolidation) and one `//go:build contract` tier-3 file, exercising the three auth modes, the mode-polymorphic mint endpoint, the `origin: "playground"` claim, scope narrowing (including the proposal-0015 `effectiveScope` mint-response field, now covered at tier1/tier2/tier3), cross-replica revocation against `miniredis`, the fail-closed Redis posture in the auth middleware, and the WebSocket bearer carrier plus 4401 close code in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp` (also regrouped from `pkg/gateway/mcp`). The coverage stops at the in-process component tier. No integration (tier4) test drives the auth gatekeepers through the real `cmd/lenny-gateway` binary against a real Redis container, no e2e (tier5/tier6) test exercises the browser login flow on a chart with `playground.enabled=true`, no security (tier9) test treats the paste-form phishing surface or the cross-replica revocation-bypass as an adversarial scenario end to end, and no conformance test pins the OIDC authorization-code-with-PKCE flow against an OAuth/OIDC provider because every component test substitutes a `fakeOIDC` that bypasses the real provider exchange. The OIDC-callback tenant-rejection redirect branches, the `apiKey`-mode yellow banner, and the dev-tenant Ready-gate self-heal are unverified above the in-process level, and the declared tier5/tier9 surface in TESTING.md §14.12 and the tier7 `playground_revocation` load scenario are both stubbed because the e2e overlay never enables the playground. Proposal 0032 (documentation-only, applied 2026-07-03) gave the pre-existing `pg:user` per-user session index and `pg:sess-tenant` fan-in index a spec home in this subsection's "Session record backing store" table; both keys and their component-level tests (`user_invalidation_test.go`, `cookie_opaque_test.go`) predate the 2026-06-03 audit and introduce no new test-coverage obligation.
Counts: 4 High, 5 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-27.3.1 — OIDC authorization-code-with-PKCE flow has no conformance test against a real OAuth/OIDC provider [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`GET /playground/auth/callback?code=…&state=…` — OIDC provider redirects here. The gateway verifies `state` against the state cookie, performs the PKCE-protected token exchange with the provider, validates the returned ID token (signature, `iss`, `aud`, `exp`, `nbf`)" (spec/27_web-playground.md:81); the source sets `code_challenge_method=S256` and `code_verifier` (pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/oidc.go:153,171).
- **Existing tests:** `TestOIDCLoginRedirectsAndSetsStateCookie` (pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/playground_test.go:725) asserts the 302 and the state cookie path, and `completeOIDCLogin` (pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/sessionrecord_test.go:236) drives login then callback, but both use the `fakeOIDC` exchanger (pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/playground_test.go:35-49) whose `Exchange` returns a fixed subject and never performs the PKCE token POST, validates an ID token signature, or checks `iss`/`aud`/`exp`/`nbf`. No tier3/tier10 test pins the authorization-request parameters (`code_challenge`, `code_challenge_method=S256`, `state`, `redirect_uri`, `scope`) or the token-exchange request against the OAuth 2.0 / OIDC / RFC 7636 PKCE wire contract. Searched tests/tier3_contract/playground, tests/tier10_conformance, and pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/*_test.go.
- **Gap:** The real OIDC `Exchanger` implementation in `oidc.go` (authorization URL construction, PKCE verifier-to-challenge derivation, ID-token signature and claim validation) is never executed under test, so a regression in the S256 challenge, the `state` binding, or ID-token validation would ship. This is a standards-conformance gap against OAuth 2.0 / OIDC / RFC 7636.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a standards-conformant OIDC provider stub that serves a JWKS endpoint, an authorization endpoint, and a token endpoint, plus a known signing key. tests/testinfra/stubs and tests/testinfra/tokenservice exist; the OIDC-provider stub does not exist yet and building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier3_contract/playground/oidc_pkce_conformance_test.go that stands the real OIDC `Exchanger` against the provider stub, asserts the authorization request carries `code_challenge_method=S256` and a `state` echoed back, and asserts the gateway rejects an ID token with a bad signature, wrong `aud`, or expired `exp`.

### - [ ] T-27.3.2 — Cross-replica revocation-bypass is verified only against miniredis in-process, never end to end with the real gateway and a security adversary [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "This check is the correctness guarantee that a logout on one replica cannot be bypassed by presenting the same cookie or bearer to a peer replica." (spec/27_web-playground.md:97); "`TestPlaygroundSessionRevocationCrossReplica` MUST assert that a logout on replica A invalidates a subsequent request carrying the same cookie or bearer on replica B, both before and after the pub/sub message is delivered" (spec/27_web-playground.md:100).
- **Existing tests:** `TestPlaygroundSessionRevocationCrossReplica_spec_27_3_1_98` (pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/cross_replica_test.go:20) and `TestRevokedBearerCheckSurvivesAcrossHandlers` (pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/sessionrecord_test.go:186) model two replicas as two `RedisSessionStore` values over one `miniredis`, in-process, with no HTTP gateway and no real Redis. `TestPlaygroundBearerRejectedWhenRevoked_spec_27_3_1_95` (pkg/gateway/middleware/auth/playground_revocation_test.go:59) uses a fake checker. The tier4 Redis integration test `TestGatewayRedisBreakerE2E` (tests/tier4_integration/gateway_redis_e2e_test.go:26) drives the real binary against a Redis container but covers only the circuit-breaker key, not playground revocation.
- **Gap:** The security-critical guarantee that logout on replica A blocks replica B is never exercised through two real `cmd/lenny-gateway` replicas sharing a real Redis with pub/sub fanout. The adversarial scenario (alice logs out, an attacker replays alice's still-cached bearer against a peer replica before pub/sub delivery) has no end-to-end or security-tier test. This is both a multi-replica deployment-combination gap and an unverified security control.
- **Dependencies:** Requires two gateway replicas (tests/testinfra/gateway can start the binary; a two-replica harness is needed) and a real Redis container (tests/testinfra/containers.StartRedis). The two-replica gateway harness does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier9_security/playground_revocation_bypass_test.go that starts two gateway replicas against one Redis, mints a bearer on replica A, logs out on A, and asserts replica B rejects the same cookie and bearer both immediately (authoritative Redis `GET`) and after pub/sub delivery, using tests/testinfra/gateway and tests/testinfra/containers.

### - [ ] T-27.3.3 — apiKey-mode paste-form phishing surface and its server-sourced warning banner have no end-to-end security test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`apiKey` mode ships a bearer-token paste form as its primary UX — operationally similar to asking a human user to paste a production credential into a web form, which is a well-known phishing vector." (spec/27_web-playground.md:258); "the playground UI renders a persistent, server-sourced yellow banner \"API KEY MODE — paste only operator-issued tokens\" ... The banner text is emitted by the gateway (not the embedded bundle), so swapping or patching the asset bundle does not suppress it." (spec/27_web-playground.md:257).
- **Existing tests:** `TestConfigJSONCarriesDevBanner` (pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/playground_test.go:703) asserts only the `dev`-mode danger banner; the source sets the `apiKey` warning banner at assets.go:106-107 but no test asserts it. The preflight `WARNING`/acknowledgement path is covered for chart-flag rendering in charts/lenny/tests/preflight-job_test.yaml:351 and pkg/preflight/playground_test.go. No security-tier or e2e test verifies the banner is server-sourced and survives a bundle swap, and none treats the paste form as an adversarial credential-handling surface.
- **Existing tests (continued):** Searched tests/tier9_security and tests/tier5_e2e_kind for any `apiKey`-mode playground coverage and found none.
- **Gap:** The user-facing warning banner for `apiKey` mode is unverified at every tier, including the spec's central claim that the gateway sources it so a swapped bundle cannot suppress it. The phishing surface that motivates the `playground.acknowledgeApiKeyMode` acknowledgement has no security-tier test confirming the banner is present and that a service-account token (not a human credential) is the only accepted material. This is a missing user-journey assertion (an operator sees the warning) and a missing adversarial assertion (a tampered bundle cannot hide it).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness with a chart rendered at `playground.enabled=true, authMode=apiKey` (tests/testinfra/kind) and an asset-swap fixture. The chart overlay enabling the playground does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier9_security/playground_apikey_banner_test.go (component-level, buildable today against `config.json`) asserting `apiKey` mode emits the yellow `warning` banner with the documented text, plus a tier5 case that serves a stripped bundle and confirms `GET /playground/config.json` still returns the gateway-sourced banner.

### - [ ] T-27.3.4 — No e2e test drives the browser OIDC login-to-WebSocket journey on a deployed chart [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The playground never bypasses gateway auth. A user hitting `/playground` is routed through the gateway's auth chain identical to API traffic." (spec/27_web-playground.md:57); TESTING.md declares "Coverage spans Tier 5 e2e (full chart with `playground.enabled: true`) and Tier 9 (security)" (TESTING.md:1955) and the tier5 acceptance gate "OIDC, API-key, and dev auth modes work; CSP and HttpOnly cookies present" (TESTING.md:1083).
- **Existing tests:** All playground auth tests run in-process via `httptest` and `miniredis` in pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground and one `contract`-tagged file in tests/tier3_contract/playground. `tests/tier4_integration/gateway_full_e2e_test.go` does not reference `/playground` (grep returned no matches). No file under tests/tier5_e2e_kind or tests/tier6_e2e_cloud references the playground; no Kind overlay sets `playground.enabled=true` (grep of tests/testinfra/kind and tests/tier5_e2e_kind returned none).
- **Gap:** The declared tier5 surface in TESTING.md §14.12 does not exist on disk. The full user journey (alice opens `/playground`, is redirected to the OIDC provider, returns with a session cookie, mints a bearer, and connects the MCP WebSocket through the real Ingress with NetworkPolicy and TLS) is never exercised end to end. This is a core user-journey gap and a spec-versus-TESTING.md inconsistency (a declared suite is absent).
- **Dependencies:** Requires a tier5 Kind chart overlay with `playground.enabled=true` and `authMode=oidc`, a deployed OIDC provider stub, and the tier5 Kind harness (tests/testinfra/kind, tests/testinfra/sessiondriver). The playground-enabled overlay and OIDC stub do not exist yet; building them is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier5_e2e_kind/playground_oidc_journey_test.go that installs the chart with the playground enabled in OIDC mode, completes the login redirect against the provider stub, mints a bearer at `POST /v1/playground/token`, and opens an MCP WebSocket at `/mcp/v1/ws` asserting the session carries the `origin=playground` label.

### - [ ] T-27.3.5 — OIDC callback tenant-claim rejection redirects to the error page are untested [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "when extraction fails the gateway **does not** establish a session record or set `lenny_playground_session`, and instead redirects the browser to the playground error page `GET /playground/auth/error?error=<code>`" (spec/27_web-playground.md:81); the `TENANT_CLAIM_MISSING` / `TENANT_NOT_FOUND` / `TENANT_CLAIM_INVALID_FORMAT` table maps each to a `?error=` query param (spec/27_web-playground.md:106), and "No `lenny_playground_session` cookie is set for any row; the state cookie is cleared as part of the error redirect" (spec/27_web-playground.md:110).
- **Existing tests:** The component tests cover the `apiKey`-mode JSON-envelope tenant rejections in `TestAPIKeyModeTenantClaimRejectionsEmitMintRejected` (pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/playground_test.go:324), which is explicitly the JSON path, not the OIDC-callback redirect path. `handleCallback` in pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/auth.go:102 redirects to `/playground/auth/error` for invalid/missing/mismatched/expired state, exchange failure, tenant-not-found, and tenant-lookup-failure, but no test in pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/*_test.go drives a failing callback. Searched for `auth/error`, `error=tenant`, and `exchangeErr` usage and found the fields defined but never exercised in a callback test.
- **Gap:** Every OIDC-callback failure branch (state mismatch, expired state, exchange failure, `TENANT_CLAIM_MISSING`, `TENANT_NOT_FOUND`, `TENANT_CLAIM_INVALID_FORMAT`) is unverified, including the security-relevant guarantees that no session cookie is set and the state cookie is cleared on the error redirect. This is a failure-path component gap and a standards-conformance gap (the OIDC redirect-error contract).
- **Dependencies:** None — buildable today. The `fakeOIDC` exchanger already supports `exchangeErr` and a subject with an empty or unknown `TenantID`, and `fakeTenants` can report a tenant absent.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier2_component or pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground callback-rejection cases driving the callback with a mismatched `state`, a subject whose `tenant_id` is empty, malformed, and unknown, asserting a 302 to `/playground/auth/error?error=<code>`, no `lenny_playground_session` cookie, and a cleared state cookie.

### - [ ] T-27.3.6 — Redis-unavailable fail-closed posture is unverified against a real Redis outage [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The revocation check fails **closed**: when Redis is unreachable during the per-request check, playground-origin requests are rejected with `503 REDIS_UNAVAILABLE` rather than permitted ... prevents a Redis outage from silently converting into a revocation-bypass window." (spec/27_web-playground.md:99).
- **Existing tests:** `TestPlaygroundBearerFailsClosedOnStoreError_spec_27_3_1_97` (pkg/gateway/middleware/auth/playground_revocation_test.go:122) injects a fake checker returning `context.DeadlineExceeded` and asserts 503. This is an in-process unit assertion against a fake, not a real Redis outage through the gateway binary.
- **Gap:** The fail-closed behavior is never exercised against a real Redis container that is then made unreachable, so the actual `RedisSessionStore.IsBearerRevoked` error path, its timeout handling, and the resulting 503 on a live playground-origin request are unverified. This is a chaos / resilience deployment-combination gap (Redis outage fail-closed).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the gateway binary against a real Redis container that the test can pause or kill mid-request. tests/testinfra/containers.StartRedis and tests/testinfra/chaos exist; a Redis-kill primitive may need wiring into the chaos harness.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier8_chaos/playground_redis_failclosed_test.go that starts the gateway with the playground enabled against a real Redis, mints a playground bearer, kills Redis, and asserts a subsequent playground-origin request returns `503 REDIS_UNAVAILABLE` rather than being honored, using tests/testinfra/gateway, tests/testinfra/containers, and tests/testinfra/chaos.

### - [ ] T-27.3.7 — Logout propagation SLO (P99 ≤ 500 ms across replicas) has no load or e2e test; the declared scenario is a skip [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "**Logout propagation SLO:** a revocation published on any replica MUST be visible to the per-request revocation check on every other replica within **500 ms at P99** under nominal Redis health" (spec/27_web-playground.md:98); TESTING.md §12.7 declares the `playground_revocation` scenario "1000 active playground sessions; tenant-wide revoke | P99 propagation ≤ 500ms" (TESTING.md:1186).
- **Existing tests:** The propagation mechanics (encode/parse, cache warm, sample emission) are unit-tested in pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/revocation_propagation_test.go, but those tests assert a synthetic 120 ms latency from a hand-constructed message, not a measured cross-replica P99. The declared tier7 scenario `TestPlaygroundRevocation` (tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go:440) is a `t.Skip` because "the §27 playground is disabled on the e2e gateway (playground routes return 404)".
- **Gap:** The 500 ms P99 propagation SLO is never measured under the declared 1000-session, tenant-wide-revoke load, so an SLO regression would not be caught. The declared suite is a scaffold blocked on the missing playground-enabled overlay. This is a load/SLO deployment-combination gap and a declared-suite-is-a-skip finding.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a multi-replica gateway with the playground enabled, a real Redis, and the k6 load harness (tests/testinfra/load, tests/testinfra/loadgen). The playground-enabled load overlay does not exist yet; building it is part of this finding and unblocks the existing skip.
- **Suggested test:** Replace the `t.Skip` in tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go::TestPlaygroundRevocation with a run that seeds 1000 playground sessions across replicas, issues a tenant-wide revoke, and asserts the `lenny_playground_session_revocation_propagation_seconds` P99 stays under 500 ms.

### - [ ] T-27.3.8 — Dev-tenant Ready-gate self-heal and the post-install bootstrap-ordering window are unverified end to end [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "if the tenant id is well-formed yet **absent** from Postgres at startup the gateway process starts normally and only the `/playground/*` route family returns `503 LENNY_PLAYGROUND_DEV_TENANT_NOT_SEEDED` with `Retry-After: 5` until the tenant row appears ... the 503 self-heals the instant the bootstrap Job commits the tenant row; no gateway restart or rollout is required" (spec/27_web-playground.md:61); non-playground routes "remain fully available so that the `lenny-bootstrap` Job ... is not deadlocked" (spec/27_web-playground.md:61).
- **Existing tests:** `TestDevModeReadyGateRejectsUnseededTenant` (pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/playground_test.go:227) asserts the 503 and `Retry-After: 5` against a `fakeTenants` reporting the tenant absent. No test asserts the self-heal transition (503 then 200 once the tenant row commits) or that non-playground routes (`/healthz`, `/v1/sessions`, MCP) stay available during the window. The chart-side ordering is covered only as flag rendering in charts/lenny/tests/gateway-deployment_test.yaml.
- **Gap:** The self-healing transition and the deadlock-avoidance guarantee (the bootstrap Job's `/healthz` poll succeeds while `/playground/*` returns 503) are never exercised end to end, so a regression that gated `/healthz` on tenant existence or cached the negative lookup would not be caught. This is an integration / e2e deployment-combination gap for the `lenny up` and post-install bootstrap topology.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the gateway binary against a real Postgres with the tenant row seeded after startup. tests/testinfra/containers and tests/testinfra/gateway exist; a post-start tenant-seed step is needed.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/playground_dev_ready_gate_test.go that starts the gateway in dev mode with an unseeded `devTenantId` against a real Postgres, asserts `/playground/` returns 503 while `/healthz` and `/v1/sessions` return 200, then seeds the tenant row and asserts the next `/playground/` request returns 200 with no restart.

### - [ ] T-27.3.9 — Cross-mode admission rejections are covered for two modes but not the dev-mode ignore semantics and the apiKey cookie rejection [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** The Auth-by-mode table requires: `oidc` rejects `Authorization: Bearer` with `400 LENNY_PLAYGROUND_WRONG_AUTH_MATERIAL`; `apiKey` rejects a presented `lenny_playground_session` cookie with the same code; `dev` "Any `Authorization: Bearer` or `lenny_playground_session` cookie presented in `dev` mode is **ignored** (not rejected — dev mode never gates on caller material)." (spec/27_web-playground.md:135); the error body carries `details.presentedMaterial ∈ {cookie, bearer, both}` (spec/27_web-playground.md:137).
- **Existing tests:** `TestOIDCModeRejectsBearerOnTokenEndpoint` (pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/playground_test.go:569) and `TestOIDCModeRejectsBearerMaterial` (tests/tier3_contract/playground/playground_test.go:338) cover the `oidc`-rejects-bearer case and assert `details.configuredAuthMode`. No test covers the `apiKey`-mode rejection of a presented cookie, the `oidc`-mode rejection when both a cookie and a bearer are presented, the `dev`-mode ignore of presented material, or the `details.presentedMaterial` field for any branch.
- **Gap:** Three of the documented cross-mode admission cells and the `details.presentedMaterial` operator-debugging field are unverified, leaving the route-stamped mode-enforcement contract only partially tested. This is a partial-coverage finding on a security-relevant admission boundary (preventing auth-mode flipping by presenting the wrong material).
- **Dependencies:** None — buildable today against the in-process handler with the in-memory session store.
- **Suggested test:** Extend tests/tier3_contract/playground/playground_test.go with cases asserting `apiKey` mode rejects a cookie-only request with `LENNY_PLAYGROUND_WRONG_AUTH_MATERIAL` and `details.presentedMaterial=cookie`, `oidc` mode reports `both` when a cookie and a bearer are sent together, and `dev` mode mints `200` while ignoring a presented bearer and cookie.

## §27.4-27.6 Web Playground: UI Surface, Protocol, Session Lifecycle <a id="t-27.4-27.6"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/27_web-playground.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The playground gateway-side logic carries dense component-level coverage in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground` (auth modes, mint invariants, revocation, session-record isolation) and one tier3 contract suite, and the cross-replica revocation primitive is exercised against miniredis. Above the component tier the coverage drops away entirely. TESTING.md §14.12 claims the playground surface is covered by Tier 5 e2e and Tier 9 security, and the suite tables name a tier5 `playground` suite, a tier5 `oidc_authentication` suite, and a tier7 `playground_revocation` load scenario, but none of these exist on disk: the only artifact is a `t.Skip` stub in `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go`, and there is no tier4, tier5, tier6, tier8, tier9, or tier10 test that references the playground. The §27.4 React UI is verified only by grepping the embedded `app.js` source for substrings, so no screen, control, or browser-to-WebSocket flow is exercised behaviorally. The §27.5 protocol claim that the playground drives the public MCP WebSocket end to end, and the §27.6 idle-override/duration-cap enforcement against a live pod, are both unverified through any running stack. Since the 2026-06-03 audit, proposal 0002 re-keyed the §27.6 idle-timeout override from the runtime's `maxIdleTimeSeconds` to the pool's effective `sessionPolicy.maxClientIdleSeconds` (the requirement is unchanged, only the terminology), proposal 0015 added an `effectiveScope` field to the `POST /v1/playground/token` mint response and a scope-gated delegation-policy affordance to §27.4 (both are exercised by the existing string-grep-style UI tests, so they do not change this section's coverage class), and proposal 0032 gave the `pg:user:{user_id}` and `pg:sess-tenant:{session_id}` Redis keys a home in this section's backing-store table (both are already covered at component level). Separately, F-27.3.7 landed a real test for the `idle_timeout` reason previously flagged as untested in T-27.6.4; the `admin_revoke` reason remains untested and, on inspection, unwired to any caller. The whole package also moved from `pkg/gateway/playground` to `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground` (and `pkg/gateway/mcp` to `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp`) in a C3 subsystem-grouping refactor; every existing-test file path below is updated to the new location. Counts: 3 High, 5 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-27.5.1 — No end-to-end test drives the playground browser flow through a live gateway and MCP WebSocket [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The playground is a client of the public MCP surface — for session, chat, and discovery traffic it uses exactly the same endpoints as any other client. … Chat stream: MCP WebSocket at `/mcp/v1/ws` with a session-capability JWT as the bearer." (spec/27_web-playground.md:189, spec/27_web-playground.md:192). TESTING.md §14.12 asserts "Coverage spans Tier 5 e2e (full chart with `playground.enabled: true`)" (TESTING.md:1955) and the tier5 suite table names "playground | Web playground serves `/playground`; OIDC, API-key, and dev auth modes work; CSP and HttpOnly cookies present" (TESTING.md:1083).
- **Existing tests:** The tier3 contract suite `tests/tier3_contract/playground/playground_test.go` composes the playground handler with the sessionserver behind the auth middleware via `httptest` and asserts a minted JWT is accepted by `POST /v1/sessions` (`TestPlaygroundJWTAcceptedByPublicSessionsAPI`, lines 170-219). No browser, no real Ingress, no live `/mcp/v1/ws` upgrade. A search of `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/` returns no playground reference; the suite named in TESTING.md:1083 does not exist on disk. spec-map.json §27.5 lists only two tier3 functions (`TestPlaygroundJWTAcceptedByPublicSessionsAPI`, `TestLoginEndpointIsOIDCModeOnly`).
- **Gap:** The full user journey (alice loads `/playground`, picks a runtime, creates a session via `POST /v1/sessions`, opens the MCP WebSocket with the minted bearer, and exchanges a chat message) is never exercised against the real gateway binary on a cluster. This is the primary persona journey for §27.4-27.6 and the protocol-as-living-reference claim in §27.5. Target tier5 e2e on Kind, with the chart installed at `playground.enabled=true`.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`), the gateway installed with `playground.enabled=true`, and either the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: lenny.bearer.*` carrier or an `Authorization` header on the WS dial. The e2e overlay currently installs the playground disabled (per the tier7b skip at `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go:440-447`), so an overlay that enables it is part of this finding. A browser driver is not strictly required; an HTTP+WebSocket client journey covers the protocol path.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/playground_test.go` that installs the chart with `playground.enabled=true, authMode=dev`, drives `POST /v1/playground/token`, then `POST /v1/sessions`, then dials `/mcp/v1/ws` with the minted bearer and sends one chat frame, asserting a runtime reply, using `tests/testinfra/kind` and `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`.

### - [ ] T-27.6.1 — Playground idle-timeout override and hard duration cap are never enforced against a live session pod [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Playground-initiated sessions MUST NOT remain idle for longer than `playground.maxIdleTimeSeconds` (default: `300` / 5 min). The gateway enforces this value as a hard override of the pool's effective `sessionPolicy.maxClientIdleSeconds` … The effective idle cap is `min(maxClientIdleSeconds, playground.maxIdleTimeSeconds)`, where `maxClientIdleSeconds` is the pool's effective value." (spec/27_web-playground.md:204). "Hard duration cap. `min(sandboxTemplate.spec.maxSessionMinutes, playground.maxSessionMinutes)`." (spec/27_web-playground.md:203). Proposal 0002 re-keyed this bullet from "the runtime's `maxIdleTimeSeconds`" to the pool's effective `sessionPolicy.maxClientIdleSeconds`; the MUST itself (a tightened idle cap for playground-origin sessions) is unchanged, only the platform concept it overrides is renamed.
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/playground_test.go::TestEffectiveIdleAndDurationCaps` (line 173) checks the `min()` arithmetic on the `Config` struct. `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/playground_create_test.go::TestCreatePlaygroundOriginStampsCapsAndLabel_spec_27_6` asserts the create response and persisted row carry the computed timeout values. Both verify that the numbers are stamped; neither verifies that an idle playground session is actually reclaimed at the tightened cap rather than the platform default.
- **Gap:** The MUST that a playground session is reclaimed within 5 min of idleness (rather than the platform's longer default) is a behavior of the reaper running against a live or simulated-clock session, and it is untested above the arithmetic level. No test advances a clock and asserts the session transitions to a terminal state at `playground.maxIdleTimeSeconds`. This is a normative MUST with no behavioral coverage. Target tier4 integration with a clock-injection harness, or tier5 e2e on Kind.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a session-lifecycle reaper driven by an injectable clock (`tests/testinfra/clockstep` or `tests/testinfra/timectl`) plus the gateway harness (`tests/testinfra/gateway`). Buildable today against the compose stack with the clock harness.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/playground_idle_override_test.go` that creates an `origin=playground` session against a runtime whose `maxIdleTimeSeconds` is 600, advances the injected clock past 300 s with no activity, and asserts the session is reclaimed at 300 s; add a sibling case asserting a session is terminated at `min(sandboxTemplate.maxSessionMinutes, playground.maxSessionMinutes)`, using `tests/testinfra/clockstep` and `tests/testinfra/gateway`.

### - [ ] T-27.6.2 — Cross-replica logout-propagation SLO (P99 ≤ 500 ms) has no load or multi-replica integration test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Logout propagation SLO: a revocation published on any replica MUST be visible to the per-request revocation check on every other replica within 500 ms at P99 under nominal Redis health" (spec/27_web-playground.md:98). TESTING.md names the load scenario "playground_revocation | 1000 active playground sessions; tenant-wide revoke | P99 propagation ≤ 500ms" (TESTING.md:1186) and §14.12 lists "Cross-replica revocation propagation P99 ≤ 500ms" (TESTING.md:1960).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/cross_replica_test.go::TestPlaygroundSessionRevocationCrossReplica_spec_27_3_1_98` proves correctness (a revocation on replica A is observed on replica B before and after pub/sub delivery) against a single miniredis, but asserts nothing about latency or the P99 budget. `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/revocation_propagation_test.go` checks the propagation-sample encoding and that a single sample lands in the right histogram bucket. The named load scenario `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go::TestPlaygroundRevocation` is a `t.Skip` stub (lines 440-447): "the §27 playground is disabled on the e2e gateway … so the playground_revocation scenario has no surface to load-test." No `playground_revocation` scenario directory exists under `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/`.
- **Gap:** The 500 ms-P99 SLO is a measurable performance claim with a named load scenario that is an empty skip. It is unverified under the stated conditions (1000 active sessions, tenant-wide revoke, real multi-replica gateway sharing one Redis). This is both a declared-suite-is-a-scaffold inconsistency and a missing SLO test. Target tier7 load on Kind, with a multi-replica gateway.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the playground enabled on the load overlay, a multi-replica gateway Deployment, a real Redis, and the load harness (`tests/testinfra/loadgen`, `tests/testinfra/load`). The e2e/load overlay must enable the playground; building that overlay is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Replace the skip in `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go` with a real `playground_revocation` scenario under `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/playground_revocation/` that seeds 1000 sessions across replicas, issues a tenant-wide revoke, and asserts the `lenny_playground_session_revocation_propagation_seconds` P99 ≤ 500 ms, using `tests/testinfra/loadgen` and a multi-replica gateway.

### - [ ] T-27.4.1 — The React UI surface is verified only by source-string grep, with no behavioral or browser-driven test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The playground ships as a single-page React app with three screens: 1. Runtime picker. … 2. Session configuration. … 3. Chat. A single-session chat pane backed by the MCP WebSocket. Renders messages, tool-call events, delegation events, and errors. Includes an Interrupt button, a Cancel button, a raw-frame inspector … and a 'Copy as client SDK snippet' button that emits equivalent code in Go/Python/TS." (spec/27_web-playground.md:177-181).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/runtime_visible_test.go` reads the embedded `app.js` and asserts the source contains substrings such as `renderSchemaForm`, `runtimeOptionsSchema`, `lang === "python"`, and `LENNY_BEARER_TOKEN` (`TestPlaygroundSchemaDrivenConfig_spec_27_4_item2`, `TestPlaygroundSDKSnippetCoversThreeLanguages_spec_27_4_item3`, `TestPlaygroundPickerFiltersAllowedRuntimes_spec_27_5_190`). The same file now also grep-asserts the proposal-0015 `effectiveScope`-gated delegation-policy affordance (`TestPlaygroundStoresEffectiveScope_spec_27_3_1`, `TestPlaygroundGatesDelegationField_spec_27_4_item2`) via the same string-grep technique. These confirm strings exist in the bundle; none of them execute the SPA, render a screen, or exercise the Interrupt, Cancel, raw-frame-inspector, or delegation-field controls. There are no `*.test.js` / Playwright / Cypress files anywhere in the tree.
- **Gap:** No test verifies that the three screens render, that the runtime picker lists only allowed runtimes, that the chat pane renders tool-call and delegation events, or that the Interrupt and Cancel buttons emit `lenny/interrupt_session` / `lenny/cancel_session`. The §27.4 spec-map-exceptions entry classifies §27.4 as non-normative "visual layout description," but the controls have observable behavior (interrupt, cancel, browser-close cancel hint per §27.6 line 205, and now the scope-gated delegation-policy field) that a string-grep cannot confirm. Target a browser-driven e2e (tier5) or a DOM-level unit/component test of the bundle.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a browser or DOM harness (Playwright, jsdom, or vitest). No such harness exists in `tests/testinfra/` (confirmed: no browser/playwright/webdriver building block). Adding a JS test runner and a headless-browser driver is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add a Playwright e2e under `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/playground_ui_test` (or a jsdom unit suite beside `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/ui/`) that loads `/playground` against a dev-mode gateway, walks picker → config → chat, sends a message, and asserts the Interrupt button issues `lenny/interrupt_session` and the raw-frame inspector renders a frame.

### - [ ] T-27.6.3 — Browser-close `session.cancel` best-effort hint with reason `playground_client_closed` is untested [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "On browser close / navigation away, the client sends `session.cancel` with reason `playground_client_closed`. Gateway treats this as a best-effort hint; a dropped WebSocket that cannot send the frame falls back to the idle-timeout path described above, which, because of the override, fires within the 5-minute playground default rather than after the platform `maxClientIdleSeconds` default." (spec/27_web-playground.md:205).
- **Existing tests:** The cancel-on-unload wiring is present in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/ui/app.js` (the `beforeunload` handler near line 944 sends `lenny/cancel_session` with reason `playground_client_closed` near line 951), but only as source text the runtime-visible grep tests do not assert. On the gateway side, `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcptools/session_control_test.go::TestCancelSessionTool_bestEffortHintOnTerminalIsNoOp` and `TestCancelSessionTool_bestEffortHintOnUnknownIsAccepted` now assert that a `session.cancel` call carrying reason `playground_client_closed` against an already-terminal or already-reclaimed session is an idempotent no-op accepted response (F-27.6.5) — this is new since the 2026-06-03 audit. Neither of these covers the happy path (a `session.cancel` with this reason delivered against a *running* session, cancelling it and recording the reason) or the dropped-WebSocket idle-timeout fallback.
- **Gap:** The happy path (cancel frame delivered against a running session, session cancelled with the documented reason recorded) and the failure path (WebSocket dropped, idle-timeout fallback fires) remain unexercised; only the terminal/unknown-session idempotency edge cases are now covered. This is a SHOULD-adjacent best-effort behavior with a specific reason code and a failure fallback, both still untested on their primary paths. Target tier4 integration for the frame acceptance on a running session and the dropped-connection fallback.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the gateway harness (`tests/testinfra/gateway`) and the clock harness (`tests/testinfra/clockstep`) to drive the idle fallback. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/playground_client_closed_test.go` that opens a playground MCP WebSocket, sends `session.cancel` with reason `playground_client_closed` against a running session, and asserts the session is cancelled with that reason; add a second case that drops the WebSocket without sending the frame and asserts the idle-timeout reaper reclaims the session within `playground.maxIdleTimeSeconds`, using `tests/testinfra/clockstep`.

### - [ ] T-27.5.2 — `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: lenny.bearer.*` carrier path has no end-to-end browser-WebSocket test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Browsers that cannot set `Authorization` headers on WebSocket upgrades MUST use the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` sub-protocol carrier defined for this purpose: the client sends `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: lenny.mcp.v1, lenny.bearer.<bearerToken>` and the gateway echoes back `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: lenny.mcp.v1`. The `lenny.bearer.*` sub-protocol entry MUST be treated as a credential (not logged, not emitted in access logs, redacted in audit traces)." (spec/27_web-playground.md:145).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/wscarrier_test.go` covers the carrier-to-Authorization promotion and the redaction of the `lenny.bearer.*` entry at unit level (`TestWebSocketBearerCarrierPromotesAndRedacts` and siblings). `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/websocket_auth_test.go::TestWebSocketEchoesSubprotocol` asserts the gateway echoes `lenny.mcp.v1` over an `httptest` server. These verify the mechanism in isolation; no test drives the carrier path with a real playground-minted bearer through the gateway binary, and none asserts the credential is absent from emitted access logs or audit traces end to end.
- **Gap:** The carrier is the only WebSocket auth path available to browsers, and the MUST that the bearer sub-protocol is redacted from access logs and audit traces is a security-relevant claim verified only at the unit boundary. The end-to-end behavior (browser-style dial with the sub-protocol, against the live gateway, with a log/audit assertion that the token never appears) is untested. Target tier4 integration with log capture, or tier5 e2e.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the gateway harness with access-log and audit capture (`tests/testinfra/gateway`, `tests/testinfra/audit`). Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/playground_ws_carrier_test.go` that mints a playground bearer, dials `/mcp/v1/ws` with `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: lenny.mcp.v1, lenny.bearer.<token>`, asserts the echo is exactly `lenny.mcp.v1`, and asserts the bearer string never appears in the captured access log or audit events, using `tests/testinfra/gateway` and `tests/testinfra/audit`.

### - [ ] T-27.6.4 — Admin-revoke driving the playground revocation path is untested above the unit tier, and appears unwired [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Logout (`POST /playground/auth/logout`), `user.invalidated`, idle timeout, and admin revocation all drive the same revocation path: `DEL` on the session-record key + `SET` on the per-bearer `pg:revoked:{jti}` key + `PUBLISH` on `t:{tenant_id}:pg:revocations`." (spec/27_web-playground.md:207). The §27.8 counter enumerates `reason ∈ {user_logout, idle_timeout, admin_revoke, oidc_session_ended, user_invalidated}` (spec/27_web-playground.md:243).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/sessionrecord_test.go::TestLogoutRevokesSessionBearer` covers the `user_logout` reason end to end at component level, and `user_invalidation_test.go::TestRevokeSessionsForUserRevokesEveryUserSession_spec_27_6_204` covers `user_invalidated`. Since the 2026-06-03 audit, F-27.3.7 landed `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/idle_sweep_test.go::TestSweepIdleSessionsRevokesIdleThroughPrimitive_spec_27_3_1_94`, which drives `SweepIdleSessions` → `RevokeSession(..., RevokeIdleTimeout)` on a genuinely idle record and asserts `lenny_playground_session_revocations_total{reason="idle_timeout"}` increments by 1 — this closes the `idle_timeout` half of the original finding. The `admin_revoke` reason (`RevokeAdmin` in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/sessionrecord.go:78`) remains untested, and a repo-wide search finds no caller anywhere in non-test code that invokes `RevokeSession` with `RevokeAdmin` — no admin-facing HTTP endpoint currently drives this reason.
- **Gap:** The `admin_revoke` reason is declared in the revocation-reason enum and named in the §27.8 metric but has neither a test nor a production call site. This is now a narrower partial-coverage gap than at generation time (one of five reasons rather than two), and it borders on a spec/implementation gap in its own right: the spec names admin revocation as a first-class trigger of the shared revocation path, but no code path exercises it. Target tier2 component (direct `Handler.RevokeSession` call) at minimum; a full closure of the gap likely also needs an admin-facing revoke endpoint, which is outside this finding's scope but worth flagging to the implementer.
- **Dependencies:** The session store and metrics exporter exist in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground`; `RevokeSession` already accepts `RevokeAdmin` as a reason value, so the primitive itself needs no new plumbing to test directly. Buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add a case beside `TestSweepIdleSessionsRevokesIdleThroughPrimitive_spec_27_3_1_94` (or in `sessionrecord_test.go`) that calls `Handler.RevokeSession(ctx, tenant, id, RevokeAdmin)` directly and asserts the record is deleted, the `pg:revoked:{jti}` marker is set, and `lenny_playground_session_revocations_total` increments with `reason="admin_revoke"`.

### - [ ] T-27.5.3 — No multi-mode deployment-combination test exercises the playground over the public surface in each authMode [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The JWT is minted by the single mode-polymorphic endpoint `POST /v1/playground/token` in all three `playground.authMode` values — cookie-authenticated in `oidc` mode, `Authorization: Bearer`-authenticated in `apiKey` mode, and admission-material-free in `dev` mode. … the WebSocket codepath itself is identical across modes because all three produce the same standard session-capability JWT with the `origin: "playground"` claim stamped." (spec/27_web-playground.md:192). TESTING.md §14.12: "Three auth modes: OIDC, API Key, Dev." (TESTING.md:1958) and the tier5 suite expects "OIDC, API-key, and dev auth modes work" (TESTING.md:1083).
- **Existing tests:** The tier3 contract suite exercises the mint endpoint per mode in isolation via `httptest` (dev mint returns a bearer, oidc rejects a bearer, apiKey rejects a capability subject token). The tier3 protocol assertion that a minted JWT is honored by `POST /v1/sessions` (`TestPlaygroundJWTAcceptedByPublicSessionsAPI`) runs only in `dev` mode. There is no test that walks the full mint-then-session-then-WebSocket path in `oidc` and `apiKey` modes, so the spec claim that the WebSocket codepath is identical across all three modes is verified for one mode only.
- **Gap:** The spec applies the "identical codepath across all three authModes" claim to a deployment dimension (auth mode: OIDC with PKCE, apiKey, dev), and a test exercises the full protocol path in only one of the three. This is a Partial deployment-combination gap. Target tier4 integration (compose stack) parameterized over the three auth modes.
- **Dependencies:** Requires an OIDC provider stub for the oidc-mode path (`tests/testinfra/stubs` or `tests/testinfra/tokenservice`) and the gateway harness. The OIDC stub for the playground callback may need to be added; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/playground_authmode_matrix_test.go` that runs the mint → `POST /v1/sessions` → `/mcp/v1/ws` chat journey once per `authMode` (oidc with a PKCE stub, apiKey with a pasted service-account token, dev), asserting an identical session-capability JWT and WebSocket outcome, using `tests/testinfra/matrix`, `tests/testinfra/gateway`, and an OIDC stub.

## §27.7-27.10 Web Playground: Assets/CSP, Metrics, Security, Roll-Forward <a id="t-27.7-27.10"></a>
**Spec file:** `spec/27_web-playground.md`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
Component-level coverage of §27.7 (asset serving and CSP) exists in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/playground_test.go` and the tier3 contract suite, but those tests assert a subset of the CSP directives and never verify the headers reach a browser through a real Ingress on Kind. §27.8 (metrics) is still the weakest area: the only test the spec-map claims, `TestMetricCatalogIsCompleteAgainstSpec161`, does not cover the playground metrics because they are absent from the `spec161Metrics` list, so the metric names, types, labels, and histogram buckets have no completeness or contract test. Runtime-increment coverage of the counters has improved since generation — `idle_sweep_test.go` and `user_invalidation_test.go` now assert `lenny_playground_session_revocations_total{reason}` increments for the `idle_timeout` and `user_invalidated` reasons through the real revocation path — but `user_logout`, `admin_revoke`, and `oidc_session_ended` remain unasserted, and `lenny_playground_page_views_total`, `lenny_playground_sessions_created_total`, `lenny_playground_ws_connect_total`, and `lenny_playground_dev_tenant_not_seeded_total` have no increment test at all. §27.9 (security) still has no tier9 test for the playground end to end, though the raw-frame redaction guarantee itself is now unit- and component-tested in the `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp` package (credential-scalar scrubbing, schema preservation, and the `origin=playground` egress gate over a live WebSocket handler); what remains missing is the CSP-through-a-real-Ingress and browser-facing adversarial path, and the apiKey-mode yellow banner assertion. §27.10 carries a normative roll-forward claim about in-flight sessions yet is still exempted from spec coverage in `spec-map-exceptions.yaml` and has no test. The declared tier5 `playground` e2e suite and tier7 `playground_revocation` load suite remain absent or skipped, and the cross-replica revocation path is still exercised only against miniredis, never against real Redis HA or a multi-replica gateway.
Counts: 3 High, 6 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-27.8.1 — Playground metric catalog has no completeness or contract test; the claimed catalog test does not cover it [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`lenny_playground_page_views_total` … `lenny_playground_sessions_created_total` … `lenny_playground_ws_connect_total` … `lenny_playground_session_revocations_total` … `lenny_playground_session_revocation_propagation_seconds` … `lenny_playground_dev_tenant_not_seeded_total`" with their declared types, labels, and reason enumerations (spec/27_web-playground.md:240-245).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/spec-map.json` §27.8 lists exactly one test, `pkg/observability/metrics/catalog_test.go::TestMetricCatalogIsCompleteAgainstSpec161`. That test iterates the `spec161Metrics` list, and a grep of `pkg/observability/metrics/` shows no `lenny_playground` entry in that list or the catalog, so the test asserts nothing about playground metrics. The playground metric names are declared only in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/metrics.go`, which has no `_test.go` exercising `NewMetrics` directly (the increment tests described in T-27.8.2 build a partial `*Metrics` literal rather than calling `NewMetrics` against a registry).
- **Gap:** The §27.8 metric surface has no contract test pinning the metric names, Prometheus types (Counter versus Histogram), label sets (`authMode`, `runtime`, `outcome`, `reason`, none), the `reason ∈ {user_logout, idle_timeout, admin_revoke, oidc_session_ended, user_invalidated}` enumeration, the `outcome ∈ {pubsub_delivered, redis_authoritative, resubscribe}` enumeration, or the histogram bucket boundaries `[5 ms … 2.5 s]`. A rename, a dropped label, or a changed bucket set would ship undetected. The work is a standards-conformance check against the spec metric table. The spec-map entry is also inconsistent because it claims coverage that does not exist.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground` and a `prometheus.NewRegistry()` are sufficient.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier2 component test `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/metrics_catalog_test.go` that calls `NewMetrics` against a fresh registry, gathers the registered families via `reg.Gather()`, and asserts each §27.8 metric name, type, label set, and the histogram buckets match the spec table; assert the `reason` and `outcome` label domains.

### - [ ] T-27.8.2 — No test asserts playground counters and the propagation histogram increment on their runtime paths [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`lenny_playground_session_revocations_total` … Incremented exactly once per `DEL t:{tenant_id}:pg:sess:{session_id}` performed by the revocation path." and "`lenny_playground_dev_tenant_not_seeded_total` … `/playground/*` requests rejected with `503 LENNY_PLAYGROUND_DEV_TENANT_NOT_SEEDED`." (spec/27_web-playground.md:243,245).
- **Existing tests:** Partial coverage has landed since generation. `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/idle_sweep_test.go::TestSweepIdleSessionsRevokesIdleThroughPrimitive_spec_27_3_1_94` and `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/user_invalidation_test.go::TestRevokeSessionsForUserRevokesEveryUserSession_spec_27_6_204` both build a real `Handler` over a partial `*Metrics` (a bare `revocations` `CounterVec`, not the full `NewMetrics` registry) and assert `lenny_playground_session_revocations_total{reason="idle_timeout"}` and `{reason="user_invalidated"}` increment by exactly the expected count through the real `SweepIdleSessions` / `RevokeSessionsForUser` paths, using `testutil.ToFloat64`. `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/revocation_propagation_test.go` still exercises only the `propObserver` callback shape for the histogram, not the registered Prometheus histogram. No test asserts `lenny_playground_session_revocations_total{reason="user_logout"}` increments on `POST /playground/auth/logout` (`TestLogoutRevokesSessionBearer` builds the handler with `Metrics: nil` and checks only the session-store and audit-log side effects), `{reason="admin_revoke"}` or `{reason="oidc_session_ended"}` on their respective paths, `lenny_playground_dev_tenant_not_seeded_total` increments on the 503 ready-gate path (`TestDevModeReadyGateRejectsUnseededTenant` checks only the HTTP response and error code, not the counter), `lenny_playground_page_views_total{authMode}` increments on an index load, or that `lenny_playground_ws_connect_total{outcome}` and `lenny_playground_sessions_created_total{runtime}` increment.
- **Gap:** Two of the five `reason` values and one of the six §27.8 metrics now have real increment coverage; the other three `reason` values (`user_logout`, `admin_revoke`, `oidc_session_ended`) and the remaining five metrics (`page_views_total`, `sessions_created_total`, `ws_connect_total`, `dev_tenant_not_seeded_total`, the propagation histogram's registered form) are still unasserted. The metric-emission wiring between those handler paths and the registered collectors remains untested at the component tier, so a regression in the bootstrap-window `dev_tenant_not_seeded` counter or the logout/admin-revoke reason attribution could still ship silently.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. Use `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground` with `NewMetrics` against a test registry and `testutil.ToFloat64` from `github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus/testutil`, following the pattern already established in `idle_sweep_test.go` and `user_invalidation_test.go`.
- **Suggested test:** Add `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/metrics_increment_test.go` that wires a full `NewMetrics` registry and drives the remaining paths (index GET, dev ready-gate 503, `POST /playground/auth/logout`, admin revoke, `oidc_session_ended`) against it, asserting each counter delta and label value with `testutil.ToFloat64`; extend `TestLogoutRevokesSessionBearer` to pass a real `*Metrics` instead of `nil` and assert `revocations{reason="user_logout"}`.

### - [ ] T-27.9.1 — No tier9 security test exercises the playground attack surface end to end [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The raw-frame inspector displays redacted frames only; the gateway applies the same redaction rules as the audit log … before sending frames to the browser." and "`frame-ancestors 'none'` prevents clickjacking." (spec/27_web-playground.md:254,232).
- **Existing tests:** A grep of `tests/tier9_security/` still returns no playground test; `live_session_test.go`, `network_policy_test.go`, and `credential_leakage_test.go` do not reference `/playground` or `origin=playground`. The CSP is asserted at the component tier (`TestSecurityHeadersAndCSP`) and tier3 (`TestPlaygroundResponsesCarryCSP`), and the bearer-token-in-`sessionStorage` and HttpOnly-cookie posture lives only in the SPA source `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/ui/app.js`. The frame-redaction guarantee itself has gained real unit and component coverage since generation: `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/playground_redact_internal_test.go` (`TestRedactPlaygroundFrameScrubsCredentialScalars_spec_27_9_251`, `TestRedactPlaygroundFramePreservesSchemaAndID_spec_27_9_251`, `TestPlaygroundEgressGate_spec_27_9_251`) injects credential-literal scalars at depth and in arrays and asserts they are scrubbed while structural schema fields and non-sensitive siblings survive, and `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/websocket_test.go` (`TestWebSocketPlaygroundEgressPreservesSchema_spec_27_9_251`, `TestWebSocketNonPlaygroundEgressUnredacted_spec_27_9_251`) drives the same gate over a live WebSocket handler keyed on the `origin=playground` claim. TESTING.md §14.12 states coverage "spans … Tier 9 (security)", but no such suite exists on disk.
- **Gap:** The credential-redaction logic and its origin-keyed gate are now exercised at tier1/tier2, closing the sharpest part of the original gap (no test injecting a secret-carrying frame). What remains unverified is the adversarial, browser-facing, and deployment-combination surface: no test asserts the CSP, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, and `Referrer-Policy` headers survive a real gateway-plus-Ingress path, and no test drives a full chat session whose runtime emits a secret-carrying frame and asserts the browser-delivered copy (as opposed to the in-process redactor call) is redacted. This is both a missing user journey (a security reviewer exercising the policy/audit pipeline via the UI, §27.1) and a missing deployment-combination test. The declared Tier 9 surface in TESTING.md §14.12 is absent.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5/tier9 Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind`) with the playground enabled on the e2e overlay, the audit-assertion helpers in `tests/testinfra/audit`, and the security helpers in `tests/testinfra/security`. The e2e overlay (`tests/testinfra/kind/e2e-values.yaml`) still does not enable the playground today (see T-27.9.4); enabling it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier9_security/playground_test.go` that enables the playground, drives a chat session whose runtime emits a frame containing a secret, asserts the browser-delivered raw-frame is redacted per §16.4, and asserts the CSP, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, and `Referrer-Policy` headers are present on `/playground/*` through the Ingress.

### - [ ] T-27.7.1 — CSP component test pins only a subset of directives; no byte-exact or external-schema conformance [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** The §27.7 CSP block lists `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; connect-src 'self' wss://<gateway-host>; img-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; media-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'` (spec/27_web-playground.md:218-228).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/playground_test.go::TestSecurityHeadersAndCSP` asserts `default-src`, `script-src`, `object-src`, `media-src`, `frame-ancestors`, and the `wss://` host. The tier3 `TestPlaygroundResponsesCarryCSP` asserts only `frame-ancestors 'none'` and `object-src 'none'`. Neither asserts `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`, `img-src 'self' data:`, `base-uri 'self'`, or `form-action 'self'`, and neither pins the full directive string or validates against an external CSP grammar.
- **Gap:** Four directives the spec calls out explicitly are unverified, so dropping `base-uri 'self'` or `form-action 'self'` (both relevant to injection defense) would not fail any test. There is no conformance check that the header parses as a valid Level-3 CSP. The work is a standards-conformance hardening of the existing component and contract tests.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Strengthen `TestSecurityHeadersAndCSP` to assert every directive in the spec block, and add a tier3 case in `tests/tier3_contract/playground/playground_test.go` that parses the header into directive→source-list pairs and compares the full set against the spec, rejecting any extra or missing directive.

### - [ ] T-27.7.2 — Asset cache-header behavior is not verified end to end through a real Ingress on Kind [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Static assets … are served from the embedded FS with long cache headers (`Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`). `index.html` is served with `Cache-Control: no-store` so new releases propagate immediately." (spec/27_web-playground.md:213).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/playground_test.go::TestStaticAssetCacheHeaders` asserts the immutable header on `app.js` and `TestSecurityHeadersAndCSP` asserts `no-store` on the index, both via `httptest`. No tier5 test confirms the differentiated cache headers and the `index.html` no-store behavior survive a real gateway behind the chart Ingress, where an intermediary or the embedded-FS handler ordering could change them. No test exercises the SPA-fallback path (an unknown route serving `index.html` with `no-store` rather than the immutable header).
- **Gap:** The roll-forward correctness guarantee (a new release propagates because `index.html` is `no-store` while hashed bundles stay cacheable) is only unit-verified. The SPA-fallback content-type and cache behavior for an arbitrary client-side route is untested. This is a deployment-combination gap (real Ingress) plus a missing edge case.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness with the playground enabled (see T-27.9.4); none beyond that.
- **Suggested test:** Add a case to `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/` (a new `playground_assets_test.go`) that GETs `/playground/`, a hashed bundle, and an unknown client-side route through the Ingress and asserts the `Cache-Control` and `Content-Type` for each.

### - [ ] T-27.9.2 — The apiKey-mode yellow banner is not asserted; only the dev-mode banner is tested [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "When `playground.authMode=apiKey`, the playground UI renders a persistent, server-sourced yellow banner 'API KEY MODE — paste only operator-issued tokens' … The banner text is emitted by the gateway (not the embedded bundle), so swapping or patching the asset bundle does not suppress it." (spec/27_web-playground.md:257).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/playground_test.go::TestConfigJSONCarriesDevBanner` builds the handler in dev mode and asserts the dev banner and `bannerSeverity: "danger"`. `assets.go::handleConfigJSON` emits the apiKey banner with `bannerSeverity: "warning"`, but no test builds the handler in apiKey mode and asserts that `config.json` carries the yellow-banner text and severity. The install-time preflight WARNING for the same posture is now covered separately (`pkg/preflight/playground_test.go::TestCheckPlaygroundAPIKeyModeWarning_F_27_9_2` and siblings), but that exercises the `lenny-preflight` acknowledgement row, not the SPA-facing `config.json` banner this finding targets.
- **Gap:** The server-sourced apiKey warning, the user-visible counterpart to the documented paste-form phishing surface, is unverified. A regression that drops or mislabels the apiKey banner (which is the install's only in-UI signal of the phishing posture) would not fail any test. The work is a component-level assertion mirroring the dev-banner test.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Add `TestConfigJSONCarriesAPIKeyBanner` in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/playground_test.go` that builds the handler with `AuthMode: AuthModeAPIKey`, GETs `/playground/config.json`, and asserts `banner == "API KEY MODE — paste only operator-issued tokens"` and `bannerSeverity == "warning"`.

### - [ ] T-27.10.1 — The normative roll-forward claim about in-flight sessions is untested and the spec-map exempts it as non-executable [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "disabling `playground.enabled` is safe at any time and has no effect on in-flight non-playground sessions. Playground-initiated sessions already in flight continue to run to completion or their configured cap; only new playground sessions are blocked." (spec/27_web-playground.md:265). The §27.2 gating row states `playground.enabled=false` makes `/playground/*` return `404` and unmounts the bundle (spec/27_web-playground.md:33).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/spec-map-exceptions.yaml:59-61` still exempts §27.10 with the justification "Forward-compatibility guidance, no executable behavior." That justification is inaccurate: the paragraph asserts a testable behavior. No test on disk disables `playground.enabled` and asserts that an in-flight playground-origin session and a concurrent non-playground session both continue while new `/playground/*` requests return `404`.
- **Gap:** A spec-versus-test-map inconsistency that would let a regression ship: toggling the flag could break in-flight sessions or fail to return `404` for new requests and no test would catch it. The work is a real user journey (an operator disables the playground while a session is live) plus the roll-forward correctness assertion. The exception entry should be replaced with a real test rather than left as a blanket exemption.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier4 compose stack (`tests/testinfra/gateway`, `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`) able to flip `playground.enabled` between two gateway configurations while a session is live, or the tier5 Kind harness for a true rolling reconfiguration.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier4_integration/playground_rollforward_test.go` that starts the gateway with the playground enabled, opens a playground-origin session and a non-playground session, reconfigures with `playground.enabled=false`, and asserts both sessions still run while `GET /playground/` returns `404`.

### - [ ] T-27.3.10 — Cross-replica revocation is verified only against miniredis, never on real Redis HA or a multi-replica gateway, and the declared load suite is skipped [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "a revocation published on any replica MUST be visible to the per-request revocation check on every other replica within 500 ms at P99 under nominal Redis health" and "The revocation check fails closed: when Redis is unreachable … rejected with `503 REDIS_UNAVAILABLE`." (spec/27_web-playground.md:98-99).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/cross_replica_test.go::TestPlaygroundSessionRevocationCrossReplica_spec_27_3_1_98` covers the pre-delivery (authoritative Redis GET) and post-delivery (pub/sub-warmed cache) cases using two stores over one `miniredis`. `pkg/gateway/middleware/auth/playground_revocation_test.go::TestPlaygroundBearerFailsClosedOnStoreError_spec_27_3_1_97` covers the fail-closed `503`. The declared tier7 load suite `playground_revocation` (TESTING.md:1186, P99 ≤ 500 ms) is a `t.Skip` in `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go:443` because "the §27 playground is disabled on the e2e gateway."
- **Gap:** The 500 ms propagation SLO and the fail-closed posture are never measured against real Redis, a real pub/sub fanout, or two real gateway replicas. The miniredis tests model the logic but cannot validate latency, the resubscribe-on-dropped-subscription path (`outcome="resubscribe"`), or behavior during a Redis HA failover. This is a deployment-combination gap (HA multi-replica gateway plus Redis HA and outage) and an unimplemented declared load suite. The fail-open-versus-fail-closed Redis-outage dimension and the Redis-HA-failover dimension are both unexercised.
- **Dependencies:** Requires enabling the playground on the tier5/tier7 Kind overlay (see T-27.9.4), the `tests/testinfra/loadgen` k6 harness for the `playground_revocation` scenario, the `tests/testinfra/chaos` fault injector for the Redis-outage and failover cases, and a multi-replica gateway deployment.
- **Suggested test:** Implement the skipped `TestPlaygroundRevocation` in `tests/tier7b_load_kind/` against a two-replica gateway with real Redis, asserting P99 propagation ≤ 500 ms; add a tier8 chaos case in `tests/tier8_chaos/` that drops Redis mid-flight and asserts `503 REDIS_UNAVAILABLE` (fail closed) and recovery on Redis return.

### - [ ] T-27.9.3 — The "Copy as client SDK snippet" credential-omission guarantee has no test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The 'Copy as client SDK snippet' feature generates code that never includes credentials; snippets reference environment variables / OIDC flow only." (spec/27_web-playground.md:259).
- **Existing tests:** A grep for the snippet feature finds only the SPA source `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/ui/app.js`, `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/runtime_visible_test.go` (unrelated runtime-visibility logic), and `tests/tier11_docs/code_blocks_test.go` (doc code-block linting). No test asserts that the generated Go, Python, or TypeScript snippet omits the bearer token and references only environment variables or the OIDC flow.
- **Gap:** A security-relevant guarantee (the demo UI must not paste a live credential into copyable code) is unverified. If the snippet generator interpolated the live bearer, a user would copy a credential into source. The work is an adversarial assertion that the snippet for each language contains no token material. Because the generation may be client-side only, this is a UI-level test gap.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a UI-level test harness for the SPA snippet generator (jsdom or a Playwright/vitest setup under `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/ui/`), which does not exist today; building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add a UI unit/component test under `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/ui/` that invokes the snippet generator with a live bearer in client state for each of Go/Python/TS and asserts the output contains no bearer substring and references an env-var or the OIDC login flow.

### - [ ] T-27.7.3 — No test asserts the chart wires the gateway-host into the playground CSP `connect-src` [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`connect-src 'self' wss://<gateway-host>`" so the SPA can open the MCP WebSocket (spec/27_web-playground.md:221); `contentSecurityPolicy` appends `wss://` + `h.cfg.GatewayHost` only when set (pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/assets.go:191-194).
- **Existing tests:** `TestSecurityHeadersAndCSP` passes `GatewayHost: "gw.example.com"` directly to the handler and asserts `wss://gw.example.com` appears. `charts/lenny/tests/gateway-deployment_test.yaml` asserts the `--playground-*` flags render but does not assert a gateway-host flag flows into the CSP `connect-src`, and a grep of that file for `Content-Security`/`gateway-host` finds nothing.
- **Gap:** The chart-to-gateway wiring for the CSP host is untested, so a misrendered or empty gateway-host value (which would drop `wss://` from `connect-src` and break the WebSocket while leaving the page loadable) would not fail a helm unit test. This is a low-risk deployment-wiring edge case. There is also no test for the empty-`GatewayHost` branch where `connect-src` is `'self'` only.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today (helm unit test plus a component-test case).
- **Suggested test:** Add a helm unit case in `charts/lenny/tests/gateway-deployment_test.yaml` asserting the gateway-host value renders into the playground configuration, and a component case asserting `contentSecurityPolicy` with an empty `GatewayHost` emits `connect-src 'self'` without a trailing `wss://`.

### - [ ] T-27.7.4 — The X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy headers are not asserted on non-HTML asset responses [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The gateway also sets `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Referrer-Policy: same-origin` on all playground responses." (spec/27_web-playground.md:232).
- **Existing tests:** `TestSecurityHeadersAndCSP` asserts both headers on `GET /playground/` (the index) and `TestPlaygroundResponsesCarryCSP` asserts them on the same index route. `TestStaticAssetCacheHeaders` fetches `app.js` but asserts only the cache header, not `nosniff` or the referrer policy, and no test asserts these headers on `config.json` or the OIDC error page.
- **Gap:** The "all playground responses" scope is verified only for the index, so a regression that applied the security headers solely to the HTML handler (and not to JS/CSS/JSON asset responses, where `nosniff` is most load-bearing) would pass. This is a single missing-assertion edge case.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `TestStaticAssetCacheHeaders` and the `config.json` test in `pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/playground/playground_test.go` to also assert `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Referrer-Policy: same-origin` on the asset and config responses.

### - [ ] T-27.8.3 — Coverage relocation note: §27.8 propagation-histogram logic lives under §27.6 test ids, not §27.8 [Info] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`lenny_playground_session_revocation_propagation_seconds` … P99 alert threshold is the 500 ms logout propagation SLO." (spec/27_web-playground.md:244).

The spec-map §27.8 entry does not reference this file at all; it points only at the unrelated catalog test.
