## Docs — Getting Started (quickstart, concepts, architecture) <a id="t-doc-getting-started"></a>
**Source:** `docs/getting-started/`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The Getting Started area documents the first-run journey through `lenny up`, an offline chat session, a coding-agent session, the web playground, and teardown, plus concept and architecture pages. The distinctive surface is the embedded-stack quickstart, and that exact path has no executing test: the only doc-gate test (`tests/tier11_docs/time_to_hello_world_test.go`) checks CLI argument dispatch and explicitly defers the live bring-up to a "tier-7 tthw benchmark" that does not exist, and the tier7b `TestTimeToHelloWorld` it points at is an unconditional `t.Skip` scaffold. TESTING.md §12.11 #9 declares the Getting Started docs "execute end-to-end against a fresh clone" and TESTING.md line 1819 cites a `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/tthw.go` file that is absent, so the declared coverage is overstated in three places. The concept and architecture mechanism claims (session state machine, default-deny NetworkPolicy, LLM proxy, RLS) carry real coverage in other domains' tiers, and markdown link integrity for these pages is covered by the static link-check script, so the gaps concentrate on the embedded-stack user journey and the reference-runtime session rather than the underlying mechanisms. Counts: 2 High, 3 Medium, 1 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-DOC-GS.1 — The end-to-end quickstart journey (lenny up → chat session → teardown) has no executing test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "install Lenny on your laptop, chat with an agent, and shut it down -- in under five minutes." and the six-step flow `lenny up` → `lenny session new --runtime chat` → `lenny session send` → coding agent → playground → `lenny down` (docs/getting-started/quickstart.md:10-152). TESTING.md §12.11 check #9 makes this an obligation: "Onboarding docs (`README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/getting-started/`) execute end-to-end against a fresh clone." (TESTING.md:1340).
- **Existing tests:** tests/tier11_docs/time_to_hello_world_test.go::TestTimeToHelloWorld is the §22.7 documentation gate. It builds `cmd/lenny` and asserts only that `lenny up` and `lenny session new` are recognized commands with the documented flags; step_2_lenny_up states "the end-to-end bring-up is covered by the tier-7 tthw load-tier benchmark" (lines 117-121) and step_3 / step_4 defer the live session and the five-minute wall-clock to the same benchmark. The embedded-stack packages under pkg/embedded/{stack,localcli,k3s,postgres,redis} have unit tests only (for example pkg/embedded/stack/lifecycle_test.go exercises `RunDown` against a temp `LENNY_HOME`, never `RunUp`). No tier2, tier4, or tier5 test brings up a real embedded stack and drives a session through it. Searched tiers: tier2_component, tier4_integration, tier5_e2e_kind, tier7a_load_local, tier7b_load_kind, and pkg/embedded/**.
- **Gap:** The central first-run user journey a fresh operator follows is unverified end to end. No test starts the embedded stack with `lenny up`, opens a chat session, sends a follow-up, and tears the stack down with `lenny down`. This is a real user-journey gap (the persona alice running the quickstart) at the integration and e2e tiers, and it is the behavior TESTING.md §12.11 #9 and §22.7 declare to be tested.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a host with Docker/containerd for k3s plus an embedded-stack test harness that invokes `pkg/embedded/stack.RunUp` and tears down with `RunDown`. No such harness exists today; building the install-replay harness (the missing piece named at tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go:424-428) is part of this finding. The tier5 Kind harness (tests/testinfra/kind) installs the Helm chart in dev mode, which is a different path from the embedded `lenny up` single binary, so it cannot stand in for this journey.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier5_e2e_kind/embedded_quickstart_test.go (or a gated tier7b tthw scenario at tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/tthw/main.go) that runs `lenny up`, creates a `chat` session via `lenny session new`, sends a follow-up with `lenny session send`, asserts a non-empty assistant reply within the five-minute budget, then runs `lenny down --purge` and asserts the stack is gone, reusing tests/testinfra building blocks where the embedded path overlaps the dev-mode gateway driver.

### - [ ] T-DOC-GS.2 — TESTING.md and the tier11 gate cite a tthw benchmark that does not exist; the tier7b TTHW test is an unconditional skip [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`time-to-hello-world` benchmark under `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/tthw.go` confirms the < 5-minute target." (TESTING.md:1819) and "The `time-to-hello-world` sequence works: `brew install`, `lenny up`, `lenny session start` against the bundled `chat` runtime, terminate within five minutes total wall-clock." (TESTING.md:2100). The quickstart this gates is docs/getting-started/quickstart.md.
- **Existing tests:** No file `tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/tthw.go` exists; the only scenario under tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/ is `startup_latency`. tests/tier7b_load_kind/scaffolds_test.go::TestTimeToHelloWorld (line 429) is an unconditional `t.Skip` whose own comment reads "the §17a TTHW install-replay harness does not exist, so the time-to-hello-world scenario has nothing to measure on the current build" (lines 432-433). tests/groups.yaml:414 wires a `subset: tthw` into the phase-17a-gate, and tests/tier11_docs/time_to_hello_world_test.go points at this benchmark repeatedly (lines 117-121, 132-134, 163-165) as the place the live flow is covered.
- **Gap:** This is a spec-versus-test inconsistency that lets a regression ship. Three artifacts (TESTING.md line 1819, the tier11 doc-gate comments, the phase-17a gate subset) assert the quickstart bring-up is covered by a benchmark that is a skip scaffold, so a break in `lenny up`, the `chat` session path, or `lenny down` would pass every gate. The declared suite is an empty scaffold, and the file path cited in TESTING.md is absent.
- **Dependencies:** Resolving the inconsistency requires either building the tthw install-replay benchmark (shares the dependency in T-DOC-GS.1: a Docker/containerd host and the embedded-stack harness) or correcting TESTING.md and the tier11 comments to stop claiming coverage. The benchmark build is buildable once the embedded-stack harness from T-DOC-GS.1 lands; the documentation correction is buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Implement tests/tier7b_load_kind/scenarios/tthw/main.go as the install-replay benchmark TESTING.md:1819 names, registered as the `tthw` subset, measuring wall-clock from a fresh deploy to a successful `chat` session; until it lands, update TESTING.md:1819 and the deferral comments in tests/tier11_docs/time_to_hello_world_test.go to name the skip rather than assert coverage, and add a tier0 check that fails when TESTING.md cites a scenario path absent on disk.

### - [ ] T-DOC-GS.3 — The chat reference-runtime session and the embedded mock-LLM deterministic-reply path are unverified above unit tier [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Start a session with the built-in `chat` runtime. It's a plain LLM chat, no tools -- the simplest useful agent. No API keys needed; the embedded stack ships with a mock provider that returns deterministic replies." (docs/getting-started/quickstart.md:62-63), with the seeded catalog listing `chat` among the nine reference runtimes (quickstart.md:48-49).
- **Existing tests:** pkg/embedded/stack/catalog_test.go asserts the seeded catalog contains the nine runtime names including `chat` (lines 15-16), and pkg/embedded/stack/bootstrap_seed_admin_test.go checks stored runtime fields. tests/testinfra/stubs/llmprovider/llmprovider_test.go exercises a stub LLM provider in isolation. Integration and e2e session tests drive the echo family and `streaming-echo` (the runtime names appearing in tests/tier4_integration and tests/tier5_e2e_kind), not `chat`. No test runs a session against the `chat` runtime, and no test verifies that the embedded stack wires a mock provider so a `chat` session returns a deterministic reply with no API key. Searched tiers: tier2_component, tier3_contract, tier4_integration, tier5_e2e_kind.
- **Gap:** The quickstart's centerpiece (the first message a new operator sends) depends on the `chat` runtime resolving from the seeded catalog and on the embedded mock provider returning a reply offline. The catalog entry points at `ghcr.io/lennylabs/runtime-chat:1.0.0` (pkg/embedded/stack/catalog.go:171), an external image, and neither the image resolution nor the deterministic-reply contract is exercised. This is a real user-journey gap and a deployment-combination gap (embedded mock-LLM mode).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the embedded-stack harness from T-DOC-GS.1 plus the published `runtime-chat` image (or a local stand-in registered under the `chat` name). The image is an external artifact not built in this repo; standing up a local `chat`-named stub runtime in tests/testinfra/stubs is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier4 or tier5 case (for example tests/tier5_e2e_kind/embedded_chat_session_test.go) that creates a session with `--runtime chat` against the embedded stack with no API key set and asserts the assistant reply is the documented deterministic mock output, using tests/testinfra/stubs/llmprovider as the deterministic backend wired into the embedded gateway.

### - [ ] T-DOC-GS.4 — Embedded-stack bring-up (RunUp / k3s + Postgres + Redis + gateway) and cmd/lenny-dev have no component or integration coverage [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`lenny up`, a single binary that runs the whole platform on your machine: an embedded Kubernetes cluster, the database and cache it needs, a stand-in key-management service and identity provider for development, the gateway, the management plane, and the nine reference runtimes." (docs/getting-started/quickstart.md:12), with the success banner enumerating each subsystem coming ready (quickstart.md:41-52).
- **Existing tests:** The bring-up entry points exist at pkg/embedded/stack/lifecycle.go:40 (`RunUp`) and pkg/embedded/stack/stack.go:97 (`Up`), but no test calls either. pkg/embedded/stack tests assert argument/env construction (gateway_test.go), down/purge state handling (lifecycle_test.go), and `ps` parsing (resource_usage_test.go); pkg/embedded/{k3s,postgres,redis} tests carry no build tag and do not start real backends. spec-map.json §17.4 ("Local Development Mode (lenny-dev)") lists only tests/tier11_docs/time_to_hello_world_test.go and the package cmd/lenny-dev, which has no `_test.go` files at all (verified under cmd/lenny-dev). Searched: pkg/embedded/**, cmd/lenny-dev, tier2_component, tier4_integration.
- **Gap:** The assertion that `lenny up` brings each subsystem to a ready state is verified only by unit-level fakes. No tier2 component test starts the embedded k3s, Postgres, Redis, KMS, and OIDC stand-ins together and confirms the readiness sequence the banner prints, and the `cmd/lenny-dev` binary that spec-map §17.4 ties this surface to is untested. This is a failure-path and happy-path gap at the component tier for the embedded topology.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a Docker/containerd host for the embedded k3s plus a component harness that drives `RunUp` to readiness and then `RunDown`. No such harness exists; it can be built on the same foundation as T-DOC-GS.1. Until a host with containerd is available the test gates on that tool being present, in the style of tests/testinfra/kind.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier2_component/embedded/stack_bringup_test.go that calls `stack.Up`, polls each subsystem's readiness signal (cluster, database, cache, KMS, OIDC, gateway, management plane), asserts the nine runtimes are seeded, and then calls `RunDown`, plus a smoke test for cmd/lenny-dev that asserts the embedded dev entry point starts and stops cleanly.

### - [ ] T-DOC-GS.5 — The coding-agent quickstart journey (workspace upload → gVisor sandbox → artifact download) is unexercised through the embedded path [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Each one wraps its respective CLI inside a gVisor sandbox with a fresh workspace prepared from a directory you give it. ... The gateway copies your repo into the pod's workspace, starts the agent, and streams its output back. Anything the agent writes into its output directory is downloadable as an artifact after the session ends." (docs/getting-started/quickstart.md:103-112).
- **Existing tests:** tests/tier4_integration covers session lifecycle and workspace source modes against the compose stack with the echo family (for example source_mode_smoke_test.go), and tests/tier5_e2e_kind covers pod lifecycle and the gateway probe on Kind. No test drives the documented coding-agent journey end to end: pass `--workspace ./repo` to a session, run under the gVisor isolation profile, and download the produced artifact after the session reaches a terminal state. The `claude-code` references in tier4/tier5 are catalog and policy fixtures, not a running coding agent. Searched: tier3_contract (artifact/download), tier4_integration, tier5_e2e_kind.
- **Gap:** The quickstart promises a workspace round-trip (local directory in, artifact out) under the default gVisor profile, and that combination is not exercised as a single journey. This is a real user-journey gap and a deployment-combination gap (the `sandboxed`/gVisor isolation profile that quickstart.md:182 and concepts.md:248 name as the default).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness (tests/testinfra/kind, tests/testinfra/sessiondriver) and a node configured with the gVisor RuntimeClass; for the embedded variant it also depends on the harness from T-DOC-GS.1. The gVisor RuntimeClass on the Kind node is the missing infrastructure and is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier5_e2e_kind/coding_agent_workspace_roundtrip_test.go that uploads a workspace, starts a session on a gVisor-profile pool, lets a runtime write to its output directory, terminates the session, and downloads the sealed artifact, asserting the uploaded files materialized and the produced artifact is retrievable, driven through tests/testinfra/sessiondriver.

### - [ ] T-DOC-GS.6 — The web playground browser journey (pick runtime, upload workspace, chat) has only a gateway-side auth contract test [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The playground is a small web UI that lets you pick a runtime, upload a workspace, and chat with a session ... It uses the same public API the CLI and SDKs use. On the embedded stack it runs open with a red \"not for production\" banner." (docs/getting-started/quickstart.md:125-127).
- **Existing tests:** tests/tier3_contract/playground/playground_test.go drives the gateway-side token-mint, the playground-minted JWT being honored by the public sessions API, and the CSP header (TestDevModeMintReturnsBearer, TestPlaygroundJWTAcceptedByPublicSessionsAPI, TestPlaygroundResponsesCarryCSP). Its header states "No browser is involved." pkg/gateway/sessionserver/playground_create_test.go and pkg/gateway/sessionserver/playground_runtime_visible_test.go cover server-side visibility. No test exercises the documented browser journey (select a runtime, upload a workspace, chat) or asserts the "not for production" banner renders on the embedded stack.
- **Gap:** The auth and protocol contract for the playground is covered, but the user-facing browser journey the quickstart describes is not. This is a missing real user-journey test for the playground UI and a missing assertion that the embedded-mode banner is present.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a headless-browser driver (Playwright or chromedp) plus the embedded or dev-mode gateway. No browser-driver building block exists under tests/testinfra today; adding one is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add a browser-driven tier5 test (for example tests/tier5_e2e_kind/playground_journey_test.go) that loads `/playground`, asserts the "not for production" banner, selects the `chat` runtime, uploads a small workspace, sends a message, and asserts a streamed reply, with a new headless-browser helper under tests/testinfra.

### - [ ] T-DOC-GS.7 — Concept and architecture mechanism claims and markdown link integrity are covered in adjacent tiers [Info] — OPEN

Markdown link integrity for docs/getting-started is covered by scripts/check-markdown-links.sh (the static-tier link check, which rewrites `.html` cross-links to `.md` via .markdown-link-check.json), and code-block syntax by tests/tier11_docs/code_blocks_test.go, which walks docs/ including these pages.

## Docs — Client Guide (REST, MCP, OpenAI, Responses) <a id="t-doc-client-guide"></a>
**Source:** `docs/client-guide/`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The Client Guide documents four interchangeable client protocols (REST, MCP over Streamable HTTP, OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Open Responses) plus webhooks, streaming, delegation, authentication, and error handling. REST has strong contract coverage (`tests/tier3_contract/rest_sessions`, `rest_auth`, `oauth_token`, `rest_idempotency`) and one cloud e2e path (`tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/session_lifecycle_test.go`). The OpenAI Chat Completions and Open Responses surfaces are covered only by in-process non-streaming fidelity tests in `tests/tier3_contract/rest_openai_chat` and `rest_openai_responses`, plus unit-level streaming substring checks; neither surface is driven by any conformance, integration, or end-to-end test, and the OpenAI/Anthropic fidelity matrix lives in `tests/tier10_conformance/scaffolds_test.go` while the rest of tier 10 is an explicit scaffold. The MCP client surface documented across `mcp-sdk.md` and `streaming.md` is exercised only by a one-line `initialize` smoke check at tier 4 and by `pkg/gateway/mcp` unit tests; no test drives the documented MCP tool lifecycle (`create_and_start_session`, `attach_session`, `send_message`, elicitation callback) over the real Streamable HTTP transport. The OWASP ZAP adversarial sweep against the REST and MCP surfaces is a deferred release-pipeline stub, so the guide's malformed-client paths are unverified end to end. Counts: 4 High, 5 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-DOC-CLI.1 — OpenAI Chat Completions and Open Responses surfaces have no integration or end-to-end coverage in any deployment combination [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Accepts the OpenAI Chat Completions wire format. Point your `openai` client at Lenny's base URL and each Lenny runtime shows up as a model (via `GET /v1/models`). Streaming works the same way it does against OpenAI." and "Accepts the OpenAI Responses API wire format and supports clients that target the Open Responses specification." (docs/client-guide/index.md:82, docs/client-guide/index.md:86)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier3_contract/rest_openai_chat/scaffolds_test.go` and `tests/tier3_contract/rest_openai_responses/scaffolds_test.go` drive the translators in-process against `memstore` and `EchoExecutor` for the non-streaming fidelity matrix only. `pkg/gateway/translator/openai_chat_test.go` and `open_responses_test.go` cover the surfaces at unit tier. `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/session_lifecycle_test.go` exercises REST only; `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/lifecycle_test.go` exercises ops and bootstrap only. No tier4 (`tests/tier4_integration`) or tier5/tier6 e2e test sends an OpenAI-format request through the running gateway, and the `/v1/models` happy path is verified only at contract tier (`tests/tier3_contract/rest_sessions/unexercised_endpoints_test.go::TestListModelsReturnsList`).
- **Gap:** Two of the four documented client protocols are never exercised against a real gateway process backed by real stores, so a regression in routing, auth, runtime resolution, or the model listing on these surfaces would ship. This is a real user journey (alice points the OpenAI SDK at the gateway and completes a chat) and a deployment-combination gap (the surfaces are only ever driven in the in-process httptest combination).
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The tier4 compose harness used by `gateway_full_e2e_test.go` and the `tests/testinfra/stubs/llmprovider` stub already exist.
- **Suggested test:** Add tier4 `tests/tier4_integration/openai_surfaces_e2e_test.go` that drives `POST /v1/chat/completions` and `POST /v1/responses` plus `GET /v1/models` against `cmd/lenny-gateway` on the compose stack, asserting a runtime appears as a model and a non-streaming completion round-trips; extend `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/session_lifecycle_test.go` with one OpenAI-format completion per provider.

### - [ ] T-DOC-CLI.2 — Streaming envelope for the OpenAI Chat Completions and Open Responses surfaces has no contract or conformance test against the external schema [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Streaming works the same way it does against OpenAI." (docs/client-guide/index.md:82) and the wire-format table mapping `OpenAI Chat Completions` and `Open Responses` responses to `application/json` or `text/event-stream` (docs/client-guide/wire-format.md:37, docs/client-guide/wire-format.md:38). TESTING.md §12.3 requires "streaming envelope semantics" as a canonical contract-tier check for each surface (TESTING.md:1916).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/translator/openai_chat_test.go::TestOpenAIChatStreamEmitsSSEChunks` and `open_responses_test.go::TestOpenResponsesStreamEmitsTypedEvents` assert SSE chunks at unit tier with substring matches (`assistant role delta`, `[DONE]`, `event: response.created`). The tier3 contract suites (`rest_openai_chat/scaffolds_test.go`, `rest_openai_responses/scaffolds_test.go`) post only `simple/request.json` and never set `stream:true`. A `streaming/events.sse` fixture exists for OpenAI Chat under `tests/testdata/openai_chat/streaming/` but is consumed only by the §4.9 outbound-proxy test `tests/tier2_component/translators/openai_chat_translator_test.go`, not by the inbound client-surface contract. `tests/testdata/openai_responses/` has no streaming fixture at all.
- **Gap:** The streaming wire form of two public protocol surfaces is pinned only by in-process substring assertions, not against the external OpenAI `chat.completion.chunk` schema or the Open Responses typed-event sequence (`response.created`, `response.output_text.delta`, `response.completed`). A standards-conformance test pinning each emitted event against the external schema is required and absent.
- **Dependencies:** Requires an Open Responses streaming corpus under `tests/testdata/openai_responses/streaming/`; building it is part of this finding. The OpenAI Chat streaming corpus already exists.
- **Suggested test:** Add tier3 contract cases in `rest_openai_chat/scaffolds_test.go` and `rest_openai_responses/scaffolds_test.go` that post with `stream:true`, parse the SSE stream, and assert each frame validates against the pinned external-schema golden (using `tests/testinfra/golden`), including the `[DONE]` sentinel for Chat and the typed-event ordering for Responses.

### - [ ] T-DOC-CLI.3 — The MCP client lifecycle documented in the SDK guide is never exercised over the real Streamable HTTP transport [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "MCP sessions use Streamable HTTP: SSE for server-to-client events, POST for client-to-server messages. The gateway acts as an MCP server at the `/mcp` endpoint." (docs/client-guide/streaming.md:93) and the documented tool flow `create_and_start_session` -> `attach_session` -> `send_message` -> elicitation callback -> `terminate_session` (docs/client-guide/sdk-examples/mcp-sdk.md:701-760).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier4_integration/gateway_full_e2e_test.go::TestGatewayFullSurfaceE2E` posts a single `{"method":"initialize"}` to `/mcp` and asserts a non-empty result (gateway_full_e2e_test.go:194-204). `pkg/gateway/mcp/version_internal_test.go` and `mcp_test.go` cover version negotiation and `initialize` at unit tier. `tests/tier3_contract/rest_mcp_consistency/scaffolds_test.go` calls MCP tools over a single JSON-RPC POST, not the SSE-plus-POST Streamable HTTP transport, and several of its parity functions remain explicit no-parity acknowledgements by design (`TestRESTMCPElicitation`, `TestRESTMCPDelegation`, `TestRESTMCPWebhookSubscription`).
- **Gap:** The documented interactive MCP journey (bidirectional streaming, attach, mid-session message, elicitation callback over Streamable HTTP) is never driven through the actual MCP SDK against a running gateway, so the SSE server-to-client channel and the `elicitation/create` callback the guide instructs clients to implement are unverified end to end. This is a real user journey (alice runs the `mcp-sdk.md` TypeScript example) and a protocol-conformance gap for the Streamable HTTP transport.
- **Dependencies:** Requires an MCP Streamable HTTP client harness in `tests/testinfra` (none exists today; `sdkhelper` covers the REST SDK only). Building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tier4 `tests/tier4_integration/mcp_streamable_lifecycle_test.go` that opens the SSE channel, runs `create_and_start_session` -> `attach_session` -> `send_message` against `cmd/lenny-gateway` with the `streaming-echo` runtime, and asserts streamed `agent_output` plus `session_complete`; reference `tests/testinfra/gateway` and a new MCP client building block.

### - [ ] T-DOC-CLI.4 — Tier 10 conformance and the OpenAI/Anthropic fidelity matrix the guide depends on ship as an explicit scaffold [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "When this page and the spec disagree, the spec wins." with the wire format declared the source of truth SDK examples and tests cite (docs/client-guide/wire-format.md:13), and the OutputPart type registry the OpenAI and Responses adapters translate (docs/client-guide/wire-format.md:136-153, docs/client-guide/streaming.md:72-87). TESTING.md §12.10 requires the fidelity matrix and the per-runtime conformance battery (TESTING.md:1323).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier10_conformance/scaffolds_test.go` is still present alongside `concurrent_slot_conformance_test.go` and `recycle_scrub_conformance_test.go`, but no `fidelity_matrix_test.go` exists; its README states "The suite is a placeholder" and `TestReferenceCatalogNightly`, `TestThirdPartyRegistration`, and `TestFidelityMatrix` are documented as blocked. `TestFidelityMatrix` does run a table sweep over `pkg/gateway/outputpartfidelity` for the OpenAI Completions and Open Responses adapters, but it is gated behind `//go:build conformance` and asserts only `[dropped]`, `[exact]`, and `[extended]` cells; `[lossy]` cells are explicitly skipped in `assertFieldMatrix`. The nine reference runtimes are catalog-checked structurally only (the image-pull arm requires `LENNY_REFERENCE_IMAGE_REGISTRY`).
- **Gap:** The documented translation behavior for the public OpenAI and Responses surfaces (which fields survive, which are dropped, which degrade) is verified only against an internal `outputpartfidelity` table and never against the runtime adapters end to end, and the `[lossy]` degradations the guide implies (for example `reasoning_trace`) are unasserted. A spec-versus-test inconsistency here would let a translator regression ship under a green tier 3. This is a standards-conformance gap.
- **Dependencies:** The `[lossy]` per-cell assertions need the documented degradation goldens; the reference-catalog image-pull arm needs the §26 runtime OCI images published. Record both as missing infrastructure.
- **Suggested test:** Promote `TestFidelityMatrix` out of `scaffolds_test.go` into `tests/tier10_conformance/fidelity_matrix_test.go`, add per-cell `[lossy]` assertions for every canonical OutputPart type against the OpenAI Completions and Open Responses translators, and wire the reference-catalog conformance run for the nine runtimes once the images publish.

### - [ ] T-DOC-CLI.5 — Malformed-client adversarial paths across MCP and OpenAI surfaces are only covered by a deferred OWASP ZAP stub [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Unknown types MUST be preserved and forwarded verbatim by middleware; unprefixed custom types collapse to `text` with `annotations.originalType` set." (docs/client-guide/wire-format.md:153) and "parts above 50 MB are rejected at ingress with `413 OUTPUTPART_TOO_LARGE`." (docs/client-guide/wire-format.md:153). TESTING.md §12.9.6 runs OWASP ZAP against the REST and MCP surfaces with oversize payloads, malformed JSON, and deeply nested objects (TESTING.md:1276).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/translator/openai_chat_test.go::TestOpenAIChatRejectsMalformedJSON` and `RejectsEmptyMessages` cover malformed OpenAI Chat input at unit tier. `pkg/gateway/mcp` fuzz targets and `tests/testinfra/fuzz` cover the MCP envelope parser. `tests/tier9_security/scaffolds_test.go::TestInputFuzzingOWASPZAP` is a `t.Logf` stub stating the black-box ZAP run is a release-pipeline CI job, and `tests/testinfra/security/zap` is a runner with no in-tree target invocation against the live MCP or OpenAI endpoints.
- **Gap:** The documented ingress rejections (oversize OutputPart, unknown-type collapse, malformed JSON, deeply nested objects) are not exercised against the running gateway on the MCP or OpenAI surfaces as a security tier test; only the REST parsers and the OpenAI Chat unit path are covered. This is an adversarial-path gap for a documented MUST.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the ZAP black-box runner pointed at a live gateway target, plus malformed-client fixtures for the MCP and Responses surfaces. The runner exists; the live-target wiring and fixtures do not.
- **Suggested test:** Add tier9 `tests/tier9_security/malformed_client_test.go` driving oversize, deeply nested, and unknown-type payloads at `/mcp`, `/v1/chat/completions`, and `/v1/responses` against `cmd/lenny-gateway`, asserting `413 OUTPUTPART_TOO_LARGE`, the unknown-type collapse, and the documented validation envelope; reference `tests/testinfra/security/zap` and `tests/testinfra/gateway`.

### - [ ] T-DOC-CLI.6 — SSE reconnection, replay-window boundary, and bounded-error backpressure are only covered through the Go SDK [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "On reconnect, provide your last-seen cursor via the `Last-Event-ID` header or `?cursor=` query parameter ... If your cursor falls outside this window, the gateway sends a `checkpoint_boundary` event" (docs/client-guide/streaming.md:113-121) and "If the client's read loop falls behind and the buffer fills, the gateway closes the connection within 100ms" (docs/client-guide/streaming.md:146).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier3_contract/sdks/go_client_test.go::TestGoClientStreamingReconnect` forces a mid-stream disconnect and asserts zero gaps and zero duplicates across six events via `Last-Event-ID`. `pkg/gateway/sessionserver/events_test.go` and `pkg/gateway/events/ring_test.go` cover the SSE handler and ring buffer at unit tier. No test emits a `checkpoint_boundary` event with `events_lost > 0` against a running gateway, and the 100ms bounded-error connection close under a slow reader is not exercised at component or integration tier.
- **Gap:** The replay-window-exceeded path (the documented `checkpoint_boundary` with non-zero `events_lost`) and the backpressure close-within-100ms behavior are documented for every streaming client but verified by neither a real user-journey nor a failure-path test beyond the Go SDK happy reconnect. This is a partial-coverage finding (happy reconnect only) and a failure-path gap.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a `clockstep`-driven replay-window expiry and a throttled SSE reader in `tests/testinfra` (the `watchlag` building block is the closest existing primitive). Building the slow-reader harness is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tier4 `tests/tier4_integration/sse_replay_boundary_test.go` that advances the replay window past the client cursor and asserts a `checkpoint_boundary` event with `events_lost > 0`, plus a component test in `tests/tier2_component/gateway_subsystems` that stalls the reader and asserts the connection closes within the documented bound.

### - [ ] T-DOC-CLI.7 — Webhook delivery through the running gateway and undelivered-event retrieval have no integration test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "If your webhook endpoint is unreachable or returns a non-2xx status code, the gateway retries delivery with exponential backoff ... After all retry attempts are exhausted, the event is stored as an undelivered event." (docs/client-guide/webhooks.md:104-115) and "If webhook delivery fails after all retries, retrieve undelivered events via the API: `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/webhook-events`" (docs/client-guide/webhooks.md:121-124).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/session/sessioncallback/delivery_test.go` (`TestDispatcherDeliversSuccess_spec_14_114`, `TestDispatcherRetriesThenSucceeds_spec_14_150`, `TestDispatcherExhaustion_spec_14_150`) and `pkg/webhookdelivery/transport_test.go` cover delivery, retry schedule, signature, SSRF guard, and redirect refusal against an `httptest` receiver at unit tier. `tests/tier3_contract/cloudevents/cloudevents_test.go` pins the CloudEvents envelope. No tier4 or tier5 test creates a session with `callbackUrl`, lets it complete through the running gateway, verifies the `X-Lenny-Signature` at a real receiver, and then reads back `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/webhook-events`.
- **Gap:** The end-to-end async-job journey the webhooks page documents (alice creates a session with `callbackUrl`, the gateway fires the CloudEvent, alice verifies the signature and retrieves results) is verified only at the dispatcher-unit boundary; the wiring from session terminal-state to delivery and the undelivered-event retrieval endpoint are not exercised together against a running gateway. This is a real user journey gap.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a webhook receiver stub registered with the compose-stack gateway (none in `tests/testinfra/stubs` today). Building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tier4 `tests/tier4_integration/webhook_delivery_e2e_test.go` that starts `cmd/lenny-gateway`, posts `POST /v1/sessions/start` with `callbackUrl` and `callbackSecret` pointed at a receiver stub, asserts a valid `dev.lenny.session_completed` CloudEvent arrives with a verifying signature, then forces a delivery failure and asserts the event surfaces via `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/webhook-events`.

### - [ ] T-DOC-CLI.8 — Delegation credential-propagation modes (inherit, independent, deny) have no per-mode integration coverage [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The `credentialPropagation` field in the delegation lease controls how child sessions get LLM credentials. Three modes are available" with `inherit`, `independent`, and `deny` rows (docs/client-guide/delegation-and-tasks.md:299-305).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier4_integration/delegation_test.go::TestDelegation` exercises the spawn-and-tree contract and `tracingContext` propagation per §8.2/§8.3. `tests/tier4_integration/credential_test.go` covers the `/v1/credentials` register/list/rotate/revoke surface. No test drives a delegation with each of the three `credentialPropagation` modes and asserts the child's resulting credential source (same pool for `inherit`, an independent lease for `independent`, no lease for `deny`).
- **Gap:** The three documented credential-propagation behaviors a multi-agent client relies on are not each verified end to end; a regression where `deny` silently grants a lease, or `independent` reuses the parent pool, would ship. This is a partial-coverage finding (delegation happy path only) covering both a user journey (a `deny` child that processes files with no LLM access) and a security-relevant behavior.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The tier4 delegation harness and `tests/testinfra/stubs/llmprovider` already exist.
- **Suggested test:** Add tier4 `tests/tier4_integration/delegation_credential_propagation_test.go` parameterized over `inherit`, `independent`, and `deny`, asserting the child lease source matches the documented mode and that a `deny` child receives no proxy URL or lease token.

- **Spec/Doc:** "Delivery semantics vary by session state" with the `running` (tool call in flight) -> buffered, `suspended` -> inbox, `resume_pending` / `awaiting_client_action` -> dead-letter-queue rows (docs/client-guide/session-lifecycle.md:246-254), and the MCP SDK comment documenting `deliveryReceipt.status` of `delivered`, `queued`, and `dropped` (docs/client-guide/sdk-examples/mcp-sdk.md:377-381).

### - [ ] T-DOC-CLI.13 — Webhook-only clients cannot answer elicitations; the documented limitation is verified only indirectly [Info] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Webhook-only clients cannot respond to elicitations. Elicitations require an active SSE or MCP streaming connection because the gateway delivers `elicitation_request` events on the session's event stream and expects a synchronous response." (docs/client-guide/webhooks.md:155-157)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier4_integration/elicitation_test.go::TestMCPElicitationChain` drives the hop-by-hop chain with a REST respond, and `TestMCPProvenance` covers url-mode provenance controls. The webhook CloudEvents catalog (`tests/tier3_contract/cloudevents/cloudevents_test.go`) confirms no `elicitation_request` CloudEvents type is emitted (`TestCloudEventsEnvelopeShape`, `TestCloudEventsLennyExtensions`, `TestCloudEventsTenantPrefixedChannels`, `TestCloudEventsAuditBearingContentType`, `TestCloudEventsInlineOCSFWireForm`), which is the structural reason webhook-only clients cannot answer, but no test states this as the asserted contract.
- **Gap:** The coverage of this limitation is implicit (no elicitation CloudEvents type exists) rather than an explicit assertion, so the observation is that the negative contract holds by construction. No additional component or integration test is strictly required; a documentation-tier assertion that the CloudEvents catalog excludes `elicitation_request` would make the documented limitation self-checking.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Optionally add a tier3 assertion in `tests/tier3_contract/cloudevents/cloudevents_test.go` that the published CloudEvents type set contains no elicitation type, pinning the documented webhook-only limitation as an explicit contract.

## Docs — Operator Guide: Installation and Configuration <a id="t-doc-operator-install"></a>
**Source:** `docs/operator-guide/ (installation, install-wizard, configuration, krew-install, upgrades, lenny-ctl, ingress-and-tls)`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The install, configure, and upgrade documentation is backed by strong tier0/tier1 coverage: `cmd/lenny-ctl/install_test.go`, `install_detect_test.go`, `install_smoke_test.go`, and the `pkg/preflight/*_test.go` suite verify answer-file parsing, validation, values composition, detection, and every individual preflight check, and the `charts/lenny/tests/*.yaml` helm-unittest suites verify chart rendering for presets, webhooks, ingress, bootstrap, and the phase-stamp ConfigMap. Component and end-to-end coverage of the documented operator journeys is thin. The `lenny-ctl install` wizard and the answer-file replay path are exercised only with `--dry-run`, so no test runs the documented detection → preflight → `helm install` → bootstrap → smoke-test journey against a live cluster; the Kind harness (`tests/testinfra/kind/install.sh`) installs raw `helm` with a static values file and an echo workload instead. TESTING.md §14 declares `bootstrap_first_install` and `pool_upgrade` e2e suites and an `admin_bootstrap`/`migration_upgrade` integration suite that are absent on disk, leaving the documented bootstrap, pool-image-upgrade state machine, version-to-version upgrade, CRD-staleness recovery, and Helm rollback journeys with no live test. The cloud tier (tier6) install, upgrade, managed-backend, and workload-identity paths are entirely `planned` in `parity-matrix.yaml`. The embedded `lenny up` stack now has bring-up and local-only-enforcement coverage at tier2/tier4/tier9; the krew/`kubectl-lenny` invocation-name equivalence now has a dispatch-level test, leaving only the release-checksum half of that invariant open.
Counts: 4 High, 6 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info. Of these, 2 Medium (T-DOC-INST.9, T-DOC-INST.10) are now resolved.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-DOC-INST.1 — The `lenny-ctl install` wizard end-to-end journey is never run against a live cluster [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "After collecting the answers, the wizard validates them, prints the composed Helm values and the `helm install` command it will run, and then runs Helm." and "The wizard orchestrates the flow from Installation: cluster detection → question phase → preview → preflight → `helm install` → bootstrap seed → smoke test." (docs/operator-guide/install-wizard.md:53, docs/operator-guide/lenny-ctl.md:482)
- **Existing tests:** `cmd/lenny-ctl/install_test.go` exercises flag parsing, answer-file parsing, validation, and `composeValues`, but every `cmdInstall` test runs with `--dry-run` so `helm` is never invoked (for example `TestCmdInstallDryRunFromAnswerFile` install_test.go:620). `tests/tier11_docs/time_to_hello_world_test.go:300` runs `install --non-interactive --answers --dry-run` and explicitly defers the live install (`smoke_session_after_install` at line 369 logs that it "needs a live gateway from a real `helm install` (not the --dry-run path)"). The Kind harness `tests/testinfra/kind/install.sh:355` runs raw `helm install` with `e2e-values.yaml`, not the wizard. spec-map.json §24.20 (line 2716) and §17.9 (line 2417) point only at the `cmd/lenny-ctl/...` glob. No tier5 test drives `lenny-ctl install`.
- **Gap:** The production install journey a reader follows (the wizard composing values, layering the tier preset, running preflight, invoking `helm install`, seeding bootstrap, and running the smoke test) is a real user journey that no test exercises end to end. The target tier is tier5 (Kind). This is the canonical operator path and a regression in values composition, preset layering order, or the helm subprocess wiring would ship undetected.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness (tests/testinfra/kind). The harness must be extended to invoke `lenny-ctl install --non-interactive --answers <file>` against the Kind cluster instead of raw `helm install`; the `helm` and `kubectl` binaries and a built `lenny-ctl` image already exist in install.sh. No new external credentials are needed.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier5_e2e_kind/install_wizard_test.go that runs `lenny-ctl install --non-interactive --answers charts/lenny/answers/tier1-local.yaml` against the Kind cluster, then asserts the `lenny` Helm release reports `deployed`, the preset-derived replica counts match `values-tier1.yaml`, and the gateway becomes Ready, reusing `tests/testinfra/kind` for cluster access.

### - [ ] T-DOC-INST.2 — The declared `bootstrap_first_install` e2e suite is missing and no test runs the documented post-install smoke test against the chat runtime [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Fresh chart install with the default values produces a Ready gateway; smoke test against `chat` runtime succeeds within five minutes" (TESTING.md:1081) and "After `helm install` succeeds, the wizard runs a smoke test against the `chat` reference runtime. It polls the gateway `/healthz` endpoint for up to 120 seconds, then issues a `lenny/create_session` MCP round-trip when an admin token is available." (docs/operator-guide/install-wizard.md:212)
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/bootstrap_first_install_test.go` is named in TESTING.md §14 (line 1081, critical-path subset at line 1088) but does not exist on disk (verified by file lookup). `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/lifecycle_test.go` asserts the `lenny-ops` Deployment and the bootstrap hook Jobs ran, but does not create a session or run a smoke test. The wizard smoke-test orchestration is unit-tested with a stub gateway in `cmd/lenny-ctl/install_smoke_test.go` (`stubTester`, `TestRunSmokeTestSkipNoURL` at line 33); the MCP round-trip is never issued against a real gateway. `tests/tier4_integration/scaffolds_test.go:54` (`TestAdminBootstrap`) is a `t.Logf` scaffold, not a live bootstrap.
- **Gap:** The fresh-install-produces-a-working-session journey and the smoke-test `lenny/create_session` MCP round-trip are unverified end to end. The target tiers are tier5 (the declared `bootstrap_first_install` suite) and tier4 (the declared `admin_bootstrap` idempotency suite). This is the documented acceptance gate for an install and is a real user journey.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness (tests/testinfra/kind) and the `chat` reference runtime image; the chat runtime is deferred per spec-map-exceptions §26.7, so the smoke test can run against a seeded echo runtime in the interim with a follow-up to swap in `chat`. The sessiondriver harness (tests/testinfra/sessiondriver) drives the MCP round-trip.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier5_e2e_kind/bootstrap_first_install_test.go that installs the chart with default values, waits for the gateway Ready, retrieves the `lenny-admin-token` Secret, and issues a `lenny/create_session` MCP round-trip via tests/testinfra/sessiondriver, asserting completion inside the documented budget; add tests/tier4_integration/admin_bootstrap_test.go asserting `lenny-ctl bootstrap --from-values` upsert idempotency and `--dry-run` diff accuracy against the compose stack.

### - [ ] T-DOC-INST.3 — The pool image upgrade state machine has no live integration or e2e test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Runtime image upgrades use a 6-state upgrade machine that provides canary validation and safe rollback at every phase." and the documented `lenny-ctl admin pools upgrade start / proceed / pause / resume / rollback --restore-old-pool` workflow (docs/operator-guide/upgrades.md:59, docs/operator-guide/upgrades.md:93). TESTING.md §14: "`lenny-ctl admin pools upgrade start` drives the state machine through expanding, draining, contracting, complete; pause/resume/rollback work" (TESTING.md:1079).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/runtime/upgrade/state` and `pkg/upgrade/upgrade_test.go` unit-test the state-transition logic (`TestNextWalksTheFullSequence`). `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/crd_test.go:116` (`TestPoolUpgrade`) only asserts the `lenny-pool-config-validator` webhook intercepts UPDATE; it does not drive a pool through the phases. `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/pool_upgrade_test.go` is declared in TESTING.md (lines 1079, 1543) but is absent on disk; TESTING.md line 1543 records it as deferred. `tests/tier8_chaos/scaffolds_test.go` references "runtime upgrade stuck" and "pool upgrade rollback during expanding phase" (TESTING.md:1215) without a live test.
- **Gap:** Driving a real pool through Expanding → Draining → Contracting → Complete with new sessions routed to the new pool and old sessions draining, plus the `rollback --restore-old-pool` recovery from `RuntimeUpgrade.previousPoolSpec`, is unverified against live CRDs and pods. The target tier is tier5, with a tier8 chaos failure-path case for the rollback-during-expanding and phase-timeout (`RuntimeUpgradeStuck`) scenarios. This is both a real user journey and a failure-recovery scenario.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness with the WarmPoolController and PoolScalingController binaries and a second runtime image to upgrade to (the echo and echo-embedded images in install.sh suffice). The chaos rollback case needs the tier8 chaos harness (tests/testinfra/chaos).
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier5_e2e_kind/pool_upgrade_test.go that runs `lenny-ctl admin pools upgrade start` with a new image digest, advances through each phase asserting `lenny_runtime_upgrade_state` and `lenny_runtime_upgrade_draining_sessions`, then a separate case that rolls back from Draining with `--restore-old-pool` and asserts routing returns to the old pool; add a tier8 case asserting `RuntimeUpgradeStuck` fires after the phase timeout.

### - [ ] T-DOC-INST.4 — No live test exercises version-to-version upgrade, the CRD-must-be-applied-first sequence, CRD-staleness recovery, or Helm rollback [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Helm does not update CRDs on `helm upgrade`. This is a known limitation that causes silent production incidents if CRDs become stale." with the required apply-CRDs-then-`helm upgrade`-then-verify sequence, the `lenny-crd-validate` post-upgrade hook, the stale-CRD recovery steps, and `helm rollback lenny <previous-revision>` (docs/operator-guide/upgrades.md:186, docs/operator-guide/upgrades.md:222, docs/operator-guide/upgrades.md:168).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/preflight/crdschema_test.go` unit-tests the CRD schema-version check including a post-upgrade message (`TestCRDSchemaVersionCheckPostUpgradeMessage_spec_17_6`). `charts/lenny/tests/crd-validate-job_test.yaml` renders the validate Job. `tests/tier4_integration/scaffolds_test.go:152` (`TestMigrationUpgrade`) is a `t.Logf` scaffold; the `migration_upgrade` integration suite named in TESTING.md (lines 324, 1037) does not exist on disk. The Kind harness `install.sh:346` has a `helm upgrade` branch, but it re-applies the same chart with the same values for idempotent re-runs; no test installs version N then upgrades to N+1, makes CRDs stale, or runs `helm rollback`.
- **Gap:** The upgrade journey (apply CRDs, `helm upgrade`, CRD validation hook, verification) and the failure path where CRDs are stale (the documented silent-incident class) and the Helm rollback path are all unverified against a live cluster. The target tier is tier5, with a tier8 chaos case for stale-CRD recovery and migration dirty-flag. This is both a real user journey and an adversarial/failure scenario.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness able to install two chart revisions; building a stale-CRD fixture (install the chart, delete or downgrade a CRD annotation, run the validate hook) is part of this finding. The tier8 migration dirty-flag scenario reuses the tier2 migrations harness against the compose stack.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier5_e2e_kind/upgrade_sequence_test.go that installs revision N, applies updated CRDs, runs `helm upgrade` to revision N+1, asserts the `lenny-crd-validate` Job passes and components are Ready, then a negative case that skips the CRD apply and asserts the validate Job fails with the documented remediation message; add tests/tier4_integration/migration_upgrade_test.go for the apply-N / apply-N+1 / rollback-N+1 data-integrity round-trip.

### - [ ] T-DOC-INST.5 — Cloud install, upgrade, and managed-backend integration are entirely unvalidated (tier6 all planned) [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "For production deployments, cloud-managed services are recommended over self-managed infrastructure." with the AWS RDS/ElastiCache/S3/KMS, GCP Cloud SQL/Memorystore/GCS/Cloud KMS, and Azure Database/Cache/Blob/Key Vault tables, plus the `postgres.connectionPooler: external` tenant-guard trigger for cloud-managed proxies (docs/operator-guide/installation.md:455, docs/operator-guide/installation.md:488).

The `lenny_tenant_guard` external-pooler trigger is unit-tested in migrations and component-tested in `tests/tier2_component/rls`, but never against a real RDS Proxy or Cloud SQL Auth Proxy.
- **Gap:** Every documented cloud deployment combination (managed Postgres, managed Redis, cloud object storage, Cloud/AWS/Azure KMS envelope encryption, and the cloud-managed-pooler tenant-guard path) is a supported deployment combination that no validated test exercises. The target tier is tier6 (cloud). This is a deployment-combination gap spanning storage, KMS, and pooler dimensions.
- **Dependencies:** Requires provisioned cloud clusters and managed services (the `scripts/cloud/<provider>/up.sh` and `install-lenny.sh` harness named in TESTING.md:1352) plus provider credentials; building or wiring this provisioning is part of the finding. The tier6 harness (tests/testinfra/cloud) is the building block.
- **Suggested test:** Promote `cloud_kms`, `cloud_oidc`, and `multi_az_minio` to `validated` for at least one provider by adding tier6 cases in tests/tier6_e2e_cloud that install Lenny against managed RDS/Cloud SQL with `connectionPooler: external`, assert the `lenny_tenant_guard` trigger is installed and the gateway refuses to start when it is missing, and verify a T4 envelope-encrypted write round-trips through the provider KMS.

### - [ ] T-DOC-INST.6 — Workload identity, IRSA, and WIF authentication paths are undocumented in any test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** The cloud-managed-services integration assumes provider identity (for example "AWS KMS … Used for etcd secret encryption and for wrapping the gateway's data-encryption keys") and the platform context lists "workload identity / IRSA / WIF" as a supported auth mode; the chart wires `global.saTokenAudience` and the SPIFFE trust domain per deployment (docs/operator-guide/ingress-and-tls.md:236, docs/operator-guide/installation.md:466).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml` lists `cloud_oidc` and `cloud_secret_store` as `planned` only. No test under tests/tier5_e2e_kind, tests/tier6_e2e_cloud, or tests/tier9_security asserts the gateway or controllers authenticate to a cloud KMS or object store using a workload-identity ServiceAccount binding (IRSA on EKS, Workload Identity on GKE, or Azure AD Workload Identity).
- **Gap:** The documented workload-identity auth mode for reaching cloud KMS, object storage, and secret stores has no integration or e2e coverage. The target tier is tier6, with a tier9 security assertion that no static cloud credential is mounted when workload identity is configured. This is a deployment-combination gap and a security-control gap.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a cloud cluster with the provider's workload-identity feature configured and the IAM/role bindings provisioned; building this provisioning is part of the finding. The tier6 cloud harness and tier9 security helpers (tests/testinfra/security) are the building blocks.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier6 case in tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/eks_platform_test.go (and GKE/AKS equivalents) that configures IRSA/WIF, performs a KMS-backed T4 write and an object-store upload using only the projected ServiceAccount token, and asserts no static access key is present in the gateway pod spec.

### - [ ] T-DOC-INST.7 — The admission-plane phase-stamp downgrade guard is not exercised against a live cluster [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "On every `helm install` and `helm upgrade`, a render-time guard reads the phase-stamp … and fails closed with `PHASE_STAMP_FEATURE_FLAG_DOWNGRADE`" and "the effective pre-Sync fail-closed gate is the `lenny-preflight` Job's `Phase-stamp consistency` check (`PREFLIGHT_PHASE_STAMP_MISMATCH`)", with the `acceptFeatureFlagDowngrade.<flag>` override as "the sole authorised path" (docs/operator-guide/configuration.md:523, docs/operator-guide/configuration.md:536).
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/preflight/phasestamp_test.go` and `tests/tier2_component/preflight/minio_sse_test.go` (which seeds an empty phase-stamp ConfigMap) cover the check logic; `charts/lenny/tests/phase-stamp-configmap_test.yaml` renders the ConfigMap. `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/admission_featuregated_test.go` installs feature-gated webhooks but does not flip a flag from `true` to `false` and re-render. No live test asserts the render-time guard or the preflight Job aborts a downgrade, nor that the `acceptFeatureFlagDowngrade` override emits the documented `deployment.feature_flag_downgrade_acknowledged` audit event.
- **Gap:** The fail-closed downgrade guard and its acknowledged-override path are unverified on a live cluster, where the Helm `lookup` primitive and the installed-webhook set actually exist (the documented GitOps caveat that `lookup` returns empty under `helm template` means the live path is the one that matters). The target tier is tier5, with a tier9 security assertion on the audit event. This is an adversarial/failure scenario for a fail-closed security control.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness; the chart, the phase-stamp ConfigMap template, and the preflight Job already ship. The audit assertion reuses the tier9 audit helpers (tests/testinfra/audit).
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier5_e2e_kind/phase_stamp_downgrade_test.go that installs with `features.compliance=true`, then attempts `helm upgrade` with `features.compliance=false` and asserts the render-time guard fails with `PHASE_STAMP_FEATURE_FLAG_DOWNGRADE`; a second case supplies `acceptFeatureFlagDowngrade.compliance=true` with a justification and asserts the upgrade proceeds, the webhooks are removed, and the audit event is emitted.

### - [ ] T-DOC-INST.8 — Ingress and external/internal TLS are validated only for ingress-nginx on Kind; other controllers and the deployer-provided and self-signed TLS models are unexercised [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** The ingress-controller compatibility table covers ingress-nginx, Traefik, ALB, GKE/GCE, and Istio, and the TLS-termination table covers cert-manager ClusterIssuer, deployer-provided Secret, and self-signed; the `lenny-ops-allow-ingress-from-ingress-controller` NetworkPolicy depends on `ingress.controllerNamespace`/`controllerLabel` matching the live controller (docs/operator-guide/ingress-and-tls.md:184, docs/operator-guide/ingress-and-tls.md:102, docs/operator-guide/ingress-and-tls.md:66).

### - [x] T-DOC-INST.9 — The `lenny up` embedded stack has no component or e2e bring-up test, including the local-only enforcement [Medium] — RESOLVED c5ebc95e
- **Resolution:** The gap is closed by three landed suites. `tests/tier4_integration/embedded_mode_smoke_test.go` (introduced in c5ebc95e "F-17.4.18: embedded-mode quick-start smoke test (up → session new → down)", extended through f0f2311c, 1b7593a1, f2df2ead, b239ae8a) drives the real `cmd/lenny` binary through `lenny up` → `lenny status` → `lenny session new` → `lenny down --purge` against a temporary `LENNY_HOME`, asserting the embedded k3s substrate, the in-cluster control plane, and a placed session all come up and tear down cleanly on every supported host. `tests/tier2_component/embedded/bringup_test.go` (landed via the 0013 series, most recently 051e1efc) pins the Docker-backed bring-up leg in isolation, asserting the CRD install succeeds through the host-rewritten kubeconfig. The local-only security guard is covered by `cmd/lenny-gateway/embedded_audience_test.go` (`TestEmbeddedHMACVerifierRejectsForeignAudience_spec_17_4_182`, landed in b191d405), which asserts the gateway rejects a token whose audience is not `dev.local`, and by `tests/tier9_security/embedded_gateway_loopback_test.go` (landed 8e534807, extended in 72e0bfe0 "0017 S18: probe the gateway NodePort off-host in the tier-9 EMBEDDED_MODE_LOCAL_ONLY leg"), which probes the gateway NodePort off-host to assert the local-only enforcement.

### - [x] T-DOC-INST.10 — The krew / kubectl-lenny equivalence and release-checksum invariant has no test [Medium] — RESOLVED fd2d69ee
- **Resolution:** Partially resolved. `pkg/ctlcli/unified_dispatch_test.go` (landed in fd2d69ee "F-24.0.1/F-17.4.9: unify lenny + lenny-ctl command surface") adds `TestProgNameTracksInvocationName_spec_24_0`, which asserts `progName()` prints `lenny`, `lenny-ctl`, or `kubectl-lenny` correctly for each of the three invocation names (including a `kubectl-lenny.v1`-style krew symlink), and `TestRunIsTheUnifiedEntryForBothNames_spec_24_0`, which asserts the full operator command surface dispatches identically regardless of invocation name. This closes the invocation-name-equivalence half of the finding. The release-artifact checksum invariant (that the krew manifest and the standalone binary published for a release tag share a checksum) still has no CI check on disk; that half remains open and belongs in a release-pipeline check rather than a Go test, per the original finding's dependency note.
- **Gap:** The release-checksum invariant between the krew manifest and the standalone binary is still unverified in CI.
- **Dependencies:** The checksum invariant needs the release artifact build (the krew manifest under dist/ and the published binary).
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier0/release check that the krew manifest checksum matches the standalone binary checksum for a given release tag.

### - [ ] T-DOC-INST.11 — The wizard smoke-test MCP round-trip is not pinned against the MCP wire format [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "it issues a `lenny/create_session` MCP round-trip when an admin token is available." (docs/operator-guide/install-wizard.md:217)
- **Existing tests:** `cmd/lenny-ctl/install_smoke_test.go` tests `runSmokeTest` orchestration with a `stubTester` and a stub HTTP server for the `/healthz` poll, but the stub does not validate that the request body conforms to the MCP `tools/call` JSON-RPC envelope for `lenny/create_session`. The MCP create-session contract is covered elsewhere (tests/tier3_contract and tests/tier4_integration/mcp_runtime_lifecycle_test.go), but the install smoke path's own round-trip is not asserted against that schema.

The target tier is tier3 (contract) reuse from the install path. This is a standards-conformance edge case.
- **Dependencies:** None — buildable today. The stub server in install_smoke_test.go can assert the request body against the MCP envelope, reusing the schema fixtures the tier3 MCP contract tests already use.
- **Suggested test:** Extend cmd/lenny-ctl/install_smoke_test.go so the stub gateway validates the smoke tester's `lenny/create_session` request against the MCP `tools/call` JSON-RPC schema and returns a conformant result, asserting the tester parses it correctly.

### - [ ] T-DOC-INST.12 — The air-gapped install path (`--offline` plus image-registry mirror) has no live coverage [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "`lenny-ctl install --offline` skips the cluster-reachability detection probes. No test installs from a mirror registry on a cluster with egress blocked, nor asserts the preflight Job still runs under `--offline` against a live cluster.
