## Docs — Tutorials and Alerting Docs <a id="t-doc-tutorials-alerting"></a>
**Source:** `docs/tutorials/ and docs/alerting/`
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The bundled alerting catalog has solid tier1 and tier2 coverage for catalog hygiene, PromQL parse-validation, PrometheusRule and OpenSLO rendering, and docs-file staleness (`cmd/gen-alerting-rules -check` covers `docs/alerting/rules.yaml`, `openslo.yaml`, and `routing-recommendations.md` through `TestBundledAlertingRulesFragmentIsCurrent`). The decisive gap is that no test ever evaluates a rule's PromQL expression against synthetic time series, so the documented firing semantics of the catalog (and especially the multi-window burn-rate alerts) are unverified end to end; the repository uses `promql/parser` for syntax only and `promql.Engine` / `promqltest` / `promtool` appear nowhere. The chaos tier maps every alert-driven runbook to a chaos test, but those tests assert behavioral degradation rather than the alert firing the TESTING.md §12.8 and §15.2 patterns require, so the "alert fires" step is documented but not implemented. The runnable tutorials (`first-session`, `deploy-to-cluster`, the SDK and MCP tutorials) have no end-to-end execution test against a fresh install; `time_to_hello_world_test.go` only asserts commands are wired offline. The OpenSLO export and the Alertmanager routing block are not validated against the external OpenSLO v1 or Alertmanager schemas, and the documented `lenny-ctl slo validate` "planned" contract is unpinned.
Counts: 2 High, 5 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-DOC-TUT.1 — Bundled alerting rules have no PromQL rules-eval or firing test [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Lenny ships a single source of truth for its alerting rules and SLOs (`pkg/alerting/rules`) ... Tour the catalog: `StartupLatencyBurnRate`, `TTFTBurnRate`, `WarmPoolExhausted`, `WarmPoolLow`, `CredentialPoolExhausted`, `CredentialPoolLow`, and the full catalog from Spec §16.5." (docs/tutorials/alerting-and-openslo.md:16, :23) and the rendered catalog in docs/alerting/rules.yaml:14 onward (for example `WarmPoolExhausted: (min by (pool) (lenny_warmpool_idle_pods) == 0) unless on (pool) (lenny_warmpool_fill_grace_active == 1)`).
- **Existing tests:** pkg/alerting/rules/rules_test.go::TestRuleValidateRejectsBadPromQL validates expr syntax only through `prometheus/prometheus/promql/parser.ParseExpr` (pkg/alerting/rules/rules.go:161). tests/tier2_component/observability/catalog_crosscheck_test.go::TestPrometheusRuleFieldsMatchCatalog asserts the rendered expr string equals the catalog expr string. pkg/alerting/evaluator/evaluator_test.go drives the inactive/pending/firing state machine through a fake `ExprEvaluator` that returns a fixed boolean per expr string, so it never evaluates the PromQL itself. A repo-wide search for `promql.Engine`, `promqltest`, and `promtool` across tests/, pkg/, and the Makefile returns no rule-evaluation usage; the only match is the chart template. No test feeds synthetic series to confirm any rule fires under its documented condition and clears when the condition resolves.
- **Gap:** The firing semantics of every bundled rule are unverified. A typo in a label matcher, an inverted comparison, a wrong `unless` join, or a broken burn-rate denominator would pass parse-validation and string-equality yet never fire (or fire constantly) in production. This is a tier2 standards-conformance gap against PromQL evaluation and a failure-path gap for the catalog the operator tutorial tells readers to rely on. The burn-rate expressions (for example `lenny_session_creation_error_ratio / (1 - 0.995) > 14`, docs/alerting/rules.yaml:337) and the histogram-quantile expressions are the highest-risk because their arithmetic is opaque to a parser.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. `github.com/prometheus/prometheus v0.302.1` is already in go.mod, so `promql/promqltest` (or a `promql.Engine` driving an in-memory `storage.Storage`) is available without a new dependency. Optionally add a `promtool test rules` fixture set under tests/testinfra/ if the project prefers the upstream rule-unit-test format.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier2_component/observability/rules_eval_test.go that, for a representative critical, warning, and burn-rate rule from `rules.Catalog()`, loads synthetic series into a `promqltest` fixture, evaluates the expr, and asserts the series count crosses the firing threshold under the documented condition and returns empty when resolved; reference tests/testinfra/clockstep for the `for`-window advance.

### - [ ] T-DOC-TUT.2 — Chaos tests for alert-driven runbooks do not assert the documented alert fires [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Every chaos test follows the same shape: ... 3. Assert the documented behavior: alert fires, fallback engages, audit trail records the event ... 5. Assert recovery: alert clears, system returns to healthy." (TESTING.md:1224) and "Each has a Tier 8 chaos test that: ... 2. Confirms the documented alert fires." (TESTING.md:2067). The rules under test are bundled in docs/alerting/rules.yaml (for example `RedisUnavailable` at :50, `MinIOUnavailable` at :67, `TokenServiceUnavailable` at :111).
- **Existing tests:** tests/tier8_chaos/store_failure_test.go::TestRedisClusterDegraded, ::TestMinIOUnavailable, ::TestPostgresUnavailable, ::TestDualStoreUnavailable and tests/tier8_chaos/component_failure_test.go::TestTokenServiceOutage inject the failure and assert health-endpoint degradation and no crash-loop (assertStoreOutageDegrades, assertNoCrashLoop). tests/tier8_chaos/runbook-map.yaml binds each alert-driven runbook to one of these tests (for example `redis-failure`, `minio-failure`, `token-service-outage`). A grep for `alert`, `firing`, `WarmPoolExhausted`, or `PrometheusRule` across the implemented tier8 test files returns only scaffolds_test.go and runbook-map.yaml; no chaos test queries the rule expr or a live Prometheus to confirm the mapped alert transitions to firing.
- **Gap:** The chaos suite verifies the system degrades but not that the operator is paged. The "alert fires" and "alert clears" steps the TESTING.md pattern mandates are absent, so a regression that breaks a rule expr (see T-DOC-TUT.1) would leave the chaos suite green while the alert silently never fires. This is a failure-path and observability gap on the security-relevant and availability-relevant runbooks the routing recommendations escalate to PagerDuty.

## Theme — Standards and Protocol Conformance <a id="t-theme-conformance"></a>
**Source:** spec/ and docs/ (cross-cutting)
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
Lenny has a broad surface of external-standard touchpoints (the MCP protocol, the OpenAI Chat Completions and Open Responses APIs, OAuth2/OIDC/PKCE/RFC 9068, CloudEvents v1.0.2, OCSF v1.1.0, OpenSLO v1, JSON-RPC 2.0, SSE, and the runtime-adapter JSON-Lines protocol). Each surface has a contract-tier or unit test, but with one exception (the adapter JSON-Lines protocol, which validates against Lenny's own committed JSON Schema) every test validates Lenny output against Lenny's own internal types, constants, and mapping contracts rather than against the published external schema or a golden vector taken from the standard. No external schema artifact for OpenAI, MCP, CloudEvents, OCSF, or OpenSLO is vendored anywhere in the repository, so a structural divergence from any of these standards that still satisfies Lenny's internal expectations would ship undetected. The contract-tier OpenAI and REST↔MCP suites exercise the inbound adapters in-process only, no tier5 or tier6 e2e test drives any external client protocol (MCP, OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses) against a deployed gateway, and several TESTING.md claims (OCSF schema validation, byte-for-byte published-schema SDK conformance, and two named contract directories) do not match what is on disk. Counts: 4 High, 6 Medium, 2 Low, 2 Info.

### Findings

### - [x] T-STD.1 — OpenAI Chat Completions and Open Responses output is never pinned against the published OpenAI schema [High] — RESOLVED 6595f98146620a69b7e3f50bbd4f1fc301d191e8
- **Resolution:** Added tests/tier3_contract/rest_openai_chat/published_schema_test.go and rest_openai_responses/published_schema_test.go, which validate the raw `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses` response bodies against the OpenAI `CreateChatCompletionResponse` and Responses `Response` component schemas vendored (with full `$ref` closure) from openai/openai-openapi at tests/testdata/openai_chat/schema and tests/testdata/openai_responses/schema. Running the new tests against the unmodified gateway failed: it omits several fields OpenAI's own schema requires (`logprobs`, `refusal`, `error`, `incomplete_details`, `instructions`, `tools`, `parallel_tool_calls`, `metadata`, `tool_choice`, `temperature`, `top_p`, per-content-block annotations/logprobs, and the usage input/output token-detail breakdowns). Both translators (pkg/gateway/environment/translator/openai_chat.go and open_responses.go) now emit every required field, using the exact default values OpenAI's own API documentation shows for a call made with no options set (for example `tool_choice: "auto"`, `parallel_tool_calls: true`, `temperature: 1`, `metadata: {}`), so the wire body validates cleanly against the published schema while asserting no behavior (tool calling, sampling) the translator doesn't implement. The fix is unambiguous under spec/15_external-api-surface.md's built-in adapter inventory, which names `OpenAICompletionsAdapter` and `OpenResponsesAdapter` as conforming to OpenAI Chat Completions and the Open Responses specification (a superset relationship for OpenAI Responses clients), and under TESTING.md's §12.3.2/§12.3.3 translation-fidelity framing that this suite extends with a check against the vendored, published OpenAI OpenAPI component schemas.

### - [ ] T-STD.2 — OCSF audit records are validated against Lenny's own mapping, not the published OCSF v1.1.0 schema [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The suite generates one of each event type and asserts the translated event passes OCSF schema validation." (TESTING.md:1000)
- **Existing tests:** tests/tier3_contract/ocsf_audit/ocsf_audit_test.go asserts the §11.7 structural contract (`class_uid`, `category_uid`, `type_uid == class_uid*100+activity_id`, `metadata.version`, the `unmapped.lenny_chain` extension) against Lenny's `pkg/audit/ocsf` types. Its own header states: "The OCSF v1.1.0 JSON schema bundle is not vendored — §11.7 pins the field mapping, not an external schema artifact ... This suite therefore validates the record against the §11.7 mapping contract directly." schemas/ocsf-mapping.yaml is Lenny's mapping, not the OCSF schema; schemas/audit-events/v1.json is the Lenny-native tuple view.
- **Gap:** This is a spec-versus-test inconsistency and a standards-conformance gap. TESTING.md claims OCSF schema validation, the test validates against Lenny's internal mapping. A record that satisfies Lenny's mapping but violates the OCSF class definition (for example an `activity_id` outside the class's allowed enum, or a `severity_id` of 0 which Lenny rejects but OCSF reserves as "Unknown") would not be caught against the standard. Target tier3 contract. Either vendor the OCSF schema and validate against it, or correct TESTING.md to state that validation is against the §11.7 mapping.
- **Dependencies:** Requires vendoring the OCSF v1.1.0 class schemas for the classes Lenny emits (Authentication, API Activity, and the others in schemas/ocsf-mapping.yaml) into tests/testdata/ocsf. tests/testinfra/schematest compiles them. No new infrastructure beyond the fixture.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier3_contract/ocsf_audit/published_schema_test.go that translates one record per catalog event type and validates each against the vendored OCSF class schema selected by `class_uid`, asserting OCSF-level structural conformance; alternatively reconcile TESTING.md:1000 with the internal-mapping reality.
- **Needs human input (as of 2026-07-06):** Lenny's OCSF translator (and the spec text backing it, across §11.7, §12.8, §16.7 and §25.9) assigns class_uid 3006 to "Account Change" (real OCSF 1.1.0: 3006 = Group Management, real Account Change = 3001), class_uid 5001 to "Entity Management" (real: 5001 = Device Inventory Info, real Entity Management = 3004), class_uid 6004 to "File System Activity" (real: 6004 = Web Resource Access Activity, real File System Activity = 1001), and class_uid 2004 to a class Lenny calls "Application Security Finding" (real: 2004 = Detection Finding; "Application Security Finding" is not an OCSF v1.1.0 class name at all). §11.7 states OCSF v1.1.0 is "the single, canonical wire format" for SIEM interoperability, so any external OCSF-aware SIEM parsing these class_uids on the wire will misclassify roughly two-thirds of Lenny's non-Authentication/API-Activity audit events. Do you want a change-proposal opened to correct the class_uid assignments (and every spec section/doc page that names them) to match the real published OCSF v1.1.0 registry, or is there a reason (not documented anywhere I could find) that Lenny deliberately diverges from the published registry, in which case the "OCSF is the canonical wire format" / "SIEM tools parse OCSF natively" claims in §11.7 and docs/operator-guide/audit-ocsf.md need to be qualified instead?

### - [x] T-STD.3 — The gateway-edge MCP surface has no contract or e2e test pinning initialize, tools/list, and the per-kind wire projection against the published MCP schema [High] — RESOLVED 68b525e1
- **Resolution:** Added tests/tier3_contract/rest_mcp_consistency/published_schema_test.go, which vendors the MCP protocol's own `schema.json` for both revisions the gateway concurrently serves (tests/testdata/mcp/schema/2025-03-26.schema.json and 2024-11-05.schema.json, with provenance recorded in the adjacent README) and validates the `/mcp` `initialize` result and `tools/list` catalog against the schema's `InitializeResult`/`Tool`/`ListToolsResult` definitions for the negotiated revision, closing the gap where only Lenny's own `map[string]any` construction and struct tags were checked. The finding's per-kind outbound wire projection (`elicitation/create`, `notifications/tasks/statusUpdate`, `notifications/lenny/toolCall`) is not yet implemented in pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp (the package's own comments mark it a tracked follow-on), so it remains out of scope for this pass; the vendored schemas also do not define those methods at either supported MCP revision, which the new README notes for whoever picks up that follow-on. Per spec/15_external-api-surface.md §15.2 ("Once negotiated, the connection is pinned to that version for its lifetime. The `MCPAdapter` dispatches to version-specific serialization logic internally"), the added test validates exactly the version-pinned surface the spec describes; no product-code change was needed since the existing `initialize`/`tools/list` responses already conformed to the published schema.

### - [ ] T-STD.4 — No tier5/tier6 e2e test drives any external client protocol (MCP, OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses) against a deployed gateway [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Wire-format round-trip. Every documented REST operation in the OpenAPI spec, every documented MCP tool, exercised through the SDK against a live gateway ... Request and response shapes match the published schemas byte-for-byte modulo language-idiomatic field naming." (TESTING.md:1981); "Pre-release: SDK conformance against the production-grade chart on Tier 5 (Kind) and Tier 6 (cloud)" (TESTING.md:2028).
- **Existing tests:** The OpenAI and MCP contract suites (tests/tier3_contract/rest_openai_chat, rest_openai_responses, rest_mcp_consistency) run in-process against a memstore and the EchoExecutor. tests/tier3_contract/sdks drives the SDKs against an in-process gateway. A grep of tests/tier5_e2e_kind/*.go and tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/*.go for `chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/mcp`, and `elicitation` returns only scaffolds_test.go. tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml has no OpenAI, MCP, OpenAI-Responses, CloudEvents, or OCSF capability row.
- **Gap:** This is a deployment-combination gap on the public wire surfaces. The protocol adapters are exercised only in-process with a synthetic executor; they are never validated against a runtime serving real output through the full chart (TLS termination, ingress, the real gateway binary, a reference runtime). The byte-for-byte and Tier 5/Tier 6 SDK-conformance claims in TESTING.md have no implementation. The work is a real user journey (alice connects an OpenAI-compatible client or an MCP client to a deployed Lenny and receives conformant output). Target tier5 Kind and tier6 cloud.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the tier5 Kind harness (tests/testinfra/kind) and the tier6 cloud lifecycle (tests/testinfra/cloud). The reference runtimes echo and streaming-echo already exist. The vendored OpenAI and MCP schemas from T-STD.1 and T-STD.3 are reused for assertion.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier5_e2e_kind/openai_conformance_test.go and tests/tier5_e2e_kind/mcp_conformance_test.go that install the chart, register the echo runtime, drive `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, and the `/mcp` surface through the SDK, and validate each response against the vendored external schema; promote a subset to tier6 and add the rows to parity-matrix.yaml.
- **Needs human input (as of 2026-07-06):** The two new tier-5 Kind tests (tests/tier5_e2e_kind/mcp_conformance_test.go, openai_conformance_test.go) prove the MCP surface (/mcp initialize + tools/list, both protocol versions) works end to end and schema-validates against the deployed gateway — that portion is fully closed and both MCP tests pass. Driving the other two built-in adapters spec/15 calls "Always available" (OpenAICompletionsAdapter at /v1/chat/completions, OpenResponsesAdapter at /v1/responses) against the same live gateway shows every request fails with "podexec: session ... is not bound to a pod", because the standard chart wires a PodExecutor (via --agent-namespace, on by default) and the two translators bypass the pod-claim path entirely, unlike POST /v1/sessions/start. This means on any standard Helm deployment the spec's "Always available" built-in OpenAI-dialect adapters are non-functional today, not just on this Kind harness. Fixing this is a design question, not a small patch: a single-shot, non-continuous request (OpenAIChatAdapterCapabilities declares SupportsSessionContinuity: false) needs to claim a pod, dispatch, and release synchronously within one HTTP request, reusing or mirroring sessionserver's warm-pool claim logic (with its retries, concurrent-slot handling, and SLOT_ID_REQUIRED invariants per pkg/gateway/session/executor/pod.go) without turning every OpenAI-dialect call into a full two-step session lifecycle. Should this go through change-proposal, and what is the intended pod-binding model for these two adapters when the gateway runs a PodExecutor: claim-per-request against the existing warm pool, a dedicated always-warm pool for translator traffic, or something else? Separately: the finding's suggested test also asked for a parity-matrix.yaml row, but tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml is scoped (per TESTING.md §12.6 and its own header) to capabilities that vary by cloud provider (gVisor/Kata isolation, cloud KMS, etc.); OpenAI/MCP protocol conformance is provider-independent, so no row was added there — please confirm that reading is correct before this is closed out.

### - [x] T-STD.5 — CloudEvents envelopes are validated against Lenny's own Validate(), not the published CloudEvents v1.0.2 schema [Medium] — RESOLVED 4bb27a5dd33f10977c6586aec685218b5b032060
- **Resolution:** Added tests/tier3_contract/cloudevents/published_schema_test.go, which vendors the published CloudEvents v1.0.2 JSON Schema (tests/testdata/cloudevents/v1.0.2-cloudevents.schema.json, provenance in the adjacent README) via tests/testinfra/schematest and validates one marshalled `eventbus.Event` per kind (a plain control event, a delegation-tree event with extensions, and an audit-bearing OCSF event) against it, in addition to the existing `ev.Validate()` checks. The test also directly asserts the two CloudEvents-spec constraints the published schema itself leaves unchecked: extension attribute names must be lower-case ASCII letters or digits, and `datacontenttype` must be a valid RFC 2046 media type. The test passed immediately against the current, unmodified eventbus package, so this closes the finding as an added test with no product-code change. Registered in tests/spec-map.json under §12.6 alongside the existing cloudevents_test.go entry. The added coverage is unambiguous under the CloudEvents v1.0.2 Attribute Naming Convention ("CloudEvents attribute names MUST consist of lower-case letters ('a' to 'z') or digits ('0' to '9') from the ASCII character set") and the `datacontenttype` Constraints clause ("If present, MUST adhere to the format specified in RFC 2046"), supplementing the TESTING.md:1008 CloudEvents v1.0.2 framing this suite extends.

### - [ ] T-STD.6 — OpenSLO export is checked only for apiVersion equality, not validated against the published OpenSLO v1 schema [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "the Helm chart renders the latency and availability SLOs from §16.5 as OpenSLO v1 YAML documents ... so that external SLO tooling produces burn-rate alerts consistent with the bundled multi-window alerts" (spec/16_observability.md:734-736).
- **Existing tests:** pkg/alerting/rules/openslo_test.go asserts `d.APIVersion == openSLOAPIVersion` where the constant is `"openslo/v1"` (pkg/alerting/rules/openslo.go:14), and checks the document `Kind` and metric references. charts/lenny/tests/openslo-configmap_test.yaml is a helm-unittest render check. No test validates the emitted `SLI`, `SLO`, and `AlertPolicy` documents against the published OpenSLO v1 JSON schema.
- **Gap:** This is a standards-conformance gap on an interoperability export consumed by Sloth, Nobl9, and OpenSLO Reliably. The test confirms the apiVersion string and Lenny's own struct fields, but a structural divergence from the OpenSLO v1 object model (a required `objectives` field omitted on the `SLO`, a `ratioMetric` missing `total`, or an `AlertPolicy` with a malformed `conditions` entry) would not be caught and would break the downstream generator. Target tier3 contract or tier0 static against the rendered chart fragment.
- **Dependencies:** Requires vendoring the OpenSLO v1 schema into tests/testdata/openslo. tests/testinfra/schematest compiles it. The rendered fragment is already produced by pkg/alerting/rules.RenderOpenSLO and charts/lenny/files/openslo.yaml.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier3 or tier0 test that renders the OpenSLO documents and validates each against the vendored OpenSLO v1 schema, asserting the export is structurally consumable by an OpenSLO-conformant tool.
- **Needs human input (as of 2026-07-06):** The §16.10 OpenSLO export has three confirmed structural non-conformances against the external OpenSLO v1 object model (verified against both the OpenSLO README prose and the official OpenSLO Go SDK's machine-enforced validation rules): (1) each rendered AlertPolicy document packs two AlertCondition entries (fast-burn + slow-burn) into one `conditions` array, but OpenSLO v1 caps that array at exactly one condition per policy; (2) every AlertPolicy document omits `notificationTargets`, which OpenSLO v1 requires to be non-empty, and Lenny currently has no config surface for what an operator's real notification destination would be; (3) SLO documents render `alertPolicies` as a bare list of name strings, but OpenSLO v1 requires each entry to be an object of the form `{alertPolicyRef: <name>}` (or an inline AlertPolicy). Fixing (1) and (3) is close to mechanical (split into two AlertPolicy documents per SLO, wrap the alertPolicies references), but fixing (2) requires inventing new deployer-facing configuration (what value(s) populate notificationTargets, and how an operator overrides it) that spec/16_observability.md §16.10 does not currently define. Should this go through the change-proposal pipeline to add a §16.10 notification-target configuration surface (and formalize the one-condition-per-policy / alertPolicyRef-object fixes) before any code changes land, or is there an existing intended notification-target value/config this task missed that would let a narrower code-fix proceed without a spec change?

### - [x] T-STD.7 — PKCE conformance asserts S256 method and verifier presence but never pins the BASE64URL(SHA256(verifier))==challenge transformation from RFC 7636 [Medium] — RESOLVED a1364e9ef41315eaf58ecd7f62b0ba5de657e196
- **Resolution:** Extended tests/tier4_integration/connector_oauth_test.go's TestOAuthConnector to recompute BASE64URL(SHA256(code_verifier)) from the verifier captured at the fake provider's token exchange and assert it equals the code_challenge captured from the /oauth/authorize response's authorization URL, pinning the RFC 7636 transformation end-to-end through the real gateway binary. The test passed unmodified against current gateway code (pkg/connectoroauth/pkce.go already derives the challenge correctly via CodeChallengeS256 using base64.RawURLEncoding(SHA256(verifier))), confirming no product defect; the new assertion closes the regression gap the finding identified. Registered in tests/spec-map.json already (existing test file, no new test function); validate-maps passes. Spec basis: "the gateway MUST generate a `code_verifier` (≥43 random characters, unreserved alphabet) and send the corresponding `code_challenge` (SHA-256 hash, base64url-encoded, `code_challenge_method=S256`) in the authorization request" (spec/09_mcp-integration.md §9.3, OAuth security requirements — PKCE (S256) for public clients).

### - [ ] T-STD.8 — RFC 9068 scope-claim enforcement is exercised on the MCP management surface but the claim parser is never validated against the RFC 9068 space-separated-string format end to end [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Per RFC 9068, the `scope` claim is a **space-separated string** of scope values (not an array)" (spec/25_agent-operability.md:66); "Every `tools/call` invocation checks the caller's `scope` JWT claim (RFC 9068, space-separated values) against the tool's declared `x-lenny-scope` identifier. A caller whose scope doesn't match receives `403 SCOPE_FORBIDDEN`" (spec/25_agent-operability.md:4535).
- **Existing tests:** pkg/common/scopes (the RFC 9068 parser, spec/04_system-components.md:26) has unit coverage. The token-exchange contract suite tests/tier3_contract/oauth_token/oauth_token_test.go asserts scope is preserved and broadening is rejected, decoding into Lenny's `jwt.Claims`. No contract or integration test asserts that a JWT carrying a space-separated `scope` string (the RFC 9068 wire form) drives a `403 SCOPE_FORBIDDEN` on `/mcp/management` `tools/call` versus a permitted call, end to end through the management server.
- **Gap:** This is a standards-conformance gap and a security-control gap. The narrowing layer is the enforcement boundary that lets an operator hand a `platform-admin` agent a restricted token. Whether a real RFC 9068 space-separated claim is parsed and enforced on the live MCP management surface (not only in the parser unit) is unverified. Target tier3 contract on the ops `/mcp/management` server, extending tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/mcp_test.go.
- **Dependencies:** Requires minting a JWT with a space-separated `scope` claim via tests/testinfra/tokenservice. The ops MCP server fixture (opsServer) already exists in tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints.
- **Suggested test:** Add a case to tests/tier3_contract/ops_endpoints/mcp_test.go that mints a token with `scope: "tools:health:read"` (space-separated), calls a `tools:pool:*` tool and asserts `403 SCOPE_FORBIDDEN`, then calls `tools:health:read` and asserts success, pinning RFC 9068 claim handling on the wire.
- **Needs human input (as of 2026-07-07):** This finding surfaces a real, already-partially-documented product defect (BUILD-GAPS.md §25.12 H4 + M4, plus related H5/H6/M5), not just a test gap: the MCP management server's /mcp/management tools/call never wires the authenticated JWT `scope` claim into its RFC 9068 scope-enforcement check (only the dev-only X-Lenny-Scope header works), and separately, opsInvoker.Invoke drops the Authorization header on its internal REST replay, so once §25.4 auth is enabled (mandatory in production) every ops-owned tools/call's REST leg is anonymous and 401s. Should this go through the change-proposal/implement-proposal pipeline as a proper fix (likely changing the mcp.Invoker interface to carry the caller's identity/context, per BUILD-GAPS H4, plus bridging Principal.Scopes into mcp.WithScopes per M4), given the blast radius touches pkg/ops/mcp, pkg/ops/opsserver, and their existing test suites? Or is there a narrower fix you'd prefer scoped to just the scope-claim bridging (leaving the Authorization-forwarding defect as a separately tracked, still-open BUILD-GAPS item)?

### - [x] T-STD.10 — SSE event framing (id: line carrying SeqNum, Last-Event-ID resume, gap_detected) is not pinned against SSE semantics on the MCP streaming surface [Medium] — RESOLVED (moot)
- **Resolution:** Already covered by since-landed work, found during batch review. Commit cbe7fce2 ("F-15.2.2/F-9.1.7: MCP Streamable HTTP SSE channel via attach_session") built the §15.2 attach_session Streamable HTTP SSE transport in pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/stream.go and its test suite in pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/stream_test.go, which is registered under spec-map.json section "15.2". That suite directly asserts every behavior this finding calls out: TestWriteMCPSessionEventCarriesSeqOnIDLine and TestAttachStreamsBacklogThenLive assert each frame's SSE `id:` line carries SessionEvent.SeqNum; TestAttachResumeFromSeqReplaysOnlyNewer and TestAttachLastEventIDResume assert resumeFromSeq and the Last-Event-ID header both resume replay from the correct cursor; TestAttachGapDetected and TestWriteMCPGapDetectedHasNoIDLine assert the `notifications/lenny/gapDetected` frame fires with the correct lastSeenSeq/nextSeq payload and carries no `id:` line when the cursor has been evicted from the buffer; and TestAttachKeepalive asserts the `:keepalive` comment frame is written on idle, framed separately from any `id:`-bearing event frame. The finding's cited blocker (gatewaymetrics not forwarding http.Flusher) is also already fixed — pkg/gateway/metrics/gatewaymetrics/gatewaymetrics.go's statusRecorder.Flush forwards to the underlying http.Flusher, verified passing by TestMiddlewareForwardsFlusher in gatewaymetrics_elicitation_test.go. All of these tests were re-run against the current tree and pass (`go test ./pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp/...` and `go test ./pkg/gateway/metrics/gatewaymetrics/... -run TestMiddlewareForwardsFlusher`), so the spec-map.json note at line 593 ("blocked on the gatewaymetrics middleware forwarding http.Flusher") and the finding's premise that the streaming_reconnect path is still a `t.Skip` are both stale as of the current tree; scaffolds_test.go's TestStreamingReconnect is a `t.Logf` composite pointer, not a skip. Spec basis: spec/15_external-api-surface.md §15.2 "Event-stream resume": "Every SessionEvent frame the MCPAdapter writes to the client carries its SeqNum as the SSE id: line on the Streamable HTTP transport... attach_session accepts an optional resumeFromSeq: uint64 parameter; when supplied, the gateway replays buffered events with SeqNum > resumeFromSeq before switching to live delivery... clients MAY also rely on the SSE Last-Event-ID header as an equivalent, implicit resumeFromSeq on plain reconnects. When the requested sequence has been evicted from the buffer, the adapter emits a single protocol-level gap_detected frame carrying {"lastSeenSeq": <resumeFromSeq>, "nextSeq": <oldestRetainedSeq>}..." and "Stream keepalive": "Comment lines are invisible to conforming SSE parsers... and carry no id: — they do not affect SeqNum, Last-Event-ID tracking, or the gap_detected contract."

## Theme — Real End-to-End User Journeys <a id="t-theme-user-journeys"></a>
**Source:** spec/ and docs/ (cross-cutting)
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The platform has strong per-component, contract, and admission coverage, but no single test exercises a complete persona journey through a real warm pod. The richest end-to-end test, `TestGatewayFullSurfaceE2E` (tier4), drives one prompt through the in-process `EchoExecutor` rather than a pod over mTLS/gRPC, and never iterates. On Kind and cloud, sessions are created and state-transitioned, yet no e2e test sends a prompt and asserts the echoed content returns through the full data path; the tier6 cloud lifecycle test explicitly accepts a `500 EXECUTOR_FAILURE` because `/start` never bound a pod. The client-over-four-protocols journey is covered only as single-shot fidelity-matrix contract tests for the OpenAI surfaces and a bare `initialize` for MCP, with no full session driven over MCP, OpenAI Chat Completions, or Open Responses. The agent-delegation, operator-upgrade, compliance-erasure, and runtime-author-publishing journeys each terminate in unit coverage, scaffolds, or CLI-usage assertions; the declared `erasure_job` tier4 suite and the tier5 legal-hold override flow do not exist, and a tier4 scaffold cites a `tier5_e2e_kind/checkpoint_test.go` that is absent. Counts: 6 High, 4 Medium, 1 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-JRN.1 — No end-to-end test drives an interactive developer session through a real pod with iteration [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "18. Client ↔ Gateway: Full interactive session (prompts, responses, tool use, interrupts, elicitation, credential rotation on RATE_LIMITED)" (spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:45)
- **Existing tests:** tests/tier4_integration/gateway_full_e2e_test.go:120 injects a single message and asserts the echo output contains "hello e2e", but it runs against the in-process `executor.NewEchoExecutor()` started by `gateway.StartWith(t, "--dev-mode")`, not a pod over mTLS/gRPC, and it sends exactly one prompt with no interrupt-then-resume, no second prompt, and no credential rotation. tests/tier4_integration/session_lifecycle_test.go:35 walks finalize → start → interrupt → terminate without sending any prompt. tests/tier5_e2e_kind/pod_lifecycle_test.go:32 inspects pod topology and Sandbox phase only. No tier4 or tier5 test drives the spec §7.1 step-18 loop (multiple prompts, interrupt, resume, rotation) against a runtime.
- **Gap:** The core developer journey (start a session, iterate with several prompts, interrupt and resume, observe a credential rotation) has no end-to-end test. This is a real user journey and is the platform's primary capability. The missing tiers are tier4 (against a runtime executor) and tier5 (against a real warm pod on Kind). It overlaps the per-subsection §7.2 interactive-model findings.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today for the tier4 multi-prompt loop against the echo executor; the tier5 variant uses tests/testinfra/sessiondriver and the agent-workload echo pools that tests/testinfra/kind/install.sh already deploys.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/interactive_iteration_test.go that creates a session, sends three prompts, interrupts, resumes, sends a fourth, and asserts the transcript ordering and per-prompt echo; add tests/tier5_e2e_kind/interactive_session_test.go using sessiondriver.CreateAndStart plus SendMessage to assert the echoed content returns from a real `echo-runtime-sidecar` pod.
- **Needs human input (as of 2026-07-07):** A first attempt at tests/tier4_integration/interactive_iteration_test.go was rejected by independent verification and discarded rather than committed. The test's fourth message used `delivery:"immediate"` sent right after an interrupt, while the pod was still held well within the default 900s `maxSuspendedPodHoldSeconds` window. Per spec/07_session-lifecycle.md path 6 (lines ~326-330), the gateway MUST atomically resume the suspended session and deliver that message, with `deliveryReceipt.status == "delivered"`. The attempted test instead asserted the opposite (`status == "queued"`, session remains `suspended`) with a comment admitting the atomic pod-held resume-and-deliver path is "still unimplemented" — i.e. it pinned the code's current, spec-violating fallback rather than the spec-required behavior. This surfaces a real product-code gap (missing atomic resume-and-deliver for path 6 with `delivery:immediate`), not just a missing test. A human should decide: (a) implement the missing atomic resume-and-deliver behavior via the code-fix route with a test that pins the spec-required `delivered` outcome, or (b) rewrite the test to send a non-immediate message so it validates only the buffering case the code actually supports today, leaving the pod-held-immediate gap as its own explicitly tracked finding.

### - [ ] T-JRN.2 — No e2e test asserts a prompt round-trips to a real runtime pod and returns content on Kind or cloud [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "16. Client → Gateway: AttachSession(session_id) / 17. Gateway ↔ Pod: Bidirectional stream proxy" (spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:43)
- **Existing tests:** tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/session_lifecycle_test.go:115 sends `POST /messages` and accepts `http.StatusInternalServerError` because the comment states "the executor then surfaces a 500 EXECUTOR_FAILURE ... because /start has not run yet"; it never asserts an echoed response. tests/tier5_e2e_kind/scaffolds_test.go:102 and tests/tier9_security/live_session_test.go:53 call `CreateAndStart` but assert only state, cross-tenant isolation, or pool replenishment. A grep for an echoed-content assertion across tier5, tier6, tier8, and tier9 returns no match. The sessiondriver harness exposes `SendMessage` and `DeliveryReceipt` (tests/testinfra/sessiondriver/sessiondriver.go:90) but no e2e test reads the returned output.
- **Gap:** No test on Kind or cloud proves the gateway-to-pod bidirectional data path: a client prompt reaching the runtime and the runtime's output returning to the client. This is the platform's central guarantee and is unverified end to end. The missing tiers are tier5 and tier6. It overlaps the §6.3 and §15.1 per-subsection findings.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the e2e gateway to bind sessions to agent pods (the chart sets `--agent-namespace` from `agentNamespaces`, but the scaffold tests skip with "no SandboxClaim binding found," indicating the binding is not reliably exercised); confirming and fixing that wiring is part of this finding. Building blocks: tests/testinfra/sessiondriver and tests/testinfra/kind.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier5_e2e_kind/prompt_roundtrip_test.go that drives `CreateAndStart` → `SendMessage("ping")` → reads the SSE event stream and asserts the echo runtime returns "ping"; extend tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/session_lifecycle_test.go to `/start` the session before `/messages` and assert the echoed content rather than tolerating a 500.
- **Needs human input (as of 2026-07-07):** The tier5 test tests/tier5_e2e_kind/prompt_roundtrip_test.go (committed, currently t.Skip'd) and its supporting e2e config fix (tests/testinfra/kind/agent-workload.yaml, tests/testinfra/kind/install.sh — both add capabilities.injection.supported:true to echo-runtime-sidecar) are in place. Running the test against the current 17-day-old persistent Kind cluster with LENNY_SKIP_BUILD=1 triggered a helm upgrade that rolled the gateway Deployment (the bootstrap overlay's resolved image digests changed the pod template checksum), and the new gateway pods CrashLoopBackOff with "flag provided but not defined: -proxy-extension-wait-timeout" — the deployed gateway binary predates a chart-template flag, a pre-existing skew unrelated to this diff (no chart file under charts/lenny was touched). A background full (non-skip-build) `bash tests/testinfra/kind/install.sh` rebuild+reinstall was kicked off to clear this, but did not finish within this session. Please either wait for that rebuild to complete and confirm `kubectl -n lenny-system get pods` shows lenny-gateway Running, then run `go test -tags e2e_kind ./tests/tier5_e2e_kind/ -run TestPromptRoundTripsToRealPodAndReturnsContent -v` (removing the t.Skip first) and confirm it passes; or re-run install.sh fresh if the background attempt also failed, and report back so the skip can be lifted and the finding closed.

### - [x] T-JRN.3 — No client-driven journey exercises the same session across all four protocols [High] — RESOLVED 3a7d8391
- **Resolution:** Added tests/tier3_contract/multiprotocol_journey/journey_test.go: a matrix.Run test over {rest, mcp, openai-chat, openai-responses} that wires all four §15 protocol adapters against one shared memstore/EchoExecutor/session-event-bus gateway and drives create → prompt → stream → terminate on each surface (REST via POST /v1/sessions/start + /messages + SSE GET /events + /terminate; MCP via lenny/create_and_start_session + lenny/send_message + SSE lenny/attach_session + lenny/terminate_session; OpenAI Chat and Open Responses via their single-shot stream:true POST, since those protocols create-and-complete a turn per call by design). Each cell asserts the EchoExecutor's echoed transcript is present on that surface's response and that the surface's own streaming mechanism (SSE) delivers a final chunk reporting completion. Passed on first run against the unmodified gateway; a mutation check (redacting the echoed content) was applied and reverted to confirm all four cells fail when the cross-protocol content does not actually flow, ruling out a tautological assertion. Registered under spec-map.json §15.2.1 and extended the contract selectors for pkg/gateway/sessionserver, pkg/gateway/mcpfabric/mcp, and pkg/gateway/environment/translator in change-graph.json so `--changed` picks the new test up. Per README.md:75 ("One gateway, four protocols. REST, MCP (Streamable HTTP), OpenAI Chat Completions, and Open Responses all terminate at the same gateway and share one auth, policy, routing, and audit path.") and spec/15_external-api-surface.md §15.2 ("Session flows — MCP. Creating and interacting with sessions ... flows through the MCP API," the create_and_start_session/send_message/attach_session/terminate_session tool list) and §15.1's REST session-lifecycle table (POST /v1/sessions/start, /messages, /events with Accept: text/event-stream, /terminate) that this test's per-protocol journeys drive.

### - [x] T-JRN.4 — No end-to-end test exercises an agent delegating to children and collecting their results [High] — RESOLVED edbbde15
- **Resolution:** Added tests/tier4_integration/delegation_await_collect_test.go (TestDelegationAwaitChildren), a tier-4 test that drives a parent delegating two children through the real cmd/lenny-gateway binary and calling the lenny/await_children platform MCP tool: one subtest terminates only the first child and asserts mode="any" returns exactly that child's TaskResult while the still-running sibling is left untouched (not auto-cancelled), and a second subtest terminates both children and asserts mode="all" returns both children's TaskResults. The test passed immediately against the unmodified product code, so this closes the coverage gap with no code change. Registered in tests/spec-map.json under section 8.5. Per spec/08_recursive-delegation.md §8.5/§8.8: "`lenny/await_children(child_ids, mode)` | Wait for multiple children (`all`, `any`, or `settled`). Streaming response — unblocks on `input_required`." and "`any` — return as soon as any child reaches a terminal state. Returns the first `TaskResult`. **Remaining children continue running** — they are not auto-cancelled." and "`all` — wait until all children reach a terminal state (completed, failed, cancelled, or expired). Returns list of `TaskResult`."

### - [x] T-JRN.5 — The compliance-officer erasure journey has no integration or e2e test; the declared erasure_job suite and tier5 legal-hold override flow are absent [High] — RESOLVED 5cbbc3415faf15ac881c84df89f549731d590830
- **Resolution:** Added tests/tier4_integration/erasure_job_test.go (build tag `integration`), which drives the §12.8 `DeleteByUser` sequence and the legal-hold preflight/override through the real cmd/lenny-gateway binary against a live Postgres container: it seeds a user's session and transcript, runs erasure via POST /v1/admin/users/{userId}/erase, confirms the FK-constrained sessions/session_messages rows are actually gone and the gdpr.erasure_completed receipt is recorded; a second scenario sets a legal hold, confirms erasure is rejected with ERASURE_BLOCKED_BY_LEGAL_HOLD, then exercises the platform-admin --acknowledgeHoldOverride path and confirms erasure completes with gdpr.legal_hold_overridden and legalHoldOverride recorded on the receipt. Registered under spec section 12.8 in tests/spec-map.json (validated clean by `lenny-test validate-maps`). This closes the tier4 half of the finding; no tier5/Kind test was added because the legal-hold-override behavior is pure admin-API business logic with no cluster-specific mechanism (no CRD, admission webhook, or pod lifecycle involved), so tier4 is the lowest tier that genuinely exercises it — TESTING.md's tier5 framing described the suite's home in the wall-clock/e2e config, not a behavior that requires Kind. Per spec/12_storage-architecture.md §12.8: "The `DeleteByUser(user_id)` erasure job executes store deletions in the following dependency order. Each step is individually idempotent to support crash recovery... If any active hold is present, the erasure job MUST abort before step 1 with error code `ERASURE_BLOCKED_BY_LEGAL_HOLD` (HTTP 409, `POLICY` category)... An operator with the `platform-admin` role (tenant-admins cannot self-override) may invoke `POST /v1/admin/users/{user_id}/erase` with request body `{"acknowledgeHoldOverride": true, "justification": "<required free-text>"}` to bypass the preflight... On a successful override, the erasure job records the override in its receipt (`legal_hold_override: true`, `override_by`, `override_justification`, `override_at`...) and emits a `gdpr.legal_hold_overridden` critical audit event."

### - [x] T-JRN.6 — The runtime-author publishing journey is verified only by CLI-usage and scaffold checks, never end to end [High] — RESOLVED ec5a3b16d6b19096baca4bdc07045e190cdba77d
- **Resolution:** Added tests/tier5_e2e_kind/runtime_publish_journey_test.go, a real (no mocking) tier-5 Kind test that scaffolds a runtime, builds and pushes its image to a real local OCI registry via a genuine `lenny runtime publish` (not --skip-push), applies the resulting Runtime CRD, creates a warm pool, grants tenant access, and drives a live session against it, asserting the echoed reply. Running that journey for real against unmodified code failed for three genuine reasons, all fixed in pkg/ctlcli/runtime.go and the four cmd/lenny-ctl/runtimescaffold/templates/runtime-*.yaml.tmpl plus binary-minimal.main.go.tmpl scaffold templates: `lenny runtime publish` could never register a freshly pushed image because it reused the pre-push tag instead of the post-push digest-pinned reference the admin API requires; every scaffolded runtime.yaml omitted the required `labels` field the same admin API also rejects; and the `--language binary --template minimal` scaffold read/wrote JSON frames over the container's raw stdin/stdout instead of the sidecar model's LENNY_ADAPTER_SOCKET, so it exited immediately on every real pod. The journey test now passes reproducibly (two consecutive fresh runs, ~3 minutes each). Fixed against "Images **must** be pinned by digest (not tag) in Runtime definitions" (spec/05_runtime-registry-and-pool-model.md:690); "**Labels are required from v1** — primary mechanism for environment `runtimeSelector` and `connectorSelector` matching" (spec/05_runtime-registry-and-pool-model.md:51); "Each entry is a complete runtime definition that a deployer can install and use for real workloads without additional coding, once the deployer registers the published image digest, applies a Runtime CRD instance, and creates a warm pool for it" (spec/26_reference-runtime-catalog.md:3); "Operators grant access per tenant via `POST /v1/admin/runtimes/{name}/tenant-access` with body `{"tenantId": "<uuid>"}` ... after install" (spec/26_reference-runtime-catalog.md:30); "`lenny runtime publish <name> --image <ref>` | Convenience wrapper for `docker push` and `lenny-ctl admin runtimes register` that pushes the built image to the configured registry and registers the runtime against the target gateway" (spec/24_lenny-ctl-command-reference.md:233)

### - [x] T-JRN.7 — The operator scale-then-upgrade journey is not exercised; pool_upgrade and schema_migration are admission-only or scaffolds on Kind [Medium] — RESOLVED 238c82941175fe18ea95395af20d0ef4767d1179
- **Resolution:** Added tests/tier4_integration/schema_migration_journey_test.go. `TestSchemaMigrationJourney_ExpandGateContract` drives a real Phase 1 (expand) → Phase 2 (backfill) → Phase 3 (gated contract) migration against a live Postgres container via a dedicated test-only two-phase migration fixture (tests/testinfra/fixtures/expand_contract_migration/), including a genuine Phase 3 gate rejection on an un-migrated row (asserting the exact spec-documented error text and the resulting dirty flag) and the documented clear-dirty-flag-and-retry recovery, ending in a passing gate and the old column dropped. `TestSchemaMigrationJourney_GatewayCoexistsAcrossExpandStepAndRestart` starts a real cmd/lenny-gateway process, applies a concurrent additive schema change to its live Postgres, and starts a second gateway process (representing a rolling-deploy replica) against the same, now-migrated Postgres, confirming both processes stay healthy and the new process sees the prior process's data. This closes the schema_migration half of the finding at tier4 (the pool_upgrade half was already closed at tier4 by commit b4e7931a); tier5 Kind is not used because schema migration is pure Postgres/gateway-process behavior with no CRD, NetworkPolicy, or admission dimension that a Kind cluster would add over a live Postgres container plus the real gateway binary, matching the precedent already accepted for the pool_upgrade half. Both tests are registered under §10.5 in tests/spec-map.json and under a new tests/testinfra/fixtures/expand_contract_migration glob in tests/change-graph.json; `lenny-test validate-maps` passes. Per spec/10_gateway-internals.md §10.5: "Expand-contract discipline: Phase 1 (expand): Add new columns/tables, deploy code that writes to both old and new. Phase 2 (migrate reads): Switch reads to new schema. Phase 3 (contract): Drop old columns/tables in a subsequent release." and the Phase 3 enforcement gate ("Phase 3 gate failed: &lt;N&gt; un-migrated rows remain in &lt;table&gt;.&lt;old_column&gt;. Resolve data migration before retrying."), plus the recovery procedure from spec/17_deployment-topology.md §17.6 (clear the dirty flag, release stale advisory locks, re-run the migration Job).

This is a genuine product design decision, not a test-only change: should the watch mechanism be a new controller that observes pod deletionTimestamp/eviction events (deployed alongside the existing sandbox controller), or should the agent pod's own preStop hook (pkg/controller/sandbox/podspec/podspec.go preStopDrainHook) directly call back into the gateway's Checkpoint RPC before its grace period expires? Separately, POST /v1/sessions/{id}/resume (a sessiondriver.Resume helper) does not exist yet and needs its own design/implementation, and the MinIO-outage variant additionally needs a live toxiproxy/testcontainers injector (tests/tier8_chaos/minio_outage_during_checkpoint_test.go is itself an unimplemented stub). Who owns scoping and building this wiring, and on what timeline should tests/tier5_e2e_kind/checkpoint_resume_test.go's two t.Skip calls be expected to lift?

## Theme — Deployment Combination Coverage <a id="t-theme-deployment-matrix"></a>
**Source:** spec/ and docs/ (cross-cutting)
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The deployment cross-product is exercised in one narrow corner and is unverified almost everywhere else. The only combination driven end to end on a real cluster is session mode, runc isolation, single-node or AWS/EKS topology, single-replica Postgres/Redis/MinIO, the REST protocol, and header-injected (dev) auth. Every sandboxed-isolation cell (gVisor, Kata, Firecracker, Confidential Containers) is a skip-stub that passes vacuously, and the parity matrix marks all of them `planned`. The cloud tier is AWS-only in practice: the GCS, Azure Blob, Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault, Workload Identity Federation, and Azure AD store and auth implementations claimed in §17.5 have no cloud e2e despite GKE and AKS being declared first-class providers. Non-REST protocols (MCP, OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Open Responses) and the task and concurrent execution modes are exercised only against the compose stack and never on Kind or cloud, so no protocol-by-isolation-by-topology cell beyond the canonical one is covered. HA datastore failover, multi-zone DR, and air-gapped installation are mapped to scaffolds, unused fixtures, or unit tests rather than to cluster-level exercises. Counts: 6 High, 5 Medium, 3 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-DEP.1 — No deployment combination runs a sandboxed isolation profile (gVisor, Kata, Firecracker) end to end; every cell is a vacuous skip-stub [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Default isolation profile (sandboxed) creates pods on the gVisor (or provider-equivalent) node pool. Process namespace, syscall filtering, and capability dropping behave per documented sandbox semantics." (TESTING.md:1110) and the matrix marks every isolation row `planned`: "gvisor_isolation ... gke: planned / eks: planned / aks: planned" (tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml:27).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/cluster_assertions_test.go::TestGvisorIsolation` logs and returns when no node is labeled `lenny.dev/pool=sandbox-gvisor` (line 147), and `TestKataIsolation` logs and returns when no Kata or Firecracker RuntimeClass exists (line 177). Both pass without asserting any sandbox behavior. On Kind, `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/pod_lifecycle_test.go:81` asserts `runtimeClassName == "runc"` only. spec-map.json §6.1 lists exactly these two cloud scaffolds. No test confirms a pod actually boots under a sandboxed RuntimeClass, drops capabilities, or enforces syscall filtering.
- **Gap:** The default production isolation profile (sandboxed) is never exercised in any tier. The entire isolation dimension collapses to runc. This is both a missing user journey (alice runs a session on the default sandboxed profile) and a missing security verification (the sandbox boundary holds). Target tiers: tier6 e2e cloud for gVisor and Kata on a provisioned sandbox node pool, and a tier5 Kind gVisor lane when the Kind node image carries the gVisor RuntimeClass.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a provisioned sandbox node pool per provider (GKE built-in sandbox, EKS Bottlerocket/Fargate, AKS Kata-equivalent) wired through `scripts/cloud/<provider>/up.sh`, and a gVisor-capable Kind node image. These do not exist yet; building them and flipping the parity-matrix cells to `validated` is part of this finding. Reuse `tests/testinfra/cloud` and `tests/testinfra/kind`.
- **Suggested test:** Extend `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/cluster_assertions_test.go` so `TestGvisorIsolation` claims a `SandboxWarmPool` with `isolationProfile: sandboxed`, drives a session onto the sandboxed pod via `sessiondriver`, and asserts process-namespace isolation and capability drop; add a tier5 `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/gvisor_isolation_test.go` gated on RuntimeClass presence.
- **Partial progress (as of 2026-07-07):** The tier5 Kind gVisor lane is closed: `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/gvisor_isolation_test.go` (commit 34e5489c) claims a session on the `gvisor-echo-pool` and confirms the sentry kernel is active by reading `/proc/version` from inside the pod (`"Linux version ... #1 SMP ... (gVisor sentry confirmed)"`) — verified passing directly against the live Kind cluster. The tier6 cloud assertion was strengthened (commits a3ef5dfd, 031755a0): `TestGvisorIsolation` now checks pods actually scheduled under the gvisor RuntimeClass drop all Linux capabilities per §5.3/§13.1, backed by an exported, unit-tested `pkg/podsecurity.CapabilitiesDropped` rule (matching the same rule the admission validator applies) rather than a hand-rolled comparison — but it still soft-skips, since no cloud sandbox node pool exists yet to schedule a pod onto. The tier6 cloud half (a provisioned sandbox node pool per provider — GKE built-in sandbox, EKS Bottlerocket/Fargate, AKS Kata-equivalent — wired through `scripts/cloud/<provider>/up.sh`) is still not built; `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml`'s `gvisor_isolation` row remains `planned` for all three providers. This finding stays OPEN until the cloud half lands too.
- **Needs human input (as of 2026-07-08):** Closing T-DEP.1 requires standing up real sandboxed-isolation infrastructure that does not exist anywhere reachable from this environment: no GKE/EKS/AKS cluster is currently provisioned (GCP project lenny-tier6 has owner-level access but zero clusters and zero Artifact Registry images; AWS SSO for the pre-configured lenny-e2e-eks/lenny-load-small-eks contexts is expired and needs an interactive browser re-auth; Azure has no logged-in account at all), and tests/tier6_e2e_cloud tests are fail-closed (they FAIL, not skip, with no cloud provider configured), so no test-only change can close this without a live cluster. Should this be (a) provisioned now — a real GKE cluster plus a GKE-Sandbox gvisor node pool in the lenny-tier6 project, images built and pushed to Artifact Registry, and the chart install plus TestGvisorIsolation run end to end there (accepting the cloud spend and multi-hour build/debug time, leaving GCP as the only validated provider for now) — or (b) left to an operator with AWS SSO / Azure login access and an approved cloud budget to run `scripts/cloud/<provider>/up.sh` plus the new sandbox-node-pool wiring across all three providers?

### - [ ] T-DEP.5 — Task mode and concurrent (slotId) execution are exercised only on the compose stack, never under real isolation or a real cluster [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "concurrent_workspace | `slotId` multiplexing: N prompts on same pod; per-slot credential isolation; per-slot cleanup timeout" and "concurrent_stateless | Tenant-affinity routing; cross-tenant routing rejected; pod assignment correctness" (TESTING.md:1033-1034); §14.9 names "task mode workspace scrub, concurrent workspace mode per-slot directories" as Tier 5 coverage (TESTING.md:1929).

- **Gap:** The execution-mode dimension (session, task, concurrent) is covered end to end only in session mode on a cluster; task and concurrent modes are verified only in compose, which uses no real pod, no RuntimeClass, and no per-slot filesystem isolation. Per-slot credential isolation and workspace scrub are security-relevant and unverified against a real sandbox. This is a deployment-combination gap and a spec-versus-test inconsistency with §14.9. - **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/execution_modes_test.go` that brings up a task-mode pool, runs two sequential tasks on one pod and asserts the workspace is scrubbed between them, then a concurrent pool and asserts per-slot credential and directory isolation, using `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver`.

The same commit also fixed a real defect it surfaced along the way: `podsession.PoolPolicyMirror` never carried `sessionPolicy.recycle.enabled`, so a standard-profile recycling pool's pod was always retired instead of scrubbed and reused. The task-mode workspace-scrub half (`TestTaskModeRecycleScrubsWorkspaceBetweenSessions`) is written but stays skipped: it surfaced a separate, pre-existing gap — `cmd/lenny-adapter` never wires a `CheckpointSink` at all, so seal-and-export always fails and the pod is always retired per §6.2 regardless of `recycle.enabled`. This finding stays OPEN until that CheckpointSink-wiring gap is fixed and the task-mode half can actually pass.
- **Needs human input (as of 2026-07-09):** tests/tier5_e2e_kind/execution_modes_test.go::TestTaskModeRecycleScrubsWorkspaceBetweenSessions is already written, spec-cited, committed (f96dfe6d), and t.Skip'd because cmd/lenny-adapter never wires a CheckpointSink, so every Checkpoint RPC returns Unimplemented and §6.2 always retires the pod on the resulting failed disposition instead of recycling it. Fixing that is not a small wiring tweak: I confirmed there is no production CheckpointSink implementation anywhere in the tree (only test fakes), no ObjectStorage/MinIO fields on pkg/controller/sandbox/podspec.Inputs, and no secret/credential plumbing from the chart into the sandbox pod's adapter container at all (the gateway container has this; the per-pod adapter container does not). This is the same gap BUILD-GAPS.md §4.4 already tracks at a larger scope ("the adapter Checkpoint RPC streams via an in-process pipe to a CheckpointSink interface; no production sink is configured for partial-chunk uploads or AbortMultipartUpload cleanup"), which itself depends on a still-missing checkpoint-manifest object layer (BUILD-GAPS.md line 12924). Should this be handled as its own dedicated proposal/build effort (given it touches credential handling in the sandbox pod spec, chart secret wiring, and multiple new packages) rather than as a fix bundled into this test-gap closure? If so, should T-DEP.5 stay open pointing at that BUILD-GAPS.md §4.4 work rather than be treated as a standalone code-fix here?
