### - [ ] T-DEP.13 — The cloud TestMain runs AWS-shaped suites against GCP/Azure clusters, where they skip rather than fail [Info] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "the user-facing contract: tier-6 fails (not skip, not vacuous-pass) when no provider is configured, and fails per-provider when a configured provider isn't reachable." (tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/scaffolds_test.go:25).
- **Existing tests:** `TestMain` (scaffolds_test.go:53) iterates `LENNY_CLOUD_PROVIDERS` and runs the whole package per provider. The AWS-specific tests gate on `p != "aws"` and skip (`aws_resources_test.go:73`) or read `LENNY_AWS_*` env that is unset on a GCP/Azure run and then skip. The stated contract is fail-closed on an unreachable provider, but a GKE or AKS run silently skips the entire managed-service surface because no GCP/Azure-shaped test exists to fail.
- **Gap:** Until T-DEP.2 adds GCP/Azure-shaped tests, a green tier-6 run against GKE or AKS proves almost nothing about those providers, which contradicts the documented fail-closed contract. Recording this so the parity-matrix gate and the per-provider skip semantics are revisited when the sibling tests land. No standalone test is required beyond T-DEP.2.
- **Dependencies:** none — observational, resolved by T-DEP.2.
- **Suggested test:** When the GCP/Azure managed-service tests land, add a tier0 or matrix-validation assertion that every provider in `LENNY_CLOUD_PROVIDERS` has at least one non-skipping managed-service test, so a vacuous per-provider pass is itself a failure.
- **Needs human input (as of 2026-07-09):** This finding was attempted 1 time(s) and the independent verifier rejected every attempt: The finding (T-DEP.13) describes a runtime behavior defect: tier-6's TestMain loops over each configured provider (LENNY_CLOUD_PROVIDERS) and reruns the full package each iteration, so AWS-shaped test files (e.g. managed_rds_test.go) execute even when the current provider is gcp/azure. requireCloud(t) only checks that the *current* provider's CLI is authenticated (tests/testinfra/cloud SkipUnlessAvailable), not that the test's target provider matches the running one; requireRDS(t) then finds LENNY_AWS_RDS_ENDPOINT unset, logs, and returns a zero-value struct, and every TestCloudRDS* test does `if p.host == ""` { return }`, which is a silent vacuous PASS with zero assertions executed -- exactly the 'skip rather than fail' behavior the finding names. The added commit (0d6aa6de) does not test or touch any of that: it adds a tier0 static AST scan (tests/tier0_static/tier6_managed_service_provider_coverage_test.go) that only checks (a) each provider has at least one tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/managed_*_test.go file, and (b) that file contains the literal pattern t.Fatalf/t.Errorf/t.Fatal/t.Error somewhere in its source, via a flat AST walk with no reachability/control-flow analysis. The managed_rds_test.go etc. files already existed long before this commit (added in earlier commits d1e49ffd/ddf0231a/34c10eeb/66a6134c) and already contain t.Fatalf calls (unreachable in the actual cross-provider bug path, but present as source text), so the new test passes trivially against both the pre-fix and post-fix tree and would never catch the actual defect. Ran it directly (go test ./tests/tier0_static/... -run TestTier6ManagedServiceCoverageEveryProvider -v) and confirmed PASS, but this is orthogonal to the finding: removing the requireCloud/requireRDS guard or making TestMain skip-vs-fail incorrectly would not turn this test red. The // spec: citation attached is the generic scaffolds_test.go prose about failing when no provider is configured / failing per-provider when a configured provider is unreachable. It does not establish that a static file-existence-plus-substring check is the right enforcement for the specific cross-provider vacuous-pass scenario T-DEP.13 names, and the new test never exercises TestMain, requireCloud, or requireRDS. Net effect: the finding is not closed by this commit. A genuine fix requires a design decision this batch should not make unilaterally -- should an AWS-shaped test explicitly t.Skip when the configured provider isn't AWS, should the per-provider TestMain loop only execute the subset of test files tagged for that provider, or should a mismatched test fail per the fail-closed contract -- recommend routing to a human to decide the intended cross-provider behavior before implementing and testing the fix. A human should review the attempt history before a future batch retries this finding, since repeating the same approach is likely to hit the same rejection.

### - [x] T-DEP.14 — `kube(t)`'s documented "skip on stale/unreachable kubeconfig" contract is not honored by most of its callers, which panic instead [Low] — RESOLVED bdf36e777ea2adf46a287daea724bd84ba16a8b8
- **Resolution:** The tier-6 `kube()` test helper documented a skip-on-unreachable contract but returned a nil clientset on all three failure paths (kubeconfig-load, clientset-build, unreachable API server); its ~17 call sites dereference the result with no nil check, so a torn-down cluster or stale kubeconfig (provider CLI session still valid) panicked with a nil-pointer trace instead of skipping. Each failure branch now calls `t.Skip`, and a new test (`TestKubeSkipsWhenKubeconfigInvalid`) pins that an invalid kubeconfig skips the calling test rather than returning nil. This finding has no product spec section (it is a test-infrastructure robustness gap); the contract the fix and test enforce is the `kube()` helper's own documented contract in `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/cluster_assertions_test.go` ("kube returns a Clientset for the cluster the operator's kubeconfig points at, or skips when the kubeconfig is missing / invalid"), under the governing test-harness section TESTING.md §12.6 (Tier 6 — E2E on cloud), whose deployment matrix runs the cloud suites per provider against the provider's cluster with every suite obtaining its clientset from `kube()`. The sibling provider guard is fail-closed on a separate axis (`tests/testinfra/cloud/cloud.go` `SkipUnlessAvailable`: provider CLI configured and authenticated), distinct from the cluster-reachability axis `kube()` governs.

### - [ ] T-DEP.15 — parity-matrix validator never enforces that any capability reaches `validated`; the all-planned matrix passes tier-0 forever [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "CI fails if a capability is claimed but missing from the matrix" (TESTING.md:1122).
- **Existing tests:** `cmd/lenny-test/cmd_validate_yaml.go:351-375` is the parity-matrix validator. It computes `hasValidated` per capability but discards it (`_ = hasValidated`, line 375) under the comment "planned everywhere is acceptable today". The only enforcement is that a claimed capability appears as a matrix row; there is no assertion that any provider cell ever reaches `validated`.
- **Gap:** The validator enforces presence but never exercise: `tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml` currently holds 39 cells, all `planned` or `skip` and zero `validated`, and it passes tier-0 indefinitely. This is the enforcement gap that lets the sandboxed-isolation coverage hole tracked by T-DEP.1 and the testbed hole tracked by T-BED.10 persist silently: no gate flags a capability that is claimed but never actually driven on any provider. Target tier: tier0 static (extend the existing validator plus a test around it).
- **Dependencies:** A hard `validated`-required threshold cannot fire until the provider clusters exist (the same missing sandbox/cloud infrastructure T-DEP.1 depends on), so a warn-level check is the buildable-today portion; the fail-level gate lands with that infrastructure.
- **Suggested test:** Add a warn-or-fail threshold to the parity-matrix validator (emit a non-fatal "N capabilities still `planned`" warning today, and require at least one `validated` cell per capability once the provider clusters exist), and add a tier0 test asserting the validator flags an all-`planned` matrix rather than passing it.

## Theme — Adversarial and Abuse Scenarios <a id="t-theme-adversarial"></a>
**Source:** spec/ and docs/ (cross-cutting)
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
Several adversarial controls are verified at the unit and contract level but never through a hostile actor end to end. Token-exchange scope forgery, idempotency-key collision, OAuth state replay, and webhook HMAC replay each have a negative test at tier1/tier2/tier3 plus a tier4 integration check, and those vectors are in good shape. The delegation cycle, maxDepth, and fan-out budget controls, the elicitation content-integrity rejection, the credential-exfiltration probe, the cross-tenant isolation of the OpenAI Chat Completions and Open Responses surfaces, the NetworkPolicy agent-pod egress block, the connector-per-delegation enforcement, and the malicious-upload extraction path are either unit-only or stand behind skipping scaffolds that the tier9 suite records as ops-backlog work. The §12.9.9 elicitation "tamper" tests in tier9 assert only the admin config round-trip and never inject a tampered payload, which diverges from the TESTING.md §12.9.9 declaration. The OWASP ZAP black-box fuzzing run and the external pen-test replay are release-pipeline artifacts that no in-tree test exercises against a live gateway, and the JWT algorithm-confusion and key-substitution forgeries have no contract test at all.
Counts: 4 High, 6 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [ ] T-ADV.1 — Delegation cycle, maxDepth, and fan-out budget rejections are unit-only; no integration or e2e adversarial path through the gateway [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "If the resolved target's `(runtime_name, pool_name)` tuple appears anywhere in the caller's lineage, the gateway applies the cycle-detection decision matrix below before any pod allocation." and "Every effective delegation lease MUST carry a positive integer `maxDepth` ... no delegation chain can grow without bound under any mode" (spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:64, spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:81-89)
- **Existing tests:** The cycle decision matrix and the maxDepth resolution chain are covered by unit tests only: pkg/delegation/cycle/cycle_test.go (TestDecideEnforceRejectsAndAttributesBlocker, TestDecidePoolDifferentiatedIsNotCycle, and siblings) and pkg/delegation/lease/lease_test.go (TestCheckDepthRejectsAtCeiling, TestValidateChildSliceRejectsParallelOverrun, TestResolveMaxDepthApplies82BisPrecedence), which are the entries spec-map.json lists for §8.2 and §8.3. The only integration test, tests/tier4_integration/delegation_test.go (TestDelegation), drives the happy path (a single child spawned through lenny/delegate_task appears in GET /v1/sessions/{id}/tree). The tier7b load suite tests/tier7b_load_kind/delegation_test.go runs a depth=10 fan-out for latency, not for rejection. No test drives DELEGATION_CYCLE_DETECTED, DELEGATION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED, or BUDGET_EXHAUSTED through the real cmd/lenny-gateway binary.
- **Gap:** The adversarial delegation paths are the security-relevant branches and are unverified above the unit layer. A regression in the gateway's lineage walker, the lease maxDepth narrowing, or the budget_reserve.lua wiring would not be caught by any tier2-or-above test. The work is an adversarial scenario: a malicious or buggy parent agent that delegates into a runtime-identity cycle (A->B->A), past the resolved maxDepth ceiling, or beyond maxParallelChildren / maxTreeSize, asserting the typed rejection and the delegation.cycle_warning / admission-rejection audit pair reach the caller. Target tiers are tier4 integration and tier5 e2e on Kind.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. The delegation-echo runtime and the gateway harness exist; tests/testinfra/gateway starts the binary against Redis (tests/testinfra/containers.StartRedis) and Postgres, and tests/testinfra/scenkit can express the chain.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/delegation_adversarial_test.go that uses tests/testinfra/gateway and a delegation-echo lineage to drive a self-recursive hop (assert DELEGATION_CYCLE_DETECTED with details.blockedBy), a depth-ceiling overrun (assert DELEGATION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED), and a fan-out budget overrun (assert BUDGET_EXHAUSTED with details.limitType), plus a tier5 Kind case that exercises the same rejections under real NetworkPolicy.

### - [ ] T-ADV.2 — Elicitation content-integrity rejection is never exercised; the tier9 "tamper" tests assert only the admin config round-trip [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "In `enforce` mode, a tampering intermediate pod modifying the elicitation payload is rejected with `ELICITATION_CONTENT_TAMPERED`. In `detect-only` mode, the tampered version is delivered, the audit event fires, and the `ElicitationContentIntegrityPermissiveTamper` alert is recorded." (TESTING.md:1288; the chain walker is spec/09_mcp-integration.md)
- **Existing tests:** tests/tier9_security/elicitation_tamper_test.go (TestElicitationTamperEnforceMode, TestElicitationTamperDetectOnlyMode, TestElicitationPlatformFloor) only PUT and GET /v1/admin/tenants/acme/elicitation-content-integrity and assert storedMode/effectiveMode round-trip; they inject no tampered payload and skip when the admin path is not wired. The §9.2 chain walker with TamperError is covered by unit tests in pkg/elicitation/chain_test.go and pkg/elicitation/elicitation_test.go. tests/tier4_integration/elicitation_test.go exercises the happy-path chain. The tier9 scaffolds_test.go records the live tamper exercise as "on the tier-9 ops backlog."
- **Gap:** The control that the TESTING.md suite names as the headline §12.9.9 assertion has no test that actually tampers an elicitation response and asserts ELICITATION_CONTENT_TAMPERED, the lenny_elicitation_content_tamper_detected_total counter, and the §16.5 alert. This is both a missing adversarial scenario and a spec-versus-test inconsistency, since the tier9 file name and the TESTING.md text both imply a tamper-rejection that is not exercised. It overlaps with the per-subsection finding for §9.2 and broadens it: no test anywhere drives a tampered payload through the live chain.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a tampering-intermediary connector or runtime stub in tests/testinfra/stubs (a malicious child that mutates the elicitation body and recomputes nothing); the elicitation-echo runtime exists, the malicious intermediary does not. Building it is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier4 negative case in tests/tier4_integration/elicitation_test.go that routes an elicitation response through a tampering stub and asserts ELICITATION_CONTENT_TAMPERED under enforce mode and delivery-plus-alert under detect-only, plus a tier5 Kind exercise (tests/tier5_e2e_kind/elicitation_chain_test.go) under real mTLS and NetworkPolicy using tests/testinfra/kind.

### - [ ] T-ADV.3 — Cross-tenant isolation is not attacked on the OpenAI Chat Completions and Open Responses surfaces [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "A composed adversarial scenario: seed tenants A and B with rich state on every store, then for each store and each operation, attempt cross-tenant reads and writes through every code path (REST, MCP, OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, admin API, MCP management server, audit query, drift detection, lenny-ops endpoints). Every attempt must fail with the documented isolation error." (TESTING.md:1242)
- **Existing tests:** Cross-tenant isolation is asserted on the REST and admin/audit paths: tests/tier9_security/tenant_isolation_test.go (cross-store reads plus the cross-tenant audit-query 403), tests/tier4_integration/rls_tenant_guard_test.go (RLS denies tenant A reading tenant B rows), tests/tier4_integration/redis_tenant_isolation_test.go, and pkg/gateway/sessionserver/upload_test.go (TestBlobGetRejectsCrossTenant). The OpenAI Chat Completions and Open Responses contract dirs tests/tier3_contract/rest_openai_chat and tests/tier3_contract/rest_openai_responses contain only fidelity-matrix tests (TestRESTOpenAIChatFidelityMatrix, TestRESTOpenAIResponsesFidelityMatrix); neither carries the substring "tenant." No test attempts a cross-tenant read or write through either OpenAI-compatible surface.
- **Gap:** The §12.9.1 suite is explicit that every client surface, including OpenAI Completions and OpenAI Responses, must reject cross-tenant access, yet two of the four named client protocols have no adversarial isolation test. A tenant-confusion regression on the chat-completions or responses router would ship undetected. The work is an adversarial scenario plus a deployment-combination gap (the same control across the full client-protocol dimension).
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. tests/testinfra/gateway plus a two-tenant seed (alice@acme.com and bob@globex.com) and tests/testinfra/sdkhelper for the OpenAI dialects.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/openai_cross_tenant_test.go that mints a tenant-acme session JWT, then issues a POST /v1/chat/completions and a POST /v1/responses bearing a session_id and resources owned by tenant globex, asserting the documented isolation error rather than a leaked completion.

### - [ ] T-ADV.4 — Credential-exfiltration probe and the agent-pod NetworkPolicy egress block skip on any cluster without the cred-shell-echo workload [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Adversarial inspection of agent pods: process environment dumped, filesystem walked, `/proc/<pid>/environ` examined, network egress captured. No standing LLM-provider credentials are present." and "Test pods attempt to reach forbidden endpoints: agent pod to internet, agent pod to Postgres, agent pod to Redis, agent pod to another tenant's namespace, ephemeral container to credentials, agent pod to cloud metadata service. Every attempt times out at the CNI layer." (TESTING.md:1284, TESTING.md:1268)
- **Existing tests:** tests/tier9_security/credential_leakage_test.go (TestCredentialLeakageEnvironment, …Filesystem, …NetworkEgress) drives kubectl exec against a cred-shell-echo pod but calls t.Skip in findCredShellPod when that pod is absent, which is the default on any cluster the standard install does not seed with cred-shell-echo-pool. tests/tier9_security/network_policy_test.go (TestNetworkPolicyAdversarial) covers only the lenny-system default-deny egress; the agent-namespace egress half is the skipping scaffold TestNetworkPolicyAgentEgress in scaffolds_test.go. The egress-capture sidecar (cmd/lenny-egress-capture) and the SSRF egress except-blocks have unit coverage only.
- **Gap:** The two highest-value runtime-isolation probes (a pod cannot exfiltrate a leased credential, and a pod cannot egress to the internet, the data stores, IMDS, or a sibling tenant's namespace) are gated behind preconditions that are absent in CI, so they pass vacuously. The agent-to-IMDS (169.254.169.254) and agent-to-other-tenant-namespace probes named in TESTING.md §12.9.4 have no live assertion at all. The work is an adversarial scenario and a deployment-combination gap (the probes must run on the default Kind overlay and on a sandboxed-runtime profile).
- **Dependencies:** Requires the cred-shell-echo workload and the egress-capture sidecar wired into the default tier5 Kind overlay (commit 3aa580b added agent-workload.yaml wiring) so the probes do not skip, plus a second-tenant namespace fixture. The wiring exists but is not applied by the default install path; making it default is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Wire cred-shell-echo-pool and the egress-capture sidecar into the standard tests/testinfra/kind install so the existing credential_leakage_test.go probes execute, and add a tier5 NetworkPolicy case that curls the IMDS address and a sibling tenant namespace from an agent pod and asserts a CNI timeout (curl exit 28).

### - [ ] T-ADV.5 — Malicious-upload defenses (archive bomb, path traversal, oversize) are unit-only; no extraction through the adapter materialize path [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Maximum decompressed size per archive: **256 MiB**. Maximum decompression ratio (compressed:uncompressed): **100:1** ... Validator violations surface to clients as `UPLOAD_ARCHIVE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` with `details.reason` carrying the specific sub-code." (spec/13_security-model.md:658-666)
- **Existing tests:** The ceilings and traversal rules are tested at the unit layer: pkg/upload/upload_test.go (TestValidateArchiveRejectsExtremeRatio, TestValidateEntryRejectsTraversal, TestValidateEntryRejectsOversizedEntry, TestValidateEntryRejectsAbsolutePath), pkg/adapter/workspace/uploadarchive_zip_ratio_test.go (TestExtractionZipEnforcesRatioBound), and pkg/adapter/workspace/extract_test.go. The gateway upload endpoint is tested in pkg/gateway/sessionserver/upload_test.go for token validation and a 413 oversize-body cap, but it does not extract an archive. No tier2-or-above test sends a malicious archive through the upload-to-materialize-to-extract path and asserts UPLOAD_ARCHIVE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with the correct details.reason reaches the client.
- **Gap:** The decompression-ratio bound, the entry-count ceiling, and the path-traversal rejection are enforced during adapter-side extraction inside the pod, a code path no component or integration test exercises with a hostile archive. The unit tests prove the validator in isolation; they do not prove the validator is invoked on the real extraction path or that the typed error propagates to the API caller. The work is an adversarial scenario at tier2 component (adapter plus its workspace store) or tier4 integration.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. pkg/adapter/workspace materializeArchive helpers and the testdata builders (buildZip) exist; tests/testinfra/compose or the adapter component harness can drive the extraction.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier2_component/adapter_upload/malicious_archive_test.go that materializes a zip-bomb (ratio past 100:1), a tar with a ../ traversal entry, and an over-count archive through the adapter's workspace materialize path and asserts each aborts with the documented UPLOAD_ARCHIVE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED sub-code and increments lenny_upload_extraction_aborted_total.

### - [ ] T-ADV.6 — Prompt injection routed through an external MCP tool: connector-per-delegation enforcement is unit-only [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "The gateway validates the `connector_id` in every external tool call against the calling pod's effective delegation policy before proxying. A child cannot use connectors not permitted by its policy, even if tokens exist for them at the root level." (spec/09_mcp-integration.md:164)
- **Existing tests:** The policy-deny-before-dial decision is covered by unit tests: pkg/gateway/connectorauthz/connectorauthz_test.go (TestAuthorizeConnectorRuntimePolicyDenies_spec_9_3_164) and pkg/gateway/connectorinvoke/invoker_test.go (TestInvokerCallToolDeniedByPolicy_spec_9_3_164, which asserts zero outbound dials on a policy denial). tests/tier4_integration/connector_oauth_test.go drives the connector OAuth authorize/callback flow but does not exercise a child whose policy denies a root-permitted connector, and it does not model tool output flowing back into the agent context. No test routes an external-tool result through a child session whose effective delegation policy forbids that connector.
- **Gap:** The cross-delegation-level connector boundary (a child cannot reach a connector that exists at the root) is the control that contains prompt-injection routed through a nested agent, and it is verified only with a fake resolver at the unit layer. There is no component or integration test that confirms the gateway re-evaluates connector_id against the child's effective policy on the live proxy path. The work is an adversarial scenario at tier4 integration.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a stub external MCP tool server in tests/testinfra/stubs/runtime (or a new connector stub) that returns attacker-controlled tool output; the runtime stub package exists and can be extended. Building the connector stub is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/connector_delegation_scope_test.go that registers a connector at the root, delegates to a child whose DelegationPolicy omits it, and asserts the child's lenny/call_tool against that connector_id is rejected with the §9.3 policy error and no outbound dial occurs, even though a root-level token exists.

### - [ ] T-ADV.7 — Gateway resource exhaustion (slow-loris, slow-subscriber backpressure) is modeled only as a load scenario, not asserted as a control [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Send returns a non-nil error within `MaxOutboundSendTimeoutMs` (default: 100 ms). The gateway then closes the channel and drops the connection. ... This ensures a single slow client cannot cause unbounded memory growth in the gateway." (spec/07_session-lifecycle.md:363; the OutboundChannel bounded-error policy is spec/15_external-api-surface.md:125-164)
- **Existing tests:** tests/tier7a_load_local/scenarios/slow_loris_protection/scenario.go and tests/tier7a_load_local/scenarios/pubsub_slow_consumer/scenario.go model the §10.1 slow-client and the §4.8 slow-subscriber drop as load scenarios. The OutboundChannel bounded-error behavior has no direct test: a search for MaxOutboundSendTimeoutMs, the 100 ms bound, or lenny_outbound_channel_buffer_drop_total in the gateway packages returns nothing. No tier8 chaos or tier9 security test asserts that a slow client is dropped within the timeout and that gateway memory stays bounded.
- **Gap:** The control that prevents a single slow or malicious client from exhausting gateway memory is described normatively but is verified only indirectly through a load scenario that measures throughput, not the drop-and-bound guarantee. An adversary holding open many slow SSE or attach_session streams is the threat, and no test asserts the gateway sheds them. The work is an adversarial scenario at tier8 chaos or tier9 security, plus a missing component assertion on the OutboundChannel timeout.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today for the component assertion (the OutboundChannel implementation lives in pkg/gateway). A live slow-client flood uses tests/testinfra/loadgen against tests/testinfra/gateway.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier2 assertion in the gateway's outbound-channel package that a subscriber whose read loop stalls causes Send to return within MaxOutboundSendTimeoutMs and the channel to close, plus a tier8 case in tests/tier8_chaos that opens many slow attach_session streams and asserts lenny_outbound_channel_buffer_drop_total rises and gateway RSS stays bounded.

### - [ ] T-ADV.8 — OWASP ZAP black-box fuzzing (path traversal in artifact keys, SQL injection, oversize headers, deeply nested objects) has no in-tree run against a live gateway [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "OWASP ZAP runs against the REST and MCP surfaces with the project's policy. Oversize payloads, malformed JSON, SQL-injection strings, path-traversal in artifact keys, oversize headers, and deeply nested objects are all rejected with the appropriate error codes." (TESTING.md:1276)
- **Existing tests:** tests/tier9_security/scaffolds_test.go::TestInputFuzzingOWASPZAP records that the ZAP black-box run is a release-pipeline CI job and pins only the contract that each attack class has an in-process Go fuzz target (pkg/audit, pkg/auth/jwt, pkg/upload, pkg/idempotency, and siblings). tests/testinfra/security/zap/ holds the ZAP policy and a unit test for the driver. No test runs ZAP against a deployed cmd/lenny-gateway, and the specific black-box classes named in TESTING.md (path traversal in artifact keys, oversize headers, deeply nested objects) are exercised only as Go fuzz units against individual packages, not as wire-level requests to the running gateway.
- **Gap:** The black-box fuzzing the suite names is deferred entirely to release engineering, so the REST and MCP wire surfaces have no in-tree negative test for over-large headers, deeply nested JSON, or a traversal-laden artifact key reaching the blob endpoint. The in-process fuzz targets cover parsers in isolation but not the assembled gateway. The work is a standards-conformance and adversarial gap at tier9 security.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a ZAP run wired against tests/testinfra/gateway, or a lightweight in-tree black-box battery using tests/testinfra/security/zap. The driver and policy exist; standing up the gateway target in CI is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier9_security/blackbox_fuzz_test.go that starts the gateway via tests/testinfra/gateway and sends a corpus of oversize headers, a 64-level-nested JSON body, and a path-traversal artifact key to the REST and MCP surfaces, asserting each returns the documented 4xx envelope rather than a 5xx or a leak.

### - [ ] T-ADV.9 — JWT algorithm-confusion (alg:none) and key-substitution (wrong kid) forgeries have no contract test [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Standard OIDC/RFC 9068 claims (`iss`, `sub`, `aud`, `exp`, `iat`, `nbf`, `jti`, `scope`)" minted through a single canonical endpoint, with the gateway verifying token signatures against the IdP's JWKS for the bootstrap path. (spec/13_security-model.md:571, spec/13_security-model.md:613)
- **Existing tests:** tests/tier3_contract/rest_auth/auth_test.go asserts the expired-token (TestExpiredTokenReturns401), tampered-signature (TestTamperedTokenReturns401 flips the last signature byte), missing-credentials, and malformed-tenant-claim rejections, all against an HMAC signer. tests/tier4_integration/jwks_test.go and tests/tier4_integration/jwt_rotation_audit_test.go cover key rotation and JWKS publication. No test presents a token with alg set to none, a token re-signed under an attacker key with a forged kid header, or an RS-to-HS algorithm-confusion attack against a gateway configured for asymmetric verification.
- **Gap:** Two canonical JWT forgery classes (alg:none acceptance and key substitution via a forged kid) are absent from the auth contract suite even though the gateway accepts upstream OIDC ID tokens verified against a JWKS. The tampered-byte test catches a corrupted signature but not a structurally valid token signed under the wrong key or algorithm. The work is a standards-conformance negative test at tier3 contract.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. tests/testinfra/stubs/oidc and tests/testinfra/tokenservice can mint forged tokens; pkg/auth/jwt is the verifier under test.
- **Suggested test:** Add cases to tests/tier3_contract/rest_auth/auth_test.go (or a new jwt_forgery_test.go) that submit an alg:none token, a token re-signed under an unknown key with a spoofed kid, and an RS256-header-over-HS256-verification confusion attempt, asserting each returns 401 TOKEN_INVALID and no session is created.

### - [ ] T-ADV.10 — External pen-test replay runs against an internal baseline bundle; the partner-engagement gate is unexercised in CI [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Pre-release ships an artifact bundle to the external pen-test partner. The pen-test driver under `tests/tier9_security/pentest/` is the harness for replaying the partner's findings against future builds." (TESTING.md:1298; the §18.33 replay is spec/18_build-sequence.md)
- **Existing tests:** tests/tier9_security/scaffolds_test.go::TestPentestReplay loads the bundle that LENNY_PENTEST_BUNDLE points at, and when the variable is unset it falls back to tests/tier9_security/pentest/v1-baseline-bundle.json. That baseline encodes 25 internal-review findings (partner "Lenny v1 internal review (baseline)"), all already marked remediated, so AssertAllRemediated always passes. The driver logic itself is unit-tested in tests/tier9_security/pentest/driver_test.go against committed fixtures.
- **Gap:** The pen-test replay gate passes against an internal baseline whose findings are pre-marked remediated, so in the default CI configuration it asserts nothing about a real adversarial engagement. The control is exercised only when release engineering supplies an external bundle, which no automated path guarantees. The work is a gating-completeness gap: the §18.33 replay is effectively a self-fulfilling check until a partner bundle is wired.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a real external pen-test engagement bundle, which is a genuine external artifact this repository cannot synthesize. Recording the missing bundle and a CI gate that fails when no partner bundle is present at release time is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier9 or release-gate assertion that fails the Phase 14 gate when LENNY_PENTEST_BUNDLE is unset at release time (rather than silently falling back to the baseline), so the partner-engagement replay cannot be skipped on a release build.

### - [ ] T-ADV.11 — No adversarial test for concurrent credential-pool exhaustion racing the point-in-time availability check [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "This is a point-in-time check, not a reservation: concurrent `delegate_task` calls can each pass the check individually while collectively exhausting the pool. If the actual credential assignment fails after pod claim (due to this race), the gateway releases the pod back to the warm pool and returns `CREDENTIAL_POOL_EXHAUSTED`." (spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:468)
- **Existing tests:** pkg/gateway/credassign and pkg/credential/select carry unit coverage for the assignment and selection logic. tests/tier8_chaos/scaffolds_test.go records the live credential-pool exhaustion exercise as needing "a seeded finite-lease pool; on the ops backlog." No test drives concurrent delegate_task calls that each pass the pre-claim check yet collectively exhaust the pool and asserts the loser receives CREDENTIAL_POOL_EXHAUSTED with the pod released back to the warm pool.
- **Gap:** The documented race between the point-in-time availability check and concurrent claims has no test that the post-claim failure path returns the typed error and does not leak a warm pod. This is a low-risk negative path because the unit layer covers the assignment logic, but the concurrency race itself is unexercised above unit. The work is an adversarial concurrency scenario at tier4 integration or tier8 chaos.
- **Dependencies:** Requires a finite-lease credential pool fixture seeded against the gateway; tests/testinfra/gateway plus a seeded credentialpoolstore. Buildable with the existing store fixtures.
- **Suggested test:** Add a tier4 case that seeds a pool with one assignable slot, fires N concurrent inherit-mode delegate_task calls, and asserts exactly one succeeds while the rest return CREDENTIAL_POOL_EXHAUSTED and the warm-pod count returns to baseline.

### - [ ] T-ADV.12 — Rate-limit (sliding-window) evasion across the window boundary is not exercised end to end [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Configurable per-session and per-tenant rate limits, enforced by the gateway via Redis sliding-window counters ... Excess requests receive `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header." (spec/10_gateway-internals.md:938)
- **Existing tests:** tests/tier2_component/quota/quotastore_sliding_test.go (TestQuotaSlidingWindowContract) covers accumulation, bucket isolation, and rolling-boundary reset on the store. tests/tier4_integration/quota_test.go (TestQuotaEnforcement, TestQuotaRecovery) drives the token-budget hard limit and the MAX-rule recovery through the gateway, asserting QUOTA_EXCEEDED. No test drives the eval-submission RATE_LIMITED path (perSessionPerMinute / perTenantPerMinute) through the gateway, and none probes the classic sliding-window evasion where a client front-loads requests at the tail of one window and the head of the next.
- **Gap:** The sliding-window rate limiter is contract-tested at the store layer and the token quota is integration-tested, but the per-session eval rate limit (RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After) and the window-boundary burst-evasion case are not exercised through the gateway. This is a low-risk negative path given the store-level coverage, but the end-to-end 429 and the evasion resistance are unverified. The work is an adversarial scenario at tier4 integration.
- **Dependencies:** none — buildable today. tests/testinfra/gateway plus tests/testinfra/clockstep or timectl to advance across the window boundary deterministically.
- **Suggested test:** Add tests/tier4_integration/rate_limit_evasion_test.go that submits evals at the configured per-session ceiling, asserts RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After, then front-loads requests straddling a window boundary using tests/testinfra/clockstep and asserts the sliding window still rejects the burst.

### - [ ] T-ADV.13 — Token-exchange scope forgery and OAuth/idempotency replay are well covered; recording the strong baseline [Info] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Lenny's Token Service enforces this by: (a) rejecting any `scope` value not present in `subject_token.scope` (returns `invalid_scope`); (b) rejecting any `delegation_depth` decrement; (c) rejecting any `audience` change ...; (d) rejecting any `caller_type` elevation" (spec/13_security-model.md:583)
- **Existing tests:** Scope forgery is covered at unit (pkg/tokenexchange/tokenexchange_test.go: TestValidateRejectsScopeBroadening, TestValidateRejectsAudienceBroadening, TestValidateRejectsCallerTypeElevation, TestValidateRejectsCrossTenantCaller; pkg/tokenexchange/authorized_tools_test.go and fuzz_test.go) and contract level (tests/tier3_contract/oauth_token/oauth_token_test.go: TestScopeBroadeningRejected, TestCrossTenantExchangeRejected, TestCallerTypeElevationRejected, TestExpiredSubjectRejected, TestPerDialectCapCapsExp). OAuth state replay is covered in tests/tier4_integration/connector_oauth_test.go (single-use state and forged-state rejection). Idempotency-key collision is covered at unit (pkg/gateway/middleware/idempotency/idempotency_test.go: same-key/different-body 422, in-flight 409), contract (tests/tier3_contract/rest_idempotency), and integration (tests/tier4_integration/idempotency_test.go: tenant-scoped replay). Webhook HMAC replay is covered at unit (pkg/webhooksig/webhooksig_test.go: TestVerifyEnforcesReplayWindow) and SDK contract (tests/tier3_contract/sdks/go_client_test.go: TestGoClientWebhookSignatureVerification with the 5-minute window).

They are recorded here so the theme summary is not read as a blanket deficiency: scope forgery, cross-tenant token exchange, OAuth state replay, idempotency-key collision, and webhook replay each have a negative test at multiple tiers, including a contract test pinned against the RFC 8693 / §14 wire format. The remaining adversarial work is concentrated in the findings above.
- **Dependencies:** none — observational.
- **Suggested test:** None required. When the alg-confusion gap in T-ADV.9 is closed, fold the new cases next to the existing oauth_token and rest_auth contract tests so the JWT-forgery surface stays in one place.

## Theme — Integrated Testbed Scenarios <a id="t-theme-testbed"></a>
**Source:** spec/ and docs/ (cross-cutting)
**Reviewed:** 2026-07-06

### Summary
The test tree exercises each platform concern in isolation but has no integrated testbed that runs several moving parts at once. Delegation, MCP elicitation, the LLM proxy, and the four client protocols each have unit, component, or single-concern integration coverage, yet no test combines multiple interacting agents, a mix of platform and third-party MCP servers, a live or stubbed LLM provider through the gateway proxy, more than one client protocol, and failure injection in a single scenario. Three building blocks the testbeds require are absent or unused: the `llmprovider` stub is wired into no test outside its own unit test, there is no external third-party MCP server stub at all, and the `sessiondriver` harness speaks only REST. The most consequential composite scenarios are deferred: `TestAgentToLLMProviderPartition`, `TestChildCrashMidTask`, `TestParentCrashDuringAwaitChildren`, `TestCrossEnvironmentDelegation`, and `TestConcurrentExecutionModes` are `t.Logf` or `t.Skip` scaffolds, the reference-runtime conformance battery is scaffolded, and the tier-6 cloud parity matrix lists every capability as `planned`.
Counts: 6 High, 5 Medium, 2 Low, 1 Info.

### Findings

### - [x] T-BED.1 — No integrated testbed drives a live agent through the LLM Proxy to a stubbed upstream provider [High] — RESOLVED e75159139d5d8860f470ae9e7c7b4ccb91d07b2b
- **Resolution:** Added tier-4 integration coverage of the §4.9 LLM proxy proxy-mode delivery path (tests/tier4_integration/llm_proxy_roundtrip_test.go) plus a reusable tests/testinfra/proxylease helper. A live agent Anthropic Messages request is driven through the proxy to the llmprovider stub, asserting the opaque lease token resolves to a minted pool-backed proxy lease, the real upstream key is injected upstream (lease-token-to-real-key substitution) and never leaks to the pod, the response is translated back, and the authoritative token usage is extracted; a second test asserts an unknown lease token is rejected 401 before any upstream call. The tests pass against unmodified product code. The first run failed only because the helper omitted the mint-required proxyUrl field; that was corrected in the helper (test-side) and the tests then passed with no product change.

### - [x] T-BED.2 — No external third-party MCP server stub exists, so no testbed mixes platform-hosted and external MCP tools [High] — RESOLVED 10109489fa5b772f5f64ac03943c51fc2afd4363
- **Resolution:** Added a reusable external third-party MCP server stub (tests/testinfra/stubs/mcpserver) that serves the Streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC the gateway's outbound connector client drives (initialize, tools/list, tools/call) over HTTPS, with configurable latency and error injection. A new tier-4 integration test (tests/tier4_integration/external_mcp_tool_test.go) wires the real connectortools.Bridge, connectorinvoke.Invoker, connectorauthz.Authorizer, and outbound MCP client against the stub: a session lists and invokes an external tool, a policy-scoped child is denied the connector with the documented leasecontrol.ErrConnectorNotPermitted error while the parent is admitted, and the denial is re-checked at call time so a tightened policy blocks a previously-permitted connector. All tests passed against unmodified product code; no defect found.

### - [x] T-BED.3 — No testbed drives all four client protocols against one running deployment [High] — RESOLVED 9c494d5570fe58ee8206f0430837e45d5ab967f4
- **Resolution:** Added tier4 tests/tier4_integration/multi_protocol_same_deployment_test.go, which boots one real cmd/lenny-gateway process (via tests/testinfra/gateway) serving all four §15 client-facing protocols on one mux, runs create/prompt/read once per protocol against a single tenant, and asserts the four sessions are semantically identical rows (same tenant, same runtime) readable back through the one deployment, land in a single intact §11.7 audit chain (chainIntegrityReport broken==0, verified>=1), and reject the same invalid input consistently with identical code/category/retryable on the REST and MCP surfaces that share the §16.3 error taxonomy. It passes against unmodified product code; the prior tier3 rest_mcp_consistency / fidelity / multiprotocol_journey suites only asserted equivalence per operation (or one journey per protocol) across separate in-process httptest servers, never one deployment against shared session and audit state.

### - [x] T-BED.4 — No multi-agent testbed combines a delegation tree with the LLM proxy and external MCP tools [High] — RESOLVED 9d1b3534
- **Resolution:** Added tests/tier4_integration/multi_agent_testbed_test.go::TestMultiAgentDelegationTestbedPerHopInvariants, a tier-4 integration testbed that drives a live depth-3, fan-2 delegation tree through the real delegation Service while every node calls a model through the §4.9 LLM reverse proxy (llmprovider stub) and invokes an external §9.3 MCP tool (mcpserver stub via the real connector bridge). It asserts all three §8.2 per-hop invariants hold across the whole tree and that a cooperating runtime cannot bypass them: budget carving (each carved child budget is bounded by the parent's, and an over-budget hop is rejected with *lease.BudgetExceededError committing no child), scope subsetting (a grandchild scoped to a different connector is denied the tracker its sibling was admitted for, and the denied call never reaches the external server), and isolation monotonicity (children inherit the sandboxed profile and a hop requesting the weaker `standard` profile is rejected with *IsolationViolationError). It passed against the current product code on the first run and is registered under §8.2 in spec-map.json; the anti-collusion invariant that the finding said was covered "only in unit cycle/lease tests" is now exercised end to end across an integrated multi-agent tree. Verified with `go test -tags integration -race` and `lenny-test validate-maps`.

### - [x] T-BED.5 — No integrated testbed injects a failure mid-scenario while multiple parts are in flight [High] — RESOLVED 8378d45a282ab39ebc06f665e687ec08eb47bc99
- **Resolution:** Added tier-8 chaos test TestProviderPartitionMidDelegationRecovers that runs a live delegation tree with model traffic through the §4.9 LLM proxy, partitions the upstream provider mid-scenario, and asserts the §12.8 six-step chaos contract: the circuit breaker trips open, PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE reaches the pod without further dialing the doomed upstream, the breaker recovers via its half-open probe after the cooldown, and the in-flight delegation tree's session rows and carved token budgets are uncorrupted. Extended the proxylease testinfra helper with an injectable circuit breaker so the fault can be driven deterministically across requests. Passed against unmodified product code.

### - [x] T-BED.6 — Reference-runtime conformance battery and the OpenAI/Anthropic fidelity matrix are scaffolds [High] — RESOLVED 048e279d

All seven named tests in the original finding now execute real assertions against the bundled runtimes and translators; none remains a `t.Skip`/`t.Logf` scaffold.

### - [x] T-BED.7 — No testbed exercises concurrent execution mode together with delegation and multi-protocol traffic [Medium] — RESOLVED c169611c83054bcb8f8532b1f03b7ef1ffecc3f1
- **Resolution:** Added tier-4 integration test tests/tier4_integration/concurrent_delegation_proxy_test.go::TestConcurrentSlotsDelegationAndProxyIsolation_spec_5_2, which opens two slots on one concurrent-mode pod (real adapter.Server per-slot path + echo-concurrent runtime), has slot 0 delegate a child through the delegation Service while slot 1 calls a model through the LLM reverse proxy under concurrent mixed load, and asserts per-slot credential isolation (each slot's independent lease in its own /run/lenny/slots/{slotId}/credentials.json with no cross-slot leak and no pod-global file), independent per-session budget accounting (a slice denied to slot 0's session is admitted under slot 1's session on the same pod, proving budget is bound to the session not pooled), and independent per-slot cleanup (one ReportSessionScrub per release, releasing one slot leaves the sibling's session and credential file intact). It passed on the first run against unmodified product code; the concurrent-mode + delegation + proxy interaction was already correct and simply uncovered.

### - [ ] T-BED.8 — Cross-environment delegation testbed is a scaffold; the credential-compatibility rejection is unexercised end to end [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** "Before approving a cross-environment `delegate_task` call with `credentialPropagation: inherit`, the gateway performs a **provider compatibility check** ... If the intersection is empty ... the delegation is **rejected** with error code `CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_MISMATCH` before pod allocation." (spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:470)
- **Existing tests:** tests/tier5_e2e_kind/scaffolds_test.go:298 `TestCrossEnvironmentDelegation` calls `kind.InstallLenny` then only logs that the reachability rule is covered by the envaccess unit suite and `delegate_task_filtering_test`, deferring the composite e2e to the ops backlog (commit 94e184e0, "tier-5 e2e: retire TestCrossEnvironmentDelegation by-design", reclassified this as a documented backlog item rather than an unconditional skip, but did not build the composite exercise). No test drives a delegation across an environment boundary with `credentialPropagation: inherit` and asserts the `CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_MISMATCH` rejection or the successful intersection path.
- **Gap:** Cross-environment delegation, a multi-agent scenario that spans the §10.6 environment model, has no executing assertion at the integration or e2e tier. Both the admit path (non-empty provider intersection) and the deterministic reject path are untested as a journey. This is a failure-path and deployment-combination gap. Target tier4 then tier5.
- **Dependencies:** Requires two runtimes with differing `supportedProviders` and two environments configured in the test gateway. Building the two-environment fixture is part of this finding.
- **Suggested test:** Add tier4 tests/tier4_integration/cross_environment_delegation_test.go with a parent in environment A delegating with `inherit` to a child runtime in environment B, one case asserting admission on a non-empty intersection and one asserting `CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_MISMATCH` before pod allocation on an empty intersection.
- **Needs human input (as of 2026-07-11):** The §8.3 cross-environment `credentialPropagation: inherit` provider compatibility check (compute intersection of parent credential-pool providers with child runtime supportedProviders; reject empty with CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_MISMATCH before pod allocation) is fully specified but entirely absent from the delegation path — there is no `credentialPropagation` field on the delegate_task schema or the delegation Request, and no code produces the error (only the error-classification table and docs mention it). This is an unimplemented spec feature, not a testbed scaffold gap. Should the feature be built through the implement-proposal / BUILD-GAPS pipeline (adding the credentialPropagation lease field, origin-pool provider tracking, cross-environment detection, and the pre-claim intersection check), after which this tier-4 test's t.Skip is removed to close the gap? It cannot be closed as a test-only fix because there is no product behavior to assert against.

- **Spec/Doc:** "every component is exercised ... through an in-process multi-component harness (`tests/testinfra/inproc`) that boots a single-binary Lenny with `miniredis`, an embedded Postgres adapter, and a fake Kubernetes API surface." (TESTING.md:1136)

Multi-component harness scenarios named in TESTING.md §12.7.a (`tenant_isolation_load`, `mixed_workload`, `delegation_depth_n`, `error_injection_matrix`, and others) therefore still run against a hand-written mock rather than Lenny code.

- **Needs human input (as of 2026-07-11):** Should the tier-7a in-process harness actually boot the real cmd/lenny-gateway composition root (a large refactor to make that root constructible in-process against miniredis + an embedded Postgres adapter + fakekube, then reworking the six scenarios that drive it), or should TESTING.md §12.7.a's "boots a single-binary Lenny" wording be reconciled through the proposal pipeline with the current per-scenario approach where scenarios drive real product packages directly (as delegation_depth_n drives pkg/delegation/cycle.Decide and error_injection_matrix drives the runtime stub)? The blast radius (whole gateway composition root plus six scenarios) and the architectural question of whether the gateway root can be booted in-process without real Postgres/KMS/PKI make this exceed a scoped test-gap fix.

### - [x] T-BED.10 — Tier-6 cloud parity matrix lists every integrated capability as planned, so no cross-provider testbed runs [Medium] — RESOLVED 62d174c03b05c7af4f287c6a08e3e057fd21b20b

### - [ ] T-BED.13 — No testbed covers a mixed auth-mode deployment where different clients use different auth on the same gateway [Low] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** The auth dimensions include "OIDC with PKCE, API key, dev mode, pod-to-gateway mTLS, JWT with RFC 9068 scopes, workload identity / IRSA / WIF", and the playground suite asserts "Three auth modes: OIDC, API Key, Dev" work (TESTING.md:1958).
- **Existing tests:** tests/tier5_e2e_kind/scaffolds_test.go and the playground tier-5 suite cover the three playground auth modes, and tests/tier4_integration/jwks_test.go plus jwt_rotation_audit_test.go cover JWT verification. Each auth mode is tested in isolation. No integrated scenario drives one deployment where, for example, alice authenticates via OIDC PKCE, an automation client uses an API key, and pods authenticate over mTLS, all against the same tenant concurrently.
- **Gap:** The interaction between auth modes on one deployment is unexercised. A scoped JWT (RFC 9068) narrowing access while an API-key client and an mTLS-bound pod operate on the same session is an integrated path with no coverage. This is a deployment-combination gap. Target tier5.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the OIDC stub (tests/testinfra/stubs/oidc), API-key provisioning, and the mTLS install variant together in one Kind install. The pieces exist; composing them is the work.
- **Suggested test:** Add tier5 tests/tier5_e2e_kind/mixed_auth_modes_test.go that, on one tenant, runs an OIDC-PKCE client, an API-key client, and an mTLS-bound pod against the same session and asserts each is authorized for its documented scope and rejected outside it.
- **Needs human input (as of 2026-07-11):** The integrated scenario as written cannot be built faithfully as one passing tier-5 test: (a) per §10.2/§27.2/§27.4 there is no separate "API-key" credential primitive in v1 — the playground "oidc" and "apiKey" modes are the same standard gateway bearer, so "an OIDC-PKCE client and an API-key client" are not two distinct auth mechanisms (already proven e2e by auth_modes_test.go); and (b) the RFC 9068 scoped-JWT centerpiece is not reachable end-to-end on the e2e Kind install (global.devMode:true, no in-cluster OIDC provider, dev-headers carry no scope claim; and minting a scoped token via /v1/oauth/token from the admin bearer fails because gateway and token-service use independent local KMS keys) — which is exactly why tier-9 admin_scope_enforce_test.go tests scope narrowing in-process. Given standard-bearer (auth_modes_test.go), mTLS (mtls_test.go), and scope narrowing (tier-9) are each already covered, should this finding be closed as moot, or should a reduced tier-5 integrated test be added that composes only the standard-bearer + mTLS-pod + invalid-credential axes on one deployment (dropping the spec-contradicted distinct "API-key client" and the e2e-unreachable scope-narrowing assertion)? If a true e2e scope-narrowing assertion is wanted, the e2e install needs an OIDC provider (an OIDC stub exists) or a shared KMS key between gateway and token-service so a scoped token can be minted and verified in-cluster — that is an install/config change beyond this finding.

## Coverage meta-analysis <a id="t-meta"></a>

**Source:** spec/ and docs/ (cross-cutting meta-review of the per-unit audit set)
**Reviewed:** 2026-06-03

This document reviews the per-unit audit set for gaps in the audit itself. The per-section passes are detailed and the five cross-cutting themes (conformance, adversarial, deployment-matrix, user-journeys, integrated-testbed) cover most of the integration surface. The findings below are the layer above: spec subsections that received too few findings to be plausibly complete, whole standards and capabilities that no single unit took ownership of, deployment cells that fall between the per-unit reviews, and a build order for the integrated testbeds that the theme audits each proposed in isolation. Where a finding restates a theme conclusion, it is recorded as a consolidation rather than a new defect, and the overlap is named.

A repeated structural observation underlies several findings: the test infrastructure to close these gaps largely exists already. The `llmprovider` stub speaks Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Chat Completions, Open Responses, and Vertex/Gemini; the `delegation-echo`, `streaming-echo`, and `mcp-reference` runtimes exist as source under `cmd/runtimes/`; a JSON Schema compiler is wrapped in `tests/testinfra/schematest`; and the `matrix`, `sessiondriver`, and `sdkhelper` harnesses are present. The gaps are concentrated in wiring (building images into the Kind workload, vendoring external schemas, pointing the gateway at the stubs) rather than in net-new component construction. This makes the integrated testbeds cheaper to build than the per-unit summaries individually suggest, which is the central reason to prioritize them.

### Likely under-audited areas

### - [ ] T-META.1 — The §1-3 architecture chapter was audited as a single unit with 7 findings; the controller sub-sections §4.6.1/§4.6.2/§4.6.3 carry distinct test sets that no unit owned individually [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** spec/03_high-level-architecture.md and spec/04_system-components.md; spec-map.json maps §4.6.1 (Warm Pool Controller, ADR-007 optimistic locking) to 11 tests, §4.6.2 (PoolScalingController) to 7 tests, and §4.6.3 (CRD field-ownership matrix) to 4 tests, each a separate test set.
- **Existing tests:** The §4.6 audit unit ("Pod Lifecycle Controllers", 13 findings) reviewed the controller surface as a whole and surfaced the leader-kill-mid-claim, etcd-unavailability, and SSA 409 findings. The architecture chapters §1-3 were folded into a single 7-finding unit. The three §4.6.x sub-sections each have their own spec-map entry, their own blocked-until-phase, and their own test list (`tests/tier2_component/poolscaling`, the SandboxClaim envtest suites, the ownership-matrix Go check), but no audit unit is keyed to the sub-section granularity.
- **Gap:** Auditing a chapter as one unit risks averaging out a sub-section whose coverage is weaker than the chapter mean. The §4.6.2 PoolScalingStrategy interface (Phase 3) and the §4.6.3 ownership matrix (Phase 3.5) are exactly the kind of late-phase normative surface that a chapter-level pass under-weights. The architecture chapters §1-3, audited together, restate the §4.x platform goals; the Tier-3 ten-thousand-session horizontal-scaling goal noted there is the only structural finding, which is thin for an entire architecture chapter. Re-check whether the §4.6.2 demotion-circuit-breaker and leader-failover paths and the §4.6.3 SSA field-ownership matrix have a component-or-higher assertion, not only the unit-tier Go matrix.
- **Dependencies:** none — this is a re-audit at finer granularity, not a new test. The envtest harness (`tests/testinfra/envtest`) and the poolscaling component suite already exist.

### Standards and protocols not owned by any unit

This section consolidates the standards-conformance gaps that the conformance theme (T-STD.*) identified, and adds dimensions that even that theme did not enumerate. The unifying defect is that with one exception (the adapter JSON-Lines protocol, validated against Lenny's own committed schema) no test validates Lenny output against a vendored external schema, and no external schema artifact for OpenAI, MCP, CloudEvents, OCSF, OpenSLO, or OFREP exists in the repository. A JSON Schema compiler (`tests/testinfra/schematest`) is already present, so the gap is vendoring plus assertion, not infrastructure.

### - [ ] T-META.6 — The OpenAI Open Responses streaming SSE event taxonomy has no contract or conformance owner; coverage is unit-only and the conformance theme addressed only the non-streaming envelope [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** spec/15_external-api-surface.md serves `/v1/responses` as a built-in adapter; the API-reference doc audit (doc-api-reference) names "Open Responses streaming SSE event taxonomy has no contract/conformance test against the external schema."
- **Existing tests:** `pkg/gateway/translator/open_responses_test.go` covers the translator at unit tier; `tests/tier3_contract/rest_openai_responses/scaffolds_test.go` decodes the non-streaming body into Lenny's own `OpenResponsesResponse` struct (the conformance theme's T-STD.1 addresses this non-streaming envelope). The streaming SSE event taxonomy for Open Responses (`response.created`, `response.output_text.delta`, `response.completed`, and siblings) has no contract test; `tests/testdata/openai_responses` contains only a single non-streaming `simple/` fixture, with no `streaming/events.sse` counterpart to the one the OpenAI Chat corpus has.
- **Gap:** Open Responses is one of the four advertised client protocols and its streaming taxonomy is the half a real client consumes. The conformance theme pinned the static envelope and the deployment-matrix theme noted no e2e drives the surface, but neither owns the streaming event-name taxonomy against OpenAI's published Responses streaming schema. A renamed or mistyped streaming event would ship. Target tier3 contract with the schema reused at tier5.
- **Dependencies:** Requires vendoring the OpenAI Responses streaming event schemas into tests/testdata/openai_responses/streaming and a captured golden SSE stream. `tests/testinfra/schematest` and the existing chat streaming fixture pattern (`tests/testdata/openai_chat/streaming/events.sse`) are the template.
- **Suggested test:** Add `tests/tier3_contract/rest_openai_responses/streaming_schema_test.go` that drives a streaming `/v1/responses` request, parses the SSE frames, and validates each event against the vendored Open Responses streaming schema, plus a `streaming/` golden corpus mirroring the chat corpus (overlaps T-STD.1, T-STD.4).

- **Spec/Doc:** spec/15_external-api-surface.md:1356-1374 (each frame MUST carry SeqNum on the SSE `id:` line; the per-kind projection maps each SessionEventKind to one MCP frame such as `elicitation/create`, `notifications/tasks/statusUpdate`, `notifications/lenny/toolCall`).

### Uncovered deployment combinations

The deployment cross-product is execution-mode × isolation × topology × storage × protocol × auth. The deployment-matrix theme (T-DEP.*) enumerated the major empty cells. This section adds the cells that fall between the theme's findings and names the combinatorial blind spots the per-axis findings do not capture.

### - [ ] T-META.11 — The audited cross-product collapses to one canonical cell; the combinations that pair two weak axes (sandboxed isolation × non-REST protocol, task/concurrent mode × real cluster, cloud KMS × proxy mode) are doubly uncovered and no unit owns the pairing [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** TESTING.md:1110 (sandboxed isolation), :1916 (per-surface equivalence), :1929 (task/concurrent on Kind), §12.6 cloud_kms; the deployment dimensions are listed across spec/17 and TESTING.md §12.5-§12.6.
- **Existing tests:** The only combination driven on a real cluster is session-mode × runc × single-node/EKS × single-replica stores × REST × dev-header auth (the deployment-matrix theme T-DEP.1 through T-DEP.9 establish this). Each weak axis has its own finding: sandboxed isolation is a skip-stub (T-DEP.1), non-REST protocols never reach a cluster (T-DEP.4), task/concurrent modes run only on compose (T-DEP.5), cloud KMS is skip-guarded (T-DEP.3, T-BED.10).
- **Gap:** The per-axis findings each fix one dimension while holding the others at the canonical value, so they never test a cell where two weak axes meet. A regression that only manifests when, for example, an MCP client drives a concurrent-mode pod under gVisor, or when proxy-mode credential injection runs against Cloud KMS on a sandboxed node, is invisible to every single-axis finding. No audit unit owns the pairing of weak axes, which is where the highest-risk integration defects hide. Target tier5 Kind for the on-cluster pairings and tier6 cloud for the KMS pairing.
- **Dependencies:** Requires the sandboxed node pool (T-DEP.1), the non-REST cluster drivers (T-DEP.4), the task/concurrent Kind workload (T-DEP.5), and the cloud KMS provisioning (T-DEP.3). These are the same dependencies the single-axis findings name; the new work is composing them into paired cells.
- **Suggested test:** Once the single-axis dependencies land, add `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/paired_dimensions_test.go` that drives an MCP session onto a concurrent-mode pod under the sandboxed RuntimeClass (pairing protocol × execution-mode × isolation), and a tier6 `sandbox_proxy_kms_test.go` that runs a proxy-mode session on a gVisor node with a Cloud KMS-backed T4 credential (pairing isolation × delivery-mode × storage; this extends T-BED.10 to also vary isolation).

### - [ ] T-META.12 — The compose-stack tier (tier4) and the cluster tiers (tier5/tier6) cover disjoint dimension subsets, so no single deployment ever exercises both real stores and a real pod under a real protocol [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** TESTING.md §12.4 (tier4 compose with real Postgres/Redis/MinIO), §12.5 (tier5 Kind with real pods), §12.6 (tier6 cloud).

Tier5 Kind runs real pods but the agent-workload deploys only echo, echo-embedded, cred-shell-echo, and elicitation-echo (confirmed: `tests/testinfra/kind/agent-workload.yaml`), and the cluster lifecycle tests drive REST against memstore-or-minimal state, with the cloud lifecycle test (T-JRN.2) tolerating a 500 because `/start` never binds a pod.

No tier verifies a prompt round-tripping through a real pod while the session, checkpoint, and audit state live in real Postgres/MinIO under a non-REST protocol. This is the gap between the compose and cluster tiers that the per-tier findings (T-JRN.1, T-JRN.2, T-DEP.4) each see from one side.
