Target tier5 Kind for OIDC/API-key/JWT and tier6 cloud for WIF and Azure AD.
- **Dependencies:** The OIDC stub exists for Kind; GCP/Azure workload-identity provisioning is the T-DEP.2 dependency.
- **Suggested test:** Add the T-DEP.8 `auth_modes_test.go` (OIDC, API key, scoped JWT on Kind) and extend the cloud `behavior_test.go` with GCP WIF and Azure AD assertions, parameterized over the provider axis so the auth × provider cube has at least one validated cell per provider (consolidates T-DEP.8, T-JRN.11).

### Priority integrated testbeds to build first

The five theme audits each proposed integrated testbeds (T-BED.1 through T-BED.14, T-JRN.1 through T-JRN.12, T-DEP.1 through T-DEP.13). They were authored independently and share dependencies that no single audit sequenced. This section orders them by value-per-unit-of-shared-infrastructure, so the earliest testbeds unlock the most downstream ones. The ordering principle is that three building blocks gate almost everything: the LLM-proxy wiring to the `llmprovider` stub, an external MCP server stub, and the multi-runtime Kind workload (building `delegation-echo` and `streaming-echo` images, which exist as source). Each testbed below names the agents and runtimes, the MCP and LLM topology, the assertions, the target tier, and the infrastructure dependencies.

### - [ ] T-META.15 — Priority 1: the LLM-proxy round-trip testbed, because it is the foundation every model-bearing testbed depends on and is buildable at tier4 today [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** spec/04_system-components.md:1459 (the LLM Proxy validates the lease, runs the interceptor chain, injects the real upstream key, forwards, and extracts authoritative usage); the proxy-mode "real key never enters the pod" invariant is normative in §4.9 and §13.3.
- **Existing tests:** The `llmprovider` stub (`tests/testinfra/stubs/llmprovider`) speaks Anthropic, OpenAI Chat, Open Responses, and Vertex/Gemini but is imported only by its own unit test. `tests/tier4_integration/scaffolds_test.go::TestLLMProxyAnthropic` logs and asserts nothing. The §4.9 audit (17 findings, the highest in the set) and the testbed theme T-BED.1 both name this as the missing foundation.
- **Gap:** No test boots the real gateway, leases a proxy credential, and drives an agent request through the proxy to the stub. Agents and runtimes: one echo session acting as the LLM-calling agent. MCP/LLM topology: no MCP tools; the gateway's LLM proxy points its upstream base URL at the `llmprovider` stub; one credential pool in `deliveryMode: proxy`. Assertions: the stub received the injected upstream key (and the pod never saw it), the request was translated to the upstream dialect, the response was translated back to the agent dialect, and authoritative token usage was extracted. Target tier4, then tier5.
- **Dependencies:** The stub exists; the missing piece is a testinfra helper that points the gateway upstream at the stub and provisions a pool-backed proxy lease. Reuse `tests/testinfra/gateway` and `tests/testinfra/stubs/llmprovider`. This dependency has the widest reach because T-META.16, T-META.17, T-META.18, and the chaos testbed all consume it.
- **Suggested test:** Implement T-BED.1's `tests/tier4_integration/llm_proxy_roundtrip_test.go` (boot gateway, register a proxy pool pointed at the stub, issue Anthropic Messages and OpenAI Chat through `{proxyUrl}`, assert injection, translation, and usage extraction), and build the reusable `proxylease` testinfra helper as part of it.

### - [ ] T-META.16 — Priority 2: the external-MCP-tool testbed plus the connector-scoping adversarial assertion, because it is the only missing primitive (an external MCP server stub) and unlocks both the tool journey and the prompt-injection defense [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** spec/09_mcp-integration.md:10 (gateway ↔ external MCP tools), :164 (the gateway validates `connector_id` against the calling pod's effective delegation policy before proxying; a child cannot use connectors not permitted by its policy).
- **Existing tests:** No external MCP server stub exists anywhere under `tests/testinfra/stubs` (confirmed: only `cmd/runtimes/mcp-reference`, which is a runtime, not a third-party tool server). The connector-scoping decision is unit-only (`pkg/gateway/connectorinvoke`). The testbed theme T-BED.2 and the adversarial theme T-ADV.6 both depend on this stub.
- **Gap:** No test connects the gateway to a real external MCP server, lists and invokes its tools from a session, and asserts per-delegation connector scoping. Agents and runtimes: a parent echo session and a scoped echo child. MCP/LLM topology: the gateway hosts its platform MCP tools at `/mcp` and proxies to one external MCP server stub registered as a connector; no LLM traffic required. Assertions: the parent lists and calls the external tool successfully, the scoped child is denied the external connector with the documented §9.3 policy error, and no outbound dial occurs on the denial even though a root-level token exists. Target tier4, then tier5. This testbed doubles as the prompt-injection defense (tool output flowing into a nested agent's context).
- **Dependencies:** Build a new external MCP server stub under `tests/testinfra/stubs/mcpserver` serving Streamable HTTP `initialize`/`tools/list`/`tools/call` with configurable latency and error injection. This is the only net-new component; once it exists, T-BED.2, T-ADV.6, and the external-tool half of T-META.18 are buildable.
- **Suggested test:** Build the stub, then implement T-BED.2's `tests/tier4_integration/external_mcp_tool_test.go` (register the stub as a connector, drive a session that calls one platform tool and one external tool, assert the scoped child is denied) and fold in T-ADV.6's tool-output-into-child-context assertion.

### - [ ] T-META.17 — Priority 3: the multi-protocol single-deployment testbed, because the harness gap is small (sessiondriver is REST-only) and it pins the headline "one gateway, four protocols" claim plus the §15.2.1 equivalence contract [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** spec/15_external-api-surface.md:1388 (contract tests call REST and every built-in external adapter and assert structural and behavioral equivalence); README.md:75 (one gateway, four protocols, one auth/policy/routing/audit path).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver` covers only the REST surface (its doc comment says "methods cover the §15.1 session REST surface"). The protocol contract suites are single-shot fidelity scaffolds. The testbed theme T-BED.3, the user-journeys T-JRN.3, the deployment-matrix T-DEP.4, the conformance T-STD.4, and the meta finding T-META.2 all converge here.
- **Gap:** No test stands up one gateway and drives the same session or tenant through REST, MCP, OpenAI Chat Completions, and Open Responses together. Agents and runtimes: one echo (or streaming-echo) session per protocol against one tenant. MCP/LLM topology: one gateway serving all four client surfaces; no external MCP or LLM proxy required for the equivalence assertion (it can run against the EchoExecutor). Assertions: identical session rows, a single shared audit chain, equivalent error envelopes across surfaces, and a streamed final chunk on the two streaming surfaces. Target tier3 for the equivalence matrix and tier4/tier5 for the composed journey. This is the testbed that retires the largest cluster of overlapping findings.
- **Dependencies:** Extend `tests/testinfra/sessiondriver` with MCP, OpenAI Chat, and Open Responses methods (the `sdkhelper` and `matrix` harnesses already exist). No new runtime or stub. Note the dependency on T-META.7: the MCP streaming leg requires the per-kind projection to be implemented first; the non-streaming MCP leg is buildable today.
- **Suggested test:** Implement T-BED.3's `tests/tier4_integration/multi_protocol_same_deployment_test.go` and T-META.2's tier3 `equivalence_matrix_test.go` together, sharing the extended sessiondriver, so the equivalence contract (§15.2.1) and the four-protocol journey land on one harness.

### - [ ] T-META.18 — Priority 4: the multi-agent delegation tree with the LLM proxy and external MCP tools, because it is the headline integrated journey and it composes Priorities 1 through 3 plus the multi-runtime workload [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** spec/08_recursive-delegation.md:9 (the gateway enforces three invariants on every hop: budget carving, scope subsetting, isolation monotonicity; a runtime cannot bypass these by cooperating with another runtime); :530 (`lenny/await_children`).
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier4_integration/delegation_test.go` spawns one echo-child against the in-process executor, one hop, no LLM proxy, no external MCP tool, and never calls `await_children`. The `delegation-echo` runtime exists as source (`cmd/runtimes/delegation-echo`) but is not built into the Kind workload (confirmed: `agent-workload.yaml` deploys only echo variants and elicitation-echo). The testbed theme T-BED.4, the user-journeys T-JRN.4, and the adversarial T-ADV.1 all target this tree.
- **Gap:** No testbed exercises several agents delegating while each calls a model through the proxy and invokes platform and external MCP tools, then asserts the anti-collusion invariants hold across the tree. Agents and runtimes: a delegation-echo root spawning a depth-3 fan-2 tree of delegation-echo and echo children. MCP/LLM topology: each node calls the `llmprovider` stub through the proxy (Priority 1) and one external MCP tool (Priority 2), with the four-protocol driver (Priority 3) able to drive the root over any surface. Assertions: per-hop budget carving, scope subsetting, isolation monotonicity, correct `await_children` collection in `all`/`any`/`settled` modes, and the cycle/depth/fan-out rejections (DELEGATION_CYCLE_DETECTED, DELEGATION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED). Target tier4, then tier5 on real pods.
- **Dependencies:** Composes Priorities 1, 2, and 3, plus building `delegation-echo` into a deployable image and adding it to `tests/testinfra/kind/agent-workload.yaml`. The runtime source exists; the work is the image build and workload wiring.
- **Suggested test:** Implement T-BED.4's `tests/tier5_e2e_kind/multi_agent_testbed_test.go` (depth-3 fan-2 tree, each node calling the stub and one external tool, asserting per-hop invariants) and fold in T-JRN.4's `await_children` collection and T-ADV.1's rejection assertions; add `delegation-echo` to the Kind workload as the enabling step.

### - [ ] T-META.19 — Priority 5: the composite-chaos testbed (failure injection mid-scenario), because it is the resilience half of the platform guarantee and reuses Priority 4 unchanged [High] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** TESTING.md:1224 (every chaos test brings the system to a known-good state, injects the failure, asserts documented behavior, resolves, asserts recovery, and asserts no data loss or bounded loss); the network-failure group names "agent-to-LLM-provider partition."
- **Existing tests:** `tests/tier8_chaos/scaffolds_test.go` carries `TestAgentToLLMProviderPartition`, `TestChildCrashMidTask`, `TestParentCrashDuringAwaitChildren`, and `TestDelegationBudgetExhaustion` as `t.Logf` placeholders. `live_session_test.go` injects a single pod kill against one REST echo session. The testbed theme T-BED.5 and the deployment-matrix T-DEP.6 (HA failover) target this.
- **Gap:** Failure injection is never combined with a live multi-part scenario. Agents and runtimes: the Priority 4 delegation tree, unchanged. MCP/LLM topology: the same tree-with-proxy-and-external-tools, with a fault injected mid-task. Assertions: partitioning the agent from the LLM provider (or returning PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE from the stub) opens the circuit breaker and surfaces the documented error; killing a child triggers the documented recovery; on resolution, in-flight work recovers without budget or task-tree corruption. Target tier8. A second variant exercises Postgres HA failover (T-DEP.6) against an in-flight tree using the unused `datastores-ha-postgres.yaml` overlay.
- **Dependencies:** Reuses Priority 4 plus a partition primitive on the gateway-to-upstream egress path (the `llmprovider` stub has `SetResponseOverride` for provider errors; the network partition needs the chaos helper extended) and, for the HA variant, wiring `datastores-ha-postgres.yaml` into the Kind installer with a `pg_ctl promote` step.
- **Suggested test:** Implement T-BED.5's `tests/tier8_chaos/testbed_partition_test.go` (run the Priority 4 tree, partition the agent from the provider mid-task, assert breaker-open and bounded recovery) and T-DEP.6's `postgres_ha_failover_test.go` against the same tree (kill the primary, promote the replica, assert the in-flight tree survives).

### - [ ] T-META.20 — Priority 6: the sandboxed-isolation cloud testbed, because it is the only family that needs genuinely new infrastructure (provisioned sandbox node pools) and gates the largest deployment-matrix cell cluster [Medium] — OPEN
- **Spec/Doc:** TESTING.md:1110 (the default sandboxed profile creates pods on gVisor or a provider-equivalent node pool with documented sandbox semantics); the parity matrix marks every isolation row `planned` (tests/tier6_e2e_cloud/parity-matrix.yaml).
- **Existing tests:** `TestGvisorIsolation` and `TestKataIsolation` log and return when no sandbox node is present, passing vacuously. On Kind, `pod_lifecycle_test.go` asserts `runtimeClassName == "runc"` only. The deployment-matrix theme T-DEP.1, T-DEP.12 (Confidential Containers), the testbed T-BED.10, and the cross-cutting §5.3/§1-3 isolation findings all converge here.
- **Gap:** The default production isolation profile is never exercised in any tier; the entire isolation dimension collapses to runc. Agents and runtimes: one echo session on the sandboxed node pool, and a security-probe pod attempting capability and syscall escapes. MCP/LLM topology: optionally the Priority 1 proxy and a Cloud KMS-backed T4 credential, to pair isolation with the storage and delivery-mode axes per T-META.11. Assertions: a pod boots under the sandboxed RuntimeClass, process-namespace isolation and capability drop hold, syscall filtering is enforced, and (in the paired variant) the proxy and the KMS fail-closed behavior hold on the sandbox. Target tier6 cloud (gVisor on GKE, Kata-equivalent on AKS, Firecracker on EKS), with a tier5 Kind gVisor lane when the node image carries the RuntimeClass.
- **Dependencies:** Requires provisioned sandbox node pools per provider through `scripts/cloud/<provider>/up.sh` and a gVisor-capable Kind node image. This is the family with the most genuinely new infrastructure, which is why it is sequenced after the buildable-today testbeds despite its high security value. It also depends on the GCP/Azure provisioning scripts (T-DEP.2) for the AKS Confidential Containers and GKE gVisor cells.
- **Suggested test:** Implement T-DEP.1's sandbox node-pool assertion (claim a SandboxWarmPool, drive a session onto the sandboxed pod, assert namespace isolation and capability drop), promote at least one parity-matrix row per provider to `validated`, and add the T-BED.10 KMS-fail-closed pairing on the sandbox node (this is the cloud realization of T-META.11's weak-axis pairing).
